short_description: Two volumes on the Thorin measure whose positivity is equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis, computed in certified ball arithmetic: Volume I on representations of Xi, Thorin measures and the reciprocal Xi function, Volume II on Cauchy deconvolution and certified computation.
description:
The Riemann Hypothesis can be restated as the positivity of a measure, the Thorin measure of a ratio of values of Riemann's Xi function. This book computes that measure from Pólya's integral for Xi, without primes or a list of zeros, in certified ball arithmetic, and asks what such computations can and cannot teach about the zeros.

A certified zero off the critical line would refute the hypothesis, but no finite computation can prove it. From the zeros verified up to height 3 × 10^12 the book certifies that the derivatives of the heat trace have the predicted signs up to order 1.16 × 10^25, and proves that such finite positivity tests cannot settle it: a perturbation of Xi with the same zeros below a large height, and zeros off the line above it, passes them. No proof of the hypothesis is claimed.

New results: the reciprocal Xi function at x to the power p is hyperbolically completely monotone exactly when the absolute value of p is at most one minus twice the largest zero angle over pi; at the basepoint one the Thorin density is certified smallest at the origin, so the shifted clock is a stable variable plus a generalized gamma convolution; between the basepoints one half and one the shifted clocks are almost generalized gamma convolutions, unconditionally; the clock of Pólya's Bessel function is the hitting time of an explicit diffusion; adjacent real zeros of a polynomial cannot meet under the backward heat flow before an explicit time; and the Pólya law lies within 2 × 10^-6 in total variation of the ferromagnetic laws of Lee and Yang, a distance that is zero exactly under the hypothesis.

The book is in two volumes. Volume I, Representations of Xi, Thorin Measures and the Reciprocal Xi Function, develops the theory: the analytic and probabilistic representations of Xi, infinite divisibility, generalised gamma convolutions and the Bondesson hierarchy, the heat trace, the reciprocal zeta function, the basepoints and the critical strip, Dedekind eta and Dirichlet L functions, hitting times and Krein strings, extreme value and ferromagnetic laws with a two spin Lee and Yang form of the hypothesis, Pólya and Haseo Ki on the zeros of entire functions, and a route to the Riemann Hypothesis assembled from the whole book. Volume II, Cauchy Deconvolution and Certified Computation, holds the computations: what computation can and cannot decide, Xi in ball arithmetic, the Thorin measure at finite resolution, the de Bruijn Newman flow and the barrier method in Thorin form, the Thorin phase diagram, Cauchy deconvolution from the level one measure down to the zeros (the backward Cauchy flow, the explicit formula as a deconvolution, particle filters and the Balazard, Saias and Yor criterion by Monte Carlo), Weil positivity in the windows of Yoshida and Zhu, truncations and friable approximants of Xi with certified real zeros, approximating clocks, and conditional results under a quasi Riemann hypothesis.

The October 2026 claims of a zero free half plane Re s > 7/8 for all L functions, and the later preprints that lower the constant slightly, are not refereed: the book states only conditional consequences (a principal signal for zeta, the sliver and Mertens estimate, the Thorin property at every basepoint above 7/8), credited to their authors.

The scripts and data files behind the tables and figures are in the book's repository https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh, listed in code/README.md.

chapters.title: Introduction: the Riemann Hypothesis as the positivity of a measure
chapters.summary:
This chapter states the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) as a positivity condition and sets out the plan of the two volumes. For the completed zeta function $\xi$, put $G(u)=\xi(\frac12+\sqrt{u})/\xi(\frac12)$; the reciprocal $1/G$ is the clock. RH holds exactly when the clock is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution (GGC), whose Thorin measure is then the sum of unit atoms at the squared ordinates of the zeros. This is the Thorin condition. Its equivalent forms are sign conditions: $G'/G$ is a Stieltjes transform, the heat trace of the zeros is completely monotone, the Thorin density $\rho_\varepsilon(\theta)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\frac12+\varepsilon+i\theta)$ is nonnegative at every resolution $\varepsilon>0$ (Lagarias's criterion), Weil's explicit formula functional is positive, and the clock is hyperbolically completely monotone (HCM). The chapter introduces the Hadamard product, the Pólya kernel and density, van Dantzig pairs, the Poisson smoothing of the zeros (the Cauchy flow) and the sine squared lemma, which gives the Thorin density from the primes. It treats GGCs for computation: the Bondesson hierarchy, diagnostics of the Thorin condition and the sinh clock benchmark. It explains why computation can measure but not prove the Thorin condition. The overture describes the division of the material between the theory of Volume I and the computation of Volume II, fixes the status words (proved, computed, certified, conditional, heuristic, open) and one notation for the Thorin density at a basepoint or level, and states the clearest path to RH found in the two volumes: a positivity argument for a zero free half plane that uses the Euler product, with three constraints on any proof. Nothing here proves RH.

#### From the literature

- The Thorin representation of generalised gamma convolutions (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992); extended generalised gamma convolutions (Thorin 1978)
- The HCM characterisation of GGC Laplace transforms (Bondesson 1992)
- Lagarias's criterion (Lagarias 1999); Weil's explicit formula (Weil 1952); Pólya's integral for $\xi$ (Pólya 1926)
- Van Dantzig pairs (Lukacs 1968) and their link with RH (Konstantopoulos, Patie and Sarkar 2024)
- The Bessel hitting time form of $\xi$ (Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001, after Williams 1990)
- Verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021)

#### New results

The chapter restates the rigidity and shifted clock theorems of Polson (2026), proves the sine squared lemma of Polson (2017) again, and adds one open question on positivity on a single line. The overture is a statement of the programme and of what any proof along it would need.
No new results of this chapter are catalogued.

#### Key terms

Riemann Hypothesis, RH, Riemann xi function, completed zeta function, Thorin condition, Thorin measure, generalized gamma convolution, generalised gamma convolution, GGC, clock, rigidity theorem, Pólya kernel, Polya kernel, heat trace, van Dantzig pair, Cauchy flow, sine squared lemma, Bondesson class, HCM, Lagarias criterion, sinh clock, zero free half plane, overture, two volumes

chapters.title: Analytic representations of the Riemann Xi function
chapters.summary:
This chapter collects the analytic representations of the completed Riemann zeta function $\xi$ and the Riemann Xi function $\Xi$ on which the rest of the book rests. It asks how the zeros of $\xi$, the Pólya kernel and density, the heat trace and the Thorin density at a shifted basepoint are related, and when the reciprocal of $\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u)/\xi(\frac12)$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution (GGC). From the Hadamard product and the partial fraction expansion of $\xi'/\xi$ it defines the clock variable $T$ with Laplace transform $1/G$, and proves a rigidity proposition: the clock is a GGC if and only if the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) holds, with Thorin measure the sum of unit atoms at the squared ordinates. It derives the Pólya kernel $\Phi$ from the theta function, shows that it is even, positive and analytic in a strip, and gives the Pólya density $p=\Phi/\Xi(0)$ with moment generating function $\xi(\frac12+s)/\xi(\frac12)$, so that the clock and the characteristic function of the Pólya variable form a van Dantzig pair exactly when RH holds. The heat trace $W(t)$ of the zeros is given in spectral and arithmetic form and checked numerically. The chapter proves a Poisson structure formula writing the Thorin density at basepoint $\alpha$ as Cauchy kernels centred at the zeros, which is a GGC for every $\alpha$ to the right of all zeros (in particular $\alpha\ge1$, unconditionally), and derives the same density from the primes through the sine squared lemma, compared in floating point with the Pólya route. Statements about $\alpha<1$ are conditional on RH or on a zero free half plane.

#### From the literature

- Hadamard factorisation and the partial fraction expansion of $\xi'/\xi$ (classical; Titchmarsh)
- The Pólya kernel representation of $\Xi$ through the theta function (Pólya 1926; Titchmarsh)
- Generalised gamma convolutions and Thorin measures (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992)
- Van Dantzig pairs and the equivalence of RH with the Pólya law pairing (van Dantzig; Lukacs 1968; Konstantopoulos, Patie and Sarkar 2024)
- The hitting time construction of $2\xi(s)$ as a Mellin transform (Williams 1990; Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001)
- The sine squared lemma and the Thorin density at a shifted basepoint, the rigidity of the clock and the unconditional heat trace identity (Polson 2017; Polson 2026)

#### New results

Results of this chapter, with their status.

- [Rigidity of the clock, a GGC if and only if RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rigidity_clock_ggc_iff_rh) (Volume I, Proposition 2.1.1, page 18; proved): The clock, the reciprocal of the normalised completed zeta function in the variable $u=s^2$, is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution exactly when the Riemann Hypothesis holds, and then its Thorin measure is the sum of unit atoms at the squared ordinates of the zeros. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Shifted clock is a GGC to the right of every zero](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#shifted_clock_ggc_right_of_every_zero) (Volume I, Theorem 2.1.2, page 22; proved): To the right of every zero of the completed zeta function, in particular at every basepoint $\alpha\ge 1$, the shifted clock is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution with an explicit positive Thorin density, and it is one exactly when $\alpha$ is at least the supremum of the real parts of the zeros. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Positivity of the Thorin density on one line, open question](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#one_line_positivity_exclusion_open) (Volume I, Remark 2.1.4, page 23; open): It is not known, without assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, whether nonnegativity of the real part of the logarithmic derivative of the completed zeta function on a single vertical line excludes zeros to the right of that line. New in this book.

chapters.title: Probabilistic representations of Xi
chapters.summary:
This chapter asks whether the clock variable $T$ of the reciprocal Xi function, the positive random variable with Laplace transform $\xi(\tfrac12)/\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt u)$ for the completed Riemann zeta function $\xi$, can be represented by Brownian motion itself and not only through its spectrum, the set $\{\gamma^2\}$ of squared ordinates of the zeros. Under the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) with simple zeros, Kent's theorem makes $T$ the hitting time of a level by a diffusion, but that diffusion is described only through the zeros. The chapter proves that unconditionally $T$ is not the first passage time of Brownian motion with drift $c\ge0$ to an independent random level, by a growth argument along a parabola in the $u$ plane using Stirling's formula. It then treats the inverse first passage problem: by theorems of Ekström and Janson a curved Brownian boundary exists whose crossing time has the law of the clock, and the chapter computes it from the Volterra integral equation of the first kind, in three zones (small times, the bulk, and a right tail with a logarithmic correction), and compares it with the Roberts Shortland tangent boundary and with simulation. Wald's identities constrain the exact boundary. Finally Williams' representation of the Pólya kernel through hitting times of the three dimensional Bessel process (Biane, Pitman and Yor) explains the tilted contour, supplies a Gamma(2) benchmark with a closed Thorin measure, and gives Maślanka's series for $(\sigma-1)\zeta(\sigma)$ as Laguerre moments of Williams' variable; none of this transfers positivity to the Thorin measure of the clock. The boundary computations are floating point.

#### From the literature

- Kent's theorem: under RH with simple zeros the clock is a hitting time of a diffusion (Kent 1978)
- The inverse first passage problem, and existence and uniqueness of the continuous boundary (Cheng, Chadam, Cheng and Sheu 2011; Ekström and Janson 2016), with the Volterra equation of the first kind (Peskir 2002)
- The tangent approximation of a Brownian first passage hazard (Roberts and Shortland 1995)
- De Bruijn's exponential Tauberian theorem (Bingham, Goldie and Teugels 1987)
- Williams' representation of $2\xi(s)$ through Bessel hitting times and the variable $S_2$ (Williams 1990; Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001)
- Maślanka's series for the zeta function (Maślanka 2001), proved rigorously by Báez Duarte (2010)
- Exact sampling of Gamma(2) type sums (Devroye 1986)

#### New results

The status words below refer to the proved statements on $T$; the boundary numbers are computed in floating point.

- [The clock is not a Brownian first passage time to an independent random level](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#clock_not_first_passage_time_to_random_level) (Volume I, Proposition 3.1.1, page 25; proved): The clock variable of the Riemann xi function is not, for any constant drift and any independent random level, the first passage time of Brownian motion with that drift to that level, and the proof uses no hypothesis on the zeros. New in this book.
- [Maślanka coefficients as Laguerre moments of Williams' variable](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#maslanka_coefficients_as_laguerre_moments_of_williams_variable) (Volume I, Proposition 3.1.2, page 29; proved): The coefficients of Maślanka's series for (sigma minus 1) zeta(sigma) are Laguerre moments of Williams' variable, with an explicit generating function and an integral formula, with no zeros and no primes, for (sigma minus 1) zeta(sigma) on the strip from zero to two. New in this book.

chapters.title: Infinite divisibility, GGC, EGGC and the Bondesson hierarchy
chapters.summary:
This chapter sets out the class of generalised gamma convolutions (GGC) in which the Thorin condition for the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) lives, and places it among the infinitely divisible laws. A random variable $H\ge0$ is a GGC when its Laplace transform is $\exp\{-du-\int\log(1+u/z)\,U(dz)\}$ with drift $d\ge0$ and a Thorin measure $U$. The chapter gives three readings of this definition: through the Lévy measure and a completely monotone canonical function $k$, through the Stieltjes transform and Stieltjes inversion, and as a product over the atoms of $U$. For the clock $1/G$, with $G(s^2)=\xi(\frac12+s)/\xi(\frac12)$ built from the completed zeta function, it identifies the Thorin condition with complete monotonicity of the heat trace and writes the Thorin density at resolution $\varepsilon$ as a regularised Stieltjes inversion along a parabola. It then lays out the Bondesson hierarchy: HCM, GGC, self decomposable (SD), the Bondesson class (BO) and infinitely divisible (ID) laws, with Bondesson's theorem that a transform is that of a GGC exactly when it is hyperbolically completely monotone, extended GGCs (EGGC) as Gaussian mixtures over a GGC time, and Urbanik's classes of multiply self decomposable laws. A table records which sign conditions on the heat trace are proved for the clock (with the zeros verified to a stated height) and which are equivalent to RH and open. A second table lists diagnostics for the Thorin condition and what a failure of each proves, and the chapter closes with explicit Thorin measures and the sinh benchmark, where distances to the lattice of atoms are computed in closed form.

#### From the literature

- generalised gamma convolutions and the Thorin measure (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992)
- extended generalised gamma convolutions and the representation of a symmetric EGGC as $Z\sqrt{2H}$ (Thorin 1978; Bondesson 1992)
- Bondesson's theorem that a Laplace transform with value one at the origin belongs to a GGC exactly when it is hyperbolically completely monotone (Bondesson 1992)
- Frullani's integral, Bernstein's theorem and Stieltjes inversion, as they enter the Lévy and Stieltjes readings (James, Roynette and Yor 2008)
- the classes SD and BO and the examples separating them (Polson 2017)
- Urbanik's classes of multiply self decomposable laws
- the hyperbolic laws as Brownian exit times (Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001)
- the Thorin condition as a reformulation of RH, and the diagnostics for it (Polson 2017, 2026)

#### New results

Statements are proved unless a table marks them as computed or equivalent to RH, in which case RH is not assumed; the tables of distances for the sinh clock are closed forms.

- [The variable Z sqrt(2T) of the van Dantzig pair is self decomposable with no hypothesis, with an explicit canonical function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#self_decomposability_of_z_sqrt_2t_and_its_canonical_function_for_the_clock) (Volume I, Result 4.1.2, page 33; proved): With no hypothesis, $Z\sqrt{2T}$ (standard normal $Z$ independent of the clock $T$) is self decomposable, with canonical function $k(r)=\sum_je^{-r\sqrt{a_j}}$ obtained by subordinating the Lévy measure of $T$ to the heat kernel; it is an extended generalised gamma convolution exactly when RH holds. New in this book.

#### Key terms

chapters.title: The reciprocal Xi function
chapters.summary:
Can the reciprocal of the normalised Riemann xi function, which is the Laplace transform of the law of a clock, be shown to be a hitting time, and what would that say about the Riemann Hypothesis (RH)? The chapter studies the clock $T$ with Laplace transform $\xi(\tfrac12)/\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt u)=1/G(u)$, where $G$ is the Hadamard product over the zeros, and asks whether the argument that gives a Krein string hitting time under RH can be run backwards. It computes the density of the law by a residue expansion over the zeros, bounds its tail and decay rate, proves log concavity on a half line, treats truncations of the Hadamard product, Jensen polynomial laws, extreme value representations and the total positivity route to hypergeometric complete monotonicity, and shows by a Thorin rigidity theorem that a factorisation into two generalised gamma convolutions (GGC) forces RH. On the prime side it builds hitting times from truncated Euler products, proves a stable limit of index three halves, and constructs prime built hitting times for the base point laws under the quasi Riemann hypothesis. It adds the inverse first passage boundary of Roberts and Shortland, the Biane, Pitman and Yor variable, and a coefficient ladder in which the Taylor coefficients of xi form a Pólya frequency sequence exactly when RH holds. Further readings of the sine squared lemma (Brownian subordination, Weil's criterion, the prime side near the critical line), numerical fits of Kent approximants and Prony sums to the clock, and exercises close the chapter. Each route ends in an equivalence with RH whose unconditional part stops where classical knowledge stops.

#### From the literature

- The Krein string and Kent's eigenfunction expansion of hitting times, and Krein's class of entire functions (Kent 1980, Krein)
- Generalised gamma convolutions, Thorin measures and Dirichlet means (Bondesson 1992, James, Roynette and Yor 2008)
- The Brownian laws whose Mellin transform is xi (Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001) and the hyperbolic laws (Pitman and Yor 2003)
- Jensen polynomials of the xi function (Griffin, Ono, Rolen and Zagier 2019) and the verification of RH to height $3\cdot10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021)
- Lagarias's criterion $\operatorname{Re}\xi'/\xi>0$ for RH (Lagarias 1999) and the inverse first passage problem (Anulova 1980, Roberts and Shortland 1995)
- The Davenport and Heilbronn function with zeros off the critical line (Davenport and Heilbronn 1936)
- Contour inversion of Laplace transforms (Talbot 1979) and Prony's method for sums of exponentials

#### New results

The results are proved, computed or conditional on RH as marked in each statement.

- [Möbius series for the density of the clock with no hypothesis, with terms g_n a convolution of one fixed function with a first passage kernel](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#mobius_series_for_clock_density_converges_absolutely_for_every_t) (Volume I, Proposition 5.2.1, page 44; proved): With no hypothesis the density $f$ of the clock equals $\sum_n\mu(n)n^{-1/2}g_n(t)$, $g_n=g_1*q_{\log n}$, an absolutely convergent series (faster than any power of $n$) whose terms are bounded through an erfc factor; $g_1$ grows like $2\xi(\frac12)e^{t/4}$, so for large $t$ the series rests on the prime number theorem, and for small $t$ it converges very fast. New in this book.
- [Lower tail of the clock: P(T at most y) is at most exp of minus (log 1/y) squared over 16 y, so the density vanishes to infinite order at the origin](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#clock_lower_tail_chernoff_bound_density_vanishes_to_infinite_order_at_origin) (Volume I, Result 5.2.1, page 45; proved): With no hypothesis $P(T\le y)\le\exp\{-(1+o(1))(\log\frac1y)^2/16y\}$ as $y\downarrow0$, by Chernoff's bound with $\log G(u)\sim\frac{\sqrt u}4\log u$ optimised at $\sqrt u\approx\log(1/y)/4y$; so the density vanishes to infinite order at the origin. New in this book.
- [RH holds if and only if the density of the clock is a Pólya frequency function of infinite order](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rh_equivalent_to_clock_density_being_polya_frequency_function_of_infinite_order) (Volume I, Proposition 5.2.2, page 45; proved): RH is equivalent to the density $f$ of the clock being a Pólya frequency function of infinite order, the one sided form of the two sided criterion: under RH $f$ is the density of $\sum_\gamma e_\gamma/\gamma^2$, and conversely Schoenberg's theorem forces $G$ to have only real zeros. New in this book.
- [The density of the reciprocal xi law is the limit of grouped residue sums, with no hypothesis on the zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#grouped_residue_expansion_of_the_density_of_the_reciprocal_xi_law_with_no_hypothesis) (Volume I, Theorem 5.3.1, page 51; proved): There are radii $R_n\in[n,2n]$ with $f(y)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\sum_{|u_\rho|<R_n}\operatorname{Res}_{u=u_\rho}e^{uy}/G(u)$ for every $y>0$, with an explicit error bound, whatever the zeros. New in this book.
- [Residue expansion: absolute convergence of the density series given a lower bound for the derivative of xi at the zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#absolutely_convergent_residue_series_for_the_density_given_a_lower_bound_for_xi_prime_at_zeros) (Volume I, Theorem 5.3.2, page 52; conditional on the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are simple and $|\xi'(\rho)|\ge e^{-C|\gamma|}$ for some constant $C$ and all zeros): If the zeros of $\zeta$ are simple and $|\xi'(\rho)|\ge e^{-C|\gamma|}$ for all zeros, the residue series for $f$ converges absolutely and locally uniformly, and under RH equals $\sum_{\gamma>0}w_\gamma e^{-\gamma^2y}$. New in this book.
- [Upper tail of the density of the reciprocal xi law: two exponential terms and an explicit remainder](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#tail_of_the_density_of_the_reciprocal_xi_law_has_two_exponential_terms) (Volume I, Proposition 5.3.3, page 53; proved): With no hypothesis, $f(y)=w_1e^{-\gamma_1^2y}+w_2e^{-\gamma_2^2y}+O(e^{-c_3y})$ as $y\to\infty$, with $c_3=\frac12(\gamma_2^2+\gamma_3^2)$ and the same bound for each derivative. New in this book.
- [Kent's eigenfunction expansion is the residue expansion under RH with simple zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#kent_formula_is_the_residue_expansion_under_rh_with_simple_zeros) (Volume I, Proposition 5.4.1, page 54; proved): Under RH with simple zeros the residue series is Kent's expansion with $\lambda_n=\gamma_n^2$ and $f$ is the density of the hitting time of a Krein string with Dirichlet spectrum $\{\gamma_n^2\}$; without these hypotheses the grouped expansion only continues Kent's formula to complex eigenvalues. New in this book.
- [The function xi(1/2+it) is not in Krein's class and the partial fraction series of 1/G diverges under RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#xi_of_one_half_plus_it_is_not_in_krein_class_and_the_partial_fraction_series_diverges) (Volume I, Proposition 5.4.2, page 55; proved): $\xi(\frac12+it)$ is not in Krein's class, with or without RH, and under RH the partial fraction series of $1/G$ over the points $-\gamma_n^2$ does not converge absolutely. New in this book.
- [RH holds if and only if the reciprocal xi law is a weak limit of GGC laws](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rh_equivalent_to_weak_approximation_of_the_reciprocal_xi_law_by_ggc_laws) (Volume I, Proposition 5.5.1, page 56; proved): RH holds if and only if there are GGC laws, for instance hitting times of strings, converging weakly to $\mu$. New in this book.
- [Truncations of the Hadamard product: GGC if and only if the first N zeros lie on the line, and GGC up to the verified height](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#truncated_hadamard_product_laws_are_ggc_exactly_while_the_zeros_used_lie_on_the_line) (Volume I, Proposition 5.7.1, page 57; proved): The law $\mu_N$ with transform $1/G_N$ (first $N$ zeros) is a GGC iff the first $N$ zeros are on the line, hence for every $N$ up to the zeros below $3\cdot10^{12}$; RH holds iff every $\mu_N$ is a GGC; under RH $0\le\log G-\log G_N\le u\tau_1(N)$ on $u\ge0$. - [Log concavity of the reciprocal xi density near the origin, given the saddle point approximation](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#log_concavity_of_the_density_near_the_origin_given_the_saddle_point_approximation) (Volume I, Proposition 5.7.3, page 59; conditional on the saddle point approximation of $\log f(y)$ holds as $y\to0$ together with two derivatives): If the saddle point approximation of $\log f(y)$ holds as $y\to0$ together with two derivatives, then $f$ is strictly log concave on $(0,y_0]$ for some $y_0>0$. chapters.title: Riemann's continuation and the generalised gamma convolution question
chapters.summary:
This chapter asks how close Riemann's own analytic continuation of 1859 comes to proving that the reciprocal $\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u)$ of the completed zeta function, the Laplace transform of the Pólya clock, is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution (GGC), the Thorin condition that is equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis (RH). Riemann's second proof writes $\xi$ as the Mellin transform of a differential operator applied to the theta function, which is a signed mixture of Gamma(2) and exponential densities over the rates $\pi n^2$ and the density of Williams' variable $V=\frac\pi2S_2$. The chapter tests the two facts that suggest a GGC (scale mixtures of Gamma(2) laws, and closure of the class under harmonic means) and finds that neither holds as usually stated: a scale mixture of Gamma(2) laws need not be a GGC, and the natural harmonic mean closure is false (proved). It treats Stefanski's normal scale mixture of the logistic law and the extreme value (Gumbel) law as exponential generalised gamma convolutions, recovers a Thorin density from the heat trace by the sine squared lemma (positive with no hypothesis, but belonging to the positive half of the reciprocal law, not to the clock), and studies the de Bruijn tilt and the tilt by $e^{-|u|}$, whose Fourier transform has finitely many real zeros (proved; a floating point scan on $[0,80]$ finds none, computed). Every step of the continuation is unconditional except the passage from a Mellin transform to the reciprocal of a Laplace transform, a harmonic mean, and making that step a GGC is equivalent to RH. No new route to RH results.

#### From the literature

- Riemann's second proof of the functional equation (Riemann 1859; Edwards 1974)
- Williams' representation of $\xi$ as a mixture of Gamma(2) laws and a Bessel hitting time (Williams 1990; Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001)
- generalised gamma convolutions and their closure properties (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992)
- the logistic law as a normal scale mixture (Andrews and Mallows 1974; Stefanski 1991)
- the de Bruijn tilt and the strip theorem (de Bruijn 1950)

#### New results

- [Riemann's variable V as a GGC with a signed Gamma mixture density](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#riemann_variable_ggc_and_signed_gamma_mixture) (Volume I, Proposition 6.1.1, page 72; proved): The variable V with Mellin transform 2 xi(s) is a sum of independent Gamma(2) variables over pi n squared, hence a GGC, its density is a signed mixture of Gamma(2) and exponential densities, and it is not a scale mixture of Gamma laws. New in this book.
- [A GGC with an entire Laplace transform is constant, so X squared and |X| are not GGC](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#ggc_with_entire_transform_is_constant) (Volume I, Proposition 6.2.1, page 75; proved): A generalised gamma convolution whose Laplace transform extends to an entire function is a constant, so neither the square nor the absolute value of the Pólya variable is a GGC and Bondesson's product theorem does not apply to the arithmetic mean factorisation. New in this book.
- [Positive Thorin density m at the centre with no hypothesis on the zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#half_line_thorin_density_positive_without_hypothesis) (Volume I, Theorem 6.4.1, page 77; proved): From the heat trace K the function m is positive for every theta with no hypothesis on the zeros and is the Thorin density of the half line law with transform P of the square root, and RH holds exactly when its continuation M is a Stieltjes function. New in this book.
- [The de Bruijn tilt as a normal mixture of Esscher tilts, and the failure of the weight e to the minus |u|](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#de_bruijn_tilt_as_normal_mixture_of_esscher_tilts) (Volume I, Proposition 6.5.1, page 78; proved): The Gaussian tilts of the Pólya density are normal mixtures of Esscher tilts or horizontal smoothings of Xi, while the exponential weight gives a Fourier transform with only finitely many real zeros. New in this book.
- [Question: is the Laplace transform E sech(sqrt(u) X) a GGC transform](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_arithmetic_mean_sech_is_ggc) (Volume I, Problem 6.1, page 80; open): The book asks whether the arithmetic mean of sech(sqrt(u) X), the Laplace transform of one half X squared times C, is a GGC transform, which would not bear on RH directly. New in this book.
- [Question: a class of mixing laws whose harmonic mean of GGC transforms is a GGC transform](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_harmonic_mean_class_of_mixing_laws) (Volume I, Problem 6.2, page 81; open): The book asks for a class of mixing laws for which the harmonic mean of GGC transforms is again a GGC transform, not already explained by Pólya's theorems on real zeros. New in this book.
- [Question: a quantitative lower bound for Im M(-x - i eta)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_quantitative_bound_on_continuation_of_m) (Volume I, Problem 6.3, page 81; open): The book asks for a quantitative bound from below on the imaginary part of the continuation M just off the negative axis, in terms of computable data and a zero free region. New in this book.
- [Question: even weights w for which w times Phi has a Fourier transform with only real zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_even_weights_preserving_real_zeros_of_tilted_polya) (Volume I, Problem 6.4, page 81; open): The book asks for which even weights other than mixtures of cosh the tilted Pólya density has a Fourier transform with only real zeros under RH, and whether smoothness at the origin with log w convex suffices. New in this book.

chapters.title: The reciprocal Xi function as an extended generalised gamma convolution
chapters.summary:
This chapter reads $u\mapsto\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+u)$, the reciprocal of the Riemann Xi function on the imaginary axis, as the characteristic function of a normal scale mixture $Y=Z\sqrt{2T}$, with $Z$ standard normal and $T$ the clock, and asks what the $z$ distributions add to that reading. That $Y$ is an extended generalised gamma convolution (EGGC) exactly when the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) holds is taken from an earlier chapter. The chapter adds the $z$ laws $z(a,b)$ as an explicit model of the same structure, with their normal variance mean mixture representation, the symmetric case $z(c,c)$ as the EGGC $\sum_k L_k/(c+k)$, and their Fourier duality with the Meixner laws. It shows that the pair formed by the characteristic function of $z(c,c)$ and the reciprocal of its moment generating function is a van Dantzig pair exactly when $c\ge\frac12$, and that the gamma factor of $\xi$ sits at $c=\frac14$, where it is not. The archimedean factor of $\xi^2$ is written through one $z$ law, and the arithmetic remainder has negative mean, so it is not a law on the half line. The mixing law that makes $Y$ an EGGC is the clock itself, so the property is RH. The de Bruijn Newman heat flow is shown to be a family of laws that are EGGC exactly for $t\ge\Lambda$ (hence unconditionally for $t\ge0.2$), and an unconditional approximating family of EGGC laws is built by truncating the zeros at a height where RH is verified, with an explicit error bound. The sine squared lemma is applied on the $z$ laws. The chapter is a change of coordinates and not a new route to RH, and it poses five open problems.

#### From the literature

- The $z$ distributions as normal variance mean mixtures (Barndorff-Nielsen, Kent and Sørensen 1982); the chapter has not read the text of that paper and derives the mixing law itself
- Van Dantzig pairs (Lukacs 1968); the Meixner laws
- The de Bruijn Newman constant (de Bruijn 1950; Newman 1976), $\Lambda\ge0$ (Rodgers and Tao 2020), $\Lambda\le0.2$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021)
- Generalised gamma convolutions and their extended form (Thorin 1977, 1978; Bondesson 1992)

#### New results

Propositions on the $z$ laws, the archimedean factor and the heat flow are proved, with numerical checks computed in floating point at 30 digits; the approximating family is unconditional, the tilted family is conditional on RH, and the problems are open.
- [The z distribution as a normal variance mean mixture and Laplace sum](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#z_distribution_normal_variance_mean_mixture) (Volume I, Proposition 7.1.1, page 84; proved): The z(a,b) law has an explicit moment generating function and Weierstrass product, is a normal variance mean mixture with a GGC mixing law, and in the symmetric case is the EGGC sum of Laplace variables over c plus k. New in this book.
- [Meixner duality for the symmetric z law](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#meixner_duality_symmetric_z_law) (Volume I, Proposition 7.2.1, page 85; proved): The density of z(c,c) and the density of the Meixner law of order c are, up to constants, the characteristic function of each other, and both are symmetric EGGC laws. New in this book.
- [Van Dantzig pairs for the symmetric z law exist exactly when c is at least one half](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#van_dantzig_pair_for_symmetric_z_law) (Volume I, Proposition 7.2.2, page 86; proved): The characteristic function of z(c,c) is the second member of a van Dantzig pair if and only if c is at least one half, and the first member is then Gamma(c) squared divided by Gamma(c+v)Gamma(c minus v). New in this book.
- [The archimedean factor of xi squared is a z law, and T plus T tilde does not contain H infinity](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#archimedean_factor_of_xi_squared_is_z_law) (Volume I, Proposition 7.3.1, page 87; proved): The archimedean factor of xi squared is the moment generating function of z(1/4,1/4) up to a polar factor, and the remainder D_0 has negative mean, so T plus T tilde has no independent summand H infinity. New in this book.
- [Sine squared image of the z law Lévy density and the Gamma ratio as a Cauchy factor times an EGGC](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#sine_squared_image_of_z_law_levy_density_and_gamma_ratio) (Volume I, Proposition 7.5.1, page 89; proved): The sine squared transform of the completely monotone Lévy density of z(c,c) is the Thorin density of the progression c plus n, and Gamma(a)/Gamma(a+|u|) is an exponential factor times the characteristic function of a symmetric EGGC. New in this book.
- [The heat flow of laws Y_t is a symmetric EGGC exactly for t at least the de Bruijn Newman constant](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_flow_of_laws_eggc_exactly_from_lambda) (Volume I, Theorem 7.6.1, page 90; proved): The normal scale mixtures Y_t built from the de Bruijn Newman flow are symmetric EGGC laws exactly for t at least Lambda, so with no hypothesis for t at least 0.2, and after scaling they converge to the z(1/2,1/2) law as t grows. New in this book.
- [A limit of symmetric EGGC laws equal to Y forces RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#eggc_limit_of_symmetric_eggc_laws_is_equivalent_to_rh) (Volume I, Proposition 7.7.1, page 92; proved): If symmetric EGGC laws converge weakly to the law of Y then RH holds, and conversely under RH the constant sequence works. New in this book.
- [A truncated EGGC law within v to the fourth times epsilon of the law of Y](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#truncated_zero_sum_is_eggc_close_to_y) (Volume I, Proposition 7.7.2, page 92; conditional on All zeros of the zeta function with ordinate at most $T_0=3\times10^{12}$ lie on the critical line, read as quoted from Platt and Trudgian (PT21); this is a finite computation by others that the book does not repeat): Replacing the zeros above a height T' by their second moment as a Gaussian gives a symmetric EGGC law that is within v to the fourth times a tiny epsilon of the law of Y in the log characteristic function. New in this book.
- [Question: is the BNKS mixing law the GGC of the z law proposition](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_mixing_law_of_bnks_z_laws) (Volume I, Problem 7.1, page 93; open): The book asks whether the mixing law in the paper of Barndorff-Nielsen, Kent and Sørensen is the GGC derived here, and whether their asymmetric results have an analogue for the tilted Pólya variables. New in this book.
- [Question: positive sequences c_k for which the sum of L_k over c_k is a van Dantzig second member](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_sequences_giving_van_dantzig_pairs) (Volume I, Problem 7.2, page 94; open): The book asks which positive sequences with square summable reciprocals give a van Dantzig pair, a condition on the regularity of the sequence and not on its density alone. New in this book.
- [Question: an unconditional EGGC family from the z law to Y other than the heat flow](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_family_of_eggc_laws_joining_z_law_to_y) (Volume I, Problem 7.3, page 94; open): The book asks for a one parameter family of unconditional EGGC laws joining the scaled z(1/2,1/2) law to Y other than the heat flow, along which the EGGC property is followed by a computation not reducing to reality of the zeros. New in this book.
- [Question: is the Lévy density K_t(y) of Y_t monotone in t](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_levy_density_of_y_t_monotone_in_t) (Volume I, Problem 7.4, page 94; open): The book asks whether the Lévy density of the heat flow law Y_t is monotone in t for each fixed y. New in this book.
- [Question: the set of lambda for which the ratio of transforms of T plus T tilde and H lambda is a Laplace transform](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_remainder_after_partial_h_infinity) (Volume I, Problem 7.5, page 94; open): The book asks for which lambda between 0 and 1 the ratio of the Laplace transforms of T plus T tilde and of H lambda is again a Laplace transform, whether the set is an interval, and what its right end is. New in this book.

chapters.title: The heat trace and the hierarchy of positivity
chapters.summary:
How much of the Thorin condition on the reciprocal Xi function, which is the Riemann Hypothesis (RH), follows from sign conditions on the heat trace $W(t)=\sum_k e^{-a_kt}$ of the zeros of the Riemann $\xi$ function, and what can finite information not decide? The chapter climbs the Bondesson hierarchy from the bottom: each rung is a sign condition on $W$, the lower rungs are unconditional theorems proved from a finite verification of RH (Platt and Trudgian 2021) and Weil's explicit formula for the primes, and the top rung is RH. It defines the Thorin functional from the gamma factor and the primes with no reference to a zero, and proves that $W$ is positive and decreasing, so that the clock is infinitely divisible and self decomposable. It shows that the derivatives of $W$ alternate in sign up to order $1.16\times10^{25}$ by a window theorem (positivity of the Williamson measures), and that $W$ is completely monotone on $(0,1.70]$, the proof running in ball arithmetic. Positive semidefinite Hankel matrices of the derivatives at one time are equivalent to RH, the numbers of negative eigenvalues of Hankel blocks of Stieltjes moments tend to the number of off line quadruples of zeros, and RH is equivalent to nonnegativity of a Gaussian smoothing of the zeros along a ray. An unconditional compound Poisson defect describes what the off line zeros add to the clock. A perturbation of $\xi$ with four off line zeros passes finite heat trace tests, so finite information cannot decide RH, and a certified zero of a Mellin transform of the Pólya density closes the Bernstein Pick route. The chapter also compares the spacings of the first 1700 zeros with the Gaussian unitary ensemble (GUE) surmise and measures the cell distance to first order. The exercises of the chapter are included.

#### From the literature

- Weil's explicit formula (Weil 1952) and the verification of RH to a finite height (Platt and Trudgian 2021; Hutchinson 1925)
- Self decomposability of laws with $W(t)/t$ as Lévy density (Sato 1999), unimodality (Yamazato 1978), Mase's theorem on indecomposable factors (Mase 1975), Linnik's class $I_0$ (Linnik 1964)
- Williamson's theorem on $k$ monotone functions (Williamson 1956)
- Hermite's count of nonreal roots by Hankel forms (Hermite 1856), with Grommer (1914), Chebotarev (1928) and Baricz and Štampach (2018)
- The explicit Riemann von Mangoldt formula (Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong 2022)
- Solutions of the van Dantzig problem (Konstantopoulos, Patie and Sarkar 2024)
- Pair correlation (Montgomery 1973) and spacings of zeros (Odlyzko 1987), with the Wigner surmise for the GUE
- Zero density estimates (Ingham 1940; Guth and Maynard 2026)

#### New results

Results of this chapter, with their status.

- [Complete asymptotic expansion of the heat trace W(t) at t = 0 with the coefficients d_n and b_k, and the logarithmic divergence of the clock](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#small_time_expansion_of_heat_trace_w_at_the_origin_with_euler_number_coefficients) (Volume I, Result 8.1.1, page 96; proved): With no hypothesis, $W(t)$ has the asymptotic expansion $\frac{\log(1/t)-\gamma_E-4\log2-2\log\pi}{8\sqrt{\pi t}}+\sum d_nt^n+\sum b_kt^{k-1/2}$ as $t\downarrow0$, with $d_0=\frac78$; the two term case is in Polson 2017, and the integral of $W(t)/t$ from $\tau$ diverges so the clock has infinitely many jumps. New in this book.
- [The clock is infinitely divisible and self decomposable, unconditionally](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#clock_infinitely_divisible_and_self_decomposable) (Volume I, Theorem 8.1.1, page 97; proved): Using only the verification of RH below height 1000, the heat trace is positive and decreasing, so the clock is the Laplace transform of an infinitely divisible, self decomposable law with Lévy density W(t)/t, with the numerical inequalities of the proof certified in ball arithmetic. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Hankel positivity of the heat trace at one time is equivalent to RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#hankel_positivity_at_one_time_iff_rh) (Volume I, Theorem 8.1.3, page 99; proved): At any single time t, positive semidefiniteness of the two Hankel matrices of derivatives of the heat trace, equivalently of Weil's quadratic form on the span of r^m exp(-r^2 t/2), is equivalent to RH. First stated in Polson (2017, version 24 of 2026), On Hilbert's 8th problem, arXiv:1708.02653.
- [Truncation error of the residues of the reciprocal clock when the product over zeros is cut after K factors](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#truncation_error_of_residues_of_reciprocal_xi_product_over_first_zeros) (Volume I, Proposition 8.1.2, page 99; proved): For simple zeros, the residue of the truncated product at the pole $-a_k$ differs from the true residue by the factor $\prod_{j>K}(1-a_k/a_j)$, which under RH is close to one exactly for $\gamma_k\le(\gamma_K/\log\gamma_K)^{1/2}$ and not beyond. New in this book.
- [RH is equivalent to boundedness of the heat trace of the zeros on a vertical line](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rh_equivalent_to_boundedness_of_heat_trace_on_vertical_line) (Volume I, Theorem 8.1.4, page 100; proved): The Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if the heat trace $v\mapsto W(\sigma+iv)$ of the zeros is bounded on the real line, for one, equivalently every, $\sigma>0$. New in this book.
- [Positive definite Hankel blocks of the heat trace up to size 3 x 10^7](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_trace_hankel_blocks_positive_definite_to_size_3e7) (Volume I, Theorem 8.1.5, page 101; proved): If every zero of xi below height 20000 N (1 + log N)^(1/2) lies on the critical line, the leading N by N Hankel blocks of the derivatives of the heat trace are positive definite at every time, and the verification of RH to height 3 times 10^12 gives this unconditionally for every N up to 3 times 10^7. First stated in Polson (2017, version 24 of 2026), On Hilbert's 8th problem, arXiv:1708.02653.
- [Derivative signs of the heat trace up to order 10^17](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_trace_derivative_signs_to_order_1e17) (Volume I, Theorem 8.1.6, page 102; proved): Using only the verification of RH below height 10^12, the derivatives of the heat trace alternate in sign, (-1)^k W^(k)(t) > 0, for every t > 0 and every order k up to 10^17. First stated in Polson (2017, version 24 of 2026), On Hilbert's 8th problem, arXiv:1708.02653.
- [Hankel matrices of Stieltjes moments count the zeros off the critical line (eigenvalue form of the Grommer and Chebotarev criterion)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#hankel_inertia_counts_zeros_off_critical_line) (Volume I, Theorem 8.1.7, page 104; proved): In an eigenvalue form of the classical determinant criterion of Grommer (1914) and Chebotarev (1928), the numbers of negative eigenvalues of the Hankel matrices of the Stieltjes moments of the heat trace are nondecreasing in the matrix size and tend to the number of distinct zeros of xi to the right of the critical line in the upper half plane, so RH holds if and only if they are all zero. New in this book.
- [Heat trace completely monotone on (0, 1.29]; every order up to t = 0.019](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_trace_completely_monotone_near_origin) (Volume I, Theorem 8.1.9, page 107; proved): Every derivative of the heat trace of order at least one alternates in sign for t up to 0.019 using no information on the zeros, and with the verification of RH below height 10^12 the heat trace is completely monotone on (0, 1.29], with the numerical inequalities of the proof certified in ball arithmetic. New in this book.
- [Heat trace derivative along a ray is the Gaussian smoothing of the zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_trace_derivative_along_ray_is_gaussian_smoothing_of_zeros) (Volume I, Proposition 8.1.10, page 111; proved): For u at least 2 and k equal to u^2 t, not necessarily an integer, the k th derivative of the heat trace (defined by its sum over the zeros), divided by an explicit factor, equals the Gaussian smoothing of the zeros at resolution 1/(2 sqrt t) up to an explicit relative error on each zero within u/2 of u and an explicit remainder, with no hypothesis on the zeros. New in this book.
- [RH is equivalent to nonnegativity of the Gaussian smoothing of the zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rh_iff_gaussian_smoothing_of_zeros_nonnegative) (Volume I, Proposition 8.1.11, page 112; proved): The Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if the Gaussian smoothing of the zeros of xi, a sum of Gaussian bumps in complexified ordinates, is nonnegative for every real centre and every resolution. New in this book.
- [There is no Gaussian smoothing criterion for RH on a line with real part alpha above one half](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#no_gaussian_criterion_on_vertical_line_alpha_above_one_half_under_rh) (Volume I, Proposition 8.1.12, page 112; conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part $\frac12$): Under RH the Gaussian smoothing of the zeros shifted to the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha$ with $\frac12<\alpha<1$ takes negative values for some $u$ and $t$, so positivity of the Gaussian smoothing cannot be a criterion for RH on that line. New in this book.
- [Derivative signs of the heat trace up to order 1.16 x 10^25](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_trace_derivative_signs_to_order_1e25) (Volume I, Theorem 8.1.13, page 114; proved): From the verification of RH to height 3 times 10^12, every derivative of the heat trace alternates in sign, equivalently the Williamson measures are positive, up to order 1.16 times 10^25, with the numerical inequalities of the proof certified in ball arithmetic. New in this book.
- [Compound Poisson defect of the off line zeros: the clock plus an independent compound Poisson variable is a GGC](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_trace_compound_poisson_defect_of_off_line_zeros) (Volume I, Theorem 8.1.14, page 115; proved): Unconditionally, the heat trace of the zeros of xi is the Laplace transform of a Thorin measure minus an explicit nonnegative remainder carried by the off line zeros, so the clock plus an independent compound Poisson variable of rate below $10^{-12}$ (a bound certified in ball arithmetic from the verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$ and an explicit zero counting bound) is a generalized gamma convolution, and the remainder vanishes exactly when RH holds, that is, when the heat trace is completely monotone. New in this book.
- [Problem: derivative signs of the heat trace to order c H squared with c above 1.70](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_range_of_derivative_signs_of_the_heat_trace_beyond_1_70_h_squared) (Volume I, Problem 8.1, page 115; open): At the verified height $H=3\times10^{12}$ the derivatives of the heat trace have the alternating signs at every time up to order $1.70(H-23)^2$, and the book asks whether the range can be increased to $cH^2$ with an explicit $c>1.70$, suggesting a scale from a heuristic model of four zeros. New in this book.
- [Heat trace of the zeros of xi is completely monotone on (0, 1.70] and has the right sign at every order up to 1.52e25 (certified)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_trace_completely_monotone_up_to_time_1_70_and_order_1_52e25_certified) (Volume I, Theorem 8.1.16, page 117; proved): Unconditionally, the heat trace of the zeros of xi is completely monotone on $(0,1.70]$ and its derivatives have the alternating signs for all times $t>0$ and every order up to $1.70(H-23)^2>1.52\times10^{25}$ with $H=3\times10^{12}$, proved with a ball arithmetic computation (certified) of the numerical inequalities for the orders above $1.16\times10^{25}$. New in this book.

chapters.title: Weak limits, HCM and a Bosch type threshold
chapters.summary:
Can closure of generalised gamma convolutions (GGC) under weak limits, or Bondesson's characterisation of GGC Laplace transforms as hyperbolically completely monotone (HCM) functions, settle the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) without locating zeros? For the reciprocal Xi function (the clock) the chapter recalls (Polson 2017) that the Cauchy flow of Thorin measures converges vaguely to the measure of the zeros on the critical line whether or not RH holds, so weak closure cannot reach RH, and shows that HCM of the clock is RH in other forms (Stieltjes and Pick function conditions, HCM of the de Bruijn Newman deformation at every positive time). An elasticity criterion for HCM functions transfers Bosch's method for powers of the half Cauchy law: the clock composed with $x^p$ is HCM exactly when $|p|$ is at most one minus twice the largest zero angle over $\pi$, with RH the extreme case, and unconditionally for $|p|$ within about $10^{-13}$ of one, by the verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$. Further results: the Thorin density of this family, a natural boundary argument with the Dedekind eta function, a first gap condition for the Mellin variable $W$ (under RH and further hypotheses), open questions, and exercises.

#### From the literature

- Closure of generalised gamma convolutions under convergence in law (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992)
- Bondesson's theorem that a Laplace transform is a GGC transform if and only if it is HCM, and his representation of HCM functions (Bondesson 1992; James, Roynette and Yor 2008)
- Bosch's theorem on powers of the half Cauchy law (Bosch 2015) and the proof of Bondesson's conjecture on stable densities (Bosch and Simon 2016)
- Lagarias's criterion for RH (Lagarias 1999)
- The de Bruijn Newman constant (de Bruijn 1950; Newman 1976), nonnegative (Rodgers and Tao 2020), at most 0.22 (Polymath 2019) and at most 0.2 (Platt and Trudgian 2021)
- Lamperti's stable ratio density (Lamperti 1958)
- The Mellin representation of $\xi$ (Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001)
- Pólya's gap theorem (Pólya 1923, 1929)
- Verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021)

#### New results

- [RH as a weak limit criterion for generalized gamma convolutions](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rh_iff_clock_is_weak_limit_of_ggc_transforms) (Volume I, Corollary 9.1.2, page 127; proved): The Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if the reciprocal Xi function is the pointwise limit of Laplace transforms of generalized gamma convolutions on a set of points with an accumulation point in the positive half line. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [The reciprocal Xi function is HCM if and only if RH holds](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_xi_hcm_iff_rh) (Volume I, Corollary 9.1.3, page 128; proved): The reciprocal Xi function with basepoint alpha at least one is hyperbolically completely monotone (HCM) unconditionally, and with basepoint one half (the clock) it is HCM if and only if the Riemann Hypothesis holds; the equivalence for the clock is noted in versions 21 and 23 of Polson's arXiv paper 1708.02653, and both parts follow from Polson (2026) by Bondesson's theorem. New in this book.
- [Deformed reciprocal Xi function is HCM exactly for t at least Lambda](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#deformed_reciprocal_xi_hcm_iff_time_at_least_lambda) (Volume I, Corollary 9.2.5, page 134; proved): The reciprocal Xi function deformed by the de Bruijn Newman heat flow to time t is HCM exactly when t is at least the de Bruijn Newman constant, so RH is equivalent to HCM for every positive t. New in this book.
- [Question: for which beta is the density of W^beta HCM](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_hcm_powers_of_mellin_variable_w) (Volume I, Question 9.2.7, page 136; open): The book asks for which powers beta the density of W to the power beta is HCM, where W is the positive variable with Mellin transform Xi(0)/Xi(z). New in this book.
- [Question: does HCM of W^beta for a single beta imply RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_single_power_hcm_implies_rh) (Volume I, Question 9.2.8, page 136; open): The book asks whether HCM of the density of W to the power beta for one single beta already implies the Riemann Hypothesis. New in this book.
- [Elasticity criterion for HCM functions (Bondesson's representation restated as a Pick condition)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#elasticity_criterion_for_hcm_functions) (Volume I, Theorem 9.3.2, page 137; proved): A positive function on the half line is HCM exactly when it extends to a zero free analytic function off the negative axis whose elasticity is a Pick function; this restates Bondesson's representation of HCM functions, with a direct proof of sufficiency. New in this book.
- [Bosch type theorem for the reciprocal Xi function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_xi_power_hcm_threshold) (Volume I, Theorem 9.3.5, page 139; proved): The reciprocal Xi function composed with the power x to the p is HCM exactly when the absolute value of p is at most one minus twice the largest zero angle over pi, so RH is the extreme case p equal to one. New in this book.
- [Equivalent forms of RH: HCM of all powers, Pick elasticity](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rh_iff_hcm_of_all_powers_below_one_and_pick_elasticity) (Volume I, Corollary 9.3.6, page 140; proved): The Riemann Hypothesis is equivalent to HCM of the reciprocal Xi function composed with x to the p for every p of absolute value below one, to the elasticity of the reciprocal Xi function being a Pick function, and to an angular sign condition on xi prime over xi. New in this book.
- [Unconditional HCM range for the reciprocal Xi function composed with a power](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_xi_power_hcm_unconditional_range) (Volume I, Corollary 9.3.7, page 140; proved): From the verification of RH to height 3 times 10^12, the reciprocal Xi function composed with x to the p is HCM for all p of absolute value at most one minus 1/(3 pi times 10^12), which exceeds one minus 1.1 times 10^-13. New in this book.
- [Stieltjes sign of minus the logarithmic derivative of the clock outside a thin parabolic region](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#stieltjes_sign_of_clock_outside_parabolic_region) (Volume I, Theorem 9.3.9, page 141; proved): From the verification of RH to height 3 times 10^12, minus the logarithmic derivative of the reciprocal Xi function has the sign of a Stieltjes function at every point of the upper half plane outside an explicit thin parabolic region. New in this book.
- [Question: HCM exponent of the deformed reciprocal Xi function for negative time](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_hcm_exponent_deficit_negative_heat_time) (Volume I, Question 9.3.11, page 143; open): The book asks how fast one minus the HCM exponent of the deformed reciprocal Xi function tends to zero as the heat time rises to zero from below, assuming RH. New in this book.
- [Thorin measure of the reciprocal Xi function composed with a power](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_density_of_reciprocal_xi_power) (Volume I, Theorem 9.3.12, page 143; proved): For p up to the threshold, the reciprocal Xi function composed with s to the p is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution without drift, whose Thorin measure for p below the threshold has a density given by xi prime over xi along a ray, with unit atoms added at the threshold. New in this book.
- [Thorin measure of X_p under RH: scaled Lamperti laws (Bosch's variable)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_measure_of_reciprocal_xi_power_under_rh_lamperti_kernel) (Volume I, Corollary 9.3.13, page 144; conditional on the Riemann Hypothesis): Under RH the Thorin measure of X_p is p times the sum over the zeros of the law of gamma^(2/p) L_p, where L_p is a ratio of independent positive p stable variables whose power with exponent p is Bosch's variable. New in this book.
- [RH is equivalent to the existence of the GGC variable X_p for every p in (0, 1)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rh_iff_reciprocal_xi_power_is_ggc_transform_for_all_p) (Volume I, Corollary 9.3.14, page 144; proved): The Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if the reciprocal Xi function composed with s to the p is a generalized gamma convolution transform for every p between zero and one, and unconditionally it is one for p up to one minus 1/(3 pi times 10^12), in particular for p up to one minus 1.1 times 10^-13, with an explicit Thorin density. New in this book.
- [Question: construct X_{1/2} from Brownian motion without the zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_construct_x_half_without_zeros) (Volume I, Question 9.3.15, page 144; open): The book asks for a construction of the variable X_{1/2}, with Laplace transform xi(1/2)/xi(1/2+s^(1/4)), from Brownian motion, Bessel processes or the Biane Pitman Yor variables without reference to the zeros, noting that a construction surviving p to one would prove RH. New in this book.
- [Question: prove positivity of u_p for all p without locating zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_thorin_density_positive_for_all_powers) (Volume I, Question 9.3.16, page 145; open): The book asks for a direct proof, without locating zeros, that the explicit density u_p built from xi prime over xi along a ray is nonnegative for every p between zero and one, a statement equivalent to RH. New in this book.
- [Thorin density u_p is positive beyond a finite point, from the primes](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_density_of_power_positive_beyond_strip_from_primes) (Volume I, Proposition 9.3.18, page 145; proved): For each p in (0,1) the Thorin density u_p of the reciprocal Xi function composed with s to the p is positive beyond a finite point, by a lower bound that involves the gamma factor and the prime sum but no zero of zeta. New in this book.
- [Cauchy analogue of the clock: eta cubed density with natural boundary, not HCM](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#cauchy_clock_density_eta_cubed_natural_boundary) (Volume I, Theorem 9.3.20, page 147; proved): The Cauchy analogue of the clock variable has the density (4/pi) times the cube of the Dedekind eta function at 4it/pi, whose natural boundary is the imaginary axis, so its Laplace transform is HCM but its density is not. New in this book.
- [Question: natural boundary of the clock density](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_natural_boundary_of_clock_density) (Volume I, Question 9.3.21, page 147; open): The book asks whether, under RH and simple zeros, the density of the clock variable has the imaginary axis as a natural boundary, which would show that the clock variable is not HCM. New in this book.
- [Natural boundary of the clock density under RH, simple zeros and gap hypotheses](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#clock_density_natural_boundary_under_gap_hypotheses) (Volume I, Theorem 9.3.22, page 147; conditional on the Riemann Hypothesis; all zeros of the zeta function are simple; hypothesis (G), $\inf_n(\gamma_{n+1}^2-\gamma_n^2)>0$; hypothesis (D), $\log(1/|\zeta'(\tfrac12+i\gamma_n)|)=o(\gamma_n^2)$): Under RH, simple zeros and two hypotheses on the gaps between zeros and on the size of the derivative of zeta at the zeros, the imaginary axis is a natural boundary of the density of the clock variable, which is therefore not HCM. New in this book.
- [Question: for which p are X_p and its Cauchy analogue HCM](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_which_powers_of_clock_variable_are_hcm) (Volume I, Question 9.3.24, page 149; open): The book asks for the set of exponents p for which the variable X_p, with Laplace transform the reciprocal Xi function composed with s to the p, has an HCM density, and the same set for the Cauchy family. New in this book.
- [Lower bound for the density of log W: existence of W (second proof)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#mellin_variable_w_density_lower_bound_unconditional) (Volume I, Theorem 9.3.25, page 149; proved): From the verification of RH to height 3 times 10^12, the density of log W is at least 0.9998 times the density built from the real zeros alone, so the positive variable W with Mellin transform Xi(0)/Xi(z) exists unconditionally. New in this book.
- [HCM criterion for powers of the Mellin variable W](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#elasticity_criterion_for_powers_of_mellin_variable_w) (Volume I, Proposition 9.3.26, page 151; proved): The density of W to the power beta is HCM exactly when the density g of log W has no zeros in a strip of half width pi over absolute beta and minus g prime over g has nonnegative imaginary part in the upper half of that strip. New in this book.
- [First gap theorem: HCM of W^beta forces |beta| at least gamma_2 minus gamma_1](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#first_gap_necessary_condition_for_hcm_of_w_power) (Volume I, Theorem 9.3.27, page 151; conditional on the Riemann Hypothesis; all zeros of the zeta function are simple; $\log(1/|\zeta'(\rho_n)|)=O(\gamma_n)$, where $\rho_n=\tfrac12+i\gamma_n$ are the zeros of zeta in the upper half plane): Under RH, simple zeros and a growth bound on one over the derivative of zeta at the zeros, the density of W to the power beta can be HCM only if the absolute value of beta is at least the first gap gamma_2 minus gamma_1, which is 6.8873. New in this book.
- [Question: first gap conjecture for HCM powers of W](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_first_gap_conjecture) (Volume I, Question 9.3.28, page 152; open): The book asks whether the density of W to the power beta is HCM exactly when the absolute value of beta is at least the first gap gamma_2 minus gamma_1 between zeros of zeta. New in this book.
- [Refined first gap conjecture for sums of Laplace variables](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_first_gap_conjecture_refined) (Volume I, Question 9.3.29, page 153; open): The book asks whether, for e to the power of a sum of independent Laplace variables over frequencies lambda_n, the HCM threshold of the powers is exactly the first gap lambda_2 minus lambda_1 when the first gap is the largest or the characteristic function decays faster than any exponential. New in this book.

#### Key terms

chapters.title: Thorin type forms of the reciprocal zeta function
chapters.summary:
This chapter asks whether the zeros, the primes and the gamma factor of the Riemann zeta function assemble into a Thorin measure, that is, whether the reciprocal zeta function, in the clock variable, is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) or at least infinitely divisible. Up to the factor of the pole, $1/\zeta(\frac12+\sqrt s)$ is the reciprocal Xi function times the gamma factor, and unlike $\xi$ it has a Dirichlet series and an Euler product. From these the chapter computes the Thorin type measures of an Euler factor and, under the Riemann Hypothesis (RH), of the normalised reciprocal zeta function, a signed measure $dM$ with $M-1$ the argument function $S(\sqrt t)$, and from the Weierstrass product that of the gamma factor. The Lai and Vere-Jones identity gives Vere-Jones forms by hyperbolic secants and sawtooth measures, and an explicit canonical function (heat trace) that yields a criterion for RH. The sine squared lemma carries the Lévy form to the Thorin form, and the Meixner law with its Meixner Pollaczek polynomials shows that the reciprocal gamma factor is a GGC after a stable tilt, with a local Riemann Hypothesis for Mellin transforms of even Hermite functions. Multiplying the normalised reciprocal zeta function by the reciprocal gamma factor gives the floor of the reciprocal Xi function, which is infinitely divisible and is a GGC exactly when RH holds. Complete monotonicity of its canonical function is checked to finite order. Unconditional statements are proved, those using RH are conditional on RH, and tables of orders are computed.

#### From the literature

- the Thorin representation of generalised gamma convolutions (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992)
- the hyperbolic secant law as a Brownian exit time and a GGC, and its gamma powers (Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001)
- the Meixner hypergeometric law and the completeness problem for dilates of the hyperbolic secant (Lai and Vere-Jones 1979)
- the Riemann von Mangoldt formula (see Titchmarsh 1986) and the explicit formula (Weil 1952), in heat trace form (Polson 2026)
- the local Riemann Hypothesis for Mellin transforms of even Hermite functions (Bump, Choi, Kurlberg and Vaaler 2000), rederived here with no priority claimed, and Meixner Pollaczek expansions of $\Xi$ (Kuznetsov 2008; Romik 2021)
- Williamson's theorem on $n$ monotone functions (Williamson 1956)
- the verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021) and a bound for the zero count (Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong 2022)
- infinite divisibility and self decomposability of the reciprocal Xi function (Polson 2026)
- the sine squared lemmas (Polson 2017)

#### New results

The results first appeared in Part IX of Polson (2026), several corrected or sharpened here.

- [Thorin type density of an Euler factor](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#euler_factor_thorin_type_density) (Volume I, Proposition 10.1.2, page 160; proved): The Euler factor $1-qe^{-\lambda\sqrt s}$ is zero free on the cut plane and has an explicit Thorin type density, a cosine series of both signs. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Lai and Vere-Jones identity (the exponential as a Möbius sum of hyperbolic secants)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#lai_vere_jones_identity) (Volume I, Proposition 10.1.3, page 161; proved): The exponential $e^{-x}$ equals a Möbius weighted sum of the dilates $\operatorname{sech}(mx)$ of the hyperbolic secant, which expands the Dirichlet series of the reciprocal zeta function in hyperbolic secants; the book names it after Lai and Vere-Jones, who posed the completeness of these dilates as an open problem. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Vere-Jones representation of the reciprocal zeta function by hyperbolic secants](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#vere_jones_representation_reciprocal_zeta) (Volume I, Theorem 10.1.5, page 161; proved): Where the Dirichlet series converges absolutely, $1/\zeta(\frac12+\sqrt s)$ equals $1$ plus an explicit Möbius weighted series of hyperbolic secants $\operatorname{sech}(\sqrt s\log N)$, each the Laplace transform of a Brownian exit time and a GGC with atomic Thorin measure. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Logarithmic twin of the Lai and Vere-Jones identity (the exponential as a sum of logarithms with Dirichlet eta weights)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#exponential_as_eta_weighted_sum_of_log_blocks) (Volume I, Proposition 10.1.6, page 162; proved): The exponential $e^{-x}$ equals $\sum_{m\ge1}d_m\log(1+e^{-mx})$ with weights $d_m$ bounded by $1$ whose Dirichlet series is $1/\eta(1+v)$ for Dirichlet's eta function $\eta$, the logarithmic twin of the Lai and Vere-Jones identity. Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Sawtooth Thorin measure of a Vere-Jones block](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#sawtooth_thorin_measure_of_vere_jones_block) (Volume I, Lemma 10.1.7, page 162; proved): The function $2/(1+e^{-\lambda\sqrt s})$ has the signed Thorin type measure formed by unit atoms at the squares of the odd multiples of $\pi/\lambda$ minus the density $\lambda/(4\pi\sqrt t)$, a sawtooth measure. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Vere-Jones representation of log zeta by sawtooth blocks](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#vere_jones_representation_log_zeta) (Volume I, Theorem 10.1.8, page 162; proved): Where the Dirichlet series converges absolutely, $\log\zeta(\frac12+\sqrt s)$ is an explicit absolutely convergent series of the blocks $\log(1+N^{-\sqrt s})$ with weights from Dirichlet's eta function, and its derivative is a sum of Stieltjes transforms with poles on sawtooth lattices. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Thorin type measure of the normalised reciprocal zeta function under RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_measure_normalised_reciprocal_zeta_under_rh) (Volume I, Theorem 10.1.10, page 163; conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part $\frac12$): Under RH the normalised reciprocal zeta function has the signed Thorin type measure $dM$, unit atoms at the squared ordinates of the zeros plus the density of the gamma factor, with $M-1$ the argument function $S(\sqrt t)$, so it is not a GGC even under RH. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Canonical function of the normalised reciprocal zeta function, prime and zero forms](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#canonical_function_normalised_reciprocal_zeta) (Volume I, Theorem 10.1.11, page 165; proved): With no hypothesis, $-\varphi'/\varphi$ is the Laplace transform of the canonical function $w(x)=e^{x/4}-P(x)$, explicit in the primes, which by the arithmetic form of the heat trace (Weil's explicit formula; Polson 2026, Theorem 4.4) equals the heat trace over the zeros minus the heat trace of their smooth count. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Theta function series for the canonical function w](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#theta_series_for_canonical_function_reciprocal_zeta) (Volume I, Proposition 10.1.13, page 166; proved): The canonical function $w$ equals $e^{x/4}$ plus an absolutely convergent series of Jacobi theta functions, one for each prime power, with the weights $B_N$ of the Vere-Jones representation. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Sawtooth expansion of the argument function after Gaussian averaging, under RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#sawtooth_expansion_argument_function_gaussian_average) (Volume I, Corollary 10.1.14, page 167; conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part $\frac12$): Under RH the Gaussian average of the argument function $S$ equals $(e^{x/4}-1)/x$ plus the $B_N$ weighted Gaussian averages of sawtooth functions, which makes the sawtooth expansion of $S$ rigorous after Gaussian averaging. - [Criterion for RH from the canonical function w](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rh_criterion_from_canonical_function) (Volume I, Theorem 10.1.15, page 167; proved): RH is equivalent to the function $w$, explicit in the primes, being the Laplace transform of a real signed measure $m$ on $[0,\infty)$ with $\int|m|(dt)/(1+t)<\infty$, and the measure is then $dM$. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
