First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Closed form heat trace over the zeros and formal Thorin measure of the reciprocal Xi function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_trace_closed_form_and_formal_thorin_measure_of_reciprocal_xi) (Volume I, Theorem 10.2.3, page 170; proved): The heat trace $W(x)$ over the zeros has an explicit absolutely convergent closed form, the polar term, a theta series over prime powers and complementary error functions over the poles of the gamma factor, equivalently the Laplace transform of a formal Thorin measure of the reciprocal Xi function. Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Sine squared lemma (Polson 2017, Lemma 1)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#sine_squared_lemma_polson_2017) (Volume I, Lemma 10.2.4, page 172; proved): A Lévy representation of $\log f$ gives, through the kernel $2\sin^2$, a Lévy representation in the variable $s^2/2$ of the tilted reciprocal $f(\alpha)/f(\alpha+s)$, by a linear positivity preserving map of the Lévy measure. First stated in Polson (2017, version 24 of 2026), On Hilbert's 8th problem, arXiv:1708.02653.
- [Sine squared lemma in the variable s = u squared (Polson 2017, Lemma 1)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#sine_squared_lemma_clock_variable) (Volume I, Lemma 10.2.5, page 172; proved): In the variable $s=u^2$ a Lévy measure $\tilde\mu$ of $\log f$ gives the Thorin density $\frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt t}\int2\sin^2(\frac{x\sqrt t}2)\tilde\mu(dx)$ of the tilted reciprocal $f(0)/f(\sqrt s)$, so a positive $\tilde\mu$ gives a GGC; this restates Lemma 1 of Polson (2017) with a proof by subordination. First stated in Polson (2017, version 24 of 2026), On Hilbert's 8th problem, arXiv:1708.02653.
- [Reciprocal zeta to the right of the line Re z = 1 is a GGC after a stable tilt](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_zeta_right_of_line_one_tilted_ggc) (Volume I, Proposition 10.2.6, page 173; proved): For $\beta>1$ the function $\zeta(\beta)/\zeta(\beta+\sqrt s)$ times the tilt $e^{\sqrt s\,\zeta'(\beta)/\zeta(\beta)}$ is a GGC transform with the explicit nonnegative Thorin density $\frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt t}\sum\Lambda(n)n^{-\beta}\,2\sin^2(\frac{\sqrt t\log n}2)$. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Positive Thorin density of a shifted Vere-Jones block](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#shifted_vere_jones_block_positive_thorin_density) (Volume I, Proposition 10.2.7, page 174; proved): After a shift of the basepoint by $\alpha>0$ and an explicit stable tilt, the reciprocal of the block $1+e^{-\lambda\sqrt s}$ has a positive Poisson kernel Thorin density, which tends to the lattice of atoms of the sawtooth measure as $\alpha\downarrow0$. Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Divergence of the cosine Lévy series of the Vere-Jones blocks](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#cosine_levy_series_of_vere_jones_blocks_diverges) (Volume I, Proposition 10.2.9, page 175; proved): The cosine Lévy forms of the sawtooth blocks cannot be summed with the weights $B_N$, because for every $x>0$ the series $\sum_NB_NK_{U_{\log N}}(x)$ diverges. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [The Meixner density of the gamma factor is not a Pólya frequency function of infinite order](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#meixner_density_not_polya_frequency_function) (Volume I, Proposition 10.2.10, page 176; proved): The Meixner density $|\Gamma(\frac14+\frac{i\tau}2)|^2/(2^{3/2}\pi^{3/2})$ of the gamma factor, with characteristic function $\operatorname{sech}(v)^{1/2}$, is not a Pólya frequency function of infinite order, because by Schoenberg's theorem the reciprocal $\cosh(v)^{1/2}$ of its characteristic function would have to be entire. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.

Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [The reciprocal gamma factor is a GGC after a stable tilt](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#tilted_reciprocal_gamma_factor_is_ggc) (Volume I, Theorem 10.2.12, page 177; proved): After the stable tilt $e^{-c\sqrt s}$ with $c=\zeta'(\frac12)/\zeta(\frac12)$, the reciprocal of the gamma factor is a GGC transform with the explicit nonnegative Thorin density $(\theta'(\sqrt t)-\theta'(0))/(2\pi\sqrt t)$. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.

Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Splitting of the canonical function of the floor of the reciprocal Xi function, and GGC if and only if RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#floor_reciprocal_xi_infinitely_divisible_ggc_iff_rh) (Volume I, Theorem 10.2.15, page 181; proved): With no hypothesis the canonical function $W(x)+c/(2\sqrt{\pi x})$ of the floor $e^{-c\sqrt s}\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)$ is the sum of the function $w$, explicit in the primes and proved positive with certified interval enclosures and the verification of RH to height $50$, and a completely monotone archimedean part, which reproves that the floor is infinitely divisible (this also follows from Theorem A of Polson 2026); the floor is a GGC if and only if RH holds. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Derivative signs of the canonical function of the floor to order ten billion, a separate proof (Williamson measures)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#floor_canonical_function_derivative_signs_to_order_1e10) (Volume I, Theorem 10.2.17, page 183; proved): The canonical function $k$ of the floor satisfies $(-1)^nk^{(n)}(y)>0$ for all $y>0$ and every $n\le10^{10}$, proved by a two range argument from the verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$, a bound for the zero count and one certified interval enclosure, which gives positive Williamson measures; the signs to order $10^{17}$ follow from Polson (2017, version 24 of 2026), and to order $1.16\times10^{25}$ from the book's heat trace estimates. chapters.title: Infinite divisibility, necklaces and solved models
chapters.summary:
This chapter asks where the normalised reciprocal zeta function $\varphi(s)=\zeta(\tfrac12)/((1-4s)\zeta(\tfrac12+\sqrt s))$ sits among infinitely divisible laws, and how far truncations of the Biane, Pitman and Yor lattice go towards the Riemann Hypothesis (RH). Unconditionally, and certified in interval arithmetic, it proves that the canonical function $w$ is positive, so that $\varphi$ is the Laplace transform of an infinitely divisible law with Lévy density $w(x)/x$, which is not self decomposable, not in the Bondesson class and not a generalised gamma convolution (GGC). It reads the Vere-Jones weights as necklace polynomials, extends the canonical function across the critical strip, and states the Laguerre Pólya class and the Lee and Yang property in Thorin measure terms for the solved models. For simple zeros $\rho$, zeros of the truncated lattice transforms converge to $\rho/2$ at rate $1/n$: the one sided Conjecture T is false, while the symmetrised Conjecture S is proved above explicit heights for $n\le24$ and $n=32,36$ and only checked numerically below them. It also proves Weil positivity on the Bernstein cone and reads the de Bruijn Newman flow as a path of GGCs. A final section writes the reciprocal Xi function as a harmonic mean and scale mixture of reciprocal hyperbolic cosine transforms and proves that the clock is not a gamma scale mixture. A note of Nicholas Polson shows that the approximate functional equation truncation with N equal to 2 has all but finitely many zeros on the critical line while the truncation with N equal to 3 has zeros off the line at arbitrarily large heights.

#### From the literature

- Thorin measures and generalised gamma convolutions (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992), closed under independent products (Bondesson 2015); unimodality of self decomposable laws (Yamazato 1978)
- Selberg's central limit theorem for $S(t)$ (Selberg 1946); verification of RH to height 50 (Backlund 1918) and $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021); simplicity of the first $1.5\times10^9$ zeros (van de Lune, te Riele and Winter 1986); an explicit Riemann von Mangoldt bound (Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong 2022)
- Necklace polynomials (Metropolis and Rota 1983)
- Pólya's theory of real zeros (Pólya 1926), Cardon's theorems (Cardon 2004, 2005), zeros of $\xi(s+a)+\xi(s-a)$ for $a\ge\frac12$ (Lagarias 2005), the Lee and Yang theorem (Lee and Yang 1952), Newman's characterisation of Lee and Yang spins (Newman 1974)
- The Biane, Pitman and Yor identity (Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001; Williams 1990)
- Weil's criterion (Weil 1952; Bombieri 2000)
- The de Bruijn Newman constant (de Bruijn 1950; Newman 1976; Rodgers and Tao 2020; Polymath 2019; Platt and Trudgian 2021)

#### New results

The positivity of the canonical function is proved with ball arithmetic; the truncation statements are proved above the stated heights and computed below them.

- [The normalised reciprocal zeta function is infinitely divisible](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_zeta_infinitely_divisible_unconditional) (Volume I, Theorem 11.1.1, page 185; proved): Without any hypothesis on the zeros, the normalised reciprocal zeta function is the Laplace transform of an infinitely divisible law with Lévy density $w(x)/x$, because its canonical function $w$ is positive; the proof is certified with the verification of the Riemann Hypothesis to height 50 and interval enclosures. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Negative bias of the Gaussian smoothed prime number theorem error](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#gaussian_smoothed_prime_number_theorem_error_negative_bias) (Volume I, Proposition 11.1.2, page 187; proved): The error of the prime number theorem, smoothed with a Gaussian weight in $\log y$, has a definite negative bias, about $-0.343\,(\pi x)^{-1/2}$ at large $x$, whereas a pointwise bound on the error of size $\sqrt y\log^2y$, even the one that the Riemann Hypothesis implies, controls it only up to order $x$. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [The reciprocal zeta function in the Bondesson hierarchy: not self decomposable, not a GGC](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_zeta_bondesson_hierarchy_classification) (Volume I, Theorem 11.1.3, page 188; proved): The normalised reciprocal zeta function is infinitely divisible but not self decomposable, not in the Bondesson class and not a mixture of exponentials, hence not a generalised gamma convolution, with no hypothesis on the zeros. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Density of the reciprocal zeta law at the origin](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_zeta_density_rises_from_origin) (Volume I, Theorem 11.1.4, page 190; proved): The density of the law with Laplace transform equal to the normalised reciprocal zeta function starts at $-\zeta(\frac12)/4$ with the positive slope $-\zeta(\frac12)/16$, so it is not monotone, not log convex and not completely monotone. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [The reciprocal zeta law is not a sum, product or limit of GGC variables](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_zeta_law_not_built_from_ggc_operations) (Volume I, Corollary 11.1.6, page 191; proved): The random variable with Laplace transform equal to the normalised reciprocal zeta function is not a sum, a product or a weak limit of independent generalised gamma convolution variables. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [The GGC class is not closed under the harmonic mean](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#ggc_class_not_closed_under_harmonic_mean) (Volume I, Proposition 11.1.7, page 191; proved): The harmonic mean of two independent standard exponential variables has an explicit density and is not a generalised gamma convolution, so the class of generalised gamma convolutions is not closed under harmonic means of independent variables. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Vere-Jones weights of the zeta function are necklace polynomials](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#vere_jones_weights_are_necklace_polynomials) (Volume I, Theorem 11.1.8, page 192; proved): A 2 adic variant of the cyclotomic identity of Metropolis and Rota factors $1/(1-qy)$ into factors $1+y^n$ with necklace polynomial exponents, which makes the Vere-Jones weights of the zeta function at prime powers necklace polynomials at $p^{-1/2}$; the authors have not found the identity stated in this form, but it may well be known in the combinatorics of necklaces. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Sign rule for the necklace weights of the zeta function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#necklace_weights_sign_rule) (Volume I, Proposition 11.1.9, page 193; proved): At $q=p^{-1/2}$ the necklace exponent $b_{2^a}$ is positive, and for odd $n>1$ the exponent $b_n$ is nonzero with sign $(-1)^{\omega(n)}$, where $\omega(n)$ counts the distinct prime factors of $n$. Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Lévy representation of the reciprocal zeta function across the critical strip](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#levy_representation_reciprocal_zeta_across_critical_strip) (Volume I, Theorem 11.1.12, page 195; proved): For each $\sigma$ in $(0,1)$ the shifted reciprocal zeta function has an explicit canonical function $w_\sigma$ in three equivalent forms, with the asymptotic $\zeta'(\sigma)/\zeta(\sigma)$ over $2\sqrt{\pi x}$, and it is infinitely divisible with Lévy density $w_\sigma(x)/x$ whenever $w_\sigma$ is nonnegative, a positivity that the chapter proves only for $\sigma=\frac12$. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [The shifted reciprocal zeta function is never a GGC on a line of the strip](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#shifted_reciprocal_zeta_never_ggc_on_the_strip) (Volume I, Proposition 11.1.13, page 197; proved): On every line $\sigma$ in $(0,1)$ the shifted reciprocal zeta function is not a generalised gamma convolution and, if infinitely divisible, not self decomposable, because the factor that removes the pole makes its canonical function increase at the origin. Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Laguerre Pólya class as integer atom GGCs](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#laguerre_polya_class_integer_atom_ggc) (Volume I, Proposition 11.1.15, page 200; proved): A real even entire function $G$ of order below 2 lies in the Laguerre Pólya class exactly when $G(0)/G(i\sqrt s)$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution whose Thorin measure has integer masses at the squared zeros. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Lee and Yang single spin laws as integer atom GGCs](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#lee_yang_property_integer_atom_ggc) (Volume I, Proposition 11.1.16, page 201; proved): A symmetric law with Gaussian moments of all orders has the Lee and Yang property exactly when the reciprocal of its moment generating function at $\sqrt s$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution with integer atoms at the squared zeros of its characteristic function. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Random harmonic series and the strip of the Pólya kernel](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#random_harmonic_series_matches_polya_kernel_strip) (Volume I, Proposition 11.1.17, page 202; proved): The random harmonic series $H_\kappa$ has a double exponential tail whose leading constant equals that of the Pólya kernel exactly at $\kappa^*=6.61845\ldots$, and its density is analytic in the strip $|\operatorname{Im}t|<\pi/4$, the strip of analyticity of the Pólya kernel. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [The reciprocal Xi transform is a harmonic mean of Brownian exit time transforms](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_xi_transform_harmonic_mean_of_brownian_exit_time_transforms) (Volume I, Proposition 11.1.23, page 207; proved): The Laplace transform of the clock, the reciprocal Xi function, is the harmonic mean over the Pólya density of the Laplace transforms $1/\cosh(x\sqrt s)$ of scaled Brownian exit times, so by Jensen's inequality it is at most the Laplace transform of the corresponding scale mixture. New in this book.
- [A harmonic mean of two GGC transforms that is not a Laplace transform of a positive measure](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#harmonic_mean_of_two_ggc_transforms_not_a_laplace_transform) (Volume I, Example 11.1.24, page 207; counterexample, proved): The harmonic mean of the Laplace transforms $(1+s)^{-2}$ and $(1+2s)^{-2}$ of two generalized gamma convolutions (GGC) is $1/(1+3s+\frac52s^2)$, whose inverse transform $2e^{-0.6t}\sin(0.2t)$ is negative on $(5\pi,10\pi)$, so a harmonic mean of GGC transforms need not be the Laplace transform of a positive measure. New in this book.
- [A two point scale mixture of Gamma(2) that is infinitely divisible and not a GGC](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#gamma_two_scale_mixture_infinitely_divisible_but_not_ggc) (Volume I, Example 11.1.25, page 207; counterexample, proved): A scale mixture of a Gamma(2) variable by an independent variable equal to $1$ or to a positive $\lambda\ne1$ with probability one half each is infinitely divisible but not a generalized gamma convolution, because its Laplace transform has nonreal zeros. New in this book.
- [The clock is not a Gamma scale mixture, for any shape](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#clock_is_not_a_gamma_scale_mixture) (Volume I, Theorem 11.1.26, page 208; proved): The clock is not a scale mixture of Gamma($a$) laws for any shape $a>0$, because the Laplace transform of such a mixture is at least a constant times $s^{-a}$ for large $s$, while that of the clock is at most a constant times $e^{-x\sqrt s}$ for every $x>0$. New in this book.

#### Key terms

chapters.title: The basepoint one and hitting times at the basepoints
chapters.summary:
This chapter works out the shifted clock $T_\alpha$ of the reciprocal Xi function at the basepoint $\alpha=1$, the random variable with Laplace transform $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt u)$ for the completed Riemann zeta function $\xi$, and asks three questions: what its Thorin measure and law are, whether its Thorin density comes from the sine squared lemma, and whether $T_1$ is a hitting time to which Kent's theorem applies. The Thorin measure of this generalised gamma convolution (GGC) is the Poisson smoothing of the zeros by Cauchy kernels, positive with no hypothesis because no zero lies on $\operatorname{Re}s=1$. The chapter derives a Lévy form of $\log\xi(1+s)$, proves with no hypothesis (ball arithmetic and explicit zero counts) that the Thorin density is smallest at the origin, giving an independent positive stable one half summand, and shows that the same minimum on every line with real part between one half and one is equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis (RH). It then treats the hitting time question: $T_1$ is not a diffusion hitting time in the sense of Kent and Krein because its Thorin measure is absolutely continuous, and it is not a Brownian first passage time to an independent random level (proved). The centre clock is a subordinated hitting time, the density of $T_1$ is expressed through harmonic measure, and an exact Brownian boundary with a Wald identity, valid at every basepoint above the centre, is derived; boundaries across the basepoints are compared. Statements at basepoints below one are conditional on the absence of zeros to the right.

#### From the literature

- $2\xi(s)$ as the Mellin transform of a sum of two Bessel hitting times (Williams 1990; Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001)
- generalised gamma convolutions (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992); Kent's theorem on diffusion hitting times, with Krein's inverse spectral theory (Kent 1980; Dym and McKean 1976)
- Lagarias's positivity criterion for RH (Lagarias 1999)
- sticky Brownian motion (Itô and McKean 1965); inverse first passage (Anulova 1980; Ekström and Janson 2016)
- verification of RH to $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021); explicit zero counts (Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong 2022)

#### New results

- [Barnes beta laws (after Ostrovsky): the beta case is a GGC if and only if b1 is a positive integer, and the sech squared Levy density is a Gaussian mixture whose mixing law has Mellin transform xi(2q+2)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#ostrovsky_barnes_beta_laws_as_gaussian_mixture_with_mellin_transform_xi) (Volume I, Remark 12.1.1, page 212; computed): The companion $C_2$ of $S_2$ has $\mathbb{E}e^{-uC_2}=\operatorname{sech}^2\sqrt{2u}$ and Mellin transform $\frac{2^{2q+2}-1}{q+1}(\frac2\pi)^{q+1}\xi(2q+2)$, checked numerically at four points, so the Lévy density of the Barnes beta law (Ostrovsky) is a Gaussian mixture whose mixing law has Mellin transform $\xi(2q+2)$. The law of minus the logarithm of a beta variable with parameters $b_0,b_1$ is a GGC if and only if $b_1$ is a positive integer (proved), and the sech squared Barnes beta law is not a GGC. New in this book.
- [Compensated sine squared formula at the basepoint one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#compensated_sine_squared_formula_basepoint_one) (Volume I, Proposition 12.1.3, page 215; proved): At the basepoint one the Thorin density equals an explicit digamma expression plus a compensated sine squared sum over the primes, and the limit exists by the prime number theorem. New in this book.
- [De la Vallée Poussin's zero free region from the Thorin density: the two frequency inequality 4Z(y)+Z(2y) at most 8 c_alpha](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#de_la_vallee_poussin_inequality_in_thorin_form_from_sine_squared_lemma) (Volume I, Proposition 12.1.4, page 216; proved): The prime part $Z(\alpha,y)$ of the Thorin density of $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt u)$ satisfies $0\le Z\le2c_\alpha$ and $4Z(\alpha,y)+Z(\alpha,2y)\le8c_\alpha$, and a zero $\beta_0+i\gamma_0$ then satisfies $1-\beta_0\ge c/\log\gamma_0$ for large $\gamma_0$, de la Vallée Poussin's classical zero free region read through the Thorin density. New in this book.
- [Thorin property of the reciprocal Xi function for basepoint at least 5.4962 from the sine squared lemma alone, with no information on the zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_xi_is_ggc_for_basepoint_at_least_5_4962_by_sine_squared_lemma_alone) (Volume I, Proposition 12.1.5, page 217; proved): For $\alpha\ge\alpha_0=5.4962215670\ldots$, the root of an explicit increasing function $D$, the function $u\mapsto\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt u)$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution, proved from the sine squared lemma alone without any information on the zeros. New in this book.
- [Thorin condition with the prime part dropped: the sign of m(alpha) changes at alpha_1 = 3.5747764, computed in floating point and not proved on [alpha_1, alpha_0)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#floating_point_thorin_condition_below_alpha_0_with_threshold_alpha_1_3_5748) (Volume I, Remark 12.1.6, page 217; computed): Dropping the prime part $Z\ge0$ from the Thorin density leaves $m(\alpha)=\min_y\{P+A\}+D(\alpha)$, which changes sign at $\alpha_1=3.5747764\ldots$, below $\alpha_0=5.4962$; this is computed in floating point at sampled points, not proved on $[\alpha_1,\alpha_0)$, and no bound on the primes uniform in $y$ goes below $\alpha_1$ because $\inf_yZ(\alpha,y)=0$. New in this book.
- [Unconditional GGC property of the reciprocal Xi function in the fourth root variable, compensated by the first power sum, with explicit Thorin density from the heat trace](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_trace_weighted_reciprocal_xi_in_fourth_root_is_ggc_with_absolutely_continuous_thorin_measure) (Volume I, Proposition 12.1.7, page 218; proved): Unconditionally, the function $\Psi(s)=\frac{\xi(\frac12+s^{1/4})}{\xi(\frac12)}e^{-p_1\sqrt s}$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution whose Thorin measure has an explicit density built from the heat trace $W$, and under RH it equals the Weierstrass product $\prod_{\gamma>0}(1+\sqrt s/\gamma^2)e^{-\sqrt s/\gamma^2}$. New in this book.
- [The square root is forced: xi(alpha)/xi(alpha+q) is not the Laplace transform of a positive measure in q for any alpha](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_xi_not_laplace_transform_of_positive_measure_in_q_so_clock_variable_is_u_equals_q_squared) (Volume I, Remark 12.1.8, page 218; proved): For every real $\alpha$, $q\mapsto\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+q)$ is not $\int e^{-qt}\mu(dt)$ for a positive measure $\mu\ne0$ on any half plane, because it decays faster than $e^{-qT}$ for every $T$; so the clock starts at the variable $u=q^2$. New in this book.
- [Barnes beta law of Ostrovsky with Lévy density sech squared over 4t: Mellin transform by Barnes G, GGC form with an explicit Thorin density, and zeros of the Mellin transform of that density](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#barnes_beta_law_with_levy_density_sech_squared_has_thorin_density_from_zeta_at_2w) (Volume I, Proposition 12.1.9, page 219; proved): For the Barnes beta law $\mathfrak b=e^{-Y_{\mathfrak b}}$ of Ostrovsky (Lévy density $\operatorname{sech}^2(t/4)/4t$), $\mathbb{E}\mathfrak b^q$ is a ratio of Barnes $G$ functions, $\mathbb{E}\mathfrak b^{\sqrt s}e^{\sqrt s}$ is the reciprocal of a GGC transform with Thorin density $\frac1{2\pi\sqrt z}-\frac1{\sinh2\pi\sqrt z}>0$, and the Mellin transform of that density is $-4(2\pi)^{-2w}(1-2^{-2w})\Gamma(2w)\zeta(2w)$. New in this book.
- [Lévy form of the completed zeta function at the basepoint one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#levy_form_of_xi_at_basepoint_one) (Volume I, Proposition 12.1.10, page 220; proved): The logarithm of $\xi(1+s)/\xi(1)$ has an explicit Lévy form whose drift is the sum of the reciprocals of the zeros and whose signed Lévy measure consists of a gamma density, a pole term and prime atoms, the compensated integral converging by the prime number theorem. New in this book.
- [Minimum of the Thorin density at the origin and stable summand at the basepoint one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_density_minimum_at_origin_basepoint_one) (Volume I, Proposition 12.1.11, page 221; proved): With no hypothesis on the zeros, certified with the first 1800 zeros in ball arithmetic and explicit zero counts above height 2000, the Thorin density of the shifted clock at the basepoint one is smallest only at the origin, so the clock is the sum of an independent positive stable one half variable and a generalized gamma convolution. New in this book.
- [Minimum at the origin and stable summand at every basepoint from one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_density_minimum_at_origin_every_basepoint_from_one) (Volume I, Proposition 12.1.12, page 225; proved): The same minimum at the origin and the same splitting into a positive stable one half summand and a generalized gamma convolution hold at every basepoint at or above one, certified with ball arithmetic and explicit zero counts above height 2000. New in this book.
- [Regularly varying tail of the Thorin remainder at basepoints at least one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heavy_tail_of_the_levy_density_of_the_thorin_remainder_at_basepoints_at_least_one) (Volume I, Result 12.1.4, page 226; proved): For basepoints alpha at least one the Lévy density of the Thorin remainder variable is asymptotic to a constant times t to the power minus five halves and its tail to a constant times t to the power minus three halves, a subexponential tail; a computation at alpha equal to two confirms the rate. New in this book.
- [Lévy form below the basepoint one and zero free half planes](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#levy_form_below_basepoint_one_and_zero_free_half_plane) (Volume I, Proposition 12.1.13, page 227; proved): Below the basepoint one the Lévy form of $\xi$ converges and gives a positive Thorin density when all zeros lie to the left of the basepoint, and conversely its validity at a basepoint forces a zero free half plane to the right of it. New in this book.
- [Comparison of the Thorin density across vertical lines](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_density_ratio_comparison_across_vertical_lines) (Volume I, Theorem 12.1.15, page 230; proved): The ratio of the real part of the logarithmic derivative of a completed function on a vertical line to the distance of that line from the critical line is nonincreasing as the line moves right, under a hypothesis on the zeros to the right of the critical line that holds under RH, for lines at distance at least $1/\sqrt2$ from the critical line, and below the verified height. New in this book.
- [Explicit lower bound of the Thorin density by comparison with the Euler product](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#explicit_lower_bound_of_thorin_density_by_comparison_with_euler_product) (Volume I, Corollary 12.1.16, page 231; proved): On a line to the right of one the Euler product and the digamma function give an explicit lower bound for the real part of the logarithmic derivative of a completed zeta or Dirichlet L function, and under the comparison hypothesis the bound, multiplied by the ratio of the distances of the lines from the critical line, holds on every line to the left and is of order a positive multiple of the logarithm of the height. New in this book.
- [Minimum of the Thorin density at the origin and its equivalence with RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_density_minimum_at_origin_below_one_equivalent_to_rh) (Volume I, Theorem 12.1.18, page 232; proved): RH, respectively GRH for the Dirichlet L function of the character modulo 4 or modulo 12, is equivalent to the Thorin density of the corresponding completed function on every line with real part between one half and one being smallest at the origin and only there, a property certified in ball arithmetic with no hypothesis up to the verified height. New in this book.
- [Certified positivity of the heat trace at the basepoint one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_trace_at_basepoint_one_positive_certified_from_primes) (Volume I, Proposition 12.1.24, page 239; proved): The heat trace of the shifted clock at the basepoint one is certified positive at every time, with an explicit lower bound, from the primes up to ten million and published explicit bounds for Chebyshev's error, in ball arithmetic. New in this book.
- [The heat trace identity at the centre alpha one half with a finite part](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_trace_identity_at_the_centre_with_a_finite_part) (Volume I, Remark 12.1.25, page 240; proved): At the centre alpha one half the prime sum and the Lebesgue piece of the heat trace identity diverge separately but the identity holds with a finite part and no hypothesis on the zeros, and it bounds the smoothed Chebyshev error unconditionally; a computation checks it to $3\times10^{-15}$. New in this book.
- [No Brownian first passage to a random level at the basepoint one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#no_brownian_first_passage_to_random_level_at_basepoint_one) (Volume I, Proposition 12.2.1, page 243; proved): The shifted clock at the basepoint one is not the first passage time of a Brownian motion with drift to a random level independent of the motion. New in this book.
- [Subordination of the tilted centre clock at the basepoint one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#basepoint_one_clock_subordination_of_tilted_centre_clock) (Volume I, Theorem 12.2.2, page 243; proved): The shifted clock at the basepoint one is the exponentially tilted centre clock run through the inverse local time of a sticky Brownian motion, equivalently the tilted clock plus a Brownian first passage time to a level proportional to it. New in this book.
- [Kent string hitting time of the shifted clock at the basepoint one under RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#basepoint_one_clock_kent_string_hitting_time_under_rh) (Volume I, Corollary 12.2.3, page 244; conditional on the Riemann Hypothesis (every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part one half) and the simplicity of every nontrivial zero): Assuming RH and simple zeros, the tilted centre clock is a Kent hitting time of a Krein string with spectrum the squared moduli of the zeros, and the shifted clock at the basepoint one is the first hitting time of a level by this string diffusion run on the local time of a sticky Brownian motion. New in this book.
- [Subordination of the centre clock at every basepoint above the centre](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#shifted_clock_subordination_every_basepoint_above_centre) (Volume I, Theorem 12.2.5, page 248; proved): For every basepoint above the centre the shifted clock exists with no hypothesis on the zeros and is a Brownian hitting time built from the tilted centre clock, with a stable one half tail, and, by the threshold theorem of Polson 2026, it is a generalized gamma convolution exactly when no zero lies to the right of the basepoint. New in this book.
- [Lévy measure and self decomposability of the shifted clock](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#shifted_clock_levy_measure_and_self_decomposability) (Volume I, Corollary 12.2.6, page 249; proved): The shifted clock at every basepoint above the centre is infinitely divisible and self decomposable, with an explicit Lévy measure obtained from that of the centre clock. New in this book.

#### Key terms

basepoint, shifted clock, reciprocal Xi function, Riemann xi function, generalised gamma convolution, GGC, Thorin measure, Thorin density, Lévy form, Levy form, Cauchy kernel, Poisson smoothing, sine squared lemma, positive stable law, hitting time, first passage time, Kent's theorem, Krein string, Wald identity, Brownian boundary, harmonic measure, subordination, sticky Brownian motion, Riemann Hypothesis, RH

chapters.title: The critical strip, Riesz's criterion and the squarefree series
chapters.summary:
This chapter asks how much of the unconditional structure of the reciprocal Xi function at the basepoint one survives inside the critical strip of the Riemann zeta function, and what it says about Riesz's criterion for the Riemann Hypothesis (RH). Its objects are the basepoint clocks $T_\alpha$, with Laplace transform $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt u)$, and their Thorin measures. On the real axis the reciprocal of $\xi$ is the characteristic function of an infinitely divisible normal scale mixture, an extended generalised gamma convolution (EGGC) exactly when no zero lies to the right of the basepoint. RH is equivalent to complete monotonicity of the Poisson trace of the zeros, and zero free half planes become completeness of translates of the Pólya kernel. Riesz's criterion becomes the statement that every $T_\alpha$ with $\alpha>\frac12$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC), and $1/\zeta(2k)$ is a Laplace transform value of the clocks. The squarefree integers, with Dirichlet series $\zeta(s)/\zeta(2s)$, give criteria for RH from exponentially and Gamma(2) smoothed counts, a Mertens function representation and a threshold at Gamma shape two. The chapter proves no new zero free region.

#### From the literature

- Thorin representation of generalised gamma convolutions (Thorin 1977, 1978; Bondesson 1992)
- Wiener's closure theorem (Wiener 1932; Kac 1965; Korevaar 1965); Salem's equivalent of RH (Salem 1953)
- Riesz's criterion (Riesz 1916) and its companion (Hardy and Littlewood 1916); Lagarias's positivity criterion (Lagarias 1999); the Nyman Beurling criterion (Nyman 1950; Beurling 1955; Báez Duarte 2003)
- Euler's formulae for $\zeta(2n)$ from Cauchy variables (Bourgade, Fujita and Yor 2007)
- RH verified to height $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021)
- Squarefree integers: a Math StackExchange question (2016), the conditional exponent 7/22 (Baker and Pintz 1985), Lazarević's inequality (Lazarević 1966), integer and fractional parts (Steutel and Thiemann 1989), Ingham's method (1942); a mean square criterion the chapter calls presumably folklore

#### New results

New in the book; the squarefree material and the Poisson trace conditions are from unpublished notes of Nicholas Polson.
- [Reciprocal Xi function on the real axis as a normal scale mixture](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_xi_real_axis_normal_scale_mixture) (Volume I, Proposition 13.1.1, page 254; proved): For every basepoint $\alpha\ge\frac12$, $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+|u|)$ is the characteristic function of a symmetric, unimodal, infinitely divisible law with no hypothesis on the zeros, which has a Cauchy tail when $\alpha>\frac12$. New in this book.
- [Thorin form of the reciprocal Xi function and the EGGC criterion](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_xi_thorin_form_and_eggc_criterion) (Volume I, Theorem 13.1.2, page 256; proved): When every zero of $\zeta$ has real part less than the basepoint $\alpha>\frac12$ (always for $\alpha\ge1$), the characteristic function $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+|u|)$ has an explicit Thorin form with the positive density $\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\alpha+i\theta)/\pi$, and for $\frac12<\alpha<1$ the law is an extended generalised gamma convolution exactly when there is no zero to the right of $\alpha$. New in this book.
- [EGGC property of the reciprocal Xi law across the critical strip](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#eggc_property_across_the_critical_strip) (Volume I, Theorem 13.1.3, page 258; proved): For $\frac12<\alpha<1$ the law $Y_\alpha$ is an extended generalised gamma convolution exactly when $\zeta$ has no zeros with real part above $\alpha$, and with no hypothesis its characteristic function is that of an extended generalised gamma convolution times a remainder $\mathcal{E}_{\alpha,T_0}(u)$ with $|\log\mathcal{E}_{\alpha,T_0}(u)|\le4(|u|+u^2)\log T_0/T_0$, where $T_0\ge2$ is a height up to which all zeros lie on the critical line. New in this book.
- [Complete monotonicity of the Poisson trace is equivalent to RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#poisson_trace_completely_monotone_iff_rh) (Volume I, Corollary 13.1.4, page 261; proved): RH holds exactly when the Poisson trace $\sum_ke^{-y\sqrt{a_k}}$ of the zeros is completely monotone (the same equivalence for the heat trace was shown earlier by Polson 2026), and for $\alpha\ge1$ the corresponding trace is completely monotone with no hypothesis and decays like $b_\alpha/(\pi y)$. New in this book.
- [Positive half of the reciprocal Xi law as a centred infinitely divisible law with Poisson trace Lévy density](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#poisson_trace_law_positive_half_of_reciprocal_xi_law) (Volume I, Proposition 13.1.5, page 262; proved): The symmetric law with characteristic function $\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+|u|)$ is the difference of two independent copies of a centred infinitely divisible law $A$ with Lévy density $K_{1/2}(x)/x$, which under RH is $\sum_k(E_k-1)/\gamma_k$, and any representation of this form with positive rates forces RH; the proof follows a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book. New in this book.
- [Primes as poles of the Poisson trace: the residues at plus or minus i times the logarithms of prime powers](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#poisson_trace_continuation_with_poles_at_log_prime_powers_and_residue) (Volume I, Proposition 13.1.6, page 263; proved): The Poisson trace $K_{1/2}(x)=e^{-ix/2}V(ix)$ of the zeros continues to a meromorphic function off $(-\infty,0]$ with simple poles at $x=\pm i\log n$ for prime powers $n$ and residue $-\Lambda(n)/(2\pi\sqrt n)$; the continuation and the location of the poles are due to Cramér (1919) and the residue is proved in the book, following a note of Nicholas Polson. New in this book.
- [Unconditional range of the complete monotonicity conditions of the Poisson trace](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#poisson_trace_derivative_conditions_hold_below_verified_height) (Volume I, Theorem 13.1.8, page 265; proved): If all zeros up to height $H$ lie on the critical line, the derivative conditions $(-1)^nK^{(n)}(y)>0$ of the Poisson trace $K$ hold at every $0<y<\pi$ and every order $n<H(\pi-y)$; with $H=3\times10^{12}$ this covers all orders below $4.24\times10^{11}$ for $y\le3$. New in this book.
- [Quasi Riemann hypothesis version of the range of the Poisson trace conditions: y below 4 pi over 3 and n below 4 pi T_0 over 3 under (Q_{7/8})](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rectangle_theorem_for_poisson_trace_remains_valid_under_quasi_rh_at_seven_eighths_with_range_four_pi_over_three) (Volume I, Remark 13.1.9, page 265; conditional on The quasi Riemann hypothesis $(\mathrm Q_{7/8})$ of the book, which rests on the unrefereed half plane of OpenAI (2026); the variant with Liu's claimed half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>0.874957$ rests on an unrefereed claim as well): The rectangle uses that $\varphi_k$ and $\delta_k$ have the same sign; under $(\mathrm Q_{7/8})$, $\Delta=\frac38$ and the range of the Poisson trace theorem becomes $0<y<\frac{4\pi}3$ and $n<\frac{4\pi}3T_0=1.26\times10^{13}$; Liu's claimed half plane would give $y<4.1893$. New in this book.
- [Positive definite and bounded forms of the Poisson trace criterion for RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#poisson_trace_positive_definite_and_bounded_forms_of_rh) (Volume I, Proposition 13.1.10, page 266; proved): RH is equivalent to positive definiteness of $y\mapsto K_{1/2}(x+iy)$ for every $x>0$, and to boundedness of $y\mapsto K_{1/2}(x+iy)$ on $[0,\infty)$ for some $x>0$, where $K_{1/2}$ is the Poisson trace of the zeros. New in this book.
- [Small y asymptotics of the Poisson trace and Pólya's trace](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#poisson_trace_versus_polya_trace_small_y_asymptotics) (Volume I, Proposition 13.1.11, page 268; proved): As $y\to0+$ the Poisson trace of the zeros of $\zeta$ and the trace of the zeros of Pólya's Bessel function $K_{i\theta/2}(2\pi)$ have the same main term and their difference tends to $\frac98$, with a refined second term under RH. New in this book.
- [Explicit obstruction and approximation cost for translates of the tilted Pólya kernel](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#tilted_polya_kernel_translates_obstruction_and_approximation_cost) (Volume I, Proposition 13.1.12, page 270; proved): For translates of the tilted Pólya kernel $\Phi_\alpha$ the book proves an explicit obstruction at the centre (no finite combination approximates $g\in L^1(\mathbb{R})$ with $L^1$ error below $\sup_\gamma|\hat g(\gamma)|$, over the ordinates $\gamma$ of the zeros on the critical line) and, where the translates are dense, an explicit cost of approximation (a combination within $\delta$ of $g$ has coefficient sum at least $(|\hat g(\gamma)|-\delta)/|\xi(\alpha+i\gamma)|$ for every ordinate $\gamma$ of a zero of $\zeta$); the density criteria (dense exactly when $\zeta$ has no zeros on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha$; dense for every $\alpha>\frac12$ exactly when RH holds) restate Wiener's closure theorem (Wiener 1932). New in this book.
- [Pólya kernel analogue of Salem's criterion](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#polya_kernel_analogue_of_salem_criterion) (Volume I, Corollary 13.1.13, page 272; proved): RH holds if and only if, for every $\frac12<\alpha<1$, the convolution equation with the tilted Pólya kernel $\Phi_\alpha$ has no bounded nonzero solution; at the centre $\cos(\gamma y)$ solves it for every ordinate $\gamma$ of a zero on the critical line. New in this book.
- [Twisted Riesz function and the basepoint form of Riesz's criterion](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#twisted_riesz_function_and_basepoint_riesz_criterion) (Volume I, Proposition 13.2.1, page 275; proved): Twisting Riesz's function by $(x/n^2)^{ih}$ changes the Gamma factor of its Mellin transform to $\Gamma(1-s+ih)/\zeta(2s)$ and keeps the criterion: $\zeta$ has no zeros with real part above $\alpha$ exactly when $R_h(x)=O(x^{\alpha/2+\delta})$ for every $\delta>0$. New in this book.
- [The Riesz function as an average over the centre clock](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#riesz_function_as_centre_clock_average) (Volume I, Proposition 13.2.4, page 278; proved): With no hypothesis, Riesz's function is minus the expectation of an alternating series in the centre clock whose terms decay like $e^{-4k^2T}$ instead of $1/(k-1)!$. New in this book.
- [Riesz coefficients as values of GGC Laplace transforms](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#riesz_coefficients_as_ggc_laplace_values) (Volume I, Proposition 13.2.5, page 279; proved): For $\alpha\in[\frac12,1]$, $1/\zeta(2k)$ is an explicit multiple of the Laplace transform of the basepoint clock $T_\alpha$ at $(2k-\alpha)^2$, in particular of the centre clock at $\alpha=\frac12$ and of the basepoint one clock at $\alpha=1$, and at $\alpha=1$ it is $\kappa_k$ times the exponential of minus a Thorin integral, with no hypothesis on the zeros. New in this book.
- [GGC form of Riesz's criterion](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#riesz_criterion_as_ggc_property_of_basepoint_clocks) (Volume I, Theorem 13.2.7, page 281; proved): Riesz's growth condition at exponent $\alpha/2$ is equivalent to each clock $T_{\alpha'}$ with $\alpha'>\alpha$ being a generalised gamma convolution, to positivity of $\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)$ on the lines to the right of $\alpha$, and to convergence of a compensated sine squared sum over the primes; for $\alpha=\frac12$, RH holds exactly when every $T_\alpha$ with $\alpha>\frac12$ is a GGC. New in this book.
- [Closed form constant of the squarefree reciprocal sum over number fields](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#squarefree_reciprocal_sum_closed_form_constant) (Volume I, Proposition 13.3.1, page 289; proved): Over a number field $K$ of degree $n\ge2$ the sum of $\mu(\mathfrak a)^2/N(\mathfrak a)$ over the integral ideals of norm at most $x$ equals $\frac{c_K}{\zeta_K(2)}(\log x+C_K)+O(x^{-1/n}\log x)$ with the explicit constant $C_K=\gamma_K-2\zeta_K'(2)/\zeta_K(2)$, $\gamma_K$ the Euler Kronecker constant of $K$. New in this book.
- [Squarefree Dirichlet series as a gamma factor times a ratio of Pólya moment generating functions](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#squarefree_dirichlet_series_as_gamma_factor_times_polya_ratio) (Volume I, Proposition 13.3.3, page 291; proved): The squarefree Dirichlet series $\zeta(s)/\zeta(2s)$ equals an explicit gamma factor times $\mathbb{E}\,e^{(s-1/2)X}/\mathbb{E}\,e^{(2s-1/2)X}$ for the Pólya variable $X$, which continues the series to every $s$ with $\xi(2s)\ne0$. New in this book.
- [Squarefree constant as a combination of two tilted Pólya means](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#squarefree_constant_as_difference_of_tilted_polya_means) (Volume I, Theorem 13.3.5, page 291; proved): The constant $C$ of the squarefree reciprocal sum is an elementary part plus $b_1-2b_2$, a combination of the means of the Pólya variable tilted at the basepoints one and two, which is an absolutely convergent sum over the zeros with no hypothesis. New in this book.
- [Dedekind zeta clock is a GGC if and only if RH holds for the field](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#dedekind_clock_is_ggc_iff_rh_for_dedekind_zeta) (Volume I, Proposition 13.3.6, page 292; proved): For a number field $K$ with $\zeta_K(\frac12)\ne0$, the reciprocal of the normalised completed Dedekind function is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution exactly when all nontrivial zeros of $\zeta_K$ lie on the critical line, with Thorin measure the sum of point masses at the squared ordinates; this is the number field form of the rigidity theorem of Polson 2026. New in this book.
- [Squarefree constant of a number field through the zeros of its Dedekind zeta function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#squarefree_constant_of_a_number_field_through_zeros) (Volume I, Theorem 13.3.7, page 293; proved): For a number field $K$ the constant $C_K$ is an explicit elementary term $A_K$ plus an absolutely convergent sum over the zeros of its Dedekind zeta function, and under the Riemann Hypothesis for $\zeta_K$ that sum is a combination of two Stieltjes transform values of the Thorin measure. New in this book.
- [Exponentially and Gamma(2) smoothed squarefree counts are equivalent to RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#smoothed_squarefree_counts_equivalent_to_rh) (Volume I, Theorem 13.3.9, page 296; proved): RH holds if and only if the squarefree count smoothed by an exponential law, or by a Gamma(2) law, with mean $x$ equals $6x/\pi^2+O(x^{1/4+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, and under RH with simple zeros an explicit formula with exponentially damped terms at the zeros holds. New in this book.
- [Lower bound for the squarefree error of the order of the fourth root of x](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#squarefree_error_lower_bound_order_fourth_root_of_x) (Volume I, Corollary 13.3.11, page 299; proved): With no hypothesis the squarefree error $\Delta(x)$ satisfies $\limsup\Delta(x)/x^{1/4}\ge0.1004$ and $\liminf\Delta(x)/x^{1/4}\le-0.1004$, so the order $x^{1/4}$ cannot be lowered, and the Gamma(2) smoothed error has the same property with constant $9.94\times10^{-5}$. New in this book.
- [Squarefree count at a Gamma(n) random point under RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#squarefree_gamma_n_smoothing_bound_under_rh) (Volume I, Proposition 13.3.12, page 299; conditional on the Riemann Hypothesis): Under RH, the expected squarefree count at a Gamma($n$) random point of mean $x$ is $6x/\pi^2+O(x^{1/4+\varepsilon}n^{1/8+\varepsilon})$, uniformly in $n\ge1$. New in this book.
- [Gamma(2) smoothed squarefree error as a positive average of the Mertens function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#gamma2_smoothed_squarefree_error_as_mertens_average) (Volume I, Theorem 13.3.15, page 301; proved): The squarefree count smoothed by a Gamma(2) law of mean $x$ equals $6x/\pi^2$ minus half the expected Mertens function at the random point $\sqrt{x\mathcal{V}_2/2}$, where the density $f_2$ of $\mathcal{V}_2$ is explicit and positive by Lazarević's inequality. New in this book.
- [Gamma smoothing threshold, shape two](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#gamma_smoothing_threshold_shape_two) (Volume I, Theorem 13.3.18, page 304; proved): The signed density that mixes the Mertens function in the Gamma($\nu$) smoothed squarefree error is nonnegative exactly for the shapes $\nu\in(0,2]$, the obstruction above two being the trivial zero of $\zeta$ at $-2$. New in this book.
- [Pointwise bound for the squarefree error under RH (open)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#squarefree_error_pointwise_bound_under_rh_open) (Volume I, Question 13.3.19, page 306; open): The book asks for a proof, under RH, that the squarefree count has error $O(x^{1/4+\varepsilon})$, and records forms equivalent to it or sufficient for it. New in this book.
- [Sharpening the lower bound constant for the squarefree error (open)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#squarefree_error_fejer_constant_and_unboundedness_open) (Volume I, Question 13.3.20, page 306; open): The book asks whether a Fejér kernel over many zeros improves the constant $0.1004$ in the lower bound for the squarefree error, and whether $\limsup|\Delta(x)|/x^{1/4}$ is infinite. New in this book.

#### Key terms

Riesz criterion, Riemann hypothesis, critical strip, reciprocal Xi function, basepoint clock, Thorin measure, generalised gamma convolution, generalized gamma convolution, GGC, extended generalised gamma convolution, EGGC, normal scale mixture, Poisson trace, complete monotonicity, Wiener closure theorem, Salem criterion, Pólya kernel, Möbius function, squarefree integers, square free numbers, Mertens function, Gamma smoothing, Dedekind zeta function, Nyman Beurling criterion

chapters.title: Below the basepoint one: a map of processes, free probability, almost GGCs and the Lambert law
chapters.summary:
What can be said about the Thorin measure of the reciprocal Xi function below the basepoint one, where no zero free half plane is available, and which processes realise the shifted clocks? The centre clock is self decomposable and unimodal with no hypothesis, being the stationary law of an Ornstein Uhlenbeck process driven by a subordinator whose Lévy density is minus the derivative of the heat trace, and the tilted Pólya variable is quasi infinitely divisible above the basepoint one and not at it. A Wiener gamma integral and a Riemann Ornstein Uhlenbeck process, and subordinated Brownian motion run on the clocks, give a map of processes sorted by what each needs: nothing, a zero free half plane, or the Riemann Hypothesis (RH). The Upsilon transform and the Bercovici Pata bijection give the clock a free counterpart, and RH holds exactly when the clock is the Upsilon image of an infinitely divisible law; the semicircle law is a local model for the Jacobi parameters, with Gamma(2), Laguerre polynomials and finite free convolution as exact examples. The almost generalised gamma convolution (almost GGC) theorem uses zero density estimates to show, with no hypothesis, that every shifted clock is a GGC up to a defect carried by the zeros to its right, whose Cauchy kernels carry a vanishing fraction of the mass of the others, with a power saving; the verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$ bounds the defect explicitly, and the moments of zeta of Keating and Snaith are read as exponential moments of the Thorin density. The last sections treat Pakes's questions: the solved Lambert law as a Thorin problem, Urbanik's classes (the centre clock lies in $L_2$ and not in $L_3$, with no hypothesis), the absence of a branching process realisation, and a criticality filter along the de Bruijn Newman flow that tests candidate properties implying RH. Computed inequalities are in ball arithmetic.

#### From the literature

- Self decomposable laws and GGCs (Sato 1999; Bondesson 1992), driving subordinators (Wolfe 1982; Jurek and Vervaat 1983), unimodality (Yamazato 1978), subexponential tails (Embrechts, Goldie and Veraverbeke 1979)
- Quasi infinite divisibility (Lindner, Pan and Sato 2018), proved above the basepoint one by Nakamura (2015)
- Bessel hitting times (Williams 1990; Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001)
- The Bercovici Pata bijection (Bercovici and Pata 1999), free regular laws (Arizmendi, Hasebe and Sakuma 2013), free self decomposability (Barndorff-Nielsen and Thorbjørnsen 2002) and its unimodality (Hasebe and Thorbjørnsen 2016), the Upsilon transform (Barndorff-Nielsen and Thorbjørnsen 2004; Barndorff-Nielsen, Maejima and Sato 2006), finite free convolution (Marcus, Spielman and Srivastava 2022)
- Zero density estimates (Ingham 1940; Huxley 1972; Guth and Maynard 2026), verification of RH to $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021)
- Moments of zeta and the Barnes function (Keating and Snaith 2000)
- The Dedekind eta function and the Dirichlet $L$ function of the real character modulo 12
- Pakes's work on size biasing, Steutel's theorem and infinite divisibility (Steutel 1973; Pakes and Khattree 1992; Pakes 2014)
- The Lambert $W$ function as a Thorin problem (Kalugin, Jeffrey and Corless 2011)
- Urbanik's classes (Urbanik) and the de Bruijn Newman constant (Rodgers and Tao 2020)

#### New results

Results of this chapter, with their status.

- [Background driving subordinator of the centre clock](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#centre_clock_background_driving_subordinator) (Volume I, Proposition 14.1.1, page 308; proved): With no hypothesis the centre clock is the integral of $e^{-t}$ against a subordinator whose Lévy density is minus the derivative of the heat trace of the zeros, and RH holds if and only if that density is completely monotone. New in this book.
- [Unimodality of the centre clock and the shifted clocks](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#centre_clock_and_shifted_clocks_unimodal) (Volume I, Corollary 14.1.2, page 309; proved): The centre clock and every shifted clock with basepoint above one half have unimodal laws, with no hypothesis. New in this book.
- [The tilted Pólya variable at the basepoint one is not quasi infinitely divisible](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#polya_tilt_basepoint_one_not_quasi_infinitely_divisible) (Volume I, Proposition 14.1.3, page 311; proved): The tilted Pólya variable at the basepoint one, with moment generating function $\xi(1+s)/\xi(1)$, is not quasi infinitely divisible, hence not infinitely divisible. New in this book.
- [Thorin Bernstein form of the shifted clock criterion](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_bernstein_criterion_for_shifted_clock_exponent) (Volume I, Proposition 14.1.4, page 314; proved): The Laplace exponent of the shifted clock is a Thorin Bernstein function with no hypothesis when the basepoint is at least one, and for basepoints between one half and one exactly when zeta has no zero to the right of the basepoint, while the exponent of the centre clock is one if and only if RH holds. New in this book.
- [Upsilon image and free counterpart of the centre clock](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#upsilon_image_and_free_counterpart_of_centre_clock) (Volume I, Theorem 14.2.3, page 324; proved): With no hypothesis the Upsilon image of the centre clock is a generalised gamma convolution with an explicit Thorin measure and its Bercovici Pata counterpart is a freely self decomposable unimodal law carried by a half line $[c,\infty)$ with $c>0$, and RH holds if and only if the clock is itself the Upsilon image of an infinitely divisible law. New in this book.
- [RH holds if and only if a freely infinitely divisible law nu_xi with free cumulant transform log xi(1/2)/xi(1/2+sqrt(-z)) exists](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rh_equivalent_to_existence_of_freely_infinitely_divisible_law_with_cumulant_transform_log_xi_ratio) (Volume I, Proposition 14.2.4, page 326; proved): RH holds exactly when the function $\mathcal{C}_\xi(z)=\log\{\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt{-z})\}$ is the free cumulant transform of a freely infinitely divisible probability measure, which under RH is $\Lambda_{\rm BP}(\mu_0)$, with compact support, free cumulants $m_{n-1}/n$ and free Lévy measure $N(y^{-1/2})dy/y$. New in this book.
- [Dickman reading of the preimage mu_0 of the clock under the Upsilon transform: a sum of independent Dickman variables over the zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#dickman_reading_of_the_upsilon_preimage_of_the_clock_under_rh) (Volume I, Result 14.2.3, page 326; proved): Under RH the preimage $\mu_0$ of the clock under $\Upsilon$ is the law of $\sum_{\gamma>0}D_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent Dickman variables $D_\gamma$, since $\Upsilon(D/\gamma^2)$ is the exponential law of rate $\gamma^2$; with no hypothesis $\psi_0(s)=\sum_k\operatorname{Ein}(s/a_k)$ is entire with $\int_0^\infty\psi_0(sx)e^{-x}dx=\log G(s)$. New in this book.
- [Peeling a gamma layer from the Pólya generating function keeps zeros real under RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#gamma_layer_peeling_keeps_real_zeros_under_rh) (Volume I, Proposition 14.2.9, page 334; conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis): If RH holds, dividing the Taylor coefficients of the Pólya generating function by $(a)_k$ keeps all zeros real and negative for every $a>0$, whereas multiplying the coefficients of a polynomial by $(a)_k$ need not preserve real zeros. New in this book.
- [No gamma scale mixture for the Pólya variable and Williams' variable](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#no_gamma_scale_mixture_for_polya_and_williams_variables) (Volume I, Theorem 14.2.10, page 335; proved): For no shape $a>0$ is the absolute value of the Pólya variable, its square or Williams' variable $S_2$ a scale mixture of Gamma($a$) laws. New in this book.
- [Almost GGC theorem for the shifted clocks](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#almost_ggc_theorem) (Volume I, Theorem 14.3.2, page 340; proved): With no hypothesis, for every basepoint between one half and one the Cauchy kernels of the zeros to the right of the basepoint carry a vanishing fraction of the mass of the kernels of the other zeros, with a power saving from zero density estimates. New in this book.
- [Canonical factorisation of the shifted clock transform into a GGC and a defect](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#canonical_factorisation_of_shifted_clock_transform) (Volume I, Proposition 14.3.3, page 341; proved): The Laplace transform of the shifted clock factorises exactly as the transform of a GGC times an explicit defect that carries every zero to the right of the basepoint and equals one if and only if there is none. New in this book.
- [Signed Thorin representation of the reciprocal Xi function at every basepoint alpha at least one half, with damped sinusoid factors for zeros to the right](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#signed_thorin_representation_of_clock_at_every_basepoint_with_damped_sinusoid_factors) (Volume I, Theorem 14.3.4, page 342; proved): For every basepoint $\alpha\ge\frac12$ the function $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt u)$ is the exponential of a signed Thorin integral times an explicit product over the zeros to the right of $\alpha$, each factor being the Laplace transform of a damped sinusoid, with no hypothesis on the zeros. New in this book.
- [The critical line basepoint: the signed Thorin measure at alpha one half is the sum of point masses at the ordinates of the zeros on the line](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#signed_thorin_measure_at_critical_line_basepoint_is_atoms_at_ordinates_of_zeros_on_the_line) (Volume I, Corollary 14.3.5, page 342; proved): Unconditionally, at basepoint one half the signed Thorin measure is the nonnegative sum of point masses at the ordinates of the zeros on the critical line, and the clock equals the product of the corresponding factors $\gamma^2/(\gamma^2+u)$ times a product of damped sinusoid factors over the zeros off the line; RH is the statement that the second product is empty. New in this book.
- [Explicit bounds on the defect from the verification of RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#explicit_defect_bounds_from_rh_verification) (Volume I, Theorem 14.3.6, page 343; proved): Using the verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$, with part of the proof certified in ball arithmetic, the defect of the shifted clock is within $e^{\pm1.5\times10^{-12}(u+\sqrt{u})}$ of one and the density attached to the shifted clock is positive for heights up to $1.5\times10^{12}$ once the basepoint exceeds one half by more than $6\times10^{-10}$. New in this book.
- [Positivity of the Thorin density on the verified window](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_density_positive_on_verified_window) (Volume I, Corollary 14.3.7, page 344; proved): For every basepoint above one half the density attached to the shifted clock is positive for heights up to $3\times10^{12}$ minus one half, and for basepoints up to $7.35$ it is smallest at the origin up to the height $3\times10^{12}-(1+\sqrt{2})/2$. New in this book.
- [Size biased clock and the exponential mixture form of RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#size_biased_clock_decomposition_exponential_mixture_iff_rh) (Volume I, Proposition 14.4.1, page 355; proved): With no hypothesis the size biased clock is the clock plus an independent variable whose density is the heat trace divided by its integral, and RH holds exactly when that variable is a mixture of exponential laws (Steutel's decomposition applied to the clock). New in this book.
- [Centre clock lies in Urbanik class L2 and not in L3](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#centre_clock_urbanik_class_l2_not_l3) (Volume I, Theorem 14.4.8, page 361; proved): With no hypothesis on the zeros, and certified in ball arithmetic, the centre clock lies in Urbanik's class $L_2$ and not in $L_3$, because the third ladder function of the heat trace is positive while the fourth is negative at $e^{-4.15}$. New in this book.
- [First two driving processes of the clock are self decomposable and unimodal](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#clock_first_two_driving_processes_self_decomposable_unimodal) (Volume I, Corollary 14.4.9, page 363; proved): With no hypothesis, at every time the laws of the driving process of the clock and of the driving process of that process are self decomposable, hence unimodal, and the first lies in Urbanik's class $L_1$. New in this book.
- [The clock is not the martingale limit of a supercritical continuous state branching process](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#clock_not_supercritical_csbp_martingale_limit) (Volume I, Theorem 14.4.11, page 367; proved): Certified in ball arithmetic, the sixteenth Taylor coefficient of the function $g$ built from the clock has the wrong sign, so no positive multiple of the clock is the martingale limit of a supercritical continuous state branching process with finite Malthusian parameter. New in this book.
- [Criticality filter for properties of the Pólya kernel](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#criticality_filter_damped_polya_kernel) (Volume I, Proposition 14.4.12, page 368; proved): By the theorem of Rodgers and Tao that the de Bruijn Newman constant is nonnegative, no property shared by the damped Pólya kernels with $t<0$ (such as positivity, monotonicity, log concavity, double exponential decay or analyticity in a strip) can imply real zeros of the transform or that the normalised reciprocal of the transform on the imaginary axis is the Laplace transform of a GGC. New in this book.
- [Damped Pólya law as a mixture of arcsine laws](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#damped_polya_law_arcsine_mixture) (Volume I, Proposition 14.4.13, page 370; proved): For every $t\le0$ the Pólya law damped by $e^{tv^2/4}$ is a mixture of arcsine laws with an explicit positive mixing density, extending to all $t\le0$ the arcsine representation of the Pólya variable at $t=0$ (the arcsine route of Polson 2026). New in this book.
- [Tilted Biane Pitman Yor variable is not a GGC near t = 0 and at ten certified values of t](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#biane_pitman_yor_lognormal_tilt_not_ggc_near_zero) (Volume I, Proposition 14.4.15, page 372; proved): It is certified that the Biane Pitman Yor variable, which is a GGC, stops being a GGC after the lognormal tilt $e^{t(\log b)^2/16}$ for ten listed values of $t$ and for every sufficiently small $t\ne0$. New in this book.
- [Theta variable of the odd real character modulo 8 and its reciprocal are not GGCs](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#theta_variable_character_minus_8_not_ggc) (Volume I, Proposition 14.4.18, page 375; counterexample, proved): It is certified that neither the theta variable of the real odd character of discriminant $-8$ nor its reciprocal is a GGC, so the theta variable of an $L$ function with an Euler product need not have the GGC property. New in this book.
- [Reciprocal theta variable of odd characters is a GGC for discriminants -3 and -4, not for -8, for d congruent to 1 mod 8 and for the function of Davenport and Heilbronn](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#theta_odd_character_reciprocal_laplace_transform) (Volume I, Proposition 14.4.19, page 376; proved): For an odd theta type coefficient sequence the Laplace transform of the reciprocal theta variable is a ratio of hyperbolic sines (after Biane, Pitman and Yor), which gives the GGC property for the characters of discriminant $-3$ and $-4$ and its failure for discriminant $-8$, for odd characters of discriminant $d\equiv1 \pmod 8$ and for the function of Davenport and Heilbronn. New in this book.
- [Open problem on theta type functions whose GGC property forces zeros onto the line](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_ggc_class_theta_functions_zeros_on_line) (Volume I, Problem 14.1, page 379; open): It is an open problem to find a natural class of theta type functions containing the Riemann xi function in which a GGC theta variable forces all zeros onto the critical line (which would prove RH), or a function in such a class with a GGC theta variable and a zero off the line. New in this book.
- [Open problem, is the tilted Biane Pitman Yor variable a GGC for no t other than 0](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_biane_pitman_yor_tilt_ggc_for_no_t) (Volume I, Problem 14.2, page 379; open): It is an open problem whether the Biane Pitman Yor variable tilted by $e^{t(\log b)^2/16}$ fails to be a GGC for every $t\ne0$, which is known only for small $|t|$ and for ten listed values of $t$. New in this book.
- [Open problem on the GGC property of theta variables of characters](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_ggc_theta_variables_of_passing_characters) (Volume I, Problem 14.3, page 379; open): It is an open problem which of the theta variables of the real characters of discriminant $-4$, $-3$, $5$, $8$ and $12$, all of which pass the numerical GGC test to order 12, are GGCs. New in this book.
- [Open problem on unconditional positivity of the Li coefficients](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_li_coefficients_unconditional_positivity_size_biased_clock) (Volume I, Problem 14.4, page 379; open): It is an open problem which unconditional properties of the heat trace or of the size biased clock variable force the Li coefficients to be nonnegative for every $n$, which would prove RH by Li's criterion. New in this book.
- [Open problem on the ladder index along the de Bruijn Newman flow](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_ladder_index_along_de_bruijn_newman_flow) (Volume I, Problem 14.5, page 379; open): It is an open problem to describe the ladder index of the laws with Laplace transform $R_t$ along the de Bruijn Newman flow, which numerically drops from two to one between $t=27.8$ and $t=27.9$, and to decide whether it is nonincreasing in $t$ and equal to one for all large $t$. New in this book.

#### Key terms

generalised gamma convolution, generalized gamma convolution, GGC, almost GGC, Thorin measure, shifted clock, self decomposable, background driving Lévy process, Ornstein Uhlenbeck process, quasi infinitely divisible, Upsilon transform, Bercovici Pata bijection, free probability, semicircle law, finite free convolution, Laguerre polynomials, Dedekind eta function, Lambert W function, Pakes, size biasing, Steutel theorem, Urbanik class, ladder, branching process, criticality filter, de Bruijn Newman constant, Keating Snaith moments, Barnes function, zero density, Riemann Hypothesis

chapters.title: The Dedekind eta function, L(s, chi_12) and Ramanujan's Delta
chapters.summary:
This chapter asks how much of the Pólya route and the Thorin framework for $\xi$ survives for other completed $L$ functions whose kernels are built from the Dedekind eta function: $L(s,\chi_{12})$ for the real character modulo $12$, Ramanujan's cusp form $\Delta=\eta^{24}$, the Dirichlet beta function $L(s,\chi_4)$ with the kernel $\eta^3$, and the zeta functions of imaginary quadratic fields. The eta kernels are positive by the product formula, so the zero density identity and a count of sign changes place every zero of $L(s,\chi_{12})$ below height $100$ on the critical line (the generalised Riemann hypothesis, GRH, on that window, computed). The product formula has a probabilistic reading as the distribution function of a maximum of independent exponential variables; the chapter proves a max representation of $\xi(s,\Delta)$ and $L(s,\Delta)$ by incomplete gamma functions, a Gamma mixture form, a Rényi type identity and a Thorin (generalised gamma convolution, GGC) decomposition, and shows that the maximum for $\Delta$ is not in the Bondesson class. It treats the sine squared lemma without a pole, the de Bruijn Newman flow for $\Delta$ with $0\le\Lambda_\Delta\le\tfrac18$, a Pólya kernel for imaginary quadratic fields that is positive for $d=-3,-4,-7,-8$ and takes negative values for infinitely many discriminants $d\equiv5\pmod{24}$, and the Thorin measures of $L(s,\chi_4)$ at every basepoint $\alpha\ge1$, with GRH equivalent to positivity of the Thorin density for $\alpha>\tfrac12$. A second part repeats the basepoint one analysis for $L(s,\chi_{12})$: Thorin measure, Lévy form without a pole, the hitting time and its Brownian boundary, compared side by side with $\zeta$.

#### From the literature

- The Dedekind eta function, Euler's pentagonal number theorem, and the modular form $\Delta$ with Ramanujan's $\tau$
- The Pólya route and the Pólya kernel for $\xi$ (Pólya 1926)
- De Bruijn's strip theorem for the heat flow (de Bruijn 1950) and the existence of the de Bruijn Newman constant for the extended Selberg class (Dobner 2021)
- Lagarias's positivity criterion for RH (Lagarias 1999), Thorin's and Bondesson's theory of GGCs (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992)
- The class number formula and the Hadamard product for $L$ functions (Davenport 2000)
- Bernstein's theorem on completely monotone functions

#### New results

Zero counts and boundary values are computed in floating point; the structural statements about kernels, maxima and Thorin measures are proved, and GRH statements are equivalences or conditional.

- [Max representation of the L function of Ramanujan's Delta](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#max_representation_of_ramanujan_delta_l_function) (Volume I, Theorem 15.1.2, page 389; proved): The completed L function of Ramanujan's cusp form Delta is the expectation of an incomplete gamma function at the random point 2 pi M*, where M* is a maximum of independent exponential variables, a representation with no signs. New in this book.
- [Gamma mixture and mixed Poisson forms of L values of Delta](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#gamma_mixture_and_mixed_poisson_forms_of_delta_l_values) (Volume I, Corollary 15.1.3, page 389; proved): For real s above minus 11/2 the L value of Ramanujan's Delta is the probability that a gamma variable exceeds 2 pi M*, and at the points s equal to k minus 11/2 it is a mixed Poisson probability. New in this book.
