- [L values of Delta and chi12 as infinitely divisible probabilities](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#delta_and_chi12_l_values_as_infinitely_divisible_probabilities) (Volume I, Proposition 15.1.7, page 394; proved): By Kristiansen's theorem on Gamma(2) mixtures and the theorem of Goldie and Steutel on exponential mixtures, the L values of Ramanujan's Delta at real s between minus 11/2 and minus 7/2 and of the character chi12 at real s between 0 and 4 are probabilities that an infinitely divisible variable exceeds one. New in this book.
- [RH is equivalent to a Gamma(k) scale mixture form of the clock canonical function, and the Kolmogorov law](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rh_iff_gamma_k_scale_mixture_and_kolmogorov_law_of_the_clock) (Volume I, Remark 15.1.8, page 394; proved): For every integer k at least one, the Riemann hypothesis holds if and only if t to the power k minus one times the canonical function of the clock is proportional to a scale mixture of Gamma(k) densities, with an explicit discrete mixing law under RH, infinitely divisible for k equal to one and two but not a GGC. New in this book.
- [Laplace transform of the maximum M1 of exponentials in closed form](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#laplace_transform_of_max_of_exponentials_m1_closed_form) (Volume I, Proposition 15.1.9, page 395; proved): The Laplace transform of the maximum of independent exponential variables with rates 2 pi n is an explicit ratio of a sine and a cosine, equal to an infinite product over the numbers b_n = pi (n squared minus 1)/12. New in this book.
- [A discrete mixture of Gamma(k) laws with two rates is not a GGC](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#discrete_mixture_of_gamma_k_laws_is_not_a_ggc) (Volume I, Result 15.1.8, page 395; proved): A finite or infinite discrete mixture of Gamma(k) laws with a positive integer k and at least two distinct rates is not a generalized gamma convolution. New in this book.
- [The completed zeta function as the Mellin transform of an infinitely divisible Gamma(2) mixture, not a GGC](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#completed_zeta_function_as_mellin_transform_of_a_kristiansen_law) (Volume I, Result 15.1.8, page 395; proved): With no hypothesis, the completed zeta function for real part of s above one is a normalised Mellin transform of a Gamma(2) scale mixture over the zeta law, which is infinitely divisible by Kristiansen's theorem and not a GGC. New in this book.
- [Rényi type decomposition of the maximum M1 of exponentials](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#renyi_type_decomposition_of_max_of_exponentials_m1) (Volume I, Corollary 15.1.10, page 396; proved): The maximum of independent exponential variables with rates 2 pi n is a sum of independent exponential variables whose rates are b_{6k-1} or b_{6k+1} with explicit probabilities p_k that decrease to one half. New in this book.
- [Lévy density and Bondesson function of the maximum M1](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#levy_density_and_bondesson_function_of_max_of_exponentials_m1) (Volume I, Proposition 15.1.12, page 397; proved): The Lévy density of the maximum M1 has an explicit theta function form with stated behaviour at zero and infinity, and its Bondesson function N_1 is nonnegative and grows like a constant times the square root of z. New in this book.
- [Thorin measure of M1 as a difference of two GGC Thorin measures](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_measure_of_m1_difference_of_two_ggc_thorin_measures) (Volume I, Theorem 15.1.13, page 398; proved): The maximum M1 plus an independent GGC Z has the law of a second GGC S, so the signed Thorin measure of M1 is the difference of two positive measures with unit atoms. New in this book.
- [Certified zeros of the Laplace transform of the maximum M* of exponentials](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#certified_zeros_of_laplace_transform_of_max_of_exponentials_m_star) (Volume I, Proposition 15.1.14, page 399; proved): Certified in ball arithmetic: the Laplace transform of M* changes sign in each of 25 gaps between its poles, and has exactly one zero near each of ten nonreal points, so it has zeros off the real axis. New in this book.
- [The maximum M* of exponentials is not in the Bondesson class](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#max_of_exponentials_m_star_not_in_bondesson_class) (Volume I, Corollary 15.1.15, page 400; proved): The maximum of independent exponential variables with 24 variables of each rate 2 pi n is not in the Bondesson class and so is not a GGC, because its Laplace transform has nonreal zeros. New in this book.
- [Open question on infinite divisibility of maxima of exponentials](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_infinite_divisibility_of_maxima_of_exponentials) (Volume I, Question 15.1.16, page 402; open): Is every maximum of independent exponential variables infinitely divisible, and in particular is the maximum M* with 24 variables of each rate 2 pi n? New in this book.
- [Open question on real zeros of cosh kernels with exponential multipliers](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_real_zeros_of_cosh_kernel_with_exponential_multiplier) (Volume I, Question 15.1.17, page 404; open): For which parameters does the Fourier transform of the kernel exp(-a cosh u) times an exponential multiplier have only real zeros, a form shared by the kernels of Ramanujan's Delta, chi12 and the conductor 11 curve? New in this book.
- [Pólya kernel of an imaginary quadratic field](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#polya_kernel_of_imaginary_quadratic_field) (Volume I, Theorem 15.1.18, page 406; proved): The completed Dedekind zeta function of an imaginary quadratic field is the two sided Laplace transform of an even doubly exponentially decaying kernel, which is positive exactly when a one variable function is positive on a finite interval, in particular for the discriminants minus 3, minus 4, minus 7 and minus 8. New in this book.
- [Pólya kernel of an imaginary quadratic field takes negative values when 2 and 3 are inert](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#polya_kernel_takes_negative_values_when_two_and_three_inert) (Volume I, Theorem 15.1.19, page 408; proved): For every negative fundamental discriminant d congruent to 5 modulo 24 the Pólya kernel of Q(sqrt d) takes negative values, by an explicit evaluation of a finite sum with a bounded tail, and there are infinitely many such d. New in this book.
- [Open question on the density of positive Pólya kernels](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_density_of_positive_polya_kernels_imaginary_quadratic) (Volume I, Question 15.1.20, page 409; open): Does the proportion of imaginary quadratic fields with a positive Pólya kernel tend to a limit, is the limit positive, and is the kernel positive for infinitely many fields in which 2 and 3 split? New in this book.
- [Open question on positivity criteria for real quadratic fields](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_positivity_criterion_polya_kernel_real_quadratic) (Volume I, Question 15.1.21, page 409; open): Is there a criterion for positivity of the Pólya kernel of the Dedekind zeta function of a real quadratic field or a field of higher degree that is as simple as the one for imaginary quadratic fields? New in this book.
- [Lévy form of the Dirichlet beta function at basepoints from one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#levy_form_of_dirichlet_beta_function_from_basepoint_one) (Volume I, Proposition 15.1.24, page 413; proved): The logarithm of the completed Dirichlet beta function at every basepoint alpha at least one has a Lévy form whose signed Lévy measure is an explicit positive gamma density plus prime power atoms of both signs. New in this book.
- [Thorin measure of the Dirichlet beta function from basepoint one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_measure_of_dirichlet_beta_function_from_basepoint_one) (Volume I, Proposition 15.1.25, page 415; proved): For every basepoint alpha at least one the reciprocal of the completed Dirichlet beta function is the Laplace transform of a GGC with a positive explicit Thorin density, and, by Lagarias's criterion, GRH for chi4 is equivalent to the positivity of that density at every alpha above one half. New in this book.
- [Termwise positivity thresholds for the Dirichlet beta function and chi12](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#termwise_positivity_thresholds_dirichlet_beta_and_chi12) (Volume I, Proposition 15.1.26, page 415; proved): Bounding the prime weights by their absolute values gives a positive Thorin density exactly for basepoints above 2.2823106368 for the Dirichlet beta function and above 1.8348743295 for chi12, thresholds located by bisection with certified signs. New in this book.
- [No bound from the sizes of the prime weights beats the absolute values](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#no_bound_from_prime_weight_sizes_beats_absolute_values_kronecker) (Volume I, Proposition 15.1.27, page 416; proved): By Kronecker's theorem no lower bound for the real part of L'/L of the Dirichlet beta function better than minus the sum of the absolute weights holds at all large heights, and the height from which the termwise bound works grows like e to the power 2/(alpha minus 1). New in this book.
- [Thorin density of the Dirichlet beta function as a difference over the Gaussian field](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_density_of_dirichlet_beta_as_difference_over_gaussian_field) (Volume I, Proposition 15.1.28, page 417; proved): On every vertical line the Thorin density of the Dirichlet beta function is the difference of the Thorin densities of the Dedekind zeta function of Q(i) and of Riemann's xi function, and the canonical measures subtract in the same way. New in this book.
- [GRH for chi4 and domination of Thorin densities over Q(i)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#grh_chi4_iff_gaussian_field_thorin_density_dominates_xi) (Volume I, Corollary 15.1.29, page 418; conditional on Part (iii) assumes the Riemann hypothesis for the Riemann zeta function; parts (i) and (ii) hold without any hypothesis): GRH for chi4 is equivalent to the Thorin density of the Dedekind zeta function of Q(i) dominating that of Riemann's xi at every basepoint, and for alpha at least one the GGC of Q(i) is the sum of independent GGCs for xi and for the Dirichlet beta function. New in this book.
- [Open question on a coupling construction over the Gaussian primes](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_coupling_construction_over_gaussian_primes) (Volume I, Question 15.1.30, page 419; open): Is there a construction of the GGC attached to Q(i) from the Gaussian primes themselves that persists below the basepoint one? New in this book.
- [Thorin mass of the Dirichlet beta function as an argument](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_mass_of_dirichlet_beta_as_argument_of_completed_function) (Volume I, Proposition 15.1.31, page 419; proved): On a vertical line the cumulative Thorin mass of the Dirichlet beta function is the argument of the completed function divided by pi, with an asymptotic expansion that becomes the zero counting formula at the centre and a limit that counts the zeros on the critical line. New in this book.
- [GRH for chi4 and monotonicity of the argument of the completed function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#grh_chi4_iff_argument_of_completed_function_nondecreasing) (Volume I, Corollary 15.1.32, page 420; proved): GRH for chi4 is equivalent to the argument of the completed Dirichlet beta function being nondecreasing on every line to the right of the centre, and without any hypothesis it can fall only in short windows around zeros off the line, none below height 2.5 times 10^7 by Platt's verification. New in this book.
- [The half kernel of the Dirichlet beta function is not a gamma mixture](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#half_kernel_of_dirichlet_beta_not_a_gamma_mixture) (Volume I, Proposition 15.1.33, page 421; proved): The half kernel of the Dirichlet beta function is not a positive mixture of gamma densities of any shape, and the theta function eta(ix) cubed is not completely monotone. New in this book.
- [Open question on a reciprocal side representation from the eta product](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_reciprocal_side_representation_from_eta_product) (Volume I, Question 15.1.34, page 422; open): Can the complete monotonicity of the reciprocal of the eta cube theta function, and of the reciprocal eta product for chi12, be turned into a positive representation on the reciprocal side in the spirit of Thorin? New in this book.
- [Thorin measure of the Dedekind eta analogue at the basepoint one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#eta_analogue_thorin_measure_positive_at_basepoint_one) (Volume I, Proposition 15.2.1, page 423; proved): For the L function of the real character modulo 12, the reciprocal completed function at the basepoint one is the Laplace transform of a GGC with an explicit positive Thorin density, with no hypothesis. New in this book.
- [Lévy form of the Dedekind eta analogue at the basepoint one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#eta_analogue_levy_form_at_basepoint_one) (Volume I, Proposition 15.2.2, page 424; proved): For the completed L function of the real character modulo 12, the logarithm of $\xi(1+s,\chi_{12})/\xi(1,\chi_{12})$ has an explicit Lévy form, with a positive gamma density and prime atoms of both signs, that needs no compensation by a pole term. New in this book.

#### Key terms

Dedekind eta function, eta kernel, L(s, chi_12), Dirichlet L function, real character modulo 12, Ramanujan's Delta, tau function, cusp form, GRH, generalised Riemann hypothesis, generalized Riemann hypothesis, product formula, maximum of exponentials, max representation, incomplete gamma function, Bondesson class, de Bruijn Newman constant, imaginary quadratic field, class number, Dirichlet beta function, Catalan's constant, Thorin measure, generalised gamma convolution, basepoint one, Lévy form, hitting time, Brownian boundary

chapters.title: Dirichlet L functions and the Linnik constant
chapters.summary:
Can the Thorin representation of the reciprocal of the Riemann xi function be carried to Dirichlet $L$ functions and Dedekind zeta functions of number fields, and does it help with Linnik's constant $K$, the number of powers of two needed with two primes to represent every large even integer? The chapter proves that the reciprocal of a completed Dedekind zeta function, tilted by $u_0\ge0$, is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) exactly when every nontrivial zero lies on the critical line or is a real zero within $\sqrt{u_0}$ of the centre (with no central zero at $u_0=0$), the Thorin measure being the shifted zero counting measure. For all cyclotomic fields together, the Thorin property at the centre is equivalent to the generalised Riemann hypothesis (GRH) for all Dirichlet $L$ functions that do not vanish at the centre, and this yields only the GRH value $K=7$. The chapter also treats the centre clock of $\xi$ (moments, transfer function, negative moments), the master theorem route, the sine squared lemma, real and complex characters, and mixtures of characters, which are not GGCs in general. It lists open problems. Nothing here proves RH or lowers $K$. Statements are proved unless marked conditional on RH, GRH or GRH with nonvanishing at the centre.

#### From the literature

- Linnik's theorem (Linnik 1951, 1953) and the records $K=8$ unconditionally (Pintz and Ruzsa 2020) and $K=7$ under GRH (Heath-Brown and Puchta 2002; Pintz and Ruzsa 2003)
- Gallagher's circle method (Gallagher 1975); the zero free regions of Iwaniec and of Vinogradov (1958); symmetry types of families (Katz and Sarnak 1999)
- generalised gamma convolutions (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992, 2015); the Riemann zeta distribution (Khinchin 1938; Lin and Hu 2001); the mean value theorems of Carlson and Ingham (see Titchmarsh 1986)
- the master theorem class (Chaudhry and Qadir 2012); an exponential Tauberian theorem (Kasahara 1978); Dedekind zeta functions with a zero at the centre (Armitage 1971)
- the Thorin framework (Polson 2018, 2026) and the sine squared lemma (Polson 2017, 2026); the sign criterion for RH (Lagarias 1999); RH as a Pólya frequency property (Schoenberg 1951; Konstantopoulos, Patie and Sarkar 2024)
- a zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$, announced and not refereed (OpenAI 2026)

#### New results

Statements are proved unless marked conditional; the Linnik constant corollary is weaker than the known result under GRH; the problems are open.

- [Thorin property of the tilted clock of a Dedekind zeta function at every tilt: equivalence with the position of the zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_property_of_tilted_dedekind_zeta_clock_at_every_tilt) (Volume I, Theorem 16.2.3, page 436; proved): For a number field and a tilt $u_0\ge0$, the tilted reciprocal of the completed Dedekind zeta function is a GGC exactly when every nontrivial zero lies on the critical line or is real at distance less than $\sqrt{u_0}$ from the centre (with no central zero when $u_0=0$), and its Thorin measure is then the zero counting measure shifted by $u_0$. New in this book.
- [The tilts: Thorin property of a Dedekind zeta clock at tilt zero and at tilts above one quarter, the Thorin threshold and the shift between tilts](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_property_of_dedekind_clock_at_tilt_zero_and_above_one_quarter_threshold_and_shift) (Volume I, Corollary 16.2.4, page 437; proved): The Thorin property of a Dedekind zeta function holds at every tilt $u_0\ge\frac14$ exactly when all nontrivial zeros are on the critical line or the real axis, at tilt $0$ exactly when they are all on the critical line with $\zeta_F(\frac12)\ne0$, and, when all nonreal zeros are on the line, exactly above a threshold set by the real zero farthest from the centre, with the Thorin measures at two tilts shifts of one another. New in this book.
- [Closed form of the transfer function from the real axis to the critical line under RH, and its odd index power sum expansion](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#transfer_function_from_real_axis_to_critical_line_is_product_over_ordinates_under_rh) (Volume I, Proposition 16.3.6, page 443; conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part $\frac12$): Under RH the transfer function $\xi(\frac12+it)/\xi(\frac12+|t|)$ equals $\prod_{\gamma>0}(\gamma^2-t^2)/(\gamma^2+t^2)$, is real, even, bounded by $1$ and vanishes exactly at the ordinates, and its logarithm near $0$ involves only the odd index power sums of the inverse squared ordinates. New in this book.
- [The odd index power sums of the inverse squared ordinates determine the zeros under RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#odd_index_power_sums_of_inverse_squared_ordinates_determine_all_zeros_under_rh) (Volume I, Proposition 16.3.7, page 443; conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part $\frac12$): Under RH the generating series of the odd index power sums $p_1,p_3,p_5,\dots$ of the inverse squared ordinates continues to a meromorphic function with poles at the points $\pm\gamma^2$, so these sums determine the ordinates with multiplicities and with them every power sum. New in this book.
- [The transfer function as a Blaschke product for the right half plane under RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#transfer_function_is_blaschke_product_for_right_half_plane_under_rh) (Volume I, Proposition 16.3.8, page 443; conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part $\frac12$): Under RH the function $\mathfrak B(z)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(\gamma^2-z)/(\gamma^2+z)$, with $\mathfrak T(t)=\mathfrak B(t^2)$ for the transfer function $\mathfrak T$, is a Blaschke product for the right half plane with zeros at the points $\gamma^2$ and no singular inner factor. New in this book.
- [Negative moments of the centre clock as a Mellin transform of the reciprocal of xi on the real axis](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#negative_moments_of_centre_clock_as_mellin_transform_of_reciprocal_xi) (Volume I, Proposition 16.3.10, page 444; proved): For $\operatorname{Re}s>0$ the negative moment $\mathbb{E}[T^{-s}]$ of the centre clock of $\xi$ is the Mellin transform of $\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u)$ divided by $\Gamma(s)$, with no hypothesis on the zeros. New in this book.
- [Growth of the gamma function times the reciprocal of xi on vertical strips under RH: the growth hypothesis of the master theorem class](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#growth_of_gamma_times_reciprocal_xi_on_vertical_strips_in_the_critical_strip_under_rh) (Volume I, Lemma 16.4.1, page 447; conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis, used through the bound $1/\zeta(w)=O(|\operatorname{Im}w|^\eta)$ on $\operatorname{Re}w\ge\frac12+\sigma_1$ for every $\eta>0$): Under RH, on vertical strips $0<\sigma_1\le\operatorname{Re}s\le\sigma_2<\frac12$ the function $\Gamma(s)\,\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+s)$ is bounded by $C_\eta e^{-\pi|\tau|/4}|\tau|^{\sigma/2-9/4+\eta}$, which verifies the growth hypothesis of the master theorem class with exponential room, but a bound proved under RH cannot be an input to a proof of the Thorin property. New in this book.
- [Absolute convergence hypothesis of the master theorem route for the reciprocal of xi holds without RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#absolute_convergence_hypothesis_of_master_theorem_route_holds_for_reciprocal_xi_without_rh) (Volume I, Lemma 16.4.2, page 447; proved): With no hypothesis on the zeros, the series $\mathfrak R(w)=\sum_{k\ge1}b_kw^k$ built from $\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+k)$ is entire of order $\frac23$ and its integral against the density of the centre clock converges for every $z>0$, which is the absolute convergence needed to interchange sum and integral in the master theorem route. New in this book.
- [The reciprocal Xi function in the shifted variable lies in Hardy's class with no hypothesis on the zeros, so the master theorem carries no information on them](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#hardy_class_master_theorem_for_reciprocal_xi_in_shifted_variable_holds_and_is_empty) (Volume I, Proposition 16.4.3, page 448; proved): The function $\xi(\frac32)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt{1+w})$ is analytic and bounded on $\operatorname{Re}w\ge-\delta$ for $0<\delta<1$, hence in Hardy's class unconditionally, and the image region contains no zero of $\xi$, so Ramanujan's master theorem in this variable says nothing about the zeros. New in this book.
- [Why the square root stays: reciprocal Xi function in the variable s is not a Laplace transform of a random variable, and its values on a vertical line are not a characteristic function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_xi_is_not_laplace_transform_of_any_random_variable_and_not_characteristic_function) (Volume I, Theorem 16.4.4, page 449; proved): For every real $\alpha$ the function $s\mapsto\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+s)$ is not the Laplace transform of any real random variable, whether or not RH holds, the function $t\mapsto\xi(\alpha+it)/\xi(\alpha)$ is a characteristic function that is never infinitely divisible, and $t\mapsto\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+it)$ is unbounded. New in this book.
- [Thorin representation of the reciprocal of the completed Dirichlet L function of a real primitive character under GRH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_representation_of_reciprocal_completed_l_function_of_real_character_under_grh) (Volume I, Proposition 16.5.1, page 450; conditional on The generalized Riemann hypothesis for $L(s,\chi)$ (every nontrivial zero has real part $\frac12$) and $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$ (Chowla's conjecture for real characters, open)): For a real primitive character $\chi$, under GRH for $L(s,\chi)$ and $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$, the reciprocal $\xi(\frac12,\chi)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u,\chi)$ is the Laplace transform of the GGC $\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ over the ordinates of the zeros, and the clock identities of the Riemann case carry over. New in this book.
- [Thorin representation for a complex character through the product of the completed L function with its conjugate, under GRH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_representation_of_product_of_conjugate_completed_l_functions_of_complex_character_under_grh) (Volume I, Proposition 16.5.2, page 451; conditional on The generalized Riemann hypothesis for $L(s,\chi)$ (every nontrivial zero has real part $\frac12$) and $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$): For a complex primitive character $\chi$, the product $\xi(s,\chi)\xi(s,\bar\chi)$ is symmetric under $s\mapsto1-s$, and under GRH for $L(s,\chi)$ with $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$ the reciprocal of its ratio to the centre is the Laplace transform of the GGC $\sum e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ over all ordinates of $L(s,\chi)$ of both signs. New in this book.
- [Factorisation of the completed Dedekind zeta function of a quadratic field and clocks of cyclotomic fields as independent sums](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#completed_dedekind_zeta_of_quadratic_field_factors_and_clocks_of_cyclotomic_fields_add) (Volume I, Proposition 16.5.3, page 452; conditional on The statement on cyclotomic fields assumes GRH for the Dirichlet $L$ functions of the nonprincipal primitive characters of conductor dividing $q$ and that their values at $\frac12$ are nonzero (the hypotheses of the propositions on real and complex characters). The factorisations of the completed functions hold without any hypothesis, and the statement for quadratic fields is an implication from the Thorin property of the two factors at the tilt considered): For a quadratic field the completed Dedekind zeta function is $2\xi(s)\xi(s,\chi)$ (times $q^{-1/2}$ for odd $\chi$), so at a tilt where both factors have the Thorin property the tilted clock is the independent sum of theirs and the Thorin measures add, and for cyclotomic fields, under GRH with nonzero central values, the clock is the independent sum of the clocks of $\zeta$ and of the nonprincipal primitive characters of conductor dividing $q$. New in this book.
- [Lévy decomposition of the logarithm of the completed Dedekind zeta function of any number field, with signs](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#signed_levy_decomposition_of_log_completed_dedekind_zeta_function_with_negative_density) (Volume I, Proposition 16.5.4, page 453; proved): For $\alpha>1$ the compensated logarithm of $\xi_F(\alpha+s)/\xi_F(\alpha)$ is an integral against a signed Lévy measure whose arithmetic part has the positive weights $\Lambda_F(n)$ at $\log n$, plus gamma factor densities and the single negative density $-(1+e^x)$ coming from the factor $s(s-1)$. New in this book.
- [The sine squared lemma on the prime side for Dedekind zeta functions and real Dirichlet characters](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#sine_squared_lemma_for_dedekind_zeta_functions_and_real_dirichlet_characters) (Volume I, Proposition 16.5.6, page 454; proved): For $\alpha>1$ and $f$ the completed Dedekind zeta function of a number field or the completed $L$ function of a real primitive character, the reciprocal $f(\alpha)/f(\alpha+\sqrt u)$ equals $\exp(-\int_0^\infty\log(1+u/b^2)\,v_\alpha(b)\,db/\pi)$ with $v_\alpha(b)=\operatorname{Re}(f'/f)(\alpha+ib)$ written through a sine squared transform of the Lévy measure (Polson's sine squared lemma applied to $f$), so that the density is determined by the primes with no reference to the zeros. New in this book.
- [The basepoint family of the sine squared lemma: Thorin property at a basepoint to the right of all zeros, failure when a zero lies to the right, and the Poisson form under GRH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#basepoint_family_thorin_property_for_dedekind_zeta_functions_and_real_characters_holds_left_of_all_zeros) (Volume I, Theorem 16.5.8, page 455; conditional on Part (c) assumes GRH for $f$ (every zero has real part $\frac12$) and $f(\frac12)\ne0$. Parts (a) and (b) hold without any hypothesis, and part (a) holds unconditionally for every $\alpha\ge1$): For the completed Dedekind zeta function of a number field or the completed $L$ function of a real primitive character, the reciprocal $f(\alpha)/f(\alpha+\sqrt u)$ is a GGC with a positive Thorin density that is a sum over the zeros when every zero lies to the left of $\alpha$ (so unconditionally for $\alpha\ge1$), is not a GGC transform when a zero lies to the right, and under GRH the density is the Poisson smoothing of the zero counting measure at height $\alpha-\frac12$. New in this book.
- [GRH and nonvanishing at the centre from the Thorin property of the Dedekind zeta functions of quadratic and cyclotomic fields](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_property_of_quadratic_and_cyclotomic_dedekind_zeta_functions_implies_grh_and_central_nonvanishing) (Volume I, Theorem 16.6.1, page 459; proved): If the tilted reciprocal of the Dedekind zeta function of a quadratic field is a GGC at tilt $1$, then RH holds and the zeros of the Dirichlet $L$ function are on the critical line or real; if it is a GGC at tilt $0$, then GRH holds for that $L$ function with $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$; and if this holds at tilt $0$ for every cyclotomic field, then GRH holds for all Dirichlet $L$ functions with all central values nonzero. New in this book.
- [Mixtures of clocks: a mixture of two GGC Laplace transforms with discrete unit atom Thorin measures is not a GGC transform when it vanishes off the atoms, in particular in the odd configuration](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#mixtures_of_ggc_laplace_transforms_with_unit_atom_thorin_measures_are_not_ggc_in_odd_configuration) (Volume I, Proposition 16.6.3, page 462; proved): A mixture $\lambda\varphi_1+(1-\lambda)\varphi_2$ of two GGC Laplace transforms whose Thorin measures are sums of unit point masses is not a GGC transform if it vanishes at a negative point that is not an atom, and this happens for every weight $\lambda$ when two consecutive atoms of the union belong to different measures and an odd number of atoms lie at or below the first of them. New in this book.
- [The family of characters modulo 5: no mixture of the two clocks is a GGC, under GRH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#family_modulo_five_mixture_of_clocks_is_not_ggc_under_grh) (Volume I, Proposition 16.6.4, page 463; conditional on The generalized Riemann hypothesis for $L(s,\chi_5)$ and for $L(s,\psi)$ (every nontrivial zero has real part $\frac12$). The values $L(\frac12,\chi_5)$ and $L(\frac12,\psi)$ are certified nonzero, and the zeros below height $12$ are certified, in ball arithmetic; neither is assumed): Under GRH for the two members of the family of primitive characters modulo $5$, no mixture of their clocks, the uniform one included, is a GGC, because certified zero counts below height $12$ put their Thorin atoms in the odd configuration of the mixture criterion. New in this book.
- [A real zero of a Dirichlet L function makes the first rung of the twisted heat trace fail beyond an explicit time](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#real_zero_of_dirichlet_l_function_makes_first_rung_of_twisted_heat_trace_fail) (Volume I, Proposition 16.6.6, page 465; proved): If $L(s,\chi)$ of a primitive real character has a real zero $\beta$ in $(\tfrac12,1)$ and all its nonreal zeros lie on the critical line, the twisted heat trace grows and is increasing beyond an explicit time $t_1$, so it is not completely monotone, already at order one. New in this book.
- [Linnik constant seven from the Thorin property of all cyclotomic fields (weaker than the known result under GRH)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#seven_powers_of_two_from_thorin_property_of_all_cyclotomic_fields) (Volume I, Corollary 16.7.1, page 466; conditional on The Thorin property at tilt $0$ for every cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_q)$, $q\ge3$, which by the equivalence theorem of the chapter is GRH for all Dirichlet $L$ functions together with $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$ for every primitive character $\chi$. The proof uses only the GRH part, through the theorem of Heath-Brown and Puchta (2002) that GRH gives seven powers of two): If the centre clock of every cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_q)$, $q\ge3$, is a GGC, then every sufficiently large even integer is a sum of two primes and at most seven powers of two, which is the value that GRH already gives, so the corollary is weaker than the theorem of Heath-Brown and Puchta (2002), also proved by Pintz and Ruzsa (2003), that GRH alone gives seven, because it assumes nonvanishing at the centre as well. New in this book.
- [Open problem: the Thorin property of the Riemann clock and of cyclotomic clocks without first knowing the zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_thorin_property_of_reciprocal_xi_and_cyclotomic_clocks_without_knowing_the_zeros) (Volume I, Problem 16.1, page 467; open): Prove that the tilted reciprocal of the completed zeta function of $\mathbb{Q}$, or of a cyclotomic field, is the Laplace transform of a GGC without first knowing the zeros, in particular by settling the parabolic distortion in the master theorem route; for $\mathbb{Q}$ at the centre this is RH itself. New in this book.
- [Open problem: seven powers of two from GRH with possible real zeros, that is from the Thorin property at tilt one for cyclotomic fields](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_seven_powers_of_two_from_grh_with_possible_real_zeros) (Volume I, Problem 16.2, page 468; open): Show that every sufficiently large even integer is a sum of two primes and at most seven powers of two from the weaker hypothesis that every nontrivial zero of every Dirichlet $L$ function lies on the critical line or on the real axis, which would make real and Siegel zeros irrelevant to this value. New in this book.
- [Open problem: the anchored tail of the moment identity of the centre clock at large height and for Dirichlet L functions](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_anchored_tail_of_the_moment_identity_at_large_height_and_for_l_functions) (Volume I, Problem 16.3, page 468; open): Carry the anchored tail of the zero side of the moment identity of the centre clock to large height with tables of zeros of zeta, where the remaining integral of the zero count fluctuation sets the limit and calls for an explicit formula, and to Dirichlet $L$ functions. New in this book.
- [Open problem: the negative moment of the clock averaged over real characters of conductor in [Q,2Q] against the symplectic random matrix prediction](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_negative_moment_of_the_clock_as_a_family_statistic_and_symplectic_prediction) (Volume I, Problem 16.4, page 468; open): Compute the average of the negative moment $\mathbb{E}[T_\chi^{-1/2}]$ of the clock over real primitive characters of conductor in $[Q,2Q]$ and compare it with the prediction of the symplectic ensemble, noting that this moment is not a linear statistic of the zeros. New in this book.
- [Open problem: infinite divisibility of the family mixture of the clocks of the characters modulo q](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_infinite_divisibility_of_the_family_mixture_of_clocks_of_dirichlet_characters) (Volume I, Problem 16.5, page 469; open): Decide whether the clock of a uniformly chosen character of the family modulo $q$ is infinitely divisible, and whether some $q$ with two or more members avoids the odd configuration of the mixture criterion for every pair of members. New in this book.
- [Open problem: a sign definite explicit formula for primes in the progressions a modulo q with a not congruent to 1](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_sign_definite_explicit_formula_for_primes_in_progressions_not_congruent_to_one) (Volume I, Problem 16.6, page 469; open): Find a sign definite explicit formula for $\psi(x;q,a)$ with $a\not\equiv1\pmod q$ in terms of the zero counting measures of cyclotomic fields and their Poisson smoothings, for which the case $a\equiv1$ is already an integral against a nonnegative measure under the Thorin property. New in this book.
- [Open problem: certified backward continuation of the Thorin density of the basepoint family from the primes into the critical strip](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_certified_backward_continuation_of_the_thorin_density_from_the_primes) (Volume I, Problem 16.7, page 469; open): Determine how far into the critical strip positivity of the Thorin density $\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(f'/f)(\alpha+ib)$ can be certified from smoothed prime sums alone before the ill posedness of the backward step takes over. New in this book.
- [Open problem: the exponential sum over primes on the minor arcs as an expectation against the GGC laws of the clocks](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_exponential_sum_over_primes_on_the_minor_arcs_as_an_expectation_against_ggc_laws) (Volume I, Problem 16.8, page 470; open): Decide whether the exponential sum over primes on the minor arcs of the circle method for Linnik's problem can be written as an expectation against the GGC laws of the clocks, which would give a different route to the supremum bound on the minor arcs. New in this book.
- [Open problem: the best minor arc exponent in Linnik's problem from a zero free half plane for all Dirichlet L functions](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_best_minor_arc_exponent_in_linnik_problem_from_a_zero_free_half_plane) (Volume I, Problem 16.9, page 470; open): Under a zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta_0$ for all Dirichlet $L$ functions, find the best minor arc exponent for the sum over primes in Linnik's problem, and decide whether the half plane improves the large deviation parameter for the powers of two or the major arc constant. New in this book.
- [Open problem: does a finite order of total positivity of the density force the zeros onto the line, in a class of even entire functions containing xi](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_finite_order_total_positivity_forcing_real_zeros_in_a_class_of_entire_functions) (Volume I, Problem 16.10, page 470; open): Decide whether some finite order of total positivity of the density $f_F$ forces every zero of $F$ onto the imaginary axis, for every $F$ in the class of even entire functions with the order, type and reflection symmetry of $\xi(\frac12+s)/\xi(\frac12)$ whose reciprocal is a characteristic function. New in this book.
