chapters.title: Completeness of the secant dilates and the Möbius problem
chapters.summary:
Are the integer dilates of the hyperbolic secant complete in weighted spaces of functions, and what does this say about the zeros of the Dirichlet beta function and the Möbius problem? The chapter studies completeness of dilates of the secant, Fermi, Bose and Meixner kernels in the weighted $L^1$ spaces $W_c$. It proves that integer dilates of the secant are complete in $L^1$, that the Möbius secant series converges to the exponential in every weight with $c\ge1$ (using the prime number theorem for $\mu\chi_4$ at $c=1$), and that over any set of dilations with divergent reciprocal sum the dilates are complete in one weight whatever the zeros do. Completeness in two weights is equivalent to a zero free half plane for $L(s,\chi_4)$ and to convergence of the Möbius series, and a polynomial bound on the reciprocal of the beta function gives non completeness when the reciprocal sum converges. Salem's criterion in $L^1$ is proved for the Fermi and secant kernels, the zeta analogue holds for the Bose kernel with its pole removed, symmetric Meixner densities have complete dilates, and the cosecant kernel gives an unconditional Möbius series. Explicit approximants in one weight, a sharpness experiment, the Thorin form of the two weight criterion and open problems are included. A zero free half plane for Xi is equivalent to a reciprocal Xi transform being a generalised gamma convolution (GGC), with Cauchy law Thorin measures forming a semigroup. Results for $c$ above $7/8$ are conditional on the zero free half plane of the October 2026 quasi Riemann hypothesis preprints, which are not refereed.

#### From the literature

- Wiener's Tauberian theorem (Wiener 1932) in its homogeneous form (Kac 1965)
- Salem's equivalent of the Riemann Hypothesis in terms of dilates (Salem 1953)
- The Nyman and Beurling approximation problem, in the strengthening of Báez Duarte (2003) and the lower bound of Burnol (2002)
- The Meixner hypergeometric distribution (Lai and Vere Jones 1979)
- Generalised gamma convolutions (Bondesson 1992), and the Mellin transform and zero free regions (Titchmarsh 1939, Davenport 2000)
- Zero free half plane claims, unrefereed and unchecked here (OpenAI 2026, Liu 2026, Thorner 2026)

#### New results

The completeness theorems in one weight are proved without hypothesis; statements about two weights are equivalences with a zero free half plane, and those above $7/8$ are conditional.

- [The integer dilates of the hyperbolic secant are complete in L1 under an integrability condition at the origin and at infinity](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#completeness_of_the_secant_dilates_in_l1_with_the_weight_of_lerch) (Volume I, Theorem 17.1.4, page 475; proved): If $g$ satisfies $\int_0^1|g(x)|/x\,dx+\int_1^\infty|g(x)|e^{-x}dx<\infty$ and $\int_0^\infty g(x)\operatorname{sech}(nx)\,dx=0$ for all $n\in\mathbb N$ then $g=0$ almost everywhere, from the M\"obius identity $e^{-x}=\frac12\sum\mu(n)\chi_4(n)\operatorname{sech}(nx)$ and Lerch's theorem. New in this book.
- [The Möbius secant series converges to the exponential in every weight W_c with c at least one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#mobius_secant_series_converges_in_every_weight_with_c_at_least_one) (Volume I, Theorem 17.2.2, page 477; proved): For $c\ge1$, $S_N\to e^{-x}$ in $\mathcal W_c$: dominated convergence for $c>1$, and the prime number theorem for $\mu\chi_4$ with partial summation at $c=1$. New in this book.
- [In one weight the secant dilates over any set of dilations with divergent reciprocal sum are complete, whatever the zeros of the beta function do](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#single_weight_completeness_of_secant_dilates_is_unconditional_by_carleman) (Volume I, Theorem 17.3.2, page 478; proved): For $c>0$ and $\Lambda\subset[1,\infty)$ with $\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}1/\lambda=\infty$, $\{\operatorname{sech}(\lambda x)\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ is complete in $\mathcal W_c$, unconditionally, in particular for the integer dilates and the prime dilates, at $c=\frac12$ included; the proof is Carleman's formula for a half plane and uses no arithmetic. New in this book.
- [Completeness of the exponential in two weights forces a zero free strip for the beta function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#two_weight_necessity_zero_free_strip_for_the_beta_function) (Volume I, Proposition 17.5.1, page 480; proved): If $e^{-x}$ is a limit in $\mathcal W_a\cap\mathcal W_b$ of finite combinations of $\operatorname{sech}(nx)$ then $\beta(s)\ne0$ for $a<\Re s<b$, because point evaluation of the Mellin transform is continuous in the strip. New in this book.
- [Two weight completeness of the secant dilates is equivalent to a zero free half plane for L(s,chi_4) and to convergence of the Möbius secant series](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#two_weight_criterion_zero_free_half_plane_for_the_beta_function) (Volume I, Theorem 17.5.2, page 480; proved): For $\frac12\le\theta<1$ the following are equivalent: $L(s,\chi_4)\ne0$ for $\Re s>\theta$; $\{\operatorname{sech}(nx)\}$ is complete in $\mathcal W_a\cap\mathcal W_b$ for all $\theta<a<b<1$; $S_N\to e^{-x}$ in $\mathcal W_c$ for every $c\in(\theta,1)$. With $\theta=\frac12$ the first is the generalised Riemann hypothesis for $L(s,\chi_4)$. New in this book.
- [The zeta analogue: dilates of the Bose kernel with its pole removed are complete in one weight and in two weights exactly when zeta has the corresponding zero free half plane](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#zeta_version_one_weight_completeness_and_two_weight_criterion_for_the_bose_kernel) (Volume I, Theorem 17.6.1, page 481; proved): For $\varphi(x)=1/(e^x-1)-1/x$: (1) $\{\varphi(nx)\}$ is complete in $\mathcal W_c$ for every $c\in(0,1)$; (2) $M(x)=O(x^{\theta+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ gives $\|T_N-e^{-x}\|_c=O(N^{\theta-c+\varepsilon})$ for $\theta<c<1$; (3) two weight completeness for all $\theta<a<b<1$ is equivalent to $\zeta(s)\ne0$ for $\Re s>\theta$, and for $\theta=\frac12$ to the Riemann hypothesis. New in this book.
- [Under a polynomial bound for the reciprocal of the beta function on the line, the secant dilates over a set with convergent reciprocal sum are not complete](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#necessity_of_the_divergence_condition_for_completeness_in_one_weight) (Volume I, Theorem 17.10.2, page 484; proved): Let $c>0$ with $1/\beta(c+it)\ll(1+|t|)^A$ for some $A\ge0$. If $\Lambda\subset[1,\infty)$ has $\sum_\Lambda1/\lambda<\infty$ then $\{\operatorname{sech}(\lambda x)\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ is not complete in $\mathcal W_c$, so under the bound completeness holds if and only if $\sum_\Lambda1/\lambda=\infty$. The line $c=\frac12$ is not covered and stays open. New in this book.
- [The secant dilates are complete in W_c if and only if the reciprocal sum of the dilations diverges, for c at least one, for c above 7/8 given a zero free half plane, and for c not one half under GRH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#necessity_and_sufficiency_of_divergent_reciprocal_sum_for_the_secant_dilates_conditional) (Volume I, Corollary 17.10.3, page 485; conditional on The zero free half plane $\Re s>\frac78$ for $L(s,\chi_4)$, which holds if the quasi Riemann hypothesis preprints (OpenAI, announced for Dirichlet $L$ functions, unrefereed and not checked for this book) cover the character modulo $4$; the part for $c\ge1$ is unconditional, and the part for $c\ne\frac12$ needs the generalised Riemann hypothesis for $\beta$): For $c\ge1$ (unconditional), for $c>\frac78$ given the zero free half plane $\Re s>\frac78$ for $L(s,\chi_4)$, and for every $c>0$, $c\ne\frac12$, under the generalised Riemann hypothesis for $\beta$: $\{\operatorname{sech}(\lambda x)\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ is complete in $\mathcal W_c$ if and only if $\sum_\Lambda1/\lambda=\infty$. New in this book.
- [Salem's criterion in L1: dilates of the Fermi or secant kernel over a divergent set are complete if and only if the Mellin transform has no zero on the line](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#salem_criterion_for_the_fermi_and_secant_kernels_on_a_divergent_set_of_dilations) (Volume I, Theorem 17.11.1, page 486; proved): For $\sigma>0$, $k\in\{1/(e^x+1),\operatorname{sech}x\}$ and $\Lambda\subset[1,\infty)$ with $\sum_\Lambda1/\lambda=\infty$, $\{x^{\sigma-1}k(\lambda x)\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ is complete in $L^1(0,\infty)$ if and only if the Mellin transform of $k$ has no zero on $\Re s=\sigma$; for $\frac12<\sigma<1$ this is zero freeness of $\zeta$, respectively $\beta$, on that line. New in this book.
- [The weighted error of an arbitrary combination of secant dilates is an integral over the Mellin line with the factor 2 in 2D_N - 1/beta, split at a segment](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#residual_identity_for_the_weighted_error_of_arbitrary_secant_combinations) (Volume I, Proposition 17.12.1, page 489; proved): For $c>0$, $T\ge1$ and any coefficients $a_n$, $\|e^{-x}-\sum_{n\le N}a_n\operatorname{sech}(nx)\|_c^2=\frac1{2\pi}\int|\Gamma(c+it)|^2|1-2\beta D_N|^2dt$, which is at most the integral over $|t|\le T$ plus $C_ce^{-\pi T}T^{2c}(1+\|a\|_{N,c})^2$; where $\beta\ne0$ the integrand is $|K_c(t)|^2|2D_N-1/\beta|^2$, with the factor $2$ and not $D_N-1/\beta$. New in this book.
- [The Mellin transform of the symmetric Meixner density of order t is an explicit multiple of an entire Dirichlet type series Z_t](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#mellin_transform_of_the_meixner_density_in_terms_of_an_entire_dirichlet_type_series) (Volume I, Theorem 17.13.1, page 490; proved): For $0<\Re s<1$, $M_t(s)=\int_0^\infty x^{s-1}|\Gamma(\frac t2+\frac{ix}2)|^2dx=2^s\pi\Gamma(t)Z_t(1-s)/\sin(\pi s/2)$ with $Z_t$ entire, $Z_1(w)=2^w\beta(w)$, $Z_2(w)=\eta(w-1)$, $Z_3(w)=2^{w-3}(\beta(w)-\beta(w-2))$. New in this book.
- [The dilates of every symmetric Meixner density are complete in every weight over a set of dilations with divergent reciprocal sum](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#one_weight_completeness_throughout_the_meixner_family) (Volume I, Corollary 17.13.2, page 492; proved): For every $t>0$ and $c>0$, $\{f_t(\lambda x)\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ with $\Lambda\subset[1,\infty)$ and $\sum_\Lambda1/\lambda=\infty$ is complete in $\mathcal W_c$, in particular for the integer dilates. New in this book.
- [For the cosecant kernel the Möbius series for x e^{-x} converges in every weight, so completeness holds unconditionally in one and two weights](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#order_two_meixner_kernel_gives_an_unconditional_mobius_route) (Volume I, Theorem 17.13.3, page 493; proved): With $c_n=\mu(n)$ for odd $n$ and $0$ for even $n$, $e^{-x}=\frac12\sum c_n\operatorname{csch}(nx)$ and $xe^{-x}=\frac12\sum(c_n/n)(nx)\operatorname{csch}(nx)$ with absolute convergence for $x>0$; the second series converges in every $\mathcal W_c$, $c>0$, and $\{(nx)\operatorname{csch}(nx)\}$ is complete in every $\mathcal W_c$ and every $\mathcal W_a\cap\mathcal W_b$, unconditionally. New in this book.
- [A zero free half plane for Xi is equivalent to F_theta being a GGC Laplace transform, with Thorin measure a sum of squared folded Cauchy laws centred at the ordinates](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_form_of_the_two_weight_criterion_for_the_reciprocal_xi_function) (Volume I, Theorem 17.14.2, page 494; proved): For $\theta\ge\frac12$, $\Xi$ has no zeros in $\Re s>\theta$ if and only if $F_\theta(s)=\Xi(\theta)/\Xi(\theta+\sqrt s)$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC, if and only if $F_\theta$ is analytic in the cut plane, and then the Thorin measure is $U_\theta=\sum_{\Im\rho>0}m_\rho Q_{\theta-\Re\rho,\Im\rho}$ with no linear term; for $\Xi=\xi(\cdot,\chi_4)$ this is two weight completeness of the secant dilates on $(\theta,1)$, for $\Xi=\xi$ of the dilates of $\varphi$. New in this book.
- [Reciprocal xi and reciprocal xi of chi_4 are GGC Laplace transforms from theta equal to one unconditionally and from 7/8 given the zero free half plane](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_representations_of_reciprocal_xi_above_the_zero_free_abscissa) (Volume I, Corollary 17.14.3, page 495; conditional on The zero free half plane $\Re s>\frac78$ for the Riemann zeta function and, for the statement about $\xi(\cdot,\chi_4)$, for $L(s,\chi_4)$, from the quasi Riemann hypothesis preprints (OpenAI, unrefereed, announced for Dirichlet $L$ functions; that the theorem covers the character modulo $4$ has not been checked); the part for $\theta\ge1$ is unconditional): For every $\theta\ge1$, $\xi(\theta)/\xi(\theta+\sqrt s)$ and $\xi(\theta,\chi_4)/\xi(\theta+\sqrt s,\chi_4)$ are Laplace transforms of GGCs with absolutely continuous Thorin measure $U_\theta$; given the zero free half plane $\Re s>\frac78$ this holds for every $\theta\ge\frac78$, with an atom $m_\rho\delta_{\gamma_\rho^2}$ at $\theta=\frac78$ for a zero on $\Re s=\frac78$; for $\theta=\frac12$ and $\xi$ it is the Riemann hypothesis. New in this book.
- [The symmetrised Thorin measures of F_theta form a Cauchy convolution semigroup in theta](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#cauchy_semigroup_of_thorin_measures_of_the_reciprocal_xi_function) (Volume I, Theorem 17.14.4, page 496; proved): If $\Xi$ has no zeros in $\Re s>\theta_0$, then $\widetilde U_\theta=\frac12\sum_\rho m_\rho\,\mathrm{Cauchy}(\Im\rho,\theta-\Re\rho)$, with the factor $\frac12$, maps to $U_\theta$ under $v\mapsto v^2$ and $\widetilde U_{\theta'}=\widetilde U_\theta*\mathrm{Cauchy}(0,\theta'-\theta)$ for $\theta_0\le\theta<\theta'$; for $\xi$ this is the Cauchy flow of the book's Poisson structure, credited to Polson (Chapter 8 of his monograph On Hilbert's 8th Problem, 2026). New in this book.

#### Key terms

completeness of dilates, secant dilates, hyperbolic secant, sech, Fermi kernel, Bose kernel, cosecant kernel, Meixner density, weighted L1 space, Möbius problem, Moebius problem, Möbius series, Mobius series, Dirichlet beta function, L function of chi 4, zero free half plane, quasi Riemann hypothesis, Salem criterion, Nyman Beurling, Wiener Tauberian theorem, Mellin transform, Cauchy semigroup, generalised gamma convolution, generalized gamma convolution, GGC, Thorin measure, reciprocal xi

chapters.title: Hitting times, Krein strings and the Pólya Bessel clock
chapters.summary:
This chapter studies Pólya's function $P(\theta)=K_{i\theta/2}(2\pi)$, the Macdonald function that is the building block of his approximation $\Xi^*$ to the Riemann Xi function, as the one model in which every statement of the Thorin programme is a theorem with an explicit witness. Biane showed that $\Xi$ and $P$ are Mellin transforms of Brownian hitting times whose Thorin measures are spectral measures of radial Brownian motions on $SU(2)$ and on $SL_2(\mathbb C)/SU(2)$. The chapter restates Biane's dictionary with corrected constants, the Wick rotation and curvature family, and shows that the zeros of $P$ are the Dirichlet spectrum of a Liouville operator (a Krein string). On the index side $K_0(2\pi)/K_{\sqrt u}(2\pi)$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) with the squared zeros as Thorin atoms, and its clock is the hitting time of an explicit diffusion; its Poisson trace is completely monotone as the trace of a semigroup, and the sine squared lemma and a Klein Gordon criterion (Rindler modes) are proved for it. The analogy with $\Xi$ stops at the de Bruijn Newman flow: by a theorem of Newman the function $P$ has a finite de Bruijn Newman constant, although its zeros show no sign of colliding in the computed range. A side by side comparison with $\Xi$ lists which statements are theorems for $P$ and remain open for $\Xi$. The exercises cover the law of the clock of $\Xi$, its Brownian boundaries, Li's criterion and the Dirichlet beta function. No proof of the Riemann Hypothesis is claimed.

#### From the literature

- Pólya's replacement of the kernel $\Phi$ by $\Phi^*$ and real zeros of $\Xi^*$ (Pólya 1926)
- Biane's dictionary of hitting times and spectral measures, and the Liouville operator of the zeros, going back to Titchmarsh (Biane 2009)
- $2\xi(s)$ as a Mellin transform of Bessel hitting times (Williams 1990; Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001)
- Kent's eigenvalue expansion of hitting times and Krein's inverse spectral theory (Kent 1980; Dym and McKean 1976)
- the de Bruijn Newman constant (de Bruijn 1950; Newman 1976)
- generalised gamma convolutions (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992)

#### New results

- [Laplace transform of Bessel hitting times with curvature](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#laplace_transform_of_bessel_hitting_times_with_curvature) (Volume I, Proposition 18.1.6, page 507; proved): The hitting time of radius a by the radial Brownian motion on the three dimensional space form of curvature kappa has an explicit Laplace transform, is a GGC with equally spaced Thorin atoms shifted by minus kappa/2, and is an exponential tilt of the flat case. The flat case is classical (Ciesielski and Taylor 1962), and for kappa < 0 the process is the Bessel process of dimension three with drift (Salminen and Vallois 2007), the norm of a three dimensional Brownian motion with drift, where the formula also follows from the Cameron Martin formula; the formula for the whole family, its Thorin measure and its reading as an exponential tilt are the book's. New in this book.
- [Exact quantisation rule for the zeros of Pólya's Bessel function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#exact_quantisation_rule_for_zeros_of_polya_bessel_function) (Volume I, Proposition 18.1.8, page 510; proved): The positive zeros of nu maps to K_{i nu}(2 pi) are exactly the solutions of an explicit phase equation, so their counting function is the integer part of a smooth function with an explicit asymptotic expansion. New in this book.
- [Index side Thorin measure of Pólya's Bessel function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#index_side_thorin_measure_of_polya_bessel_function) (Volume I, Theorem 18.1.9, page 512; proved): For Pólya's Bessel function the reciprocal K_0(2 pi)/K_{sqrt u}(2 pi) is, without any hypothesis, the Laplace transform of the GGC whose Thorin atoms are the squares of the positive zeros of nu maps to K_{i nu}(2 pi). New in this book.
- [Clock of Pólya's Bessel function as a hitting time of an explicit diffusion](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#clock_of_polya_bessel_function_hitting_time_of_explicit_diffusion) (Volume I, Theorem 18.1.10, page 513; proved): The index side clock of Pólya's Bessel function, the GGC with Thorin atoms at the squares of the positive zeros of nu maps to K_{i nu}(2 pi), is the clock of a hitting time of a level by an explicit diffusion, planar Brownian motion killed at rate one half and Doob transformed by K_0. New in this book.
- [Sine squared forms of the Bessel clock, the drifted clock and Pólya's clock](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#sine_squared_forms_of_bessel_clock_drifted_clock_and_polya_clock) (Volume I, Proposition 18.1.13, page 516; proved): The Laplace exponents of the sum of two Bessel hitting times, of the drifted first passage time and of Pólya's clock have sine squared forms whose kernels are the classical Planck and Macdonald measures and, for Pólya's clock, a completely monotone wave trace of a selfadjoint operator. New in this book.
- [Klein Gordon criterion for real zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#klein_gordon_criterion_for_real_zeros) (Volume I, Theorem 18.1.14, page 518; proved): If an even positive kernel is the boundary value of a solution of a Klein Gordon equation with a real potential bounded below, with the stated decay and nonvanishing conditions, then every zero of its Fourier transform is real and its square is a Dirichlet eigenvalue. New in this book.
- [De Bruijn Newman constant of Pólya's function is finite](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#de_bruijn_newman_constant_of_polya_function_is_finite) (Volume I, Proposition 18.1.15, page 520; proved): The Gaussian deformations of Pólya's Bessel function have only real zeros exactly from a finite time Lambda_P at most zero onward, by an argument of Newman, so its de Bruijn Newman constant is not minus infinity, contrary to a conjecture of the first author's earlier note. New in this book.
- [A property that survives Gaussian damping cannot imply real zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#gaussian_damping_property_cannot_imply_real_zeros) (Volume I, Proposition 18.1.16, page 523; proved): No property of even positive kernels that implies real zeros and survives a fixed Gaussian damping can hold for Riemann's kernel Phi, for Pólya's asymptote or for the Bessel kernel, which excludes a family of constructions with room to spare, using the theorems of Rodgers and Tao and of Newman. New in this book.
- [Open question on a diffusion for the clock of the Riemann xi function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_diffusion_for_clock_of_riemann_xi_function) (Volume I, Question 18.1.17, page 524; open): Is there, without assuming RH, a diffusion on a half line with an entrance boundary whose hitting time of a level has the Laplace transform of the clock of Riemann's xi function scaled by four? New in this book.
- [Open question on a Klein Gordon extension of Pólya's kernel](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_klein_gordon_extension_of_polya_kernel) (Volume I, Question 18.1.18, page 525; open): Does the kernel of Riemann's xi function, rescaled, admit a Klein Gordon extension with a real potential asymptotic to e^{2x}, which would imply RH? New in this book.
- [Open question on the de Bruijn Newman constants of Pólya's functions](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_de_bruijn_newman_constants_of_polya_functions) (Volume I, Question 18.1.19, page 525; open): What are the de Bruijn Newman constants of Pólya's Bessel function and of his function Xi star, at what height do the first nonreal zeros appear, and do they appear through collisions of real zeros? New in this book.
- [Open question on a family joining the two clocks](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_family_joining_the_two_clocks) (Volume I, Question 18.1.20, page 525; open): Is there a one parameter family of laws joining the drifted first passage time and the sum of two Bessel hitting times, each member with a reciprocal symmetry encoding a functional equation, along which the index side Thorin measure can be followed? New in this book.

#### Key terms

Pólya Bessel function, Polya function, Macdonald function, K Bessel function, Biane dictionary, hitting time, Brownian motion, Krein string, Liouville operator, Dirichlet spectrum, generalised gamma convolution, GGC, Thorin atoms, Thorin measure, clock, Klein Gordon criterion, Rindler modes, de Bruijn Newman constant, Newman, Riemann Xi function, Riemann Hypothesis, Wick rotation, spectral measure

chapters.title: The Pólya density as a maximum and as an extreme value law
chapters.summary:
Which parts of the maximum structure behind the Pólya density of Riemann's xi function survive the passage to the Thorin measure of the clock? The Pólya kernel comes from the density of the square root of a sum of two independent copies of the maximum $M_4$ of independent exponential variables, while the clock $1/G(\lambda)=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt\lambda)$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) exactly when the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) holds. The chapter factors the tilted maximum through the zeta distribution of Khinchin, sets the maximum and the clock in the language of Wald couples, and proves a Stieltjes criterion for RH in which an off line zero appears as an atom of negative mass. It gives an explicit GGC within a stated Laplace distance of the clock, its Gumbel norming constant from the first zero, its finite order Bondesson and hyperbolically completely monotone (HCM) properties, with RH equivalent to the infinite order versions, and a finite arithmetic form of the basepoint density below $\alpha=1$. The symmetrised finite stages of the maximum give, through Hurwitz's theorem, a sufficient condition for RH. The clock is not a maximum of independent exponential variables: the maximum structure belongs to the theta function and not to the zeros. The chapter then reads the Pólya density as an extreme value law (Smith and Tawn pictures, hitting times and the Thorin variable, B splines and Hadamard products, an explicit string given by the Liouville operator, and a string test from kernel moments). It examines three reformulations of RH and finds that none is a new path, poses open problems, and claims no proof of RH.

#### From the literature

- The law with moments $2\xi(s)$ as, up to a constant factor, the maximum of a normalised Brownian excursion (Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001)
- The zeta distribution and the infinite divisibility of $\zeta(\sigma+it)/\zeta(\sigma)$ for $\sigma>1$ (Khinchin 1938; Gnedenko and Kolmogorov 1954; Lin and Hu 2001)
- The logistic law as a normal scale mixture (Andrews and Mallows 1974; Stefanski 1991); van Dantzig pairs (Lukacs 1968); Wald couples (Polson 2018)
- The limit laws of maxima (Gnedenko 1943); Bondesson's theorem that GGC Laplace transforms are the HCM functions (Bondesson 1992)
- Lagarias's criterion (Lagarias 1999); $\Lambda\ge0$ (Rodgers and Tao 2020); RH verified to $3\times10^{12}$ and $\Lambda\le0.2$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021)
- Zeros of sections of $\zeta$ (Turán 1948; Montgomery 1983), also symmetrised (Spira 1967; Gonek and Montgomery 2013)

#### New results

Theorems are proved, the finite arithmetic form below $\alpha=1$ is conditional, and the problems are open.
- [Pólya kernel from a sum of two maxima of exponential variables](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#polya_kernel_from_sum_of_two_maxima_of_exponentials) (Volume I, Proposition 19.2.1, page 530; proved): The square e^{2Y} of the variable e^Y built from Riemann's xi function has the law of a sum of two independent copies of the maximum M_4 of independent exponential variables, and the Pólya kernel is recovered from the density of the square root of that sum by an explicit change of variables. New in this book.
- [Khinchin factorisation of the tilted maximum of exponential variables](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#khinchin_factorisation_of_tilted_maximum_of_exponentials) (Volume I, Theorem 19.3.1, page 531; proved): For sigma above one, the maximum M_4 of independent exponential variables, tilted by the factor m^{sigma/2} and multiplied by an independent geometric factor 4^{-K} that modifies only the prime 2, has the law of a gamma variable divided by pi times the square of a zeta distributed integer. New in this book.
- [Wald couples of the maximum of exponential variables and the logistic law](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#wald_couples_of_maximum_of_exponentials_and_logistic_law) (Volume I, Theorem 19.4.2, page 532; proved): The maximum M_4 of independent exponential variables, paired with a uniform variable on (-1,1) scaled by the square root of pi over two, is a Wald couple, as is the pair of sums of two independent copies, and the square root of M_4 times a standard normal variable has the logistic law. The van Dantzig pair involved is classical and the logistic statement is due to Andrews and Mallows and to Stefanski; the book's addition is their reading through the maximum in the language of Wald couples. New in this book.
- [Stieltjes criterion for RH through the smoothed Thorin density of the clock](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#stieltjes_criterion_for_rh_through_smoothed_thorin_density_of_clock) (Volume I, Theorem 19.6.1, page 533; proved): The Riemann Hypothesis is equivalent to each of the following: the clock is a GGC, the function G'/G, minus the logarithmic derivative of its transform 1/G, is a Stieltjes function, its heat trace W is completely monotone, and the smoothed Thorin density r_eta(x), the imaginary part of G'/G at minus x minus i eta divided by pi, is nonnegative for all real x and all eta above zero. The form through r_eta is new, and the others are in the book. New in this book.
- [An off line zero makes the smoothed Thorin density of the clock negative](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#off_line_zero_makes_smoothed_thorin_density_of_clock_negative) (Volume I, Lemma 19.6.2, page 534; proved): If a zero has real part beta above one half and ordinate gamma, the smoothed Thorin density r_eta of the clock at the point gamma squared minus delta squared, with delta equal to beta minus one half, tends to minus infinity as eta increases to twice delta times gamma. An explicit formula gives its value for eta below that and shows when it is negative. New in this book.
- [An explicit GGC within a stated Laplace distance of the clock](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#explicit_ggc_within_laplace_distance_of_the_clock) (Volume I, Proposition 19.7.2, page 536; proved): The sum of independent exponential variables divided by the squares of the ordinates of the zeros up to height 3 times 10^12 is a GGC whose Laplace transform is within 2.5 times 10^-11 of the transform of the clock, by a certified bound that uses the verification of RH up to that height and nothing about the zeros above it. New in this book.
- [Term of one zero in the Thorin density of the basepoint family in the lambda chart](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#term_of_one_zero_in_thorin_density_of_basepoint_family_lambda_chart) (Volume I, Proposition 19.8.1, page 537; proved): In the Laplace variable lambda the term of a single zero in the Thorin density at basepoint alpha is a sum of two Poisson kernels divided by twice the square root of lambda. It equals a factor kappa above one times a function that is a Cauchy density when delta is positive, has total mass the sign of delta, and near its peak is a Lorentzian of full width 4 |delta| gamma up to a relative error of order delta squared over gamma squared. New in this book.
- [The clock is not a maximum of independent exponential variables](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#clock_is_not_a_maximum_of_independent_exponential_variables) (Volume I, Proposition 19.9.1, page 539; proved): The negative logarithm of the distribution function of the clock is not completely monotone, so the clock is not the maximum of independent exponential variables with any rates, nor of a Poisson cloud of exponential clocks. The proof compares the first two exponential terms of the tail of the clock, and the coefficient of the second is negative where complete monotonicity would force it to be nonnegative. New in this book.
- [Gumbel limit for maxima of independent copies of the clock and of the maximum M_4](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#gumbel_limit_for_maxima_of_independent_copies_of_the_clock) (Volume I, Proposition 19.10.1, page 541; proved): The maximum of n independent copies of the clock, scaled by the square of the first zero ordinate and centred at an explicit logarithm, converges to the Gumbel law, and divided by log n it tends to the reciprocal of that square; the maximum of n copies of M_4, scaled by pi and centred at log(2n), has the same Gumbel limit. This is Gnedenko's theorem applied to the exponential tails of M_4 and of the clock; the book's addition is the reading of the norming constant of the clock as the first atom of its Thorin measure, with the constant given by the first residue. New in this book.
- [Convergence of the finite maxima and of the finite stages of xi](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#finite_maxima_converge_to_maximum_and_finite_stages_to_xi) (Volume I, Theorem 19.12.1, page 544; proved): Truncating the maximum M_4 at N exponential variables of each kind gives a maximum that differs from M_4 only on an event of probability at most C sqrt(N) e^{-pi sqrt(N)/2}, and the finite stage xi_N of the xi function and its symmetrisation converge to xi uniformly on compact subsets of the open critical strip at the rate N^{1/4} e^{-pi sqrt(N)/4}. New in this book.
- [Zeros of the symmetrised finite stages and a sufficient condition for RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#hurwitz_zeros_of_finite_stages_and_sufficient_condition_for_rh) (Volume I, Corollary 19.12.2, page 545; proved): By Hurwitz's theorem the zeros of the finite stages converge to the zeros of xi in the open strip, a simple zero on the critical line is approached by exactly one zero of the symmetrised stage, which lies on the line, and if the symmetrised stages have no zeros in the right half of the strip up to heights tending to infinity along some sequence of stages then RH holds. Whether RH implies that hypothesis on the stages is open. New in this book.
- [Finite order GGC, Bondesson and HCM classes of the clock, and RH as the infinite order case](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#finite_order_ggc_bondesson_and_hcm_classes_of_the_clock) (Volume I, Theorem 19.13.2, page 549; proved): From the verification of RH up to height 3 times 10^12 the clock lies in the finite order GGC and Bondesson classes up to order 1.16 times 10^25 and its Laplace transform is hyperbolically completely monotone up to order 9 times 10^12, while RH is equivalent to the clock being a GGC, to its being in the Bondesson class, and to its transform being hyperbolically completely monotone. New in this book.
- [Finite arithmetic form of the basepoint density below basepoint one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#finite_arithmetic_form_of_basepoint_density_below_basepoint_one) (Volume I, Proposition 19.14.1, page 551; conditional on Part (b) assumes the Riemann hypothesis. Part (a) holds without any hypothesis, and part (c) holds without any hypothesis when delta is at least one half and otherwise needs that every zero lies within delta of the critical line, which the Riemann hypothesis gives for every delta above zero): For basepoint alpha equal to one half plus delta, a Fejér tapered sum over the primes below e^X, two explicit pole terms and one gamma integral define a quantity A_X, which is half the sum over all zeros rho of a function that is nonnegative on the real line, evaluated at (rho minus one half)/i, is nonnegative under RH, and tends to the real part of the logarithmic derivative of xi at alpha plus it as X grows when every zero lies within delta of the critical line. New in this book.
- [Zero freeness of the symmetric finite stages of the maximum](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_zero_freeness_of_symmetric_finite_stages_of_the_maximum) (Volume I, Problem 19.1, page 553; open): Find heights tending to infinity such that, for infinitely many N, the symmetric finite stage of the maximum has no zeros in the right half of the critical strip below that height, for instance heights of order the square root of N; either statement would prove RH. Numerical counts for N up to 96 suggest that the zeros stay on the line up to a height of order N, and a mechanism for that is the first thing to find. New in this book.
- [A termwise positive continuation of the prime form below basepoint one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_termwise_positive_continuation_of_prime_form_below_basepoint_one) (Volume I, Problem 19.2, page 554; open): Is there a continuation of the sine squared prime form of the Thorin density below basepoint one that is positive term by term, for instance through smoothed prime sums with a cutoff near e^{1/epsilon} whose loss can be controlled by the logarithmic derivative of xi at alpha, the gamma sum and the pole terms? A positive answer for every basepoint in (alpha_0, 1] would prove the zero free region beta at most alpha_0. New in this book.
- [Existence of the half flow clock for small positive times](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_existence_of_half_flow_clock_for_small_positive_times) (Volume I, Problem 19.3, page 554; open): For times t between 0 and 0.2, does the law with Laplace transform R_t(lambda/2), half of the clock of the de Bruijn Newman flow, exist as a probability law, and is it infinitely divisible? Unconditionally it is known to exist at t = 0, where it is half the clock, and to exist and be a GGC for t at least 0.2; under RH it exists and is a GGC for every t at least 0. New in this book.
- [An analogue of the Khinchin factorisation at one half](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_khinchin_analogue_of_tilted_maximum_at_one_half) (Volume I, Problem 19.4, page 555; open): Is there an analogue at sigma equal to one half of the Khinchin factorisation of the tilted maximum, that is, a factorisation of the tilted law of the clock or of the Pólya variable through a law built from the primes, with the explicit formula replacing the Euler product? New in this book.
- [Each term of the theta series kernel is an explicit combination of two Gumbel kernels of fractional order](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#gumbel_decomposition_of_each_term_of_the_theta_series_kernel) (Volume I, Theorem 19.17.1, page 556; proved): With $x=-4u-\log(\pi n^2)$, $\phi_n(u)\,du=\pi^{-1/4}n^{-1/2}\Gamma(\frac54)[\frac58g_{9/4}(x)-\frac34g_{5/4}(x)]\,dx$ with $g_k(x)=e^{-kx}\exp(-e^{-x})/\Gamma(k)$, and its Fourier transform is $\frac14n^{-s}\xi(s)/\zeta(s)$ with $s=(1+iz)/2$. New in this book.
- [Zeros of the Dirichlet polynomial of the Dyck chain at n equal to 25600 below height 60 (computed)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#dyck_chain_polynomial_has_thirteen_zeros_left_of_the_line_below_height_sixty_at_n_25600) (Volume I, Result 19.17, page 557; computed): For the Dirichlet polynomial $F_n(s)=\mathbb{E}Y_n^s$ of the Dyck chain at $n=25600$, an argument principle count in ball arithmetic gives 13 zeros with $-4<\operatorname{Re}s<6$ and $0<\operatorname{Im}s<60$, none with real part above $\frac12$ (between $0.0907$ and $0.4553$), 13 being the number of ordinates $\gamma_k$ below 60; a computation at this $n$ only. New in this book.
- [Lattice bias expansion of the Dirichlet polynomial of the Dyck chain (conjecture)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_lattice_bias_expansion_of_dyck_chain_dirichlet_polynomial) (Volume I, Conjecture 19.17.2, page 558; open): Conjecture that $F_n(s)=2\xi(s)-\frac{3s}{\sqrt{\pi n}}\xi(s-1)+O(1/n)$ locally uniformly on $\operatorname{Re}s>0$ for the Dirichlet polynomial of the Dyck chain, consistent with the mean height of de Bruijn, Knuth and Rice. New in this book.
- [First order displacement of the zeros of the Dyck chain polynomial from the zeros of xi (conditional)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#dyck_chain_zeros_first_order_displacement_given_lattice_bias_conjecture) (Volume I, Proposition 19.17.3, page 559; conditional on The lattice bias conjecture, that $F_n(s)=2\xi(s)-\frac{3s}{\sqrt{\pi n}}\xi(s-1)+O(1/n)$ locally uniformly on $\operatorname{Re}s>0$): Assuming the lattice bias conjecture, each simple zero $\rho$ of $\xi$ has exactly one zero of $F_n$ at $\rho+\delta_nc_{\rm D}(\rho)+O(1/n)$ for large $n$, with $\delta_n=3/(2\sqrt{2n})$. New in this book.
- [Phase formula for the lattice bias coefficient at a zero on the critical line](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#lattice_bias_coefficient_phase_formula_on_critical_line) (Volume I, Proposition 19.17.4, page 559; proved): For a simple zero $\frac12+i\gamma$ of $\xi$ the displacement coefficient $c_{\rm D}$ equals $-C_{\rm D}(\gamma)e^{-i\Theta(\gamma)}/Z'(\gamma)$ with explicit positive $C_{\rm D}$ and phase $\Theta$, so the sign of its real part is that of $-\cos\Theta(\gamma)/Z'(\gamma)$. New in this book.
- [Lattice bias displacement of the Dyck chain zeros, computed for 200 zeros of xi and the zero near the 64th (computed)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#lattice_bias_displacement_computed_first_200_zeros_and_zero_near_rho_64) (Volume I, Result 19.17, page 560; computed): In ball arithmetic $\operatorname{Re}c_{\rm D}(\rho_k)<0$ for $k\le63$ and $>0$ first at $k=64$, and the Dyck chain zero near $\rho_{64}$ lies to the right of the critical line for $10^5\le n\le10^8$, agreeing with the first order law; a computation and no proof. New in this book.
- [All zeros of Xi are real if and only if the reciprocal xi law is a GGC, and real and simple if and only if it is the hitting time of a string](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rh_equivalent_to_ggc_reciprocal_xi_law_and_to_the_existence_of_a_string) (Volume I, Corollary 19.19.1, page 562; proved): RH holds if and only if $L$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution with positive Thorin measure $\sum_k\delta_{\gamma_k^2}$; the zeros are all real and simple if and only if $L$ is the Laplace transform of the hitting time of a Krein string with positive mass; the same holds for any even real entire $\widehat H$ of order below two with $\widehat H(0)>0$. New in this book.
- [Under RH with simple zeros the tail of the hitting time is a sum of exponentials and its excess is exponential with rate the first squared ordinate](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#principal_eigenvalue_of_the_string_from_the_tail_of_the_hitting_time_under_rh) (Volume I, Proposition 19.19.2, page 563; conditional on RH, simple zeros, and $|\xi'(\rho)|\ge e^{-C|\gamma|}$ for some constant $C$ and all zeros $\rho=\frac12+i\gamma$): If RH holds, the zeros are simple and $|\xi'(\rho)|\ge e^{-C|\gamma|}$ for some constant $C$ and all zeros $\rho$, then $\mathbb P(T>x)=\sum_kc_ke^{-\gamma_k^2x}$ with $c_k=\prod_{j\ne k}(1-\gamma_k^2/\gamma_j^2)^{-1}$, so the excess of $T$ over a high threshold is asymptotically exponential with rate $\gamma_1^2$. New in this book.
- [Hankel test: the zeros of an even entire kernel with infinitely many zeros are real if and only if two families of Hankel determinants are positive](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#hankel_determinants_positive_if_and_only_if_all_zeros_of_a_candidate_kernel_are_real) (Volume I, Proposition 19.22.1, page 566; proved): For an even real entire $\widehat H$ of order below two with infinitely many zeros and $\sum_k|w_k|<\infty$, all zeros are real and nonzero if and only if $D_n=\det[\mu_{i+j+1}]_{i,j=0}^{n-1}$ and $D_n'=\det[\mu_{i+j+2}]_{i,j=0}^{n-1}$ are positive for all $n\ge1$. New in this book.

#### Key terms

Pólya density, Polya density, maximum order statistic, maximum of independent exponential variables, extreme value law, Smith and Tawn, Thorin measure, clock, generalized gamma convolution, generalised gamma convolution, GGC, Khinchin factorisation, zeta distribution, Wald couple, logistic law, Stieltjes criterion, Laplace distance, Gumbel norming constant, Hurwitz theorem, Bondesson class, hyperbolically completely monotone, HCM, B spline, Liouville operator, string, Riemann Hypothesis, RH

chapters.title: Ferromagnetic random variables
chapters.summary:
Which random variables are ferromagnetic, and is the Pólya law ferromagnetic? A symmetric random variable is ferromagnetic if its moment generating function vanishes only on the imaginary axis, the Lee and Yang property of a single Ising spin. The Pólya variable has density $p=\Phi/\Xi(0)$ and moment generating function $\xi(\frac12+s)/\xi(\frac12)$, so the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) says exactly that it is ferromagnetic. The chapter develops the class. It gives the Hadamard form and cumulants of a ferromagnetic law, and shows that its clock is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) with one Thorin atom per pair of zeros, giving a van Dantzig pair. It proves closure under weak limits, so that RH holds if and only if the Pólya law is a limit in law of ferromagnetic laws, and studies mixtures of uniform laws on an interval (the shoulder theorem, laws mixed towards the edges, a moment test). It proves necessary conditions for the Pólya law, that it is a mixture of uniform laws and has no component with finitely many zeros (no Gaussian component). The Mellin transform of a clock is computed, with residue formulas and sums of independent spins expressed through the Riemann zeta function, with zeros of the transform located by ball arithmetic. The exponential $e^{2X}$ of the Pólya variable, a size biased variable of Biane, Pitman and Yor, is shown not to be a GGC and to be self decomposable, with hyperbolically completely monotone (HCM) powers $e^{\beta X}$ for $|\beta|\ge5.5791422$ by a computer assisted proof in ball arithmetic. The last sections treat two arithmetic spin chains, Knauf's number theoretical chain (Stern's diatomic sequence, partition function converging to $\zeta(\beta-1)/\zeta(\beta)$ for $\operatorname{Re}\beta>2$) and the Farey chain in a field, with a Perron identity and computed Fisher zeros near the points $1+\rho$, and list open problems. Ferromagnetic approximations of the Pólya law are in Volume II.

#### From the literature

- The Lee and Yang theorem (Lee and Yang 1952), Newman's single spin laws, Hadamard form and cumulants (Newman 1974; 1975), Lieb and Sokal (1981)
- The Griffiths Simon and Ellis, Monroe and Newman classes (Simon and Griffiths 1973; Ellis, Monroe and Newman 1976) and the GHS inequality for the Pólya law (Newman 1991)
- Van Dantzig pairs (Konstantopoulos, Patie and Sarkar 2024)
- Pólya's theorems on real zeros (1918; 1926), de Bruijn's strip theorem (1950), Turán inequalities (Csordas, Norfolk and Varga 1986), Jensen polynomials (Griffin, Ono, Rolen and Zagier 2019)
- The Biane, Pitman and Yor variable (2001), Kent (1978), Fourati (2016)
- Stern's diatomic sequence (Stern 1858) and the Calkin Wilf enumeration of the rationals (Calkin and Wilf 2000)
- Knauf's number theoretical spin chain (Knauf 1993; 1998), its phase transition at $\beta=2$ (Contucci and Knauf 1997) and the Farey fraction chain (Kleban and others)

#### New results

Results of this chapter, with their status.

- [Clock and van Dantzig partner of a ferromagnetic law](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#ferromagnetic_law_clock_and_van_dantzig_partner) (Volume I, Theorem 20.1.4, page 571; proved): The clock of a ferromagnetic law is a generalised gamma convolution with drift equal to the Gaussian part and one unit Thorin atom at the square of each positive zero of its characteristic function, and the law has a partner of Pólya frequency type forming a van Dantzig pair with it. New in this book.
- [Ferromagnetic laws are closed under convergence in law](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#ferromagnetic_laws_closed_under_convergence_in_law) (Volume I, Theorem 20.1.5, page 573; proved): A limit in law of ferromagnetic random variables is ferromagnetic, the variances converge and the moment generating functions converge locally uniformly on the complex plane. New in this book.

New in this book.
- [A uniform law mixed with an atom at the origin is not ferromagnetic](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#mixture_of_uniform_law_with_atom_at_origin_is_not_ferromagnetic) (Volume I, Theorem 20.2.1, page 575; counterexample, proved): The mixture of the uniform law on [-1,1] and a point mass at the origin is symmetric and unimodal but not ferromagnetic, so mixtures of ferromagnetic laws need not be ferromagnetic. New in this book.

New in this book.
- [Computed Lee and Yang threshold of the Farey chain in a field for even N from 10 to 36](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#computed_lee_yang_threshold_of_farey_chain_for_even_n_from_ten_to_thirty_six) (Volume I, Result 20.6.3, page 602; computed): For even N from 10 to 36 there is a computed threshold, rising from 1.2424 to 1.8329 and below beta star of N, above which the zeros of the Farey partition function in the field lie on the unit circle and below which, at every computed β down to 0.2, some do not (computation on a grid with bisection; the final bracket is certified by a Sturm count for N at most 32). (open problem)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_lines_of_zeros_of_mellin_transform_of_a_clock) (Volume I, Problem 20.2, page 603; open): Decide for which ferromagnetic laws the Mellin transform of the clock has all its nonreal zeros on one vertical line, and whether the uniform pair is, up to scale, the only pair from the U shaped class with this property. New in this book.

chapters.title: Cauchy mixtures, the reverse sine squared lemma and a two spin Lee and Yang form of RH
chapters.summary:
This chapter reads the Thorin density of the reciprocal $\Xi$ function as a mixture of Cauchy (Poisson) kernels, one bump for each zero, and asks what that structure says about the ferromagnetism of the Pólya law. For every symmetric law of Xi type the Thorin density at each level is a signed Cauchy mixture. It is a positive mixture at every level exactly for the ferromagnetic laws (Lee and Yang property of the Laplace transform), and then all bumps have one common width and the mixing measure is the zero counting measure. The reverse sine squared lemma goes from the zeros back to the canonical Lévy measure, giving damped cosines $e^{-a|x|}\cos\gamma x$ unconditionally at every basepoint $\alpha\ge1$, and undamping to the critical line gives Weil's functional. The cosine tilted laws $\cosh(wx)\,p$ are ferromagnetic for every $w\ge\tfrac12$ with no hypothesis. Coupling the Pólya spin to one Ising spin with coupling $w$ gives a two spin system with the Lee and Yang property for every $w>w_0$ exactly when $\zeta$ has no zero with real part above $\tfrac12+w_0$, so the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) is the case $w_0=0$ and the case $w_0=\tfrac12$ holds unconditionally. The one variable test is shown to be weaker, by an exact two spin law and by a phase criterion with a gap law for planted zero pairs and for several pairs and multiple zeros. A strip Lee and Yang theorem shows that ferromagnetic couplings never widen the strip of zeros. The chapter also gives a function field model (the Hasse bound as ferromagnetism of a Frobenius spin) and states plainly that the dictionary is not a path to RH, since each form needs a zero free half plane to descend. Some numbers are computed in floating point.

#### From the literature

- The Lee and Yang theorem and the general theorem of Lieb and Sokal on partition functions with ferromagnetic couplings
- The Pólya kernel and the partial fraction (Hadamard) expansion of $\xi'/\xi$
- Weil's explicit formula and Weil's positivity functional
- The Hasse bound for curves over finite fields
- Thorin's and Bondesson's generalised gamma convolutions
- A zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\tfrac78$ announced in October 2026 and not yet refereed (OpenAI 2026), used only conditionally

#### New results

Statements that use the announced half plane at $\tfrac78$ are conditional on it. Exact models are proved; the planted zero computations are floating point.

- [The Thorin density of a law of Xi type is a signed Cauchy mixture](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_density_of_xi_type_law_signed_cauchy_mixture) (Volume I, Theorem 21.1.2, page 608; proved): At each level the Thorin density of a law of Xi type is a drift plus one Cauchy bump per zero, of width the horizontal distance of the zero from the level and signed by its side. New in this book.
- [Positive Cauchy mixtures at every level are exactly the ferromagnetic laws](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#positive_cauchy_mixture_at_every_level_iff_ferromagnetic) (Volume I, Theorem 21.2.1, page 609; proved): For a law of Xi type, nonnegativity of the Thorin density at every level, a positive Cauchy mixture representation, ferromagnetism and the GGC form of the reciprocal transform are equivalent, with the mixing measure the zero counting measure. New in this book.
- [Strip classes of laws of Xi type and the Cauchy defect](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#cauchy_defect_strip_classes_closure) (Volume I, Proposition 21.2.4, page 609; proved): A law of Xi type has zeros in the strip of half width delta exactly when its Thorin density is nonnegative above level delta, and these classes are closed under independent sums and under suitable tilts but not under mixtures. New in this book.
- [The Ellis, Monroe and Newman class is not inside the ferromagnetic class](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#ellis_monroe_newman_class_not_inside_ferromagnetic_class) (Volume I, Corollary 21.2.5, page 610; proved): Since the de Bruijn and Newman constant is nonnegative (Rodgers and Tao), the class of Ellis, Monroe and Newman, which is stable under Gaussian damping, cannot lie inside the class of ferromagnetic laws. New in this book.
- [The reverse sine squared kernel lemma](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reverse_sine_squared_kernel_lemma) (Volume I, Lemma 21.3.1, page 610; proved): A damped cosine on the canonical side has a pair of Cauchy bumps as its cosine transform, and the logarithmic factor of a zero and its conjugate has canonical density a damped cosine. New in this book.
- [The reverse sine squared lemma, from the zeros to the canonical measure](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reverse_sine_squared_lemma_zeros_to_canonical_measure) (Volume I, Theorem 21.3.2, page 610; proved): At every basepoint alpha at least one, the sum over the zeros of damped cosines converges as a tempered distribution, has cosine transform the Thorin density, equals minus one half of the canonical measure on the positive axis, and is positive definite. New in this book.
- [A single width Cauchy mixture at one basepoint at least one implies RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#single_width_cauchy_mixture_at_one_basepoint_implies_rh) (Volume I, Theorem 21.3.3, page 611; proved): If the Thorin density of the reciprocal of xi at one basepoint alpha at least one is a positive Cauchy mixture of the single width alpha minus one half, then RH holds, and the converse holds at every alpha above one half. New in this book.
- [The undamped reverse sine squared series is Weil's functional](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#damped_cosine_series_is_weil_functional) (Volume I, Theorem 21.3.4, page 611; proved): Pairing each zero with its reflection and removing the damping gives, for test functions with exponential decay at rate one half, a series that does not depend on alpha and is Weil's explicit formula functional. New in this book.
- [Cosine tilted laws are ferromagnetic when the tilt exceeds the strip](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#cosine_tilted_laws_ferromagnetic_for_half_and_above) (Volume I, Theorem 21.4.1, page 612; proved): The cosine tilt of a law of Xi type with all zeros of real part below w in modulus is ferromagnetic, so the cosine tilt of the Pólya law is ferromagnetic for every w at least one half with no hypothesis. New in this book.
- [The two spin Lee and Yang property is a zero free half plane](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#two_spin_lee_yang_property_iff_zero_free_half_plane) (Volume I, Theorem 21.5.1, page 613; proved): A law of Xi type coupled to a fair Ising spin with strength w has the Lee and Yang property exactly when no zero of its moment generating function has real part above w. New in this book.
- [The Pólya spin coupled to an Ising spin, unconditional at one half and equivalent to RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#polya_ising_pair_lee_yang_for_half_and_rh_form) (Volume I, Corollary 21.5.2, page 614; proved): The Pólya spin coupled to one Ising spin is a Lee and Yang ferromagnet for every coupling at least one half, and for couplings above w0 exactly when zeta has no zero with real part above one half plus w0. New in this book.
- [Truncated Euler products sit exactly at the coupling one half](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#finite_euler_products_two_spin_threshold_one_half) (Volume I, Proposition 21.5.3, page 614; proved): The two spin system built from a truncated Euler product has the Lee and Yang property exactly for couplings at least one half. New in this book.
- [The sum of two three point spins, an exact law whose tilt threshold lies inside the strip](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#sum_of_two_three_point_spins_tilt_threshold) (Volume I, Proposition 21.6.1, page 614; proved): For the sum of two independent three point spins the cosine tilt is ferromagnetic exactly from an explicit w* below the strip half width a, so ferromagnetism of the one variable tilt does not force the law into the strip class at that coupling. New in this book.
- [A pair planted in Xi has slice threshold 0.2951 below its width 0.3](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#planted_pair_in_xi_slice_threshold_computed) (Volume I, Proposition 21.6.2, page 616; computed): For Xi with the first two ordinates replaced by a pair at distance 0.3 from the line, the cosine tilt has only real zeros in a computed box from w about 0.2951, below the strip half width 0.3. New in this book.
- [The phase criterion for the real zeros of the cosine tilt](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#phase_criterion_for_real_zeros_of_the_tilt) (Volume I, Proposition 21.6.3, page 617; proved): The real zeros of the tilt are the points where the phase of F(x+iw) crosses an odd multiple of one half pi, and a planted pair off the line produces a local rise of the phase that turns two nonreal zeros into real ones when it reaches such a level. New in this book.
- [The gap law eta minus w* equals phi squared eta cubed over two for a simple pair](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#slice_threshold_gap_law_for_a_simple_pair) (Volume I, Theorem 21.7.1, page 618; proved): For a simple planted pair of small width eta, the one variable test misses the strip by one half phi squared eta cubed, where phi is the field of the other zeros at the pair, and by order eta to the seventh if the field vanishes. New in this book.
- [Slice thresholds for several pairs and pairs of higher multiplicity](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#slice_thresholds_several_pairs_and_multiple_zeros) (Volume I, Theorem 21.8.1, page 622; proved): For clusters of planted pairs the gap of an odd multiplicity cluster is phi squared eta cubed over twice the square of the multiplicity, while an even multiplicity cluster is missed by a fixed fraction of its distance from the line. New in this book.
- [Ferromagnetic coupling never widens the strip, for spins of exponential type](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#strip_lee_yang_theorem_bounded_spins_lieb_sokal) (Volume I, Theorem 21.9.1, page 624; conditional on Rests on Proposition 2.2 of Lieb and Sokal (1981), as restated by Kozitsky, not read in the original): For symmetric spins whose Laplace transforms are entire of exponential type with zeros in a strip, a ferromagnetic coupling gives a partition function with no zeros outside the same strip. New in this book.
- [Ferromagnetic coupling never widens the strip, for laws of Xi type with Gaussian moments](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#strip_lee_yang_theorem_for_laws_of_xi_type) (Volume I, Theorem 21.9.2, page 626; conditional on Rests on Proposition 2.2 of Lieb and Sokal (1981), as restated by Kozitsky, not read in the original): For laws of Xi type with Gaussian moments of all orders, including the Pólya law, a ferromagnetic coupling gives a partition function with no zeros outside the strip of the single spins. New in this book.
- [The bare Pólya Ising pair has its field zeros inside the strip](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#strip_bound_for_the_bare_pair_coupling) (Volume I, Proposition 21.9.3, page 626; proved): For a law of Xi type in the strip class coupled to a fair Ising spin, the partition function in a common field has no zero outside the strip and none off the imaginary axis when the coupling exceeds the strip. New in this book.
- [The two spin Lee and Yang property at every coupling is monotonicity of the modulus of xi](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rh_iff_modulus_of_xi_monotone_in_the_two_spin_form) (Volume I, Theorem 21.11.1, page 628; proved): The Pólya spin coupled to an Ising spin is a Lee and Yang ferromagnet at every coupling exactly when the modulus of xi is nondecreasing in the real part on the right of the line, which is RH. New in this book.
- [A Frobenius spin is ferromagnetic exactly when the Hasse bound holds](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#frobenius_spin_ferromagnetic_iff_hasse_bound) (Volume I, Proposition 21.11.2, page 628; proved): For an elliptic curve over a finite field the numerator of the zeta function is a three point spin that is ferromagnetic, a single width Cauchy mixture and a Lee and Yang pair with an Ising spin exactly when the Hasse bound holds. New in this book.
- [Open problem on the one variable tilt, intervals and the constant kappa](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_is_the_one_variable_tilt_set_an_interval_and_quantitative_converse) (Volume I, Problem 21.1, page 630; open): Is the set of w for which the cosine tilt is ferromagnetic an interval, does the gap law extend to wide clusters, and is there a constant kappa with ferromagnetism for every w above w0 forcing no zero beyond w0 over kappa? New in this book.
- [Open problem, a Lee and Yang system built from the Euler product](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_two_spin_system_from_the_euler_product) (Volume I, Problem 21.2, page 630; open): Find a coupled system of Lee and Yang spins built from the Euler product, with coupling below one half, whose Lee and Yang property would give a zero free half plane. New in this book.
- [Open problem, strict shrinking of the strip under ferromagnetic coupling](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_strict_shrinking_of_the_strip_under_coupling) (Volume I, Problem 21.3, page 630; open): Ferromagnetic couplings never widen the strip, but do they shrink it strictly, by at least an amount comparable to the coupling? New in this book.
