chapters.title: Pólya and the zeros of entire functions
chapters.summary:
Which of George Pólya's results on the zeros of entire functions are already part of the Thorin programme for the Riemann Hypothesis (RH), which would help to prove it, and is the $2\sin^2$ lemma useful with regard to his work? The chapter reads Pólya's papers one by one (the Laguerre Pólya class, the universal factors $e^{\lambda u^2}$ and $\cosh(au)$, Pólya frequency functions, the Bessel function approximation $\Xi^*$, the Mellin criterion) through the reciprocal Xi law $\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)$ and the basepoint laws $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt s)$. It proves that the zeros of $\operatorname{Re}\xi(\alpha+it)$ sit at half integer crossings of the argument clock when $\xi$ has no zero in $\operatorname{Re}s\ge\alpha$, gives the exact form of the $2\sin^2$ lemma, proves its compensated clock condition at almost every height, accounts for the zeros of the even and odd parts, certifies log concavity of the two sided reciprocal Xi density in floating point (a computation, not a ball arithmetic certificate), bounds its distance to a Pólya frequency density by $1.6\times10^{-10}$, and shows that a quasi Riemann hypothesis at $\alpha_0$ is equivalent to positivity of the compensated clock on every line to its right. The even part at basepoint one quarter has only real simple zeros, each close to a half Gram point, and the following zero is displaced from the matching zeta ordinate by a quantity involving $S$ and $\theta'$. Results that need a zero free half plane are conditional, and the open problems are marked.

#### From the literature

- the Laguerre Pólya class (Pólya 1913), multiplier sequences (Pólya and Schur 1914), universal factors and the Mellin criterion (Pólya 1927)
- the Bessel function approximation $\Xi^*$ (Pólya 1926; Gasper 2008)
- derivatives of entire functions (Pólya 1922, 1943; Craven, Csordas and Smith 1987; Kim 1990; Ki and Kim 2000; Conrey 1983)
- the strip theorem (de Bruijn 1950); zero spacing of differenced zeta functions (Lagarias 2005)
- Turán inequalities (Csordas, Norfolk and Varga 1986); Jensen polynomials (Griffin, Ono, Rolen and Zagier 2019; Farmer 2022)
- Pólya frequency functions (Schoenberg 1951); RH as a Pólya frequency property (Konstantopoulos, Patie and Sarkar 2024)
- explicit bounds for $S(T)$ (Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong 2022); zero density (Ingham 1940); RH verified to $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021)
- the zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$, announced, not refereed (OpenAI 2026)

#### New results

Theorems are proved, the log concavity certificate is a floating point computation, results needing a zero free half plane are conditional, and problems are open.

- [Five equivalent forms of the Riemann Hypothesis in the Thorin variable: Laguerre Pólya class, Pólya Schur multipliers, Jensen polynomials and GGC](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#riemann_hypothesis_five_equivalent_forms_in_the_thorin_variable) (Volume I, Proposition 22.4.1, page 636; proved): RH is equivalent to $F(s)=\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)/\xi(\frac12)$ lying in the Laguerre Pólya class of type I, to the sequence $k!\,a_k$ of its Taylor coefficients being a Pólya Schur multiplier sequence, to real rootedness of all its Jensen polynomials, and to the reciprocal Xi law being a GGC; the Laguerre Pólya, multiplier sequence and Jensen forms are equivalent by the theorem of Pólya and Schur. New in this book.
- [Open problem: an exact arithmetic proof that the reciprocal Xi density is log concave, and then Pólya frequency of every order n](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_exact_proof_that_reciprocal_xi_density_is_log_concave_and_pf_n) (Volume I, Problem 22.1, page 638; open): Prove in exact or interval arithmetic that the density of the two sided reciprocal Xi law is log concave (PF of order two, for which the book has a floating point certificate), and then that it is PF of order n for every n at least three. New in this book.
- [Even part basepoint laws: GGC laws whose Thorin atoms are the zeros of the real part of xi on a vertical line](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#even_part_basepoint_laws_are_ggc_with_thorin_atoms_at_zeros_of_real_part_of_xi) (Volume I, Corollary 22.6.2, page 639; proved): When the even part of $w\mapsto\xi(\alpha+w)$ has only imaginary zeros, the reciprocal $\xi(\alpha)/A_\alpha(\sqrt s)$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC with Thorin atoms at $\tau_k^2$, where $\pm i\tau_k$ are those zeros; this holds unconditionally for $\alpha\ge1$, for all $\alpha>\frac12$ under RH, and RH follows if it holds along a sequence $\alpha_n\downarrow\frac12$. New in this book.
- [Half integer crossings of the clock: zeros of the real part of xi on a vertical line and the even part law as a midpoint rule](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#zeros_of_real_part_of_xi_on_a_vertical_line_at_half_integer_crossings_of_the_clock) (Volume I, Proposition 22.6.3, page 639; proved): If $\xi$ has no zero in $\operatorname{Re}s\ge\alpha$, the argument clock of $\xi$ on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha$ is strictly increasing and the zeros of $\operatorname{Re}\xi(\alpha+it)$ are exactly its crossings of the levels $k-\frac12$, so the Thorin distribution of the even part law is the rounding of the clock of the basepoint law, and the even part law is the midpoint rule for the gamma clock integral. New in this book.
- [Zeros of Pólya's Xi star at half Gram points](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#zeros_of_polya_xi_star_at_half_gram_points) (Volume I, Proposition 22.7.2, page 641; proved): The zeros of Pólya's Bessel function approximation $\Xi^*$ of the Xi function satisfy $\vartheta(t_k^*)/\pi=k-\frac32-(2\pi^2-3)/(\pi t_k^*)+O((t_k^*)^{-2})$, so its zero count differs from $\vartheta(T)/\pi+\frac32$ by a bounded rounding error, whereas the zero count of zeta has the arithmetic fluctuation $S(T)$; the book derives this in outline and checks the constant numerically. New in this book.
- [The zeros of the even part at basepoint one quarter sit at half Gram points, displaced from the zeta zeros by the argument S](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#zeros_of_half_gram_skeleton_at_basepoint_one_quarter_and_their_displacement_from_zeta_zeros) (Volume I, Proposition 22.7.3, page 642; proved): The even part of the Bessel function of order one quarter plus i t over two at argument 2 pi has only real simple zeros, located by a strictly increasing phase and equal to half Gram points up to order t to the power minus one half, and their displacement from a simple zeta ordinate is pi S over theta prime; this is from a note of Nicholas Polson. New in this book.
- [Open problem: a sign condition on the primal measure of the 2 sin squared lemma that holds for the Bessel model, survives the Euler product and fails for Davenport Heilbronn](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_sign_condition_on_the_primal_measure_with_bessel_euler_and_davenport_heilbronn_tests) (Volume I, Problem 22.2, page 646; open): Find a sign condition on the primal measure of the $2\sin^2$ lemma that holds for the Bessel model at every basepoint, is preserved when the primal measures of Euler factors are added, and fails for the Davenport Heilbronn function. New in this book.
- [Open problem: only imaginary zeros of the even part of xi at one basepoint inside the critical strip, without a quasi Riemann hypothesis](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_real_rootedness_of_the_even_part_of_xi_at_one_basepoint_inside_the_strip) (Volume I, Problem 22.3, page 646; open): Prove that the even part of $w\mapsto\xi(\alpha+w)$ has only imaginary zeros for one fixed $\alpha$ in $(\frac12,1)$, by a Pólya type argument that uses the Euler product and without first proving that $\zeta$ has no zero to the right of $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha$. New in this book.
- [Open problem: are the derivative laws of xi, or of F in the Thorin variable, generalized gamma convolutions for some n](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_derivative_laws_of_xi_and_of_the_thorin_variable_function_are_ggc) (Volume I, Problem 22.4, page 646; open): Decide whether, for some $n\ge1$, the functions $\xi^{(2n)}(\frac12)/\xi^{(2n)}(\frac12+\sqrt s)$ or $F^{(n)}(0)/F^{(n)}(s)$ are Laplace transforms of GGCs; no global statement is known for any $n$ in either family, and one would be the first unconditional GGC in its family. New in this book.
- [Exact ratio of the even part and basepoint Laplace transforms, and the exact defect of the midpoint rule](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#exact_ratio_of_even_part_and_basepoint_laplace_transforms_of_the_reciprocal_xi_family) (Volume I, Theorem 22.11.1, page 647; proved): The even part and basepoint Laplace transforms of the reciprocal Xi family differ by the explicit factor $2/(1+R_\alpha(s))$ with $R_\alpha(s)=\xi(\alpha-\sqrt s)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt s)$, which gives the exact defect of the midpoint rule, two sided bounds, a rate $O(\alpha-\frac12)$ and weak convergence of both families to the reciprocal Xi law as $\alpha\downarrow\frac12$ whenever they are laws. New in this book.
- [Log concavity of the two sided reciprocal Xi density: a floating point certificate](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#log_concavity_of_two_sided_reciprocal_xi_density_floating_point_certificate) (Volume I, Theorem 22.11.5, page 649; computed): A floating point computation with explicit analytic bounds, in three ranges of the argument, shows that the density of the two sided reciprocal Xi law is log concave; it is not an interval arithmetic proof. New in this book.
- [The two sided reciprocal Xi density is uniformly close to a Pólya frequency density of every order](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#two_sided_reciprocal_xi_density_uniformly_close_to_a_polya_frequency_density_of_every_order) (Volume I, Theorem 22.11.6, page 649; proved): Unconditionally the density of the two sided reciprocal Xi law is within $1.57\times10^{-10}$, uniformly, of the PF of every order density built from the zeros on the critical line, and its $3\times3$ and $4\times4$ Pólya frequency minors are at least $-1.1\times10^{-8}$ and $-1.2\times10^{-7}$; the numerical values are floating point evaluations of explicit integrals. New in this book.
- [Exact form of the 2 sin squared lemma: the compensated reciprocal is a GGC if and only if the clock runs at least as fast at every height as at height zero](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#exact_stieltjes_form_of_the_two_sin_squared_lemma_and_the_compensated_clock_condition) (Volume I, Theorem 22.11.7, page 651; proved): Stieltjes inversion gives the Thorin density of the compensated reciprocal of a real entire function $f$ with no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}z>\alpha-\delta$, $\delta>0$, and $f'/f(z)=O(\log|z|)$ on $\operatorname{Re}z\ge\alpha$ exactly, with no sign assumption on the primal measure, so the compensated reciprocal is a GGC if and only if $\operatorname{Re}f'/f(\alpha+ir)\ge f'/f(\alpha)$ for all $r>0$. New in this book.
- [Primes and the compensated clock: the prime sum, the archimedean bracket and the threshold 7.78918](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#archimedean_and_prime_parts_of_the_compensated_clock_with_threshold_7_78918) (Volume I, Proposition 22.11.8, page 652; proved): For $\alpha>1$ the compensated clock excess $D_\alpha(r)$ is a nonnegative prime sum plus an explicit archimedean bracket, which is nonnegative for every $r$ if and only if $\alpha\ge\alpha_1=7.78918\ldots$, so that for $\alpha\ge\alpha_1$ the identity alone gives $D_\alpha\ge0$ and below it the primes must make up the deficit. New in this book.
- [The pole term needs the gamma factor, the compensated reciprocal of (s minus 1) zeta is not a GGC](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#pole_term_needs_the_gamma_factor_for_the_compensated_reciprocal) (Volume I, Remark 22.11.9, page 653; proved): For every alpha above one the compensated reciprocal of the entire function (s minus 1) times zeta is not the Laplace transform of a GGC, so the gamma terms of the archimedean bracket cannot be dropped while the pole term is kept. New in this book.
- [The compensated clock condition on every line to the right of alpha zero implies a zero free half plane](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#compensated_clock_condition_on_every_line_to_the_right_of_alpha_zero_gives_a_zero_free_half_plane) (Volume I, Proposition 22.11.10, page 654; proved): If $\operatorname{Re}\xi'/\xi(\alpha+ir)\ge\xi'/\xi(\alpha)$ for all real $r$ and every $\alpha>\alpha_0$, then $\zeta$ has no zero with real part greater than $\alpha_0$; for $\alpha_0=\frac12$ this implies RH. New in this book.
- [Compensated clock condition at almost all heights in the critical strip, unconditionally, with the exceptional set bounded by zero density](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#compensated_clock_condition_holds_at_almost_all_heights_inside_the_strip) (Volume I, Theorem 22.11.14, page 656; proved): For each $\alpha$ in $(\frac12,1]$ the set of heights in $[T,2T]$ where the compensated clock condition $D_\alpha(r)>0$ fails has, for large $T$, measure at most an absolute constant times $(1+1/(\alpha-\frac12))(N(\sigma,3T)+1)$, with $N(\sigma,3T)$ the number of zeros of real part above $\sigma=\frac12(\alpha+\frac12)$ and ordinate in $(0,3T]$; by Ingham's density theorem this is $o(T)$, so the condition holds on a set of heights of full density. New in this book.
- [Hankel determinants of the two sided reciprocal Xi density have the Pólya frequency sign far in the tail](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#hankel_determinants_of_the_reciprocal_xi_density_have_the_pf_sign_far_in_the_tail) (Volume I, Proposition 22.11.15, page 657; proved): For every $n$ with $\gamma_n$ below the verified height $H=3\times10^{12}$, the Hankel determinant of order $n$ of the two sided reciprocal Xi density is dominated as $x\to\infty$ by the term of the first $n$ zeros, whose sign is $(-1)^{n(n-1)/2}$ by the alternation of the residues, which is the PF condition at coalescing points. New in this book.
- [Zero accounting for the even and odd parts of xi: almost all zeros are purely imaginary](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#zero_accounting_for_the_even_and_odd_parts_of_xi_on_a_vertical_line) (Volume I, Theorem 22.11.16, page 658; proved): Unconditionally, for $\frac12<\alpha\le1$ with no zero of $\xi$ on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha$, the numbers of zeros of the even and odd parts of $w\mapsto\xi(\alpha+w)$ up to height $T$ are $U_\alpha(T)+2N(\alpha,T)+O(\log T)$, at least $\lfloor U_\alpha(T)+\frac12\rfloor$ and $\lfloor U_\alpha(T)\rfloor$ of them are purely imaginary, and by Ingham's density theorem all but $O(T^{3(1-\alpha)/(2-\alpha)}\log^5T)$ are. New in this book.

#### Key terms

Laguerre Pólya class, Laguerre Polya class, Pólya Schur multiplier sequence, Jensen polynomial, Pólya frequency function, log concave, universal factor, Mellin criterion, Xi star, Gram points, reciprocal Xi law, basepoint law, clock, 2 sin squared lemma, sine squared lemma, compensated clock, even part, odd part, zero accounting, quasi Riemann hypothesis, zero free half plane, generalised gamma convolution, generalized gamma convolution, GGC, Thorin measure, Riemann Hypothesis, RH

chapters.title: Haseo Ki, derivatives and the Keiper Li coefficients
chapters.summary:
What does the work of Haseo Ki and his coauthors say about the Thorin condition on the reciprocal of the Riemann Xi function, and how are the Keiper Li coefficients computed from the Pólya density? Ki and his coauthors studied Fourier transforms of rapidly decaying positive kernels, their zeros under the heat flow (the de Bruijn Newman flow) and under repeated differentiation, and zeta functions with the functional equation of $\zeta$ but no Euler product. The chapter reads this through the Thorin dictionary: a zero of an even entire function is an atom of the Thorin measure of its reciprocal, and the reciprocal is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) exactly when the zeros are real. It proves that after any positive time the reciprocal of the flowed function is a GGC transform up to a finite rational factor (the theorem of Ki, Kim and Lee), with the atoms of the factor confined to confocal parabolas that shrink with time. With the theorem of Rodgers and Tao this gives an obstruction: no property of the Pólya density that survives a Gaussian tilt can imply the Riemann Hypothesis (RH). For repeated differentiation, the rescaled reciprocals converge to the Laplace transform of the exit time of Brownian motion from an interval, a GGC, and a conjecture gives the rate. Epstein type zeta functions and the Davenport Heilbronn functions indicate that a Thorin argument must use the Euler product. A last section computes the Taylor coefficients of $\log\xi$ at $s=1$ from the Pólya density, hence the Keiper Li coefficients $\lambda_n$, and shows without hypothesis that $\lambda_n$ is a Thorin functional of the zeros, so that Li's criterion is positivity of that functional. Nothing here proves RH.

#### From the literature

- The heat flow on Fourier transforms of positive kernels, the de Bruijn Newman constant, and the zeros of $\Xi_t$ (de Bruijn 1950; Newman 1976; Ki and Kim 2002, 2003; Ki, Kim and Lee 2009)
- The de Bruijn Newman constant is nonnegative (Rodgers and Tao 2020)
- Newman's characterisation of the Lee and Yang single spin laws by the Laguerre Pólya class (Newman 1974)
- Ki's theorem on repeated differentiation, the zeros of $\zeta'$, and approximation theorems for Epstein type zeta functions and the Davenport Heilbronn functions (Ki and coauthors)
- Li's criterion for RH (Li 1997), the coefficients introduced and computed by Keiper (1992), and their arithmetic expression (Bombieri and Lagarias 1999)

#### New results

Statements are proved unless marked computed or conditional.

- [Eventually Thorin: after any positive time the reciprocal of the flowed Xi function is a GGC transform times a finite rational factor](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#after_any_positive_time_the_reciprocal_of_the_flowed_function_is_a_ggc_transform_up_to_a_rational_factor) (Volume I, Proposition 23.2.1, page 664; proved): For every $t>0$ the ratio $\Xi_t(0)/\Xi_t(i\sqrt s)$ equals a generalised gamma convolution Laplace transform times a finite product $\prod_{\eta\in E_t}(1+s/\eta)^{-1}$ over a conjugation invariant multiset off the positive axis, which is empty exactly when $\Xi_t$ has only real zeros. New in this book.
- [Shrinking parabolas: Thorin atoms of the flowed Xi function lie to the right of a parabola that collapses at t = 1/2](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_atoms_of_the_flowed_function_lie_right_of_a_shrinking_parabola) (Volume I, Corollary 23.2.2, page 664; proved): For $0<t<\frac12$ every Thorin atom of $\Xi_t$ lies in the closed region to the right of the parabola $x=y^2/(4\Delta^2)-\Delta^2$ with $\Delta^2=\frac14-\frac t2$; the parabolas share the focus $0$ and collapse onto $[0,\infty)$ at $t=\frac12$. New in this book.
- [No slack in the Gaussian direction: no class of kernels closed under Gaussian damping and containing Phi has only real zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#no_property_closed_under_a_gaussian_tilt_of_the_polya_density_can_imply_rh) (Volume I, Proposition 23.2.3, page 665; proved): If a class of positive even kernels is closed under multiplication by $e^{-bu^2}$ for every $b>0$ and every member has a Fourier transform with only real zeros, then Riemann's kernel $\Phi$ is not in the class; this follows from the theorem of Rodgers and Tao that the de Bruijn Newman constant is nonnegative. New in this book.
- [Brownian exit time limit: the reciprocals of the even derivatives of Xi, rescaled, converge to 1 over cosh of the square root of 2s](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocals_of_derivatives_of_xi_converge_to_the_laplace_transform_of_the_brownian_exit_time) (Volume I, Proposition 23.3.1, page 666; proved): For $\psi_n(s)=\Xi^{(2n)}(0)/\Xi^{(2n)}(i\sqrt{2s}/m_n)$, $\psi_n(s)\to1/\cosh\sqrt{2s}$ locally uniformly off the poles, the Laplace transform of the exit time of Brownian motion from $(-1,1)$, whose Thorin atoms $c_k^2/2$ are approached by the smallest atoms of $\psi_n$; under RH each $\psi_n$ is a GGC transform and the clocks converge in law. New in this book.
- [Conjecture: the Edgeworth rate of convergence of the zeros and clocks of the derivatives of Xi](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#conjecture_on_the_edgeworth_rate_of_convergence_of_the_derivative_clocks) (Volume I, Remark 23.3.3, page 667; open): The $k$th positive zero of $\Xi^{(2n)}$ is conjectured to satisfy $z_{k,n}m_n=c_k+\kappa_nc_k^3/(6m_n^3)(1+o(1))$ and the distance of $\psi_n$ from $1/\cosh\sqrt{2s}$ is $\sup_{x\le\sqrt{2S}}\frac{x^2}{2\cosh x}\cdot\sigma_n^2/m_n^2\,(1+o(1))$; the constant $0.53222$ is computed. New in this book.
- [Keiper Li coefficients as values of the Thorin functional](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#keiper_li_coefficients_as_thorin_functional) (Volume I, Proposition 23.6.1, page 673; proved): With no hypothesis on the zeros, each Keiper Li coefficient is the Thorin functional of the zeros paired with an explicit rational function that is nonnegative on the positive axis, so Li's criterion is nonnegativity of that functional on the cone spanned by these functions. New in this book.

chapters.title: A route to the Riemann Hypothesis
chapters.summary:
This chapter assembles the results of Volume I into one route to the Riemann Hypothesis (RH), says which steps are theorems, and states the one step that is missing. It does not prove RH. The route is the descent in level of the Thorin measure, read in the language of Lee and Yang. Its target has six equivalent forms: descent in level of the minimum of the Thorin density, backward Cauchy deconvolution through positive measures, a Cauchy mixture of one width, Weil positivity, ferromagnetism of the Pólya law (characteristic function in the Laguerre Pólya class), and the two spin Lee and Yang property, equivalently monotonicity of $|\xi(\sigma+it)|$ in $\sigma\ge\frac12$. The top of the descent, level one or the coupling $\frac12$, is proved with no hypothesis in each form, including a positive Cauchy mixture at level one, ferromagnetism of the cosh tilted law for couplings $w\ge\frac12$, and the Lee and Yang threshold of the truncated Euler product. The step from the top to the critical line passes three filters that rule out finite computations, arguments that ignore the Euler product (the Davenport and Heilbronn function has zeros off the line), and properties preserved by Gaussian damping. As a benchmark, curves over finite fields are decided by Hasse and Weil positivity through finite Toeplitz sections. For $\zeta$ the chapter reports certified ball arithmetic runs: a Weil ladder on 266 cells, Davenport and Heilbronn sections that become negative, the Hankel test, and positivity of the Thorin density with no zero on lines $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha$ up to height $10^4$ and $10^5$ at several levels (certified). The missing step is a positive form built from the primes with the values of Weil's functional (the Hilbert and Pólya problem), followed by a work plan.

#### From the literature

- Lee and Yang theorem and ferromagnetic couplings (Lee and Yang 1952; Lieb and Sokal, as restated by Kozitsky)
- Hasse and Weil: the Riemann Hypothesis for curves over finite fields, via the Hodge index theorem
- $\Lambda\ge0$ for the de Bruijn Newman constant (Rodgers and Tao 2020)
- the Davenport and Heilbronn function with zeros off the critical line (Davenport and Heilbronn)
- the Hilbert and Pólya programmes (Connes; Deninger)

New in this book.
- [A Curie Weiss coupling of strength a shrinks the zero strip of Xi type laws from delta squared to delta squared minus a](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#curie_weiss_coupling_shrinks_strip) (Volume I, Proposition 24.5.1, page 686; proved): Coupling laws of Xi type with a Curie Weiss weight of strength a puts the zeros of the partition function in a strip whose squared half width is the maximum of delta squared minus a and zero. chapters.title: Conclusions and open problems of the theory
chapters.summary:
How far does the Thorin approach to the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) reach, and what can computation add? The chapter summarises the theory and sets out a path along the basepoint $\alpha$ of the shifted clock of the reciprocal Xi function, with Laplace transform $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt u)$. For $\alpha\ge1$ it is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) with positive Thorin measure, with no hypothesis. For $\frac12<\alpha<1$ the GGC property is equivalent to a zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha$, and at the centre it is RH (Lagarias positivity). The gap is one positivity statement uniform in the height and the resolution. The chapter discusses the zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ announced in October 2026 and not refereed, the sine squared lemma, five computational work packages (among them certified Thorin densities in ball arithmetic, twisted Riesz filters, margins against the circular unitary ensemble, the almost GGC defect), closed routes, the reach of finite information (a perturbation theorem with off line zeros) and what a proof must supply. It assembles the route from the whole theory and states the missing step as a single positivity problem. It poses open problems from free probability, on Jensen polynomials, Laguerre expansions, Jacobi parameters, the Hankel test and zero collisions along the de Bruijn Newman flow, and the heat trace ladder, and sorts the open problems and lessons of the Thorin programme. Nothing here proves RH.

#### From the literature

- The Thorin representation of generalised gamma convolutions (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992)
- The criteria of Riesz (1916), Weil (1952), Li (1997; Keiper 1992) and Lagarias (1999)
- The de Bruijn Newman constant (de Bruijn 1950; Rodgers and Tao 2020; Platt and Trudgian 2021)
- Conrey and Li (2000) on a false positivity condition
- Zero density estimates (Ingham 1940; Huxley 1972; Guth and Maynard 2026)
- RH verified to height $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021); Odlyzko's tables of zeros (1987; 2001)
- The finite free convolution (Marcus, Spielman and Srivastava 2022) and the Upsilon transform (Barndorff-Nielsen and Thorbjørnsen 2004)
- The half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ is announced by OpenAI (2026) and is not refereed, so results using it are conditional

#### New results

This chapter summarises results proved earlier; its catalogued entries are open problems, among them the range of orders of the derivative signs of the heat trace.
- [Jensen polynomials of the Pólya moments as finite free products (open problem)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_jensen_polynomials_as_finite_free_products) (Volume I, Problem 25.1, page 700; open): Find factorisations of the normalised coefficients of the Jensen polynomials of the Pólya moment sequence into two real rooted polynomials, which would give real zeros, or show that none exist with factors of a given kind. New in this book.
- [Laguerre and Meixner Pollaczek expansions of the Pólya density (open problem)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_laguerre_meixner_pollaczek_expansions_of_polya_density) (Volume I, Problem 25.2, page 700; open): Find a variable in which the Pólya density or the Xi function has an expansion in Laguerre or Meixner Pollaczek polynomials with positive coefficients and truncations with only real zeros. New in this book.
- [Jacobi parameters of the zero measure and the local semicircle model (open problem)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_jacobi_parameters_of_zero_measure_and_local_semicircle_model) (Volume I, Problem 25.3, page 701; open): Prove under the Riemann Hypothesis that the Jacobi parameters of the measure of the inverse squared ordinates satisfy alpha_n ~ 2 beta_n ~ L_n/2, a spectral form of the Riemann von Mangoldt formula, and explain the scatter of the ratios. New in this book.
- [Order at which a zero collision is registered by the Hankel test (open problem)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_order_at_which_a_zero_collision_is_registered_by_hankel_test) (Volume I, Problem 25.4, page 701; open): Find the rule giving the order of the Hankel matrix at which the collision of a pair of zeros along the de Bruijn Newman flow is registered, and follow the failure times of the Hankel test to orders of a few hundred. New in this book.
- [Unconditional brackets for the collision times of zeros along the de Bruijn Newman flow (open problem)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_unconditional_collision_brackets_for_de_bruijn_newman_flow) (Volume I, Problem 25.5, page 701; open): Find a priori control of the nonreal zeros of the heat evolved Xi function at negative times so that the book's brackets for collision times become statements computed from the Xi function at time zero alone. New in this book.
- [Extending the derivative sign ladder of the heat trace without new information on the zeros (open problem)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_moving_derivative_sign_ladder_of_heat_trace_without_new_zeros) (Volume I, Problem 25.6, page 701; open): Find a mechanism, for instance a functional equation for the law of the clock under the Upsilon transform, that extends the proved ranges of derivative signs of the heat trace without further information on the zeros. chapters.title: Notation
chapters.summary:
This appendix is the notation reference of Volume I. Seven tables list the symbols used in more than one section, with their meaning and the place where each is defined. The first five cover the whole volume and record the second meanings that some letters carry in particular chapters (for example $\eta$ is a tilted height, Dedekind's eta function or Dirichlet's eta function); the last two give the separate notation of the sections on Bosch's theorem and of the chapters on the reciprocal zeta function. Conventions: the clock is a function of $u=s^2$; its Thorin measures live in a variable $z$, in which the atoms of $U_{\mathrm{RH}}=\sum_{\gamma>0}\delta_{\gamma^2}$ sit at the squared ordinates $\gamma^2$, and the chart $\theta=\sqrt z$ puts them back at the ordinates; a resolution $\varepsilon>0$ means the basepoint $\alpha=\tfrac12+\varepsilon$; a zero is $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$. Sums and products over $k$ run over the pairs $\{\rho,1-\rho\}$.

#### From the literature

None.

#### New results

This appendix fixes notation and states no result.

No new results of this appendix are catalogued.

#### Key terms

chapters.title: What computation can and cannot decide
chapters.summary:
What can a computation of the Thorin measure of the reciprocal Xi function establish about the Riemann Hypothesis (RH), and what can a finite computation never decide? The chapter opens Volume II by describing the path to RH as a descent in level: the Thorin measure at level $\theta$ is positive exactly when $\zeta$ has no zero with real part above $\theta$, and the Cauchy deconvolution from level one to the critical line is the computation the volume carries out. It then makes the limits of finite information precise. On the window below height 200 the Pólya route finds 79 zeros and an argument principle count, and the computed minimum of the Thorin density sits at the origin, where it is of order the resolution, so near the critical line positivity is never won by a fixed margin. The sine squared decomposition of the Thorin bracket into drift, archimedean, pole and prime pieces shows how the prime side amplifies errors near the basepoint one. A perturbation theorem replaces two close zeros on the line by a quadruple off it and gives an entire function with the order, type and symmetry of $\xi$ whose heat trace passes the finite tests (Hankel blocks, derivative signs to order $10^{17}$, small time expansion); for each such test the first failing order is computed on windows of low height. A finite computation can refute RH by certifying a zero off the line, can certify that windows are clean, and can measure a margin at a stated resolution and height, but cannot measure a distance to RH. The chapter also gives spacings of zeros against the Gaussian unitary ensemble and a short history of computations of the zeros of $\zeta$ from Riemann, Gram and Backlund to the verification of RH below height $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021), with the notation of the book. Results using the unrefereed October 2026 zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>7/8$ are conditional.

#### From the literature

- Verification of RH below height $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021) and the early computations of the zeros (Riemann, Gram 1903, Backlund 1914, Hutchinson 1925, Titchmarsh 1936, Turing 1953, Lehmer 1956, Rosser, Yohe and Schoenfeld 1969, van de Lune, te Riele and Winter 1986, Gourdon 2004)
- Odlyzko's computations near the $10^{12}$th zero and the Odlyzko and Schönhage fast evaluation of $\zeta$ (Odlyzko 1987; Odlyzko and Schönhage 1988)
- The perturbation of $\xi$ that passes the finite tests of the heat trace and the Hankel and derivative sign results (Polson 2017; Polson 2026)
- The sine squared lemma and the canonical measure of $\log\xi$ (Polson 2017; Polson 2026)
- The criterion of Balazard, Saias and Yor (1999) and Lagarias's positivity criterion (Lagarias 1999)

#### New results

Results of this chapter, with their status.

- [Four off line zeros that pass the finite heat trace tests](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#off_line_perturbation_passing_finite_heat_trace_tests) (Volume II, Theorem 1.4.1, page 8; proved): Moving a close pair of zeros of xi on the critical line to four zeros at distance one quarter off the line gives an even entire function whose heat trace still passes the finite tests (infinite divisibility, self decomposability, log convexity, and at large heights positive Hankel blocks and derivative signs up to order 10^17). First stated in Polson (2017, version 24 of 2026), On Hilbert's 8th problem, arXiv:1708.02653.
- [A pair of zeros off the line at the height of a line zero: its contribution to the density at resolution epsilon is positive exactly when epsilon is below d over sqrt 3 or above d](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#pair_of_zeros_off_the_line_at_the_ordinate_of_a_line_zero_is_positive_for_resolution_below_d_over_sqrt_3_or_above_d) (Volume II, Proposition 1.4.2, page 13; proved): The zeros $\frac12$ and $\frac12\pm d$ at one ordinate contribute to $\pi\rho_\varepsilon$ a rational function that is positive at every $\theta$ if and only if $\varepsilon<d/\sqrt3$ or $\varepsilon>d$; so when every off line zero shares its ordinate with a line zero and the distances have a positive infimum $d_0$, the density is positive on every line with $0<\varepsilon<d_0/\sqrt3$ although zeros lie to the right of it. New in this book.
- [Certified zero of a Mellin transform closes the Bernstein Pick route to RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#bernstein_pick_route_closed_by_certified_zero) (Volume II, Theorem 1.4.3, page 14; proved): A certified simple zero of the meromorphically continued Mellin transform M of the Pólya density near -8.494 + 2.938i gives the canonical interpolant of the moment ratios a nonreal pole, so no Bernstein interpolant is a complete Bernstein function and the Bernstein Pick route to RH is closed. First stated in Polson (2017, version 24 of 2026), On Hilbert's 8th problem, arXiv:1708.02653.
- [Local model for the first failing derivative order of the heat trace near an off line quadruple](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#first_failing_derivative_order_local_model_off_line_quadruple) (Volume II, Proposition 1.4.4, page 15; proved): To leading order, if two consecutive zeros of xi on the line are replaced by an off line quadruple at distance $\delta$ from the line and height $g$, with $\Delta$ the larger gap to the nearest line zeros and $\delta\ll\Delta\ll g$, the first derivative order at which a sign fails, for the heat trace restricted to the quadruple and its two neighbouring zeros on the line, is $k^*=\omega^*g^2/(2\delta\Delta)$, about $\frac\pi4g^2/(\delta\Delta)$, at a time depending on $\delta$ and $\Delta$ only; the comparison of this time with the seven certified failure times of the book's table, within 0.20 to 2.76 per cent, is a computation. New in this book.

chapters.title: Evaluating the Xi function in ball arithmetic
chapters.summary:
This chapter asks how to evaluate the Riemann xi function $\xi$ and its derivative at complex arguments, the raw material for computing the Thorin density at every resolution. The Pólya route applies the trapezoid rule to Pólya's integral $\Xi(\theta)=\int\Phi(u)\cos(\theta u)\,du$. It needs neither primes nor zeros and is spectrally accurate because the Pólya kernel $\Phi$ is analytic in the strip $|\operatorname{Im}u|<\pi/4$. The evaluator is two fixed polynomials in Arb ball arithmetic; below height 200 it gives about 60 correct digits and recovers the 79 zeros, with the count read from the argument principle. Cancellation costs about $0.341\,\theta$ digits at height $\theta$; tilting the contour into the strip reduces the loss to about $\delta\theta/\log 10$ digits and gives 25 digits of the Thorin density at height 5000. The chapter compares the route with the Riemann Siegel formula, the Odlyzko Schönhage algorithm and Turing's method, resolves the Lehmer pair near height 7005, reads the count $N(1000)=649$ from the Thorin mass, and ends with a worked computation from the theta series to the first zero, followed by exercises. Ball radii certify rounding only, so the results are computed, not certified.

#### From the literature

- The exponentially convergent trapezoid rule (Trefethen and Weideman 2014)
- Arb ball arithmetic (Johansson 2017)
- The Riemann Siegel formula (Siegel 1932; Gabcke 1979)
- Gram points and Gram's law (Gram 1903), Rosser's rule (Rosser, Yohe and Schoenfeld 1969) and their failures (Brent 1979; Trudgian 2011)
- Backlund's count (Backlund 1918; Hutchinson 1925)
- Turing's method (Turing 1953; Lehman 1970; Trudgian 2011)
- The Odlyzko Schönhage algorithm (Odlyzko and Schönhage 1988)

- The verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021)

#### New results

The tilted Pólya representation is new in the book. Digit counts, timings and zero counts are computed, with ball arithmetic certifying rounding only.

- [Tilted Pólya representation of xi and its derivative](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#tilted_polya_representation_of_xi) (Volume II, Proposition 2.1.1, page 21; proved): Moving the line of integration of Pólya's integral into the strip of analyticity of the Pólya kernel gives exact integral formulas for $\xi$ and $\xi'$ on a line at distance $\delta$ from the edge of the strip, with kernel bounds of order $\delta^{-5/2}$. chapters.title: The Thorin measure at finite resolution
chapters.summary:
This chapter asks what finite computations of the Thorin density $\rho_\varepsilon$, the Poisson smoothing of the zeros of $\xi$, can establish about the Riemann Hypothesis (RH). On the window below height 200, where the 79 zeros are known, it measures the distance from the computed Thorin measure to the discrete measure demanded by RH. Raw total variation is maximal, matched total variation sits at a numerical floor of about $3.7\times10^{-9}\varepsilon$, and cell distance, mass defect and heat trace error vanish linearly in the resolution $\varepsilon$. The chapter proves the first order mass defect, closed form signatures of an off line zero (including a square root law), a Littlewood identity, and a zero density identity that counts the zeros to the right of any line from the cumulative Thorin mass (at $\varepsilon=\frac12$, Backlund's count with the vertical side on $\operatorname{Re}s=1$). It shows that the sine squared lemma and Selberg's smoothed explicit formula give the Thorin density from the primes only at a cost exponential in $1/\varepsilon$, and explains why a finite computation can refute RH by certifying a zero off the line but cannot measure a distance to RH. Exercises close the chapter. Propositions are proved, and the tables of distances, masses and counts at height 200 are computed, not certified.

- Lagarias's criterion (Lagarias 1999)
- the argument principle count, the Riemann von Mangoldt formula and Littlewood's lemma (see Titchmarsh 1986)
- Backlund's method (Backlund 1918) and Turing's method (Turing 1953; Lehman 1970; Trudgian 2011)
- Selberg's smoothed explicit formula (Selberg 1946)
- Weil's positivity criterion (Weil 1952)
- zero density estimates (Ingham 1940)
- the verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021)

#### New results

The propositions below are new in the book, except where credited above.

- [Mass defect of the Thorin measure on a window](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_mass_first_order_defect) (Volume II, Proposition 3.1.2, page 36; proved): When every zero up to height $\Theta$ lies on the critical line, the Thorin mass of the window $(0,\Theta^2]$ equals the zero count $N(\Theta)$ minus $(\varepsilon/\pi)\,\Xi'(\Theta)/\Xi(\Theta)$ up to a remainder of order $\varepsilon^2$. New in this book.
- [Signatures of an off line zero in the Thorin density](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#off_line_zero_signatures) (Volume II, Proposition 3.2.1, page 39; proved): The effect of an off line pair of zeros on the Thorin density is computed in closed form: a displacement that keeps the count has total variation $\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{4\pi}(\delta/\varepsilon)^2$ per displaced zero to leading order for $\delta<\varepsilon$, an omitted pair has total variation $\frac4\pi\arcsin(\varepsilon/\delta)$, and a displaced zero has negative mass $\frac1\pi\arcsin(\varepsilon/\delta)$, the last two for $\delta>\varepsilon$; the quadratic growth of the first is the square root law of Polson (2026). - [Littlewood identity for the cumulative Thorin mass](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#littlewood_identity_thorin_mass) (Volume II, Proposition 3.3.1, page 42; proved): The cumulative Thorin mass at resolution $\varepsilon$ is $\pi^{-1}$ times the derivative in $\varepsilon$ of the integral of $\log|\xi|$ along the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\frac12+\varepsilon$, which links the mass to the integral of $\log|\xi|$ on the critical line. chapters.title: The de Bruijn Newman flow computed from the Pólya density
chapters.summary:
The de Bruijn Newman flow reads the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) from a deformation of the Pólya kernel: multiplying the kernel by a Gaussian factor turns $\Xi$ into a family of entire functions $H_t$ that evolve by the backward heat equation, and RH is the statement that no two zeros collide at positive time, equivalently that the de Bruijn Newman constant $\Lambda$ equals zero (Rodgers and Tao proved $\Lambda\ge0$). The Pólya route computes $H_t$ at the cost of $\Xi$. The chapter follows zeros backward to their collisions: the zeros move as unit charges with logarithmic repulsion, a closed form for the velocity at $t=0$ is derived through Hardy's function $Z$, and two collisions are computed from the Pólya kernel. The Hankel (Stieltjes moment) test along the flow is the Thorin positivity of the tilted clock. Collision times are bracketed with Laguerre's quantity, Biane's theorem on free convolution with the semicircle law and a Riccati comparison, and compared with the Lehmer pair lower bounds for $\Lambda$ of Csordas, Smith and Varga. A zero free half plane gives $\Lambda\le2(\alpha-\tfrac12)^2$, conditional for the October 2026 half plane preprints. Later subsections treat the shielding deficit of Newton, the Thorin atoms of the tilted clock and Gaussian smoothing of reciprocal GGC transforms, high order Laguerre expressions along the flow, and forward persistence of real zeros. Results are proved unless marked computed (floating point) or conditional, and none of them settles RH.

#### From the literature

- The flow, its real zero property for $t\ge\frac12$ and persistence forward in time (de Bruijn 1950); the constant $\Lambda$ (Newman 1976)

- Newman's results on the monotonicity of the kernel logarithm (Newman 1991)

- [Upper bound (deadline) for the closing time of a gap between real zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#backward_heat_flow_collision_deadline) (Volume II, Theorem 4.1.14, page 64; proved): If the share Q of the other zeros and the sum W over the nonreal zeros stay below constants rho and W bar for which 3 rho plus the square root of 9 rho squared plus 6 W bar is less than the initial minimum of Laguerre's quantity over a gap between two real zeros, the gap closes, by a collision of one of its bounding zeros with another zero, no later than an explicit logarithmic time. chapters.title: The barrier method in Thorin form
chapters.summary:
This chapter states the barrier method of Polymath15, as used by Platt and Trudgian, translates it into the language of Thorin measures, and runs a small barrier check. The method proves upper bounds for the de Bruijn Newman constant $\Lambda$ by combining a verification of the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) to a height, an analytic zero free region for $H_{t_0}$ at large heights, and a barrier, a window of heights through which no zero of $H_t$ can pass for any time $t\in[0,t_0]$. It gave $\Lambda\le0.22$ (Polymath15) and $\Lambda\le0.2$ (Platt and Trudgian). The criterion is stated as Polymath15 print it, with de Bruijn's strip theorem and the canopy. In Thorin language its conclusion is that the shifted clock at $\alpha_0=\frac12+\frac{y_0}2$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) transform, so the reciprocal of $H_t$ is a GGC transform for every $t\ge t_0+\frac12y_0^2$ (proved); the barrier becomes the statement that no Thorin atom crosses a window bounded by four confocal parabolas with focus at the origin (proved), and a positive density $\operatorname{Re}(\xi_t'/\xi_t)$ on the barrier rectangle at every time is a sufficient certificate (proved). A check at height about $497.4$ for $t\in[0,0.2]$ and $y_0=0.2$ is run in floating point (computed) and certified in ball arithmetic for every $t\in[0,0.2]$. The Thorin form adds a geometry and a link to the phase diagram but no analytic input, and the method cannot reach $t=0$: every certified point lies on a level set $t+2(\alpha-\frac12)^2=c$ with $c>0$, and the corner of RH needs a zero free region for $\zeta$ itself.

#### From the literature

- the barrier criterion for upper bounds on $\Lambda$ (Polymath15 2019)
- $\Lambda\le0.2$ by a barrier at larger height (Platt and Trudgian 2021)
- de Bruijn's strip theorem (de Bruijn 1950)
- $\Lambda\ge0$ (Rodgers and Tao 2020)

#### New results

No new results of this chapter are catalogued.

#### Key terms

barrier method, Polymath15, de Bruijn Newman constant, Lambda, heat flow, H_t, canopy, strip theorem, Thorin measure, generalised gamma convolution, GGC, shifted clock, confocal parabolas, phase diagram, Platt and Trudgian, ball arithmetic, zero free region, Riemann Hypothesis, RH

chapters.title: The Thorin phase diagram
chapters.summary:
Which computations can see past the height to which the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) has been verified, and which comes closest to RH? The chapter answers with the Thorin phase diagram: the GGC region of points $(t,\alpha)$, with $t\ge0$ the time of the de Bruijn Newman heat flow $\xi_t$ and $\alpha\ge\frac12$ a basepoint, at which the shifted clock $\xi_t(\alpha)/\xi_t(\alpha+\sqrt u)$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution (GGC). It proves a threshold theorem along the flow, which extends the case $t=0$ of Polson (2026) (the clock is a GGC exactly when no zero of $\xi_t$ lies to the right of $\alpha$), and the phase diagram theorem, de Bruijn's strip theorem in Thorin form: the region is carried along parabolas by the flow, the de Bruijn Newman constant $\Lambda$ is the minimum of $t+2(\alpha-\frac12)^2$ over it, and RH is the corner $(0,\frac12)$. It sorts the routes of the book into finite information routes and three that reach every height, writes a winding number certificate for the point $(0.2,0.6)$ and runs its finite part in ball arithmetic, computes Thorin densities of $\xi_t$ from the Pólya integral, reports Weil Gram matrix and zero gas experiments, fits the cost of the flow route to the Polymath15 table, and poses five open problems.

#### From the literature

- The strip theorem and $\Lambda\le\frac12$ (de Bruijn 1950), $\Lambda<\frac12$ (Ki, Kim and Lee 2009), the constant $\Lambda$ (Newman 1976), $\Lambda\ge0$ (Rodgers and Tao 2020)
- The effective Riemann Siegel type approximation of $H_t$, $\Lambda\le0.22$ and the table of conditional bounds (Polymath 2019); RH verified to $3\times10^{12}$ and $\Lambda\le0.2$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021)
- Generalised gamma convolutions and their weak limits (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992)
- Weil's explicit formula and criterion (Weil 1952); Lehmer pairs (Csordas, Smith and Varga 1994)
- Explicit bounds for $S(T)$ (Backlund 1918; Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong 2022); the Biane, Pitman and Yor lattice (2001)
- The zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$, announced and not refereed (OpenAI 2026)

#### New results

Theorems and certified computations are proved, the cost law is conditional on its fitted form, and the problems are open.
- [Threshold theorem along the flow for the shifted clocks of the heat flow function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#threshold_theorem_shifted_clock_along_heat_flow) (Volume II, Theorem 6.2.3, page 97; proved): For every time $t\ge0$ and basepoint $\alpha\ge\frac12$, the shifted clock of the heat flow function $\xi_t$ is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution exactly when no zero of $\xi_t$ has real part above $\alpha$, and its Thorin measure is then an explicit sum of Cauchy kernels and atoms over the zeros. New in this book.
- [Minimum at the origin of the Thorin density of the shifted clocks along the heat flow](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#minimum_of_thorin_density_at_origin_along_heat_flow) (Volume II, Proposition 6.2.5, page 98; proved): For $t\ge\Lambda$ and basepoint $\alpha>\frac12$ the real part of $\xi_t'/\xi_t$ on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha$ is at most $(\alpha-\frac12)V_t$ at the real point, and, under explicit bounds on $\alpha-\frac12$, is at least its value there on explicit ranges (below the first zero ordinate, near zeros, in windows with many zeros, and for all smaller basepoints once at one basepoint $\alpha'$ it is at least $(\alpha'-\frac12)V_t$ at every height above the first zero ordinate), which gives the GGC property of the shifted clock with the constant part of its Thorin density removed; the parts other than (iv) follow a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book. New in this book.
- [Heat flow function as a shifted Gaussian average of Riemann's xi function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_average_as_shifted_gaussian_average_of_xi) (Volume II, Lemma 6.2.6, page 99; proved): In the upper half plane the heat flow function $\xi_t$ equals the Gamma factor times $e^{t\ell^2/4}$ times a Gaussian average $\zeta_t$ of $\xi(s+h)$ divided by $g(s)e^{h\ell(s)}$ over a complex shifted mean, with an explicit bound on the deviation of that quotient from $\zeta(s+h)$. New in this book.
- [Zero count of the heat flow function and a Backlund type bound on its argument term](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#zero_count_of_heat_flow_function_with_argument_bound) (Volume II, Proposition 6.2.7, page 100; proved): For every $t\ge0$ the number of zeros of $\xi_t$ with ordinate in $(0,T]$ equals an explicit main term plus an argument term $S_t(T)$, with the main term $\frac T{2\pi}\log\frac T{2\pi e}+\frac78+\frac t{16}\log\frac T{2\pi}$ up to $O((1+t\log T)/T)$, and $S_t$ is bounded by a Jensen formula estimate under two checkable hypotheses; the proof follows a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book. New in this book.

The book computes it only for $\theta_1(0.2)\le\theta\le10^4$ on a grid of step $0.05$ with a Gauss Hermite quadrature whose error is not bounded, so it is not certified there and not proved for larger $\theta$ (Problem on the bound for $\zeta_{0.2}'/\zeta_{0.2}$ on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=10$). The proof also uses $\frac35\theta_1(0.2)^2\ge(\frac{19}2)^2$, which the book takes from the tabulated value $\operatorname{Var}T_{0.2}=3.77203\times10^{-5}$ (computed, not certified) through $\theta_1(0.2)\ge(\operatorname{Var}T_{0.2})^{-1/4}=12.76$): If the real part of $\xi_{0.2}'/\xi_{0.2}$ at $10+i\theta$ is at least $\frac{19}2V_{0.2}$ for all $\theta\ge\theta_1(0.2)$ (computed, not certified, on $\theta_1(0.2)\le\theta\le10^4$), then the shifted clock of $\xi_{0.2}$ with the constant part of its Thorin density removed is a GGC transform for every basepoint in $[\frac12,10]$. - [Phase diagram theorem, de Bruijn's strip theorem in Thorin form](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#phase_diagram_theorem_de_bruijn_strip_theorem_in_thorin_form) (Volume II, Theorem 6.3.2, page 102; proved): The set of points $(t,\alpha)$ where the shifted clock of the heat flow function is a generalized gamma convolution is carried along parabolas by the flow (de Bruijn's strip theorem in Thorin form), the de Bruijn Newman constant is the minimum of $t+2(\alpha-\frac12)^2$ over it, and RH holds exactly when the corner $(0,\frac12)$ belongs to it. chapters.title: The Cauchy deconvolution operator
chapters.summary:
When can a measure be recovered from its convolution with a Cauchy density, and how stably? Cauchy deconvolution inverts the Poisson semigroup, so it is the Cauchy problem for Laplace's equation, a severely ill posed inverse problem, and it is the operator behind the Thorin measures of the book: the explicit formula is this deconvolution at level one half, and the Thorin family $\mathfrak U_\theta=P_{\theta-\theta'}*\mathfrak U_{\theta'}$ is the family of its partial deconvolutions. The chapter proves uniqueness for admissible measures, describes the range of convolution on $L^2$, gives a positive datum with only a signed source, and proves that the critical width of a positive datum, beyond which no positive source exists, is attained when finite. A nonnegative source at width $c$ exists exactly when the harmonic extension continues as a nonnegative harmonic function below the line (Herglotz and Riesz representation), which at the level one Thorin density gives Lagarias's criterion for the Riemann Hypothesis; for the zeta family the critical width is one minus the supremum of the real parts of the zeros. Stability is Hölder between levels by the three lines theorem, with the sharp exponent $(b+w)/(a+w)$ for finite signed sources, and logarithmic at the boundary for Sobolev sources; the minimax statistical rate is logarithmic over smoothness classes and polynomial, as an upper bound, for sources analytic in a strip. Atomic sources are a different problem: a finite sum of atoms gives a sum of damped exponentials, recovered by Prony's method and the matrix pencil with polynomial ill posedness, with a square root rate for two atoms merging symmetrically. The chapter surveys density deconvolution, Bayesian inverse problems, positivity preserving algorithms (EM, Richardson and Lucy), super resolution and analytic continuation in physics, and poses three open problems on estimating the critical width, on rates under positivity, and on three lines with positivity on a window.

#### From the literature

- The Cauchy problem for Laplace's equation as the original ill posed problem (Hadamard 1923)
- The Herglotz and Riesz representation of nonnegative harmonic functions on a half plane (Herglotz and Riesz; see Axler, Bourdon and Ramey 2001)
- Lagarias's positivity criterion for the Riemann Hypothesis (Lagarias 1999)
- Minimax logarithmic rates for supersmooth noise (Carroll and Hall 1988; Fan 1991) and deconvoluting kernel estimators (Stefanski and Carroll 1990); sharp rates for supersmooth targets (Butucea and Tsybakov 2008)
- Posterior contraction for linear inverse problems (Knapik, van der Vaart and van Zanten 2011, 2013); mixing measures (Chen 1995; Nguyen 2013; Gao and van der Vaart 2016)
- EM for positive inverse problems (Richardson 1972; Lucy 1974; Vardi and Lee 1993)
- Prony, the matrix pencil and super resolution (Barkhuijsen et al. 1987; Hua and Sarkar 1990; Donoho 1992; Candès and Fernandez Granda 2014; Schiebinger, Robeva and Recht 2018; Li and Liao 2021)
- Analytic continuation in physics (Jarrell and Gubernatis 1996; Fei, Yeh and Gull 2021)

#### New results

Results of this chapter, with their status.

- [Uniqueness of Cauchy deconvolution for admissible measures](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#cauchy_deconvolution_is_unique_for_admissible_measures) (Volume II, Proposition 7.1.1, page 125; proved): Two admissible measures with the same convolution with a Cauchy density of width $a$ are equal, by the semigroup property and Fubini's theorem. New in this book.
- [The range of convolution with a Cauchy density on L2, unboundedness of the inverse, and a positive bounded datum outside the range](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#range_of_cauchy_convolution_on_l2_and_the_failure_of_the_naive_description) (Volume II, Proposition 7.1.2, page 126; proved): On $L^2$ the range of $P_a*$ is the set of $u$ with $\int e^{2a|\omega|}|\widehat u|^2<\infty$, the inverse is unbounded between all Sobolev norms, and $2+\cos(x^2)$ is not $P_a*\mu$ for any admissible $\mu$ although its Poisson extension continues to an entire harmonic function. New in this book.
- [A positive datum with a signed source: the two atom example and its critical width](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#positive_data_with_a_signed_source_and_the_closed_form_of_the_critical_width) (Volume II, Example 7.2.1, page 126; proved): For $\mu=\delta_0-q\delta_d$ the datum $P_a*\mu$ is nonnegative if and only if $q\le(r-d)/(r+d)$ with $r=\sqrt{d^2+4a^2}$, so a positive datum can have a signed source and no positive one at width $a$; the partial deconvolutions are positive exactly up to an explicit critical width, with $c^*=\frac14$ for $q=9-4\sqrt5$, $a=\frac12$, $d=1$. New in this book.
- [The critical width of a positive datum for Cauchy deconvolution is attained when finite](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#critical_width_of_a_positive_datum_is_attained) (Volume II, Proposition 7.2.2, page 127; proved): For a nonnegative $u$ with $\int u/(1+x^2)<\infty$, a positive source at width $c$ exists for every finite $c\le c^*(u)$ and for no larger $c$, where $c^*(u)$ is the supremum of the widths with a positive source, which is attained when finite. New in this book.
- [A positive source exists at width c if and only if the harmonic extension continues as a nonnegative harmonic function to the half plane y > -c](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#existence_of_a_positive_source_iff_nonnegative_harmonic_extension_below_the_line) (Volume II, Theorem 7.2.3, page 128; proved): For a continuous $u\ge0$ with $\int u/(1+x^2)<\infty$, $u=P_c*\nu$ with $\nu\ge0$ if and only if the Poisson extension of $u$ extends to a nonnegative harmonic function on $y>-c$, with the linear term of the Herglotz and Riesz representation shown to vanish. New in this book.
- [Hölder stability of Cauchy deconvolution between levels by the three lines theorem, with sharp exponent](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#three_lines_holder_stability_of_cauchy_deconvolution_between_levels) (Volume II, Theorem 7.3.1, page 128; proved): $\|P_b*\mu\|_2\le\|P_a*\mu\|_2^{(b-b_0)/(a-b_0)}\|P_{b_0}*\mu\|_2^{(a-b)/(a-b_0)}$ for $b_0<b<a$, so data errors $\varepsilon$ at width $a$ and a bound $M$ at width $b_0$ give an error $\varepsilon^\kappa(2M)^{1-\kappa}$ at width $b$, and the exponent is attained. New in this book.
- [Sharp Hölder exponent (b+w)/(a+w) for Cauchy deconvolution of finite signed sources](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#sharp_holder_exponent_for_finite_signed_sources) (Volume II, Proposition 7.3.2, page 129; proved): For a finite signed measure $\nu$ of total variation at most $B$ and $h=P_w*\nu$, $\|P_b*h\|_2\le\sqrt2D^{1-\kappa}\|P_a*h\|_2^\kappa$ for $w\ge0$ and $-w<b<a$, with $\kappa=(b+w)/(a+w)$ and $D=B/\sqrt{2\pi(b+w)}$, and no larger exponent holds uniformly over this class. New in this book.
- [Two level Hölder bound for positive sources of Cauchy deconvolution with data in L2 on the line](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#two_level_bound_for_positive_sources_of_cauchy_deconvolution) (Volume II, Corollary 7.3.3, page 130; proved): For nonnegative sources with data $u_j=P_a*\mu_j\in L^2$ within $\varepsilon$, $\|P_b*(\mu_1-\mu_2)\|_2\le\varepsilon^\kappa((a/d)(\|u_1\|_2+\|u_2\|_2))^{1-\kappa}$ for $0<d<b<a$, with no a priori bound needed. New in this book.
- [Logarithmic stability of Cauchy deconvolution for sources in a Sobolev ball, sharp in order and in the constant](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#logarithmic_stability_of_cauchy_deconvolution_at_the_boundary_is_sharp) (Volume II, Theorem 7.3.4, page 130; proved): If $\|\mu\|_{H^s}\le M$ and $\|P_a*\mu\|_2\le\varepsilon$ then $\|\mu\|_2\le C_sM(2a/\log(M/\varepsilon))^s$ for $\varepsilon/M$ small, and no bound of smaller order holds uniformly over the Sobolev ball. New in this book.
- [Polynomial upper rate for density deconvolution with Cauchy noise and a target analytic in a strip](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#spectral_cutoff_deconvolution_of_cauchy_noise_with_a_target_analytic_in_a_strip) (Volume II, Proposition 7.4.1, page 131; proved): For Cauchy noise of width $a$ and a density with $\int e^{2w|\omega|}|\widehat f|^2\le2\pi M^2$, the spectral cutoff estimator with $\Omega=\log n/(2(a+w))$ has root mean integrated squared error $O(n^{-w/(2(a+w))})$, an upper bound. New in this book.
- [Problem: estimating the critical width of noisy positive data](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_estimating_the_critical_width_of_a_positive_datum) (Volume II, Problem 7.1, page 134; open): Estimate the critical width $c^*(u)$ from noisy data $u+$noise; for atomic sources it is the smallest pole width, but there is no uniform rate without weights bounded below because $c^*$ is discontinuous. New in this book.
- [Problem: positivity and rates for the Thorin family](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_does_positivity_alone_give_a_polynomial_rate_for_the_thorin_family) (Volume II, Problem 7.2, page 134; open): Positive sources $P_w*\nu$ with mass at most $B$ have polynomial exponent $w/(a+w)$ from smoothing and the mass bound, not from positivity; is the Thorin family in a class on which positivity alone gives a polynomial rate? New in this book.
- [Problem: Hölder bound between levels from data on a window for positive sources](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_three_lines_with_positivity_on_a_window) (Volume II, Problem 7.3, page 135; open): For positive sources and data known only on a window, does positivity give a Hölder bound between levels without an a priori bound below the target, with an exponent determined by the data? New in this book.

#### Key terms

chapters.title: Three families of generalised gamma convolutions and the deconvolution obstruction
chapters.summary:
This chapter asks where the difficulty of the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) sits in three one parameter families of generalised gamma convolutions (GGCs, Thorin measures) that contain the clock of Riemann's xi function as a boundary case: the Esscher tilt, the basepoint family of shifted clocks, whose Thorin density is a sum of Cauchy (Poisson) kernels over the zeros, and the de Bruijn Newman heat flow. It proves that the tilt is invertible and carries no information, that the basepoint family is a Poisson semigroup to the right of the zeros and fails to be one at the levels $\varepsilon\ge0$ with a zero to their right, at positive distance from the offsets of the zeros, and that RH is equivalent to deconvolving the Thorin density at such a basepoint into a positive measure, an unbounded operation. It gives the order $N^{\sigma_{\max}-\alpha}$ of the error of smoothed prime sums for Dirichlet L functions, sharp under GRH for $\alpha<\tfrac32$, and shows that no property preserved by Gaussian averaging and implying real zeros holds for any $H_t$. It derives the visibility curve of a hypothetical off line quadruple of zeros, in closed form in three lattice models, with about $\tfrac14\log(h/2\pi)$ levels needed at height $h$.

#### From the literature

- The Thorin representation of generalised gamma convolutions (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992)
- Lagarias's positivity criterion for RH (Lagarias 1999)
- The explicit formula for a smoothed sum over primes (compare Davenport 2000)
- De Bruijn's theorem on strips of zeros under the heat flow (de Bruijn 1950)
- Newman's theorem $\Lambda>-\infty$ (Newman 1976), the nonnegativity of the de Bruijn Newman constant $\Lambda$ (Rodgers and Tao 2020), the bound $\Lambda\le0.2$ after Polymath 2019 and the verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$ (both Platt and Trudgian 2021)
- Lehmer pairs and $\Lambda$ (Csordas, Smith and Varga 1994)
- A zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\tfrac78$ announced in October 2026 and not yet refereed (OpenAI 2026), used only conditionally

#### New results

The visibility curve and the level counts concern a hypothetical off line quadruple of zeros, among the zeros of $\xi$ or in lattice models (no off line zero is known); the other results concern $\xi$ and $H_t$.

- [Tilt family of the clock: the Thorin property at one tilt is equivalent to RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#tilt_family_of_the_clock_thorin_property_invariant_and_equivalent_to_rh) (Volume II, Theorem 8.1.2, page 139; proved): The Esscher tilt of the clock of xi maps generalized gamma convolutions to generalized gamma convolutions in both directions and leaves the imaginary part of the point attached to each zero unchanged, so the Thorin property at one tilt is equivalent to the property at every tilt and to RH (the case of the rational field of the tilt theorem for Dedekind zeta functions). New in this book.
- [Poisson semigroup of the basepoint family and its converse](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#poisson_semigroup_of_basepoint_thorin_densities_and_its_converse) (Volume II, Theorem 8.2.1, page 140; proved): The Thorin densities of the shifted clocks satisfy the Poisson semigroup identity from any level to the right of all zeros, with no hypothesis from level one half on, and the identity fails from every level $\varepsilon_0\ge0$ that has a zero to its right and lies at positive distance from the offsets of the zeros. New in this book.
- [Deconvolution form of RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#deconvolution_form_of_rh_thorin_density_at_basepoint_is_smoothing_of_positive_measure) (Volume II, Theorem 8.2.2, page 140; proved): RH holds if and only if the Thorin density at a basepoint to the right of all zeros is the Cauchy smoothing of a positive measure on the line, which is then the sum of unit point masses at the ordinates of the zeros, repeated according to multiplicity, and more generally the density deconvolves to a positive measure at level $\varepsilon_1$ exactly when no zero has offset $\beta-\tfrac12$ above $\varepsilon_1$. New in this book.
- [Thorin density near the critical line and Laguerre's quantity](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_density_near_the_critical_line_is_epsilon_times_laguerre_quantity) (Volume II, Proposition 8.3.1, page 144; proved): For small epsilon the Thorin density at level epsilon equals epsilon over pi times Laguerre's quantity, the negative second derivative of the logarithm of the absolute value of Xi, up to $O(\varepsilon^3)$, and a hypothetical off line quadruple at distance delta contributes minus two over delta squared to that quantity at its own ordinate, up to $O(\gamma^{*-2})$. New in this book.
- [Visibility curve of a hypothetical off line quadruple and its closed forms in three lattice models](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#visibility_curve_of_off_line_quadruple_closed_forms_in_three_lattice_models) (Volume II, Proposition 8.3.2, page 146; proved): At the ordinate of a hypothetical off line quadruple at distance delta, the Thorin density at level epsilon, when the other zeros contribute positively there, is negative exactly when epsilon is below delta and delta is below the visibility distance $\delta_{\mathrm{det}}(\varepsilon)$, which is given in closed form in three lattice models, increases with epsilon and exceeds epsilon by about Delta over pi at large epsilon; this is a theorem about a model with a hypothetical quadruple, not about the zeros of xi. New in this book.
- [Number of levels needed in the lattice models, one quarter of log h](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#number_of_levels_in_lattice_models_is_one_quarter_of_log_height) (Volume II, Corollary 8.3.3, page 148; proved): In the lattice models a single hypothetical off line quadruple at any distance up to one half is detected at its ordinate by the sign of Laguerre's quantity together with K levels, no test of this kind uses fewer than K levels, and K equals one quarter of log(h over 2 pi) plus O(log log h) at height h; this is a statement about a model, not about the zeros of xi. New in this book.
- [No averaging stable property carries real zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#no_averaging_stable_property_carries_real_zeros_for_the_heat_flow_functions) (Volume II, Corollary 8.4.2, page 150; proved): A property of entire functions that is preserved by Gaussian averaging and implies that all zeros are real holds for no function $H_t$ of the de Bruijn Newman family, at no real time and in particular not at time zero. New in this book.
- [Question: a certificate with a few levels for the actual zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_certificate_with_levels_for_the_actual_zeros) (Volume II, Problem 8.1, page 151; open): The book asks for levels whose positivity, together with positivity of Laguerre's quantity, excludes all off line zeros of xi up to a given height, and whether the number of levels is still of order log of the height when several off line zeros, irregular spacing and minima off the ordinates are allowed. New in this book.
- [Question: stability with an a priori bound that comes from the Thorin structure](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_stability_with_an_a_priori_bound_from_the_thorin_structure) (Volume II, Problem 8.2, page 151; open): The book asks whether the a priori bound that the three lines theorem needs on a zero free strip can come from the Thorin structure itself, for instance from positivity of the Thorin density at the levels already certified. New in this book.
- [Question: which positivity statements fail for negative heat time by a mechanism visible at finite height](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_seeing_the_boundary_of_the_heat_flow_at_negative_time) (Volume II, Problem 8.3, page 152; open): The book asks which positivity statements, for instance the GGC property of the clock or the Pólya frequency property of the density of $Z\sqrt{2T}$, can be shown to fail for negative heat time by a mechanism visible at finite height, as Lehmer pairs make the de Bruijn Newman constant visible. New in this book.
- [Question: the window of levels below delta, its distribution over heights and the sine kernel](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_distribution_of_the_window_of_levels_below_delta_and_the_sine_kernel) (Volume II, Problem 8.4, page 152; open): The book asks for the distribution over heights of the visibility distance and of the onset level at which a hypothetical off line quadruple at distance delta becomes visible, in terms of local zero statistics, compared with the prediction of the sine kernel. New in this book.

#### Key terms
