chapters.title: Deconvolution as a damped Weil criterion
chapters.summary:
This chapter asks whether the deconvolution theorem for the Thorin density of the Riemann $\xi$ function can be carried out: RH holds exactly when the Thorin density at a basepoint to the right of the zeros is the Cauchy (Poisson) smoothing of a positive measure on the critical line. The deconvolved object always exists, with no hypothesis: it is Weil's distribution, the zero sum of Weil's explicit formula, computed from the gamma factor, the pole and the primes. Its Fourier dual is a damped Weil criterion: Weil's quadratic form damped by $e^{-\varepsilon|x|}$ is nonnegative exactly when no zero has real part above $\frac12+\varepsilon$, so $\varepsilon=0$ is Weil's criterion, $\varepsilon=\frac12$ holds unconditionally, and the zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ announced in October 2026 (not refereed, not assumed here) is the case $\varepsilon=\frac38$. Restricting the test functions to support $[-a,a]$ gives a ladder of finite problems in the primes up to $e^{2a}$. If no zero has real part $\ge\frac12+\varepsilon$ and the Thorin density has a strict, nondegenerate global minimum at the origin, not approached at infinity (true at $\varepsilon=\frac12$, assumed below it), the least eigenvalue decreases to $2\xi'/\xi(\frac12+\varepsilon)$ at an algebraic rate in $a$. At $\varepsilon=0$, under RH, it falls faster than any power of $a$. The eigenvalue computations are numerical, not certificates, and what can be done and what is open is set out at the end.

#### From the literature

- Weil's explicit formula and positivity criterion (Weil 1952; Iwaniec and Kowalski 2004)
- positivity of Weil's form on short windows where no prime enters (Yoshida 1992), other test functions of small support (Bombieri 2000), and a second proof of Yoshida's range (Connes and Consani 2021)
- a certified lower bound for the least eigenvalue on a short window, an empirical decay law, and under RH an upper bound $\exp(-ae^a)$ for large $a$ (Zhu 2026, preprint)
- low zeros from the lowest eigenvector of a truncated form (Connes, Consani and Moscovici 2025, preprint)
- the nonnegativity of the de Bruijn Newman constant (Rodgers and Tao 2020)
- the time and band limiting operator (Slepian and Pollak 1961); the Bochner Schwartz theorem (Gel'fand and Vilenkin 1964)
- the half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ (OpenAI 2026, announced, not refereed)

#### New results

The book proves the hypotheses of the ladder theorem only at $\varepsilon=\frac12$; statements at smaller $\varepsilon$ are conditional on the stated hypotheses.

- [The deconvolved Thorin functional is Weil's distribution](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#deconvolved_thorin_functional_is_weil_distribution_no_hypothesis) (Volume II, Theorem 9.1.1, page 154; proved): With no hypothesis on the zeros, deconvolving the Thorin density of the shifted clock by the Cauchy kernel gives a functional that does not depend on the basepoint and equals the sum of a test function over the zeros, which Weil's explicit formula computes from the gamma factor, the pole and the primes. New in this book.
- [Damped Weil criterion](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#damped_weil_criterion_no_zero_above_one_half_plus_epsilon) (Volume II, Theorem 9.1.2, page 155; proved): For $0\le\varepsilon\le\frac12$, Weil's quadratic form damped by $e^{-\varepsilon|x|}$ is nonnegative on every test function exactly when no zero of $\zeta$ has real part above $\frac12+\varepsilon$, which is Weil's criterion for RH at $\varepsilon=0$, holds with no hypothesis at $\varepsilon=\frac12$, and at $\varepsilon=\frac38$ is equivalent to the half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ announced in October 2026 and not refereed. New in this book.
- [Ladder theorem: least eigenvalue of the damped Weil form on a window](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#ladder_theorem_least_eigenvalue_damped_weil_form_algebraic_rate_and_line_dichotomy) (Volume II, Theorem 9.2.1, page 157; conditional on Parts (a) and (b), for a level $0<\varepsilon<\frac12$: that the closed half plane $\operatorname{Re}s\ge\frac12+\varepsilon$ contains no zero of $\zeta$ (that $\varepsilon$ is to the right of the zeros). This zero free half plane is not proved for any $\varepsilon<\frac12$; the half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ announced in October 2026 and not refereed would give it for $\varepsilon>\frac38$ only.; Parts (a) and (b), for a level $0<\varepsilon<\frac12$: that $v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(\theta)>v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(0)$ for every real $\theta\ne0$ and $v_{1/2+\varepsilon}''(0)>0$, that is, that the Thorin density has a strict, nondegenerate global minimum at the origin. The book certifies this only up to a finite height, and the strict minimum at the origin on every line $\frac12<\alpha<1$ at once is equivalent to RH.; Parts (a) and (b), for a level $0<\varepsilon<\frac12$: that $\liminf_{|\theta|\to\infty}v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(\theta)>v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(0)$, that is, that the minimum is not approached at infinity. This is not known for $0<\varepsilon<\frac12$ without RH, under which it holds.; Part (c), first half (the nonnegativity and the decay of $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12,a)$): the Riemann Hypothesis. All hypotheses of (a) and (b) hold at $\varepsilon=\frac12$ with no assumption on the zeros, and the second half of (c), the negativity for large $a$ if RH fails, needs no hypothesis. For $\varepsilon>\frac12$ the chapter does not discuss whether the hypotheses on $v_{1/2+\varepsilon}$ hold): At a level $\frac12+\varepsilon$ to the right of the zeros where the Thorin density has a strict, nondegenerate global minimum at the origin not approached at infinity (true at $\varepsilon=\frac12$, an assumption below it), the least eigenvalue of Weil's form damped by $e^{-\varepsilon|x|}$ on test functions supported in $[-a,a]$ decreases to $2\xi'/\xi(\frac12+\varepsilon)$ at a rate between $c/a^2$ and $(\pi^2v''(0)/4+o(1))/a^2$, with $v(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\frac12+\varepsilon+i\theta)$, while at $\varepsilon=0$, under RH, it is nonnegative and $O(a^{-N})$ for every $N$, and if RH fails it is negative for all large $a$. New in this book.
- [Certified rungs of the ladder](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_certified_rungs_of_the_damped_weil_ladder_in_interval_arithmetic) (Volume II, Problem 9.1, page 163; open): Certify in interval arithmetic that the least eigenvalue of Weil's damped form on test functions supported in $[-4,4]$ is positive at $\varepsilon=0.05$, $0.1$, $0.2$ and $0.375$, and find how far in the window a certificate can be pushed. New in this book.
- [The exact rate of the ladder](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_exact_rate_of_the_damped_weil_ladder_at_depth_epsilon) (Volume II, Problem 9.2, page 163; open): Prove that the scaled excess of the least eigenvalue of the damped Weil form over its limit tends to the upper constant $\pi^2v''(0)/4$ of the ladder theorem, and find the next term; numerical fits are consistent with the limit and with a positive correction of order $1/a$, and neither is proved. New in this book.
- [The transition of the ladder at the line](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_transition_of_the_damped_weil_ladder_at_the_line) (Volume II, Problem 9.3, page 164; open): Describe the least eigenvalue of the damped Weil form jointly as the window half length $a$ tends to infinity and the depth $\varepsilon$ tends to zero, where the rate is algebraic for fixed $\varepsilon>0$ under the hypotheses of the ladder theorem and faster than any power of $a$ at $\varepsilon=0$ under RH. New in this book.
- [Uniformity of the damped Weil form from structure](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_uniform_positivity_of_the_damped_weil_form_from_structure) (Volume II, Problem 9.4, page 164; open): Find a structural reason, valid for all windows, why Weil's form damped by $e^{-\varepsilon|x|}$ is nonnegative on test functions supported in $[-a,a]$ for some fixed $\varepsilon<\frac12$, which by the damped Weil criterion would prove the zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac12+\varepsilon$. New in this book.

#### Key terms

chapters.title: The level one measure and the backward Cauchy flow
chapters.summary:
Can the Thorin measure of reciprocal xi be computed at level one from the primes alone, and can the Cauchy semigroup be run backward from it to the critical line? The chapter computes the level one Thorin measure of the Riemann xi function in closed form: a real analytic density equal to the real part of the logarithmic derivative of xi on the line Re s = 1, a smooth gamma part minus a compensated prime sum over the von Mangoldt function. Its Fourier transform has point masses at the logarithms of prime powers, and the identity with the zero description is a Weil type explicit formula for one test function. The band limited backward Cauchy flow, a Fejér regularised deconvolution with the multiplier $e^{(1-\theta')|\omega|}$, converges to the level $\theta'$ Thorin measure if and only if the zeta function has no zeros to the right of $\theta'$, so the Riemann Hypothesis is convergence at every $\theta'$ above one half. Positive deconvolution by the EM algorithm has a total Kullback Leibler residual that detects the same zero free half plane. Computations from samples of the density on Re s = 1 locate 109 zeros to 0.035, an EM injection test with controls separates an off line quartet, and a generative Bayesian computation under a GUE prior counts zeros in unit bins. A further section recovers the atoms by nonnegative least squares from the Pólya density at small resolution, where an off line pair gives a signature that no positive measure can reproduce. The chapter argues that none of this is a path to the Riemann Hypothesis.

#### From the literature

- Generalised gamma convolutions and the Thorin measure (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992)
- The explicit formula for the zeros (Weil 1952) and the equivalence of the prime number theorem error term with a zero free half plane (Titchmarsh 1986)
- The EM algorithm for positive linear inverse problems (Shepp and Vardi 1982; Vardi and Lee 1993) and its information geometry (Csiszár and Tusnády 1984)
- Montgomery's pair correlation (Montgomery 1973) and Odlyzko's computations of the zeros (Odlyzko 1987), the source of the GUE prior
- Generative Bayesian computation (Polson and Sokolov 2025)

#### New results

The closed form of the level one measure is proved; the numerical recoveries are computed in floating point and are diagnostics, not certificates.

- [The Thorin measure of reciprocal xi is absolutely continuous with the explicit density (1/pi) Re xi'/xi at every level from one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#level_one_thorin_measure_explicit_density_with_prime_sum) (Volume II, Theorem 10.1.1, page 167; proved): For every level $\theta\ge1$ the measure $\sum_\rho\mathrm{Cauchy}(\gamma_\rho,\theta-\sigma_\rho)$ has real analytic density $\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\theta+iv)$, at $\theta=1$ a gamma part minus a compensated prime sum, valid also at $v=0$. New in this book.
- [The Fourier transform of the level one Thorin measure carries the prime powers as atoms, an explicit formula for one test function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#fourier_transform_of_the_level_one_thorin_measure_is_a_sum_of_prime_atoms) (Volume II, Proposition 10.2.1, page 169; proved): As tempered distributions $\widehat{\mathfrak U_1}$ is the transform of the smooth part plus $1$ minus point masses $\Lambda(n)/n$ at $\pm\log n$, equal on the zero side to $\sum_\rho e^{-(1-\sigma_\rho)|\omega|}e^{-i\omega\gamma_\rho}$, which is a Weil type explicit formula. New in this book.
- [Dichotomy for the band limited backward Cauchy flow from level one: convergence at level theta' if and only if zeta has no zeros to the right of theta'](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#backward_cauchy_flow_converges_exactly_when_zeta_has_the_zero_free_half_plane) (Volume II, Theorem 10.3.1, page 171; proved): The Fejér band limited backward flow from the level one measure converges to the level $\theta'$ Thorin measure if $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta'$, and has no measure limit if it has a zero there, so the Riemann hypothesis is convergence at every $\theta'>\frac12$. New in this book.
- [Computation: the Fourier backward flow from samples of the level one density on Re s = 1 places a peak within 0.035 of each of 109 zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#computed_backward_flow_locates_109_zeros_from_samples_on_the_line_one) (Volume II, Result 10.3.1, page 173; computed): A the Arb library (python flint) computation, not a theorem, samples $u_1$ on $[0,400]$ from $\zeta$ and $\zeta'$ on $\operatorname{Re}s=1$ only and shows peaks within $0.035$ of the $109$ zeros in $100<v<300$ at $\theta'=\frac34$ and within $0.027$ at $\theta'=\frac12$; the sharp cutoff rings and the Fejér window does not. New in this book.
- [A positive solution of the Cauchy deconvolution of the level one density exists exactly when zeta has the zero free half plane, and the total Kullback Leibler residual detects it](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#positive_deconvolution_of_the_level_one_density_and_the_total_kl_residual) (Volume II, Proposition 10.4.1, page 175; proved): A positive measure $x$ with $P_{1-\theta'}*x=u_1$ exists iff $\zeta\ne0$ on $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta'$ (then $x=\mathfrak U_{\theta'}$), and the total discretised residual tends to $0$ in that case and stays bounded away from $0$ otherwise. New in this book.
- [Computation: the EM inversion of the level one density separates an injected off line quartet of zeros from a control](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#computed_em_injection_test_separates_an_off_line_quartet_from_a_control) (Volume II, Result 10.4.4, page 178; computed): EM runs of $10^4$ steps on windows of $u_1$ with two consecutive zeros replaced by a quartet at real part $\sigma$ show a residual floor near $7\times10^{-3}$ for $\theta'=0.75$, $\sigma=0.85$ against below $10^{-7}$ for a control, and slower decay than the control, without a floor in $10^4$ steps, for $\sigma=\theta'=0.75$ and for $\theta'=0.5$, $\sigma=0.75$; a finite run certifies neither alternative. New in this book.
- [Computation: generative Bayesian computation under a GUE prior counts the zeros of zeta in unit bins from the level one Thorin density](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#computed_gbc_under_a_gue_prior_counts_zeros_in_unit_bins_from_the_level_one_density) (Volume II, Result 10.5.2, page 180; computed): A computation, not a theorem: a quantile network trained on GUE simulations of the level one density gives rounded posterior median counts equal to the true number of zeros in 196 and 197 of 200 unit bins for two seeds, within one in all, with quantiles calibrated to about 0.05. New in this book.
- [Open problem: the data augmentation sampler and a generative Bayesian inversion with the EM reconstruction as a feature](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_implementation_of_the_data_augmentation_sampler_and_gbc_inversion_for_level_one) (Volume II, Problem 10.1, page 182; open): Run the data augmentation sampler for the real level one density, compare its posterior spread at $\theta'=0.75$ and $0.5$ with the EM estimate, and build a calibrated GBC inversion with zero positions as continuous outputs. New in this book.
- [Open problem: characterise the level one Thorin densities of functions of the Selberg class without reference to zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_characterisation_of_level_one_thorin_densities_in_the_selberg_class) (Volume II, Problem 10.2, page 182; open): Which densities of the form of the level one prime formula with coefficients $a_n\ge0$ on prime powers are level one Thorin densities of $\Xi(1)/\Xi(1+\sqrt s)$ with $\Xi$ in the Selberg class? New in this book.
- [Open problem: the rate of convergence of the backward flow and the exponential growth lower bound when a zero lies to the right](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_rate_of_the_backward_cauchy_flow_and_the_lower_bound_off_the_half_plane) (Volume II, Problem 10.3, page 182; open): Give the rate of locally uniform convergence of the band limited backward flow in $\Omega$ and $\theta'-\theta_0$, and show growth like $e^{(\sigma_{\max}-\theta')\Omega}$ up to polynomial factors when a zero lies to the right of $\theta'$. New in this book.
- [Open problem: a prior allowing off line zeros and the posterior of the offset delta at the real level one density](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_posterior_of_the_off_line_offset_delta_under_a_prior_allowing_off_line_zeros) (Volume II, Problem 10.4, page 182; open): Replace the GUE prior of the generative Bayesian inversion by one allowing zero pairs at $\frac12\pm\delta+i\gamma$ and train the quantile network to report the posterior of $\delta$ for each detected zero. New in this book.
- [One sided approach in the Dyck chain: the criterion implies RH, and conditionally on the lattice bias conjecture it fails for T above gamma 64](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#dyck_chain_one_sided_approach_criterion_fails_for_t_above_gamma_64_conditionally) (Volume II, Result 10, page 554; conditional on The lattice bias conjecture, that $F_n(s)=2\xi(s)-\frac{3s}{\sqrt{\pi n}}\xi(s-1)+O(1/n)$ locally uniformly on $\operatorname{Re}s>0$ (for the failure of the hypothesis)): If the Dirichlet polynomial of the Dyck chain converges to $2\xi$ locally uniformly on $\operatorname{Re}s>0$ and has no zero in $\frac12<\operatorname{Re}s<1$, $0<\operatorname{Im}s<T$ for large $n$ for every $T$, then RH holds (proved); under the lattice bias conjecture the zero free hypothesis holds for $T<\gamma_{64}$ and fails for every $T>\gamma_{64}$, so this criterion cannot prove RH along this chain. New in this book.

chapters.title: Complexity and acceleration of the backward flow
chapters.summary:
What does it cost to compute the Thorin measure of the Riemann zeta function at level $\theta$ by the backward Cauchy flow, and can the EM iteration be accelerated? The chapter treats the Cauchy deconvolution of the level one density to the Thorin measure at level $\theta'$ as a positive linear inverse problem solved by the EM algorithm of Vardi and Lee, and splits the cost into three layers: evaluating $\zeta$ on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=1$, the convex inversion and its log concave Bayesian sampling, and verification by Turing's method. It proves log concavity of the Poisson posterior, the precision needed, what EM computes, a rate for EM and local linear convergence (proved), infinite variance of the von Neumann and Ulam estimator, and the heat trace form of the Thorin measure. It gives a positivity theorem for the Thorin density, a mass deficit identity and a level mass function with jumps at off line zeros, and a certificate in ball arithmetic that $u_{3/4}$ and $u_{7/8}$ are positive up to height 1420 with exactly 1000 zeros below 1419.9. The global minimum of the Thorin density at the origin is shown at level 7/8, and uniformly for levels between 7/8 and 1, conditionally on the announced zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>7/8$ (unrefereed), with a level by level equivalence. Nesterov momentum and SQUAREM are tested against EM, with an a posteriori bound and a smoothed prime sum for $u_1$. The final sections work and list open problems; readings through the Hilbert and Pólya resolvent trace are heuristic.

#### From the literature

- Positive linear inverse problems and the EM algorithm for Poisson data (Vardi and Lee 1993; Csiszár and Tusnády 1984)
- Log concave sampling in polynomial time (Applegate and Kannan 1991; Applegate, Kannan and Polson 1990)
- Lagarias's positivity property of the xi function and the Riemann Hypothesis (Lagarias 1999)
- Fast evaluation of the zeta function (Odlyzko and Schönhage 1988; Hiary 2011)
- The Riemann Hypothesis verified to height $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021) and explicit zero counting (Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong 2022)
- Zero free half plane claims, unrefereed and unchecked here (OpenAI 2026; Liu 2026)

#### New results

Results using the announced half plane are conditional; the a posteriori certificate for window masses is the authors' own computation, was not rerun and is not entered.

- [Log concavity of the Poisson likelihood and of the gamma prior posterior in the discretised Cauchy deconvolution](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#log_concavity_of_the_poisson_posterior_for_the_backward_cauchy_flow) (Volume II, Theorem 11.2.1, page 193; proved): The Poisson log likelihood of $y=Ax$ is concave on the orthant, and with independent gamma priors of shapes at least one the posterior is log concave. New in this book.
- [The level one data must be supplied to absolute precision e to the minus (1 minus theta') Omega for the linear inverse](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#precision_required_for_the_level_one_data_in_the_backward_cauchy_flow) (Volume II, Proposition 11.2.2, page 193; proved): Resolving the Thorin measure at level $\theta'$ up to frequency $\Omega$ by the linear inverse needs the density $u_1$ to absolute precision $e^{-(1-\theta')\Omega}$, which is sharp. New in this book.
- [What EM computes for the backward Cauchy flow: the Thorin measure at level theta' when zeta has no zeros to the right of theta'](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#em_limits_converge_to_the_thorin_measure_if_and_only_if_no_zero_right_of_the_level) (Volume II, Proposition 11.3.4, page 197; proved): Under three growth conditions on the grids, the EM limits converge vaguely to the Thorin measure at level $\theta'$ with residual tending to zero if $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta'$, and the residual stays bounded away from zero if it has one. New in this book.
- [The von Neumann and Ulam Monte Carlo estimator for the backward Cauchy flow has infinite variance for small grid spacing](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#von_neumann_ulam_estimator_for_the_backward_flow_has_infinite_variance) (Volume II, Proposition 11.5.1, page 203; proved): For $t=h/(\pi(1-\theta'))<t_0=0.52219\ldots$ the operator $|I-A|$ has spectral radius above one and the estimator of the Neumann series $\sum_k(I-A)^ky$ has infinite second moment from every starting state; for $t>t_0$ the radius is below one. New in this book.
- [Subordinated heat trace: the Thorin measure at level theta is the heat flow of the zeros run to first passage times of Brownian motion](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_measure_is_a_heat_flow_of_the_zeros_run_to_a_first_passage_time) (Volume II, Proposition 11.6.1, page 205; proved): The Cauchy law is a Gaussian scale mixture over the first passage time of Brownian motion, so if $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta_0$ the Thorin measure at level $\theta>\theta_0$ is the sum over the nontrivial zeros of the heat flow of $\delta_{\gamma_\rho}$ run to the random time $T_{\theta-\sigma_\rho}$. New in this book.
- [The reciprocal xi transform at level theta is a GGC if and only if zeta has no zeros right of theta, if and only if the real part of xi'/xi is positive there](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_positivity_equivalent_to_zero_free_half_plane_and_positivity_of_xi_log_derivative) (Volume II, Theorem 11.9.1, page 209; proved): For $\frac12\le\theta<1$: $F_\theta(s)=\xi(\theta)/\xi(\theta+\sqrt s)$ is a GGC Laplace transform if and only if $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta$, if and only if $\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)>0$ on $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta$; for $\theta=\frac12$ the last equivalence is Lagarias's theorem. - [Mass deficit identity: twice the number of zeros right of the level equals the drop of the integrated density plus a boundary term](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#mass_deficit_identity_counts_zeros_right_of_the_level) (Volume II, Proposition 11.9.2, page 210; proved): For $\frac12<\theta<1$ and $T$ with no zero on the two segments, $2N(\theta,T)=M_1(T)-M_\theta(T)+\pi^{-1}\Delta_{\mathrm{top}}(\theta,T)$, an identity between an integer and computable integrals that decides the existence of zeros right of $\theta$ up to height $T$. - [Certified positivity of u_{3/4} and u_{7/8} on [0,1420] and 1000 zeros on the critical line below 1419.9, in ball arithmetic](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#certified_positivity_of_the_thorin_densities_at_levels_three_quarters_and_seven_eighths_up_to_1420) (Volume II, Theorem 11.9.6, page 216; computed): A computation in ball arithmetic at two precisions (96 and 160 bits) certifies that $u_{3/4}$ and $u_{7/8}$ are positive on $[0,1420]$ and that $\xi$ has exactly $1000$ zeros below height $1419.9$, all on the critical line and simple; this is a computer assisted result covering only this range, and the count of zeros is known (Platt and Trudgian). New in this book.
- [Global minimum of the Thorin density u_{7/8} at the origin, given the announced zero free half plane](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#global_minimum_of_the_thorin_density_at_level_seven_eighths_conditional) (Volume II, Theorem 11.10.2, page 219; conditional on The zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ for the Riemann zeta function, announced in the quasi Riemann hypothesis preprints (OpenAI 2026, Liu 2026), unrefereed and not checked for this book): Given that $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>7/8$, $\mathfrak U_{7/8}\ge u_{7/8}(0)\,dv$ with $u_{7/8}(0)=0.0055146635278\ldots$ and $u_{7/8}(v)>u_{7/8}(0)$ for $v\ne0$ off the ordinates of zeros on $\operatorname{Re}s=7/8$; the verification on $[13.5,1420]$ is a computation. - [Global minimum of u_theta at the origin for every level between 7/8 and 1, given the announced zero free half plane](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#global_minimum_of_the_thorin_density_uniform_in_the_level_conditional) (Volume II, Theorem 11.11.1, page 224; conditional on The zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ for the Riemann zeta function, announced in the quasi Riemann hypothesis preprints (OpenAI 2026, Liu 2026), unrefereed and not checked for this book. The monotonicity of $\theta\mapsto u_\theta(0)$ is unconditional): Given that $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>7/8$, for every $\theta\in[7/8,1]$ and every real $v\ne0$ off the ordinates of zeros on $\operatorname{Re}s=\theta$, $u_\theta(v)>u_\theta(0)$, so $\mathfrak U_\theta-u_\theta(0)\,dv\ge0$; unconditionally $\theta\mapsto u_\theta(0)$ is increasing on $[\frac12,\infty)$. - [Level by level theorem: a zero free half plane right of theta is equivalent to the global minimum of u_theta' at the origin for all theta' in [theta,1], with an explicit excess bound](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#level_by_level_global_minimum_equivalent_to_zero_free_half_plane_with_explicit_excess) (Volume II, Theorem 11.11.3, page 226; computed): For $\frac12<\theta\le1$, no zeros of $\zeta$ in $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta$ is equivalent to $u_{\theta'}(v)\ge u_{\theta'}(0)$ for all $\theta'\in[\theta,1]$; when they hold, the excess $u_{\theta'}(v)-u_{\theta'}(0)$ has an explicit lower bound whose numerical constants ($w^*=0.0294450$, brackets above $0.1014$ and $0.0151$) are computed; the direction from (i) to (ii) is computer assisted. chapters.title: The explicit formula as a deconvolution
chapters.summary:
Is the Guinand and Weil explicit formula the deconvolution that recovers the zeros of the Riemann zeta function from the level one density of the Thorin programme, and how well posed is that problem? The chapter shows that at level one half, under the Riemann Hypothesis (RH), the Cauchy deconvolution written in Fourier variables is the explicit formula: the multiplier $e^{|\omega|/2}$ turns the weights $\Lambda(n)/n$ into $\Lambda(n)/\sqrt n$. For a general measure the problem is exponentially ill posed, but for a sum of atoms a Gaussian tapered transform of the level one density is a sum of damped exponentials, one per zero, so Prony's method and the Hua and Sarkar matrix pencil recover ordinates and real parts. The functional equation makes the problem singular: off line zeros come in pairs at one half plus and minus $\delta$, the data depend on $\delta$ only through $\delta^2$, the real part is resolved at the rate $\tau^{1/2}$, and Bayes factors for the line against the pair grow like $\tau^{-1/2}$. Computations near height 200, at $3\times10^{12}$ (inside the Platt and Trudgian verified range, a demonstration) and at $10^{13}+100$ (above it, with 53 certified zeros on the line but no certified count or real parts) are reported, with five open problems. None of it is a path to RH: the method reads real parts and does not constrain them.

#### From the literature

- The explicit formula (Guinand 1948; Weil 1952), pair correlation (Montgomery 1973; Odlyzko 1987)
- The matrix pencil method for damped exponentials (Hua and Sarkar 1990), and Prony's method
- Super resolution by total variation minimisation (Candès and Fernandez Granda 2013, 2014), for positive measures without separation (de Castro and Gamboa 2012; Schiebinger, Robeva and Recht 2018), and its limits (Donoho 1992; Li and Liao 2021)
- Singular mixture models (Chen 1995; Nguyen 2013), verified linear algebra (Rump 2010), sparse ReLU posteriors (Polson and Ročková 2018)
- Verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021), Turing's method (Turing 1953; Trudgian 2011), unrigorous zeros at large height (Gourdon 2004; Odlyzko 1992, 2001), fast zeta evaluation (Hiary 2011)

#### New results

Statements are proved unless marked; the large height computations are computed in floating point, and the open problems are open.
- [The explicit formula for every smooth compactly supported test function, read as the deconvolution at level one half](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#explicit_formula_for_all_compactly_supported_test_functions_as_deconvolution) (Volume II, Theorem 12.1.1, page 247; proved): The Guinand and Weil explicit formula is proved for every test function in C_c^infty, even or not, in the form of the Cauchy deconvolution from level one to level one half, with the multiplier e^{|omega|/2} turning the weights Lambda(n)/n into Lambda(n)/sqrt(n). New in this book.
- [An unresolvable perturbation of the Cauchy deconvolution at width one half](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#unresolvable_perturbation_of_the_cauchy_deconvolution) (Volume II, Proposition 12.1.2, page 248; proved): Two positive measures at total variation distance one have data P_{1/2} convolved with them within epsilon of one function once 0.72 e^{-Omega/2} is at most 2 epsilon, so the deconvolution is exponentially ill posed for a general measure. New in this book.
- [The Gaussian tapered Fourier transform of the level one density is a sum of damped exponentials, one per zero](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#tapered_transform_of_the_level_one_density_is_a_sum_of_damped_exponentials) (Volume II, Theorem 12.2.1, page 250; proved): The tapered transform of the level one density equals a sum over the zeros of damped complex exponentials whose poles carry both the ordinate and the real part of each zero, plus an explicit remainder of order e^{-l^2 omega^2/2}; no hypothesis on the real parts is made. New in this book.
- [Posterior concentration for the atoms of the tapered transform model on a window](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#posterior_concentration_for_zeros_in_a_window_under_the_tapered_model) (Volume II, Theorem 12.4.1, page 254; proved): In the window model of the tapered transform with a spike free prior on the atoms, the posterior concentrates at the true zeros, including their real parts, at the rate of the noise, under hypotheses on bias and aliasing that do not hold at the settings of the chapter's computations, and it decides nothing about the Riemann hypothesis. New in this book.
- [The real part of an off line pair of zeros is resolved only at the rate tau to the one half](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rate_tau_to_the_one_half_for_the_real_part_of_a_pair_of_zeros) (Volume II, Theorem 12.5.2, page 257; proved): Because the functional equation forces off line zeros to come in pairs at one half plus and minus delta and the data depend on delta only through delta squared, the real part is resolved at the rate (tau/norm of t_perp)^{1/2} for data accurate to tau, and no test, whatever the method, does better. New in this book.
- [Bayes factors for a zero on the line against a pair at one half plus and minus delta](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#bayes_factors_for_the_line_against_a_pair_of_zeros) (Volume II, Theorem 12.5.4, page 261; proved): With the spike and slab prior on the pair the Bayes factor for the line against the pair grows like tau to the minus one half, against tau to the minus one for the single zero alternative the functional equation forbids, so the functional equation takes the square root of the evidence. New in this book.
- [The density at a level between one half and one is a signed sum of Lorentzians, and the Riemann hypothesis fixes every damping rate](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#levels_below_the_zeros_signed_lorentzians_and_poles) (Volume II, Proposition 12.8.1, page 268; proved): At a level theta in (1/2,1] that is not the real part of a zero, the density and its tapered transform are signed sums over the zeros with widths abs(theta minus sigma), and the Riemann hypothesis holds if and only if every damping rate equals theta minus one half. New in this book.
- [Matrix pencil on a window at height 3e12, a demonstration inside the verified range](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#pencil_at_height_3e12_inside_the_verified_range_demonstration) (Volume II, Result 12.8.6, page 270; computed): A computation by the authors, not rerun for the book, in which the matrix pencil on data at level 0.6 returned 52 components near height 3e12 with real parts within 1.4e-8 of one half, and a sign change certificate puts a zero on the line within 1e-7 of each ordinate; the count and the real parts are not certified, and the window lies inside the range verified by Platt and Trudgian. New in this book.
- [Matrix pencil on a window at height 1e13 plus 100, above the verified range, computed](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#pencil_components_above_the_verified_range_at_height_1e13) (Volume II, Result 12.8.7, page 272; computed): At height 1e13 plus 100, above the range verified by Platt and Trudgian, the matrix pencil on data at level 0.6 returns 53 components whose real parts lie within 4.7e-9 of one half, a floating point estimate and not a certificate. New in this book.
- [Fifty three certified zeros on the critical line in a window at height 1e13 plus 100, above the verified range](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#certified_zeros_on_the_critical_line_at_height_1e13_plus_100) (Volume II, Result 12.8.7, page 272; computed): A ball arithmetic scan certifies 53 sign changes of Hardy's function, hence 53 zeros of zeta on the critical line, in a window centred at 1e13 plus 100, above the range verified by Platt and Trudgian; the count of zeros in the window and the real parts are not certified, and nothing is certified off the line. New in this book.
- [Open problem, a rigorous matrix pencil with a perturbation bound under the model error](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_rigorous_matrix_pencil_perturbation_bound) (Volume II, Problem 12.1, page 273; open): State and prove a perturbation bound for the matrix pencil under the model error of the tapered transform, so that verified linear algebra on ball data encloses the zeros, and compare the enclosures with the winding number route. New in this book.
- [Open problem, characterise and remove the spurious pencil components at the edges of windows](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_spurious_components_at_window_edges) (Volume II, Problem 12.2, page 273; open): Characterise the few components that pass the amplitude filter at the edges of overlapping windows without being zeros, and prove under explicit hypotheses that agreement of two windows or the phase of the amplitude removes them. New in this book.
- [Open problem, windows at greater height with a rigorous argument principle and the cost of a full certificate](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_pencil_at_greater_height_with_rigorous_argument_principle) (Volume II, Problem 12.3, page 273; open): Make the argument principle rigorous at large height with an explicit bound for the derivative of zeta on a small disc, estimate the height at which a certified window is feasible within a day, and compare the many window scheme above 3000175332800 with Turing's method. New in this book.
- [Open problem, the adaptive prior in full: sine kernel process with marked ordinates and a spike and slab on the pairs](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_adaptive_prior_for_the_zeros_in_a_window) (Volume II, Problem 12.4, page 274; open): Place the sine kernel determinantal process on marked distinct ordinates, a pair counting as one point marked by its displacement, implement the posterior on the number, positions and marks of the zeros in a window, and report it separately from the argument principle certificate. New in this book.
- [Open problem, the constant in the tau to the one half rate and the design that maximises the information](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_design_maximising_the_information_for_the_real_part) (Volume II, Problem 12.5, page 274; open): Find the design of taper, bandwidth and level that maximises the information norm of t_perp over tau for a given cost, and determine how it scales with the height through the gaps to the neighbouring zeros. New in this book.

#### Key terms

explicit formula as deconvolution, Weil explicit formula, Guinand formula, Cauchy deconvolution, ill posed, super resolution, Prony method, matrix pencil, tapered Fourier transform, posterior concentration, Bayes factor, spike and slab, off line zeros, zero pairs, sine kernel, Hardy Z function, argument principle, Turing method, large height zeros

chapters.title: From level one to the critical line: particle filters and nested sampling
chapters.summary:
Can the Cauchy deconvolution from the Thorin measure $\mathfrak U_1$ at level one, which the Euler product makes accessible, to $\mathfrak U_{1/2}$, the object of the Riemann Hypothesis (RH), be carried out, and can particle filtering, generative Bayesian computation (GBC) and nested sampling help? At level one the Thorin density is unconditionally a positive mixture of Cauchy laws centred at the ordinates; at level one half it is the counting measure of the critical zeros, and RH says exactly that the Cauchy flow between them can be inverted through positive measures. Under RH, $u_1$ is the Cauchy smoothing of the zero counting measure and $\mathfrak U_\theta$ is the same smoothing at scale $\theta-\frac12$. The chapter proves the Cauchy transport identity with its signed defect from zeros off the line, a concentration inequality for the idealised Feynman Kac particle system along the Cauchy flow, and an unconditional bound on the negative part of $\mathfrak U_\theta$ through zero density (Selberg), with a converse showing that every zero off the line forces negative Thorin mass at least its isolation distance over $\log T$. It proves a de la Vallée Poussin inequality in Thorin form and a multilevel version whose zero free constant is capped at order $1/\log\gamma$, with a computed ceiling about $1/(11.3\log\gamma)$, so such positivity inequalities cannot reach beyond the classical zero free region. The Davenport and Heilbronn function, which has zeros off the line, serves as a test case: a particle filter fitted to levels one and 0.9 is pushed forward to level $3/4$, contour moments of $\xi'/\xi$ recover zeros in a rectangle by Newton's identities, and nested sampling scans heights up to $10^{10}$ for near failures of Thorin positivity. The filter, GBC and nested sampling runs are heuristic and local to windows of heights; interval counted windows are certified in ball arithmetic. Nothing here proves RH, and statements using the unrefereed October 2026 zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>7/8$ are conditional.

#### From the literature

- Positivity of the Thorin density as a zero free half plane for $\xi$ (Lagarias 1999; Sondow and Dumitrescu 2010; Matiyasevich, Saidak and Zvengrowski 2014)
- The formula of Balazard, Saias and Yor (1999)
- The Davenport and Heilbronn function (Davenport and Heilbronn 1936), its low zeros (Spira 1994; Balanzario and Sánchez-Ortiz 2007)
- Contour moments of the logarithmic derivative and Newton's identities for the zeros in a rectangle (Delves and Lyness 1967)
- Verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021) and the argument of zeta (Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong 2022)
- Selberg's zero density theorem (Selberg 1946)
- Zero free regions (de la Vallée Poussin; Vinogradov 1958; Kadiri 2005; Mossinghoff and Trudgian 2015; Mossinghoff, Trudgian and Yang 2024), the pairing of Stechkin (1970), and the constant 9.646 recalled from Rosser and Schoenfeld (1975), unverified here
- Feynman Kac particle models (Del Moral 2004; Cérou, Del Moral and Guyader 2011), sequential Monte Carlo (Chopin 2002; Del Moral, Doucet and Jasra 2006; Beskos, Jasra, Kantas and Thiery 2016), nested sampling (Skilling 2006)
- The zero free half plane at $7/8$, unrefereed and unchecked here (OpenAI 2026)

#### New results

Results of this chapter, with their status.

- [Cauchy transport: the density at level theta is the Cauchy smoothing of the critical zeros plus a signed defect from zeros off the line](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#cauchy_transport_identity_for_the_density_at_every_level) (Volume II, Proposition 13.1.2, page 276; proved): For every $\theta>\frac12$, $u_\theta=P_{\theta-1/2}*\mathfrak U_{1/2}+R_\theta$ where $R_\theta$ is the sum of the Cauchy pairs of the zeros off the critical line, which is the identity of densities at every level, with $R_\theta=0$ under the Riemann hypothesis. New in this book.
- [Local positivity of the Thorin density from any zero free region that narrows with the height](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#local_positivity_of_the_density_from_a_narrowing_zero_free_region) (Volume II, Corollary 13.1.3, page 277; proved): If every zero has $\sigma_\rho\le1-\eta(\lvert\gamma_\rho\rvert)$ for a nonincreasing $\eta$ with values in $(0,\frac12]$, then $u_\theta(v)>0$ whenever $\theta>\frac12$, $\theta\ge1-\eta(\lvert v\rvert+\frac12)$ and $\xi(\theta+iv)\ne0$. New in this book.
- [The density tends to the critical zero counting measure as the level tends to one half, zeros off the line being invisible](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#zeros_off_the_line_are_invisible_in_the_limit_of_the_density_at_one_half) (Volume II, Proposition 13.2.1, page 277; proved): As $\theta\downarrow\frac12$ the densities $u_\theta$ converge in the sense of distributions to $\mathfrak U_{1/2}=\sum_{\sigma_\rho=1/2}\delta_{\gamma_\rho}$, because the pair of a zero off the line tends to $-P+P=0$. New in this book.
- [The four zeros of the Davenport and Heilbronn function off the critical line below height 200 and their enclosures](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#zeros_of_the_davenport_heilbronn_function_off_the_line_below_height_200) (Volume II, Result 13.2, page 277; computed): Computation in ball arithmetic, certifying the zeros found by Spira (1994): the zeros of the Davenport and Heilbronn function $f$ with $0<\gamma<200$ off the line are exactly $0.8085171825+85.6993484854i$, $0.6508300806+114.1633427308i$, $0.5743560505+166.4793059132i$, $0.7242576946+176.7024612429i$ and their reflections, each certified as the only zero in a square of half width $10^{-16}$. New in this book.
- [A symmetric pair of zeros off the line exceeds a double zero on the line by a second order term in the deviation, growing like the fifth inverse power of the level](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#detectability_of_a_symmetric_pair_of_zeros_off_the_line_from_one_level) (Volume II, Proposition 13.3.1, page 281; proved): At the common ordinate a pair at real parts $\frac12\pm\delta$ exceeds a double critical zero by $\frac{2\delta^2}{\pi a(a^2-\delta^2)}$ at level $a=\theta-\frac12$, and $\int(\partial_a^2P_a)^2=\frac3{4\pi a^5}$, so the information about $\delta$ is second order and grows like $a^{-5}$. New in this book.
- [Open: the best resolution of the symmetric pair parameter from data at levels above a threshold](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_best_resolution_of_the_pair_parameter_from_levels_above_a_threshold) (Volume II, Problem 13.1, page 282; open): Posed as open: what resolution of $\eta=\delta^2$ is possible from levels $\theta\ge\theta_{\min}$, and does the pair parametrised particle filter reach it. New in this book.
- [Non asymptotic concentration inequality for a Feynman Kac particle system with multinomial resampling and fixed potentials under a ratio minorisation of the mutation kernels](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#non_asymptotic_concentration_of_the_particle_approximation_with_multinomial_resampling_under_a_ratio_minorisation_of_the_mutation_kernels) (Volume II, Theorem 13.5.1, page 288; proved): For the idealised system with multinomial resampling, fixed potentials and fixed kernels, $\mathbb P(\lvert\eta_n^N(f)-\eta_n(f)\rvert\ge x)\le2(n+1)\exp(-Nx^2/(2S_n^2))$ and the root mean square error is at most $S_n/\sqrt N$, for every $f$ of oscillation at most one; it does not cover the samplers run in the chapter. New in this book.
- [Concentration bound uniform in the number of tempering steps for the Cauchy flow when the parameters stay away from the levels](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#concentration_of_the_particle_filter_along_the_cauchy_flow) (Volume II, Corollary 13.5.4, page 290; proved): On the parameter space with zeros at distance at least $\varsigma$ from every level, the total log likelihood has finite oscillation $\Omega_\varsigma$, and with equal tempering increments and ratio minorised kernels the error probability is at most $2\exp(-\frac12Nx^2\epsilon^6e^{-2c})$ for every number of steps. New in this book.
- [What the density at level one determines: unique continuation for entire functions of order one, a counterexample without the order condition, and the Poisson inversion](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#one_level_determines_the_density_only_with_an_order_condition_and_inversion_is_unstable) (Volume II, Proposition 13.6.1, page 294; proved): For real entire functions of order at most one with zeros in the strip, equal densities at level one on an interval give equal logarithmic derivatives and equal densities at every level; the order hypothesis cannot be dropped, and under no zero at or beyond $\frac34$ recovering $u_{3/4}$ from $u_1$ multiplies the error at frequency $\omega$ by $e^{\lvert\omega\rvert/4}$. New in this book.
- [The negative part of the Thorin density at level theta is bounded by the number of zeros to the right of theta, and is a fraction T to the minus (theta minus one half) over four of its mass unconditionally](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#zero_density_controls_the_negative_part_of_the_thorin_measure) (Volume II, Theorem 13.7.1, page 295; proved): For $\frac12<\theta<1$, $\int_0^Tu_\theta^-\le N(\theta,T+\frac12)$ and $\mathfrak U_\theta((0,T])=\frac T{2\pi}\log\frac T{2\pi e}-2N(\theta,T)+O(\log T)$, so with Selberg's density theorem the negative part is a fraction $O(T^{-(\theta-1/2)/4})$ of the mass, unconditionally. New in this book.
- [Open: how negative can the Thorin measure be at a level between one half and one without assuming RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_how_negative_can_the_thorin_density_be_without_the_riemann_hypothesis) (Volume II, Problem 13.2, page 295; open): Posed as open: how negative $\mathfrak U_\theta$ can be for $\frac12<\theta<1$ without assuming the Riemann hypothesis. New in this book.
- [A separated zero off the line forces negative Thorin mass in a half disc to its left](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#a_separated_zero_off_the_line_forces_negative_thorin_mass) (Volume II, Proposition 13.7.2, page 297; proved): For a zero $\rho_0=\sigma_0+i\gamma_0$ of multiplicity $k$ with $\sigma_0>\frac12$, $\gamma_0\ge3$ and $r$ at most the minimum of $1$, $\sigma_0-\frac12$, half the distance to the nearest other zero and $k/(\pi(\mathrm{cr}(\rho_0)+C_1\log\gamma_0))$, the negative part of the density has integral at least $kr/\pi$ over the rectangle $[\sigma_0-r,\sigma_0]\times[\gamma_0-r,\gamma_0+r]$. New in this book.
- [Open: does a linear bound on the negative Thorin mass defect imply a zero density bound](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_converse_of_the_negative_mass_bound_for_zero_density) (Volume II, Problem 13.3, page 297; open): Posed as open: whether $\mathrm{def}(\theta)\le A(1-\theta)$ for all $\theta$ implies $N(\theta,T)\ll T^{A(1-\theta)+\epsilon}$. New in this book.
- [Two sided bound between the negative Thorin mass and the number of separated zeros to the right of a level](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#two_sided_control_of_negative_thorin_mass_and_zero_count_for_separated_zeros) (Volume II, Corollary 13.7.3, page 298; proved): The integrated negative mass $E(\theta_0,T)$ is at least $\frac r\pi N_{\mathrm{sep}}(\theta_0+r,T;c,\delta)$ and at most $\sum(\sigma_\rho-\theta_0)$ over the zeros to the right of $\theta_0$ up to height $T+\frac32$. New in this book.
- [Every zero off the line forces negative Thorin mass at least its isolation distance over the logarithm of the height](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#every_zero_off_the_line_forces_negative_thorin_mass_in_proportion_to_its_isolation) (Volume II, Theorem 13.7.4, page 299; proved): $E(\theta_0,T)\ge\frac1\pi\sum k(\rho)r(\rho)$ over the zeros to the right of $\theta_0$, hence $E(\theta_0,T)\gg\frac1{\log T}\sum\min((\sigma_\rho-\theta_0)\log T,d(\rho),1)$, so clusters cannot hide a zero off the line from the negative mass. New in this book.
- [Under a zero free half plane the Thorin density has a positive margin proportional to the distance from the abscissa and to the logarithm of the height](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#positivity_margin_of_the_thorin_density_under_the_quasi_riemann_hypothesis) (Volume II, Proposition 13.7.5, page 300; conditional on The quasi Riemann hypothesis QRH(theta_0), that is, that the Riemann zeta function has no zero with real part greater than theta_0, for the stated theta_0 with 1/2 <= theta_0 < 1): Assuming no zero with real part above $\theta_0$, there are constants $c>0$ and $v_0$ with $u_\theta(v)\ge c(\theta-\theta_0)\log v$ for $\theta_0<\theta\le1$ and $v\ge v_0$, using the explicit bound for the argument of zeta of Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong. New in this book.
- [Open: what a zero free half plane at theta_0, for instance 7/8, gives in the Cauchy flow framework](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_consequences_of_a_zero_free_half_plane_at_7_8_for_the_thorin_framework) (Volume II, Problem 13.4, page 300; open): Posed as open: what the absence of zeros with real part above $\theta_0$, for instance $\theta_0=\frac78$, gives in the Cauchy flow framework. New in this book.
- [Open: turn the calibrated GBC screen into a proof of the zero count in each window](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_certificate_for_the_screen_in_each_window) (Volume II, Problem 13.5, page 301; open): Posed as open: turning the calibrated screen into a certificate in each window. New in this book.
- [De la Vallée Poussin inequality for the Thorin density with every nonnegative cosine polynomial (general version)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#de_la_vallee_poussin_inequality_for_the_thorin_density_in_general_cosine_form) (Volume II, Theorem 13.8.1, page 302; proved): For $\theta>1$, $3u_\theta(0)+4u_\theta(v)+u_\theta(2v)\le\pi^{-1}[3g_\theta(0)+4g_\theta(v)+g_\theta(2v)]$, and more generally $\sum a_ku_\theta(kv)\le\pi^{-1}\sum a_kg_\theta(kv)$ for every nonnegative cosine polynomial with nonnegative coefficients, with $g_\theta$ the explicit gamma part. New in this book.
- [Zero free region of width c over log gamma with every c below 14 minus 8 root 3 over 5 from the Thorin form](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#crude_zero_free_region_constant_from_the_thorin_form_of_de_la_vallee_poussin) (Volume II, Corollary 13.8.2, page 302; proved): For every $c<c_\ast=(14-8\sqrt3)/5=0.028719\ldots$ every zero with $\gamma_\rho$ large has $1-\sigma_\rho\ge c/\log\gamma_\rho$, by the classical argument of de la Vallee Poussin, the constant being the crude one of the cosine polynomial $3+4\cos\omega+\cos2\omega$, below the published constants. New in this book.
- [The Davenport and Heilbronn function satisfies the Cauchy flow identities and violates the quasi Riemann hypothesis at every level below one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#the_davenport_heilbronn_function_has_the_hadamard_density_but_violates_qrh_for_every_level) (Volume II, Proposition 13.8.3, page 303; proved): The Hadamard sum, the transport identity, Thorin positivity as a zero free half plane, the detectability proposition, the formula of Balazard, Saias and Yor and the deconvolution criterion with the line $\operatorname{Re}s=2$ hold for the Davenport and Heilbronn function, which has infinitely many zeros with real part above one, so these properties alone cannot prove a zero free half plane. New in this book.
- [Multilevel inequality for the Thorin density with a cosine polynomial and a level kernel of nonnegative Laplace transform](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#multilevel_inequality_for_the_thorin_density_with_level_kernels) (Volume II, Theorem 13.8.4, page 303; proved): For a nonnegative cosine polynomial $p$ with nonnegative coefficients and a level kernel $w$ with $\phi_w\ge0$, $\sum a_kw[u](kv)\le\pi^{-1}\sum a_kw[g](kv)$ for every $v\ge2$, which for a point mass is the single level inequality. New in this book.
- [Zero free constant y star of an admissible pair of a cosine polynomial and a level kernel](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#zero_free_constant_of_an_admissible_cosine_polynomial_and_level_kernel_pair) (Volume II, Corollary 13.8.6, page 304; proved): For an admissible pair $(p,w)$ with $(a_1-a_0)I>\frac A2\phi_w(0)$, the root $y^\ast$ of $a_1J(y)=a_0I+\frac A2\phi_w(0)$ gives $(1-\sigma_\rho)\log\gamma_\rho\ge y^\ast-o(1)$ for every zero of large height. New in this book.
- [No admissible pair of a cosine polynomial and a level kernel gives a zero free region wider than a constant below one over log gamma](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#no_admissible_pair_gives_a_zero_free_constant_above_one_over_log_gamma) (Volume II, Proposition 13.8.7, page 305; proved): If an admissible pair certifies $y$ then $y\le\frac2A(a_1-a_0-a_0\log\frac{a_1}{a_0})<\frac{2(a_1-a_0)}A\le1$, which is $0.0548$ for $3+4\cos\omega+\cos2\omega$ and $0.1051$ for the degree four polynomial of the chapter; the density of the zeros through the gamma factor caps the scheme. New in this book.
- [Computed zero free constants of admissible pairs: about 1 over 11.8 log gamma with a level kernel with derivatives](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#zero_free_constants_of_admissible_pairs_computed_by_optimisation) (Volume II, Table 13.12, page 306; computed): Numerical optimisation over cosine polynomials and three families of level kernels gives zero free constants from $0.0287$ (single level, $3+4\cos\omega+\cos2\omega$) to $0.0849$ (level with derivatives, $\deg q=5$), below the proved cap $0.1051$; the derivative rows are optima on discrete constraint grids and not certified admissible. New in this book.
- [Computed ceiling of about 1 over 11.3 log gamma for smoothings of nonnegative positive definite type, by linear programming](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#computed_ceiling_of_the_admissible_scheme_by_linear_programming) (Volume II, Table 13.13, page 308; computed): A discretised linear program over every smoothing $\phi$ with $0\le\phi\le1$ and positive definite even extension gives a ceiling $0.0450$ to $0.0460$ for $3+4\cos\omega+\cos2\omega$ and $0.0874$ to $0.0881$ for polynomials of degree at most $4$ to $8$, not certified. New in this book.
- [Stechkin pairing with one far level gives a zero free constant outside the admissible class](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#one_far_level_paired_with_its_reflection_gives_a_zero_free_constant_without_smoothing) (Volume II, Proposition 13.8.10, page 309; proved): For a nonnegative cosine polynomial with $a_1>a_0$, every zero of large height has $(1-\sigma_0)\log\gamma_0\ge\frac{2(\sqrt{a_1}-\sqrt{a_0})^2}{(1-1/\sqrt5)A}-o(1)$, which is $0.05195$ for $3+4\cos\omega+\cos2\omega$ and $0.10367=1/9.646$ for the degree four polynomial (computed values), proved by an algebraic form of the pair inequality of Stechkin (1970); the degree four value is the constant of Rosser and Schoenfeld (1975). New in this book.
- [Nested sampling of the normalised Thorin density finds both zeros of the Davenport and Heilbronn function off the line in heights 1000 to 1020](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#nested_sampling_finds_the_two_davenport_heilbronn_zeros_in_1000_to_1020) (Volume II, Result 13.9.2, page 311; computed): Nested sampling at level $0.6$ on $[1000,1100]$ found two clusters near $1012.0$ and $1018.8$ of heights where the score is negative, whose zeros $0.691404808984+1012.019981489088i$ and $0.698097971267+1018.795762313197i$ are certified, and the argument principle counts exactly two zeros with real part above $0.6$ in $[1010,1020]$ and none in $[1000,1010]$. Both zeros were known (Balanzario and Sánchez-Ortiz 2007). New in this book.

#### Key terms

Cauchy deconvolution, Cauchy flow, Thorin measure, Poisson smoothing, level one, critical line, particle filter, sequential Monte Carlo, generative Bayesian computation, GBC, Feynman Kac, concentration inequality, nested sampling, contour moments, argument principle, Newton identities, Davenport and Heilbronn function, Davenport Heilbronn, negative Thorin mass, zero density, Selberg density theorem, zero free region, de la Vallée Poussin, de la Vallee Poussin, Stechkin, multilevel inequality, linear programming, quasi Riemann hypothesis, QRH, reciprocal xi

chapters.title: Balazard, Saias and Yor: Monte Carlo along vertical lines
chapters.summary:
Is the criterion of Balazard, Saias and Yor, which expresses the Riemann hypothesis as a Cauchy average of $\log\zeta$ on the critical line, the same harmonic analysis as the book's Thorin measures, and can the average be computed? The chapter proves the criterion at every level $\theta$ and every height through the Nevanlinna formula of a half plane, which characterises the quasi Riemann hypothesis QRH($\theta$), and links it to positivity of the Thorin measures $U_\sigma$ along vertical lines, the $2\sin^2$ lemma and the extended generalised gamma convolution (EGGC) property of the reciprocal of Xi. That reciprocal has a positive Lévy density with no hypothesis; so does the Davenport and Heilbronn analogue, which has zeros off the line (three zero computations certified in ball arithmetic). Under QRH($\theta$), $\log\zeta$ and the horizontally continued argument of $h_\theta$ have equal variances and zero covariance under harmonic measure; without it the defects of the complex moments are integrals along horizontal cuts from the zeros to the line. The Cauchy averages are computed by quadrature, plain and vertical likelihood Monte Carlo and the weighted trapezoid rule. On an exact half disc form of the criterion the sorted trapezoid rule has mean square error at most of order $N^{-4}$, and $N^{-5}$ after a change of variable; a smoothed Riesz identity in the plane gives grid rules, Voronoi and Delaunay weights with proved root mean square rate $N^{-3/2}$ at independent uniform nodes when the box holds no zero, and a zero count from the horizontal logarithmic derivative. Nothing here proves the Riemann hypothesis, and the tables are floating point computations.

#### From the literature

- The criterion at level one half and height zero (Balazard, Saias and Yor 1999), and the argument of positivity of the Thorin density as a zero free half plane (Lagarias 1999)
- The Davenport and Heilbronn function (Davenport and Heilbronn 1936) and its zeros off the line (Spira 1994; Balanzario and Sanchez-Ortiz 2007)
- Vertical likelihood Monte Carlo (Polson and Scott 2014) and the weighted trapezoid rule on sorted nodes with its $N^{-4}$ bound (Yakowitz, Krimmel and Szidarovszky 1978)
- The contour argument and the tail of the truncated criterion under RH, disproving a conjecture of Borwein, Bradley and Crandall (Bui, Lester and Milinovich 2014; Borwein, Bradley and Crandall 2000); finite radius and relative entropy forms (Wunderlich 2026)
- Verification of the Riemann hypothesis to height $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021) and the zero counting bound (Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong 2022)
- The zero free half plane at $\tfrac78$, unrefereed and unchecked here (OpenAI 2026)

#### New results

- [The Balazard, Saias and Yor criterion at every level theta and every height: the Cauchy average of log of zeta minus log of h equals the sum of Green potentials of the zeros right of the level](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#balazard_saias_yor_criterion_at_every_level_and_height_by_a_cauchy_average) (Volume II, Theorem 14.2.1, page 320; proved): For every $\theta\in[\frac12,1)$ the Cauchy average of $\log|\zeta|$ on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\theta$, minus $\log|h_\theta|$ at the point, is the sum of the Green potentials of the zeros to the right of the line, so $\mathrm{QRH}(\theta)$ holds exactly when the defect is zero at one height, and at $\theta=\frac12$, $t_0=0$ this is the formula of Balazard, Saias and Yor. New in this book.
- [Computed bound: zeros above height 3 times 10 to the 12 can change the global defect D_theta(0) by at most about 10 to the minus 12](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#computed_bound_on_the_defect_from_all_possible_zeros_above_the_verified_height) (Volume II, Remark 14.2.2, page 321; computed): From the verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$ and the zero counting bound of Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong, the sum over all possible zeros above that height of their contributions to $D_\theta(0)$ is below $7.4\times10^{-13}$ at $\theta=\frac12$, $1.85\times10^{-13}$ at $\frac34$ and $4.7\times10^{-14}$ at $\frac78$, so the global criterion is numerically blind there. New in this book.
- [Equivalent forms of the Riemann hypothesis and of QRH(theta): zero defect, positivity of the Thorin measures, and Cauchy deconvolution from level one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#equivalent_forms_of_the_riemann_hypothesis_by_defect_and_positivity_of_thorin_measures) (Volume II, Corollary 14.3.3, page 323; proved): The Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the vanishing of the Cauchy defect at one height, to positivity of the measures $\mathfrak U_\sigma$ for every $\sigma\in(\frac12,1)$, and to $\mathfrak U_1$ being a Cauchy smoothing of a positive measure, and each statement has a form for $\mathrm{QRH}(\theta)$. New in this book.
- [The Levy density of the reciprocal Xi function is positive with no hypothesis, and is an extended generalised gamma convolution under the Riemann hypothesis](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#levy_density_of_the_reciprocal_xi_function_is_positive_without_hypothesis) (Volume II, Proposition 14.4.1, page 323; proved): The trace $K(u)=\sum_{\gamma>0}e^{-\gamma|u|}\cos((\beta-\frac12)u)$ of the zeros of $\xi$ is positive for every $u\ne0$, so $\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+x)$ is unconditionally infinitely divisible, and under the Riemann hypothesis it is an extended generalised gamma convolution. New in this book.
- [The Riemann hypothesis holds if and only if the reciprocal of xi is the characteristic function of an extended generalised gamma convolution](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#riemann_hypothesis_equivalent_to_reciprocal_xi_being_an_eggc) (Volume II, Proposition 14.4.2, page 324; proved): The Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to $\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+x)$ being the characteristic function of an extended generalised gamma convolution, whose Thorin measure is then the zero counting measure of the critical zeros with positive ordinate. New in this book.
- [The reciprocal of the completed Davenport and Heilbronn function is infinitely divisible with positive Levy density but is not an extended generalised gamma convolution](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#infinite_divisibility_of_the_reciprocal_davenport_heilbronn_function_without_the_eggc_property) (Volume II, Theorem 14.4.3, page 325; proved): The Levy density of the reciprocal of the completed Davenport and Heilbronn function is positive for every $u\ne0$ although the function has zeros off the line, so infinite divisibility of the reciprocal does not force the zeros onto the line; the proof rests on three finite zero computations certified in ball arithmetic. New in this book.
- [A combination of L functions of characters modulo 4, 4p, 4q and 4pq with a functional equation whose reciprocal is not infinitely divisible](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#negative_trace_for_a_combination_of_dirichlet_l_functions_of_imprimitive_characters) (Volume II, Remark 14.4.5, page 327; proved): For odd primes $p<q<2p$ with $p$ large, a real combination of Dirichlet $L$ functions of characters modulo $4$, $4p$, $4q$ and $4pq$ with a functional equation has a pair of zeros off the line below the first zero of $L(s,\chi_4)$, its trace is negative at the points $(2k+1)\pi/\delta_0$ for large $k$, and its reciprocal is not infinitely divisible; the case $p=101$, $q=103$ is computed. New in this book.
- [The criterion as optional stopping: log of h at the hitting point of the line for planar Brownian motion, a submartingale that is a martingale exactly when QRH(theta) holds](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#criterion_as_optional_stopping_of_planar_brownian_motion_on_log_h_theta) (Volume II, Proposition 14.5.1, page 328; proved): For planar Brownian motion started at $1+it_0$ and stopped on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\theta$, $\log|h_\theta|$ is a submartingale whose terminal expectation exceeds its initial value by the Green potentials of the zeros right of the line, and it is a uniformly integrable martingale if and only if there is no such zero. New in this book.
- [Under QRH(theta) the complex logarithm of h at the line has all moments equal to powers of its value at the starting point, equal variances of log of zeta and its argument, zero covariance, and a Littlewood Paley variance formula](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#moments_of_the_complex_logarithm_of_h_theta_under_harmonic_measure_given_qrh) (Volume II, Theorem 14.5.2, page 329; conditional on QRH(theta): the Riemann zeta function has no zero with real part greater than theta, for the stated theta in [1/2, 1) (for theta = 1/2 this is the Riemann hypothesis)): If $\zeta$ has no zero with real part above $\theta$, then under harmonic measure on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\theta$ the boundary values of the analytic logarithm of $h_\theta$ have $\mathbb{E}[Z^k]=z_0^k$ for all $k\ge1$, so $\log|\zeta|$ and $\arg h_\theta$ have equal variances and zero covariance, with a double integral formula for the common variance. New in this book.
- [Computed moments of the complex logarithm of h at the line for zeta and the Davenport and Heilbronn function: the identities hold for zeta and fail for Davenport and Heilbronn](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#computed_moments_of_log_h_theta_for_zeta_and_the_davenport_heilbronn_function) (Volume II, Table 14.2, page 330; computed): In floating point, $\mathbb{E}Z-z_0$, $\operatorname{Var}X$, $\operatorname{Var}Y$ and $\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y)$ of $Z=\log h_\theta$ agree with the identities of the conditional moment theorem to $2.1\times10^{-5}$ for $\zeta$ at the heights $0$, $85.7$, $1000$ and $5000$, and fail for the Davenport and Heilbronn function ($\operatorname{Var}X=0.6410$ against $\operatorname{Var}Y=4.4414$ at $\theta=\frac12$, $t_0=85.7$). New in this book.
- [Without the hypothesis that no zero lies right of the line Re s = theta: the defects of the complex moments of log h as integrals along horizontal cuts from the zeros to the line](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#complex_moments_of_log_h_theta_through_horizontal_cuts_from_the_zeros_without_qrh) (Volume II, Proposition 14.5.4, page 331; proved): For every $\theta\in[\frac12,1)$ and every polynomial $F$, $\mathbb{E}F(Z)-F(z_0)$ is an absolutely convergent sum of integrals along the horizontal cuts from the zeros right of the line, with explicit formulas for the first and second moments; the real part of the first is the Balazard, Saias and Yor identity. New in this book.
- [Finite moments of log of zeta under the Cauchy law on a line at every level and height](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#log_of_zeta_has_every_moment_under_the_cauchy_law_on_a_vertical_line) (Volume II, Lemma 14.6.1, page 333; proved): For every $\theta\in[\frac12,1)$, every height $t_0$ and every $p<\infty$ the $p$th absolute moment of $\log|\zeta(\theta+i\tau)|$ under the Cauchy law centred at $t_0$ of scale $1-\theta$ is finite, so plain Monte Carlo with exact Cauchy draws is unbiased with root mean square error $(\operatorname{Var}f/n)^{1/2}$. New in this book.
- [Computed bound on the gain of any weight over plain Monte Carlo for independent draws: the factor Var f over the squared mean absolute deviation is between 1.35 and 2.46](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#computed_gain_factor_of_the_optimal_weight_over_plain_monte_carlo_for_the_defect_integrands) (Volume II, Remark 14.6.2, page 334; computed): For independent draws the best self normalised weight $w\propto|f-\mathbb{E}_Pf|$ has asymptotic variance $(\mathbb{E}_P|f-\mu|)^2$ against $\operatorname{Var}_Pf$ for plain Monte Carlo, and for the nine integrands of the table of defects the ratio is between $1.35$ and $2.46$ (computed). New in this book.
- [Computed local defects D_theta(t_0) for zeta and the Davenport and Heilbronn function by quadrature, plain Monte Carlo and vertical Monte Carlo](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#computed_local_defects_of_the_cauchy_average_for_zeta_and_davenport_heilbronn) (Volume II, Table 14.3, page 335; computed): A floating point computation of the defect $D_\theta(t_0)$ at nine pairs $(\theta,t_0)$ finds it near zero for $\zeta$ and for the Davenport and Heilbronn function close to the predicted sum of the Green potentials of its zeros right of the line ($1.4406$ against $1.4407$ at $\theta=\frac12$, $0.47698$ against $0.4770$ at $\theta=\frac34$, $t_0=85.7$); it is a computation in a window and not a proof for $\zeta$. New in this book.
- [The integrand of the Cauchy average of log of zeta is not C^1 on the unit interval, so the N to the minus four bound of Yakowitz, Krimmel and Szidarovszky does not apply](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#why_the_trapezoid_rule_on_sorted_nodes_has_no_n_to_the_minus_four_bound_for_log_zeta) (Volume II, Proposition 14.6.4, page 338; proved): After the substitution $\tau=t_0+(1-\theta)\tan(\pi(u-\frac12))$ the function $g=\log|\zeta(\theta+i\tau(u))|$ is unbounded near each critical zero when $\theta=\frac12$ and has unbounded derivative at the ends when $\frac12<\theta<1$, so $g\notin C^1[0,1]$ and the hypothesis $g\in C^2$ of the weighted rule fails. New in this book.
- [Computed errors of plain Monte Carlo, the Yakowitz, Krimmel and Szidarovszky trapezoid rule and its Dirichlet polynomial control for the Cauchy average of log of zeta](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#computed_root_mean_square_error_of_the_weighted_trapezoid_rule_for_the_cauchy_average) (Volume II, Table 14.4, page 338; computed): In floating point, over $400$ replications at $t_0=0$, the sorted trapezoid rule with a Selberg smoothed Dirichlet polynomial control reduces the root mean square error of plain Monte Carlo by a factor $3.2$ to $4.3$ at $\theta=\frac12$ and $65$ to $75$ at $\theta=\frac78$, with fitted slopes $-0.49$ to $-0.66$ and not $-2$. New in this book.
- [The Balazard, Saias and Yor identity on a half disc: exact local form with the Green function of the half disc and zeros on the diameter subtracted](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#balazard_saias_yor_identity_on_a_half_disc_with_green_function_and_harmonic_measure) (Volume II, Theorem 14.6.6, page 340; proved): For $h$ analytic near the closed half disc $H$ centred on the line, the harmonic measure average of $\log|h|$ minus the logarithms of its zeros on the diameter equals the same quantity at an interior point plus the sum of the Green potentials of the zeros in $H$, so $H$ is free of zeros exactly when the Green sum vanishes. New in this book.
- [The half disc identity becomes the Balazard, Saias and Yor identity on the half plane as the radius tends to infinity](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#half_disc_identity_tends_to_the_balazard_saias_yor_identity_as_the_radius_tends_to_infinity) (Volume II, Remark 14.6.7, page 341; proved): For $h=h_\theta$ and $z=1+it_0$ the half disc identity tends, along suitable radii $R_k\to\infty$, to the identity of the half plane, because the arc term tends to $0$ and the density on the diameter increases to the Cauchy density. New in this book.
- [The sorted trapezoid rule at independent uniform nodes: exact leading bias and variance of order N to the minus five, so mean square N to the minus four, and N to the minus five when the end slopes agree](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#exact_bias_and_variance_of_the_sorted_trapezoid_rule_at_independent_uniform_nodes) (Volume II, Lemma 14.6.8, page 341; proved): For $g\in C^4[a,b]$ the sorted trapezoid rule at $N$ uniform nodes with the end points added has bias $\frac{(b-a)^2(g'(b)-g'(a))}{2(N+1)(N+2)}+O(N^{-3})$ and variance $O(N^{-5})$, so mean square error $O(N^{-4})$, and $O(N^{-5})$ when $g'(a)=g'(b)$. New in this book.
- [Half disc identity: the sorted trapezoid rule on the two smooth pieces of the boundary has mean square error O(N^-4), and O(N^-5) after a change of variable](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#half_disc_boundary_integral_by_sorted_trapezoid_rule_has_mean_square_rate_n_to_the_minus_four_and_minus_five) (Volume II, Result 14.6.5, page 342; proved): Each piece of the boundary integral of the half disc identity is a smooth integrand on a closed interval vanishing at the ends, so the sorted trapezoid rule has mean square error $O(N^{-4})$ and, after the change of variable $y=v+\sin(\pi v)/\pi$, $O(N^{-5})$; these are upper bounds. New in this book.
- [Computed errors of plain Monte Carlo and the sorted trapezoid rule, with and without the change of variable, on the half disc identity for zeta and for Davenport and Heilbronn](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#computed_errors_of_the_sorted_trapezoid_rule_on_the_half_disc_identity_for_zeta_and_davenport_heilbronn) (Volume II, Table 14.5, page 343; computed): In floating point at $N=32{,}768$ the sorted trapezoid rule has root mean square error between $1.9\times10^{-9}$ and $7.8\times10^{-9}$ with slopes between $-2.07$ and $-2.28$, and with the change of variable slopes between $-2.49$ and $-2.51$, against $N^{-1/2}$ for plain Monte Carlo. New in this book.
- [Under RH, the Cauchy tail of log of zeta beyond distance T from the centre is O(log T / (T^2 (log log T)^2)) at level one half and O(T^-2 log T) at levels above](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#tail_of_the_cauchy_average_of_log_zeta_beyond_height_t_under_rh) (Volume II, Result 14.6.6, page 343; conditional on The Riemann hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part 1/2): Assuming RH, the part of the Cauchy average of $\log|\zeta(\frac12+i\tau)|$ outside $|\tau-t_0|\le T$ is $O_{t_0}(\log T/(T^2(\log\log T)^2))$, and at a level $\theta\in(\frac12,1)$ it is $O_\theta(T^{-2}\log T)$. New in this book.
- [Computed errors of the truncated shifted trapezoid rule for the Cauchy average of log of zeta over a window at height 85.7, with zeros deflated at level one half](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#computed_truncation_error_of_the_cauchy_average_by_the_shifted_trapezoid_rule_on_the_whole_line) (Volume II, Table 14.6, page 345; computed): In floating point the mean error of the truncated shifted grid, which is minus the Cauchy tail beyond $T$, times $T^2$ stays below $0.27$ for $T$ from $10$ to $640$ at $\theta=\frac34$ and $\theta=\frac12$, with spread over the shifts at most $8.1\times10^{-7}$. New in this book.
- [Rates of the randomly shifted product trapezoid rule on the torus (every power for a smooth periodic integrand, order N to the minus one with a logarithmic singularity) and N to the minus three halves for Voronoi and Delaunay weights at independent uniform nodes](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rates_of_the_shifted_trapezoid_grid_for_the_smoothed_riesz_integrand) (Volume II, Proposition 14.7.2, page 347; proved): The shifted product trapezoid rule with $N=m^2$ nodes is unbiased, has error $O(N^{-k})$ for every $k$ when the integrand has a smooth periodic extension, and root mean square error $O(N^{-1})$ when it carries one logarithmic singularity times a smooth compactly supported factor; Voronoi and Delaunay weights at independent uniform nodes have root mean square error $O(N^{-3/2})$ on a box free of zeros, by the weighted Monte Carlo theorem (part (iii)). New in this book.
