- [Voronoi and Delaunay weighted Monte Carlo at independent uniform nodes for integrands flat at the boundary: root mean square error O(N^(-1/2-2/d)) in every dimension d](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#weighted_monte_carlo_voronoi_and_delaunay_rules_at_independent_uniform_nodes_have_rate_n_to_the_minus_one_half_minus_two_over_d) (Volume II, Theorem 14.7.3, page 348; proved): For $g$ of class $C^3$ on the cube $[-1,1]^d$ that vanishes near the boundary or is smooth with every derivative vanishing there, the Voronoi rule and the Delaunay rule at $N$ independent uniform nodes have bias $O(N^{-k})$ for every $k$ (exponentially small in the first case) and variance $O(N^{-1-4/d})$, so root mean square error $O(N^{-1/2-2/d})$: $N^{-5/2}$ on the line and $N^{-3/2}$ in the plane. New in this book.
- [Computed root mean square errors of the Voronoi, Delaunay and trapezoid rules at independent uniform nodes for flat and non flat integrands in one and two dimensions](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#computed_errors_of_weighted_rules_at_independent_uniform_nodes_in_one_and_two_dimensions) (Volume II, Table 14.7, page 350; computed): In floating point the fitted slopes of the root mean square error for a flat bump are $-2.51$ (Voronoi, $d=1$), $-1.46$ (Voronoi, $d=2$) and $-1.42$ (Delaunay, $d=2$), consistent with the proved exponents $-\frac52$ and $-\frac32$; for exponentials that do not vanish at the boundary the slopes are $-2.00$ and $-0.98$. New in this book.
- [Computed errors of plain, Voronoi, Delaunay, jittered, shifted grid and deflated rules for the smoothed Riesz integral of zeta and of the Davenport and Heilbronn function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#computed_errors_of_two_dimensional_weighted_rules_for_the_smoothed_riesz_integral) (Volume II, Table 14.8, page 352; computed): In floating point on the box $0.6\le\sigma\le1.4$, $83.7\le t\le87.7$ the shifted grid reaches $2.2\times10^{-14}$ for $\zeta$ at $N=262{,}144$, Voronoi and Delaunay weights have slopes near $-1.4$ to $-1.55$, and deflation with a zero estimate off by $1.4\times10^{-4}$ gives $3.5\times10^{-6}$ for the Davenport and Heilbronn function, whose box integral is $0.63165631$. New in this book.
- [Approximate deflation: the shifted trapezoid grid error with a zero estimate at distance epsilon has two regimes and no floor](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#approximate_deflation_of_a_zero_leaves_no_floor_for_the_shifted_trapezoid_grid) (Volume II, Proposition 14.7.5, page 353; proved): When a zero is deflated with an estimate at distance $\varepsilon$, the root mean square error of the shifted trapezoid grid is at most of order $\varepsilon N^{-1/2}$ (up to logarithms) while $\varepsilon\sqrt N\le1$ and of order $N^{-1}$ afterwards, so the error tends to zero for every fixed $\varepsilon$. New in this book.
- [The zero count weighted by a bump is a linear functional of the horizontal logarithmic derivative on a half strip](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#counting_zeros_from_the_horizontal_logarithmic_derivative_alone) (Volume II, Theorem 14.7.6, page 353; proved): For a meromorphic Dirichlet series $f$ with a bump $\varphi$, $\sum\varphi(\rho)-\sum\varphi(p)=-\frac12\iint d_f\,K_\varphi$, where $d_f=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(f'/f)$ is the horizontal component of the field and $K_\varphi=\partial_u\varphi+\partial_t^2\Phi$. New in this book.
- [Computed error of the deflated shifted grid for the Davenport and Heilbronn function as a function of the error in the deflating zero](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#computed_error_of_the_deflated_shifted_grid_against_the_error_of_the_deflating_zero) (Volume II, Table 14.9, page 354; computed): In floating point the deflated shifted grid for the Davenport and Heilbronn box falls to $5.1\times10^{-14}$ at $N=262{,}144$ with the exact zero, to $3.0\times10^{-6}$ with an error $10^{-4}$ in the zero, against $4.2\times10^{-5}$ without deflation. New in this book.
- [The explicit formula at a Cauchy smoothed level: the primes compute the Thorin integral against a band limited test function only when no zero lies to the right of the level](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#explicit_formula_at_a_cauchy_smoothed_level_gives_the_thorin_integral_when_no_zero_lies_right_of_the_level) (Volume II, Remark 14.8.1, page 356; proved): For a nonnegative test function with band limited Fourier transform and a level $\sigma\in(\frac12,1)$ free of zeros, the explicit formula of Weil applied to the Cauchy smoothing involves only prime powers up to $e^L$ and gives $\int F_c\,d\mathfrak U_\sigma\ge0$ when no zero lies right of $\sigma$; a zero right of $\sigma$ adds corrections that need not be positive. New in this book.
- [Open problem: an implementable sampler whose variance per unit cost for the defect is below plain Monte Carlo](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_implementable_sampler_with_variance_below_plain_monte_carlo_for_the_defect) (Volume II, Problem 14.1, page 356; open): Find a sampler for the reweighted law with weight close to $|f-\mathbb{E}_Pf|$, or another weight, that beats plain Monte Carlo for the defect $D_\theta(t_0)$ at equal total cost, or show that the Metropolis chains used cannot; for independent draws no weight gains more than a factor between $1.35$ and $2.46$ here. New in this book.
- [Open problem: the root mean square rate of Voronoi and Delaunay rules for the negative Thorin mass on a region free of zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_rate_of_voronoi_and_delaunay_rules_for_the_negative_thorin_mass) (Volume II, Problem 14.2, page 356; open): Determine the rate of the Voronoi and Delaunay rules for $\iint_Rm_\sigma^-\,d\sigma\,dt$ on a bounded region $R$ free of zeros, or after exact deflation of the zeros in $R$. New in this book.
- [Open problem: a rate in N for the truncated shifted trapezoid rule on the whole line under RH, and a certified tail correction](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_rate_in_n_of_the_truncated_whole_line_average_and_a_certified_tail_correction) (Volume II, Problem 14.3, page 357; open): On a half disc the sorted trapezoid rule reaches the mean square rates $N^{-4}$ and $N^{-5}$; for the whole line, prove a rate in $N$ for the truncated rule under RH, find a finite certified correction of the tail beyond $T$, and decide whether the observed slopes $-0.60$ and $-0.66$ for $\zeta$ are preasymptotic. New in this book.
- [Open problem: extend the rate of Voronoi and Delaunay weights to dependent nodes and find the rate for a box with an undeflated zero](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_extension_of_the_rate_of_voronoi_and_delaunay_weights_to_dependent_nodes) (Volume II, Problem 14.4, page 357; open): Extend the proved rate $N^{-1/2-2/d}$ of Voronoi and Delaunay weights at independent uniform nodes to node sets produced by the particle filter or nested sampling under coverage and mixing hypotheses, and determine the rate for a box with an undeflated zero. New in this book.
- [Open problem: do the moment identities for all heights imply QRH(theta), and a central limit theorem for the logarithm of h under the Cauchy law](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_converse_of_the_moment_identities_and_the_central_limit_theorem_for_log_h_theta) (Volume II, Problem 14.5, page 357; open): If $\mathbb{E}[Z_{t_0}^2]=(\mathbb{E}Z_{t_0})^2$ for every height, does $\mathrm{QRH}(\theta)$ follow (the cut formula reduces this to an identity over the cuts), and under RH is the variance of $\log|\zeta|$ under the Cauchy law at height $t_0$ equal to $\frac12\log\log t_0+O(1)$ with a normal limit? New in this book.
- [Open problem: a combination of L functions of primitive characters of one modulus, with a functional equation and zeros off the line, whose trace is negative somewhere](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_negative_trace_for_a_combination_of_primitive_l_functions) (Volume II, Problem 14.6, page 357; open): Is there a linear combination of Dirichlet $L$ functions over primitive characters of one modulus, with a functional equation and zeros off the line, whose trace $K$ is negative somewhere, given that imprimitive characters allow one, and where must its zeros lie? New in this book.

#### Key terms

BSY criterion, Balazard Saias Yor, Cauchy average, Nevanlinna formula, Green function, QRH, Thorin measure, 2 sin squared lemma, Lévy density, Levy density, extended generalised gamma convolution, EGGC, reciprocal xi, infinite divisibility, Davenport and Heilbronn function, Brownian motion, optional stopping, vertical likelihood Monte Carlo, Yakowitz Krimmel Szidarovszky, trapezoid rule, Voronoi, Delaunay, smoothed Riesz identity, half disc, truncation, weighted Monte Carlo, Weil explicit formula, deflation, horizontal logarithmic derivative

chapters.title: Weil positivity and Yoshida's Hermitian forms: certificates and barriers
chapters.summary:
This chapter asks how far Weil's positivity criterion for the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) can be read as a Thorin statement, how far the primes alone can certify it, and whether Yoshida's Hermitian form of Weil's explicit formula on a window gives a path to RH. Restricting Weil's functional to Gaussian test functions and their derivatives in the heat time gives the heat trace of the zeros, a Laplace transform with a Thorin (generalised gamma convolution) measure on the squared ordinates. RH holds if and only if the heat trace is completely monotone, if and only if the Thorin measure lies on the positive axis. The trace splits into an archimedean part, an integral against the Lévy density of a log Gamma variable (a Gumbel Lévy measure), and a prime part, a positive series of Fréchet distribution functions governed for small heat time by the prime 2. Window laws, one sided certificates from primes up to a bound, and energy, Hankel and sine squared forms complete the first half. In the second half the heat trace and every rung of its ladder are diagonal values of Yoshida's form on Hermite Gaussian vectors, the tent coefficient is the sine squared lemma summed over the zeros, and Yoshida's matrix is a Löwner matrix of an odd meromorphic function, a Pick function exactly when RH holds. Damped at a basepoint $\alpha$ to the right of every zero, the form is a Fourier multiplier with a sharp lower bound for its least eigenvalue, unconditional for $\alpha\ge1$ and under RH for $\frac12<\alpha<1$. An uncertainty barrier limits what prime side computations detect above the verified height. The chapter does not prove RH. The window law and the match with random matrix statistics are computed or heuristic, and the problems are open.

#### From the literature

- Weil's explicit formula and positivity criterion, with Guinand's summation formula (Weil 1952; Guinand 1948; Bombieri 2000)
- Weil positivity and the trace formula at the archimedean place (Connes and Consani 2021)
- Yoshida's Hermitian forms of Weil's explicit formula on a window (Yoshida 1992), as the authors read it, unchecked; certified positivity on one window with prime powers (Zhu 2026, preprint)
- explicit estimates for the prime counting function (Rosser and Schoenfeld 1962) and the verification of RH to $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021)
- variance of primes in short intervals and pair correlation (Cramér 1922; Goldston and Montgomery 1987; Montgomery and Soundararajan 2004)
- zeta functions over the zeros of the zeta function (Voros 2010); second order regular variation (de Haan and Stadtmüller 1996); total positivity (Karlin 1968); the explicit formula in the form of von Koch (1901)
- RH as positivity of the tent coefficient, classical in substance (Landau's theorem, Widder 1941, Ingham 1932), Landau's zero sum formula (Landau 1912), Löwner's theorem on Pick functions (Löwner 1934; Donoghue 1974)
- Lagarias's criterion for $\xi$ (Lagarias 1999), RH as monotonicity of $|\xi(\sigma+i\tau)|$ in $\sigma$ (Sondow and Dumitrescu 2010), de Bruijn's bound for the de Bruijn Newman constant (de Bruijn 1950; Rodgers and Tao 2020)
- the Vinogradov Korobov zero free region (Vinogradov 1958; Korobov 1958), the Davenport Heilbronn function (Davenport and Heilbronn 1936)

#### New results

Theorems are proved with their hypotheses stated, except computations marked as floating point or heuristic; the problems are open.

- [RH holds if and only if the heat trace of the zeros is completely monotone, if and only if the Thorin measure lies on the positive axis](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#weil_positivity_in_gaussian_form_is_the_thorin_condition_rh_iff_heat_trace_completely_monotone) (Volume II, Theorem 15.2.1, page 364; proved): RH, positivity of every $\lambda_j$, complete monotonicity of $W$ and complete monotonicity of $\mathcal A-\mathcal P$ are equivalent; the equivalence of (i), (ii) and (iii) is Polson's rigidity theorem (2026), here with the converse written out by a pole argument for the resolvent $\sum_j(s+\lambda_j)^{-1}$, and (iv) is its form on the prime side by the explicit formula. New in this book.
- [The heat trace computed from Gamma and the primes agrees with the sum over the first 1700 zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#explicit_formula_for_the_heat_trace_agrees_with_zeros_to_all_printed_digits) (Volume II, Result 15.1, page 364; computed): At 110 digits $\mathcal A(t)-\mathcal P(t)$ equals the sum over the first 1700 zeros to $10^{-70}$ or better at $t=0.005,0.02,0.05,0.1,0.2$, for example $W(0.02)=0.018541291731319482254$. New in this book.
- [The archimedean part of the heat trace is a compensated integral against u times the Levy density of minus half the logarithm of a Gamma(1/4) variable](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#archimedean_part_of_the_heat_trace_is_u_times_a_gumbel_type_levy_density_of_order_one_quarter) (Volume II, Result 15.3, page 366; proved): $\mathcal A(t)=e^{t/4}+\frac12[\psi(\frac14)-\log\pi]g_t(0)+\int_0^\infty[g_t(0)-g_t(u)]k(u)\,du$ with $k(u)=e^{-u/2}/(1-e^{-2u})$, and $k(u)$ is $u$ times the Levy density of $-\frac12\log G_{1/4}$. New in this book.
- [The prime part is a positive weighted series of Frechet distribution functions and for small t is governed by the prime 2](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#prime_part_of_the_heat_trace_is_a_weighted_series_of_frechet_distribution_functions_governed_by_the_prime_2) (Volume II, Result 15.3, page 367; proved): $\mathcal P(t)=(4\pi t)^{-1/2}\sum_{n\ge2}\Lambda(n)n^{-1/2}\exp(-(\log n)^2/4t)$, and as $t\downarrow0$, $\mathcal P(t)=\frac{\log2}{\sqrt{8\pi t}}e^{-(\log2)^2/4t}\{1+O(e^{-[(\log3)^2-(\log2)^2]/4t})\}$. New in this book.
- [Computed first sign changes of the derivatives of the archimedean part for orders one to six](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#first_sign_changes_of_the_archimedean_derivatives_for_orders_one_to_six_computed) (Volume II, Result 15.4.1, page 368; computed): The first sign change $t_n$ of $D_n$ is $0.025332,0.051040,0.076135,0.101334,0.126561,0.151805$ for $n=1,\dots,6$, within 1 percent of $n/\lambda_*$ with $\lambda_*=39.5620$. New in this book.
- [The spectral density of the archimedean part has exactly one sign change, at the square of the critical point of the Riemann Siegel theta function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#spectral_density_of_the_archimedean_part_changes_sign_exactly_once_at_the_square_of_the_critical_point_of_theta) (Volume II, Lemma 15.8.1, page 372; proved): $w$ is negative on $(0,\lambda_*)$ and positive on $(\lambda_*,\infty)$ with $w'(\lambda_*)>0$, where $\lambda_*=r_*^2$ and $r_*=6.28984$ solves $\operatorname{Re}\psi(\frac14+\frac{ir}2)=\log\pi$. New in this book.
- [Sign structure of the derivatives of the archimedean part: one sign change for odd order, at most two for even order, and a first change near n over lambda star](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#first_sign_change_of_the_derivatives_of_the_archimedean_part_lies_near_n_over_lambda_star) (Volume II, Proposition 15.8.2, page 372; proved): For every $n\ge1$, $D_n>0$ near $0$; for odd $n$ it changes sign exactly once, for even $n$ at most twice, and for large $n$ the first change is $t_n=n/\lambda_*+O(1)$. New in this book.
- [Prime by prime window law: omitting the prime powers from q on ends the order one window near log q over twice the first ordinate](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#prime_by_prime_window_law_for_the_order_one_positivity_of_the_truncated_prime_part) (Volume II, Result 15.8.2, page 373; computed): For the prime part truncated to a finite set $S$ of primes, the first failure $t_1(S)$ of $-(\mathcal A-\mathcal P)'>0$ agrees with $\log q/2\gamma_1$, $q$ the first omitted prime power, within $3.2\%$ for $S$ empty, about $1\%$ from $q=5$ on and $0.17\%$ at $q=101$. New in this book.
- [Computed short interval variance of the prime sum follows the GUE prediction and not the Poisson level](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rigidity_of_the_prime_point_process_variance_in_short_intervals_follows_the_gue_prediction_computed) (Volume II, Result 15.8.3, page 374; computed): For $\psi_{\mathrm C}$ on $[10^6,10^7]$ the normalised mean square $V_\delta$ is $10.13,7.71,5.32,4.04,3.22,1.10$ at $\delta=10^{-5},10^{-4},10^{-3},3\times10^{-3},10^{-2},10^{-1}$, against GUE $10.10,7.80,5.49,4.39,3.19,0.89$ and Poisson level $14.37$. New in this book.
- [Window law: the first sign change of the derivatives of the archimedean part is n over lambda star plus beta plus delta over n plus O of n to the minus two](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#window_law_for_the_archimedean_part_with_explicit_constants_beta_and_delta) (Volume II, Proposition 15.9.1, page 376; proved): $t_n=n/\lambda_*+\beta+\delta/n+O(n^{-2})$ with $\beta=\lambda_*^{-1}(1+\lambda_*w''(\lambda_*)/2w'(\lambda_*))$ and $\delta=\alpha^2/\lambda_*^3-\eta/\lambda_*^2$ explicit in the derivatives of $w$ at $\lambda_*$. New in this book.
- [One sided certificates: a first derivative bound with no tail estimate and a second derivative bound with the Rosser and Schoenfeld tail](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#one_sided_certificates_for_the_heat_trace_from_finitely_many_primes) (Volume II, Proposition 15.9.2, page 377; proved): For $t<(\log q)^2/2$, $-W'\ge-(\mathcal A-\mathcal P_S)'$; and with $\psi_{\mathrm C}(y)<1.03883y$, $W''\ge(\mathcal A-\mathcal P_{\le N_0})''-1.03883(N_0f(N_0)+\int_{\log N_0}^\infty e^{u/2}\partial_t^2g_t(u)\,du)$. New in this book.
- [Windows for the positivity of the second derivative of the heat trace suggested by the certificate bound (not certified)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#windows_for_positive_second_derivative_of_the_heat_trace_from_the_certificate_bound_computed_on_a_grid) (Volume II, Result 15.9.2, page 378; computed): The lower bound of part (2) of the certificate stays positive up to $t=0.0740,0.1479,0.2346$ with the prime powers up to $10,100,1000$, in floating point on a grid; this is not a certificate. New in this book.
- [The heat trace is the sum of an explicit archimedean quantity and a Gaussian derivative smoothing of the normalised prime error](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_trace_is_a_gaussian_smoothing_of_the_normalised_prime_error_with_no_hypothesis) (Volume II, Proposition 15.9.3, page 378; proved): For every $t>0$, $W(t)=\Sigma_\infty(t)+\int_0^\infty D(u)(\partial_ug_t-\frac12g_t)(u)\,du$ with $D(u)=(\psi_{\mathrm C}(e^u)-e^u)e^{-u/2}$, with no use of RH. New in this book.
- [Energy form of RH: the normalised prime error has finite discounted energy if and only if RH holds](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rh_equivalent_to_finite_discounted_energy_of_the_normalised_prime_error) (Volume II, Proposition 15.9.4, page 379; proved): RH holds if and only if $\int_0^\infty D(u)^2e^{-2\epsilon u}du<\infty$ for every $\epsilon>0$; under RH the mean square of $D$ per unit of $u$ tends to $2\sum_{\gamma>0}m_\gamma^2/(\frac14+\gamma^2)$, which is $2+\gamma_E-\log4\pi=0.0461914179$ for simple zeros. New in this book.
- [Computed mean square of the normalised prime error on four windows of the log scale](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#mean_square_of_the_normalised_prime_error_from_primes_up_to_two_times_ten_to_the_seven_computed) (Volume II, Result 15.9.4, page 380; computed): From the primes up to $2\times10^7$ the mean of $D^2$ is $0.0509,0.0442,0.0465,0.0468$ on $u\in[5,10],[8,12],[10,14],[12,16.8]$, against $2+\gamma_E-\log4\pi=0.0462$, with $\gamma_E$ Euler's constant. New in this book.
- [Hankel form of RH: all zeros are on the line if and only if two Hankel families of normalised cumulants are positive semidefinite](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rh_equivalent_to_positive_semidefiniteness_of_two_hankel_families_of_normalised_cumulants) (Volume II, Proposition 15.9.5, page 381; proved): With $m_j=\sum_k\lambda_k^{-j-1}$, RH holds if and only if $(m_{i+j})_{0\le i,j\le d}$ and $(m_{i+j+1})_{0\le i,j\le d}$ are positive semidefinite for every $d\ge0$. New in this book.
- [One heat time suffices: RH holds if and only if the sine squared functional is nonnegative for every shift at a single heat time](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#one_heat_time_suffices_rh_iff_sine_squared_functional_is_nonnegative_for_all_shifts) (Volume II, Theorem 15.10.1, page 383; proved): For any fixed $t>0$, RH holds if and only if $V(t,a)=\sum_j2\sin^2(a\gamma_j/2)e^{-\lambda_jt}\ge0$ for every $a\ge0$; the converse is by Landau's theorem for Laplace transforms of nonnegative functions. New in this book.
- [Ladder rungs are diagonal values of Weil's form on Hermite Gaussians](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#ladder_rungs_are_diagonal_values_of_weil_form_on_hermite_gaussians) (Volume II, Proposition 15.14.1, page 389; proved): Weil's Hermitian form on the Hermite Gaussian vector of order $k$ and width $x$ equals twice the rung $T_k(x)$ of the ladder of the heat trace of the zeros, and the heat trace $W(x)$ is half the value of the form on the Gaussian itself. New in this book.
- [If RH fails every large rung of the ladder fails: RH is positivity of the odd rungs](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rh_is_positivity_of_odd_ladder_rungs_and_every_large_rung_fails) (Volume II, Theorem 15.15.1, page 390; proved): The orders $k$ for which the rung $T_k$ of the ladder is nonnegative form an initial segment, and if RH fails every rung beyond some finite order takes a negative value, so RH is equivalent to nonnegativity of the rungs of any fixed infinite set of orders, in particular of the odd rungs, that is of Weil's form on odd Hermite Gaussians. New in this book.
- [Where the rungs fail: saddle point location for an off line zero](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#saddle_point_location_of_failing_ladder_rungs_for_an_off_line_zero) (Volume II, Proposition 15.15.2, page 391; proved): If RH fails, a saddle point computation shows that for every large $k$ the rung $T_k$ is negative at a point $x=k/y_k$ with $y_k$ within $O(1/k)$ of $\gamma_*^2-\delta_*^2$ for an off line zero that maximises $\log\sec\theta$, with no explicit bound for the order $k$. New in this book.
- [The tent coefficient of Yoshida's matrix: zero side, prime side and residue series](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#tent_coefficient_zero_side_prime_side_and_residue_series) (Volume II, Proposition 15.18.1, page 395; proved): The tent coefficient $D(x)$ of Yoshida's matrix is the zero sum $\sum_\rho4\sin^2(\gamma_\rho x/2)/\gamma_\rho^2$, under RH it is $8\int\sin^2(x\sqrt t/2)\,t^{-1}\,U(dt)$ for the Thorin measure $U$, and it has an explicit prime side expression, a Riesz mean of $\Lambda(n)n^{-1/2}$ plus an archimedean term given in closed form and by a residue series. New in this book.
- [Yoshida's matrix is a Löwner matrix, and RH is the Pick property of one function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#yoshida_matrix_is_a_lowner_matrix_and_rh_is_the_pick_property) (Volume II, Theorem 15.19.1, page 400; proved): Yoshida's matrix of Weil's form on a window of half length $a$ is, up to a sign change, $2/a$ times the Löwner matrix of an odd meromorphic function $g_a$ built from the zeros (under RH $g_a(\nu)=\nu\,\mathcal{S}_a(-\nu^2)$ for the Stieltjes transform $\mathcal{S}_a$ of the Thorin measure weighted by $2\sin^2(a\sqrt t)$), and RH holds if and only if $g_a$ is a Pick function, for any one $a>0$. New in this book.
- [The damped Yoshida form is a Fourier multiplier with symbol Re xi'/xi over pi](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#damped_yoshida_form_is_a_fourier_multiplier_with_symbol_xi_log_derivative) (Volume II, Proposition 15.20.1, page 402; proved): For a basepoint $\alpha\ge\sigma_{\max}$ with no zero on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha$, the damped Yoshida form of a function supported in a window is the integral of $|\widehat\varphi|^2$ against the positive density $\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\alpha+i\tau)$, a sum of Poisson kernels of the zeros. New in this book.
- [Positivity of the damped Yoshida forms: basepoints beyond the zeros, and RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#damped_yoshida_forms_are_positive_semidefinite_for_basepoints_beyond_the_zeros_and_rh_equivalence) (Volume II, Theorem 15.20.3, page 403; proved): The damped Yoshida form is positive semidefinite for every basepoint $\alpha\ge\sigma_{\max}$, hence unconditionally for $\alpha\ge1$, RH holds if and only if it is positive semidefinite for every $\alpha>\frac12$, and the supremum of the half lengths $a$ for which it is positive semidefinite on the smooth functions supported in $[-a,a]$ is nondecreasing in $\alpha$. New in this book.
- [Sharp coercivity of the damped Yoshida forms on every window](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#sharp_coercivity_of_damped_yoshida_forms_by_the_minimum_of_xi_log_derivative) (Volume II, Theorem 15.20.5, page 404; proved): For $\alpha\ge\sigma_{\max}$ with no zero on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha$, the least eigenvalue of the damped Yoshida form on a window of half length $a$ is at least $2\inf_\tau\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\alpha+i\tau)$ and tends to it as $a\to\infty$; this infimum is $\xi'(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha)$ under RH and unconditionally for $\alpha\ge1$, RH is equivalent to the bound $2\xi'(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha)$ for all $\alpha\in(\frac12,1]$ and all windows, and the constant vanishes linearly as $\alpha\downarrow\frac12$. New in this book.
- [Unconditional sharp coercivity of the damped Yoshida form at alpha equal to 1](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#unconditional_sharp_coercivity_of_the_damped_yoshida_form_at_basepoint_one) (Volume II, Corollary 15.20.8, page 406; proved): With no hypothesis on the zeros, the damped Yoshida form at $\alpha=1$ satisfies $\langle\varphi,\varphi\rangle_1\ge(2+\gamma_E-\log4\pi)\|\varphi\|^2$ on every window, and this constant, about $0.0461914$, cannot be enlarged for all windows. New in this book.
- [Uncertainty barrier for the tent coefficient above the verified height](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#uncertainty_barrier_for_the_tent_coefficient_above_the_verified_height) (Volume II, Proposition 15.21.1, page 409; proved): If all zeros up to height $H$ lie on the critical line, the zeros above $H$ change the tent coefficient $D(x)$ by at most $8\cosh^2(x/4)\sum_{\gamma>H}\gamma^{-2}$, which is below $1.184\times10^{-11}\cosh^2(x/4)$ for $H=3\times10^{12}$, a bound that grows like $e^{x/2}$ and concerns the tent coefficient only. New in this book.
- [Computed positivity of the tent coefficient up to level 47.48 from the verification of RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#tent_coefficient_computed_positive_up_to_level_47_from_the_verified_height_and_1700_zeros) (Volume II, Proposition 15.21.2, page 409; computed): A computation in double precision (a branch and bound, then a grid with a Lipschitz bound), not a ball arithmetic certificate, shows from the first 1700 zeros and the verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$ alone that the tent coefficient $D(x)$ is positive for $0.05\le x\le47.48$, so that a prime side computation of $D$ at these levels cannot produce a negative value. New in this book.
- [Open problem: the symbol inequality Re xi'/xi at least xi'/xi(alpha) below the line alpha equal to 1](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_symbol_inequality_for_xi_log_derivative_below_basepoint_one) (Volume II, Problem 15.5, page 411; open): Determine the region of lines $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha<1$ and heights $\tau$ above the verified height $3\times10^{12}$ in which $\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\alpha+i\tau)>\xi'(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha)$ can be proved with no hypothesis and with explicit constants, the Vinogradov Korobov region being the natural target. New in this book.

chapters.title: Zhu's compact windows and the Landau Widom horizon
chapters.summary:
This chapter reads Xuefeng Zhu's 2026 preprint on Weil positivity in compact windows in the language of Thorin measures. The question is how far Weil's criterion for the Riemann Hypothesis (RH), positivity of Weil's quadratic form on test functions supported in every window $[-a,a]$, can be certified by finite computation, and what a window says about the height of the zeros. The objects are the least eigenvalue of the form, the prime comb in its symbol and the Thorin measure of the clock of the Xi function. The methods are a dictionary that makes the form, under RH, a sampling functional of the Thorin measure on Paley Wiener functions, Zhu's test function through a truncated reciprocal Xi transform, the Landau Widom horizon, and damping to a basepoint $\alpha$. It proves the dictionary and a two parameter bound for the least eigenvalue of the damped form (conditional on RH below 1), reproves its coercivity for basepoints above 1 from the Euler product, and computes least eigenvalues and a detection experiment with a hypothetical off line quadruple of zeros. The passage from windows to heights is a heuristic. Four problems are open. Nothing here proves RH.

#### From the literature

- Weil's explicit formula and criterion (Weil 1952; Bombieri 2000); positivity on windows with $2a$ at most $\log 2$ (Yoshida 1992), proved again by other methods (Connes and Consani 2021)
- Zhu (2026): a finite reduction of positivity on a window, a computer assisted certificate on $[-0.8,0.8]$, the upper bound $\exp(-ae^a)$ for the least even eigenvalue under RH for large $a$, the barrier for pointwise comb certificates and the Landau Widom decay law, a conjecture fitted to computed bounds
- Positivity on each window as a sampling statement under RH (Zhu 2026), via Littlewood (1924) on gaps between ordinates and Beurling's sampling theorem (Seip 2004)
- Time and band limiting (Slepian and Pollak 1961; Landau and Pollak 1962; Landau and Widom 1980); verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021)

#### New results

Statements are proved unless marked computed (floating point), heuristic or conditional on RH.

- [Dictionary: Zhu's window form is Yoshida's Weil form and, under RH, a sampling functional of the Thorin measure](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#zhu_window_form_equals_yoshida_form_and_under_rh_is_thorin_sampling_functional) (Volume II, Proposition 16.2.1, page 415; conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis, used only for the second set of identities (the sum over the zeros, the integral against the Thorin measure and the sampling reading of the least eigenvalue). The identity $Q(f)=\langle f,f\rangle=\mathcal{Y}(f*f)$ holds with no hypothesis on the zeros): On a window of half length $a$, Zhu's quadratic form equals Yoshida's Weil form of the autocorrelation $f*f$ with no hypothesis, and under RH it equals twice the sum of $|F|^2$ over the positive ordinates, so that the least even eigenvalue is the lower sampling constant of the Thorin measure of the clock for the real even Paley Wiener functions of type $a$. New in this book.
- [Two parameter bound: the damped least eigenvalue is at least the undamped one, and under RH at least $2\xi'(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha)$](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#two_parameter_bound_for_least_eigenvalue_of_damped_weil_form_on_a_window) (Volume II, Theorem 16.5.2, page 426; conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis, used for part (ii) when $\alpha<1$, for the lower bound $2b_\alpha\ge4p_1(\alpha-\frac12)-4p_2(\alpha-\frac12)^3$ at every $\alpha>\frac12$ and for the closing maximum. Part (i), the bound $\lambda_{\min}(\alpha,a)\ge2b_\alpha$ for $\alpha\ge1$ and the upper bound $2b_\alpha\le4p_1(\alpha-\frac12)$ hold with no hypothesis on the zeros): The least eigenvalue of the damped Weil form on a window is at least the undamped one for every basepoint $\alpha>\frac12$ with no hypothesis, and under RH (or for $\alpha\ge1$) it is also at least $2\xi'(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha)$, a floor of order $\alpha-\frac12$. New in this book.
- [Open problem: the Landau Widom horizon as a theorem, the largest window on which Weil's form is positive when the zeros are controlled up to a height](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_horizon_as_a_theorem_largest_window_from_zeros_verified_to_height_h) (Volume II, Problem 16.1, page 428; open): Determine the largest half length $a(H,\delta_0)$ of a window on which Weil's form is positive when all zeros up to height $H$ lie on the critical line and the higher zeros lie within $\delta_0$ of it, and decide whether it is at least $\frac12\log\frac H{2\pi}-C(\delta_0)$ with a constant depending only on $\delta_0$. New in this book.
- [Open problem: derive Zhu's Landau Widom decay law for the least eigenvalue of Weil's form on a window from the Thorin side](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_derive_zhu_decay_law_for_least_eigenvalue_from_thorin_side) (Volume II, Problem 16.2, page 428; open): Derive Zhu's fitted decay law $-\log\lambda^{\mathrm{even}}_{\min}(\frac12,a)\approx C\,N(T_*)/\log N(T_*)$ with $T_*=2\pi e^{2a}$ for the least even eigenvalue of Weil's form on a window of half length $a$ from his product test function, and explain the constant through the Landau Widom plunge. New in this book.
- [Open problem: certified damped windows for basepoints between one half and one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_certified_damped_windows_for_basepoint_between_one_half_and_one) (Volume II, Problem 16.3, page 429; open): Extend Zhu's computer assisted certificate of positivity of Weil's form on a window to the damped forms with basepoint $\alpha\in(\frac12,1)$, where under RH the margin is at least $2\xi'(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha)$ in place of the undamped least eigenvalue, and measure how large a window can be certified. New in this book.
- [Open problem: comb cancellation on average over Paley Wiener functions](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_comb_cancellation_on_average_over_paley_wiener_functions) (Volume II, Problem 16.4, page 429; open): Determine, as a function of $T$ and $a$, the supremum over Paley Wiener functions $F$ of type $a$ of the average of the prime comb against $|F|^2$ on the frequencies $|t|\ge T$, which is at most the pointwise supremum $A_a=(4+o(1))e^a$. New in this book.

#### Key terms

Weil positivity, Weil's criterion, explicit formula, Riemann Hypothesis, RH, compact window, Yoshida form, Hermitian form, least eigenvalue, Landau Widom horizon, time and band limiting, Paley Wiener space, Thorin measure, generalized gamma convolution, generalised gamma convolution, GGC, reciprocal Xi transform, prime comb, comb barrier, damped form, basepoint, off line zeros, Zhu

chapters.title: Truncations: the Biane Pitman Yor lattice, the beta lattice and Hermite coefficients
chapters.summary:
Can truncations of a lattice of exponential variables decide the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) or the Generalised Riemann Hypothesis (GRH), and how do the zeros of the truncated transforms move? For $\zeta$, cutting the Biane, Pitman and Yor series $\mathcal S=\sum_k k^{-2}(e_k+e_k')$ after $n$ terms gives a generalised gamma convolution with finitely many Thorin atoms whose Mellin transform is a gamma factor times an exponential polynomial, with zeros converging to $\rho/2$; a condition on these zeros for infinitely many $n$ implies RH (Hurwitz). The truncated zeros move at the first order rate $\kappa(\rho)/n$, and the side of approach is tied to the Riemann Siegel phase, so to Gram's law, which makes the one sided condition (Conjecture T) fail. Symmetrising by the functional equation removes this mechanism (Conjecture S), with a Hurwitz criterion proved, single term and torus bounds for small $n$ and a statement of where they stop. The chapter writes Weil's criterion in Thorin coordinates, shows the Bernstein cone for finite order tests and weak limits to the de Bruijn Newman flow, and proves that no GGC multiplier can manufacture positivity. The same programme is carried out for the Dirichlet $L$ function of the character modulo 4: local zero free conditions equivalent to GRH, an explicit drift law, transient zeros, and symmetrised truncations. The second half computes Hermite coefficients of the Riemann Xi function as a backward heat flow, shows they sample $\Xi$ at a turning point with an error of order $a^4$, locates the first negative coefficient, and counts zeros from sign changes (computed, 379 zeros below height 500 for the modulo 4 function; the sign change count for $\zeta$ up to height 1000 is computed).

#### From the literature

- Williams' and Biane, Pitman and Yor's representation of $\xi$ through the lattice $\mathcal S$ (Williams 1990; Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001)
- Weil's explicit formula criterion (Weil 1952)
- The Hardy function, Gram's law and the Rosser rule (Titchmarsh 1986; Trudgian 2011), and the first $1.5\times10^9$ zeros simple and on the line (van de Lune, te Riele and Winter 1986)
- Fast evaluation of zeta at many points (Odlyzko and Schönhage 1988)
- Incomplete gamma approximants of the Xi function (Haglund 2009)
- The de Bruijn and Newman constant is nonnegative (Rodgers and Tao 2020)

#### New results

- [First order expansion of the zeros of the truncated lattice transforms](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#truncated_lattice_zeros_first_order_expansion) (Volume II, Proposition 17.1.2, page 435; proved): Near each simple zero $\rho$ of $\xi$ the truncated transform $F_n$ has exactly one zero, equal to $\rho/2+\kappa(\rho)/n+O(n^{-2})$ for large $n$, with an explicit constant $\kappa(\rho)$. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Displacement constant of the truncated zeros in terms of Hardy's function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#truncated_lattice_displacement_formula_hardy_function) (Volume II, Theorem 17.1.3, page 436; proved): For a simple zero on the critical line, the real and imaginary parts of the displacement constant $\kappa(\rho)$ are given in closed form by the derivative of Hardy's function $Z$ and the number $e^{i\theta(\gamma)}\zeta(\frac52+i\gamma)$. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Conjecture T is false for large n](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#conjecture_t_false_truncated_zeros_right_of_the_line) (Volume II, Corollary 17.1.4, page 437; counterexample, proved): Conjecture T, that no truncated lattice transform $F_n$ has a zero with real part above $\frac14$, is false: for all large $n$ there is such a zero near $\rho_{213}/2$, certified with a ball arithmetic enclosure of the displacement constant. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Symmetrised truncations: symmetry, limit and persistence of simple zeros on the line](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#symmetrised_truncations_symmetry_and_limit) (Volume II, Proposition 17.1.6, page 438; proved): The symmetrised truncations $K_n$ are symmetric about the line $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$, converge to $4\xi(2w)$, and keep every simple zero of $\xi(2w)$ on the line as a zero exactly on the line for all large $n$. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Real rooted symmetrised truncations for infinitely many n imply the Riemann Hypothesis](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#symmetrised_truncations_real_rooted_implies_rh) (Volume II, Theorem 17.1.7, page 438; proved): If for infinitely many $n$ all zeros of the symmetrised truncation $K_n$ in the strip $0<\operatorname{Re}w<\frac12$ lie on the line $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$, then the Riemann Hypothesis holds. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Zeros of the approximate functional equation truncations of zeta, N equal to 2 and 3](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#truncated_approximate_functional_equation_zeta_two_on_the_line_zeta_three_off_the_line) (Volume II, Proposition 17.1.8, page 439; proved): All but finitely many zeros of the approximate functional equation truncation of zeta with N equal to 2 lie on the critical line and are counted by theta over pi plus a bounded error, whereas the truncation with N equal to 3 has zeros off the line at arbitrarily large heights with real parts approaching every number in an interval; this is from a note of Nicholas Polson (compare Spira and Gonek and Montgomery). New in this book.
- [Single term bound: no off line zeros of the symmetrised truncation above explicit heights](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#symmetrised_truncations_single_term_bound_explicit_heights) (Volume II, Theorem 17.1.9, page 440; proved): A single term bound shows that for $n=1$ to $6$, $8$ and $10$ the symmetrised truncation $K_n$ has no zero off the line in the strip above explicit heights $Y_n$ between $4.81$ and $21232$, which are obtained by evaluating the explicit bounds numerically. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Conjecture S for n up to 6 and n = 8 above explicit heights](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#conjecture_s_small_n_above_explicit_heights) (Volume II, Corollary 17.1.10, page 441; proved): Conjecture S is proved for $n=1$ to $6$ and $n=8$ above the explicit heights of the single term bound, which are evaluated numerically, and below those heights it is only checked numerically by floating point argument principle counts. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Torus bound for the symmetrised truncations](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#symmetrised_truncations_torus_bound) (Volume II, Theorem 17.1.11, page 441; proved): Explicit inequalities on the extremes of the Dirichlet polynomial $P_n$ and its logarithmic derivative over the torus of prime phases imply that the symmetrised truncation $K_n$ has no zero off the line $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$ in the strip $0<\operatorname{Re}w<\frac12$ at a given height or above. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Conjecture S for n up to 24, 32 and 36 above explicit thresholds](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#conjecture_s_above_explicit_thresholds_n_to_36) (Volume II, Corollary 17.1.12, page 442; proved): Conjecture S is proved for $n=7$, $9$ to $24$, $32$ and $36$ above explicit height thresholds by torus bounds certified in ball arithmetic, and below the thresholds it is only checked numerically; with the small $n$ results it covers every $n\le24$ and $n=32,36$. Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Thorin positivity of R is Weil's criterion](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_positivity_of_reciprocal_xi_is_weil_criterion) (Volume II, Proposition 17.1.14, page 445; proved): The reciprocal Xi function $R$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution exactly when Weil's distribution is positive definite, by combining Polson's rigidity theorem with Weil's criterion, so Thorin positivity of $R$ is Weil's criterion in other coordinates and gives no new criterion. Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Weil positivity on the Bernstein cone](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#weil_positivity_on_bernstein_cone) (Volume II, Theorem 17.1.15, page 447; proved): Unconditionally, Weil's functional $\sum_\rho\hat h(\gamma_\rho)$ is positive for every test function $\hat h$ that is a Laplace transform in $r^2$ of a nonnegative weight under an integrability condition, including Thorin type products, $\operatorname{sech}(cr)$ and $(1+r^2/a)^{-m}$; it integrates the positivity of the heat trace of the zeros (Polson 2026, Theorem A), for which the book gives a second proof certified with the verification of RH to height 50 and interval enclosures. Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [The de Bruijn Newman flow as a path of GGCs](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#debruijn_newman_flow_ggc_path) (Volume II, Theorem 17.1.16, page 449; proved): For every $t$ at least the de Bruijn Newman constant, $R_t=H_t(0)/H_t(2i\sqrt s)$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution with atoms at the squared half zeros of $H_t$, so it is a GGC for every $t\ge0.2$ unconditionally, and the Riemann Hypothesis holds exactly when $R_t$ is a GGC for arbitrarily small $t>0$. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [No GGC multiplier can create the positivity of R](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#no_ggc_multiplier_can_create_positivity) (Volume II, Proposition 17.1.17, page 450; proved): Multiplying $R$ by the Laplace transform of any generalised gamma convolution gives a generalised gamma convolution exactly when the Riemann Hypothesis holds, so no such multiplier can manufacture the positivity; for the normalised reciprocal zeta function only one direction holds for every multiplier. Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Conjecture S for infinitely many n](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_conjecture_s_for_infinitely_many_n) (Volume II, Problem 17.1, page 451; open): The book asks for a proof that the symmetrised truncations $K_n$ have all their zeros in the strip $0<\operatorname{Re}w<\frac12$ on the line $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$ for infinitely many $n$, which would imply the Riemann Hypothesis. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Torus method beyond n = 36](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_torus_method_beyond_n_36) (Volume II, Problem 17.2, page 451; open): The book asks for an extension of the torus bound for the symmetrised truncations with narrower bands around $x=\frac54$, and for the first $n$ at which the torus function $P_n$ has zeros with $x\ge\frac54$. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [From finite order to all orders for the floor](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_finite_order_to_all_orders_n_monotonicity_of_the_floor) (Volume II, Problem 17.3, page 452; open): The book asks whether the argument that proves $(-1)^nk^{(n)}(y)>0$ for the canonical function $k$ of the floor of the reciprocal Xi function up to order $10^{10}$ extends to every order, which would imply the Riemann Hypothesis; the signs are already known to order $10^{17}$ (Polson 2017, version 24 of 2026) and, by the book's heat trace estimates, to order $1.16\times10^{25}$. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Beyond the Bernstein cone](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_largest_cone_of_unconditional_weil_positivity) (Volume II, Problem 17.4, page 452; open): The book asks for the largest cone of test functions, closed under the operations that preserve the Thorin structure, on which Weil positivity can be proved unconditionally, and for how far such a cone can localise in height. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Deforming the binary product](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_deforming_the_binary_product) (Volume II, Problem 17.5, page 452; open): The book asks where and how the positivity of the interference pattern of arithmetic progressions in the pseudo spectral trace formula can fail along the path from the binary product at $\sigma=0$ to the critical line. - [Regularising the autocorrelation of the Pólya kernel](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_regularising_the_autocorrelation_of_the_polya_kernel) (Volume II, Problem 17.6, page 452; open): The book asks for the regularised form of the Meixner characteristic function convolved with the positive lattice measure $\mathcal A$, and whether it has a Thorin or Lee and Yang structure in $v$. Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Unimodality of w and of the density f](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_unimodality_of_the_canonical_function_and_density) (Volume II, Problem 17.7, page 452; open): The book asks for proofs that the canonical function $w$ of the normalised reciprocal zeta function and the density $f$ of its law are unimodal, which is supported only by numerical evidence. Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Infinite divisibility across the strip](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_levy_density_positive_on_every_line_of_the_strip) (Volume II, Problem 17.8, page 453; open): The book asks whether $w_\sigma(x)>0$ for every $\sigma$ in $(0,1)$ and every $x>0$, that is whether the shifted reciprocal zeta function is infinitely divisible on every vertical line of the critical strip.
