- [Product representations of the law of R](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_product_representation_of_the_reciprocal_xi_law) (Volume II, Problem 17.11, page 453; open): The book asks whether the compensation in the formal deconvolution of the reciprocal zeta law into the reciprocal Xi law can be absorbed into a product of independent generalised gamma convolution variables, since an unconditional representation of that kind would prove the Riemann Hypothesis. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Truncations converge locally uniformly, and GRH for chi 4 is equivalent to zero free compact subsets of the left half strip for large n](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#truncated_mellin_transforms_converge_and_grh_for_chi4_is_a_local_zero_free_statement) (Volume II, Theorem 17.2.1, page 456; proved): If $R_n\to0$ in probability then $M_n\to M$ locally uniformly on $0<\Re z<\frac12$, and GRH for $\chi_4$ holds if and only if every compact subset of $0<\Re z<\frac14$ is free of zeros of $M_n$ for all large $n$. New in this book.
- [The tail cumulants of the beta lattice have an explicit expansion in the truncation index](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#midpoint_tail_cumulants_of_the_beta_lattice) (Volume II, Lemma 17.3.1, page 457; proved): For fixed $j\ge1$, $q_j(n)=\lambda_*^{-j}\{n^{1-2j}/(2j-1)-\frac j{12}n^{-2j-1}+O(n^{-2j-3})\}$, so $c_n=\mathbb ET_n=1/(\lambda_*n)+O(n^{-3})$, $v_n=\operatorname{Var}T_n=1/(3\lambda_*^2n^3)+O(n^{-5})$ and $\kappa_3(T_n)=2/(5\lambda_*^3n^5)+O(n^{-7})$. New in this book.
- [The truncated Mellin transform differs from M by a multiple of M(z+r), and each simple zero is displaced by a multiple of the first unmatched cumulant difference](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#drift_law_of_the_zeros_of_truncated_beta_mellin_transforms) (Volume II, Theorem 17.3.2, page 457; proved): With $r=m+1$ and $p=2r-1$, $M_n(z)-M(z)=-\frac{(-1)^r\Delta_{r,n}}{r!}(z)_rM(z+r)+O_K(n^{-p-2}+n^{-2p})$, and a simple zero $z_0=\rho/2$ of $M$ is displaced by $z_n-z_0=\frac{(-1)^r\Delta_{r,n}}{r!}(z_0)_r\frac{M(z_0+r)}{M'(z_0)}+O(n^{-p-2}+n^{-2p})$, with $M(z_0+r)/M'(z_0)=(2\pi)^r\xi_4(\rho+2r)/(2\xi_4'(\rho))$. New in this book.
- [The hard cutoff zeros drift at the rate 1 over n and the mean corrected zeros at 1 over n cubed, with the coefficient delta m](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#drift_of_the_hard_cutoff_and_of_the_mean_correction_zeros) (Volume II, Corollary 17.3.3, page 458; proved): For a simple zero $\rho=\frac12+i\gamma$ of $\xi_4$, $z_0=\rho/2$, $(z)_r=z(z+1)\cdots(z+r-1)$, $z_n$ the zero of $M_n$ in a fixed small disc about $z_0$ (unique and simple for large $n$) and $\delta_m=\frac{(-1)^{m+1}(z_0)_{m+1}\xi_4(\rho+2m+2)}{2(m+1)(2m+1)\pi^{m+1}\xi_4'(\rho)}$, the hard cutoff has $z_n=z_0+\delta_0/n+O(n^{-2})$ and the mean correction $R_n=\mathbb ET_n$ has $z_n=z_0+\delta_1/n^3+O(n^{-5})$; a remainder that matches the first $m$ cumulants of $T_n$, satisfies the analyticity and growth bounds of the drift law and has $\kappa_{m+1}(R_n)=o(n^{-(2m+1)})$ is displaced by $\delta_mn^{-(2m+1)}(1+o(1))$. New in this book.
- [Remainders matching mean and variance but not the third cumulant give different drifts, so the formula of delta 2 needs the matching hypothesis](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#gamma_remainders_with_matched_mean_and_variance_give_different_third_order_drifts) (Volume II, Proposition 17.3.4, page 459; proved): With $r=3$, a simple zero $\rho$ of $\xi_4$, $z_0=\rho/2$, $z_n$ the zero of $M_n$ near $z_0$ and $\delta_2=-\frac{(z_0)_3\xi_4(\rho+6)}{30\pi^3\xi_4'(\rho)}$ with $(z_0)_3=z_0(z_0+1)(z_0+2)$, the gamma remainder matching the mean and variance of $T_n$ gives $z_n=z_0+\frac49\delta_2n^{-5}+O(n^{-7})$, a sum of two such gamma variables gives $z_0-\frac19\delta_2n^{-5}+O(n^{-7})$, and a bounded two point remainder gives a displacement of exact order $n^{-3}$. New in this book.
- [The sign of the real part of the drift is the sign of minus sin Theta m times the derivative of the Hardy function of chi 4](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#side_of_approach_of_a_truncated_zero_is_set_by_a_gram_phase) (Volume II, Theorem 17.4.1, page 460; proved): For a simple zero $\rho=\frac12+i\gamma$, $\gamma>0$, of $\xi_4$ with $z_0=\rho/2$ and $\delta_m$ the drift coefficient of the zeros of the truncated Mellin transforms of the beta lattice, $\delta_m=iC_m(\gamma)e^{i\Theta_m(\gamma)}/Z_\beta'(\gamma)$ with $C_m>0$ and $\Theta_m=\vartheta_\beta(\gamma)+\arg L(\rho+2m+2,\chi_4)-\sum_{j=0}^m[\arctan\frac{1/2+2j}\gamma+\arctan\frac{3/2+2j}\gamma]$, so $\operatorname{sgn}\Re\delta_m=\operatorname{sgn}[-\sin\Theta_m\,Z_\beta'(\gamma)]$. New in this book.
- [L(s,chi 4) has 379 zeros below height 500 by sign changes, all simple and on the line as far as the computation sees, with five anomalous Gram parities](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#beta_zeros_below_height_500_located_by_sign_changes_of_the_hardy_function) (Volume II, Result 17.4.1, page 461; computed): Sign changes of $Z_\beta$ on two grids give $379$ zeros of $L(s,\chi_4)$ with $0<\gamma<500$, all simple and on the critical line as far as the computation sees (minimal gap $0.1336$); the count is not certified. Exactly five have anomalous Gram parity, at $\gamma=138.7502,290.2521,364.4197,400.8264,422.5104$, and $\Re\delta_1<0$ exactly there, where $\delta_m$ is the drift coefficient of the zeros of the truncated Mellin transforms of the beta lattice ($m=1$ for the mean correction) and $Z_\beta$ the Hardy function of $\chi_4$. New in this book.
- [One sided criterion fails at order m if some critical zero is approached from the left](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#no_one_sided_criterion_for_truncations_of_the_beta_lattice_at_a_fixed_order) (Volume II, Corollary 17.4.2, page 462; proved): For a remainder matching the first $m$ cumulants of $T_n$ under the drift law bounds, with $\eta_m$ the limiting relative deficit of $\kappa_{m+1}$ and $\delta_m$ the drift coefficient of the zeros of the truncated Mellin transforms of the beta lattice: if some simple critical zero $\rho$ of $\xi_4$ has $\Re(\eta_m\delta_m)<0$, then for all large $n$ the function $M_n$ has a zero in $0<\Re z<\frac14$, so no criterion that $M_n$ is free of zeros there for infinitely many $n$ can hold at order $m$ for this remainder. New in this book.
- [Infinitely many Gram anomalies with a margin force infinitely many zeros with negative real drift](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#anomalous_gram_parity_of_the_beta_function_forces_left_approach_with_a_margin) (Volume II, Proposition 17.4.3, page 463; proved): With $\sigma=2m+\frac52$, $\epsilon_\sigma=\sum_{k\ge1}(2k+1)^{-\sigma}<1$ and $B_m(\gamma)=\arcsin\epsilon_\sigma+\sum_{j=0}^m[\arctan\frac{1/2+2j}\gamma+\arctan\frac{3/2+2j}\gamma]$, $|\Theta_m-\vartheta_\beta|\le B_m$, and infinitely many simple critical zeros with $-\sin\vartheta_\beta(\gamma)Z_\beta'(\gamma)<0$ and $\operatorname{dist}(\vartheta_\beta(\gamma),\pi\mathbb Z)>B_m(\gamma)$ give infinitely many zeros with $\Re\delta_m<0$. New in this book.
- [If the symmetrised truncations have only critical zeros for infinitely many n then GRH holds for chi 4](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#symmetrised_truncations_give_a_hurwitz_criterion_for_grh_of_chi4) (Volume II, Theorem 17.6.1, page 465; proved): If for infinitely many $n$ all zeros of $F_n(z)=g_n(z)+g_n(\frac12-z)$ in $0<\Re z<\frac12$ lie on $\Re z=\frac14$, then GRH holds for $\chi_4$. New in this book.
- [Each simple critical zero is the limit of exactly one zero of the symmetrised truncation, and that zero is critical](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#every_simple_critical_zero_of_xi4_is_the_limit_of_one_critical_zero_of_the_symmetrised_truncation) (Volume II, Proposition 17.6.2, page 465; proved): Every simple zero of $\xi_4(2z)$ on $\Re z=\frac14$ is, for all large $n$, the limit of exactly one zero of $F_n$ in a small disc about it, and that zero lies on $\Re z=\frac14$. New in this book.
- [The Hermite coefficients of Xi are generated by the Gaussian smoothing G a, with an explicit moment formula](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#hermite_coefficients_of_xi_are_the_taylor_coefficients_of_a_gaussian_smoothing) (Volume II, Theorem 17.8.1, page 468; proved): For every $a>0$, $\sum_{m\ge0}b_m(a)z^{2m}/\sqrt{(2m)!}=\sqrt{2\pi}\,\pi^{-1/4}\sqrt a\,e^{z^2/2}G_a(\sqrt2az)$ with $G_a(\tau)=\int\Phi(u)e^{-a^2u^2/2}\cos(\tau u)\,du$, and $b_m(a)=\sqrt{2\pi}\,\pi^{-1/4}\sqrt a\sqrt{(2m)!}\sum_{k=0}^m\frac{(-1)^k2^ka^{2k}\nu_k(a)}{(2k)!\,2^{m-k}(m-k)!}$ with $\nu_k=\int\Phi(u)e^{-a^2u^2/2}u^{2k}du>0$. New in this book.
- [The normalised Hermite coefficient equals Xi at the turning point up to an explicit error of order a to the fourth](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#additive_asymptotic_of_the_hermite_coefficients_of_xi_at_the_turning_points) (Volume II, Theorem 17.9.1, page 470; proved): For $0<a\le a_0$ and $m\ge0$, $|b_m(a)/A_m(a)-\Xi(t_m)|\le M_4(a_0)a^4/12$ and $b_m/A_m=\Xi(t_m)+a^4Q(t_m)+R_m(a)$ with $|R_m|\le M_8(a_0)a^8/672$, where $Q(t)=\frac{\Xi'''(t)}{6t}-\frac{\Xi''(t)}{4t^2}+\frac{\Xi'(t)}{4t^3}$ and $Q(0)=\frac1{12}\int\Phi u^4du$. New in this book.
- [At a real zero of Xi the Hermite coefficient at the matching scale does not vanish for large m](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#hermite_coefficients_do_not_vanish_at_the_turning_points_over_zeros_of_xi) (Volume II, Proposition 17.9.2, page 471; proved): At every positive real zero $\gamma$ of $\Xi$, of any multiplicity, $b_m(a_m)\ne0$ for all large $m$ with $a_m=\gamma/\sqrt{4m+1}$, and if $Q(\gamma)\ne0$, where $Q(t)=\frac{\Xi'''(t)}{6t}-\frac{\Xi''(t)}{4t^2}+\frac{\Xi'(t)}{4t^3}$, then $b_m(a_m)=2Q(\gamma)a_m^5/\sqrt\gamma+O(a_m^9)$. New in this book.
- [The index of the first negative Hermite coefficient satisfies 4 a squared m star tends to gamma 1 squared](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#first_negative_hermite_coefficient_of_xi_marks_the_first_zero) (Volume II, Corollary 17.10.1, page 472; proved): With $m^*(a)=\min\{m:b_m(a)<0\}$ and $\gamma_1=14.134725\ldots$, for small $a$ the index $m^*(a)$ exists and $\lim_{a\to0}4a^2m^*(a)=\gamma_1^2$; more precisely $m^*(a)=\lfloor(\gamma_a^2/a^2-1)/4\rfloor+1$ with $\gamma_a=\gamma_1-a^4Q(\gamma_1)/\Xi'(\gamma_1)+O(a^8)$ and $Q(t)=\frac{\Xi'''(t)}{6t}-\frac{\Xi''(t)}{4t^2}+\frac{\Xi'(t)}{4t^3}$, the zero near $\gamma_1$ of $t\mapsto\int\Phi(u)y_{a^4,t}(u)du$. New in this book.
- [A verified sign change count of the Hermite coefficients together with an upper bound on the zero count proves real and simple zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#verified_sign_changes_of_hermite_coefficients_with_a_turing_bound_certify_all_zeros) (Volume II, Proposition 17.11.2, page 474; proved): If computed normalised coefficients with rigorous errors $e_m$ exceed $e_m+E_m$ in absolute value, where $E_m$ bounds $|b_m/A_m-\Xi(t_m)|$, the signs of $b_m$ and $\Xi(t_m)$ agree, and $S$ such sign changes together with $N(T)\le S$, with $N(T)$ the number of zeros $t$ of $\Xi$ with $0<\Re t<T$, show that all those zeros are real and simple. New in this book.
- [If each simple zero gives one sign change the mean run of the Hermite coefficient signs is asymptotic to pi T over a squared log of T over 2 pi](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#average_run_length_of_the_hermite_coefficient_signs_given_one_sign_change_per_zero) (Volume II, Proposition 17.12.1, page 476; conditional on the zeros $t$ of $\Xi$ with $T\le\Re t\le T+H$ are real and simple and the sign changes of $(b_m(a))$ with $t_m\in[T,T+H]$ correspond one to one to them): If the zeros $t$ of $\Xi$ with $T\le\Re t\le T+H$ are real and simple and the sign changes of $(b_m(a))$ with $t_m\in[T,T+H]$ correspond one to one to them, the mean number of coefficient steps per sign change is the number $TH/(2a^2)+O(H^2/a^2+1)$ of grid points in the window over $N(T+H)-N(T)$, the number of zeros $t$ of $\Xi$ with $T\le\Re t<T+H$, $=\frac H{2\pi}\log\frac T{2\pi}+O(H^2/T+\log T)$, asymptotic to $\pi T/(a^2\log(T/2\pi))$ for fixed $a$, $H\to\infty$, $H=o(T)$. New in this book.

#### Key terms

truncation, Biane Pitman Yor lattice, beta lattice, Dirichlet beta function, L function of chi 4, Dirichlet L function modulo 4, Generalised Riemann Hypothesis, GRH, Riemann Hypothesis, RH, Hurwitz theorem, Gram law, Gram point, Gram anomaly, Riemann Siegel phase, Hardy function, symmetrised truncation, one sided criterion, torus bound, Weil criterion, Bernstein cone, de Bruijn Newman flow, tail cumulants, zero drift, Hermite coefficients, Hermite expansion, Riemann Xi function, Gaussian smoothing, turning point, sign changes

chapters.title: Friable approximants of Xi after Miyatake and the cosh ladder
chapters.summary:
Which real zeros does the friable approximant of the Riemann Xi function share with Xi, and what does this test case say about computational criteria for the Riemann Hypothesis (RH)? Keep only the integers composed of the primes up to $P$ (the $P$ friable, or smooth, integers) in Riemann's theta series. The result, the friable approximant $\Xi_P$, differs from $\Xi$ by an exponentially small deficit, of size about $4\pi q^2e^{-\pi q^2}$ with $q$ the first prime left out, and yet has infinitely many zeros off the real line. The chapter proves that the folded kernel has a kink, that no summable reweighting of the theta series has infinitely many real zeros, that the deficit is positive and a sum of Lorentzians, and that real zeros live in the negative humps of $\Xi$ and are lost in pairs, with an exact count given the verification of RH to a finite height. A heuristic formula (checked by computation) puts the breakdown at height about $4q^2$. It then reads an identity of Miyatake probabilistically (Lévy's stochastic area, a Pólya Gamma clock, a logistic partition of unity), studies the exponential tail and the threshold $b=2$ of the transform of the kernel divided by $\cosh(bu)$, and places the bottom of the cosh ladder against the quasi Riemann abscissa, with a Hermite Biehler equivalence for the paired form. Nothing here proves RH. The unregularised symmetrised Euler product has zeros near its poles whose real parts tend to one (a note of Nicholas Polson).

#### From the literature

- Riemann's theta series representation of $\xi$ and the zeros of $\Xi$ on the critical line (Hardy 1914; Titchmarsh 1986)
- Friable approximants and the symmetrised Pólya kernel (Miyatake 1951; Hejhal 1990), truncated theta series in incomplete gamma form (Haglund 2009)
- The cosh ladder: reciprocals of $\cosh(bu)$ times the kernel are generalised gamma convolutions for $b\ge\frac12$ (de Bruijn 1950; Lagarias 1999)
- The de Bruijn Newman constant is nonnegative (Rodgers and Tao 2020)
- Verification of RH to height $3\cdot10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021); the bound $|\zeta(\frac12+it)|\ll t^{1/6}\log t$ with explicit constant (Hiary 2016)
- The Biane Pitman Yor identity (Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001), the Pólya Gamma mixture (Polson, Scott and Windle 2013), Ingham's density estimate (Ingham 1940), Chebotarev's theorem (Chebotarev 1928), the Davenport Heilbronn function (Davenport and Heilbronn 1936)

#### New results

Statements are proved unless marked: the imaginary axis proposition is a computation on a grid, the count conjecture and the quasi Riemann abscissa conjecture are open; the zero count heuristic and the problems are not catalogued. The Pólya mixture section adds the polar part of the Miyatake kernel at $\cos\frac{2\pi}9$, the proof that this exponent is forced, and a Meixner convolution form of the polar transform; the interlacing subsection adds Euler product criteria for the zeros of the real and imaginary parts of $\xi$ on two lines to alternate or not, and a collision law for one pair of zeros under a random vertical average (proved). A note of Nicholas Polson adds the positive transform of every theta term with the Laplace law as a mixture (proved) and computed real and nonreal zeros of the theta series cut after one or two terms.
- [The friable approximant of Xi is exponentially close to Xi in a strip, with the accuracy set by the first omitted prime](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#friable_approximant_error_bound_in_strip_set_by_first_omitted_prime) (Volume II, Theorem 18.2.1, page 483; proved): For $|\operatorname{Im}t|\le\frac32$ the friable approximant satisfies $|\Xi_P(t)-\Xi(t)|\le|t^2+\frac14|\,\delta_P$ with $\delta_P\le e^{-\pi q^2}/(\pi q^2(1-e^{-2\pi q}))$. New in this book.
- [Certified tracking: a Rouche criterion for a real zero of the friable approximant near a simple zero of Xi](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#certified_tracking_of_a_simple_zero_of_xi_by_a_real_zero_of_the_friable_approximant) (Volume II, Corollary 18.2.2, page 483; proved): If a simple zero $\gamma$ of $\Xi$ has $|\Xi|>|t^2+\frac14|\delta_P$ on a circle of radius $r\le\frac32$ about it, then $\Xi_P$ has exactly one zero in the disc, it is real, and its shift from $\gamma$ is given to first order by $-(\Xi_P-\Xi)(\gamma)/\Xi'(\gamma)$. New in this book.
- [The symmetrised finite Euler product of Xi has zeros near the lines of its poles with real part tending to one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#friable_symmetrised_euler_product_has_spurious_zeros_near_the_poles_with_real_part_tending_to_one) (Volume II, Proposition 18.1.5, page 483; proved): The unregularised symmetrisation F_P of the finite Euler product has zeros within order k to the power minus one half of the poles 1 plus 2 pi i k over log p for infinitely many k, so their real parts tend to one and those of the mirror zeros to zero; this is from a note of Nicholas Polson. New in this book.
- [The folded kernel of the friable approximant has a kink of exact size c_P, so Xi_P tends to c_P on the real line and has finitely many real zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#kink_constant_of_the_friable_approximant_and_finitely_many_real_zeros) (Volume II, Theorem 18.2.3, page 484; proved): The folded kernel of $\Xi_P$ has a corner at the origin of size $c_P=\sum_{m\notin\mathcal F(P)}(4\pi m^2-1)e^{-\pi m^2}\sim4\pi q^2e^{-\pi q^2}>0$, so $\Xi_P(t)\to c_P$ along the real axis and $\Xi_P$ has finitely many real zeros. New in this book.
- [No reweighting of Riemann's theta series by summable weights has infinitely many real zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#no_summable_reweighting_of_the_theta_series_has_infinitely_many_real_zeros) (Volume II, Theorem 18.2.4, page 484; proved): For nonzero real weights $w_n$ with $\sum|w_n|n^{-\sigma}<\infty$ for every $\sigma>0$ (this includes the friable truncations), the reweighted function has finitely many real zeros and infinitely many nonreal zeros. New in this book.
- [Theta series truncated to N terms of Xi: constants, real zeros and nonreal zeros for N equal to 1 and 2 (computed)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#truncated_theta_series_have_finitely_many_real_zeros_and_the_first_zeros_for_one_and_two_terms) (Volume II, Result 18.2, page 485; computed): For the theta series cut after one or two terms the transform tends to a positive constant $c_E$ on the real line ($1.71806\cdot10^{-4}$ and $5.89126\cdot10^{-11}$), has 2 and 6 real zeros in $0<t\le60$ against 13 for Xi, and has the listed nonreal zeros; the zero counts and positions are a computation, a note of Nicholas Polson. New in this book.
- [The deficit Xi_P minus Xi is positive on the real line and decreases as the prime bound grows](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#deficit_of_the_friable_approximant_is_positive_and_decreasing_in_the_prime_bound) (Volume II, Theorem 18.3.1, page 486; proved): For every prime $P$ and real $t$, $\Xi_P(t)-\Xi(t)>0$, and the deficit decreases strictly as $P$ increases, so $\Xi_P>\Xi_{P'}>\Xi$ on $\mathbb{R}$ for $P<P'$. New in this book.
- [The transform of no theta term vanishes on the real line, and the Laplace law is a mixture of the Polya law and a pole law](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#no_term_of_the_theta_series_has_a_vanishing_transform_and_the_laplace_law_is_a_mixture) (Volume II, Result 18.3.2, page 486; proved): The cosine transform of every term of the theta series is positive on the real line, so the zeros of Xi are exactly the solutions of $(t^2+\frac14)W(t)=1$ with $W>0$ on the real line, and the Laplace density is the mixture, with weights $1-\upsilon$ and $\upsilon$ where $\upsilon=0.00575844$ (computed), of the Polya law convolved with a Laplace law and an explicit law $p_V$; a note of Nicholas Polson. New in this book.
- [Uniform Lorentzian bound: the deficit of the friable approximant is a sum of Lorentzians with an explicit uniform relative error](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#deficit_of_the_friable_approximant_is_a_sum_of_lorentzians_with_explicit_error) (Volume II, Theorem 18.3.4, page 487; proved): For $a\ge9\pi$ the cosine transform $C_a$ of $e^{-ae^w}e^{w/4}$ equals the Lorentzian $\mathcal L_a(t)=e^{-a}b/(b^2+t^2/4)$ with relative error at most $\delta(a)\le5.61/a$, uniformly in real $t$, and the deficit $D_P$ is the corresponding sum over the omitted integers. New in this book.
- [Curvature: the logarithm of the deficit of the friable approximant is uniformly almost convex for t at least 14](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#uniform_curvature_bound_for_the_log_of_the_deficit_of_the_friable_approximant) (Volume II, Theorem 18.3.5, page 488; proved): For every prime $P$ and $t\ge14$, $(\log D_P)''(t)\ge-0.0239$ for the deficit $D_P=\Xi_P-\Xi$, with an explicit bound in terms of the least omitted prime. New in this book.
- [Real zeros of the friable approximant live in the negative humps of Xi, in pairs, and surviving humps are nested in P](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#real_zeros_of_the_friable_approximant_live_in_negative_humps_of_xi_in_pairs) (Volume II, Theorem 18.4.1, page 489; proved): Every real zero of $\Xi_P$ lies in a negative hump of $\Xi$ and each hump holds an even number of zeros; for humps below the verified height of RH and shorter than $18.29$, a hump holds none, one double or two simple zeros, according to the sign of $\max(|\Xi|-D_P)$ on it, and surviving humps are nested in $P$. New in this book.
- [Count: the number of positive real zeros of the friable approximant is twice the number of negative humps of Xi deeper than the deficit](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#count_of_real_zeros_of_the_friable_approximant_is_twice_the_number_of_deep_humps) (Volume II, Theorem 18.4.2, page 490; proved): Under the hypotheses of the hump theorem the number $R_P$ of positive real zeros of $\Xi_P$ is twice the number of humps with $\max(|\Xi|-D_P)>0$, there is a unique height $\tau_P^+$ beyond which $\Xi_P>0$, and $R_P\le2\lceil N(\tau_P^+)/2\rceil$. New in this book.
- [Conjecture: the number of real zeros of the friable approximant is the zero count at the breakdown height plus a correction from the peaks of Hardy's function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#conjecture_on_the_number_of_real_zeros_of_the_friable_approximant_and_the_peaks_of_hardys_function) (Volume II, Conjecture 18.5.1, page 491; open): The number $R_P$ of positive real zeros of $\Xi_P$ is conjectured to equal $N(\tau_P^*)$ plus $\frac2{\pi^2}\log\frac{\tau_P^*}{2\pi}$ times the mean log peak of Hardy's function on negative humps near $\tau_P^*$, up to an error of order $\sqrt{\log q\,\log\log q}$. New in this book.
- [Kink budget: the limit of the friable approximant with a smooth even kernel replacing the pole term](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#kink_budget_when_the_pole_kernel_is_replaced_by_a_smooth_even_kernel) (Volume II, Proposition 18.8.1, page 495; proved): If the pole kernel $e^{-u/2}$ in the folded kernel of $\Xi_P$ is replaced by an even smooth kernel $\kappa$ with derivatives $O(e^{-u/2})$, the limit of the modified function along the real axis is $c_P-\frac12-\kappa'(0+)$. New in this book.
- [Reweighting: among weights in [0,1] vanishing on a given set, the indicator of the complement has the smallest deficit](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reweighting_with_weights_in_zero_one_has_smallest_deficit_for_the_indicator_of_the_complement) (Volume II, Proposition 18.8.2, page 496; proved): For weights $0\le w_n\le w_n'\le1$ the deficits satisfy $D_w\ge D_{w'}\ge0$ with $D_{w'}>0$ unless all $w_n'=1$, so the friable truncation has the smallest deficit among weights in $[0,1]$ that vanish on the omitted set. New in this book.
- [The friable approximants for P = 2 and 3 are uniformly close to Xi on the imaginary axis and have no zero there](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#friable_approximant_is_uniformly_close_to_xi_on_the_imaginary_axis_for_p_2_and_3) (Volume II, Proposition 18.9.1, page 497; computed): The relative error $\sup_y|\Xi_P(iy)/\Xi(iy)-1|$ is at most $6.8\times10^{-13}$ for $P=2$ and $3.4\times10^{-35}$ for $P=3$, so neither has a zero on the imaginary axis; the suprema of a proved bound were computed on a grid. New in this book.
- [Shift identity: Xi is the average of two shifts of the transform of Phi divided by cosh, which contains Miyatake's identity](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#shift_identity_xi_is_the_cosine_of_a_shift_applied_to_the_transform_of_phi_over_cosh) (Volume II, Proposition 18.11.1, page 500; proved): For every $b>0$ and complex $z$, $\Xi(z)=\frac12\{g_b(z+ib)+g_b(z-ib)\}$, that is $\Xi=\cos(b\,d/dz)g_b$; Miyatake's identity is the case $b=\frac92$. New in this book.
- [Levy area, Polya Gamma clock and Thorin atoms: the transform of Phi over cosh is Xi smoothed by Levy's stochastic area](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#transform_of_phi_over_cosh_is_a_levy_area_smoothing_and_a_polya_gamma_mixture_of_the_flow) (Volume II, Theorem 18.11.2, page 500; proved): The transform $g_b$ equals the expectation of $\Xi(x+2b\mathcal A)$ for Lévy's stochastic area $\mathcal A$, and the expectation of the de Bruijn Newman function at a Pólya Gamma random negative time, so $\Xi\mapsto g_b$ is convolution with an extended generalised gamma convolution with Thorin atoms at the odd multiples of $\pi/(2b)$. New in this book.
- [Logistic partition: 2 xi is the sum of two logistic weighted expectations of a power of a random variable](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#logistic_partition_of_unity_splits_xi_into_two_pieces_of_the_transform_over_cosh) (Volume II, Proposition 18.11.3, page 500; proved): For $c>0$, $2\xi(s)$ is the sum of the expectations of $\Upsilon^s/(1+\Upsilon^c)$ and $\Upsilon^{s+c}/(1+\Upsilon^c)$, for the random variable $\Upsilon$ of the Biane Pitman Yor identity, and the logistic weight is a Pólya Gamma mixture. New in this book.
- [Exponential tail: the transform of Phi over cosh has a residue term C_b e^{-pi z/(2b)} exactly when b exceeds 2](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#exponential_tail_of_the_transform_of_phi_over_cosh_appears_exactly_above_b_equal_two) (Volume II, Theorem 18.12.1, page 501; proved): For $b>2$ the transform $g_b$ equals $C_be^{-\pi z/(2b)}$ plus a faster decaying error, with $C_b=\frac{2\pi}b\Phi(\frac{i\pi}{2b})$, uniformly in horizontal strips; for $b<2$ there is no residue and $g_b(x)=O(e^{-\tau x})$ for every $\tau<\pi/4$. New in this book.
- [Cusp asymptotics: the residue constant C_b of the transform of Phi over cosh as b decreases to 2](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#cusp_asymptotics_of_the_residue_constant_as_b_decreases_to_two) (Volume II, Theorem 18.12.2, page 502; proved): With $\delta=\pi(b-2)/(4b)$, as $b\downarrow2$ the constant $C_b$ is asymptotic to $-\frac{\pi^3}{32b}(2\delta)^{-1/2}\delta^{-4}e^{-\frac\pi8\cot\delta}$ and is negative and super exponentially small. New in this book.
- [For b above 2 with C_b nonzero the transform of Phi over cosh has finitely many real zeros and is not in the Laguerre Polya class](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#transform_of_phi_over_cosh_for_b_above_two_is_not_in_the_laguerre_polya_class) (Volume II, Corollary 18.12.3, page 502; proved): For $b>2$ with $C_b\ne0$ the transform $g_b$ has finitely many real zeros and infinitely many nonreal zeros, so it is not in the Laguerre Pólya class; in particular Miyatake's transform ($b=\frac92$, $C_{9/2}>0$) is not. New in this book.
- [Polar part of the Miyatake kernel in the variable cosh t: a simple pole at cos(2 pi/9) with positive residue r_0](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#polar_part_of_the_psi_m_kernel_is_a_simple_pole_at_cos_two_pi_over_nine_with_positive_residue) (Volume II, Proposition 18.13.1, page 504; proved): As a function of $c=\cosh t$ the kernel $\psi_{\mathrm M}$ is analytic on $\operatorname{Re}c>0$ except for one simple pole at $c_0=\cos\frac{2\pi}9$ with residue $r_0=0.009206406367>0$ (digits certified), so $\psi_{\mathrm M}$ is the sum of the theta terms $n^4e^{-2\pi n^2c}$, an exponential mixture $\psi_{\mathrm E}$ carrying the pole and a part analytic on the half plane; a note of Nicholas Polson. New in this book.
- [The exponent is forced: an exponential mixture of Pólya Bessel functions has finitely many real zeros unless its exponent is cos(2 pi/9)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#exponential_mixture_of_polya_bessel_functions_has_nonreal_zeros_unless_the_exponent_is_cos_two_pi_over_nine) (Volume II, Proposition 18.13.2, page 505; proved): For $0<\theta<\frac\pi2$, $\theta\ne\frac{2\pi}9$, the exponential mixture $\mathcal E_\theta$ with exponent $\cos\theta$ of the Pólya functions $\frac12\{K_{9/4+iz/2}(a)+K_{9/4-iz/2}(a)\}$ has the asymptotic $\frac{\pi\cos(9\theta/4)}{\sin\theta}e^{-\theta z/2}+O(e^{-\tau\operatorname{Re}z})$, finitely many real zeros, infinitely many nonreal zeros, and is not in the Laguerre Pólya class; only $\cos\frac{2\pi}9$, the exponent of the polar part, is left open. New in this book.
- [A Meixner convolution: the polar transform is a Pólya frequency density convolved with a Laguerre Pólya function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#polar_transform_is_a_meixner_convolution_of_a_laguerre_polya_function_and_the_meixner_law_is_a_polya_frequency_function) (Volume II, Proposition 18.13.3, page 505; proved): With $c_1=\cos\frac\pi9$ and $\mathcal U(u)=\cosh(9u/2)/(2(\cosh u-c_1))$ a universal factor, the transform $\Xi^{\mathcal U}$ of $\mathcal U(u)e^{-2\pi\cosh2u}$ is in the Laguerre Pólya class, the Meixner density $q_\varphi$ with characteristic function $(1+\cos\varphi)/(\cosh u+\cos\varphi)$ is a Pólya frequency function and a Gaussian mixture, and the polar transform $\Xi^{\mathrm E}$ equals a constant times $q_{\pi/9}*\Xi^{\mathcal U}$; a note of Nicholas Polson, using theorems of Pólya and Schoenberg. New in this book.
- [The bottom of the cosh ladder is at most the largest real part of a zero of zeta minus one half](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#bottom_of_the_cosh_ladder_is_bounded_by_the_quasi_riemann_abscissa) (Volume II, Proposition 18.14.1, page 507; proved): The bottom rung $B_{\cosh}$ of the cosh ladder satisfies $B_{\cosh}\le\sigma_{\max}-\frac12$, where $\sigma_{\max}$ is the supremum of the real parts of the nontrivial zeros of zeta. New in this book.
- [Conjecture: the bottom of the cosh ladder lies between the asymptotic and the global quasi Riemann abscissa](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#conjecture_bottom_of_the_cosh_ladder_equals_the_asymptotic_quasi_riemann_abscissa) (Volume II, Conjecture 18.14.2, page 509; open): The bottom rung of the cosh ladder is conjectured to satisfy $\sigma_{\max}^\infty-\frac12\le B_{\cosh}\le\sigma_{\max}-\frac12$ with $\sigma_{\max}^\infty=\limsup_{\gamma\to\infty}\beta$; the upper bound is proved. New in this book.
- [Paired form: zeta has no zero to the right of alpha exactly when the real and imaginary parts of xi on the line alpha interlace](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#paired_form_of_the_cosh_ladder_hermite_biehler_equivalence_with_zero_free_half_plane) (Volume II, Theorem 18.14.3, page 509; proved): For $\alpha>\frac12$, zeta has no zero with real part at least $\alpha$ exactly when $E_\alpha(z)=\xi(\alpha-iz)$ is Hermite Biehler, exactly when the real and imaginary parts of $\xi(\alpha+it)$ have only real simple strictly interlacing zeros; hence RH holds if and only if this holds for every $\alpha>\frac12$. New in this book.
- [Real zeros of the real and imaginary parts of xi on a vertical line right of one half have asymptotically full density](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#density_of_real_zeros_of_the_real_and_imaginary_parts_of_xi_on_a_line_to_the_right_of_one_half) (Volume II, Theorem 18.14.4, page 511; proved): For $\alpha>\frac12$ with no zero of zeta on the line, $\theta_\alpha(T)-\theta_\alpha(-T)=\pi(N^\pm(T)-2N^\pm_{>\alpha}(T))+O(\log T)$, so $\operatorname{Re}\xi(\alpha+it)$ and $\operatorname{Im}\xi(\alpha+it)$ each have at least $N^\pm(T)-2N^\pm_{>\alpha}(T)-O(\log T)$ real zeros in $[-T,T]$. New in this book.
- [Interlacing across rungs: criteria for the zeros of the real and imaginary parts of xi on two lines to alternate or to fail to alternate](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#zeros_of_real_parts_and_imaginary_parts_of_xi_on_two_lines_to_the_right_of_one_alternate_or_fail_to_alternate_by_the_euler_product) (Volume II, Proposition 18.14.5, page 512; proved): For $1<\alpha<\alpha'$ the phase difference of $\xi$ on the two lines is $\frac{h\pi}4$ up to $\mathcal I=\log(\zeta(\alpha)/\zeta(\alpha'))$, so the zeros of the real parts (or of the imaginary parts) alternate for large height when $[\frac{h\pi}4-\mathcal I,\frac{h\pi}4+\mathcal I]$ lies between consecutive multiples of $\pi$, and the real and imaginary parts alternate when it lies between consecutive odd multiples of $\frac\pi2$, while they fail to alternate at arbitrarily large height when a multiple of $\pi$, or an odd multiple of $\frac\pi2$, lies inside $(\frac{h\pi}4-J,\frac{h\pi}4+J)$; a note of Nicholas Polson. New in this book.
- [Non interlacing: the zeros of A_alpha and of the Bessel functions K do not alternate with the real zeros of Xi](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#zeros_of_the_real_part_of_xi_on_a_line_to_the_right_of_one_do_not_alternate_with_the_zeros_of_xi) (Volume II, Proposition 18.14.6, page 513; proved): For $\alpha>1$ the real part of $\xi(\alpha+it)$ has $N(T)-S(T)+O_\alpha(1)$ zeros up to $T$, and $\operatorname{Re}K_{9/4+it/2}(a)$ has $\frac T{2\pi}(\log\frac Ta-1)+O_a(1)$, so neither alternates with the real zeros of $\Xi$ for large $t$ (for the Bessel functions with $a>2\pi$ under the Riemann Hypothesis), and two Bessel functions with different $a$ do not alternate; a note of Nicholas Polson. New in this book.
- [Collision of one pair of zeros under a random vertical average: the critical spread depends on the variance and the fourth moment](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#collision_of_one_pair_of_zeros_under_a_vertical_random_average_is_decided_by_the_variance_and_the_kurtosis) (Volume II, Proposition 18.14.8, page 515; proved): For a real entire function $G$ of order less than two and $F_\eta(z)=((z-a)^2+\eta^2)G(z)$, the average $\mathbb{E}F_\eta(z+is\ell)$ over a symmetric unit variance bounded or normal $\ell$ has near $a$ a nonreal pair of zeros for $s<s_c$, a double real zero at $s_c$ and two real zeros for $s>s_c$, with $s_c^2=\eta^2-d_c\eta^4+O(\eta^6)$ and $d_c=\tau_1^2-\frac{m_4-1}2\tau_2$; a note of Nicholas Polson. New in this book.

#### Key terms

friable approximant, smooth number approximation of Xi, Riemann Xi function, theta series truncation, kink constant, Lorentzian, negative hump, Hardy function, cosh ladder, quasi Riemann hypothesis, quasi Riemann abscissa, Miyatake, Lévy area, Pólya Gamma, generalised gamma convolution, generalized gamma convolution, GGC, Thorin measure, Laguerre Pólya class, Hermite Biehler, de Bruijn Newman

chapters.title: Ferromagnetic and extreme value approximants with certified real zeros
chapters.summary:
Can the Pólya density of the Riemann Xi function be approximated by explicit laws whose zeros can be controlled, and how close does this bring one to the Riemann Hypothesis (RH)? The chapter has two halves with one method: replace the Pólya law $p=\Phi/\Xi(0)$ by a law with real zeros that can be certified. In the first half, RH holds exactly when the total variation distance from the Pólya law to the class of ferromagnetic laws is zero, and the chapter bounds this distance above, with no hypothesis, by distances to laws proved ferromagnetic: Pólya's approximations, tilts that shrink the strip of analyticity, multipliers $e^{-a\cosh\ell t}$ on the Pólya kernel (Bessel type laws), and laws that keep the first zeros, with distances enclosed in ball arithmetic and a computer assisted positivity proof giving distance below $1.932\times10^{-6}$. It proves that RH is equivalent to an identity in law with a series of Maxwell variables, and that a cusped weight $e^{-a|t|}$ never gives a ferromagnetic tilt. The second half writes each term of the theta series as a combination of two Gumbel kernels of fractional order and builds three families of approximations (folded Gumbel kernels, Pólya's two sided kernel, the Dyck chain). It shows that the zeros of Xi are all real if and only if the reciprocal xi law is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC), and real and simple if and only if it is the hitting time of a Krein string (Kent's theorem), and reduces RH to a height rule for the folded kernels, with a Rouché certificate in ball arithmetic for the first four levels. It studies shifted Bessel kernels through a Liouville boundary problem and a cotangent law, a Pólya frequency characterisation of RH (Schoenberg), Devroye's alternating series and an expansion of the mean excess function, and a detection rule for the first nonreal pair along the de Bruijn Newman flow. Longer runs on the open problems are floating point and marked computed. Each route stops at a known place, and none proves RH.

#### From the literature

- Pólya's theorems on real zeros and approximations of $\Xi$ (Pólya 1918; 1926), de Bruijn's strip theorem (1950)
- The Lee and Yang property and Newman's single spin laws (Lee and Yang 1952; Newman 1975)
- Kent's theorem on hitting times of one dimensional diffusions and Krein's inverse spectral theory of strings (Kent 1980; Krein)
- Fractional order statistics and the Gumbel limit process (Stigler 1977), peaks over threshold laws (Pickands 1975; Balkema and de Haan 1974)
- Schoenberg's characterisation of Pólya frequency functions (Schoenberg 1951)
- The de Bruijn and Newman constant, its lower and upper bounds (Rodgers and Tao 2020; Polymath 2019; Platt and Trudgian 2021)
- Biane's Liouville string for Pólya's kernel and Devroye's alternating series for densities
- Hurwitz's theorem and Rouché's theorem

#### New results

Results of this chapter, with their status.

- [Cosine and Gaussian tilts of the Pólya law with variance at least 9/64 if there is no zero beyond 7/8](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#cosine_and_gaussian_tilts_of_polya_law_ferromagnetic_if_no_zero_beyond_seven_eighths) (Volume II, Proposition 19.1.2, page 520; conditional on The Riemann zeta function has no zero with real part greater than 7/8 (announced by OpenAI in October 2026, not refereed, and not proved in the book)): If the Riemann zeta function has no zero with real part above 7/8, then tilting the Pólya density by cosh(at) with a at least 3/8, or by other multipliers of variance at least 9/64, gives a ferromagnetic law, against 1/2 and 1/4 with no hypothesis. New in this book.
- [Ferromagnetic laws with density proportional to a multiplier times exp(-a cosh(l t)), Bessel transform and clock](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#ferromagnetic_laws_on_a_bessel_kernel_with_multipliers) (Volume II, Theorem 19.1.4, page 522; proved): Multiplying the kernel exp(-a cosh(l t)) by a product of cosh factors and a Gaussian factor always gives a ferromagnetic law with no Gaussian component, whose moment generating function and clock are explicit averages of Macdonald functions K of real order, with the clock for no multiplier a sum of exponential variables divided by the squared zeros of K of imaginary order; this is from a note of Nicholas Polson. New in this book.
- [Laws on a Bessel kernel as logarithms of mixtures of generalised inverse Gaussian laws](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#bessel_family_laws_are_log_mixtures_of_generalised_inverse_gaussian_laws) (Volume II, Proposition 19.1.5, page 523; proved): Each law with density proportional to m(t) exp(-a cosh(l t)) is the law of the logarithm of a generalised inverse Gaussian variable with a random index weighted by the Macdonald function, so that for no Gaussian factor it can be sampled exactly; this is from a note of Nicholas Polson. New in this book.
- [No sequence of laws on a convergent Bessel kernel with Laguerre Pólya multipliers converges in law to the Pólya law](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#no_sequence_on_one_bessel_kernel_converges_in_law_to_polya_law) (Volume II, Proposition 19.1.8, page 525; proved): A sequence of laws with density proportional to a Laguerre Pólya multiplier times exp(-a_n cosh(l_n t)), with kernel parameters converging to positive limits, cannot converge in law to the Pólya law, with or without RH, because the Pólya density has a natural boundary; this answers a question of a note of Nicholas Polson. New in this book.
- [Coupled spins with Bessel kernel laws and a ferromagnetic interaction have ferromagnetic nonnegative combinations](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#coupled_bessel_spins_with_ferromagnetic_interaction_give_ferromagnetic_sums) (Volume II, Corollary 19.1.9, page 526; proved): For spins whose single laws are the Bessel kernel laws of the ferromagnetic theorem, coupled by a nonnegative symmetric interaction J, every combination of the spins with nonnegative coefficients is ferromagnetic; this is from notes of Nicholas Polson. New in this book.
- [Zeros of the transform of two weakly coupled Bessel spins move by order J at a simple zero and by plus or minus the square root of J at a common zero](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#small_coupling_moves_the_zeros_of_two_bessel_spins_by_order_j_or_square_root_of_j) (Volume II, Proposition 19.1.10, page 527; proved): For the sum of two coupled spins with Bessel kernel laws, a simple zero of one characteristic function that is not a zero of the other moves by J times the logarithmic derivative of the other, and a common simple zero splits into a real pair at distance twice the square root of J, as J decreases to zero; this is from notes of Nicholas Polson. New in this book.
- [Mellin transform of the clock of the Bessel K pair has no zero in a box where the uniform pair has two (computed)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#bessel_pair_mellin_transform_has_no_zero_in_box_computed) (Volume II, Result 19.1.3, page 527; computed): For two copies of the Bessel K law with characteristic function $K_{i\theta/4}(\pi)/K_0(\pi)$ the Mellin transform of the clock has no zero in a box holding two zeros of the uniform pair, by a sampled argument principle count that is not a ball proof. New in this book.
- [The components of the theta series in Riemann's formula and their mixture are not ferromagnetic](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#components_of_riemann_theta_series_and_their_mixture_are_not_ferromagnetic) (Volume II, Proposition 19.1.11, page 528; proved): The laws with densities proportional to $e^{|t|/2}\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2|t|})$ and to their sum over $n\ge1$ have a characteristic function that is positive on the real line, entire and with infinitely many zeros, none real, so none is ferromagnetic. New in this book.
- [Zero completed laws of the Pólya variable, the Maxwell construction and a criterion for RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#zero_completed_laws_maxwell_construction_and_rh_criterion) (Volume II, Theorem 19.1.12, page 529; proved): Keeping the first K zero factors of the Pólya characteristic function and a Gaussian factor gives laws that are exactly ferromagnetic for K up to 16 by a Maxwell construction with a certified inequality, ferromagnetic whenever nonnegative, and whose characteristic functions converge to that of the Pólya law exactly when the Riemann Hypothesis holds. New in this book.
- [RH is equivalent to an identity in law between the smoothed Pólya variable and a series of Maxwell variables](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rh_iff_polya_variable_smoothed_by_gaussian_equals_maxwell_series_in_law) (Volume II, Theorem 19.1.14, page 532; proved): The Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if the Pólya variable plus an independent Gaussian of half its variance has the law of the series of independent Maxwell variables divided by the ordinates of the zeros. New in this book.
- [Total variation distance from the Pólya law to ferromagnetic laws is below two millionths, with no hypothesis](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#polya_law_within_total_variation_two_millionths_of_a_ferromagnetic_law) (Volume II, Proposition 19.1.15, page 532; proved): With no hypothesis the total variation distance from the Pólya law to the ferromagnetic laws is below 1.932 × 10^-6 by a certified computation in ball arithmetic and below 1.266 × 10^-4 by an explicit construction, below 6.024 × 10^-6 by a fitted law on a Bessel kernel (a note of Nicholas Polson), and it is zero exactly when the Riemann Hypothesis holds. New in this book.
- [A cusped weight never gives a ferromagnetic tilt nor a GGC tilted clock](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#cusped_weight_never_gives_ferromagnetic_tilt_or_ggc_tilted_clock) (Volume II, Theorem 19.1.16, page 533; proved): For every $\mu>0$ the Pólya law tilted by the cusped weight $e^{-\mu|t|/2}$ is not ferromagnetic and the correspondingly tilted clock is not a generalized gamma convolution, because the transform $H^{(\mu)}$ of the tilted kernel is a Cauchy average of the xi function with a tail of order $1/z^2$, so it is positive beyond some height and has finitely many real zeros. New in this book.
- [Laplace weighted de Bruijn Newman function H^[a] and a sufficient condition for RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#laplace_weighted_debruijn_newman_function_and_a_sufficient_condition_for_rh) (Volume II, Proposition 19.1.17, page 534; proved): The weight 1 over 1 plus a squared u squared gives a function H^[a] that is an average of the de Bruijn Newman function at Laplace shifted points and an exponential mixture of backward heat flows, and if it has only real zeros for one a then RH holds; whether it has real zeros is open. New in this book.
- [If the folded kernels have only real zeros in the disc of radius 2c(N+1)^2 for every N then RH holds](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#height_rule_for_the_folded_kernels_reduces_rh_to_real_zeros_in_a_growing_disc) (Volume II, Proposition 19.2.1, page 537; proved): If there is $c>0$ such that for every $N\ge1$ all zeros of $H^F_N$ in the disc $|z|<2c(N+1)^2$ are real, then RH holds. The height rule itself is not proved: it is checked in the range described in the chapter (Rouch\'e certificate for $N=1,\dots,4$, computed for $N=5$). New in this book.
- [Kink bound: the error of the folded kernel decays like 1/x^2 with an explicit constant](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#kink_bound_for_the_error_of_the_folded_kernel_on_the_real_axis) (Volume II, Lemma 19.3.1, page 538; proved): For real $x\ne0$, $|E_N(x)|\le B_N/x^2$ with $B_N=|R_N'(0)|+\|R_N''\|_{L^1(0,\infty)}$, from $E_N(x)=-R_N'(0)/x^2-x^{-2}\int_0^\infty R_N''(u)\cos(xu)\,du$. New in this book.
- [Rouche certificate: a circle inequality and a sign change count show that all zeros of the folded kernel below a height are real](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rouche_certificate_that_the_folded_kernel_has_only_real_zeros_below_a_height) (Volume II, Proposition 19.3.2, page 538; proved): Let $T$ lie strictly between two consecutive ordinates and suppose $\Xi$ has exactly $2\mathcal N(T)$ zeros in $|w|<T$, all real and simple. If $|E_N|<|H|$ on $z=2Te^{i\vartheta}$, $\vartheta\in[0,\pi/2]$, and $H^F_N(2x)$ has $\mathcal N(T)$ sign changes on $(0,T)$, then every zero of $H^F_N(2x)$ with $|x|<T$ is real. The inequality was certified in ball arithmetic only for $N=1,\dots,4$ at the tabulated heights, and checked in floating point for $N=5$. New in this book.

chapters.title: The Comtet Majumdar family: damped kernels and a solved model
chapters.summary:
Can the Riemann zeta function be reached by explicit probability laws, and can approximants with all zeros real be built from them? The chapter starts from the Comtet and Majumdar identity, in which the Mellin transform of the Bose function equals $\zeta(s)$ over a sine factor, and which gives the constant in the expected maximum of a random walk with symmetric stable steps. It writes the logarithm of the Laplace transform of the uniform law as a regularised integral against Lebesgue minus counting measure, and proves that the reciprocal of an even entire function of order below two is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if all its zeros are real. The $2\sin^2$ lemma turns a signed Lévy measure into a Thorin density, which is nonnegative if and only if a logarithmic derivative inequality holds. For the tilted uniform law the Thorin density is strictly positive for every positive tilt, a Lorentzian smoothing of the lattice $2\pi m$, with Mellin transform the shifted zeta function. The obstructions are proved as well: the shifted $\xi$ function is meromorphic with a pole at $s=3$, so its reciprocal is not a GGC transform, and a kink theorem shows that the Gauss damped Riemann kernel has finitely many real zeros and infinitely many nonreal zeros. Modular constraints on damped kernels in the Laguerre and Pólya class follow, together with a treatment of the de Bruijn Newman family and of what the identity contributes to it. RH itself is not proved, and each route is marked where it stops.

#### From the literature

- The Comtet and Majumdar identity for the expected maximum of a random walk (Comtet and Majumdar 2005), with the combinatorial lemma of Spitzer (1956)
- Generalised gamma convolutions and Thorin measures (Bondesson 1992)
- Probability laws related to the Jacobi theta and Riemann zeta functions (Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001)
- The theory of the Riemann zeta function and of entire functions, including zeros of Fourier transforms (Titchmarsh 1986)
- Zeta functions over the zeros of zeta (Voros 2010)
- The de Bruijn Newman constant (de Bruijn 1950; Newman 1976)

#### New results

- [A proof by Spitzer's identity and Euler Maclaurin summation that the expected maximum of a symmetric stable walk has the constant of Comtet and Majumdar, zeta of s over a sine factor](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#expected_maximum_of_a_stable_walk_has_the_zeta_constant_of_comtet_and_majumdar) (Volume II, Proposition 20.1.2, page 559; proved): For a random walk with symmetric stable steps of index $\mu\in(1,2]$ and $s=1/\mu$, $\mathbb EM_n=\frac{\Gamma(1-s)}{\pi s}n^s+\frac{\Gamma(1-s)\zeta(1-s)}{\pi}+O(n^{s-1})$, so the constant is $\zeta(s)/((2\pi)^s\sin(\pi s/2))$, by Spitzer's identity and Euler Maclaurin summation. New in this book.
- [The logarithm of the Laplace transform of the uniform law is a regularised integral against Lebesgue minus counting measure](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#logarithm_of_the_uniform_transform_as_a_regularised_signed_levy_integral) (Volume II, Proposition 20.1.3, page 560; proved): For $x>0$, $\ln\frac{1-e^{-x}}{x}=-\lim_{R\to\infty}\{\int_0^R(1-e^{-xt})\frac{dt}t-\sum_{1\le n\le R}\frac{1-e^{-xn}}n\}$, and for $0<\operatorname{Re}z<1$, $\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_0^Rt^{-z}(d\lfloor t\rfloor-dt)=\zeta(z)$. New in this book.
- [If locally uniform limits of GGC reciprocals approximate Xi then RH holds](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#locally_uniform_limit_of_ggc_reciprocals_implies_real_zeros) (Volume II, Corollary 20.2.2, page 561; proved): If even real entire functions $\Xi_\delta$ of order below two with $\Xi_\delta(0)>0$, each with $\Xi_\delta(0)/\Xi_\delta(i\sqrt w)$ a GGC transform, converge to $\Xi$ locally uniformly, then RH holds; under RH the constant family qualifies. New in this book.
- [The shifted zeta is an explicit series of zeta at s plus k with a tangent factor](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#exact_expansion_of_the_shifted_zeta_in_zeta_at_integer_translates) (Volume II, Theorem 20.3.2, page 562; proved): For $0<\delta<2\pi$, $\pi I_\delta(s)=\Gamma(1-s)F_\delta(s)$ with $F_\delta(s)=\operatorname{Li}_{1-s}(e^{-\delta})-\Gamma(s)\delta^{-s}=\sum_{k\ge0}\zeta(1-s-k)(-\delta)^k/k!$, and $\zeta_\delta(s)=\sum_{k\ge0}(\delta/2\pi)^k\frac{(s)_k}{k!}\frac{\sin(\pi s/2)}{\sin(\pi(s+k)/2)}\zeta(s+k)=\zeta(s)+\frac\delta{2\pi}s\tan\frac{\pi s}2\zeta(s+1)-\cdots$. New in this book.
- [Obstructions: the shifted xi function has a pole at s equal 3, its zeros drift, and its reciprocal is not a GGC transform](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#shifted_family_has_poles_drifting_zeros_and_no_ggc_reciprocal) (Volume II, Proposition 20.3.3, page 562; proved): For $0<\delta<2\pi$, $\xi_\delta$ is meromorphic and not entire, with a pole at $s=3$ for every such $\delta$ and poles at $s=-1,-2,\dots$; a pole at $s=2m+1$ ($m\ge2$) occurs exactly when $F_\delta(2m+1)\ne0$ and fails for some $\delta$ (computed values $4.7215$ at $s=5$, $3.0416$ at $s=7$). The zeros move by a first order drift and, when $\xi_\delta(\frac12)\ne0$, $\xi_\delta(\frac12)/\xi_\delta(\frac12+\sqrt w)$ is not a GGC transform nor the Laplace transform of any positive measure. New in this book.
- [A signed L\'evy measure gives a Thorin density, which is nonnegative if and only if a logarithmic derivative inequality holds](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_density_from_a_signed_levy_measure_with_logarithmic_derivative_condition) (Volume II, Theorem 20.4.2, page 565; proved): If $f'/f(s)-f'/f(\alpha)=\int(e^{-\alpha x}-e^{-sx})M(dx)$ for a signed measure $M$, then $\log\frac{f(\alpha+w)}{f(\alpha)}-w\frac{f'}f(\alpha)=\int_0^\infty\log(1+w^2/y^2)\kappa_\alpha(y)\,dy$ with $\kappa_\alpha(y)=\frac1\pi[\operatorname{Re}\frac{f'}f(\alpha+iy)-\frac{f'}f(\alpha)]$, and if $\kappa_\alpha\ge0$ the compensated reciprocal is a GGC transform. New in this book.
- [Zeros on a vertical line give a Thorin density that is a sum of Lorentzians tending to point masses at the ordinates](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#zeros_on_one_vertical_line_give_lorentzian_thorin_densities_tending_to_point_masses) (Volume II, Corollary 20.4.3, page 565; proved): If $f'/f(s)=a+\sum_k(s-\rho_k)^{-1}$ with all $\rho_k=\beta_0+it_k$ on one line, $\{t_k\}$ symmetric, $0\notin\{t_k\}$, then at $\alpha=\beta_0+\varepsilon$, $\kappa_\alpha(y)=\frac1\pi\sum_k[\ell_\varepsilon(y-t_k)-\ell_\varepsilon(t_k)]$, and if $\sum t_k^{-2}<\infty$, $\kappa_\alpha(y)\,dy\to\sum_{t_k>0}\delta_{t_k}$ vaguely as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$. New in this book.
- [The tilted uniform law has a strictly positive Thorin density for every positive tilt, a Lorentzian smoothing of the lattice 2 pi m](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_density_of_the_tilted_uniform_law_is_positive_for_every_tilt) (Volume II, Theorem 20.4.4, page 566; proved): For every $\delta>0$, $\pi\kappa_\delta(y)=\frac{y^2}{\delta(\delta^2+y^2)}-\frac12\coth\frac\delta2\frac{1-\cos y}{\cosh\delta-\cos y}=\sum_{m\ge1}[\ell_\delta(y-2\pi m)+\ell_\delta(y+2\pi m)-2\ell_\delta(2\pi m)]>0$ for $y>0$, so the compensated tilted reciprocal of $\varphi_U(s)=(1-e^{-s})/s$ is a GGC transform, and as $\delta\downarrow0$ the Thorin measure tends to $\sum_{m\ge1}\delta_{2\pi m}$ vaguely. New in this book.
- [The shifted zeta equals (2 pi) to the s times the Mellin transform of the positive Thorin density of the tilted uniform law](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#shifted_zeta_is_the_mellin_transform_of_the_thorin_density_of_the_tilted_uniform_law) (Volume II, Theorem 20.4.5, page 567; proved): For $1<\operatorname{Re}s<3$ and every $\delta>0$, $\zeta_\delta(s)=(2\pi)^s\int_0^\infty y^{-s}\kappa_\delta(y)\,dy$, and at $\delta=0$ the right side is formally $\zeta(s)$; formally the identity of Comtet and Majumdar is the Mellin transform of the lattice Thorin measure $\sum_m\delta_{2\pi m}$ of the uniform law, divergent for $0<s<1$, and the shift smooths it into a positive density. New in this book.
- [Kink theorem: the Gauss damped Riemann kernel has finitely many real zeros and infinitely many nonreal zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#gauss_damped_theta_kernel_has_finitely_many_real_zeros_and_no_ggc_reciprocal) (Volume II, Theorem 20.5.1, page 570; proved): For every $\delta>0$, $\Xi_\delta(t)=2\int_0^\infty\Phi_\delta(u)\cos(ut)\,du$ with $\Phi_\delta=2\sum_ne^{-\pi n^2\delta}\Phi_n$ has finitely many real zeros and infinitely many nonreal zeros, because $\Phi_\delta'(0)>0$ gives $t^2\Xi_\delta(t)\to-2\Phi_\delta'(0)<0$; so $\Xi_\delta(0)/\Xi_\delta(i\sqrt w)$ is not a GGC transform. New in this book.
- [Modular constraints: a Laguerre P\'olya damped kernel must have vanishing odd derivatives of the damped kernel at the origin](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#modular_constraints_on_the_weights_for_a_laguerre_polya_damped_kernel) (Volume II, Corollary 20.5.2, page 571; proved): For real weights $w_n$ with $\sum_n|w_n|n^Ae^{-\pi n^2}<\infty$ for every $A\ge0$, if $\Xi_w\in\mathcal{LP}$ and $\Xi_w$ is not $e^{-at^2}$ times a polynomial, then $\sum_nw_n\Phi_n^{(2j+1)}(0)=0$ for every $j\ge0$. New in this book.

#### Key terms

chapters.title: Approximating clocks: Jensen, Euler product and boundary hitting times
chapters.summary:
RH holds if and only if some generalised gamma convolutions (GGC), the approximating clocks, converge weakly to the reciprocal Xi law $\mu$, whose Laplace transform is $1/G$ with $G(u)=\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u)/\xi(\frac12)$. This chapter tests the candidate approximations and asks of each whether it is built from data known without the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) and whether it can see an off line zero, in particular that of the Davenport Heilbronn function. It treats Jensen hitting times, laws built from the Taylor coefficients of $G$ (the probabilistic form of the Jensen and Pólya criterion), extreme value hitting times given by fractional order statistics and B splines, and prime side hitting times from truncated Euler products, with a Brownian truncated Euler product and a universal stable limit of index three halves. A Thorin rigidity theorem shows that any factorisation of $\mu$ into two GGC laws forces RH. The chapter states what the prime side limit would have to be, discusses diffusion approximations, and presents the curved boundary of Roberts and Shortland for the inverse first passage problem, the Brownian variable of Biane, Pitman and Yor, the probabilistic Riemann function of Marc Yor and coauthors, and the Davenport Heilbronn test, which every proposed argument must fail. A coefficient ladder shows that the Taylor coefficients of $F(s)=\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)/\xi(\frac12)$ form a Pólya frequency sequence exactly when RH holds, with an angle theorem and an unconditional count of rungs from the verified height. Each route ends in an equivalence with RH or in an open problem. Statements are proved unless marked computed or conditional on RH or the quasi Riemann hypothesis.

#### From the literature

- the Krein string and Kent's eigenfunction expansion of hitting times (Kent 1980; Krein)
- generalised gamma convolutions, Thorin measures and Dirichlet means (Bondesson 1992; James, Roynette and Yor 2008)
- the Brownian laws whose Mellin transform is $\xi$ (Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001) and the hyperbolic laws (Pitman and Yor 2003); the Barnes $G$ function (Nikeghbali and Yor 2009)
- Jensen polynomials of the $\xi$ function (Griffin, Ono, Rolen and Zagier 2019)
- the verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021)
- the inverse first passage problem (Anulova 1980; Roberts and Shortland 1995)
- diffusion approximations (Roberts, Gelman and Gilks 1997)
- the Davenport and Heilbronn function with zeros off the critical line (Davenport and Heilbronn 1936; Spira 1994)
- Schoenberg's characterisation of Pólya frequency sequences (Schoenberg 1951)

#### New results

Each route ends in an equivalence with RH whose unconditional part stops where classical knowledge stops; computed parts are marked as computed.

- [Jensen polynomial laws mu_d of the reciprocal xi function: convergence, existence if and only if RH, and existence up to degree 2e17](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#jensen_laws_of_the_reciprocal_xi_function_exist_iff_rh_and_for_degrees_up_to_2e17) (Volume II, Proposition 21.1.1, page 576; proved): $J_d\to G$ locally uniformly; if $J_d$ has only real zeros then $1/J_d$ is the transform of a GGC law $\mu_d$ (a pure birth chain passage time); RH iff $\mu_d$ exists for all $d$, and then $\mu_d\Rightarrow\mu$; $\mu_d$ exists for $d\le2\cdot10^{17}$ unconditionally (quoted); $\mu_d$ has mean $c_1$ and variance exceeding that of $\mu$ by $2c_2/d$. New in this book.
- [Density of a sum of independent exponentials as a Laplace transform of a B spline, the Dirichlet mean form](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#b_spline_and_dirichlet_mean_form_of_the_density_of_a_sum_of_exponentials) (Volume II, Proposition 21.2.1, page 580; proved): For $0<\lambda_1<\dots<\lambda_N$ the density of $\sum e_k/\lambda_k$ is $(\prod\lambda_k)\frac{y^{N-1}}{(N-1)!}\int M(x;\lambda)e^{-xy}\,dx$ with $M$ the Curry and Schoenberg B spline, the density of the Dirichlet mean $\sum W_k\lambda_k$. New in this book.
- [A sum of exponentials is a linear functional of the Gumbel extremal process](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#sum_of_exponentials_as_a_linear_functional_of_the_gumbel_extremal_process) (Volume II, Theorem 21.2.2, page 581; proved): For $0<\lambda_1\le\lambda_2\le\cdots$ with $\sum1/\lambda_k<\infty$ and $b_k=k/\lambda_k$, $\sum e_k/\lambda_k\overset d=\sum_kb_k(G_k-G_{k+1})$, rearranged to $b_1G_1+\sum_{k\ge2}(b_k-b_{k-1})G_k$ if $k\log k/\lambda_k\to0$; under RH $\mu$ is $\sum k\gamma_k^{-2}(G_k-G_{k+1})$. New in this book.
- [Truncated Euler products give GGC laws Y_P, and first passage to the mean level decomposes as Y_P plus the first passage to the log of N_P](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#truncated_euler_products_give_ggc_laws_and_first_passage_decomposition_at_the_mean_level) (Volume II, Proposition 21.3.1, page 584; proved): For every $\alpha>0$ and $P$, $e^{-B\sqrt{2u}}\zeta_P(\alpha)/\zeta_P(\alpha+\sqrt{2u})$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC law $Y_P$ with zero drift and an explicit nonnegative Thorin density, in particular unconditionally at $\alpha=\frac12$; and $T_{\mathbb E\log N_P}\overset d=Y_P+T_{\log N_P}$. New in this book.
- [One prime blocks, Möbius and Liouville factors and the Pólya Gamma law](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#one_prime_blocks_mobius_liouville_and_polya_gamma_laws) (Volume II, Remark 21.3.2, page 585; proved): For a single prime the Thorin density of the Euler factor sums in closed form, the Liouville factor gives a GGC with density nonnegative although its terms are not, and its limit as alpha decreases to zero is the Laplace transform of a Pólya Gamma law, while for alpha above one the full products give GGC laws and for alpha below one the continued functions are not Laplace transforms. New in this book.
- [Brownian truncated Euler product identity for xi centred at one half](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#brownian_truncated_euler_product_identity_centred_at_one_half) (Volume II, Theorem 21.3.3, page 586; proved): With no hypothesis on the zeros, the ratio of xi at one half and at one half plus s is for every truncation time U an exact product of a smoothed Euler product over the primes, an archimedean factor and a smoothed product over the zeros whose remainder has an explicit bound, with first passage densities as smoothing kernels. New in this book.
- [Numerical check of the Brownian truncated Euler product identity](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#brownian_truncated_euler_product_numerical_check) (Volume II, Table 21.4, page 588; computed): A floating point computation with primes up to $10^3$ or $10^6$ and the first 1700 zeros agrees with the Brownian truncated Euler product identity to better than $10^{-30}$ at six values of s and U, and the zero remainder stays below its bound; it checks the identity at these points only. New in this book.
- [The Euler hitting times converge after scaling to a spectrally positive stable law of index 3/2](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#universal_three_halves_stable_limit_of_the_euler_hitting_times) (Volume II, Theorem 21.3.4, page 589; proved): As $P\to\infty$, $Z_P=(Y_P-\kappa_2(P))/\kappa_3(P)^{2/3}\Rightarrow Z$ with $\log\mathbb Ee^{-sZ}=(2s)^{3/2}/6$, with the bound $|\log\mathbb Ee^{-sZ_P}-(2s)^{3/2}/6|\le\frac{|s|^2}6\rho_4(P)$ for $\operatorname{Re}s\ge0$ and $\rho_4(P)\to0$. New in this book.
- [Thorin rigidity: any factorisation of the reciprocal xi law into two GGC laws forces RH and splits the zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_rigidity_of_ggc_factorisations_of_the_reciprocal_xi_law) (Volume II, Theorem 21.4.1, page 590; proved): If $\mu=\mu_1*\mu_2$ with both factors GGC, then RH holds and the Thorin measures are $\sum a_\gamma\delta_{\gamma^2}$ and $\sum(m_\gamma-a_\gamma)\delta_{\gamma^2}$ with $0\le a_\gamma\le m_\gamma$; no GGC law with drift or a nonzero absolutely continuous Thorin part is a GGC factor with a GGC cofactor. New in this book.
- [Small time enclosure of the inverse first passage boundary of the reciprocal xi law, independent of RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#small_time_enclosure_of_the_boundary_of_the_reciprocal_xi_law_independent_of_rh) (Volume II, Proposition 21.7.1, page 593; proved): With $F(t)=\mu(0,t]$ and $m(t)=\inf_{s\le t}b(s)$, $\sqrt t\bar\Phi_N^{-1}(F(t))\le b(t)$ and $m(t)\le\sqrt t\bar\Phi_N^{-1}(\frac12F(t))$; $-\log F(t)\sim\log^2(1/t)/(16t)$, so $\liminf b/\log(1/t)\ge1/(2\sqrt2)\ge\limsup m/\log(1/t)$, and $b\sim\log(1/t)/(2\sqrt2)$ if $b$ is nonincreasing near $0$; no use of RH. New in this book.
- [Moving a pair of zeros off the line by delta multiplies the Laplace transform by 1+6 delta^2 s/gamma^4 to first order](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#first_order_response_of_the_laplace_transform_to_moving_a_zero_off_the_line) (Volume II, Proposition 21.7.2, page 596; proved): Moving the pair at height $\gamma$ off the line by $\delta$ multiplies the Laplace transform, relative to the control, by $1+6\delta^2s/\gamma^4+O(\delta^2s^2/\gamma^6)$ for $|s|\ll\gamma^2$, which to first order shifts the mean by $-6\delta^2/\gamma^4$. New in this book.

chapters.title: The quasi Riemann hypothesis and the Thorin programme
chapters.summary:
What are the zero free half planes announced in October 2026, who claims them with what status, how far could their arguments be followed here, and what would such a half plane do for the Thorin programme? The chapter records the claims: $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ and $\frac{11}{12}$ for every Dirichlet $L$ function, zeta included, and for Hecke $L$ functions over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$ (OpenAI 2026, with a Lean formalisation of the $\frac78$ statement by its authors), and the constant $0.874957\ldots$ of Liu, with later lower constants. All are unrefereed preprints, so every statement using them is conditional on the hypothesis named $(\mathrm Q_\theta)$, that no Dirichlet $L$ function has a zero with real part above $\theta$. It sets out the structure of the argument as far as read: a continuation criterion turning a power saving for smoothed Möbius sums into a half plane (whose short proof is checked), Poisson summation in a sextic twist, Kubota's cubic theta function and a large sieve type recursion, with an exponent bookkeeping that bounds one step at $\frac67$. Under $(\mathrm Q_\theta)$ the Thorin measure of reciprocal xi is positive and has its minimum at the origin at every level above $\theta$, the shifted clock being a generalised gamma convolution. The sine squared lemma adds nothing to the half plane because the canonical measure is signed. The descent in level from $\theta$ to $\frac12$ is analysed in four readings, none a reduction, and five open problems are posed. The chapter concludes that the announcement gives no path to the Riemann Hypothesis.

#### From the literature

- Zero free half planes $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ and $\frac{11}{12}$ (OpenAI 2026, unrefereed) and an absolute lower bound for $1-\beta$ at real zeros of real Dirichlet $L$ functions of conductor $q$, in the form $(1-\beta)\log q\ge c$ (OpenAI 2026)
- Improved constants near $0.875$ and a further lowering (Liu 2026; Xu and Sang 2026), unrefereed
- Littlewood's equivalence between bounds for the Mertens function and zero free half planes, in a smoothed form
- Kubota's cubic theta function and Poisson summation in twists
- The Thorin programme for reciprocal xi (Polson 2026), the Biane, Pitman and Yor laws, and the verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021)
- A report of the reception in the press (Quanta Magazine, 19 October 2026)

#### New results

Everything that uses a half plane is conditional on $(\mathrm Q_\theta)$; the arithmetic checks of the quoted constants and the computed condition numbers are floating point or exact rational computations, not ball arithmetic.

chapters.title: Conditional certificates under a quasi Riemann hypothesis at 7/8
chapters.summary:
What follows for the Thorin programme if $\zeta(s)\ne0$ for $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$? This chapter takes as hypothesis ($\mathrm Q_{7/8}$) the half plane announced in October 2026 (OpenAI, unrefereed, with a companion manuscript for $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac{11}{12}$), so every result is conditional unless it says otherwise. Under ($\mathrm Q_{7/8}$): for every basepoint $\alpha\ge\frac78$ the reciprocal $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt s)$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) with absolutely continuous Thorin density, the clock is strictly increasing and $\operatorname{Re}\xi'/\xi>0$ on $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ (the one sided bound of Lagarias type for $\zeta'/\zeta$), the even and odd parts have only imaginary zeros, the de Bruijn Newman constant satisfies $\Lambda\le\frac9{32}$ by de Bruijn's theorem alone, the poles of the reciprocal lie in a thinner parabolic region, the Mertens function is $O(x^{7/8+\varepsilon})$, and density estimates sharpen. Unconditional parts are a window count lemma and a signal proposition. The chapter proves a counting form and a general theorem: if $\zeta$ has no zero with $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha_0$ then the compensated clock derivative $D_\alpha(r)>0$ for all $\alpha>\alpha_0$, with a computer assisted constant check using ball arithmetic for the first 1700 zeros, and a corollary that a quasi Riemann hypothesis at $\alpha_0$ is equivalent to positivity of the compensated Thorin densities on every line to the right of $\alpha_0$. The basepoints at which the compensated reciprocal is a GGC form a closed half line. Floating point scans of $D_\alpha$ are computed. The strip $\frac12<\alpha<\frac78$ remains open, and Bondesson's closure would need a sequence of basepoints tending to $\frac12$.

#### From the literature

- de Bruijn's strip theorem and the bound $\Lambda\le2\Delta^2$ (de Bruijn 1950)
- Bondesson's closure properties of generalised gamma convolutions (Bondesson 1992)
- the Mertens function under zero free half planes (Titchmarsh 1986)
- verification of RH to $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021)
- Zero free half plane claims, unrefereed (OpenAI 2026)

#### New results

All results here are conditional on ($\mathrm Q_{7/8}$) or a general quasi Riemann hypothesis unless stated.

- [Under (Q_{7/8}) the poles of 1/xi(1/2+sqrt w) lie in a parabola with vertex at most 9/64, and the sliver of the local theorem becomes thinner](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#poles_of_the_reciprocal_of_xi_lie_in_a_thinner_parabola_under_q_7_8) (Volume II, Proposition 23.1.2, page 629; conditional on The quasi Riemann hypothesis $(\mathrm Q_{7/8})$ of the book, which rests on the unrefereed half plane of OpenAI (2026)): Under $(\mathrm Q_{7/8})$ every pole $(\rho-\frac12)^2$ of $1/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt w)$ has $(\operatorname{Im}w)^2\le\frac9{16}(\frac9{64}-\operatorname{Re}w)$, a parabola with vertex at most $\frac9{64}$ against $\frac14$ with no hypothesis, and the sliver in Theorem bs:thm:local can be replaced by a set of half width about $\frac34X$ instead of $X$ at abscissa $-X^2$. - [Gaussian smoothed Möbius sum: explicit formula over the zeros, with RH and the quasi Riemann hypothesis as growth exponents, and the trivial zero term as a finite range leading term only](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#gaussian_smoothed_mobius_sum_explicit_formula_and_growth_equivalent_to_sigma_max) (Volume II, Proposition 23.1.3, page 631; proved): For the Gaussian smoothed Möbius sum $M_{\rm g}(x)$ the explicit formula over zeros and trivial zeros holds with a divergent trivial zero series, $\sup\operatorname{Re}\rho\le\sigma$ if and only if $M_{\rm g}(x)=O(x^{\sigma-2/3+\varepsilon})$, and the leading trivial zero term $c_1x^{-8/3}$ dominates $M_{\rm g}$ on a finite range of $x$ only; nothing in it depends on the quasi Riemann hypothesis. - [Under (Q_{7/8}), M(x) is O(x^{7/8+epsilon}), the Möbius series converges to 1/zeta on Re s above 7/8, and the Möbius series of 1/zeta(1/2+sqrt s) converges on the parabola region H_{3/8}](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#mertens_function_is_o_of_x_to_7_8_plus_epsilon_and_mobius_series_converges_on_re_s_above_7_8_under_q_7_8) (Volume II, Proposition 23.1.4, page 632; conditional on The quasi Riemann hypothesis $(\mathrm Q_{7/8})$ of the book, which rests on the unrefereed half plane of OpenAI (2026)): Under $(\mathrm Q_{7/8})$, $M(x)=\sum_{n\le x}\mu(n)=O(x^{7/8+\varepsilon})$ and $\sum\mu(n)n^{-s}=1/\zeta(s)$ on $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$, so the Möbius series of $1/\zeta(\frac12+\sqrt s)$ converges on $H_{3/8}$, which contains the region $H_{1/2}$ of absolute convergence; the proof is Titchmarsh's argument for RH with $\frac78$ in place of $\frac12$. - [Compensated clock positivity on every line to the right of alpha zero under a zero free half plane, by pairing each zero with its mirror image](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#compensated_clock_positivity_on_every_line_under_a_zero_free_half_plane_by_pairing_zeros) (Volume II, Theorem 23.1.8, page 634; conditional on $\zeta(s)\ne0$ for $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha_0$, a fixed $\alpha_0$ with $\frac12\le\alpha_0<1$ (RH when $\alpha_0=\frac12$)): If $\zeta$ has no zero with real part greater than $\alpha_0$, then $D_\alpha(r)=\operatorname{Re}\xi'/\xi(\alpha+ir)-\xi'/\xi(\alpha)$ is positive for every $\alpha>\alpha_0$ and every real $r\ne0$, proved by pairing each zero with its mirror image under $\rho\mapsto1-\bar\rho$, so that the position of a zero near the boundary does not matter. New in this book.
- [One block for each zero, the Hadamard blocks of the compensated reciprocal of xi](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#one_block_for_each_zero_compensated_reciprocal_of_xi) (Volume II, Remark 23.1.9, page 635; proved): Under the quasi Riemann hypothesis every zero pair contributes an explicit factor whose Thorin density is a recentred pair of Cauchy bumps, no single factor is a GGC, and the blocks sum to the Thorin density of the compensated reciprocal. chapters.title: What would close the gap: open problems of the computational programme
chapters.summary:
This closing chapter of Volume II sorts the open problems of the computational chapters by what they would accomplish, so that a reader looking for the next step can see which bear on the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) itself and which would sharpen a computation. The sorting follows the path of Volume I: the descent in level of the Thorin density from the basepoint one to the critical line, and the three constraints on any proof (a proof cannot be finite, must use the Euler product, and must not rest on a property that survives a Gaussian tilt). Four groups are distinguished. Problems on the descent itself concern what a proof by deconvolution would still need, whether the backward Cauchy flow is a path at all, the explicit formula read as a deconvolution including a rigorous matrix pencil, the Balazard, Saias and Yor criterion at every level, and where a uniform step of the Thorin phase diagram could come from, the de Bruijn Newman flow being the only known source of an analytic tail below the basepoint one. Problems on windows of the explicit formula concern Weil positivity certified in compact windows to finite support lengths. Problems on approximants concern truncations, friable approximants, extreme value approximants and approximating clocks, which agree with Xi to high accuracy and can have zeros off the line. Problems on cost and certification concern evaluating the level one density in time polynomial in the logarithm of the height and the number of digits, a posteriori bounds for the accelerated flow, and a calibrated Bayesian inversion. The chapter states no new theorem and proves nothing about RH; results using the announced zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ of October 2026 (not refereed) are conditional.

#### From the literature

None.

#### New results

None. The chapter is a classification of open problems stated in earlier chapters.
No new results of this chapter are catalogued.
