chapters.title: The Pólya evaluators
chapters.summary:
This appendix describes the two evaluators of $\xi$ and $\xi'$ built on the Pólya kernel $\Phi$ of the Riemann Xi function, and states exactly what their error balls do and do not bound. The question it answers is how the numbers of the book, the Thorin density $\rho_\varepsilon$, counts of zeros on the critical line, the Laplace transform of the clock and the Keiper Li coefficients, are computed, and which errors a ball arithmetic enclosure leaves outside the stated radius. The untilted evaluator computes node values $\Phi(jh)$ from the theta series and forms trapezoid approximations to $\xi(\frac12+s)$ and $\xi'(\frac12+s)$ through two polynomials in $e^{sh}$; its defaults are 240 bits, step $1/200$ and $|u|\le3$, and most runs use 420 bits. The tilted evaluator integrates along a line shifted into the strip of analyticity of $\Phi$, which keeps the cost manageable at large height, and the appendix lists the shift, precision, step and cut used for the Lehmer pair and its de Bruijn Newman flow, for the count of zeros at height 1000 and for the clock transform. The radii of the returned balls bound only the rounding errors of the finite sums. Three errors lie outside them: the discretisation error of the trapezoid rule (bounded in the main text), the cut of the axis, and the truncation of the theta series, whose stopping test does not add the tail to the radius and, because it compares double precision numbers, never triggers at working precision of 1055 bits or more. The untilted route needs more than 1054 bits for thirty digits above height about 840, so there the stopping test has to be made in ball arithmetic. The runs reported in the book use at most 600 bits and are not affected. Results computed with these evaluators are computed, and certified only where the three outside errors are bounded separately.

#### From the literature

- Ball arithmetic as the basis of rigorous numerical enclosures, and arbitrary precision reference values in floating point, as cited by the appendix
- The theta series and the Pólya kernel representation of $\Xi$ (Pólya; Titchmarsh)

#### New results

None are claimed beyond the error accounting.

No new results of this appendix are catalogued.

chapters.title: Notation
chapters.summary:
This appendix is the notation reference of the book. Seven tables list the symbols used in more than one section, with their meaning and the place where each is defined. The first five cover the whole book and record the second meanings that some letters carry in particular chapters (for example $\eta$ is a tilted height, Dedekind's eta function or Dirichlet's eta function); the last two give the separate notation of the sections on Bosch's theorem and of the numerical checks behind it. Conventions: the clock is a function of $u=s^2$; its Thorin measures live in a variable $z$, in which the atoms of $U_{\mathrm{RH}}=\sum_{\gamma>0}\delta_{\gamma^2}$ sit at the squared ordinates $\gamma^2$, and the chart $\theta=\sqrt z$ puts them back at the ordinates; a resolution $\varepsilon>0$ means the basepoint $\alpha=\frac12+\varepsilon$; a zero is $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$, and sums and products over $k$ run over the pairs $\{\rho,1-\rho\}$. The symbols include the completed zeta function $\xi$ and $\Xi$, the Pólya kernel, the Thorin measure of a generalised gamma convolution, the heat trace and the canonical function of an infinitely divisible law.

results.name: Rigidity of the clock, a GGC if and only if RH
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: The clock, the reciprocal of the normalised completed zeta function in the variable $u=s^2$, is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution exactly when the Riemann Hypothesis holds, and then its Thorin measure is the sum of unit atoms at the squared ordinates of the zeros.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12 s(s - 1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be the completed zeta function, an entire function whose zeros are the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$, and put $G(u)=\xi(\frac12+\sqrt{u})/\xi(\frac12)$, an entire function of $u$. The clock is the function $1/G$. A random variable $H\ge 0$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if $\mathbb{E}\,e^{-uH}=\exp\{-du-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+u/z)\,U(dz)\}$ for $u>0$, with a drift $d\ge 0$ and a positive measure $U$ on $(0,\infty)$, the Thorin measure, such that $\int_{(0,1)}|\log z|\,U(dz)+\int_{(1,\infty)}z^{-1}U(dz)<\infty$; the drift and the Thorin measure are unique. Then $1/G$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC if and only if the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) holds, that is, if and only if every zero of $\xi$ has real part $\frac12$. In that case the drift is zero, the Thorin measure is $U_{\mathrm{RH}}=\sum_{\gamma>0}\delta_{\gamma^2}$, where $\frac12+i\gamma$ runs over the zeros of $\xi$ with $\gamma>0$, counted with multiplicity, and the clock variable is $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential random variables $e_\gamma$.
results.label: prop:rigid

results.name: Shifted clock is a GGC to the right of every zero
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: To the right of every zero of the completed zeta function, in particular at every basepoint $\alpha\ge 1$, the shifted clock is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution with an explicit positive Thorin density, and it is one exactly when $\alpha$ is at least the supremum of the real parts of the zeros.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed zeta function, and for real $\alpha$ and real $r$ put $v_\alpha(r)=\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\alpha+ir)$. If $\alpha>\operatorname{Re}\rho$ for every zero $\rho$ of $\xi$, in particular for every $\alpha\ge 1$, then $u\mapsto\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt{u})$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution $T_\alpha$ (a random variable $H\ge 0$ with $\mathbb{E}\,e^{-uH}=\exp\{-du-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+u/z)\,U(dz)\}$ for $u>0$, a drift $d\ge 0$ and a positive Thorin measure $U$) whose Thorin measure has density $v_\alpha(\sqrt{z})/(2\pi\sqrt{z})$ with respect to $dz$ on $(0,\infty)$, and $v_\alpha>0$. The function $u\mapsto\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt{u})$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution if and only if $\alpha\ge\sup_\rho\operatorname{Re}\rho$.
results.label: thm:poisson

results.name: Positivity of the Thorin density on one line, open question
results.summary: It is not known, without assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, whether nonnegativity of the real part of the logarithmic derivative of the completed zeta function on a single vertical line excludes zeros to the right of that line.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed zeta function and, for real $\alpha>\frac12$ and real $r$, put $v_\alpha(r)=\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\alpha+ir)$, so that $v_\alpha(r)/\pi$ is the Thorin density at resolution $\alpha - \frac12$. If some zero of $\xi$ has real part greater than $\alpha$, the shifted clock $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt{u})$ is not the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution. The question is whether, without assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, $v_\alpha(r)\ge 0$ for all real $r$ implies that $\xi$ has no zero with real part greater than $\alpha$. The book states that this is not known for $\xi$. What is known is that if $v_\alpha\ge 0$ for every $\alpha>\sigma_0$ then no zero has real part greater than $\sigma_0$ (for $\sigma_0=\frac12$ this is Lagarias's criterion for RH), and that for an explicit entire function with the order, symmetry and reality of $\xi$ the answer is negative.
results.label: rem:ch2:oneline

results.name: The clock is not a Brownian first passage time to an independent random level
results.summary: The clock variable of the Riemann xi function is not, for any constant drift and any independent random level, the first passage time of Brownian motion with that drift to that level, and the proof uses no hypothesis on the zeros.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\tfrac12 s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be Riemann's completed zeta function, and let $T$ be the clock variable, the nonnegative random variable whose Laplace transform is $\mathbb{E}e^{-uT}=\xi(\tfrac12)/\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt{u})$ for $u\ge0$ (it exists with no hypothesis on the zeros of $\xi$). For a drift $c\ge0$ and a level $a>0$, the first passage time of standard Brownian motion with drift $c$ (unit variance per unit time) to the level $a$ has the inverse Gaussian law, with Laplace transform $\exp\{a(c-\sqrt{c^2+2u})\}$. Then for no drift $c\ge0$ and no probability law $F$ on $(0,\infty)$ is $T$ equal in law to the first passage time of Brownian motion with drift $c$ to an independent random level $A$ with law $F$. For a drift $c<0$ the first passage time is infinite with probability $1-\mathbb{E}e^{2cA}>0$, so equality is impossible as well.
results.label: prop:nogo

results.name: Maślanka coefficients as Laguerre moments of Williams' variable
results.summary: The coefficients of Maślanka's series for (sigma minus 1) zeta(sigma) are Laguerre moments of Williams' variable, with an explicit generating function and an integral formula, with no zeros and no primes, for (sigma minus 1) zeta(sigma) on the strip from zero to two.
results.statement: Let $W=\pi^2S_2/2=\sum_{n\ge1}\Gamma_n/n^2$ with independent Gamma(2) variables $\Gamma_n$ of unit scale, so that $\mathbb{E}e^{-\lambda W}=(\pi\sqrt\lambda/\sinh\pi\sqrt\lambda)^2$, and let $L^{(1)}_k$ be the generalized Laguerre polynomials. Let $A_k=\sum_{j=0}^k(-1)^j\binom kj(2j+1)\zeta(2j+2)$, the coefficients in Maślanka's expansion $(\sigma-1)\zeta(\sigma)=\sum_{k\ge0}A_k(1-\frac\sigma2)_k/k!$. Then (i) $A_k=\mathbb{E}[WL^{(1)}_k(W)]/(2(k+1))$; (ii) $\sum_{k\ge0}A_ky^k=(1-\mathbb{E}e^{-Wy/(1-y)})/(2y)$ for $0<|y|<1$; (iii) for $0<\operatorname{Re}\sigma<2$, $(\sigma-1)\zeta(\sigma)=\frac{\sin(\pi\sigma/2)}{2\pi}\int_0^\infty r^{-\sigma/2-1}(1-\mathbb{E}e^{-rW})dr$, and for real $0<\sigma<2$ this equals $\mathbb{E}[(1-\mathbb{E}[e^{-WR}\mid\mathcal B])/(2(1-\mathcal B))]$ with $\mathcal B$ a beta variable of parameters $\frac\sigma2$ and $1-\frac\sigma2$ independent of $W$ and $R=(1-\mathcal B)/\mathcal B$, so that expanding (ii) at $y=1-\mathcal B$ gives Maślanka's series, whose rigorous proof is due to Báez-Duarte (2010). The coefficients determine the law of $W$ but transfer no positivity to the Thorin measure of the clock. Credited to a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book.
results.label: prop:ch19:maslanka

results.name: The variable Z sqrt(2T) of the van Dantzig pair is self decomposable with no hypothesis, with an explicit canonical function
results.summary: With no hypothesis, $Z\sqrt{2T}$ (standard normal $Z$ independent of the clock $T$) is self decomposable, with canonical function $k(r)=\sum_je^{-r\sqrt{a_j}}$ obtained by subordinating the Lévy measure of $T$ to the heat kernel; it is an extended generalised gamma convolution exactly when RH holds.
results.statement: Let $T$ be the clock, with Lévy measure $W(v)\,dv/v$, $W(v)=\sum_je^{-a_jv}$, $a_j=-(\rho_j-\frac12)^2$, let $Z$ be a standard normal variable independent of $T$, so that $\mathbb{E}e^{i\theta Z\sqrt{2T}}=\mathbb{E}e^{-\theta^2T}$. With no hypothesis $Z\sqrt{2T}$ is self decomposable: subordinating the Lévy measure of $T$ to the heat kernel gives the Lévy density $k(|x|)/|x|$ with $k(r)=\int_0^\infty e^{-1/4v}(4\pi v)^{-1/2}W(r^2v)\,dv/v=\sum_je^{-r\sqrt{a_j}}$ (the first passage identity for each term, with the principal root), and $k$ decreases because $W$ does. Since the characteristic function determines the law of $T$, $Z\sqrt{2T}$ is an extended generalised gamma convolution if and only if $T$ is a GGC, that is if and only if RH holds.
results.label: tx3:res:sdz

results.name: Möbius series for the density of the clock with no hypothesis, with terms g_n a convolution of one fixed function with a first passage kernel
results.summary: With no hypothesis the density $f$ of the clock equals $\sum_n\mu(n)n^{-1/2}g_n(t)$, $g_n=g_1*q_{\log n}$, an absolutely convergent series (faster than any power of $n$) whose terms are bounded through an erfc factor; $g_1$ grows like $2\xi(\frac12)e^{t/4}$, so for large $t$ the series rests on the prime number theorem, and for small $t$ it converges very fast.
results.statement: Write $\xi=\eta\zeta$ with $\eta(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)$ and $\phi_\eta(u)=\xi(\frac12)/\eta(\frac12+\sqrt u)$. Let $c>\frac14$, $g_1$ the inverse Laplace transform of $\phi_\eta$ along $\operatorname{Re}u=c$, $q_\lambda(x)=\frac{\lambda}{2\sqrt\pi}x^{-3/2}e^{-\lambda^2/4x}$ for $x>0$, both extended by $0$ to $x\le0$. Then for every $t>0$, $f(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{\mu(n)}{\sqrt n}g_n(t)$ with $g_n=g_1*q_{\log n}$ and $|g_n(t)|\le\sup_{0<x\le t}|g_1(x)|\operatorname{erfc}\big(\frac{\log n}{2\sqrt t}\big)$, so the series converges absolutely, faster than any power of $n$. Moreover $g_1(t)=2\xi(\frac12)e^{t/4}+O(e^{\varepsilon t})$ as $t\to\infty$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, so $g_1$ is not a density and for large $t$ the series rests on $\sum_n\mu(n)/n=0$. Numerically (Talbot inversion at 30 digits) the terms with $n\le5$ reproduce $f$ to at least $20$ digits at $t=0.008,\dots,0.04$.
results.label: tx3:prop:mobius

results.name: Lower tail of the clock: P(T at most y) is at most exp of minus (log 1/y) squared over 16 y, so the density vanishes to infinite order at the origin
results.summary: With no hypothesis $P(T\le y)\le\exp\{-(1+o(1))(\log\frac1y)^2/16y\}$ as $y\downarrow0$, by Chernoff's bound with $\log G(u)\sim\frac{\sqrt u}4\log u$ optimised at $\sqrt u\approx\log(1/y)/4y$; so the density vanishes to infinite order at the origin.
results.statement: Let $T$ be the clock, $\mathbb{E}e^{-uT}=1/G(u)$, $G(u)=\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u)/\xi(\frac12)$. With no hypothesis, $P(T\le y)\le\exp\{-(1+o(1))(\log\frac1y)^2/16y\}$ as $y\downarrow0$, so the density of $T$ vanishes to infinite order at the origin. The proof is Chernoff's bound $P(T\le y)\le e^{uy}/G(u)$, with $\log G(u)\sim\frac{\sqrt u}4\log u$ by Stirling's formula for $\xi$, optimised at $\sqrt u\approx\log(1/y)/4y$. The saddlepoint exponent has the same leading term but converges slowly: at $y=0.006$ it gives $-272$ against $-33.0$ for the exact $\log f$.
results.label: tx3:res:lowertail

results.name: RH holds if and only if the density of the clock is a Pólya frequency function of infinite order
results.summary: RH is equivalent to the density $f$ of the clock being a Pólya frequency function of infinite order, the one sided form of the two sided criterion: under RH $f$ is the density of $\sum_\gamma e_\gamma/\gamma^2$, and conversely Schoenberg's theorem forces $G$ to have only real zeros.
results.statement: RH holds if and only if the density $f$ of the clock $T$ is a Pólya frequency function of infinite order, that is $\det[f(x_i-y_j)]_{i,j\le r}\ge0$ for every $r$ and all $x_1<\cdots<x_r$, $y_1<\cdots<y_r$. Under RH $f$ is the density of $\sum_\gamma e_\gamma/\gamma^2$, exponential densities are Pólya frequency functions, and the class is closed under convolution and weak limits. Conversely, by Schoenberg's theorem the bilateral Laplace transform of an integrable Pólya frequency function of infinite order is $1/\Psi$ with $\Psi(u)=Ce^{-cu^2+bu}\prod_k(1+\lambda_ku)e^{-\lambda_ku}$, $\lambda_k$ real; here the transform is $1/G$, so $G(u)=\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u)/\xi(\frac12)$ has only real zeros $u=-a_k$, which forces $\rho-\frac12$ real or purely imaginary, and $\xi$ has no real zeros, so every $\rho$ is on the critical line. The book adds, as necessary conditions tested in floating point and not proved, $(\log f)''<0$ on $91$ points of $[0.006,0.08]$ with maximum $-0.026$.
results.label: tx2:prop:pf

results.name: The density of the reciprocal xi law is the limit of grouped residue sums, with no hypothesis on the zeros
results.summary: There are radii $R_n\in[n,2n]$ with $f(y)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\sum_{|u_\rho|<R_n}\operatorname{Res}_{u=u_\rho}e^{uy}/G(u)$ for every $y>0$, with an explicit error bound, whatever the zeros.
results.statement: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. There are radii $R_n\to\infty$ with $R_n\in[n,2n]$ such that for every $y>0$, $f(y)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\sum_{|u_\rho|<R_n}\operatorname{Res}_{u=u_\rho}e^{uy}/G(u)$, with no hypothesis on the zeros. A simple zero contributes $e^{u_\rho y}/G'(u_\rho)$, a zero of multiplicity $m$ contributes $e^{u_\rho y}P_\rho(y)$ with $P_\rho$ a polynomial of degree $m-1$, and a pair of zeros $\frac12\pm\delta+i\gamma$ off the line contributes $2\operatorname{Re}(e^{u_\rho y}/G'(u_\rho))$. For $y$ in a compact subset of $(0,\infty)$ the error after the $n$th group is at most $R_n\exp(-\frac12R_ny+C\sqrt{R_n}\log R_n)+\exp(-c\sqrt{R_n}\log R_n)$ for constants $c,C>0$.
results.label: ht:thm:grouped

results.name: Residue expansion: absolute convergence of the density series given a lower bound for the derivative of xi at the zeros
results.status_text: conditional on the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are simple and $|\xi'(\rho)|\ge e^{-C|\gamma|}$ for some constant $C$ and all zeros
results.conditions: the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are simple and $|\xi'(\rho)|\ge e^{-C|\gamma|}$ for some constant $C$ and all zeros
results.summary: If the zeros of $\zeta$ are simple and $|\xi'(\rho)|\ge e^{-C|\gamma|}$ for all zeros, the residue series for $f$ converges absolutely and locally uniformly, and under RH equals $\sum_{\gamma>0}w_\gamma e^{-\gamma^2y}$.
results.statement: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. Assume that the zeros of $\zeta$ are simple and that $|\xi'(\rho)|\ge e^{-C|\gamma|}$ for some constant $C$ and all zeros (a hypothesis not known to hold). Then $f(y)=\sum_{\gamma>0}e^{u_\rho y}/G'(u_\rho)$, $y>0$, converges absolutely and locally uniformly. Under RH it reads $f(y)=\sum_{\gamma>0}w_\gamma e^{-\gamma^2y}$ with $w_\gamma=\gamma^2\prod_{\gamma'\ne\gamma}(1-\gamma^2/\gamma'^2)^{-1}$.
results.label: ht:thm:res

results.name: Upper tail of the density of the reciprocal xi law: two exponential terms and an explicit remainder
results.summary: With no hypothesis, $f(y)=w_1e^{-\gamma_1^2y}+w_2e^{-\gamma_2^2y}+O(e^{-c_3y})$ as $y\to\infty$, with $c_3=\frac12(\gamma_2^2+\gamma_3^2)$ and the same bound for each derivative.
results.statement: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. Let $c_3=\frac12(\gamma_2^2+\gamma_3^2)$. With no hypothesis, $f(y)=w_1e^{-\gamma_1^2y}+w_2e^{-\gamma_2^2y}+O(e^{-c_3y})$ as $y\to\infty$, with the same bound for each derivative, where $w_1=1.01635\times10^4>0$ and $w_2=-1.17754\times10^6<0$.
results.label: ht:prop:tail

results.name: Kent's eigenfunction expansion is the residue expansion under RH with simple zeros
results.summary: Under RH with simple zeros the residue series is Kent's expansion with $\lambda_n=\gamma_n^2$ and $f$ is the density of the hitting time of a Krein string with Dirichlet spectrum $\{\gamma_n^2\}$; without these hypotheses the grouped expansion only continues Kent's formula to complex eigenvalues.
results.statement: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. If RH holds and the zeros are simple, the residue series $\sum_{\gamma>0}e^{u_\rho y}/G'(u_\rho)$ is Kent's expansion with $\lambda_n=\gamma_n^2$, and $f$ is the density of the hitting time of a Krein string with Dirichlet spectrum $\{\gamma_n^2\}$. Without these hypotheses the grouped expansion is the formal continuation of Kent's formula to complex eigenvalues: an off line pair contributes $2\operatorname{Re}(e^{u_\rho y}/G'(u_\rho))$, a multiple zero contributes a polynomial times an exponential, and no string has such a spectrum.
results.label: ht:prop:kent

results.name: The function xi(1/2+it) is not in Krein's class and the partial fraction series of 1/G diverges under RH
results.summary: $\xi(\frac12+it)$ is not in Krein's class, with or without RH, and under RH the partial fraction series of $1/G$ over the points $-\gamma_n^2$ does not converge absolutely.
results.statement: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. The function $\xi(\frac12+it)$ does not belong to Krein's class, whether or not RH holds. Moreover, under RH the partial fraction series of $1/G$ over the points $u_\rho=-\gamma_n^2$ does not converge absolutely.
results.label: ht:prop:krein

results.name: RH holds if and only if the reciprocal xi law is a weak limit of GGC laws
results.summary: RH holds if and only if there are GGC laws, for instance hitting times of strings, converging weakly to $\mu$.
results.statement: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. RH holds if and only if there are GGC laws, for instance hitting times of strings, converging weakly to $\mu$.
results.label: ht:prop:red

results.name: Truncations of the Hadamard product: GGC if and only if the first N zeros lie on the line, and GGC up to the verified height
results.summary: The law $\mu_N$ with transform $1/G_N$ (first $N$ zeros) is a GGC iff the first $N$ zeros are on the line, hence for every $N$ up to the zeros below $3\cdot10^{12}$; RH holds iff every $\mu_N$ is a GGC; under RH $0\le\log G-\log G_N\le u\tau_1(N)$ on $u\ge0$.
results.statement: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. Order the zeros in the upper half plane by height, let $G_N(u)=\prod_{n\le N}(1-u/u_{\rho_n})$, $\varphi_N=1/G_N$, $\varphi=1/G$, and let $\mu_N$ be the law with Laplace transform $\varphi_N$. (i) $\varphi_N\to\varphi$ pointwise on $[0,\infty)$, and for each fixed zero $1/G_N'(u_\rho)\to1/G'(u_\rho)$, with correction factor $\prod_{n>N}(1-u_\rho/u_{\rho_n})^{-1}\approx\exp(u_\rho\sum_{n>N}u_{\rho_n}^{-1})$, which under RH equals $\exp(\gamma^2\sum_{n>N}\gamma_n^{-2})>1$. (ii) $\mu_N$ is a GGC if and only if the first $N$ zeros lie on the line; in particular it is a GGC, unconditionally, for every $N\le N_0(H)$, the number of zeros below the verified height $H=3\cdot10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian). (iii) RH holds if and only if every $\mu_N$ is a GGC, and then $\mu$ is a GGC by Bondesson's continuity theorem. (iv) Under RH, for $u\ge0$, $0\le\log G(u)-\log G_N(u)\le u\,\tau_1(N)$ with $\tau_1(N)=\sum_{n>N}\gamma_n^{-2}\approx(\log(T_N/2\pi)+1)/(2\pi T_N)$, where $T_N$ is the height of the $N$th zero.
results.label: ht:prop:trunc

results.name: The density of the reciprocal xi law is strictly log concave on a half line, with no hypothesis
results.summary: There is $Y$ such that $f$ is strictly log concave on $[Y,\infty)$, with no hypothesis on the zeros.
results.statement: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. There is $Y$ such that $f$ is strictly log concave on $[Y,\infty)$, with no hypothesis.
results.label: ht:thm:lctail

results.name: Log concavity of the reciprocal xi density near the origin, given the saddle point approximation
results.status_text: conditional on the saddle point approximation of $\log f(y)$ holds as $y\to0$ together with two derivatives
results.conditions: the saddle point approximation of $\log f(y)$ holds as $y\to0$ together with two derivatives
results.summary: If the saddle point approximation of $\log f(y)$ holds as $y\to0$ together with two derivatives, then $f$ is strictly log concave on $(0,y_0]$ for some $y_0>0$.
results.statement: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. Let $\psi=\log G$, $\Lambda_f(y)=\sup_{u>0}(\psi(u)-uy)$ and $u_y$ the solution of $\psi'(u_y)=y$. Suppose the saddle point approximation $\log f(y)\approx-\Lambda_f(y)-\frac12\log(2\pi|\psi''(u_y)|)$ holds as $y\to0$ together with two derivatives (this is assumed, not proved). Then $f$ is strictly log concave on $(0,y_0]$ for some $y_0>0$.
results.label: ht:prop:lc0

results.name: The density of the reciprocal xi law is the sum of its first 120 residue terms up to an explicit exponentially small error
results.summary: For every $y>0$ and $j\ge0$, $|f^{(j)}(y)-\sum_{n\le120}w_n(-\gamma_n^2)^je^{-\gamma_n^2y}|\le M_je^{-cy}$ with $M_j=\frac1{2\pi}\int|{-c}+it|^j/|G(-c+it)|\,\mathrm dt$, and numerically $\log M_0=206.26$.
results.statement: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. With no hypothesis, for every $y>0$ and $j\ge0$, $|f^{(j)}(y)-\sum_{n\le120}w_n(-\gamma_n^2)^je^{-\gamma_n^2y}|\le M_je^{-cy}$, where $c$ is the constant of the book's contour shift beyond the 120th zero, $w_n$ and $\gamma_n$ are the weights and ordinates of the first $120$ zeros, and $M_j=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{-\infty}^\infty|{-c}+it|^j/|G(-c+it)|\,\mathrm dt$. Numerically $\log M_0=206.26$ and $M_{j+1}/M_j=1.0000185\,c$ for $j=0,1,2$ (computed).
results.label: ht:prop:explicit

results.name: Log concavity of the reciprocal xi density on [0.008, infinity) from computed constants
results.summary: Assuming the quadrature values of the constants $M_j$, $j\le8$, of the explicit truncation bound, $f$ is strictly log concave on $[0.008,\infty)$ with no hypothesis on the zeros.
results.statement: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. Assume the values of the constants $M_j$, $j\le8$, of the explicit truncation bound for $f$ with its first $120$ residue terms (computed by quadrature). Then, with no hypothesis on the zeros, $f$ is strictly log concave on $[Y_*,\infty)$ with $Y_*=0.008$.
results.label: ht:thm:lc

results.name: If the density of the reciprocal xi law were HCM then RH would hold
results.summary: If $f$ is hyperbolically completely monotone (HCM) then $\mu$ is a GGC and RH holds.
results.statement: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. If the density $f$ of $\mu$ is HCM (hyperbolically completely monotone), then $\mu$ is a GGC and RH holds.
results.label: ht:prop:hcm

results.name: No HCM: sums of exponentials are not HCM, and the continued reciprocal xi density has a computed zero in the right half plane
results.status_text: conditional on for part (ii), an explicit remainder bound for the omitted terms on a sector containing $z_*$
results.conditions: for part (ii), an explicit remainder bound for the omitted terms on a sector containing $z_*$
results.summary: No density of a sum of $n\ge2$ independent exponentials with distinct rates is HCM (proved); the continuation of $f$ from its first 120 residue terms vanishes at $z_*=0.01383187+0.02000180i$ (computed), which proves $f$ is not HCM once the omitted terms are controlled on a sector containing $z_*$.
results.statement: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. (i) No density of a sum of $n\ge2$ independent exponential variables with distinct rates is HCM. (ii) With the first $120$ terms of the residue series for $f$, the continuation of $f$ to $\operatorname{Re}z>0$ vanishes at $z_*=0.013831874754506+0.020001801712034\,i$ (computed). If the omitted terms are controlled by an explicit remainder bound on a sector containing $z_*$, this proves that $f$ is not HCM.
results.label: ht:thm:nohcm

results.name: Partial complete monotonicity of the canonical function of the reciprocal xi law up to an order growing with x, from the verified zeros
results.summary: With $T=3\cdot10^{12}$, for every $x\ge1/T$ and every integer $0\le n\le((T^2-\gamma_1^2-1)x-5)/\log(T^2/\gamma_1^2)$, $(-1)^n\Theta^{(n)}(x)>0$ (numerically $n\le1.7\cdot10^{23}x$); RH holds iff the bound can be replaced by $n<\infty$ for every $x>0$.
results.statement: Let $\gamma_1$ be the first ordinate, $s_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ and $\Theta(x)=\sum_{\gamma>0}e^{s_\rho x}$ the canonical function of the reciprocal xi law. Let $T=3\cdot10^{12}$, so that every zero with $0<\gamma\le T$ is on the line (Platt and Trudgian). For every $x\ge1/T$ and every integer $0\le n\le\frac{(T^2-\gamma_1^2-1)x-5}{\log(T^2/\gamma_1^2)}$ we have $(-1)^n\Theta^{(n)}(x)>0$. Numerically the bound is $n\le1.7\cdot10^{23}x$. RH holds if and only if the bound can be replaced by $n<\infty$ for every $x>0$.
results.label: ht:thm:partialcm

results.name: Equivalent forms of the quasi Riemann hypothesis QRH(alpha) through the prime counting error, the prime Dirichlet series and the base point laws
results.summary: For $\frac12\le\alpha<1$ the following are equivalent: QRH($\alpha$); $\psi(x)=x+O(x^{\alpha+\varepsilon})$; $\sum(\Lambda(n)-1)n^{-s}$ converges for $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha$; $\operatorname{Re}\xi'/\xi(s)>0$ for $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha$; the base point laws $\mu^{(\beta)}$ are GGCs for every $\beta>\alpha$.
results.statement: Write $\mathrm{QRH}(\alpha)$ for the statement that every nontrivial zero of $\zeta$ has real part at most $\alpha$, $\frac12\le\alpha<1$. Let $\psi$ be the Chebyshev function, $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function, and $\mu^{(\beta)}$ the base point law with Laplace transform $\xi(\beta)/\xi(\beta+\sqrt s)$. For $\frac12\le\alpha<1$ the following are equivalent. (1) $\mathrm{QRH}(\alpha)$. (2) $\psi(x)=x+O(x^{\alpha+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. (3) The Dirichlet series $D(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}(\Lambda(n)-1)n^{-s}$ converges for $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha$, so that $-\zeta'/\zeta=\zeta+D$ there. (4) $\operatorname{Re}\xi'/\xi(s)>0$ for $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha$. (5) The base point laws $\mu^{(\beta)}$ are GGCs, that is diffusion hitting times, for every $\beta>\alpha$.
results.label: ht:prop:qrh

results.name: The function 1/xi(beta+w) is never a Laplace transform of a positive measure in w
results.summary: For no real $\beta$ is $w\mapsto1/\xi(\beta+w)$ the one sided or two sided Laplace transform of a positive measure.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function. For no real $\beta$ is $w\mapsto1/\xi(\beta+w)$ the one or two sided Laplace transform of a positive measure.
results.label: ht:lem:landau

results.name: Prime built GGC hitting times converge to the base point laws for theta < beta < 2 - theta under QRH(theta)
results.status_text: conditional on the quasi Riemann hypothesis QRH($\theta$) for some $\theta<1$ (every nontrivial zero has real part at most $\theta$)
results.conditions: the quasi Riemann hypothesis QRH($\theta$) for some $\theta<1$ (every nontrivial zero has real part at most $\theta$)
results.summary: Assume QRH($\theta$) and $\theta<\beta<2-\theta$. Then $|d_X(t)-\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}\xi'/\xi(\beta+it)|\ll_\beta X^{\theta-\beta}\log(t+2)$ uniformly in $t$, $d_X\ge0$ for $X\ge X_0(\beta,\theta)$, the GGC laws $\mu^{(\beta)}_X$ with Thorin density $d_X$ converge weakly to $\mu^{(\beta)}$, and conversely nonnegativity of $d_X(t)$ for large $X$ at one $\beta$ gives QRH($\beta$).
results.statement: Assume $\mathrm{QRH}(\theta)$ for some $\theta<1$ (every nontrivial zero of $\zeta$ has real part at most $\theta$) and let $\theta<\beta<2-\theta$. Let $w(u)=(1-u)_+^3$ with Mellin transform $W(z)=6/(z(z+1)(z+2)(z+3))$, and for $\beta>\theta$ let $d_X(t)=\frac1\pi(\operatorname{Re}A(\beta+it)-\operatorname{Re}\sum_{n\le X}\Lambda(n)n^{-\beta-it}(1-n/X)^3+\operatorname{Re}X^{1-\beta-it}W(1-\beta-it))$, where $A$ is the archimedean (gamma function) term of the explicit formula as defined in the book, so that $d_X$ uses only the primes up to $X$. Then $|d_X(t)-\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}\xi'/\xi(\beta+it)|\ll_\beta X^{\theta-\beta}\log(t+2)$ uniformly in $t$, and there is $X_0(\beta,\theta)$ such that for $X\ge X_0$ the function $d_X$ is nonnegative. The GGC laws $\mu^{(\beta)}_X$ with Thorin density $d_X$ in the variable $z=t^2$ are then hitting times built from the primes up to $X$, and $\mu^{(\beta)}_X\Rightarrow\mu^{(\beta)}$ as $X\to\infty$, where $\mu^{(\beta)}$ has Laplace transform $\xi(\beta)/\xi(\beta+\sqrt s)$. Conversely, if for some $\beta$ and every $t$ the values $d_X(t)$ are nonnegative for all large $X$, then $\mathrm{QRH}(\beta)$ holds. The unconditional range $1<\beta<2$ is not covered.
results.label: ht:thm:primebuilt

results.name: Riemann's variable V as a GGC with a signed Gamma mixture density
results.summary: The variable V with Mellin transform 2 xi(s) is a sum of independent Gamma(2) variables over pi n squared, hence a GGC, its density is a signed mixture of Gamma(2) and exponential densities, and it is not a scale mixture of Gamma laws.
results.statement: Let $V$ be the positive random variable of Riemann's functional equation, with $\mathbb E V^{s/2}=2\xi(s)$. (i) (Williams; Biane, Pitman and Yor.) $V=\sum_{n\ge1}\Gamma_n/(\pi n^2)$ with independent Gamma(2) variables $\Gamma_n$, so $V$ is a GGC with Thorin measure $2\sum_n\delta_{\pi n^2}$. (ii) The density of $V$ is $f_V(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}\big[4\,g_2(x;\pi n^2)-6\,g_1(x;\pi n^2)\big]$ for $x>0$, with $g_j(x;r)$ the Gamma($j$) density of rate $r$; this is a signed mixture of Gamma(2) and exponential densities over the rates $\pi n^2$, each term has mass $-2$, and the masses sum to $1$ under zeta regularisation since $-2\zeta(0)=1$. (iii) For $\operatorname{Re}s>1$, $\mathbb E V^{s/2}=\sum_{n\ge1}(\pi n^2)^{-s/2}\big(4\Gamma(2+\tfrac s2)-6\Gamma(1+\tfrac s2)\big)=s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\tfrac s2)\zeta(s)=2\xi(s)$. (iv) $V$ is not a scale mixture of Gamma($a$) laws for any $a>0$; its density is positive, and the negative terms of the series for $f_V$ cannot be absorbed into a positive mixture.
results.label: riemanncont:prop:riemann

results.name: A GGC with an entire Laplace transform is constant, so X squared and |X| are not GGC
results.summary: A generalised gamma convolution whose Laplace transform extends to an entire function is a constant, so neither the square nor the absolute value of the Pólya variable is a GGC and Bondesson's product theorem does not apply to the arithmetic mean factorisation.
results.statement: A GGC whose Laplace transform extends to an entire function is a constant. In particular neither $X^2$ nor $|X|$ is a GGC, for the Pólya variable $X$. So Bondesson's product theorem does not apply to the factorisation $\tfrac12X^2\cdot C$ of the law whose Laplace transform is the arithmetic mean $\mathbb E\operatorname{sech}(\sqrt uX)$.
results.label: riemanncont:prop:entire

results.name: Positive Thorin density m at the centre with no hypothesis on the zeros
results.summary: From the heat trace K the function m is positive for every theta with no hypothesis on the zeros and is the Thorin density of the half line law with transform P of the square root, and RH holds exactly when its continuation M is a Stieltjes function.
results.statement:
Let $ho_k=	frac12+\delta_k+i\gamma_k$ be the nontrivial zeros with $\gamma_k>0$ (conjugate pairs taken together), $a_k=-(ho_k-	frac12)^2$, $c_k=\sqrt{a_k}$ with positive real part (so $c_k=\gamma_k-i\delta_k$), $K(x)=\sum_ke^{-c_kx}$ and $P(s)=\prod_k(1+s/c_k)e^{-s/c_k}$. With no hypothesis on the zeros, let $m(	heta)= rac1\pi\int_0^\infty(1-\cos x	heta)K(x)\,dx= rac1\pi\sum_k rac{	heta^2}{c_k(c_k^2+	heta^2)}$ for $	heta>0$. (i) $m(	heta)>0$ for every $	heta>0$, and $u\mapsto P(\sqrt u)$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC whose Thorin measure has density $m$ in the chart $	heta=\sqrt z$: $-\log P(s)=\int_0^\infty\log ig(1+s^2/	heta^2 ig)m(	heta)\,d	heta$ for $s\ge0$. Moreover $P(s)P(-s)=\xi(	frac12+is)/\xi(	frac12)$, and $1/P(s)=\mathbb E e^{-sA}$ for the law $A$ of the book's half line proposition. (ii) The function $M(w)=\pi m(\sqrt w)/w=\sum_k ig(c_k(w+a_k) ig)^{-1}$ extends to a meromorphic function on $\mathbb C$, with simple poles at the points $-a_k$ of simple zeros and residues $1/c_k$ there. (iii) RH holds if and only if $M$ is a Stieltjes function, that is $M(w)=\int
u(dz)/(w+z)$ for $w>0$ with a positive measure $
u$. In that case $
u=\sum_{\gamma>0}\gamma^{-1}\delta_{\gamma^2}$, which is $z^{-1/2}U_{\mathrm{RH}}(dz)$ with $U_{\mathrm{RH}}=\sum_{\gamma>0}\delta_{\gamma^2}$.
results.label: riemanncont:thm:half

results.name: The de Bruijn tilt as a normal mixture of Esscher tilts, and the failure of the weight e to the minus |u|
results.summary: The Gaussian tilts of the Pólya density are normal mixtures of Esscher tilts or horizontal smoothings of Xi, while the exponential weight gives a Fourier transform with only finitely many real zeros.
results.statement: Let $\Phi$ be the Pólya density, so that $\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)\cosh(su)\,du=\xi(\tfrac12+s)$ and $\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)e^{izu}\,du=\Xi(z)=\xi(\tfrac12+iz)$, and let $N$ be standard normal. (i) For $\lambda>0$, $e^{\lambda u^2}=\mathbb E\cosh(\sqrt{2\lambda}\,Nu)$, and for every $s,z\in\mathbb C$, $\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)e^{\lambda u^2}\cosh(su)\,du=\mathbb E\,\xi\big(\tfrac12+s+\sqrt{2\lambda}N\big)$ and $\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)e^{\lambda u^2}e^{izu}\,du=\mathbb E\,\Xi\big(z+i\sqrt{2\lambda}N\big)$; the de Bruijn tilt is a normal scale mixture of Esscher tilts, a Gaussian average of the basepoint moves $\alpha=\tfrac12+\sqrt{2\lambda}N$. (ii) For $b>0$, $e^{-bu^2}=\mathbb E\cos(\sqrt{2b}\,Nu)$ and $\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)e^{-bu^2}e^{izu}\,du=\mathbb E\,\Xi(z+\sqrt{2b}N)$, a horizontal Gaussian smoothing of $\Xi$. (iii) $e^{-|u|}=\mathbb E\big[(\pi\tau)^{-1/2}e^{-u^2/(4\tau)}\big]$, so $e^{-|u|}\Phi$ is a positive mixture, over $b=1/(4\tau)$, of the damped kernels of (ii), and $F(z)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)e^{-|u|}e^{izu}\,du=\frac1\pi\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{\Xi(z-y)}{1+y^2}\,dy$. (iv) $F(x)=2\Phi(0)/x^2+O(x^{-4})$ as $x\to\infty$ along the real axis, so $F$ has only finitely many real zeros.
results.label: riemanncont:prop:tilts

results.name: Question: is the Laplace transform E sech(sqrt(u) X) a GGC transform
results.summary: The book asks whether the arithmetic mean of sech(sqrt(u) X), the Laplace transform of one half X squared times C, is a GGC transform, which would not bear on RH directly.
results.statement: Is $u\mapsto\mathbb E\operatorname{sech}(\sqrt u\,X)$, the Laplace transform of $\tfrac12X^2C$ (with $X$ the Pólya variable), a GGC transform? Bondesson's product theorem does not apply to the factorisation $\tfrac12X^2\cdot C$, since $X^2$ is not a GGC. An answer would not bear on RH directly, but it would show whether the arithmetic mean side of Jensen's inequality keeps the Thorin property.
results.label: riemanncont:prob:arith

results.name: Question: a class of mixing laws whose harmonic mean of GGC transforms is a GGC transform
results.summary: The book asks for a class of mixing laws for which the harmonic mean of GGC transforms is again a GGC transform, not already explained by Pólya's theorems on real zeros.
results.statement: Find a class $\mathcal C$ of mixing laws for which the harmonic mean $1/\mathbb E[1/\varphi_X(u)]$ of GGC transforms $\varphi_x$ is again a GGC transform, and which is not already explained by Pólya's theorems on real zeros. Any such class containing the Pólya density must use the Euler product, since otherwise the Davenport and Heilbronn function refutes it.
results.label: riemanncont:prob:hm

results.name: Question: a quantitative lower bound for Im M(-x - i eta)
results.summary: The book asks for a quantitative bound from below on the imaginary part of the continuation M just off the negative axis, in terms of computable data and a zero free region.
results.statement: The density $m$ of the half line theorem is positive with no hypothesis, and its continuation $M(w)$ has the poles $-a_k$. Is there a quantitative statement, in the spirit of the book's strip theorem (part 3), that bounds $\operatorname{Im}M(-x-i\eta)$ from below on $x>0$, for some $\eta>0$, in terms of computable data and a zero free region? Such a bound is a positivity statement at a level below one, so it would be at least as strong as a zero free half plane.
results.label: riemanncont:prob:half

results.name: Question: even weights w for which w times Phi has a Fourier transform with only real zeros
results.summary: The book asks for which even weights other than mixtures of cosh the tilted Pólya density has a Fourier transform with only real zeros under RH, and whether smoothness at the origin with log w convex suffices.
results.statement: For which even weights $w$ with $w(0)=1$, other than $\mathbb E\cosh(uB)$ (a mixture of cosh factors), does $w\Phi$ have a Fourier transform with only real zeros under RH? The weight $e^{-|u|}$ fails, and the same argument covers every weight that is smooth on $[0,\infty)$ with $w'(0+)\ne0$. Is smoothness at the origin together with $\log w$ convex sufficient?
results.label: riemanncont:prob:tilt

results.name: The z distribution as a normal variance mean mixture and Laplace sum
results.summary: The z(a,b) law has an explicit moment generating function and Weierstrass product, is a normal variance mean mixture with a GGC mixing law, and in the symmetric case is the EGGC sum of Laplace variables over c plus k.
results.statement: Let $X\sim z(a,b)$, the law of $\log(G_a/G_b)$ for independent gamma variables of shapes $a$ and $b$. (i) For $-a<\operatorname{Re}s<b$, $\mathbb E e^{sX}=B(a+s,b-s)/B(a,b)=\Gamma(a+s)\Gamma(b-s)/(\Gamma(a)\Gamma(b))$. (ii) For the same $s$, $\mathbb E e^{sX}=\prod_{k\ge0}\frac{(a+k)(b+k)}{(a+k+s)(b+k-s)}$. (iii) $X\overset d=\mu W+\sqrt W\,Z$ with $\mu=\tfrac{a-b}2$, $Z$ standard normal and $W$ independent of $Z$ with $W=\sum_{k\ge0}\frac{2E_k}{(a+k)(b+k)}$, the $E_k$ independent standard exponential variables; so $W$ is a GGC with unit Thorin atoms at the points $\tfrac12(a+k)(b+k)$, and $X$ is a normal variance mean mixture. (iv) In the symmetric case $a=b=c$, $X\overset d=\sum_{k\ge0}L_k/(c+k)$ with independent standard Laplace variables $L_k$, and $X$ is a symmetric EGGC with Thorin measure $\sum_{k\ge0}\delta_{c+k}$ in the chart $\theta$; its characteristic function is $|\Gamma(c+i v)|^2/\Gamma(c)^2$.
results.label: zdist:prop:mix

results.name: Meixner duality for the symmetric z law
results.summary: The density of z(c,c) and the density of the Meixner law of order c are, up to constants, the characteristic function of each other, and both are symmetric EGGC laws.
results.statement: For $c>0$, the density of $z(c,c)$ is $f_{c,c}(x)=(2\cosh\tfrac x2)^{-2c}/B(c,c)$, a constant multiple of the characteristic function of the Meixner law of order $c$, and the characteristic function of $z(c,c)$ is $|\Gamma(c+iv)|^2/\Gamma(c)^2$, a constant multiple of the Meixner density $m_c(v)$. Both laws are symmetric EGGC laws: $z(c,c)$ with Thorin measure $\sum_{k\ge0}\delta_{c+k}$ and the Meixner law with Thorin measure $2c\sum_{k\ge0}\delta_{(2k+1)\pi}$, both in the chart $\theta$. For $c=\tfrac12$ the two coincide up to scale with the hyperbolic secant law.
results.label: zdist:prop:dual

results.name: Van Dantzig pairs for the symmetric z law exist exactly when c is at least one half
results.summary: The characteristic function of z(c,c) is the second member of a van Dantzig pair if and only if c is at least one half, and the first member is then Gamma(c) squared divided by Gamma(c+v)Gamma(c minus v).
results.statement: Let $c>0$ and $\varphi_2(v)=|\Gamma(c+iv)|^2/\Gamma(c)^2$, the characteristic function of $z(c,c)$. There is a characteristic function $\varphi_1$ with $\varphi_2(\theta)=1/\varphi_1(i\theta)$ for all real $\theta$ if and only if $c\ge\tfrac12$. Then $\varphi_1(v)=\Gamma(c)^2/(\Gamma(c+v)\Gamma(c-v))$; for $c>\tfrac12$ it is the characteristic function of $2\Theta$, where $\Theta$ has density proportional to $\cos^{2c-2}\theta$ on $(-\tfrac\pi2,\tfrac\pi2)$, and for $c=\tfrac12$ it is $\cos(\pi v)$, the characteristic function of a symmetric sign times $\pi$.
results.label: zdist:prop:vd

results.name: The archimedean factor of xi squared is a z law, and T plus T tilde does not contain H infinity
results.summary: The archimedean factor of xi squared is the moment generating function of z(1/4,1/4) up to a polar factor, and the remainder D_0 has negative mean, so T plus T tilde has no independent summand H infinity.
results.statement: Let $X\sim z(\tfrac14,\tfrac14)$, $\xi(\tfrac12)/\xi(\tfrac12+u)=\mathbb E e^{-u^2T}$ with $\tilde T$ an independent copy of $T$, $Y=Z\sqrt{2T}$ with $Y'$ an independent copy, and $H_\infty$ the GGC with unit Thorin atoms at $c_k^2$, $c_k=2k+\tfrac12$. (i) For real $|s|<\tfrac12$, $\frac{\xi(\frac12+s)^2}{\xi(\frac12)^2}=(1-4s^2)^2\,\mathbb E e^{sX/2}\,\frac{\zeta(\frac12+s)\zeta(\frac12-s)}{\zeta(\frac12)^2}$, and on the critical line, for real $v$, $\frac{\Xi(v)^2}{\Xi(0)^2}=(1+4v^2)^2\,\mathbb E e^{ivX/2}\,\frac{|\zeta(\frac12+iv)|^2}{\zeta(\frac12)^2}$. (ii) Let $D_0=T+\tilde T-H_\infty$, with $T$, $\tilde T$ and $H_\infty$ independent. For $0\le w<\tfrac14$, $\mathbb E e^{-wD_0}=\frac{\zeta(\frac12)^2}{(1-4w)^2\,\zeta(\frac12+\sqrt w)\,\zeta(\frac12-\sqrt w)}$. (iii) $\mathbb E D_0=2\mathbb E T-\tfrac14\psi'(\tfrac14)=-8+(\log\zeta)''(\tfrac12)=-4.2531223024$. Consequently there is no law $Q$ on $[0,\infty)$, independent of $H_\infty$, with $T+\tilde T\overset d=H_\infty+Q$, and no random variable $R$ independent of $X$ with $Y+Y'\overset d=X/2+R$.
results.label: zdist:prop:arch

results.name: Sine squared image of the z law Lévy density and the Gamma ratio as a Cauchy factor times an EGGC
results.summary: The sine squared transform of the completely monotone Lévy density of z(c,c) is the Thorin density of the progression c plus n, and Gamma(a)/Gamma(a+|u|) is an exponential factor times the characteristic function of a symmetric EGGC.
results.statement: (i) The law $z(c,c)$ has Lévy density $k_c(|x|)/|x|$ with $k_c(r)=e^{-cr}/(1-e^{-r})=\sum_{n\ge0}e^{-(c+n)r}$, completely monotone, and the sine squared image of $k_c$, $\frac1\pi\int_0^\infty2\sin^2(x\theta/2)\,k_c(x)\,dx$, is $\frac1\pi\sum_n\theta^2/\big((c+n)((c+n)^2+\theta^2)\big)$. (ii) For $a>0$ and real $u$, $e^{\psi(a)|u|}\frac{\Gamma(a)}{\Gamma(a+|u|)}=\exp\Big\{-\frac1\pi\int_0^\infty\log\Big(1+\frac{u^2}{\theta^2}\Big)\big(\operatorname{Re}\psi(a+i\theta)-\psi(a)\big)\,d\theta\Big\}$, and $\operatorname{Re}\psi(a+i\theta)-\psi(a)>0$ for $\theta\ne0$. So the left side is the characteristic function of a symmetric EGGC, and $\Gamma(a)/\Gamma(a+|u|)$ is the product of $e^{-\psi(a)|u|}$, a Cauchy factor when $\psi(a)>0$ (that is $a>1.4616$), and that EGGC.
results.label: zdist:prop:sin2

results.name: The heat flow of laws Y_t is a symmetric EGGC exactly for t at least the de Bruijn Newman constant
results.summary: The normal scale mixtures Y_t built from the de Bruijn Newman flow are symmetric EGGC laws exactly for t at least Lambda, so with no hypothesis for t at least 0.2, and after scaling they converge to the z(1/2,1/2) law as t grows.
results.statement: Let $\Lambda$ be the de Bruijn Newman constant, $H_t(z)=\int_0^\infty e^{tw^2}\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(w)\cosh(zw)\,dw$, $\xi_t(s)=8H_t(-2i(s-\tfrac12))$ and $R_t(u)=H_t(0)/H_t(2i\sqrt u)$, so that $\xi_0=\xi$ and $R_t(v^2)=\xi_t(\tfrac12)/\xi_t(\tfrac12+v)$ for real $v$. (i) For every real $t$, $H_t(iy)>0$ for real $y$. If $R_t$ is the Laplace transform of a law $T_t$ on $[0,\infty)$, then $v\mapsto R_t(v^2)$ is the characteristic function of the symmetric law $Y_t=Z\sqrt{2T_t}$. (ii) For $t\ge\Lambda$ the law $T_t$ exists, and $v\mapsto R_t(v^2)$ is the characteristic function of a symmetric EGGC if and only if $t\ge\Lambda$, and then $Y_t\overset d=\sum_kL_k/\theta_k(t)$ over the positive zeros $\tfrac12\pm i\theta_k(t)$ of $\xi_t$. In particular $Y_t$ is an EGGC for every $t\ge0.2$, with no hypothesis, and $Y_0=Y$ is an EGGC if and only if RH holds. (iii) With $u_t$ the mode of the book's large $t$ proposition, $Y_t/u_t\Rightarrow\tfrac2\pi X_{1/2}$ as $t\to\infty$, where $X_{1/2}\sim z(\tfrac12,\tfrac12)$; the limit has characteristic function $1/\cosh(2v)$.
results.label: zdist:thm:flow

results.name: A limit of symmetric EGGC laws equal to Y forces RH
results.summary: If symmetric EGGC laws converge weakly to the law of Y then RH holds, and conversely under RH the constant sequence works.
results.statement: Let $Y=Z\sqrt{2T}$ with $\mathbb E e^{-u^2T}=\xi(\tfrac12)/\xi(\tfrac12+u)$. If there are symmetric EGGC laws $Y_n$ with $Y_n\Rightarrow Y$, then RH holds. Conversely, under RH the constant family $Y_n=Y$ is such a family.
results.label: zdist:prop:closure

results.name: A truncated EGGC law within v to the fourth times epsilon of the law of Y
results.status_text: conditional on All zeros of the zeta function with ordinate at most $T_0=3\times10^{12}$ lie on the critical line, read as quoted from Platt and Trudgian (PT21); this is a finite computation by others that the book does not repeat
results.conditions: All zeros of the zeta function with ordinate at most $T_0=3\times10^{12}$ lie on the critical line, read as quoted from Platt and Trudgian (PT21); this is a finite computation by others that the book does not repeat.
results.summary: Replacing the zeros above a height T' by their second moment as a Gaussian gives a symmetric EGGC law that is within v to the fourth times a tiny epsilon of the law of Y in the log characteristic function.
results.statement: Let $T_0=3\times10^{12}$, the height below which every zero lies on the critical line, and for $2\le T'\le T_0$ put $m(T')=\sum_{k:\ \gamma_k>T'}1/a_k$ and $Y^{(T')}=\sqrt{2m(T')}\,Z_0+\sum_{0<\gamma\le T'}L_\gamma/\gamma$, with $a_k=-(\rho_k-\tfrac12)^2$ summed over the zeros with $\gamma_k>T'$, $Z_0$ standard normal and the $L_\gamma$ standard Laplace, all independent. Then $m(T')>0$, $Y^{(T')}$ is a symmetric EGGC, $\operatorname{Var}Y^{(T')}=\operatorname{Var}Y=2\mathbb E T$, and for real $v$ with $v^2\le T'^2/2$, $\big|\log\mathbb E e^{ivY}-\log\mathbb E e^{ivY^{(T')}}\big|\le v^4\,\epsilon(T')$ with $\epsilon(T')=\frac2\pi\Big(\frac{\log T'}{3T'^3}+\frac1{9T'^3}\Big)$.
results.label: zdist:prop:trunc

results.name: Question: is the BNKS mixing law the GGC of the z law proposition
results.summary: The book asks whether the mixing law in the paper of Barndorff-Nielsen, Kent and Sørensen is the GGC derived here, and whether their asymmetric results have an analogue for the tilted Pólya variables.
results.statement: Read the paper of Barndorff-Nielsen, Kent and Sørensen on the $z$ laws and determine whether its mixing law for $z(a,b)$ is the GGC of the book's mixture proposition, part (iii), and whether its results on the asymmetric laws, $\mu\ne0$, have an analogue for the tilted Pólya variables $V_\alpha$, whose characteristic functions $\xi(\alpha+i\theta)/\xi(\alpha)$ are never infinitely divisible.
results.label: zdist:prob:bnks

results.name: Question: positive sequences c_k for which the sum of L_k over c_k is a van Dantzig second member
results.summary: The book asks which positive sequences with square summable reciprocals give a van Dantzig pair, a condition on the regularity of the sequence and not on its density alone.
results.statement: The van Dantzig proposition decides the property for the arithmetic progressions $c_k=c+k$. Characterise the positive sequences $(c_k)$ with $\sum c_k^{-2}<\infty$ for which $\sum_kL_k/c_k$ is the second member of a van Dantzig pair. Under RH the ordinates $\gamma_k$ are such a sequence, with first member $\Xi(v)/\Xi(0)$; the condition is that $\prod_k(1-v^2/c_k^2)$ be a characteristic function.
results.label: zdist:prob:vd

results.name: Question: an unconditional EGGC family from the z law to Y other than the heat flow
results.summary: The book asks for a one parameter family of unconditional EGGC laws joining the scaled z(1/2,1/2) law to Y other than the heat flow, along which the EGGC property is followed by a computation not reducing to reality of the zeros.
results.statement: Is there a one parameter family of symmetric laws, each an EGGC with no hypothesis, joining $\tfrac2\pi X_{1/2}$ to $Y$ other than by the heat flow, along which the EGGC property can be followed by a computation that does not reduce to the reality of the zeros of $H_t$? The closure proposition implies that such a family cannot reach $Y$ unconditionally, so the question is which property of the family degenerates at the endpoint.
results.label: zdist:prob:interp

results.name: Question: is the Lévy density K_t(y) of Y_t monotone in t
results.summary: The book asks whether the Lévy density of the heat flow law Y_t is monotone in t for each fixed y.
results.statement: Is the Lévy density $K_t(|y|)/|y|$ of $Y_t$, with $K_t(y)=\sum_ke^{-\theta_k(t)y}$ for $t\ge\Lambda$, monotone in $t$ for each fixed $y$? The same question for the stochastic order of $T_t$ is a problem of an earlier chapter; for $Y_t$ it would say that the flow moves Lévy mass monotonically between scales.
results.label: zdist:prob:flow

results.name: Question: the set of lambda for which the ratio of transforms of T plus T tilde and H lambda is a Laplace transform
results.summary: The book asks for which lambda between 0 and 1 the ratio of the Laplace transforms of T plus T tilde and of H lambda is again a Laplace transform, whether the set is an interval, and what its right end is.
results.statement: The variable $D_0$ of the archimedean proposition has negative mean, so $T+\tilde T$ does not contain $H_\infty$ as an independent summand. For $0\le\lambda\le1$ let $H^{(\lambda)}$ be the GGC with Thorin atoms of mass $\lambda$ at the points $c_k^2$. For which $\lambda$ is $\mathbb E e^{-w(T+\tilde T)}/\mathbb E e^{-wH^{(\lambda)}}$ the Laplace transform of a law on $[0,\infty)$? The mean gives the necessary condition $\lambda\le2\mathbb E T/\mathbb E H_\infty=0.01075$, and at $\lambda=0$ the answer is yes. Is the set of such $\lambda$ an interval $[0,\lambda^*]$ with $\lambda^*>0$, and what is $\lambda^*$?
results.label: zdist:prob:remainder

results.name: Complete asymptotic expansion of the heat trace W(t) at t = 0 with the coefficients d_n and b_k, and the logarithmic divergence of the clock
results.summary: With no hypothesis, $W(t)$ has the asymptotic expansion $\frac{\log(1/t)-\gamma_E-4\log2-2\log\pi}{8\sqrt{\pi t}}+\sum d_nt^n+\sum b_kt^{k-1/2}$ as $t\downarrow0$, with $d_0=\frac78$; the two term case is in Polson 2017, and the integral of $W(t)/t$ from $\tau$ diverges so the clock has infinitely many jumps.
results.statement: Let $\vartheta$ be the Riemann Siegel theta function, $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function. With no hypothesis $W(t)=e^{t/4}+\frac1\pi\int_0^\infty e^{-u^2t}\vartheta'(u)\,du-\frac1{\sqrt{4\pi t}}\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\Lambda(n)}{\sqrt n}e^{-(\log n)^2/4t}$, the prime terms are $O(t^{-1/2}e^{-(\log2)^2/4t})$, and for every $N$, as $t\downarrow0$, $W(t)=\frac{\log\frac1t-\gamma_E-4\log2-2\log\pi}{8\sqrt{\pi t}}+\sum_{n=0}^Nd_nt^n+\sum_{k=1}^Nb_kt^{k-1/2}+O(t^{N+1/2})$, with $d_n=(1-\frac{E_{2n}}8)\frac{4^{-n}}{n!}$, $b_k=\frac{(1-2k)\Gamma(\frac12-k)}{2\pi}\beta_k$, $E_{2n}$ the Euler numbers and $\beta_k=\frac{(1-2^{1-2k})|B_{2k}|}{4k(2k-1)}$ the coefficients of Stirling's series for $\vartheta$. After the leading term the series is $\frac78+\frac{\sqrt t}{48\sqrt\pi}+\frac9{32}t-\frac{7t^{3/2}}{2880\sqrt\pi}+\frac3{256}t^2+\frac{31t^{5/2}}{60480\sqrt\pi}+\frac{69}{3072}t^3+\cdots$, and it diverges. Consequently $\int_\tau^\infty W(t)\,dt/t=\frac{\log\frac1\tau-\gamma_E-4\log2-2\log\pi-2}{4\sqrt{\pi\tau}}+\frac78\log\frac1\tau+O(1)$ as $\tau\downarrow0$, so the clock has infinitely many jumps. The two term version is in Polson 2017, Corollary 5.5; the full series is checked numerically through order $t^{5/2}$ in a 40 digit computation for $10^{-6}\le t\le10^{-3}$.
results.label: tx3:res:wzero

results.name: The clock is infinitely divisible and self decomposable, unconditionally
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: Using only the verification of RH below height 1000, the heat trace is positive and decreasing, so the clock is the Laplace transform of an infinitely divisible, self decomposable law with Lévy density W(t)/t, with the numerical inequalities of the proof certified in ball arithmetic.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function, $\Xi(z)=\xi(\tfrac12+iz)$, and let $W(t)=\sum_je^{-a_jt}$ be the heat trace, where $a_j=-(\rho_j-\tfrac12)^2$ and $\rho_j$ runs over one zero of each pair $\{\rho,1-\rho\}$ of zeros of $\xi$, counted with multiplicity. Unconditionally, that is, using only the verification of RH below height $1000$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021), $W(t)>0$ and $W'(t)<0$ for every $t>0$. Consequently the clock $\xi(\tfrac12)/\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt u)=\exp\bigl(-\int_0^\infty(1-e^{-ut})\,W(t)\,dt/t\bigr)$ is the Laplace transform of an infinitely divisible, self decomposable law on $[0,\infty)$ with Lévy density $W(t)/t$, and $\bigl(\Xi(\theta)/\Xi(0),\ \xi(\tfrac12)/\xi(\tfrac12+\theta)\bigr)$ is a van Dantzig pair, that is, a pair $(\varphi_1,\varphi_2)$ of characteristic functions with $\varphi_2(\theta)=1/\varphi_1(i\theta)$.
results.label: thm:ch12:idsd

results.name: Hankel positivity of the heat trace at one time is equivalent to RH
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2017, version 24 of 2026), On Hilbert's 8th problem, arXiv:1708.02653.
results.summary: At any single time t, positive semidefiniteness of the two Hankel matrices of derivatives of the heat trace, equivalently of Weil's quadratic form on the span of r^m exp(-r^2 t/2), is equivalent to RH.
results.statement: Let $W(t)=\sum_je^{-a_jt}$ be the heat trace of the completed Riemann zeta function $\xi$ ($a_j=-(\rho_j-\tfrac12)^2$, one zero $\rho_j$ from each pair $\{\rho,1-\rho\}$, counted with multiplicity) and $c_k(t)=(-1)^kW^{(k)}(t)=\sum_ja_j^ke^{-a_jt}$. For any fixed $t>0$ the following are equivalent: both infinite Hankel matrices $[c_{i+j}(t)]_{i,j\ge0}$ and $[c_{i+j+1}(t)]_{i,j\ge0}$ are positive semidefinite; Weil's quadratic form $f\mapsto\sum_\rho\hat f(\gamma_\rho)\overline{\hat f(\bar\gamma_\rho)}$, where $\rho=\tfrac12+i\gamma_\rho$ runs over the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$ and $\hat f(r)=\int f(x)e^{irx}\,dx$, is positive semidefinite on the span of the test functions $f$ with $\hat f(r)=r^me^{-r^2t/2}$, $m=0,1,2,\dots$; the Riemann Hypothesis.
results.label: thm:ch12:hankel

results.name: Truncation error of the residues of the reciprocal clock when the product over zeros is cut after K factors
results.summary: For simple zeros, the residue of the truncated product at the pole $-a_k$ differs from the true residue by the factor $\prod_{j>K}(1-a_k/a_j)$, which under RH is close to one exactly for $\gamma_k\le(\gamma_K/\log\gamma_K)^{1/2}$ and not beyond.
results.statement: Let $a_j=-(\rho_j-\frac12)^2$ for one zero $\rho_j$ of each pair $\{\rho,1-\rho\}$ of nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function, ordered by increasing modulus, assumed simple, so that the $a_j$ are distinct, and let $G(u)=\prod_j(1+u/a_j)$ be the clock function $\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u)/\xi(\frac12)$ with $\xi$ the completed zeta function. Let $r_k$ and $r_k^{(K)}$ be the residues at $u=-a_k$, $k\le K$, of $1/G(u)=\prod_ja_j/(a_j+u)$ and of its product over $j\le K$. Then $r_k=a_k\prod_{j\ne k}a_j/(a_j-a_k)$ and, when $|a_j|>|a_k|$ for $j>K$, $\log\frac{r_k^{(K)}}{r_k}=\sum_{j>K}\log\big(1-\frac{a_k}{a_j}\big)=-a_k\sum_{j>K}a_j^{-1}-\frac{a_k^2}{2}\sum_{j>K}a_j^{-2}-\cdots$. Under the Riemann Hypothesis, $a_j=\gamma_j^2$ for the ordinates $\gamma_j$ and $\sum_{j>K}\gamma_j^{-2}\sim\log\gamma_K/(2\pi\gamma_K)$, so the first term is $-\gamma_k^2\log\gamma_K/(2\pi\gamma_K)$: the truncated residue is close to the true one for $\gamma_k\le(\gamma_K/\log\gamma_K)^{1/2}$, and not beyond.
results.label: tx:prop:trunc

results.name: RH is equivalent to boundedness of the heat trace of the zeros on a vertical line
results.summary: The Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if the heat trace $v\mapsto W(\sigma+iv)$ of the zeros is bounded on the real line, for one, equivalently every, $\sigma>0$.
results.statement: Let $\rho_j=\frac12+\delta_j+i\gamma_j$ be the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function, one from each pair $\{\rho,1-\rho\}$, counted with multiplicity, and put $a_j=-(\rho_j-\frac12)^2$ and $W(t)=\sum_je^{-a_jt}$ for $t>0$, extended to complex $t=\sigma+iv$ with $\sigma>0$ (the series converges absolutely there). Then the Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if $v\mapsto W(\sigma+iv)$ is bounded on $\mathbb{R}$, for one, equivalently every, $\sigma>0$. Under RH the bound is $|W(\sigma+iv)|\le W(\sigma)$ for every $\sigma>0$ and every real $v$.
results.label: tx:thm:vertical

results.name: Positive definite Hankel blocks of the heat trace up to size 3 x 10^7
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2017, version 24 of 2026), On Hilbert's 8th problem, arXiv:1708.02653.
results.summary: If every zero of xi below height 20000 N (1 + log N)^(1/2) lies on the critical line, the leading N by N Hankel blocks of the derivatives of the heat trace are positive definite at every time, and the verification of RH to height 3 times 10^12 gives this unconditionally for every N up to 3 times 10^7.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function, $W(t)=\sum_je^{-a_jt}$ its heat trace ($a_j=-(\rho_j-\tfrac12)^2$, one zero $\rho_j$ from each pair $\{\rho,1-\rho\}$, counted with multiplicity) and $c_k(t)=(-1)^kW^{(k)}(t)$, so that the two Hankel matrices of the heat trace at time $t$ are $[c_{i+j}(t)]_{i,j\ge0}$ and $[c_{i+j+1}(t)]_{i,j\ge0}$. For $N\ge1$ let $T_N=20000N\sqrt{1+\log N}$. If all zeros of $\xi$ below height $T_N$, that is, with ordinate in $(0,T_N)$, lie on the critical line, then the leading $N\times N$ blocks $[c_{i+j}(t)]_{i,j<N}$ and $[c_{i+j+1}(t)]_{i,j<N}$ are positive definite at every $t>0$. By the verification of the Riemann Hypothesis to height $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021) this holds unconditionally for every $N\le3\times10^7$.
results.label: thm:ch12:blocks

results.name: Derivative signs of the heat trace up to order 10^17
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2017, version 24 of 2026), On Hilbert's 8th problem, arXiv:1708.02653.
results.summary: Using only the verification of RH below height 10^12, the derivatives of the heat trace alternate in sign, (-1)^k W^(k)(t) > 0, for every t > 0 and every order k up to 10^17.
results.statement: Let $W(t)=\sum_je^{-a_jt}$ be the heat trace of the completed Riemann zeta function $\xi$ ($a_j=-(\rho_j-\tfrac12)^2$, one zero $\rho_j$ from each pair $\{\rho,1-\rho\}$, counted with multiplicity). Unconditionally, that is, using only the verification of RH below height $10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021), $(-1)^kW^{(k)}(t)>0$ for every $t>0$ and every integer $0\le k\le10^{17}$.
results.label: thm:ch12:cm

results.name: Hankel matrices of Stieltjes moments count the zeros off the critical line (eigenvalue form of the Grommer and Chebotarev criterion)
results.summary: In an eigenvalue form of the classical determinant criterion of Grommer (1914) and Chebotarev (1928), the numbers of negative eigenvalues of the Hankel matrices of the Stieltjes moments of the heat trace are nondecreasing in the matrix size and tend to the number of distinct zeros of xi to the right of the critical line in the upper half plane, so RH holds if and only if they are all zero.
results.statement: Let $W(t)=\sum_je^{-a_jt}$ be the heat trace of the completed Riemann zeta function $\xi$ ($a_j=-(\rho_j-\tfrac12)^2$, one zero $\rho_j$ from each pair $\{\rho,1-\rho\}$, counted with multiplicity), let $m_n=\frac1{n!}\int_0^\infty t^nW(t)\,dt=\sum_ja_j^{-n-1}$ be its Stieltjes moments, and for $N\ge1$ let $\mathcal H_N=[m_{i+j}]_{i,j<N}$ and $\mathcal H'_N=[m_{i+j+1}]_{i,j<N}$ be the Hankel matrices, with $\iota_N$ and $\iota'_N$ the numbers of negative eigenvalues of $\mathcal H_N$ and $\mathcal H'_N$. Let $K\in\{0,1,2,\dots\}\cup\{\infty\}$ be the number of distinct zeros $\rho$ of $\xi$ with $\operatorname{Re}\rho>\tfrac12$ and $\operatorname{Im}\rho>0$. Then $\iota_N$ and $\iota'_N$ are nondecreasing in $N$, $\iota_N\le K$ and $\iota'_N\le K$ for every $N$, and $\iota_N\to K$ and $\iota'_N\to K$ as $N\to\infty$. In particular RH holds if and only if $\iota_N=0$ for every $N$, and if it fails, $\iota_N\ge1$ from some $N$ on; the same holds for $\iota'_N$.
results.label: thm:ch12:inertia

results.name: Heat trace completely monotone on (0, 1.29]; every order up to t = 0.019
results.summary: Every derivative of the heat trace of order at least one alternates in sign for t up to 0.019 using no information on the zeros, and with the verification of RH below height 10^12 the heat trace is completely monotone on (0, 1.29], with the numerical inequalities of the proof certified in ball arithmetic.
results.statement: Let $W(t)=\sum_je^{-a_jt}$ be the heat trace of the completed Riemann zeta function $\xi$ ($a_j=-(\rho_j-\tfrac12)^2$, one zero $\rho_j$ from each pair $\{\rho,1-\rho\}$, counted with multiplicity). (a) For every integer $k\ge1$ and every $t\in(0,0.019]$, $(-1)^kW^{(k)}(t)>0$; the proof uses no information on the zeros. (b) Unconditionally, that is, using only the verification of RH below height $10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021), $W$ is completely monotone on $(0,1.29]$: $(-1)^kW^{(k)}(t)>0$ for every $t\in(0,1.29]$ and every integer $k\ge0$.
results.label: thm:ch12:cmint

results.name: Heat trace derivative along a ray is the Gaussian smoothing of the zeros
results.summary: For u at least 2 and k equal to u^2 t, not necessarily an integer, the k th derivative of the heat trace (defined by its sum over the zeros), divided by an explicit factor, equals the Gaussian smoothing of the zeros at resolution 1/(2 sqrt t) up to an explicit relative error on each zero within u/2 of u and an explicit remainder, with no hypothesis on the zeros.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function and $W(t)=\sum_je^{-a_jt}$ its heat trace ($a_j=-(\rho_j-\tfrac12)^2$, one zero $\rho_j$ from each pair $\{\rho,1-\rho\}$, counted with multiplicity). Take each $\rho_j$ with positive imaginary part, write $\rho_j=\tfrac12+\delta+i\gamma$ with $\gamma>0$ and $\delta$ real, and put $\tilde\gamma=\gamma-i\delta$, so that $a_j=\tilde\gamma^2$. Let $N(r)$ be the number of zeros of $\xi$ with ordinate in $(0,r]$, counted with multiplicity. Let $u\ge2$, $t>0$ and $k=u^2t$, not necessarily an integer, let $c_k(t)=\sum_ja_j^ke^{-a_jt}$ with $a_j^k$ the principal power (for an integer $k$ this is $(-1)^kW^{(k)}(t)$), and let $f_0=k(\log u^2-1)$. Then $e^{-f_0}c_k(t)=\sum_{|\tilde\gamma-u|\le u/2}e^{-2t(\tilde\gamma-u)^2}\,(1+\varepsilon_\rho)+R$, where the sum runs over the zeros with $|\tilde\gamma-u|\le u/2$, $\varepsilon_\rho$ is the relative error of the Gaussian bump of the zero $\rho$, $R$ is the contribution of the other zeros, and $|\varepsilon_\rho|\le\exp\bigl\{\tfrac{4t}{3u}|\tilde\gamma-u|^3\bigr\}-1$. With $\ell_\pm=u\pm\tfrac12\sqrt{u^2-1}$, $H(r)=u^2\log\frac{r^2+1/4}{u^2}-r^2+\tfrac14+u^2$ and $\eta=1-u^2/(\ell_+^2+\tfrac14)$, which is positive, $|R|\le N(\ell_-)\,e^{tH(\ell_-)}+\bigl(\ell_+^2+\frac1{t\eta}\bigr)e^{tH(\ell_+)}$. No hypothesis on the zeros is used.
results.label: prop:ch12:ray

results.name: RH is equivalent to nonnegativity of the Gaussian smoothing of the zeros
results.summary: The Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if the Gaussian smoothing of the zeros of xi, a sum of Gaussian bumps in complexified ordinates, is nonnegative for every real centre and every resolution.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function. Write each zero of $\xi$ with positive imaginary part, counted with multiplicity, as $\rho=\tfrac12+\delta+i\gamma$ with $\gamma>0$ and $\delta$ real, and put $\tilde\gamma=\gamma-i\delta$. For real $u$ and $t>0$ let $\mathcal G(u,t)=\sum e^{-2t(\tilde\gamma-u)^2}$, the sum over these zeros, the Gaussian smoothing of the zeros at resolution $1/(2\sqrt t)$ (it is real, because zeros off the critical line occur in pairs with conjugate values of $\tilde\gamma$). Then the Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if $\mathcal G(u,t)\ge0$ for every real $u$ and every $t>0$.
results.label: prop:ch12:gauss

results.name: There is no Gaussian smoothing criterion for RH on a line with real part alpha above one half
results.status_text: conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part $\frac12$
results.conditions: The Riemann Hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part $\frac12$.
results.summary: Under RH the Gaussian smoothing of the zeros shifted to the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha$ with $\frac12<\alpha<1$ takes negative values for some $u$ and $t$, so positivity of the Gaussian smoothing cannot be a criterion for RH on that line.
results.statement: Assume the Riemann Hypothesis, and let $\gamma>0$ run over the ordinates of the zeros $\frac12+i\gamma$ of the Riemann zeta function, with multiplicity. For $\frac12<\alpha<1$ let $\eta=\alpha-\frac12$ and $\mathcal{G}_\alpha(u,t)=\operatorname{Re}\sum_{\gamma>0}e^{-2t(\gamma+i\eta-u)^2}$ for real $u$ and $t>0$ (the Gaussian smoothing of the zeros at resolution $1/(2\sqrt t)$ shifted to the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha$; it equals the plain smoothing $\mathcal{G}$ at $\eta=0$). Then $\mathcal{G}_\alpha(u,t)<0$ for some $u$ and $t$; in fact, with $u=\gamma_1+\pi/(4t\eta)$ where $\gamma_1$ is the lowest ordinate (a simple zero), $\mathcal{G}_\alpha(u,t)=-e^{2t\eta^2}(1+o(1))<0$ as $t\to\infty$. So there is no Gaussian criterion for RH on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha$.
results.label: tx:prop:offline

results.name: Derivative signs of the heat trace up to order 1.16 x 10^25
results.summary: From the verification of RH to height 3 times 10^12, every derivative of the heat trace alternates in sign, equivalently the Williamson measures are positive, up to order 1.16 times 10^25, with the numerical inequalities of the proof certified in ball arithmetic.
results.statement: Let $W(t)=\sum_je^{-a_jt}$ be the heat trace of the completed Riemann zeta function $\xi$ ($a_j=-(\rho_j-\tfrac12)^2$, one zero $\rho_j$ from each pair $\{\rho,1-\rho\}$, counted with multiplicity). Let $H=3\times10^{12}$, the height to which RH is verified (Platt and Trudgian 2021). Then $(-1)^kW^{(k)}(t)>0$ for every $t\ge1.29$ and every integer $k$ with $0\le k\le t(H-23)^2$. Consequently $(-1)^kW^{(k)}(t)>0$ for every $t>0$ and every integer $k$ with $0\le k\le1.29(H-23)^2$, and $1.29(H-23)^2>1.16\times10^{25}$.
results.label: thm:ch12:window

results.name: Compound Poisson defect of the off line zeros: the clock plus an independent compound Poisson variable is a GGC
results.summary: Unconditionally, the heat trace of the zeros of xi is the Laplace transform of a Thorin measure minus an explicit nonnegative remainder carried by the off line zeros, so the clock plus an independent compound Poisson variable of rate below $10^{-12}$ (a bound certified in ball arithmetic from the verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$ and an explicit zero counting bound) is a generalized gamma convolution, and the remainder vanishes exactly when RH holds, that is, when the heat trace is completely monotone.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\tfrac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be the completed Riemann zeta function and $W(t)=\sum_je^{-a_jt}$ its heat trace ($a_j=-(\rho_j-\tfrac12)^2$, one zero $\rho_j$ from each pair $\{\rho,1-\rho\}$, counted with multiplicity).
