results.name: Open problem on unconditional positivity of the Li coefficients
results.summary: It is an open problem which unconditional properties of the heat trace or of the size biased clock variable force the Li coefficients to be nonnegative for every $n$, which would prove RH by Li's criterion.
results.statement:
Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function, $G(u)=\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt u)/\xi(\tfrac12)$, with zeros $-a_k$, $a_k=-(\rho_k-\tfrac12)^2$, one for each pair $\{\rho,1-\rho\}$ of zeros of $\xi$ counted with multiplicity. Let $W(t)=\sum_ke^{-a_kt}$ be the heat trace, $m_0=\sum_ka_k^{-1}$, and $A$ a variable with density $W(t)/m_0$ on $(0,\infty)$ (the size biased clock is the clock plus an independent copy of $A$). The Li coefficients are $\lambda_n=\sum_\rho\big(1-(1-1/\rho)^n\big)$, $n\ge1$, the sum over the zeros $\rho$ of $\xi$ grouped in pairs $\{\rho,1-\rho\}$; they satisfy $\lambda_n=\sum_k\varphi_n(a_k)$ with $\varphi_n(z)=2-\big(\frac{2\sqrt z+i}{2\sqrt z-i}\big)^n-\big(\frac{2\sqrt z-i}{2\sqrt z+i}\big)^n$, a rational function of $z$ with a pole of order $n$ at $z=-\tfrac14$ and no constant term in $(z+\tfrac14)^{-1}$ (for example $\varphi_1(z)=(z+\tfrac14)^{-1}$ and $\varphi_2(z)=4z(z+\tfrac14)^{-2}$). Let $k_n$ be the function with $\int_0^\infty e^{-zt}k_n(t)\,dt=\varphi_n(z)$; it has the form $k_n(t)=e^{-t/4}p_n(t)$ with $p_n$ a polynomial of degree $n-1$ (for example $k_1(t)=e^{-t/4}$ and $k_2(t)=(4-t)e^{-t/4}$).
With no hypothesis, $\lambda_n=\int_0^\infty k_n(t)W(t)\,dt=m_0\,\mathbb{E}k_n(A)$. Question. Which unconditional properties of $W$, or of $A$, force $\mathbb{E}k_n(A)\ge0$ for every $n$, which is the Riemann Hypothesis by Li's criterion? Positivity of $W$ gives $n=1$; complete monotonicity of $W$, which is equivalent to RH, gives every $n$, since $\varphi_n\ge0$ on $(0,\infty)$.
results.label: pk:prob:li

results.name: Open problem on the ladder index along the de Bruijn Newman flow
results.summary: It is an open problem to describe the ladder index of the laws with Laplace transform $R_t$ along the de Bruijn Newman flow, which numerically drops from two to one between $t=27.8$ and $t=27.9$, and to decide whether it is nonincreasing in $t$ and equal to one for all large $t$.
results.statement:
Let $\Phi$ be the Pólya kernel, with $\xi(\tfrac12+i\theta)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(v)\cos(\theta v)\,dv$ for the completed Riemann zeta function $\xi$, let $\Phi_t(v)=e^{tv^2/4}\Phi(v)$, $\Xi_t(\theta)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi_t(v)\cos(\theta v)\,dv$ and $R_t(s)=\Xi_t(0)/\Xi_t(i\sqrt s)$, so that $R_0(s)=\xi(\tfrac12)/\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt s)$ is the Laplace transform of the clock. The zeros of $\Xi_t$ are all real exactly when $t\ge\Lambda$, where $\Lambda$ is the de Bruijn Newman constant, $0\le\Lambda\le0.2$ (Rodgers and Tao; Platt and Trudgian). For $t\ge\Lambda$, in particular unconditionally for every $t\ge0.2$, let $\pm\theta_k(t)$, $0<\theta_1(t)<\theta_2(t)<\cdots$, be the zeros of $\Xi_t$ and $a_k(t)=\theta_k(t)^2$; then $R_t(s)=\prod_k(1+s/a_k(t))^{-1}$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC (generalised, or generalized, gamma convolution) with Thorin measure $\sum_k\delta_{a_k(t)}$. At $t=0$ put $a_k(0)=a_k=-(\rho_k-\tfrac12)^2$, one for each pair $\{\rho,1-\rho\}$ of zeros of $\xi$ (real when RH holds), the numbers of the clock. Put $W(x;t)=\sum_ke^{-a_k(t)x}$ and $W^{[j]}(x;t)=(-x\,\partial_x)^jW(x;t)$. A law with this Laplace transform lies in Urbanik's class $L_n$ exactly when $W^{[n+1]}(\cdot\,;t)\ge0$ on $(0,\infty)$ (the classes $L_n$: $L_0$ is the class of self decomposable laws and $L_n$ the class of laws in $L_{n-1}$ all of whose components lie in $L_{n-1}$); the index on the window $0\le-\log x\le8$ is the largest $n$ with $W^{[1]},\dots,W^{[n+1]}\ge0$ there.
Question. Describe the ladder index of $R_t$ along the de Bruijn Newman flow. A numerical computation (not certified for $t>0$) finds on the window the index two of the clock at the tested values of $t$ up to $27.8$ and the index one at the tested values $t=27.9$, $30$, $40$ and $50$. Is the index nonincreasing in $t$, and is it one for all large $t$?
results.label: pk:prob:ladder

results.name: Max representation of the L function of Ramanujan's Delta
results.summary: The completed L function of Ramanujan's cusp form Delta is the expectation of an incomplete gamma function at the random point 2 pi M*, where M* is a maximum of independent exponential variables, a representation with no signs.
results.statement: Let $E_{n,j}$, $n\ge1$, $1\le j\le24$, be independent exponential random variables, $E_{n,j}$ of rate $2\pi n$, and let $M^*=\sup_{n,j}E_{n,j}$ (almost surely attained and finite, with $\Pr(M^*\le y)=\prod_{n\ge1}(1-e^{-2\pi ny})^{24}$ for $y>0$). Let $\Delta(z)=\eta(z)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)e^{2\pi inz}$ be Ramanujan's cusp form, $\eta$ Dedekind's eta function, $L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-s-11/2}$ its L function, normalised so that the critical line is $\operatorname{Re}s=\frac12$, and $\xi(s,\Delta)=(2\pi)^{-s-11/2}\Gamma(s+\frac{11}2)L(s,\Delta)$ its completed function. With $\Gamma(a,x)=\int_x^\infty e^{-v}v^{a-1}\,dv$ and $Q(a,x)=\Gamma(a,x)/\Gamma(a)$, for every complex $s$, $\xi(s,\Delta)=(2\pi)^{-s-11/2}\,\mathbb{E}\,\Gamma(s+\frac{11}2,2\pi M^*)$ and $L(s,\Delta)=\mathbb{E}\,Q(s+\frac{11}2,2\pi M^*)$, and both expectations converge absolutely. In particular $L(s,\Delta)=0$ at the points $s=-\frac{11}2-k$, $k=0,1,2,\dots$, where $Q(-k,x)=0$.
results.label: thm:maxexp:max

results.name: Gamma mixture and mixed Poisson forms of L values of Delta
results.summary: For real s above minus 11/2 the L value of Ramanujan's Delta is the probability that a gamma variable exceeds 2 pi M*, and at the points s equal to k minus 11/2 it is a mixed Poisson probability.
results.statement: Let $M^*$ be the maximum of independent exponential random variables, $24$ of each rate $2\pi n$, $n\ge1$, with distribution function $F(y)=\prod_{n\ge1}(1-e^{-2\pi ny})^{24}$, and let $L(s,\Delta)$ be the L function of Ramanujan's cusp form $\Delta$, normalised so that the critical line is $\operatorname{Re}s=\frac12$. Let $G_a$ be a gamma variable of shape $a>0$ and scale one and $N$ a Poisson process of unit rate, both independent of $M^*$. For real $s>-\frac{11}2$, with $a=s+\frac{11}2$, $L(s,\Delta)=\Pr(G_a>2\pi M^*)=\mathbb{E}\,F(G_a/2\pi)=\mathbb{E}\prod_{n\ge1}(1-e^{-nG_a})^{24}$, and for every integer $k\ge1$, $L(k-\frac{11}2,\Delta)=\Pr\big(N(2\pi M^*)\le k-1\big)=\mathbb{E}\Big[e^{-2\pi M^*}\sum_{j<k}\frac{(2\pi M^*)^j}{j!}\Big]$.
results.label: cor:maxexp:forms

results.name: L values of Delta and chi12 as infinitely divisible probabilities
results.summary: By Kristiansen's theorem on Gamma(2) mixtures and the theorem of Goldie and Steutel on exponential mixtures, the L values of Ramanujan's Delta at real s between minus 11/2 and minus 7/2 and of the character chi12 at real s between 0 and 4 are probabilities that an infinitely divisible variable exceeds one.
results.statement: Let $M^*$ be the maximum of independent exponential random variables, $24$ of each rate $2\pi n$, $n\ge1$, and for real $a>0$ let $G_a$ be a gamma variable of shape $a$ and scale one independent of $M^*$ and $V_a=G_a/(2\pi M^*)$. Let $L(s,\Delta)$ be the L function of Ramanujan's cusp form $\Delta$, normalised so that the critical line is $\operatorname{Re}s=\frac12$. Then $V_a$ is a scale mixture of Gamma($a$) laws, the mixing law being that of $1/(2\pi M^*)$, and $L(a-\frac{11}2,\Delta)=\Pr(V_a>1)$. For $0<a\le2$, that is $-\frac{11}2<s\le-\frac72$, $V_a$ is infinitely divisible. In the same way, with $M_1$ the maximum of independent exponential random variables, one of each rate $2\pi n$, $n\ge1$, $G_{s/2}$ a gamma variable of shape $s/2$ and scale one independent of $M_1$ and $\chi_{12}$ the real primitive character modulo $12$ (equal to $1$ at $\pm1$ and to $-1$ at $\pm5$ modulo $12$), $L(s,\chi_{12})=\Pr\big(12G_{s/2}/(\pi M_1)>1\big)$ for real $s>0$, where $12G_{s/2}/(\pi M_1)$ is infinitely divisible for $s\le4$, and is a mixture of exponential laws for $s\le2$, in particular at the centre $s=\frac12$.
results.label: prop:maxexp:krist

results.name: RH is equivalent to a Gamma(k) scale mixture form of the clock canonical function, and the Kolmogorov law
results.summary: For every integer k at least one, the Riemann hypothesis holds if and only if t to the power k minus one times the canonical function of the clock is proportional to a scale mixture of Gamma(k) densities, with an explicit discrete mixing law under RH, infinitely divisible for k equal to one and two but not a GGC.
results.statement: Let $W(t)=\sum_{\operatorname{Re}\gamma>0}e^{-t\gamma^2}$ be the canonical function of the clock $T$, whose Lévy density is $W(t)/t$, the sum running over the zeros $\gamma$ of $\xi(\frac12+iz)$ with multiplicity. For every integer $k\ge1$, the Riemann hypothesis holds if and only if $t^{k-1}W(t)$ is proportional to a scale mixture of Gamma$(k)$ densities. The proof is that RH is equivalent to the complete monotonicity of $W$, that is $W(t)=\int e^{-tz}U(dz)$ with $U\ge0$ (Bernstein's theorem), and that a Gamma$(k)$ scale mixture divided by $t^{k-1}$ is completely monotone. Under RH the law with density proportional to $t^{k-1}W(t)$ is that of $G_k/\gamma_J^2$ with $G_k$ a Gamma$(k)$ variable independent of $J$ and $\Pr(J=\gamma)$ proportional to $\gamma^{-2k}$. For $k=1$ it is a mixture of exponential laws, infinitely divisible by the theorem of Goldie and Steutel; for $k=2$ it is the Kolmogorov law of $T$ with density $tW(t)/\operatorname{Var}T$, infinitely divisible by Kristiansen's theorem. Neither is a GGC. Kristiansen's theorem applies only once the Gamma(2) mixture is known, which is RH itself. Credited to a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book.
results.label: rem:maxexp:kolmogorov

results.name: Laplace transform of the maximum M1 of exponentials in closed form
results.summary: The Laplace transform of the maximum of independent exponential variables with rates 2 pi n is an explicit ratio of a sine and a cosine, equal to an infinite product over the numbers b_n = pi (n squared minus 1)/12.
results.statement: Let $M_1$ be the maximum of independent exponential random variables, one of each rate $2\pi n$, $n\ge1$, so that $\Pr(M_1\le y)=\prod_{n\ge1}(1-e^{-2\pi ny})$ for $y>0$, and put $b_n=\pi(n^2-1)/12$. For $\theta>0$ let $w=\sqrt{1-12\theta/\pi}$, positive or purely imaginary. Then $\mathbb{E}e^{-\theta M_1}=\frac{\pi(1-w^2)\sin(\pi w/3)}{2\sqrt3\,w\cos(\pi w/2)}=\prod_{k\ge1}\frac{1+\theta/b_{6k}}{(1+\theta/b_{6k-1})(1+\theta/b_{6k+1})}$.
results.label: prop:ch16:M1

results.name: A discrete mixture of Gamma(k) laws with two rates is not a GGC
results.summary: A finite or infinite discrete mixture of Gamma(k) laws with a positive integer k and at least two distinct rates is not a generalized gamma convolution.
results.statement: Let $k$ be a positive integer and $\varphi(z)=\sum_nw_n(1+z/\lambda_n)^{-k}$ the Laplace transform of a mixture of Gamma$(k)$ laws with rates $\lambda_1<\lambda_2<\cdots$ (finitely many, or tending to infinity), at least two of them, and weights $w_n>0$ summing to one. Then the law is not a generalized gamma convolution. The proof: $\varphi$ is meromorphic with a pole of order $k$ at each $-\lambda_n$; if it were a GGC transform, $-\varphi'/\varphi=a+\int U(dt)/(z+t)$ with $a\ge0$ and $U\ge0$ would be holomorphic off $(-\infty,0]$ with poles of positive residue, so $\varphi$ would have no zeros, $U=k\sum_n\delta_{\lambda_n}$ and $\varphi(z)=e^{-az}\prod_n(1+z/\lambda_n)^{-k}\le(1+z/\lambda_1)^{-k}(1+z/\lambda_2)^{-k}$ for $z>0$, contradicting $\varphi(z)\ge w_1(1+z/\lambda_1)^{-k}$ as $z\to\infty$. Credited to a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book.
results.label: res:maxexp:nonggc

results.name: The completed zeta function as the Mellin transform of an infinitely divisible Gamma(2) mixture, not a GGC
results.summary: With no hypothesis, the completed zeta function for real part of s above one is a normalised Mellin transform of a Gamma(2) scale mixture over the zeta law, which is infinitely divisible by Kristiansen's theorem and not a GGC.
results.statement: Let $N$ have the zeta law $\Pr(N=n)=n^{-4}/\zeta(4)$, let $G_2$ be a Gamma(2) variable independent of $N$, and put $Q=G_2/(\pi N^2)$. Then $Q$ has density $\frac{\pi^2}{\zeta(4)}x\omega(x)$ with $\omega(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}e^{-\pi n^2x}$, $\mathbb{E}Q^q=\Gamma(q+2)\pi^{-q}\zeta(2q+4)/\zeta(4)$, and for $\operatorname{Re}s>1$, $\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)\zeta(s)=\frac{\pi^2}{90}\mathbb{E}[Q^{s/2-2}]$ and $\xi(s)=\frac{\pi^2}{180}s(s-1)\mathbb{E}[Q^{s/2-2}]$, a normalisation of Riemann's integral $\int_0^\infty x^{s/2-1}\omega(x)dx$; beyond $\operatorname{Re}s>1$ the identities hold after continuation, not as expectations. So $Q$ is a scale mixture of Gamma(2) laws and infinitely divisible by Kristiansen's theorem, and, being a discrete mixture of Gamma(2) laws with the rates $\pi n^2$, not a GGC. Credited to a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book.
results.label: res:maxexp:zetaq

results.name: Rényi type decomposition of the maximum M1 of exponentials
results.summary: The maximum of independent exponential variables with rates 2 pi n is a sum of independent exponential variables whose rates are b_{6k-1} or b_{6k+1} with explicit probabilities p_k that decrease to one half.
results.statement: Let $M_1$ be the maximum of independent exponential random variables, one of each rate $2\pi n$, $n\ge1$, and $b_n=\pi(n^2-1)/12$. Then $M_1\overset{d}{=}\sum_{k\ge1}Y_k$ with independent $Y_k$, where $Y_k$ is exponential of rate $b_{6k-1}$ with probability $p_k$ and of rate $b_{6k+1}$ with probability $1-p_k$, and $p_k=\big(1-\frac{b_{6k-1}}{b_{6k}}\big)\frac{b_{6k+1}}{b_{6k+1}-b_{6k-1}}=\frac{(12k-1)(3k+1)}{2(36k^2-1)}$, so that $p_1=\frac{22}{35}$, $p_2=\frac{161}{286}$, and $p_k\downarrow\frac12$.
results.label: cor:maxexp:renyi

results.name: Lévy density and Bondesson function of the maximum M1
results.summary: The Lévy density of the maximum M1 has an explicit theta function form with stated behaviour at zero and infinity, and its Bondesson function N_1 is nonnegative and grows like a constant times the square root of z.
results.statement:
Let $M_1$ be the maximum of independent exponential random variables, one of each rate $2\pi n$, $n\ge1$, and $b_n=\pi(n^2-1)/12$. Put $a(n)=1$ for $n\equiv\pm1\pmod6$, $a(n)=-1$ for $6\mid n$ and $a(n)=0$ otherwise, $k_1(t)=\sum_{n\ge2}a(n)e^{-b_nt}$, so that $-\log\mathbb{E}e^{-	heta M_1}=\int_0^\infty(1-e^{-	heta t})\,
u_1(t)\,dt$ with the Lévy density $
u_1(t)=k_1(t)/t$ (the canonical function of $M_1$ is $k_1$), and let $U_1=\sum_{n\ge2}a(n)\delta_{b_n}$ be the signed Thorin measure of $M_1$ and $N_1(z)=U_1((0,z])$ its Bondesson function. Then $k_1(t)= rac12e^{\pi t/12}\Big(1+ rac{\vartheta_0-3\vartheta_{1/2}-4\vartheta_{1/3}}{\sqrt{3t}}\Big)-1$ with $\vartheta_\alpha=\sum_{m\in\mathbb{Z}}e^{-12\pi(m+\alpha)^2/t}$, so that $
u_1(t)=(2\sqrt3)^{-1}t^{-3/2}-(2t)^{-1}+O(t^{-1/2})$ as $t\downarrow0$ and $
u_1(t)\sim e^{-2\pi t}/t$ as $t	o\infty$. Moreover $N_1(z)\ge0$ for all $z>0$, and $N_1(z)\sim rac13\sqrt{3z/\pi}$ as $z	o\infty$.
results.label: prop:maxexp:levy

results.name: Thorin measure of M1 as a difference of two GGC Thorin measures
results.summary: The maximum M1 plus an independent GGC Z has the law of a second GGC S, so the signed Thorin measure of M1 is the difference of two positive measures with unit atoms.
results.statement: Let $b_n=\pi(n^2-1)/12$, let $E_n$ and $E'_m$ be independent standard exponential variables, $S=\sum_{n\text{ odd},\,n\ge3}E_n/b_n$ and $Z=\sum_{m\ge1}E'_m/b_{3m}$, with $Z$ independent of $M_1$, the maximum of independent exponential random variables, one of each rate $2\pi n$, $n\ge1$. Then $S$ and $Z$ are GGCs (generalised gamma convolutions: laws on $[0,\infty)$ with Laplace transform $\exp(-d\theta-\int\log(1+\theta/z)\,U(dz))$ for a drift $d\ge0$ and a positive measure $U$, the Thorin measure), with $\mathbb{E}e^{-\theta S}=\frac\pi4\,\frac{1-w^2}{\cos(\pi w/2)}$ and $\mathbb{E}e^{-\theta Z}=\frac{\sqrt3\,w/2}{\sin(\pi w/3)}$, where $w=\sqrt{1-12\theta/\pi}$, and $M_1+Z\overset{d}{=}S$. Equivalently, the signed Thorin measure of $M_1$, the signed measure $U_1=\sum_{n\ge2}a(n)\delta_{b_n}$ with $-\log\mathbb{E}e^{-\theta M_1}=\int\log(1+\theta/z)\,U_1(dz)$, where $a(n)=1$ for $n\equiv\pm1\pmod6$, $a(n)=-1$ for $6\mid n$ and $a(n)=0$ otherwise, equals $U_S-U_Z$ with $U_S=\sum_{n\text{ odd},\,n\ge3}\delta_{b_n}$ and $U_Z=\sum_{m\ge1}\delta_{b_{3m}}$, the atoms at $b_{3m}$ with $m$ odd cancelling.
results.label: thm:maxexp:ggc

results.name: Certified zeros of the Laplace transform of the maximum M* of exponentials
results.summary: Certified in ball arithmetic: the Laplace transform of M* changes sign in each of 25 gaps between its poles, and has exactly one zero near each of ten nonreal points, so it has zeros off the real axis.
results.statement: Let $M^*$ be the maximum of independent exponential random variables, $24$ of each rate $2\pi n$, $n\ge1$, let $\tau(n)$ be Ramanujan's tau function (the coefficients of $\Delta=\eta^{24}$), and let $\psi^*(\theta)=\mathbb{E}e^{-\theta M^*}$, which extends to a meromorphic function of $\theta\in\mathbb{C}$ with poles only at $\theta=-2\pi m$, $m\ge1$ (simple, with residue $-2\pi m\,\tau(m+1)$). (1) For each of the $25$ values $m\le60$ with $\tau(m+1)\tau(m+2)>0$, $\psi^*$ changes sign in an interval of length $2\times10^{-20}$ inside the gap $(-2\pi(m+1),-2\pi m)$; the zeros begin $\theta/2\pi=-5.48830041$, $-8.66373325$, $-11.4203774$, $-13.2533839$, $-14.7973058$, and the last is $-60.7670708$. (2) $\psi^*$ has exactly one zero in the disc of radius $10^{-7}$ about each of the ten points $-155.5940822775511402804\pm2.7631188861212609656\,i$, $-215.6211277570694988944\pm2.9647292148515237348\,i$, $-307.4008549057072052743\pm3.2283287024583906394\,i$, $-322.6135369899940182007\pm3.0449254921259967464\,i$, $-347.8816009468099010890\pm2.7171007701068929577\,i$, and it lies within $10^{-19}$ of that point.
results.label: prop:maxexp:psizeros

results.name: The maximum M* of exponentials is not in the Bondesson class
results.summary: The maximum of independent exponential variables with 24 variables of each rate 2 pi n is not in the Bondesson class and so is not a GGC, because its Laplace transform has nonreal zeros.
results.statement: Let $M^*$ be the maximum of independent exponential random variables, $24$ of each rate $2\pi n$, $n\ge1$. Then $M^*$ is not in the Bondesson class BO (the infinitely divisible laws on $[0,\infty)$ with a completely monotone Lévy density, and a drift $d\ge0$); in particular $M^*$ is not a generalised gamma convolution.
results.label: cor:maxexp:notBO

results.name: Open question on infinite divisibility of maxima of exponentials
results.summary: Is every maximum of independent exponential variables infinitely divisible, and in particular is the maximum M* with 24 variables of each rate 2 pi n?
results.statement: Is every maximum of independent exponential random variables infinitely divisible? In particular, is $M^*$ infinitely divisible, where $M^*$ is the maximum of independent exponential random variables, $24$ of each rate $2\pi n$, $n\ge1$?
results.label: q:maxexp:id

results.name: Open question on real zeros of cosh kernels with exponential multipliers
results.summary: For which parameters does the Fourier transform of the kernel exp(-a cosh u) times an exponential multiplier have only real zeros, a form shared by the kernels of Ramanujan's Delta, chi12 and the conductor 11 curve?
results.statement: For which $a>0$, $c_m\ge0$ and $\beta_m>0$ does the Fourier transform of $e^{-a\cosh u}\exp\Big(-\sum_mc_m\big(e^{-\beta_me^u}+e^{-\beta_me^{-u}}\big)\Big)$ have only real zeros? (The kernels of the completed L functions of Ramanujan's cusp form, of the character $\chi_{12}$ and of the elliptic curve of conductor $11$ have this form.)
results.label: q:maxexp:mult

results.name: Pólya kernel of an imaginary quadratic field
results.summary: The completed Dedekind zeta function of an imaginary quadratic field is the two sided Laplace transform of an even doubly exponentially decaying kernel, which is positive exactly when a one variable function is positive on a finite interval, in particular for the discriminants minus 3, minus 4, minus 7 and minus 8.
results.statement: Let $d<0$ be a fundamental discriminant, $K=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt d)$, $\chi_d$ the Kronecker symbol of $d$ (a real primitive odd character modulo $|d|$), $h$ the class number of $K$ and $w$ the number of roots of unity in $K$. Let $\zeta_K(s)=\zeta(s)L(s,\chi_d)=\sum_{n\ge1}a_nn^{-s}$, where $a_n=\sum_{m\mid n}\chi_d(m)\ge0$ is the number of ideals of norm $n$, and put $\Lambda_K(s)=(\sqrt{|d|}/2\pi)^s\Gamma(s)\zeta_K(s)$, $\xi_K(s)=2s(s-1)\Lambda_K(s)$, $\vartheta_K(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}a_ne^{-2\pi nx/\sqrt{|d|}}$, $\Psi(y)=y(y-2)e^{-y}$, $H_K(x)=(x^2\vartheta_K'(x))'$ and $\Phi_K(u)=2e^{u/2}H_K(e^u)$. Then (i) $\vartheta_K(1/x)=x\,\vartheta_K(x)+\frac hw(x-1)$ for $x>0$. (ii) $H_K(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}a_n\Psi(2\pi nx/\sqrt{|d|})$ and $H_K(1/x)=x\,H_K(x)$; the kernel $\Phi_K$ is even, analytic in the strip $|\operatorname{Im}u|<\frac\pi2$ and decays doubly exponentially. (iii) $\xi_K(\frac12+s)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi_K(u)e^{su}\,du$ for every $s\in\mathbb{C}$; in particular $\xi_K(\frac12+i\theta)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi_K(u)\cos(\theta u)\,du$. (iv) $\Phi_K>0$ on $\mathbb{R}$ if and only if $H_K>0$ on $[1,\sqrt{|d|}/\pi]$; in particular $\Phi_K>0$ when $|d|<\pi^2$, that is for $d=-3,-4,-7,-8$. (v) If $\Phi_K>0$, then $\zeta_K(\frac12)<0$ and $L(\frac12,\chi_d)>0$; in particular $L(\frac12,\chi_d)>0$ for $d=-3,-4,-7,-8$.
results.label: thm:sqfree:kernelK

results.name: Pólya kernel of an imaginary quadratic field takes negative values when 2 and 3 are inert
results.summary: For every negative fundamental discriminant d congruent to 5 modulo 24 the Pólya kernel of Q(sqrt d) takes negative values, by an explicit evaluation of a finite sum with a bounded tail, and there are infinitely many such d.
results.statement: For a fundamental discriminant $d<0$ let $K=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt d)$, $\chi_d$ the Kronecker symbol of $d$, $a_n=\sum_{m\mid n}\chi_d(m)$ the number of ideals of norm $n$ in $K$, $\vartheta_K(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}a_ne^{-2\pi nx/\sqrt{|d|}}$, $H_K(x)=(x^2\vartheta_K'(x))'$ and $\Phi_K(u)=2e^{u/2}H_K(e^u)$ the Pólya kernel of $K$ (the kernel with $\xi_K(\frac12+s)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi_K(u)e^{su}\,du$ for the completed Dedekind zeta function $\xi_K$), and let $K_{\chi_d}(u)=2e^{3u/2}\sum_{n\ge1}n\chi_d(n)e^{-\pi n^2e^{2u}/|d|}$ be the kernel of the odd character $\chi_d$, with $\xi(\frac12+s,\chi_d)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}K_{\chi_d}(u)e^{su}\,du$ for $\xi(s,\chi_d)=(|d|/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)L(s,\chi_d)$. Let $d<0$ be a fundamental discriminant with $\chi_d(2)=\chi_d(3)=-1$, that is $d\equiv5\pmod{24}$. Then $H_K(x)<0$ at $x=1.42\sqrt{|d|}/2\pi$, so $\Phi_K$ takes negative values, and so does the kernel $K_{\chi_d}$. There are infinitely many such $d$, for instance $d=-p$ for every prime $p\equiv19\pmod{24}$.
results.label: thm:sqfree:inert

results.name: Open question on the density of positive Pólya kernels
results.summary: Does the proportion of imaginary quadratic fields with a positive Pólya kernel tend to a limit, is the limit positive, and is the kernel positive for infinitely many fields in which 2 and 3 split?
results.statement: For a fundamental discriminant $d<0$ let $\Phi_K$ be the Pólya kernel of $K=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt d)$, the even kernel with $\xi_K(\frac12+s)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi_K(u)e^{su}\,du$ for the completed Dedekind zeta function $\xi_K(s)=2s(s-1)(\sqrt{|d|}/2\pi)^s\Gamma(s)\zeta_K(s)$. Does the proportion of fundamental discriminants $-X\le d<0$ with $\Phi_K>0$ tend to a limit as $X\to\infty$, and is the limit positive? Is $\Phi_K$ positive for infinitely many $d$, for instance among the $d$ in which $2$ and $3$ split (that is, $\chi_d(2)=\chi_d(3)=1$ for the Kronecker symbol $\chi_d$), where the proportion up to $20000$ is $676/767$?
results.label: q:sqfree:density

results.name: Open question on positivity criteria for real quadratic fields
results.summary: Is there a criterion for positivity of the Pólya kernel of the Dedekind zeta function of a real quadratic field or a field of higher degree that is as simple as the one for imaginary quadratic fields?
results.statement: For a number field $K$ with $r_1$ real and $r_2$ complex places the completed Dedekind zeta function $\xi_K$ has the gamma factor $\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)^{r_1}\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)^{r_2}$, with $\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)$ and $\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)=2(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)$, and its Pólya kernel is the kernel $\Phi_K$ with $\xi_K(\frac12+s)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi_K(u)e^{su}\,du$. For real quadratic fields and for fields of higher degree the gamma factor replaces the exponentials in the theta series of an imaginary quadratic field by other kernels, for $\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)^2$ by a Bessel function $K_0$. For an imaginary quadratic field of discriminant $d$, $\Phi_K>0$ on $\mathbb{R}$ if and only if $H_K>0$ on $[1,\sqrt{|d|}/\pi]$ for an explicit function $H_K$ of one variable. Is there a criterion for the positivity of the Pólya kernel of $\xi_K$ for real quadratic fields and for fields of higher degree that is as simple as this one?
results.label: q:sqfree:realquad

results.name: Lévy form of the Dirichlet beta function at basepoints from one
results.summary: The logarithm of the completed Dirichlet beta function at every basepoint alpha at least one has a Lévy form whose signed Lévy measure is an explicit positive gamma density plus prime power atoms of both signs.
results.statement: Let $L(s,\chi_4)=\sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^n(2n+1)^{-s}$ be the Dirichlet beta function ($\chi_4$ the nonprincipal character modulo $4$), $\xi(s,\chi_4)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)L(s,\chi_4)$ its completed function (entire, with $\xi(s,\chi_4)=\xi(1-s,\chi_4)$) and $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function. For $\alpha\ge1$, $\log\frac{\xi(\alpha+s,\chi_4)}{\xi(\alpha,\chi_4)}=b_\alpha s+\int_0^\infty\big(e^{-sx}-1+sx\big)\,\Pi_\alpha(dx)$ with $b_\alpha=\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\alpha,\chi_4)$ and the signed Lévy measure $\Pi_\alpha(dx)=\frac{e^{-\alpha x}}{2x\sinh x}\,dx+\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\chi_4(n)\Lambda(n)}{n^\alpha\log n}\,\delta_{\log n}(dx)$, whose canonical measure $x\Pi_\alpha(dx)$ has the positive density $e^{-\alpha x}/(2\sinh x)$ and the atoms $\chi_4(n)\Lambda(n)n^{-\alpha}$ at $\log n$. For $\alpha>1$ the form holds for $\operatorname{Re}s>1-\alpha$, with absolute convergence. At $\alpha=1$ it holds for $\operatorname{Re}s>0$, the prime sum converging conditionally, as a limit over $n\le X$.
results.label: prop:dbeta:levy

results.name: Thorin measure of the Dirichlet beta function from basepoint one
results.summary: For every basepoint alpha at least one the reciprocal of the completed Dirichlet beta function is the Laplace transform of a GGC with a positive explicit Thorin density, and, by Lagarias's criterion, GRH for chi4 is equivalent to the positivity of that density at every alpha above one half.
results.statement: Let $L(s,\chi_4)=\sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^n(2n+1)^{-s}$ be the Dirichlet beta function, $\xi(s,\chi_4)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)L(s,\chi_4)$ its completed function and $v_\alpha(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\alpha+i\theta,\chi_4)$. For every $\alpha\ge1$, $u\mapsto\xi(\alpha,\chi_4)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt u,\chi_4)$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution whose Thorin measure has, in the chart $\theta=\sqrt z$, the positive density $v_\alpha(\theta)/\pi$ (that is, it is the image of $v_\alpha(\theta)\,d\theta/\pi$ under $\theta\mapsto\theta^2$), and $\log\frac{\xi(\alpha+\sqrt u,\chi_4)}{\xi(\alpha,\chi_4)}=\frac1\pi\int_0^\infty\log\Big(1+\frac u{\theta^2}\Big)v_\alpha(\theta)\,d\theta$ for $u\ge0$. For $\alpha>\frac12$ it is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution if and only if no zero of $L(s,\chi_4)$ has real part greater than $\alpha$. GRH for $\chi_4$ holds if and only if $v_\alpha\ge0$ for every $\alpha>\frac12$, and the Thorin measures at resolution $\varepsilon=\alpha-\frac12$ converge vaguely, as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, to the sum of the point masses $\delta_{\gamma^2}$ over the zeros $\frac12+i\gamma$ of $L(s,\chi_4)$ on the critical line (under GRH this sum is the Thorin measure of $\xi(\frac12,\chi_4)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u,\chi_4)$).
results.label: prop:dbeta:thorin

results.name: Termwise positivity thresholds for the Dirichlet beta function and chi12
results.summary: Bounding the prime weights by their absolute values gives a positive Thorin density exactly for basepoints above 2.2823106368 for the Dirichlet beta function and above 1.8348743295 for chi12, thresholds located by bisection with certified signs.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s,\chi_4)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)L(s,\chi_4)$ be the completed Dirichlet beta function, $v_\alpha(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\alpha+i\theta,\chi_4)$, $\psi=\Gamma'/\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function. For $\alpha>1$ and real $\theta$, $v_\alpha(\theta)\ge A^\infty_4(\alpha,\theta)-S_4(\alpha)$, where $A^\infty_4(\alpha,\theta)=\frac12\log\frac4\pi+\frac12\operatorname{Re}\psi\Big(\frac{\alpha+1+i\theta}2\Big)$ and $S_4(\alpha)=\sum_{n\text{ odd}}\frac{\Lambda(n)}{n^\alpha}=-\frac{\zeta'}\zeta(\alpha)-\frac{\log2}{2^\alpha-1}$, and $A^\infty_4(\alpha,\theta)$ increases in $|\theta|$. The bound is positive at every $\theta$ exactly when $\alpha>\alpha_c(\chi_4)=2.2823106368$, the root of $A^\infty_4(\alpha,0)=S_4(\alpha)$. For the real primitive character $\chi_{12}$ modulo $12$, with $\xi(s,\chi_{12})=(12/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)L(s,\chi_{12})$ and $v_\alpha(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\alpha+i\theta,\chi_{12})$, the same bound with $A^\infty_{12}(\alpha,\theta)=\frac12\log\frac{12}\pi+\frac12\operatorname{Re}\psi\Big(\frac{\alpha+i\theta}2\Big)$ and $S_{12}(\alpha)=S_4(\alpha)-\frac{\log3}{3^\alpha-1}$ is positive at every $\theta$ exactly when $\alpha>\alpha_c(\chi_{12})=1.8348743295$.
results.label: prop:dbeta:termwise

results.name: No bound from the sizes of the prime weights beats the absolute values
results.summary: By Kronecker's theorem no lower bound for the real part of L'/L of the Dirichlet beta function better than minus the sum of the absolute weights holds at all large heights, and the height from which the termwise bound works grows like e to the power 2/(alpha minus 1).
results.statement: Let $L(s,\chi_4)=\sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^n(2n+1)^{-s}$ be the Dirichlet beta function, $\xi(s,\chi_4)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)L(s,\chi_4)$ its completed function, $v_\alpha(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\alpha+i\theta,\chi_4)$, $A^\infty_4(\alpha,\theta)=\frac12\log\frac4\pi+\frac12\operatorname{Re}\psi\big(\frac{\alpha+1+i\theta}2\big)$ with $\psi=\Gamma'/\Gamma$, and $S_4(\alpha)=\sum_{n\text{ odd}}\Lambda(n)n^{-\alpha}$ with $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function. For $\alpha>1$ and every $T>0$, $\inf_{\theta\ge T}\big(v_\alpha(\theta)-A^\infty_4(\alpha,\theta)\big)=\inf_{\theta\ge T}\operatorname{Re}\frac{L'}L(\alpha+i\theta,\chi_4)=-S_4(\alpha)$, so no lower bound for $\operatorname{Re}\frac{L'}L(\alpha+i\theta,\chi_4)$ better than $-S_4(\alpha)$ holds at all large heights. The bound $v_\alpha\ge A^\infty_4-S_4$ yields $v_\alpha(\theta)>0$ exactly for $|\theta|>t_0(\alpha)$, where $A^\infty_4(\alpha,t_0)=S_4(\alpha)$, for $1<\alpha\le\alpha_c$ (so that $t_0(\alpha_c)=0$), and at every real $\theta$ for $\alpha>\alpha_c$, with $\alpha_c=2.2823106368$ the threshold at which $A^\infty_4(\alpha,0)=S_4(\alpha)$, and $\log t_0(\alpha)=\frac2{\alpha-1}-2\gamma_E-\log\frac8\pi+O(\alpha-1)$ as $\alpha\downarrow1$, where $\gamma_E$ is Euler's constant and $-2\gamma_E-\log\frac8\pi=-2.0891$.
results.label: prop:dbeta:kron

results.name: Thorin density of the Dirichlet beta function as a difference over the Gaussian field
results.summary: On every vertical line the Thorin density of the Dirichlet beta function is the difference of the Thorin densities of the Dedekind zeta function of Q(i) and of Riemann's xi function, and the canonical measures subtract in the same way.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)\zeta(s)$, let $\xi(s,\chi_4)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)L(s,\chi_4)$ be the completed Dirichlet beta function, $K=\mathbb{Q}(i)$ with $\zeta_K(s)=\zeta(s)L(s,\chi_4)$, and $\xi_K(s)=2s(s-1)\pi^{-s}\Gamma(s)\zeta_K(s)=\xi(s)\,\xi(s,\chi_4)$. Write $v^K_\alpha(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi_K'}{\xi_K}(\alpha+i\theta)$, $v^\xi_\alpha(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\alpha+i\theta)$ and $v_\alpha(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\alpha+i\theta,\chi_4)$. On every vertical line, $v_\alpha=v^K_\alpha-v^\xi_\alpha$. For $\alpha>1$ the canonical measure of the Lévy form of $\xi_K$ at the basepoint $\alpha$ is $x\Pi^K_\alpha(dx)=\Big(\frac{e^{-(\alpha+1)x}}{1-e^{-x}}-e^{-(\alpha-1)x}\Big)dx+\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{(1+\chi_4(n))\Lambda(n)}{n^\alpha}\,\delta_{\log n}(dx)$, and the canonical measure $x\Pi_\alpha$ of the Lévy form of $\xi(\cdot,\chi_4)$ at $\alpha$ (with density $e^{-\alpha x}/(2\sinh x)$ and atoms $\chi_4(n)\Lambda(n)n^{-\alpha}$ at $\log n$) equals $x\Pi^K_\alpha-x\Pi^\xi_\alpha$, where $x\Pi^\xi_\alpha(dx)=\Big(\frac{e^{-(\alpha+2)x}}{1-e^{-2x}}-e^{-(\alpha-1)x}\Big)dx+\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\Lambda(n)}{n^\alpha}\,\delta_{\log n}(dx)$ is that of $\xi$: the pole densities $-e^{-(\alpha-1)x}$ cancel, the gamma densities differ by $e^{-\alpha x}/(2\sinh x)$, and the atoms by $\chi_4(n)\Lambda(n)n^{-\alpha}$. Here $\Lambda$ is the von Mangoldt function.
results.label: prop:dbeta:factor

results.name: GRH for chi4 and domination of Thorin densities over Q(i)
results.status_text: conditional on Part (iii) assumes the Riemann hypothesis for the Riemann zeta function; parts (i) and (ii) hold without any hypothesis
results.conditions: Part (iii) assumes the Riemann hypothesis for the Riemann zeta function; parts (i) and (ii) hold without any hypothesis.
results.summary: GRH for chi4 is equivalent to the Thorin density of the Dedekind zeta function of Q(i) dominating that of Riemann's xi at every basepoint, and for alpha at least one the GGC of Q(i) is the sum of independent GGCs for xi and for the Dirichlet beta function.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)\zeta(s)$, $\xi(s,\chi_4)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)L(s,\chi_4)$ the completed Dirichlet beta function, $\xi_K(s)=\xi(s)\,\xi(s,\chi_4)$ the completed Dedekind zeta function of $K=\mathbb{Q}(i)$, and $v^K_\alpha(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi_K'}{\xi_K}(\alpha+i\theta)$, $v^\xi_\alpha(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\alpha+i\theta)$. (i) For every $\alpha\ge1$ there are independent GGC variables (generalised gamma convolutions) $H^\xi_\alpha$ and $H^{(4)}_\alpha$ with Laplace transforms $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt u)$ and $\xi(\alpha,\chi_4)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt u,\chi_4)$, whose sum $H^K_\alpha=H^\xi_\alpha+H^{(4)}_\alpha$ is the GGC with Laplace transform $\xi_K(\alpha)/\xi_K(\alpha+\sqrt u)$ and Thorin density $v^K_\alpha/\pi$ (in the chart $\theta=\sqrt z$). (ii) GRH for $\chi_4$ holds if and only if $v^K_\alpha\ge v^\xi_\alpha$ on every line $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha>\frac12$: the Thorin density of $\xi_K$ dominates that of $\xi$ at every basepoint. (iii) Under the Riemann hypothesis, GRH for $\chi_4$ holds if and only if, for every $\alpha>\frac12$, $\xi_K(\alpha)/\xi_K(\alpha+\sqrt u)$ is the Laplace transform of $H^\xi_\alpha+H$ for some GGC $H$ independent of $H^\xi_\alpha$.
results.label: cor:dbeta:dom

results.name: Open question on a coupling construction over the Gaussian primes
results.summary: Is there a construction of the GGC attached to Q(i) from the Gaussian primes themselves that persists below the basepoint one?
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function, $\xi(s,\chi_4)$ the completed Dirichlet beta function, $\xi_K=\xi\cdot\xi(\cdot,\chi_4)$ the completed Dedekind zeta function of $K=\mathbb{Q}(i)$, and for $\alpha\ge1$ let $H^\xi_\alpha$ and $H^{(4)}_\alpha$ be independent generalised gamma convolutions with Laplace transforms $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt u)$ and $\xi(\alpha,\chi_4)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt u,\chi_4)$, so that $H^K_\alpha=H^\xi_\alpha+H^{(4)}_\alpha$ has Laplace transform $\xi_K(\alpha)/\xi_K(\alpha+\sqrt u)$. Is there a construction of $H^K_\alpha$ from the Gaussian primes themselves, two of norm $p$ for each prime $p\equiv1\pmod4$ and one of norm $p^2$ for each prime $p\equiv3\pmod4$, that persists below the basepoint one, that is for $\frac12<\alpha<1$? Such a construction must see the phases $p^{-i\theta}$ of the primes, not only the sizes of the weights, and below $\alpha=1$ its existence is equivalent, under the Riemann hypothesis, to GRH for $\chi_4$.
results.label: q:dbeta:coupling

results.name: Thorin mass of the Dirichlet beta function as an argument
results.summary: On a vertical line the cumulative Thorin mass of the Dirichlet beta function is the argument of the completed function divided by pi, with an asymptotic expansion that becomes the zero counting formula at the centre and a limit that counts the zeros on the critical line.
results.statement: Let $L(s,\chi_4)=\sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^n(2n+1)^{-s}$ be the Dirichlet beta function, $\xi(s,\chi_4)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)L(s,\chi_4)$ its completed function and $v_\alpha(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\alpha+i\theta,\chi_4)$. Let $\alpha>\frac12$ be such that no zero of $\xi(s,\chi_4)$ lies on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha$; this holds for every $\alpha\ge1$. Then for $\theta>0$, $\frac1\pi\int_0^\theta v_\alpha(t)\,dt=\frac1\pi\arg\xi(\alpha+i\theta,\chi_4)$, with the argument continuous along the segment from $\alpha$ to $\alpha+i\theta$ and zero at $\alpha$; for $\alpha\ge1$ the left side is the mass of $(0,\theta^2]$ under the Thorin measure of $u\mapsto\xi(\alpha,\chi_4)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt u,\chi_4)$. As $\theta\to\infty$, with $a=\frac{\alpha+1}2$, $\frac1\pi\arg\xi(\alpha+i\theta,\chi_4)=\frac\theta{2\pi}\log\frac{2\theta}{\pi e}+\frac\alpha4+\frac1\pi\arg L(\alpha+i\theta,\chi_4)-\frac{a(a-1)+\frac16}{\pi\theta}+O(\theta^{-3})$, with $\arg L$ continuous along the same segment. As $\alpha\downarrow\frac12$, for $\theta$ not an ordinate, the left side tends to the number of zeros on the critical line with $0<\gamma<\theta$, which is $N(\theta)$ under GRH; at $\alpha=\frac12$ the expansion is the counting formula $N(T)=\frac T{2\pi}\log\frac{2T}{\pi e}+\frac18+\frac1\pi\arg L(\frac12+iT,\chi_4)+\frac1{48\pi T}+O(T^{-3})$, where $N(T)$ counts the zeros of $L(s,\chi_4)$ with $0<\operatorname{Im}\rho\le T$, for $T$ not an ordinate, with $\arg L(\frac12+iT,\chi_4)$ continued from $L(2,\chi_4)>0$ along $2\to2+iT\to\frac12+iT$.
results.label: prop:dbeta:arg

results.name: GRH for chi4 and monotonicity of the argument of the completed function
results.summary: GRH for chi4 is equivalent to the argument of the completed Dirichlet beta function being nondecreasing on every line to the right of the centre, and without any hypothesis it can fall only in short windows around zeros off the line, none below height 2.5 times 10^7 by Platt's verification.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s,\chi_4)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)L(s,\chi_4)$ be the completed Dirichlet beta function. GRH for $\chi_4$ holds if and only if, for every $\alpha>\frac12$, $\theta\mapsto\arg\xi(\alpha+i\theta,\chi_4)$ (continued along the vertical line from the real point $\alpha$) is nondecreasing. With no hypothesis, the heights $\theta>0$ at which it decreases lie in the union of the windows $|\theta-\gamma|<\sqrt{\delta^2-(\alpha-\frac12)^2}$, each of length less than $1$, over the zeros $\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ of $L(s,\chi_4)$ with $\delta>\alpha-\frac12$, and there are none at heights below $2.5\times10^7-\frac12$.
results.label: cor:dbeta:argmono

results.name: The half kernel of the Dirichlet beta function is not a gamma mixture
results.summary: The half kernel of the Dirichlet beta function is not a positive mixture of gamma densities of any shape, and the theta function eta(ix) cubed is not completely monotone.
results.statement: Let $K_4(u)=2e^{3u/2}\eta(ie^{2u})^3$ be the kernel of the completed Dirichlet beta function, $\xi(\frac12+s,\chi_4)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}K_4(u)e^{su}\,du$, with $\eta$ Dedekind's eta function. For no $a>0$ is $u^{1-a}K_4(u)$ completely monotone on $u>0$; in particular the half kernel $K_4(u)\mathbf 1\{u>0\}$ is not a positive mixture of Gamma($a$) densities $u^{a-1}e^{-\lambda u}$, for any shape $a$. The theta function $\eta(ix)^3$ is not completely monotone on $x>0$.
results.label: prop:dbeta:nocm

results.name: Open question on a reciprocal side representation from the eta product
results.summary: Can the complete monotonicity of the reciprocal of the eta cube theta function, and of the reciprocal eta product for chi12, be turned into a positive representation on the reciprocal side in the spirit of Thorin?
results.statement: Let $q=e^{-2\pi x}$ and let $\eta$ be Dedekind's eta function. The function $e^{-\pi x/4}/\eta(ix)^3=\prod_{m\ge1}(1-q^m)^{-3}=\exp\Big(3\sum_{N\ge1}\sigma_{-1}(N)e^{-2\pi Nx}\Big)$ of $x>0$, with $\sigma_{-1}(N)=\sum_{d\mid N}1/d$, is completely monotone, since its logarithm is, and so is the analogue $\prod_{m\ge1}(1-q^m)^{-1}$ for the kernel of $L(s,\chi_{12})$. Can this complete monotonicity be turned into a positive representation on the reciprocal side, in the spirit of Thorin's construction for the reciprocal of a GGC transform?
results.label: q:dbeta:recip

results.name: Thorin measure of the Dedekind eta analogue at the basepoint one
results.summary: For the L function of the real character modulo 12, the reciprocal completed function at the basepoint one is the Laplace transform of a GGC with an explicit positive Thorin density, with no hypothesis.
results.statement: Let $\chi_{12}$ be the real primitive even Dirichlet character modulo $12$ ($\chi_{12}(n)=1$ for $n\equiv\pm1$ and $-1$ for $n\equiv\pm5 \pmod{12}$, and $0$ if $\gcd(n,12)>1$), $L(s,\chi_{12})$ its Dirichlet $L$ function and $\xi(s,\chi_{12})=(12/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma(s/2)L(s,\chi_{12})$ the completed function, which is entire (there is no pole to remove) and satisfies $\xi(s,\chi_{12})=\xi(1-s,\chi_{12})$. Put $v_1(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(1+i\theta,\chi_{12})$. Then $\varphi_1(u)=\xi(1,\chi_{12})/\xi(1+\sqrt{u},\chi_{12})$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) with no drift, whose Thorin measure, in the variable $\theta=\sqrt{z}$, has the density $\frac{1}{\pi}v_1(\theta)=\frac{1}{\pi}\sum_\rho\frac{1-\beta}{(1-\beta)^2+(\theta-\gamma)^2}>0$, the sum over the nontrivial zeros $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ of $L(s,\chi_{12})$, in conjugate pairs. Positivity is unconditional because $L(1+it,\chi_{12})\ne0$ for real $t$.
results.label: bp:eta:prop:thorin

results.name: Lévy form of the Dedekind eta analogue at the basepoint one
results.summary: For the completed L function of the real character modulo 12, the logarithm of $\xi(1+s,\chi_{12})/\xi(1,\chi_{12})$ has an explicit Lévy form, with a positive gamma density and prime atoms of both signs, that needs no compensation by a pole term.
results.statement: Let $\chi_{12}$ be the real primitive even Dirichlet character modulo $12$ ($\chi_{12}(n)=1$ for $n\equiv\pm1$ and $-1$ for $n\equiv\pm5 \pmod{12}$, and $0$ if $\gcd(n,12)>1$), $\xi(s,\chi_{12})=(12/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma(s/2)L(s,\chi_{12})$ the completed function of its Dirichlet $L$ function, $b_1=(\xi'/\xi)(1,\chi_{12})$ (which equals $\sum_\rho\rho^{-1}$ over the nontrivial zeros and is $0.1650833123$), $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function and $\Lambda_{\chi_{12}}(n)=\chi_{12}(n)\Lambda(n)$. For $\operatorname{Re}s>0$, $\log\frac{\xi(1+s,\chi_{12})}{\xi(1,\chi_{12})}=b_1s+\int_0^\infty(e^{-sx}-1+sx)\,\Pi(dx)$, where $\Pi(dx)=\frac{e^{-x}}{x(1-e^{-2x})}\,dx+\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\Lambda_{\chi_{12}}(n)}{n\log n}\,\delta_{\log n}(dx)$, the prime sum converging conditionally, as a limit over $n\le X$ as $X\to\infty$.
results.label: bp:eta:prop:levy

results.name: Thorin property of the tilted clock of a Dedekind zeta function at every tilt: equivalence with the position of the zeros
results.summary: For a number field and a tilt $u_0\ge0$, the tilted reciprocal of the completed Dedekind zeta function is a GGC exactly when every nontrivial zero lies on the critical line or is real at distance less than $\sqrt{u_0}$ from the centre (with no central zero when $u_0=0$), and its Thorin measure is then the zero counting measure shifted by $u_0$.
results.statement:
Let $F$ be a number field with $r_1$ real and $r_2$ complex places, discriminant $d_F$ and Dedekind zeta function $\zeta_F$. Put $\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)$, $\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)=2(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)$ and $\xi_F(s)=s(s-1)|d_F|^{s/2}\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)^{r_1}\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)^{r_2}\zeta_F(s)$; this is an entire function of order one, real on the real axis, with $\xi_F(s)=\xi_F(1-s)$, and for $F=\mathbb{Q}$ it equals $2\xi(s)$ with $\xi$ Riemann's xi function. Its zeros are the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta_F$; write them as $ho= rac12+w_ho$, put $z_ho=w_ho^2$ (one value for each pair $\{ho,1-ho\}$, with multiplicity), and let $2m_F$ be the order of vanishing of $\xi_F$ at $ rac12$. A generalized gamma convolution (GGC) is a probability law on $[0,\infty)$ whose Laplace transform is $\exp ig(-bs-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+s/t)\,U(dt) ig)$ with drift $b\ge0$ and a nonnegative Thorin measure $U$. For $u_0\ge0$ with $\xi_F( rac12+\sqrt{u_0})
e0$ put $\varphi_{F,u_0}(s)=\xi_F( rac12+\sqrt{u_0})/\xi_F( rac12+\sqrt{u_0+s})$, $s\ge0$. For $u_0\ge0$ the following are equivalent. (i) $\xi_F( rac12+\sqrt{u_0})
e0$ and $\varphi_{F,u_0}$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC. (ii) Every $z_ho$ is real with $z_ho<u_0$, and $m_F=0$ if $u_0=0$; equivalently, every nontrivial zero of $\zeta_F$ lies on the critical line or is a real zero $ eta$ with $| eta- rac12|<\sqrt{u_0}$, and $\zeta_F( rac12)
e0$ when $u_0=0$. When they hold, $b=0$ and the Thorin measure is $U_{F,u_0}=\sum_{\gamma>0}\delta_{u_0+\gamma^2}+m_F\,\delta_{u_0}+\sum_ eta\delta_{u_0-( eta- rac12)^2}$, where $ rac12+i\gamma$ runs over the zeros on the critical line with $\gamma>0$ and $ eta$ over the real zeros in $( rac12,1)$, all with multiplicity.
results.label: gl:thm:family

results.name: The tilts: Thorin property of a Dedekind zeta clock at tilt zero and at tilts above one quarter, the Thorin threshold and the shift between tilts
results.summary: The Thorin property of a Dedekind zeta function holds at every tilt $u_0\ge\frac14$ exactly when all nontrivial zeros are on the critical line or the real axis, at tilt $0$ exactly when they are all on the critical line with $\zeta_F(\frac12)\ne0$, and, when all nonreal zeros are on the line, exactly above a threshold set by the real zero farthest from the centre, with the Thorin measures at two tilts shifts of one another.
results.statement: Let $F$ be a number field with $r_1$ real and $r_2$ complex places, discriminant $d_F$ and Dedekind zeta function $\zeta_F$, and $\xi_F(s)=s(s-1)|d_F|^{s/2}\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)^{r_1}\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)^{r_2}\zeta_F(s)$ with $\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)$ and $\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)=2(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)$, an entire function, real on the real axis, with $\xi_F(s)=\xi_F(1-s)$ (it equals $2\xi$ for $F=\mathbb{Q}$). For $u_0\ge0$ put $\varphi_{F,u_0}(s)=\xi_F(\frac12+\sqrt{u_0})/\xi_F(\frac12+\sqrt{u_0+s})$, and say that the Thorin property holds at tilt $u_0$ if $\xi_F(\frac12+\sqrt{u_0})\ne0$ and $\varphi_{F,u_0}$ is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution (GGC); its Thorin measure is then written $U_{F,u_0}$ (the drift is $0$). (a) At $u_0=0$: $\xi_F(\frac12)/\xi_F(\frac12+\sqrt s)$ is a GGC Laplace transform if and only if all nontrivial zeros of $\zeta_F$ lie on the critical line and $\zeta_F(\frac12)\ne0$. (b) For every $u_0\ge\frac14$, in particular at $u_0=\frac14$ and $u_0=1$, where $\xi_F$ is read from $1$ and from $\frac32$: $\varphi_{F,u_0}$ is a GGC Laplace transform if and only if every nontrivial zero of $\zeta_F$ lies on the critical line or on the real axis. (c) Define the Thorin threshold $u^*_F=\max(\beta-\frac12)^2$ over the real zeros $\beta\in[\frac12,1)$ of $\xi_F$, with $u^*_F=0$ if there are none. If all nonreal zeros lie on the critical line, the Thorin property holds at tilt $u_0$ exactly for $u_0>u^*_F$, and also at $u_0=0$ when there are no real zeros at all. (d) When the Thorin property holds at two tilts $u_1<u_0$, the measures are shifts of one another, $U_{F,u_0}(A)=U_{F,u_1}(A-(u_0-u_1))$ for Borel sets $A$ (each atom moves to the right by $u_0-u_1$), and $\varphi_{F,u_1}(s)=\varphi_{F,u_0}(s-(u_0-u_1))/\varphi_{F,u_0}(-(u_0-u_1))$, the exponential tilt of a GGC.
results.label: gl:cor:basepoints

results.name: Closed form of the transfer function from the real axis to the critical line under RH, and its odd index power sum expansion
results.status_text: conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part $\frac12$
results.conditions: The Riemann Hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part $\frac12$.
results.summary: Under RH the transfer function $\xi(\frac12+it)/\xi(\frac12+|t|)$ equals $\prod_{\gamma>0}(\gamma^2-t^2)/(\gamma^2+t^2)$, is real, even, bounded by $1$ and vanishes exactly at the ordinates, and its logarithm near $0$ involves only the odd index power sums of the inverse squared ordinates.
results.statement: Assume the Riemann Hypothesis. Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function, let $\gamma>0$ run over the ordinates of the zeros $\frac12+i\gamma$ of $\xi$ with multiplicity, let $\gamma_1$ be the smallest of them, and put $p_j=\sum_{\gamma>0}\gamma^{-2j}$. For all real $t$, $\mathfrak T(t):=\frac{\xi(\frac12+it)}{\xi(\frac12+|t|)}=\prod_{\gamma>0}\frac{\gamma^2-t^2}{\gamma^2+t^2}$, and $\mathfrak T$ is real, even, bounded by $1$ in modulus, and vanishes exactly at $t=\pm\gamma$. For $|t|<\gamma_1$, $\log\mathfrak T(t)=-2\sum_{\gamma>0}\operatorname{artanh}\big(\frac{t^2}{\gamma^2}\big)=-2\sum_{m\ge1}\frac{p_{2m-1}}{2m-1}\,t^{4m-2}$, which involves only the odd index power sums $p_1,p_3,p_5,\dots$.
results.label: gl:prop:transfer

results.name: The odd index power sums of the inverse squared ordinates determine the zeros under RH
results.status_text: conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part $\frac12$
results.conditions: The Riemann Hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part $\frac12$.
results.summary: Under RH the generating series of the odd index power sums $p_1,p_3,p_5,\dots$ of the inverse squared ordinates continues to a meromorphic function with poles at the points $\pm\gamma^2$, so these sums determine the ordinates with multiplicities and with them every power sum.
results.statement: Assume the Riemann Hypothesis. Let $\gamma>0$ run over the ordinates of the zeros $\frac12+i\gamma$ of Riemann's xi function with multiplicity, let $\gamma_1$ be the smallest of them, and put $p_j=\sum_{\gamma>0}\gamma^{-2j}$. The series $\sum_{m\ge1}p_{2m-1}z^{2m-1}$ converges for $|z|<\gamma_1^2$ and continues to the meromorphic function $\frac12\sum_{\gamma>0}\Big(\frac{1}{1-z/\gamma^2}-\frac{1}{1+z/\gamma^2}\Big)$, whose poles are the points $\pm\gamma^2$, each with residue $-\frac12\gamma^2$ times the multiplicity of $\gamma$. Hence the odd index power sums $\{p_{2m-1}\}$ determine the ordinates $\{\gamma\}$ with multiplicities, and with them every $p_j$.
results.label: gl:prop:odd

results.name: The transfer function as a Blaschke product for the right half plane under RH
results.status_text: conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part $\frac12$
results.conditions: The Riemann Hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part $\frac12$.
results.summary: Under RH the function $\mathfrak B(z)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(\gamma^2-z)/(\gamma^2+z)$, with $\mathfrak T(t)=\mathfrak B(t^2)$ for the transfer function $\mathfrak T$, is a Blaschke product for the right half plane with zeros at the points $\gamma^2$ and no singular inner factor.
results.statement: Assume the Riemann Hypothesis. Let $\gamma>0$ run over the ordinates of the zeros $\frac12+i\gamma$ of Riemann's xi function with multiplicity, and put $\mathfrak B(z)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(\gamma^2-z)/(\gamma^2+z)$, so that the transfer function $\mathfrak T(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)/\xi(\frac12+|t|)$ equals $\mathfrak B(t^2)$. Then $\mathfrak B$ is a Blaschke product for the right half plane: the product converges there, $|\mathfrak B(z)|<1$ for $\operatorname{Re}z>0$, $|\mathfrak B(z)|=1$ for $\operatorname{Re}z=0$, its zeros are the points $\gamma^2$, and it has no singular inner factor.
results.label: gl:prop:inner

results.name: Negative moments of the centre clock as a Mellin transform of the reciprocal of xi on the real axis
results.summary: For $\operatorname{Re}s>0$ the negative moment $\mathbb{E}[T^{-s}]$ of the centre clock of $\xi$ is the Mellin transform of $\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u)$ divided by $\Gamma(s)$, with no hypothesis on the zeros.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and let $T$ be the centre clock, the positive self decomposable random variable with Laplace transform $\mathbb{E}[e^{-uT}]=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u)$ for $u\ge0$ (it exists without any hypothesis on the zeros). For $\operatorname{Re}s>0$, with no hypothesis on the zeros, $\mathbb{E}[T^{-s}]=\frac{1}{\Gamma(s)}\int_0^\infty u^{s-1}\,\frac{\xi(\frac12)}{\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u)}\,du=\frac{2\,\xi(\frac12)}{\Gamma(s)}\int_0^\infty\frac{w^{2s-1}}{\xi(\frac12+w)}\,dw$.
results.label: gl:prop:negmom

results.name: Growth of the gamma function times the reciprocal of xi on vertical strips under RH: the growth hypothesis of the master theorem class
results.status_text: conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis, used through the bound $1/\zeta(w)=O(|\operatorname{Im}w|^\eta)$ on $\operatorname{Re}w\ge\frac12+\sigma_1$ for every $\eta>0$
results.conditions: The Riemann Hypothesis, used through the bound $1/\zeta(w)=O(|\operatorname{Im}w|^\eta)$ on $\operatorname{Re}w\ge\frac12+\sigma_1$ for every $\eta>0$.
results.summary: Under RH, on vertical strips $0<\sigma_1\le\operatorname{Re}s\le\sigma_2<\frac12$ the function $\Gamma(s)\,\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+s)$ is bounded by $C_\eta e^{-\pi|\tau|/4}|\tau|^{\sigma/2-9/4+\eta}$, which verifies the growth hypothesis of the master theorem class with exponential room, but a bound proved under RH cannot be an input to a proof of the Thorin property.
results.statement: Assume the Riemann Hypothesis. Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function, $F(s;0)=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+s)$, $0<\sigma_1\le\sigma_2<\frac12$ and $\eta>0$. Then for $s=\sigma+i\tau$ with $\sigma_1\le\sigma\le\sigma_2$ and $|\tau|\ge1$, $|\Gamma(s)\,F(s;0)|\le C_\eta\,e^{-\pi|\tau|/4}\,|\tau|^{\sigma/2-9/4+\eta}$, uniformly in $\sigma$ and $\tau$ in this range. In particular the growth condition $|\Gamma(s)F(s;0)|\le C|\tau|^{\kappa(\sigma-\delta)}$ with $\kappa=1$ and $\delta=\frac12$, the growth condition of the class $Q_\infty(1,\frac12)$ (the extension by Chaudhry and Qadir (2012) of Hardy's class for Ramanujan's master theorem), holds on such strips, with exponential room. By the functional equation the same argument gives, for $-\sigma_2\le\sigma\le-\sigma_1$, the exponent $\frac32\sigma-\frac94+\eta$, which is smaller.
results.label: gl:lem:stirling

results.name: Absolute convergence hypothesis of the master theorem route for the reciprocal of xi holds without RH
results.summary: With no hypothesis on the zeros, the series $\mathfrak R(w)=\sum_{k\ge1}b_kw^k$ built from $\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+k)$ is entire of order $\frac23$ and its integral against the density of the centre clock converges for every $z>0$, which is the absolute convergence needed to interchange sum and integral in the master theorem route.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function, let $T$ be the centre clock, the self decomposable random variable with Laplace transform $\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u)$ (it exists without any hypothesis on the zeros), and let $g$ be its density. Put $b_k=\frac{1}{\Gamma(k)}\,\frac{\xi(\frac12)}{\xi(\frac12+k)}$ and $\mathfrak R(w)=\sum_{k\ge1}b_kw^k$. With no hypothesis on the zeros, $\mathfrak R$ is entire of order $\frac23$, and $\int_0^\infty g(y)\,\mathfrak R(z/y)\,dy<\infty$ for every $z>0$.
results.label: gl:lem:fubini

results.name: The reciprocal Xi function in the shifted variable lies in Hardy's class with no hypothesis on the zeros, so the master theorem carries no information on them
results.summary: The function $\xi(\frac32)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt{1+w})$ is analytic and bounded on $\operatorname{Re}w\ge-\delta$ for $0<\delta<1$, hence in Hardy's class unconditionally, and the image region contains no zero of $\xi$, so Ramanujan's master theorem in this variable says nothing about the zeros.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(1+\frac s2)\zeta(s)$ be the completed Riemann zeta function and $0<\delta<1$. Hardy's class consists of the functions $\varphi$ analytic on $\operatorname{Re}w\ge-\delta$ with $|\varphi(v+i\tau)|\le Ce^{Pv+A|\tau|}$ for some constants $C,P$ and $A<\pi$; for them $\int_0^\infty x^{w-1}\sum_{k\ge0}(-x)^k\varphi(k)/k!\,dx=\Gamma(w)\varphi(-w)$ for $0<\operatorname{Re}w<\delta$. The function $\varphi(w)=\xi(\frac32)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt{1+w})$, with the principal square root, is analytic and bounded on $\operatorname{Re}w\ge-\delta$. Hence, with no hypothesis on the zeros, it lies in Hardy's class with $P=0$ and any $A$. The image of $\operatorname{Re}w\ge-\delta$ under $w\mapsto\frac12+\sqrt{1+w}$ lies in $\{\sigma+i\tau:\sigma-\frac12\ge\sqrt{1-\delta+\tau^2}\}$, which contains no zero of $\xi$, so the master theorem identity in this variable carries no information on the zeros.
results.label: tx:prop:hardy

results.name: Why the square root stays: reciprocal Xi function in the variable s is not a Laplace transform of a random variable, and its values on a vertical line are not a characteristic function
results.summary: For every real $\alpha$ the function $s\mapsto\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+s)$ is not the Laplace transform of any real random variable, whether or not RH holds, the function $t\mapsto\xi(\alpha+it)/\xi(\alpha)$ is a characteristic function that is never infinitely divisible, and $t\mapsto\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+it)$ is unbounded.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(1+\frac s2)\zeta(s)$ be the completed Riemann zeta function, and let $L$ be the class of the functions $s\mapsto\mathbb{E}e^{-sX}$, $X$ a real random variable, finite on an interval. Let $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2u})$ be the Pólya kernel, so that $\xi(\frac12+iz)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)e^{izu}\,du$. (a) For every real $\alpha$, $s\mapsto\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+s)$ is not in $L$, whether or not RH holds. (b) For every real $\alpha$, $t\mapsto\xi(\alpha+it)/\xi(\alpha)$ is, unconditionally, the characteristic function of the probability density $\Phi(u)e^{(\alpha-\frac12)u}/\xi(\alpha)$, but it is never infinitely divisible, hence never the law of an exponential generalised gamma convolution. At $\alpha=\frac12$ it is $\Xi(t)/\Xi(0)$, where $\Xi(t)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du=\xi(\frac12+it)$. (c) For every real $\alpha$, $t\mapsto\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+it)$ is unbounded, so it is not a characteristic function.
results.label: tx:thm:nosqrt

results.name: Thorin representation of the reciprocal of the completed Dirichlet L function of a real primitive character under GRH
results.status_text: conditional on The generalized Riemann hypothesis for $L(s,\chi)$ (every nontrivial zero has real part $\frac12$) and $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$ (Chowla's conjecture for real characters, open)
results.conditions: The generalized Riemann hypothesis for $L(s,\chi)$ (every nontrivial zero has real part $\frac12$) and $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$ (Chowla's conjecture for real characters, open).
results.summary: For a real primitive character $\chi$, under GRH for $L(s,\chi)$ and $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$, the reciprocal $\xi(\frac12,\chi)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u,\chi)$ is the Laplace transform of the GGC $\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ over the ordinates of the zeros, and the clock identities of the Riemann case carry over.
results.statement:
Let $\chi$ be a real primitive character modulo $q>1$ of parity $a\in\{0,1\}$ (so $\chi(-1)=(-1)^a$) and $\xi(s,\chi)=(q/\pi)^{(s+a)/2}\Gamma( rac{s+a}2)L(s,\chi)$ the completed Dirichlet $L$ function, an entire function of order one, real on the real axis, with $\xi(s,\chi)=\xi(1-s,\chi)$. Assume GRH for $L(s,\chi)$ and $L( rac12,\chi)
e0$, and write the zeros as $ rac12\pm i\gamma$ with $\gamma>0$, counted with multiplicity. Then $T_\chi\stackrel{d}{=}\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$, with $e_\gamma$ independent standard exponential variables, is a GGC with $\xi( rac12,\chi)/\xi( rac12+\sqrt u,\chi)=\mathbb{E}[e^{-uT_\chi}]$ for $u\ge0$ and cumulants $(j-1)!\,p_j(\chi)$, $p_j(\chi)=\sum_{\gamma>0}\gamma^{-2j}$. The analogues for $\xi(\cdot,\chi)$ of the statements for Riemann's $\xi$ under RH on the transfer function from the real axis to the critical line, the odd index power sums of the inverse squared ordinates, the Blaschke product of the transfer function and the negative moments of the clock hold, with GRH for $L(s,\chi)$ and $L( rac12,\chi)
e0$ in place of RH and $\xi( rac12)
e0$. At the tilt $u_0= rac14$, $\sum_{\gamma>0} rac{1}{\gamma^2+1/4}= rac{\xi'}{\xi}(1,\chi)= rac12\log rac q\pi+ rac12\,\psi ig( rac{1+a}{2} ig)+ rac{L'}{L}(1,\chi)$, with $\psi$ the digamma function, and $\mathbb{E}[e^{-T_\chi/4}]=\xi( rac12,\chi)/\xi(1,\chi)$.
results.label: gl:prop:Lreal

results.name: Thorin representation for a complex character through the product of the completed L function with its conjugate, under GRH
results.status_text: conditional on The generalized Riemann hypothesis for $L(s,\chi)$ (every nontrivial zero has real part $\frac12$) and $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$
results.conditions: The generalized Riemann hypothesis for $L(s,\chi)$ (every nontrivial zero has real part $\frac12$) and $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$.
results.summary: For a complex primitive character $\chi$, the product $\xi(s,\chi)\xi(s,\bar\chi)$ is symmetric under $s\mapsto1-s$, and under GRH for $L(s,\chi)$ with $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$ the reciprocal of its ratio to the centre is the Laplace transform of the GGC $\sum e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ over all ordinates of $L(s,\chi)$ of both signs.
results.statement: Let $\chi$ be a complex primitive character modulo $q>1$ of parity $a\in\{0,1\}$ and $\xi(s,\chi)=(q/\pi)^{(s+a)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+a}2)L(s,\chi)$ the completed Dirichlet $L$ function, an entire function of order one with $\xi(s,\chi)=W_\chi\,\xi(1-s,\bar\chi)$ and $|W_\chi|=1$. Put $\xi_{\chi\bar\chi}(s)=\xi(s,\chi)\,\xi(s,\bar\chi)$. Then $\xi_{\chi\bar\chi}(s)=\xi_{\chi\bar\chi}(1-s)$ and $\xi_{\chi\bar\chi}(\sigma)=|\xi(\sigma,\chi)|^2$ for real $\sigma$. If GRH holds for $L(s,\chi)$ and $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$, then $\xi_{\chi\bar\chi}(\frac12)/\xi_{\chi\bar\chi}(\frac12+\sqrt u)=\mathbb{E}[e^{-uT_{\chi\bar\chi}}]$ for $u\ge0$, where $T_{\chi\bar\chi}\stackrel{d}{=}\sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma_\chi}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$, $\Gamma_\chi$ is the multiset of all ordinates $\gamma$, of both signs, of the zeros $\frac12+i\gamma$ of $L(s,\chi)$, and the $e_\gamma$ are independent standard exponential variables.
results.label: gl:prop:Lcomplex

results.name: Factorisation of the completed Dedekind zeta function of a quadratic field and clocks of cyclotomic fields as independent sums
results.status_text: conditional on The statement on cyclotomic fields assumes GRH for the Dirichlet $L$ functions of the nonprincipal primitive characters of conductor dividing $q$ and that their values at $\frac12$ are nonzero (the hypotheses of the propositions on real and complex characters). The factorisations of the completed functions hold without any hypothesis, and the statement for quadratic fields is an implication from the Thorin property of the two factors at the tilt considered
results.conditions: The statement on cyclotomic fields assumes GRH for the Dirichlet $L$ functions of the nonprincipal primitive characters of conductor dividing $q$ and that their values at $\frac12$ are nonzero (the hypotheses of the propositions on real and complex characters). The factorisations of the completed functions hold without any hypothesis, and the statement for quadratic fields is an implication from the Thorin property of the two factors at the tilt considered.
results.summary: For a quadratic field the completed Dedekind zeta function is $2\xi(s)\xi(s,\chi)$ (times $q^{-1/2}$ for odd $\chi$), so at a tilt where both factors have the Thorin property the tilted clock is the independent sum of theirs and the Thorin measures add, and for cyclotomic fields, under GRH with nonzero central values, the clock is the independent sum of the clocks of $\zeta$ and of the nonprincipal primitive characters of conductor dividing $q$.
results.statement: Let $\chi$ be a real primitive character of conductor $q$ and parity $a\in\{0,1\}$, with $\xi(s,\chi)=(q/\pi)^{(s+a)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+a}2)L(s,\chi)$, let $F=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt D)$ with $D=\chi(-1)q$ a fundamental discriminant (so $\zeta_F=\zeta\cdot L(\cdot,\chi)$, and $F$ is real quadratic for even $\chi$ and imaginary quadratic for odd $\chi$), let $\xi_F(s)=s(s-1)|d_F|^{s/2}\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)^{r_1}\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)^{r_2}\zeta_F(s)$ be its completed Dedekind zeta function ($d_F$ the discriminant, $r_1$ and $r_2$ the numbers of real and complex places, $\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)$, $\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)=2(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)$) and let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function. Then $\xi_F(s)=2\,\xi(s)\,\xi(s,\chi)$ when $\chi$ is even and $\xi_F(s)=2q^{-1/2}\,\xi(s)\,\xi(s,\chi)$ when $\chi$ is odd. For a function $f$ the tilted clock at tilt $u_0\ge0$ is the random variable with Laplace transform $f(\frac12+\sqrt{u_0})/f(\frac12+\sqrt{u_0+s})$, and the centre clock is the case $u_0=0$. Consequently, at any tilt $u_0\ge0$ at which $\xi$ and $\xi(\cdot,\chi)$ both have the Thorin property (this reciprocal is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution), so does $\xi_F$, its tilted clock is the independent sum of the tilted clocks of $\xi$ and of $\xi(\cdot,\chi)$, and the Thorin measures add, $U_{F,u_0}=U_{\mathbb{Q},u_0}+U_{\chi,u_0}$, where $U_{\chi,u_0}$ is the Thorin measure of the tilted clock of $\xi(\cdot,\chi)$; at $u_0=0$ this reads $T_F\stackrel d=T_\zeta+T_\chi$ for the centre clocks, and the cumulants add, $p_j(F)=p_j(\zeta)+p_j(\chi)$ with $p_j=\sum_{\gamma>0}\gamma^{-2j}$ over the ordinates of the zeros. For the cyclotomic field $F_q=\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_q)$, $q\ge3$, under GRH for the Dirichlet $L$ functions of the nonprincipal primitive characters of conductor dividing $q$ and with their values at $\frac12$ nonzero, the centre clock $T_{F_q}$ is the independent sum of $T_\zeta$ (the centre clock of $\xi$), of $T_\chi$ (the centre clock of $\xi(\cdot,\chi)$) over the real primitive characters $\chi$ of conductor $f\mid q$ with $f>1$, and of $T_{\chi\bar\chi}$ (the centre clock of $\xi(s,\chi)\xi(s,\bar\chi)$) over the conjugate pairs of complex primitive characters of conductor dividing $q$.
results.label: gl:prop:dedekind

results.name: Lévy decomposition of the logarithm of the completed Dedekind zeta function of any number field, with signs
results.summary: For $\alpha>1$ the compensated logarithm of $\xi_F(\alpha+s)/\xi_F(\alpha)$ is an integral against a signed Lévy measure whose arithmetic part has the positive weights $\Lambda_F(n)$ at $\log n$, plus gamma factor densities and the single negative density $-(1+e^x)$ coming from the factor $s(s-1)$.
results.statement: Let $F$ be a number field with $r_1$ real and $r_2$ complex places and Dedekind zeta function $\zeta_F$, and $\xi_F(s)=s(s-1)|d_F|^{s/2}\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)^{r_1}\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)^{r_2}\zeta_F(s)$ its completed Dedekind zeta function ($d_F$ the discriminant, $\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)$, $\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)=2(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)$). Let $\Lambda_F(n)=\sum_{N\mathfrak p^r=n}\log N\mathfrak p\ge0$, the sum over prime ideals $\mathfrak p$ and integers $r\ge1$ with $N\mathfrak p^r=n$, and $h_s(x)=e^{-sx}-1+sx\ge0$. For $\alpha>1$ and $s\ge0$, $\log\frac{\xi_F(\alpha+s)}{\xi_F(\alpha)}-s\,\frac{\xi_F'}{\xi_F}(\alpha)=\int_0^\infty h_s(x)\,e^{-\alpha x}\,\frac{\nu_F(dx)}x$ with the signed measure $\nu_F(dx)=\Big(\frac{r_1}{1-e^{-2x}}+\frac{r_2}{1-e^{-x}}-1-e^x\Big)dx+\sum_{n\ge2}\Lambda_F(n)\,\delta_{\log n}(dx)$.
results.label: gl:prop:levyF

results.name: The sine squared lemma on the prime side for Dedekind zeta functions and real Dirichlet characters
results.summary: For $\alpha>1$ and $f$ the completed Dedekind zeta function of a number field or the completed $L$ function of a real primitive character, the reciprocal $f(\alpha)/f(\alpha+\sqrt u)$ equals $\exp(-\int_0^\infty\log(1+u/b^2)\,v_\alpha(b)\,db/\pi)$ with $v_\alpha(b)=\operatorname{Re}(f'/f)(\alpha+ib)$ written through a sine squared transform of the Lévy measure (Polson's sine squared lemma applied to $f$), so that the density is determined by the primes with no reference to the zeros.
results.statement:
Let $f$ be either $\xi_F(s)=s(s-1)|d_F|^{s/2}\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)^{r_1}\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)^{r_2}\zeta_F(s)$, the completed Dedekind zeta function of a number field $F$ with discriminant $d_F$, $r_1$ real and $r_2$ complex places, $\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)$ and $\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)=2(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)$, or $\xi(\cdot,\chi)$, the completed Dirichlet $L$ function $\xi(s,\chi)=(q/\pi)^{(s+a)/2}\Gamma( rac{s+a}2)L(s,\chi)$ of a real primitive character $\chi$ modulo $q>1$ of parity $a\in\{0,1\}$. Let $\alpha>1$, $h_w(x)=e^{-wx}-1+wx$, and let $
u$ be the signed Lévy measure of $f$, defined by $\log rac{f(\alpha+w)}{f(\alpha)}-w\, rac{f'}{f}(\alpha)=\int_0^\infty h_w(x)\,e^{-\alpha x}\, rac{
u(dx)}x$ for $w\ge0$: for $f=\xi_F$, $
u_F(dx)=\Big( rac{r_1}{1-e^{-2x}}+ rac{r_2}{1-e^{-x}}-1-e^x\Big)dx+\sum_{n\ge2}\Lambda_F(n)\,\delta_{\log n}(dx)$ with $\Lambda_F(n)=\sum_{N\mathfrak p^r=n}\log N\mathfrak p$; for $f=\xi(\cdot,\chi)$, $
u_\chi(dx)=\sum_{n\ge2}\chi(n)\Lambda(n)\,\delta_{\log n}(dx)+ rac{e^{(1-a)x}}{2\sinh x}\,dx$, where $\Lambda$ is the von Mangoldt function. Then, for $u\ge0$, $ rac{f(\alpha)}{f(\alpha+\sqrt u)}=\exp\Big(-\int_0^\infty\log\Big(1+ rac u{b^2}\Big)\, rac{v_\alpha(b)}\pi\,db\Big)$, where $v_\alpha(b)= rac{f'}{f}(\alpha)+\int_0^\infty2\sin^2\Big( rac{bx}2\Big)e^{-\alpha x}\,
u(dx)=\operatorname{Re} rac{f'}{f}(\alpha+ib)$.
results.label: gl:prop:sinsq

results.name: The basepoint family of the sine squared lemma: Thorin property at a basepoint to the right of all zeros, failure when a zero lies to the right, and the Poisson form under GRH
results.status_text: conditional on Part (c) assumes GRH for $f$ (every zero has real part $\frac12$) and $f(\frac12)\ne0$. Parts (a) and (b) hold without any hypothesis, and part (a) holds unconditionally for every $\alpha\ge1$
results.conditions: Part (c) assumes GRH for $f$ (every zero has real part $\frac12$) and $f(\frac12)\ne0$. Parts (a) and (b) hold without any hypothesis, and part (a) holds unconditionally for every $\alpha\ge1$.
results.summary: For the completed Dedekind zeta function of a number field or the completed $L$ function of a real primitive character, the reciprocal $f(\alpha)/f(\alpha+\sqrt u)$ is a GGC with a positive Thorin density that is a sum over the zeros when every zero lies to the left of $\alpha$ (so unconditionally for $\alpha\ge1$), is not a GGC transform when a zero lies to the right, and under GRH the density is the Poisson smoothing of the zero counting measure at height $\alpha-\frac12$.
