results.name: GRH and nonvanishing at the centre from the Thorin property of the Dedekind zeta functions of quadratic and cyclotomic fields
results.summary: If the tilted reciprocal of the Dedekind zeta function of a quadratic field is a GGC at tilt $1$, then RH holds and the zeros of the Dirichlet $L$ function are on the critical line or real; if it is a GGC at tilt $0$, then GRH holds for that $L$ function with $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$; and if this holds at tilt $0$ for every cyclotomic field, then GRH holds for all Dirichlet $L$ functions with all central values nonzero.
results.statement: Let $\chi$ be a real primitive character of conductor $q$, $F=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt D)$ with $D=\chi(-1)q$ the quadratic field of $\chi$ (so that $\zeta_F(s)=\zeta(s)L(s,\chi)$), $\xi_F(s)=s(s-1)|d_F|^{s/2}\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)^{r_1}\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)^{r_2}\zeta_F(s)$ its completed Dedekind zeta function ($d_F$ the discriminant, $r_1$ and $r_2$ the numbers of real and complex places, $\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)$, $\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)=2(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)$), and $\varphi_{F,u_0}(s)=\xi_F(\frac12+\sqrt{u_0})/\xi_F(\frac12+\sqrt{u_0+s})$ for $u_0\ge0$. (a) If $\varphi_{F,1}$ is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution (GGC), then RH holds and every nontrivial zero of $L(s,\chi)$ lies on the critical line or is real. (b) If $\varphi_{F,0}$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC, equivalently $\varphi_{F,1}$ is one with Thorin measure in $(1,\infty)$, then $L(s,\chi)$ satisfies GRH (all its nontrivial zeros lie on the critical line) and $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$. If $\varphi_{F_q,0}$ is a GGC Laplace transform for every $q\ge3$, with $F_q=\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_q)$, then GRH holds for all Dirichlet $L$ functions, and $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$ for every primitive character $\chi$.
results.label: gl:thm:grh

results.name: Mixtures of clocks: a mixture of two GGC Laplace transforms with discrete unit atom Thorin measures is not a GGC transform when it vanishes off the atoms, in particular in the odd configuration
results.summary: A mixture $\lambda\varphi_1+(1-\lambda)\varphi_2$ of two GGC Laplace transforms whose Thorin measures are sums of unit point masses is not a GGC transform if it vanishes at a negative point that is not an atom, and this happens for every weight $\lambda$ when two consecutive atoms of the union belong to different measures and an odd number of atoms lie at or below the first of them.
results.statement: Let $\varphi_1,\varphi_2$ be Laplace transforms of generalized gamma convolutions (GGCs: laws on $[0,\infty)$ with Laplace transform $\exp(-bs-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+s/t)\,U(dt))$, drift $b\ge0$ and Thorin measure $U$) with zero drift and Thorin measures $U_1,U_2$ that are sums of unit point masses, repeated according to multiplicity, so that $\varphi_i(s)=\prod_t t/(t+s)$, over the atoms $t$ of $U_i$, is meromorphic on $\mathbb{C}$ with poles at the points $-t$. Let $0<\lambda<1$ and $\varphi=\lambda\varphi_1+(1-\lambda)\varphi_2$. (a) If $\varphi(-x)=0$ for some $x>0$ that is not an atom of $U_1$ or $U_2$, then $\varphi$ is not the Laplace transform of a GGC. (b) Let $t_1<t_2$ be consecutive points of $\operatorname{supp}U_1\cup\operatorname{supp}U_2$ with $t_1$ an atom of only one of the measures and $t_2$ an atom of only the other. If $U_1+U_2$ has an odd number of atoms in $(0,t_1]$, counted with multiplicity, then $\varphi$ has a zero in $(-t_2,-t_1)$, so $\varphi$ is not the Laplace transform of a GGC, for any $\lambda$.
results.label: gl:prop:mixture

results.name: The family of characters modulo 5: no mixture of the two clocks is a GGC, under GRH
results.status_text: conditional on The generalized Riemann hypothesis for $L(s,\chi_5)$ and for $L(s,\psi)$ (every nontrivial zero has real part $\frac12$). The values $L(\frac12,\chi_5)$ and $L(\frac12,\psi)$ are certified nonzero, and the zeros below height $12$ are certified, in ball arithmetic; neither is assumed
results.conditions: The generalized Riemann hypothesis for $L(s,\chi_5)$ and for $L(s,\psi)$ (every nontrivial zero has real part $\frac12$). The values $L(\frac12,\chi_5)$ and $L(\frac12,\psi)$ are certified nonzero, and the zeros below height $12$ are certified, in ball arithmetic; neither is assumed.
results.summary: Under GRH for the two members of the family of primitive characters modulo $5$, no mixture of their clocks, the uniform one included, is a GGC, because certified zero counts below height $12$ put their Thorin atoms in the odd configuration of the mixture criterion.
results.statement: Let $\chi_5$ be the real primitive character modulo $5$ (the Legendre symbol, even) and $\psi$ the primitive character modulo $5$ with $\psi(2)=i$ (odd). For a primitive character $\chi$ modulo $q$ of parity $a\in\{0,1\}$ let $\xi(s,\chi)=(q/\pi)^{(s+a)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+a}2)L(s,\chi)$, and put $\xi_{\psi\bar\psi}(s)=\xi(s,\psi)\,\xi(s,\bar\psi)$. A generalized gamma convolution (GGC) is a probability law on $[0,\infty)$ whose Laplace transform is $\exp\big(-bs-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+s/t)\,U(dt)\big)$ with drift $b\ge0$ and a nonnegative Thorin measure $U$. Assume GRH for $L(s,\chi_5)$ and $L(s,\psi)$. Then for every $\lambda\in(0,1)$ the function $u\mapsto\lambda\,\xi(\frac12,\chi_5)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u,\chi_5)+(1-\lambda)\,\xi_{\psi\bar\psi}(\frac12)/\xi_{\psi\bar\psi}(\frac12+\sqrt u)$, $u\ge0$, is not the Laplace transform of a GGC. In particular the case $\lambda=\frac12$, the clock of a uniformly chosen member of the family $\{\chi_5,\{\psi,\bar\psi\}\}$ of primitive characters modulo $5$, is not a GGC.
results.label: gl:prop:mod5

results.name: A real zero of a Dirichlet L function makes the first rung of the twisted heat trace fail beyond an explicit time
results.summary: If $L(s,\chi)$ of a primitive real character has a real zero $\beta$ in $(\tfrac12,1)$ and all its nonreal zeros lie on the critical line, the twisted heat trace grows and is increasing beyond an explicit time $t_1$, so it is not completely monotone, already at order one.
results.statement: Let $\chi$ be a primitive real Dirichlet character of conductor $q\ge3$, $L(s,\chi)$ its $L$ function, and $\xi(s,\chi)$ the completed $L$ function, an entire function with $\xi(s,\chi)=\xi(1-s,\chi)$. With zeros counted with multiplicity and $z_\rho=(\rho-\tfrac12)^2$, the twisted heat trace is $W(t;\chi)=\sum_{\operatorname{Im}\rho>0}e^{tz_\rho}+\tfrac12\sum_{\rho\text{ real}}e^{tz_\rho}$ for $t>0$. Let $\beta\in(\tfrac12,1)$ be the largest real zero of $L(s,\chi)$, suppose that every nonreal zero of $L(s,\chi)$ lies on the critical line, and put $c=(\beta-\tfrac12)^2$. Then $W(t;\chi)\to\infty$ as $t\to\infty$, and $-W'(t;\chi)<0$ for all $t>t_1=\max\{1,c^{-1}\log(C'\log q/c)\}$, where $C'$ is an absolute constant. Hence $W(\cdot\,;\chi)$ is not completely monotone, the first rung of the ladder $(-1)^kW^{(k)}>0$ failing at order $k=1$ beyond $t_1$. The book adds the following consequence, which rests on the unrefereed theorem of Banks and Kerr (October 2026) that there are absolute constants $q_0$ and $\delta_0>0$ with $(1-\beta)\log q\ge\delta_0$ for every real zero $\beta$ of every primitive real character of conductor $q\ge q_0$: for $q\ge q_0$ and $\eta=\delta_0/\log q$ one has $c\le\tfrac14-\eta(1-\eta)$, so the growth rate $c$ is at least $\eta(1-\eta)$ below the rate $\tfrac14$ of the pole term $e^{t/4}$ of $\zeta$. That consequence is conditional on the Banks and Kerr theorem and is not part of the proved status of this entry; the first part (the growth and the sign of $-W'$) uses only the bound $N(T,\chi)\ll(T+1)\log(q(T+2))$ for the number of zeros up to height $T$.
results.label: gl:prop:rung1

results.name: Linnik constant seven from the Thorin property of all cyclotomic fields (weaker than the known result under GRH)
results.status_text: conditional on The Thorin property at tilt $0$ for every cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_q)$, $q\ge3$, which by the equivalence theorem of the chapter is GRH for all Dirichlet $L$ functions together with $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$ for every primitive character $\chi$. The proof uses only the GRH part, through the theorem of Heath-Brown and Puchta (2002) that GRH gives seven powers of two
results.conditions: The Thorin property at tilt $0$ for every cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_q)$, $q\ge3$, which by the equivalence theorem of the chapter is GRH for all Dirichlet $L$ functions together with $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$ for every primitive character $\chi$. The proof uses only the GRH part, through the theorem of Heath-Brown and Puchta (2002) that GRH gives seven powers of two.
results.summary: If the centre clock of every cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_q)$, $q\ge3$, is a GGC, then every sufficiently large even integer is a sum of two primes and at most seven powers of two, which is the value that GRH already gives, so the corollary is weaker than the theorem of Heath-Brown and Puchta (2002), also proved by Pintz and Ruzsa (2003), that GRH alone gives seven, because it assumes nonvanishing at the centre as well.
results.statement: Suppose that for every integer $q\ge3$ the function $\varphi_{F,0}(s)=\xi_F(\frac12)/\xi_F(\frac12+\sqrt s)$, with $\xi_F(s)=s(s-1)|d_F|^{s/2}\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)^{\varphi(q)/2}\zeta_F(s)$, $\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)=2(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)$, the completed Dedekind zeta function of the cyclotomic field $F=\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_q)$, a totally complex field of degree $\varphi(q)$ and discriminant $d_F$, is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution. Then every sufficiently large even integer is a sum of two primes and at most seven powers of two.
results.label: gl:cor:K7

results.name: Open problem: the Thorin property of the Riemann clock and of cyclotomic clocks without first knowing the zeros
results.summary: Prove that the tilted reciprocal of the completed zeta function of $\mathbb{Q}$, or of a cyclotomic field, is the Laplace transform of a GGC without first knowing the zeros, in particular by settling the parabolic distortion in the master theorem route; for $\mathbb{Q}$ at the centre this is RH itself.
results.statement: Let $\xi_F(s)=s(s-1)|d_F|^{s/2}\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)^{r_1}\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)^{r_2}\zeta_F(s)$ be the completed Dedekind zeta function of a number field $F$ ($d_F$ the discriminant, $r_1$ and $r_2$ the numbers of real and complex places, $\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)$, $\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)=2(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)$) and $\varphi_{F,u_0}(s)=\xi_F(\frac12+\sqrt{u_0})/\xi_F(\frac12+\sqrt{u_0+s})$ its tilted reciprocal. Prove that $\varphi_{\mathbb{Q},u_0}$, or $\varphi_{F,u_0}$ for the cyclotomic fields $F$, is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution (the first condition of the equivalence theorem on the Thorin property of the tilted clock), without first knowing the second condition, namely the position of the zeros. In the route through Ramanujan's master theorem, which expands $\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u)$ term by term, settle the parabolic distortion (the Laplace variable is $u=s^2$, and the squaring map carries the strip $|\operatorname{Re}s|<1$ onto the region $\{|\operatorname{Im}u|<2\sqrt{1-\operatorname{Re}u}\}$), uniformly in the field, and find a substitute for the residue bookkeeping at the zeros. For $\mathbb{Q}$ at $u_0=0$ the statement to be proved is the Riemann Hypothesis, so a growth bound that is itself proved under RH cannot be an input to its proof.
results.label: gl:op:direct

results.name: Open problem: seven powers of two from GRH with possible real zeros, that is from the Thorin property at tilt one for cyclotomic fields
results.summary: Show that every sufficiently large even integer is a sum of two primes and at most seven powers of two from the weaker hypothesis that every nontrivial zero of every Dirichlet $L$ function lies on the critical line or on the real axis, which would make real and Siegel zeros irrelevant to this value.
results.statement: Show that every sufficiently large even integer is a sum of two primes and at most seven powers of two (the Linnik constant $K=7$) from the hypothesis that for every cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_q)$, $q\ge3$, the tilted reciprocal $\varphi_{\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_q),1}$ of the completed Dedekind zeta function at tilt $u_0=1$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution; by the equivalence theorem of the chapter this hypothesis says that every nontrivial zero of every Dirichlet $L$ function lies on the critical line or on the real axis, that is, GRH with possible real zeros. The book locates, by a heuristic estimate, the arcs of the circle method on which a real zero can make the minor arc bound of exponent $\frac34$ for the sum over primes fail; what remains is to move these arcs into the major arcs and to redo the main term of the major arc estimate with several real zeros, checking that its constant $2.7895$ survives. The major arc estimate of Heath-Brown and Puchta that gives this constant (their Lemma 7) is stated for $K\ge9$, with zero density estimates in place of GRH, and their paper does not say how it is used for $K=7$; the computation of the constant itself holds for $K\ge7$. If it works, real zeros, and with them Siegel zeros, become irrelevant to $K=7$.
results.label: gl:op:exceptional

results.name: Open problem: the anchored tail of the moment identity of the centre clock at large height and for Dirichlet L functions
results.summary: Carry the anchored tail of the zero side of the moment identity of the centre clock to large height with tables of zeros of zeta, where the remaining integral of the zero count fluctuation sets the limit and calls for an explicit formula, and to Dirichlet $L$ functions.
results.statement: Let $T$ be the centre clock of Riemann's xi function. Its moments are computed from the power sums $p_j=\sum_{\gamma>0}\gamma^{-2j}$ of the inverse squared ordinates of the zeros, summed over the first zeros and completed by a tail. With $N(t)$ the zero count, $N_0=\vartheta/\pi$ with $\vartheta$ the Riemann Siegel theta function, and $S(t)=N(t)-N_0(t)-1$, the tail beyond a height $H$ satisfies exactly $\sum_{\gamma>H}\gamma^{-2j}=\int_H^\infty t^{-2j}\,\frac{\vartheta'(t)}{\pi}\,dt+\big(N_0(H)+1-N(H)\big)H^{-2j}+2j\int_H^\infty S(t)\,t^{-2j-1}\,dt$, and the anchored tail keeps the first two terms. Carry the anchoring to large height with tables of zeros of the Riemann zeta function, where the remaining term, the integral of $S(t)\,t^{-2j-1}$ over the tail, sets the limit and calls for an explicit formula for $\int S$, and to Dirichlet $L(s,\chi)$ with tables of their zeros. The book reproduces the anchoring only for the first ordinates; large heights and the characters are open.
results.label: gl:op:numerics

results.name: Open problem: the negative moment of the clock averaged over real characters of conductor in [Q,2Q] against the symplectic random matrix prediction
results.summary: Compute the average of the negative moment $\mathbb{E}[T_\chi^{-1/2}]$ of the clock over real primitive characters of conductor in $[Q,2Q]$ and compare it with the prediction of the symplectic ensemble, noting that this moment is not a linear statistic of the zeros.
results.statement: For a real primitive character $\chi$ let $T_\chi$ be the clock (under GRH for $L(s,\chi)$ and $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$) with Laplace transform $\xi(\frac12,\chi)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u,\chi)$, and $T$ the centre clock of Riemann's xi function. The negative moment $\mathbb{E}[T^{-1/2}]=\Gamma(\frac12)^{-1}\int_0^\infty u^{-1/2}\prod_{\gamma>0}(1+u/\gamma^2)^{-1}\,du$, the product being over the ordinates $\gamma>0$ of the zeros, is computed from $\xi$ alone, and the book finds it to be mostly a smooth statistic of the zeros, so that a single function says little and the natural comparison with random matrix theory is in families. Compute the average of $\mathbb{E}[T_\chi^{-1/2}]$ over the real primitive characters $\chi$ of conductor in $[Q,2Q]$ and compare it with the prediction of the symplectic ensemble. Since $\mathbb{E}[T^{-1/2}]$ is not a linear statistic of the zeros, the one level density of the family (Katz and Sarnak 1999) alone does not give this prediction, and all the correlation functions enter. The single function is computed in the book; the family average is open.
results.label: gl:op:negmoment

results.name: Open problem: infinite divisibility of the family mixture of the clocks of the characters modulo q
results.summary: Decide whether the clock of a uniformly chosen character of the family modulo $q$ is infinitely divisible, and whether some $q$ with two or more members avoids the odd configuration of the mixture criterion for every pair of members.
results.statement: Let $\mathcal F_q$ consist of the real primitive characters modulo $q$ together with one representative of each conjugate pair of complex primitive characters modulo $q$. Assume GRH for the members and that their central values are nonzero, so that their clocks exist: $T_\chi\stackrel d=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ for a real member (the ordinates $\gamma>0$ of $L(s,\chi)$, with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$) and $T_{\chi\bar\chi}\stackrel d=\sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma_\chi}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ for a complex pair (all ordinates of both signs). Let $T^{(q)}$ be the clock of a uniformly chosen member. Is $T^{(q)}$ infinitely divisible? Does any $q$ for which $\mathcal F_q$ has two or more members avoid, for every pair of its members, the odd configuration of the mixture criterion (two clocks whose Thorin measures are sums of unit point masses, with consecutive atoms $t_1<t_2$ of the union belonging to different clocks and an odd number of atoms of the union in $(0,t_1]$)? It is settled that $T^{(q)}$ is not a GGC for $q=5$ and every weight, under GRH for the two members (their values at $\frac12$ are nonzero numerically), and, under the same hypotheses, for every $q$ whose family has exactly two members, when these are in the odd configuration; this does not decide whether $T^{(5)}$ is infinitely divisible.
results.label: gl:op:family

results.name: Open problem: a sign definite explicit formula for primes in the progressions a modulo q with a not congruent to 1
results.summary: Find a sign definite explicit formula for $\psi(x;q,a)$ with $a\not\equiv1\pmod q$ in terms of the zero counting measures of cyclotomic fields and their Poisson smoothings, for which the case $a\equiv1$ is already an integral against a nonnegative measure under the Thorin property.
results.statement: Let $F_q=\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_q)$ and $\psi(x;q,a)=\sum_{n\le x,\ n\equiv a\ (q)}\Lambda(n)$ with $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function. Suppose that the centre clock of the completed Dedekind zeta function $\xi_{F_q}(s)=s(s-1)|d_{F_q}|^{s/2}\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)^{\varphi(q)/2}\zeta_{F_q}(s)$, with $\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)=2(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)$ and $d_{F_q}$ the discriminant, is a generalized gamma convolution (equivalently, GRH for the Dirichlet $L$ functions of conductor dividing $q$ with nonzero central values). Then the explicit formula for $\psi(x;q,1)$, which up to the factor $\varphi(q)$ counts the prime ideals of $F_q$, becomes an integral against the nonnegative zero counting Thorin measure $U_{F_q,0}$, and the positive family $\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi_{F_q}'/\xi_{F_q})(\alpha+ib)$ of the basepoint family joins it to the primes. For $a\not\equiv1\pmod q$ the characters enter the explicit formula for $\psi(x;q,a)$ with the weights $\bar\chi(a)$, which are complex or negative, and no sign is available. These are zero counting measures and their Poisson smoothings, so any gain must come from structure beyond counting, such as monotonicity or log concavity of the associated GGC densities, transported to bounds on $L'/L$ near the line. Is there a sign definite explicit formula for $\psi(x;q,a)$ with $a\not\equiv1\pmod q$, in terms of such measures?
results.label: gl:op:signdefinite

results.name: Open problem: certified backward continuation of the Thorin density of the basepoint family from the primes into the critical strip
results.summary: Determine how far into the critical strip positivity of the Thorin density $\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(f'/f)(\alpha+ib)$ can be certified from smoothed prime sums alone before the ill posedness of the backward step takes over.
results.statement: Let $f$ be the completed Dedekind zeta function $\xi_F(s)=s(s-1)|d_F|^{s/2}\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)^{r_1}\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)^{r_2}\zeta_F(s)$ of a number field $F$ ($d_F$ the discriminant, $r_1$ and $r_2$ the numbers of real and complex places, $\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)$, $\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)=2(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)$) or the completed Dirichlet $L$ function $\xi(s,\chi)=(q/\pi)^{(s+a)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+a}2)L(s,\chi)$ of a real primitive character $\chi$ modulo $q>1$ of parity $a\in\{0,1\}$. The Thorin density $\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(f'/f)(\alpha+ib)$ of the basepoint family is computable from the primes, with rigorous error bounds, for $\alpha>1$, and its positivity on every line $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha'$ with $\alpha'>\alpha$ is a zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha$. How far into the critical strip (that is, to which $\alpha<1$) can positivity be certified from the primes alone, using smoothed prime sums of the kind that locate the zeros of a Dirichlet $L$ function, before the ill posedness of the backward step takes over? The backward step is a deconvolution of the Poisson smoothing, which is unbounded, and the number of primes it needs grows without bound as $\alpha\downarrow\frac12$; for the heat flow the corresponding step is stable but cannot carry real zeros. What smoothed prime sums can certify below $\alpha=1$ is open; the book finds the output of the sine squared lemma not computable from the primes alone in practice for $\alpha\le1$ (a computation for a character modulo $4$ with the prime powers up to a finite cutoff), so that the minima it computes there come from the zeros.
results.label: gl:op:backward

results.name: Open problem: the exponential sum over primes on the minor arcs as an expectation against the GGC laws of the clocks
results.summary: Decide whether the exponential sum over primes on the minor arcs of the circle method for Linnik's problem can be written as an expectation against the GGC laws of the clocks, which would give a different route to the supremum bound on the minor arcs.
results.statement:
For $F=\mathbb{Q}$ let $
u_F$ be the signed Lévy measure of the completed zeta function $\xi_F$, defined by $\log rac{\xi_F(\alpha+w)}{\xi_F(\alpha)}-w rac{\xi_F'}{\xi_F}(\alpha)=\int_0^\infty(e^{-wx}-1+wx)\,e^{-\alpha x}\, rac{
u_F(dx)}x$ for $\alpha>1$ and $w\ge0$, that is $
u_F(dx)= ig( rac1{1-e^{-2x}}-1-e^x ig)dx+\sum_{n\ge2}\Lambda(n)\,\delta_{\log n}(dx)$ with $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function, and let the GGC laws of the clocks be the laws with Laplace transform $\xi_F(\alpha)/\xi_F(\alpha+\sqrt u)$, $u\ge0$, for $\alpha>1$. The atoms of $
u_F$ at the primes $p$ have mass $\log p$, the weights that enter the exponential sum $\mathcal S(\alpha)=\sum_{\varpi N<p\le N}e(p\alpha)$ of the circle method for Linnik's problem (with $e(x)=\exp(2\pi ix)$ and $\varpi>0$ small); the prime powers in $
u_F$ do not enter $\mathcal S(\alpha)$. Can $\mathcal S(\alpha)$ on the minor arcs be written as an expectation against the GGC laws of the clocks? Such a representation would be a different route to the supremum bound for $\mathcal S$ on the minor arcs; nothing in the chapter shows that it exists.
results.label: gl:op:arith

results.name: Open problem: the best minor arc exponent in Linnik's problem from a zero free half plane for all Dirichlet L functions
results.summary: Under a zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta_0$ for all Dirichlet $L$ functions, find the best minor arc exponent for the sum over primes in Linnik's problem, and decide whether the half plane improves the large deviation parameter for the powers of two or the major arc constant.
results.statement:
Consider the circle method for Linnik's problem of writing large even $N$ as $p_1+p_2+2^{k_1}+\cdots+2^{k_K}$, with $\mathcal S(\alpha)=\sum_{\varpi N<p\le N}e(p\alpha)$, $e(x)=\exp(2\pi ix)$. Assume $L(s,\chi)
e0$ for $\operatorname{Re}s>	heta_0$ and every Dirichlet character $\chi$. What is the best exponent $	heta(	heta_0)$ in the minor arc bound $\mathcal S(\alpha)\ll N^{	heta+o(1)}$ obtainable by combining the explicit formula with Vaughan's identity? A one line heuristic balance gives $	heta= rac12(1+	heta_0)$, which is better than the unconditional exponent $ rac{263}{308}$ exactly when $	heta_0< rac{109}{154}$, so it does nothing at $	heta_0= rac78$; it is not shown to be optimal. Does a hybrid bound, using the half plane only for the characters of small conductor, improve the parameter $\lambda$ of the large deviation estimate for the sum over powers of two (the measure of the set where $|\sum_{1\le
u\le L}e(2^
u\alpha)|\ge\lambda L$)? And does the half plane, which excludes exceptional zeros of large conductor, raise the constant of the major arc main term? The paper of Heath-Brown and Puchta (2002) suggests that it does not by itself: they state that zeros close to $\sigma=1$ play no role there; the constant is a sum over small divisors, and the restriction $q\le P=N^{45/154-4\varpi}$ of the major arcs comes from zero density estimates whose critical zeros have $\sigma\le rac34$ and are not removed by a half plane at $ rac78$.
results.label: gl:op:quasi

results.name: Open problem: does a finite order of total positivity of the density force the zeros onto the line, in a class of even entire functions containing xi
results.summary: Decide whether some finite order of total positivity of the density $f_F$ forces every zero of $F$ onto the imaginary axis, for every $F$ in the class of even entire functions with the order, type and reflection symmetry of $\xi(\frac12+s)/\xi(\frac12)$ whose reciprocal is a characteristic function.
results.statement: Let $T$ be the centre clock of Riemann's xi function, $Z$ an independent standard normal variable and $Y=\sqrt{2T}\,Z$. RH holds if and only if the density of $Y$ is a Pólya frequency function of infinite order, that is, every determinant $\det[f(x_i-y_j)]$ with $x_1<\dots<x_n$ and $y_1<\dots<y_n$ is nonnegative. For this one density the question whether a finite order already implies RH has a trivial answer: the orders decrease, so if RH holds every such implication is true, and if RH fails the property fails at some finite order, where the implication is vacuous. The question has content for a class of functions. Let $\mathcal E$ be the class of even entire functions $F$ with $F(0)=1$ and the order, type and reflection symmetry of $\xi(\frac12+s)/\xi(\frac12)$ for which $1/F$ is the characteristic function of a probability density $f_F$; the density of $Y$ is $f_F$ for $F=\xi(\frac12+\cdot)/\xi(\frac12)$. Is there a finite $k$ such that, for every $F\in\mathcal E$, the property that $f_F$ is a Pólya frequency function of order $k$ implies that every zero of $F$ lies on the imaginary axis?
results.label: gl:op:pf

results.name: The integer dilates of the hyperbolic secant are complete in L1 under an integrability condition at the origin and at infinity
results.summary: If $g$ satisfies $\int_0^1|g(x)|/x\,dx+\int_1^\infty|g(x)|e^{-x}dx<\infty$ and $\int_0^\infty g(x)\operatorname{sech}(nx)\,dx=0$ for all $n\in\mathbb N$ then $g=0$ almost everywhere, from the M\"obius identity $e^{-x}=\frac12\sum\mu(n)\chi_4(n)\operatorname{sech}(nx)$ and Lerch's theorem.
results.statement: Let $\operatorname{sech}=1/\cosh$ and let $g$ be a measurable function on $(0,\infty)$ with $\int_0^1|g(x)|x^{-1}dx+\int_1^\infty|g(x)|e^{-x}dx<\infty$. If $\int_0^\infty g(x)\operatorname{sech}(nx)\,dx=0$ for all $n\in\mathbb N$, then $g=0$ almost everywhere. The same holds with $\mathbb N$ replaced by a set $\Lambda\subset(0,\infty)$ containing an interval, provided the integrals $\int g\operatorname{sech}(\lambda x)\,dx$, $\lambda\in\Lambda$, converge absolutely and vanish. The proof uses $e^{-kx}=\frac12\sum_{n\ge1}\mu(n)\chi_4(n)\operatorname{sech}(nkx)$ for $k\in\mathbb N$, with $\mu$ the M\"obius function and $\chi_4$ the nonprincipal character modulo $4$, together with Lerch's theorem that $\int_0^\infty e^{-kx}h(x)\,dx=0$ for all $k\in\mathbb N$ forces $h=0$ when $\int|h|e^{-x}<\infty$.
results.label: lv:thm:L1

results.name: The Möbius secant series converges to the exponential in every weight W_c with c at least one
results.summary: For $c\ge1$, $S_N\to e^{-x}$ in $\mathcal W_c$: dominated convergence for $c>1$, and the prime number theorem for $\mu\chi_4$ with partial summation at $c=1$.
results.statement: For $c>0$ let $\mathcal W_c=L^2((0,\infty),x^{2c-1}dx)$ and $\operatorname{sech}=1/\cosh$, let $\beta(s)=L(s,\chi_4)=1-3^{-s}+5^{-s}-\cdots$ be the Dirichlet beta function, with $\chi_4$ the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$, let $\mu$ be the M\"obius function, $M_\chi(x)=\sum_{n\le x}\mu(n)\chi_4(n)$ and $S_N(x)=\frac12\sum_{n\le N}\mu(n)\chi_4(n)\operatorname{sech}(nx)$. For $c\ge1$, $S_N\to e^{-x}$ in $\mathcal W_c$, that is $\|S_N-e^{-x}\|_c\to0$. For $c>1$ this follows from $|\sum_{n\le N}\mu(n)\chi_4(n)n^{-s}|\le\zeta(c)$ and dominated convergence in the Mellin Plancherel formula; for $c=1$ it follows from the prime number theorem $M_\chi(x)\ll x\exp(-a\sqrt{\log x})$ for some $a>0$ and partial summation.
results.label: lv:thm:c1

results.name: In one weight the secant dilates over any set of dilations with divergent reciprocal sum are complete, whatever the zeros of the beta function do
results.summary: For $c>0$ and $\Lambda\subset[1,\infty)$ with $\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}1/\lambda=\infty$, $\{\operatorname{sech}(\lambda x)\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ is complete in $\mathcal W_c$, unconditionally, in particular for the integer dilates and the prime dilates, at $c=\frac12$ included; the proof is Carleman's formula for a half plane and uses no arithmetic.
results.statement: For $c>0$ let $\mathcal W_c=L^2((0,\infty),x^{2c-1}dx)$ and $\operatorname{sech}=1/\cosh$. Let $c>0$ and let $\Lambda\subset[1,\infty)$ satisfy $\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}1/\lambda=\infty$. Then $\{\operatorname{sech}(\lambda x)\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ is complete in $\mathcal W_c$, that is, a function of $\mathcal W_c$ orthogonal to every $\operatorname{sech}(\lambda x)$ is zero. In particular the integer dilates $\operatorname{sech}(nx)$ and the prime dilates $\operatorname{sech}(px)$, $p$ prime, are complete in every $\mathcal W_c$, including $c=\frac12$. The proof writes the Mellin transform of the orthogonal function against $\Gamma(c+it)\beta(c+it)$ and applies Carleman's formula to an analytic function on the right half plane that vanishes on $\Lambda$.
results.label: lv:thm:single

results.name: Completeness of the exponential in two weights forces a zero free strip for the beta function
results.summary: If $e^{-x}$ is a limit in $\mathcal W_a\cap\mathcal W_b$ of finite combinations of $\operatorname{sech}(nx)$ then $\beta(s)\ne0$ for $a<\Re s<b$, because point evaluation of the Mellin transform is continuous in the strip.
results.statement: For $c>0$ let $\mathcal W_c=L^2((0,\infty),x^{2c-1}dx)$ and $\operatorname{sech}=1/\cosh$, let $\beta(s)=L(s,\chi_4)=1-3^{-s}+5^{-s}-\cdots$ be the Dirichlet beta function, with $\chi_4$ the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$, and let $0<a<b$ with $\mathcal W_a\cap\mathcal W_b$ normed by $\|f\|_a+\|f\|_b$. If $e^{-x}$ is a limit in $\mathcal W_a\cap\mathcal W_b$ of finite linear combinations of the functions $\operatorname{sech}(nx)$, $n\in\mathbb N$, then $\beta(s)\ne0$ for $a<\Re s<b$.
results.label: lv:prop:nec

results.name: Two weight completeness of the secant dilates is equivalent to a zero free half plane for L(s,chi_4) and to convergence of the Möbius secant series
results.summary: For $\frac12\le\theta<1$ the following are equivalent: $L(s,\chi_4)\ne0$ for $\Re s>\theta$; $\{\operatorname{sech}(nx)\}$ is complete in $\mathcal W_a\cap\mathcal W_b$ for all $\theta<a<b<1$; $S_N\to e^{-x}$ in $\mathcal W_c$ for every $c\in(\theta,1)$. With $\theta=\frac12$ the first is the generalised Riemann hypothesis for $L(s,\chi_4)$.
results.statement: For $c>0$ let $\mathcal W_c=L^2((0,\infty),x^{2c-1}dx)$ and $\operatorname{sech}=1/\cosh$, let $\beta(s)=L(s,\chi_4)=1-3^{-s}+5^{-s}-\cdots$ be the Dirichlet beta function, with $\chi_4$ the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$, and let $\mu$ be the M\"obius function, $M_\chi(x)=\sum_{n\le x}\mu(n)\chi_4(n)$ and $S_N(x)=\frac12\sum_{n\le N}\mu(n)\chi_4(n)\operatorname{sech}(nx)$. For $\frac12\le\theta<1$ the following are equivalent: (i) $L(s,\chi_4)\ne0$ for $\Re s>\theta$; (ii) $\{\operatorname{sech}(nx)\}_{n\in\mathbb N}$ is complete in $\mathcal W_a\cap\mathcal W_b$ (normed by $\|f\|_a+\|f\|_b$) for all $\theta<a<b<1$; (iii) $S_N\to e^{-x}$ in $\mathcal W_c$ for every $c\in(\theta,1)$. With $\theta=\frac12$, (i) is the generalised Riemann hypothesis for $L(s,\chi_4)$. When these hold, $\|S_N-e^{-x}\|_c=O_\varepsilon(N^{\theta-c+\varepsilon})$ for $c\in(\theta,1)$.
results.label: lv:thm:two

results.name: The zeta analogue: dilates of the Bose kernel with its pole removed are complete in one weight and in two weights exactly when zeta has the corresponding zero free half plane
results.summary: For $\varphi(x)=1/(e^x-1)-1/x$: (1) $\{\varphi(nx)\}$ is complete in $\mathcal W_c$ for every $c\in(0,1)$; (2) $M(x)=O(x^{\theta+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ gives $\|T_N-e^{-x}\|_c=O(N^{\theta-c+\varepsilon})$ for $\theta<c<1$; (3) two weight completeness for all $\theta<a<b<1$ is equivalent to $\zeta(s)\ne0$ for $\Re s>\theta$, and for $\theta=\frac12$ to the Riemann hypothesis.
results.statement: For $c>0$ let $\mathcal W_c=L^2((0,\infty),x^{2c-1}dx)$ and $\operatorname{sech}=1/\cosh$, let $\varphi(x)=1/(e^x-1)-1/x$ (so $\varphi\in\mathcal W_c$ exactly for $0<c<1$ and $\int_0^\infty x^{s-1}\varphi(x)\,dx=\Gamma(s)\zeta(s)$ for $0<\Re s<1$), let $\mu$ be the M\"obius function, $M(x)=\sum_{n\le x}\mu(n)$ and $T_N(x)=\sum_{n\le N}\mu(n)\varphi(nx)$. (1) For every $c\in(0,1)$ the dilates $\{\varphi(nx)\}_{n\in\mathbb N}$ are complete in $\mathcal W_c$, unconditionally. (2) Let $\frac12\le\theta<1$ and suppose $M(x)=O_\varepsilon(x^{\theta+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. Then $T_N\to e^{-x}$ in $\mathcal W_c$ with $\|T_N-e^{-x}\|_c=O_\varepsilon(N^{\theta-c+\varepsilon})$ for $\theta<c<1$ and $0<\varepsilon<c-\theta$. (3) For $\frac12\le\theta<1$, completeness of $\{\varphi(nx)\}$ in $\mathcal W_a\cap\mathcal W_b$ for all $\theta<a<b<1$ is equivalent to $\zeta(s)\ne0$ for $\Re s>\theta$ (the pole at $1$ being allowed); with $\theta=\frac12$ it is equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis.
results.label: lv:thm:zeta

results.name: Under a polynomial bound for the reciprocal of the beta function on the line, the secant dilates over a set with convergent reciprocal sum are not complete
results.summary: Let $c>0$ with $1/\beta(c+it)\ll(1+|t|)^A$ for some $A\ge0$. If $\Lambda\subset[1,\infty)$ has $\sum_\Lambda1/\lambda<\infty$ then $\{\operatorname{sech}(\lambda x)\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ is not complete in $\mathcal W_c$, so under the bound completeness holds if and only if $\sum_\Lambda1/\lambda=\infty$. The line $c=\frac12$ is not covered and stays open.
results.statement: For $c>0$ let $\mathcal W_c=L^2((0,\infty),x^{2c-1}dx)$ and $\operatorname{sech}=1/\cosh$ and let $\beta(s)=L(s,\chi_4)=1-3^{-s}+5^{-s}-\cdots$ be the Dirichlet beta function, with $\chi_4$ the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$. Let $c>0$ and assume $(\mathrm N_c)$: $1/\beta(c+it)\ll(1+|t|)^{A}$ for some $A\ge0$ and all real $t$. If $\Lambda\subset[1,\infty)$ and $\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}1/\lambda<\infty$, then $\{\operatorname{sech}(\lambda x)\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ is not complete in $\mathcal W_c$. So under $(\mathrm N_c)$ the dilates are complete in $\mathcal W_c$ if and only if $\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}1/\lambda=\infty$. The hypothesis $(\mathrm N_c)$ holds unconditionally for $c\ge1$ and fails at $c=\frac12$, where $\beta$ has zeros on the line.
results.label: lv:thm:nec

results.name: The secant dilates are complete in W_c if and only if the reciprocal sum of the dilations diverges, for c at least one, for c above 7/8 given a zero free half plane, and for c not one half under GRH
results.status_text: conditional on The zero free half plane $\Re s>\frac78$ for $L(s,\chi_4)$, which holds if the quasi Riemann hypothesis preprints (OpenAI, announced for Dirichlet $L$ functions, unrefereed and not checked for this book) cover the character modulo $4$; the part for $c\ge1$ is unconditional, and the part for $c\ne\frac12$ needs the generalised Riemann hypothesis for $\beta$
results.conditions: The zero free half plane $\Re s>\frac78$ for $L(s,\chi_4)$, which holds if the quasi Riemann hypothesis preprints (OpenAI, announced for Dirichlet $L$ functions, unrefereed and not checked for this book) cover the character modulo $4$; the part for $c\ge1$ is unconditional, and the part for $c\ne\frac12$ needs the generalised Riemann hypothesis for $\beta$
results.summary: For $c\ge1$ (unconditional), for $c>\frac78$ given the zero free half plane $\Re s>\frac78$ for $L(s,\chi_4)$, and for every $c>0$, $c\ne\frac12$, under the generalised Riemann hypothesis for $\beta$: $\{\operatorname{sech}(\lambda x)\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ is complete in $\mathcal W_c$ if and only if $\sum_\Lambda1/\lambda=\infty$.
results.statement: For $c>0$ let $\mathcal W_c=L^2((0,\infty),x^{2c-1}dx)$ and $\operatorname{sech}=1/\cosh$ and let $\beta(s)=L(s,\chi_4)=1-3^{-s}+5^{-s}-\cdots$ be the Dirichlet beta function, with $\chi_4$ the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$. For $\Lambda\subset[1,\infty)$, $\{\operatorname{sech}(\lambda x)\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ is complete in $\mathcal W_c$ if and only if $\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}1/\lambda=\infty$, in each of these cases: for $c\ge1$ (unconditionally); for $c>\frac78$ given that $L(s,\chi_4)\ne0$ for $\Re s>\frac78$; and for every $c>0$ with $c\ne\frac12$ under the generalised Riemann hypothesis for $\beta$.
results.label: lv:cor:iff

results.name: Salem's criterion in L1: dilates of the Fermi or secant kernel over a divergent set are complete if and only if the Mellin transform has no zero on the line
results.summary: For $\sigma>0$, $k\in\{1/(e^x+1),\operatorname{sech}x\}$ and $\Lambda\subset[1,\infty)$ with $\sum_\Lambda1/\lambda=\infty$, $\{x^{\sigma-1}k(\lambda x)\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ is complete in $L^1(0,\infty)$ if and only if the Mellin transform of $k$ has no zero on $\Re s=\sigma$; for $\frac12<\sigma<1$ this is zero freeness of $\zeta$, respectively $\beta$, on that line.
results.statement: Let $\sigma>0$, let $k$ be $1/(e^x+1)$ or $\operatorname{sech}x$, and let $\Lambda\subset[1,\infty)$ satisfy $\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}1/\lambda=\infty$. Then $\{x^{\sigma-1}k(\lambda x)\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ is complete in $L^1(0,\infty)$ if and only if the Mellin transform of $k$ has no zero on the line $\Re s=\sigma$. In particular, for $\frac12<\sigma<1$ the integer dilates of the Fermi kernel $1/(e^x+1)$ are complete in $L^1$ if and only if the Riemann zeta function has no zero on $\Re s=\sigma$, and the integer dilates of $\operatorname{sech}$ if and only if the Dirichlet beta function $\beta=L(\cdot,\chi_4)$ has none.
results.label: lv:thm:salem

results.name: The weighted error of an arbitrary combination of secant dilates is an integral over the Mellin line with the factor 2 in 2D_N - 1/beta, split at a segment
results.summary: For $c>0$, $T\ge1$ and any coefficients $a_n$, $\|e^{-x}-\sum_{n\le N}a_n\operatorname{sech}(nx)\|_c^2=\frac1{2\pi}\int|\Gamma(c+it)|^2|1-2\beta D_N|^2dt$, which is at most the integral over $|t|\le T$ plus $C_ce^{-\pi T}T^{2c}(1+\|a\|_{N,c})^2$; where $\beta\ne0$ the integrand is $|K_c(t)|^2|2D_N-1/\beta|^2$, with the factor $2$ and not $D_N-1/\beta$.
results.statement: For $c>0$ let $\mathcal W_c=L^2((0,\infty),x^{2c-1}dx)$ and $\operatorname{sech}=1/\cosh$, let $\beta(s)=L(s,\chi_4)=1-3^{-s}+5^{-s}-\cdots$ be the Dirichlet beta function, with $\chi_4$ the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $c>0$, $T\ge1$ and $a_n$ arbitrary complex coefficients, with $D_N(s)=\sum_{n\le N}a_nn^{-s}$, $\|a\|_{N,c}=\sum_{n\le N}|a_n|n^{-c}$ and $K_c(t)=\Gamma(c+it)\beta(c+it)$. Then $\|e^{-x}-\sum_{n\le N}a_n\operatorname{sech}(nx)\|_c^2=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}|\Gamma(c+it)|^2|1-2\beta(c+it)D_N(c+it)|^2dt$, and this is at most $\frac1{2\pi}\int_{|t|\le T}|\Gamma(c+it)|^2|1-2\beta D_N|^2dt+C_ce^{-\pi T}T^{2c}(1+\|a\|_{N,c})^2$ for a constant $C_c$ depending only on $c$. Where $\beta\ne0$ the integrand of the first term is $|K_c(t)|^2|2D_N-1/\beta|^2$. The Mellin transform of $\operatorname{sech}(nx)$ carries the factor $2$, which is why $2D_N-1/\beta$ appears and not $D_N-1/\beta$.
results.label: lv:prop:segment

results.name: The Mellin transform of the symmetric Meixner density of order t is an explicit multiple of an entire Dirichlet type series Z_t
results.summary: For $0<\Re s<1$, $M_t(s)=\int_0^\infty x^{s-1}|\Gamma(\frac t2+\frac{ix}2)|^2dx=2^s\pi\Gamma(t)Z_t(1-s)/\sin(\pi s/2)$ with $Z_t$ entire, $Z_1(w)=2^w\beta(w)$, $Z_2(w)=\eta(w-1)$, $Z_3(w)=2^{w-3}(\beta(w)-\beta(w-2))$.
results.statement: For $t>0$ let $f_t(x)=|\Gamma(\frac t2+\frac{ix}2)|^2$, $x>0$. For $0<\Re s<1$, $M_t(s)=\int_0^\infty x^{s-1}f_t(x)\,dx=2^s\pi\,\Gamma(t)Z_t(1-s)/\sin(\pi s/2)$, where $Z_t$ is the entire function $Z_t(w)=\Gamma(w)^{-1}\int_0^\infty u^{w-1}(2\cosh(u/2))^{-t}\,du=\sum_{k\ge0}(-1)^k\binom{t+k-1}{k}(k+\frac t2)^{-w}$ for $\Re w>t-1$. With $\beta$ the Dirichlet beta function, $\eta(w)=(1-2^{1-w})\zeta(w)$ the Dirichlet eta function and $\zeta$ the Riemann zeta function, $Z_1(w)=2^w\beta(w)$, $Z_2(w)=\eta(w-1)=(1-2^{2-w})\zeta(w-1)$ and $Z_3(w)=2^{w-3}(\beta(w)-\beta(w-2))$. For integer $t$, $Z_t$ is a linear combination of $\eta(w-j)$, $j$ odd, when $t$ is even, and of $2^{w-2i}\beta(w-2i)$ when $t$ is odd.
results.label: lv:thm:meixner

results.name: The dilates of every symmetric Meixner density are complete in every weight over a set of dilations with divergent reciprocal sum
results.summary: For every $t>0$ and $c>0$, $\{f_t(\lambda x)\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ with $\Lambda\subset[1,\infty)$ and $\sum_\Lambda1/\lambda=\infty$ is complete in $\mathcal W_c$, in particular for the integer dilates.
results.statement: For $c>0$ let $\mathcal W_c=L^2((0,\infty),x^{2c-1}dx)$ and $\operatorname{sech}=1/\cosh$ and $f_t(x)=|\Gamma(\frac t2+\frac{ix}2)|^2$ for $t>0$. For every $t>0$ and every $c>0$, $\{f_t(\lambda x)\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ with $\Lambda\subset[1,\infty)$ is complete in $\mathcal W_c$ whenever $\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}1/\lambda=\infty$; in particular the integer dilates are complete. The proof checks that $f_t\in\mathcal W_c$ and that its Mellin transform on $\Re s=c$ is nonzero almost everywhere with the bound $C(1+|\tau|)^Ae^{-\pi|\tau|/2}$, the only properties used in the proof of single weight completeness.
results.label: lv:cor:meixner

results.name: For the cosecant kernel the Möbius series for x e^{-x} converges in every weight, so completeness holds unconditionally in one and two weights
results.summary: With $c_n=\mu(n)$ for odd $n$ and $0$ for even $n$, $e^{-x}=\frac12\sum c_n\operatorname{csch}(nx)$ and $xe^{-x}=\frac12\sum(c_n/n)(nx)\operatorname{csch}(nx)$ with absolute convergence for $x>0$; the second series converges in every $\mathcal W_c$, $c>0$, and $\{(nx)\operatorname{csch}(nx)\}$ is complete in every $\mathcal W_c$ and every $\mathcal W_a\cap\mathcal W_b$, unconditionally.
results.statement: For $c>0$ let $\mathcal W_c=L^2((0,\infty),x^{2c-1}dx)$ and $\operatorname{sech}=1/\cosh$ and let $\mu$ be the M\"obius function, $c_n=\mu(n)$ for odd $n$ and $c_n=0$ for even $n$, and $\operatorname{csch}=1/\sinh$. Then for every $x>0$, with absolute convergence, $e^{-x}=\frac12\sum_{n\ge1}c_n\operatorname{csch}(nx)$ and $xe^{-x}=\frac12\sum_{n\ge1}(c_n/n)(nx)\operatorname{csch}(nx)$, and $\sum_n(c_n/n)n^{-s}=1/((1-2^{-s-1})\zeta(s+1))$ converges absolutely for $\Re s>0$. Consequently the series for $xe^{-x}$ converges absolutely in every $\mathcal W_c$, $c>0$, and $\{(nx)\operatorname{csch}(nx)\}_{n\in\mathbb N}$ is complete in every $\mathcal W_c$ and in every $\mathcal W_a\cap\mathcal W_b$, $0<a<b$, unconditionally.
results.label: lv:thm:t2

results.name: A zero free half plane for Xi is equivalent to F_theta being a GGC Laplace transform, with Thorin measure a sum of squared folded Cauchy laws centred at the ordinates
results.summary: For $\theta\ge\frac12$, $\Xi$ has no zeros in $\Re s>\theta$ if and only if $F_\theta(s)=\Xi(\theta)/\Xi(\theta+\sqrt s)$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC, if and only if $F_\theta$ is analytic in the cut plane, and then the Thorin measure is $U_\theta=\sum_{\Im\rho>0}m_\rho Q_{\theta-\Re\rho,\Im\rho}$ with no linear term; for $\Xi=\xi(\cdot,\chi_4)$ this is two weight completeness of the secant dilates on $(\theta,1)$, for $\Xi=\xi$ of the dilates of $\varphi$.
results.statement: Let $\Xi$ be either the Riemann function $\xi$ or $\xi(\cdot,\chi_4)$ with $\xi(s,\chi_4)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)\beta(s)$; both are entire of order one, real and positive on the real axis, satisfy $\Xi(s)=\Xi(1-s)$ and have the Hadamard product $\Xi(s)=\Xi(0)\prod_\rho(1-s/\rho)$ over the nontrivial zeros $\rho$, paired with $\bar\rho$. For $\theta\ge\frac12$ let $F_\theta(s)=\Xi(\theta)/\Xi(\theta+\sqrt s)$ for $s$ in the plane cut along $(-\infty,0]$, with the principal square root. A probability law on $[0,\infty)$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if its Laplace transform is $\exp(-as-\int_0^\infty\log(1+s/u)U(du))$ with $a\ge0$ and a locally finite positive Thorin measure $U$ on $(0,\infty)$ with $\int_{(0,1)}|\log u|U(du)<\infty$ and $\int_1^\infty u^{-1}U(du)<\infty$. For $a\ge0$ and $\gamma>0$ let $Q_{0,\gamma}=\delta_{\gamma^2}$ and, for $a>0$, $Q_{a,\gamma}$ be the probability measure on $(0,\infty)$ that is the image under $v\mapsto v^2$ of the law of $|\gamma+aC|$ with $C$ standard Cauchy, with density $\frac1{2\pi\sqrt u}[\frac a{a^2+(\sqrt u-\gamma)^2}+\frac a{a^2+(\sqrt u+\gamma)^2}]$. Let $\theta\ge\frac12$. The following are equivalent: (i) $\Xi$ has no zeros in $\Re s>\theta$; (ii) $F_\theta$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC; (iii) $F_\theta$ is analytic in the cut plane. When they hold, the Thorin measure of $F_\theta$ is $U_\theta=\sum_{\rho,\ \Im\rho>0}m_\rho Q_{\theta-\Re\rho,\ \Im\rho}$ over the distinct zeros $\rho$ in the upper half plane with multiplicity $m_\rho$, and $F_\theta(s)=\exp(-\int_0^\infty\log(1+s/u)U_\theta(du))$ with no linear term. For $\Xi=\xi(\cdot,\chi_4)$, (i) is equivalent to two weight completeness of the secant dilates on $(\theta,1)$ (for $\theta<1$, the two weight criterion for $\beta$); for $\Xi=\xi$, to two weight completeness of the dilates of $\varphi(x)=1/(e^x-1)-1/x$ (the zeta version of the two weight criterion).
results.label: lv:thm:thorin

results.name: Reciprocal xi and reciprocal xi of chi_4 are GGC Laplace transforms from theta equal to one unconditionally and from 7/8 given the zero free half plane
results.status_text: conditional on The zero free half plane $\Re s>\frac78$ for the Riemann zeta function and, for the statement about $\xi(\cdot,\chi_4)$, for $L(s,\chi_4)$, from the quasi Riemann hypothesis preprints (OpenAI, unrefereed, announced for Dirichlet $L$ functions; that the theorem covers the character modulo $4$ has not been checked); the part for $\theta\ge1$ is unconditional
results.conditions: The zero free half plane $\Re s>\frac78$ for the Riemann zeta function and, for the statement about $\xi(\cdot,\chi_4)$, for $L(s,\chi_4)$, from the quasi Riemann hypothesis preprints (OpenAI, unrefereed, announced for Dirichlet $L$ functions; that the theorem covers the character modulo $4$ has not been checked); the part for $\theta\ge1$ is unconditional
results.summary: For every $\theta\ge1$, $\xi(\theta)/\xi(\theta+\sqrt s)$ and $\xi(\theta,\chi_4)/\xi(\theta+\sqrt s,\chi_4)$ are Laplace transforms of GGCs with absolutely continuous Thorin measure $U_\theta$; given the zero free half plane $\Re s>\frac78$ this holds for every $\theta\ge\frac78$, with an atom $m_\rho\delta_{\gamma_\rho^2}$ at $\theta=\frac78$ for a zero on $\Re s=\frac78$; for $\theta=\frac12$ and $\xi$ it is the Riemann hypothesis.
results.statement: Let $\Xi$ be either the Riemann function $\xi$ or $\xi(\cdot,\chi_4)$ with $\xi(s,\chi_4)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)\beta(s)$; both are entire of order one, real and positive on the real axis, satisfy $\Xi(s)=\Xi(1-s)$ and have the Hadamard product $\Xi(s)=\Xi(0)\prod_\rho(1-s/\rho)$ over the nontrivial zeros $\rho$, paired with $\bar\rho$. For $\theta\ge\frac12$ let $F_\theta(s)=\Xi(\theta)/\Xi(\theta+\sqrt s)$ for $s$ in the plane cut along $(-\infty,0]$, with the principal square root. A probability law on $[0,\infty)$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if its Laplace transform is $\exp(-as-\int_0^\infty\log(1+s/u)U(du))$ with $a\ge0$ and a locally finite positive Thorin measure $U$ on $(0,\infty)$ with $\int_{(0,1)}|\log u|U(du)<\infty$ and $\int_1^\infty u^{-1}U(du)<\infty$. Let $U_\theta=\sum_{\Im\rho>0}m_\rho Q_{\theta-\Re\rho,\Im\rho}$, over the distinct zeros $\rho$ with $\Im\rho>0$ and with $m_\rho$ the multiplicity of $\rho$, be the Thorin measure of $F_\theta$ when $\Xi$ has no zeros in $\Re s>\theta$, where for $a\ge0$ and $\gamma>0$, $Q_{0,\gamma}=\delta_{\gamma^2}$ and, for $a>0$, $Q_{a,\gamma}$ is the image under $v\mapsto v^2$ of the law of $|\gamma+aC|$ with $C$ standard Cauchy. For every $\theta\ge1$, $F_\theta$ for $\xi$ and for $\xi(\cdot,\chi_4)$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC with the absolutely continuous Thorin measure $U_\theta$, since the zeros have $\Re\rho<1$. Conditionally on the zero free half plane $\Re s>\frac78$ the GGC representation holds for every $\theta\ge\frac78$, and the Thorin measure is absolutely continuous for $\theta>\frac78$, and at $\theta=\frac78$ if no zero lies on $\Re s=\frac78$; a zero $\rho$ on that line contributes an atom $m_\rho\delta_{\gamma_\rho^2}$, $\gamma_\rho=\Im\rho$. For $\theta=\frac12$ the statement for $\xi$ is the Riemann Hypothesis and the Thorin measure is then $\sum_{\gamma>0}m_\gamma\delta_{\gamma^2}$, over the ordinates $\gamma>0$ of the zeros $\frac12+i\gamma$ of $\xi$ with multiplicity $m_\gamma$.
results.label: lv:cor:uncond

results.name: The symmetrised Thorin measures of F_theta form a Cauchy convolution semigroup in theta
results.summary: If $\Xi$ has no zeros in $\Re s>\theta_0$, then $\widetilde U_\theta=\frac12\sum_\rho m_\rho\,\mathrm{Cauchy}(\Im\rho,\theta-\Re\rho)$, with the factor $\frac12$, maps to $U_\theta$ under $v\mapsto v^2$ and $\widetilde U_{\theta'}=\widetilde U_\theta*\mathrm{Cauchy}(0,\theta'-\theta)$ for $\theta_0\le\theta<\theta'$; for $\xi$ this is the Cauchy flow of the book's Poisson structure, credited to Polson (Chapter 8 of his monograph On Hilbert's 8th Problem, 2026).
results.statement: Let $\Xi$ be either the Riemann function $\xi$ or $\xi(\cdot,\chi_4)$ with $\xi(s,\chi_4)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)\beta(s)$; both are entire of order one, real and positive on the real axis, satisfy $\Xi(s)=\Xi(1-s)$ and have the Hadamard product $\Xi(s)=\Xi(0)\prod_\rho(1-s/\rho)$ over the nontrivial zeros $\rho$, paired with $\bar\rho$. For $\theta\ge\frac12$ let $F_\theta(s)=\Xi(\theta)/\Xi(\theta+\sqrt s)$ for $s$ in the plane cut along $(-\infty,0]$, with the principal square root. A probability law on $[0,\infty)$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if its Laplace transform is $\exp(-as-\int_0^\infty\log(1+s/u)U(du))$ with $a\ge0$ and a locally finite positive Thorin measure $U$ on $(0,\infty)$ with $\int_{(0,1)}|\log u|U(du)<\infty$ and $\int_1^\infty u^{-1}U(du)<\infty$. Let $\mathrm{Cauchy}(\gamma,a)$ be the Cauchy law of centre $\gamma$ and scale $a>0$ and $\mathrm{Cauchy}(\gamma,0)=\delta_\gamma$, and let $U_\theta=\sum_{\Im\rho>0}m_\rho Q_{\theta-\Re\rho,\Im\rho}$, over the distinct zeros $\rho$ with $\Im\rho>0$ and with $m_\rho$ the multiplicity of $\rho$, be the Thorin measure of $F_\theta$ when $\Xi$ has no zeros in $\Re s>\theta$, where for $a\ge0$ and $\gamma>0$, $Q_{0,\gamma}=\delta_{\gamma^2}$ and, for $a>0$, $Q_{a,\gamma}$ is the image under $v\mapsto v^2$ of the law of $|\gamma+aC|$ with $C$ standard Cauchy. Suppose $\Xi$ has no zeros in $\Re s>\theta_0$. For $\theta\ge\theta_0$ let $\widetilde U_\theta=\frac12\sum_\rho m_\rho\,\mathrm{Cauchy}(\Im\rho,\theta-\Re\rho)$ be the symmetric measure on $\mathbb R$ in the variable $v$, summed over the distinct zeros $\rho$ of both half planes with multiplicity $m_\rho$ (the factor $\frac12$ is needed: without it the image is $2U_\theta$). Then $U_\theta$ is the image of $\widetilde U_\theta$ under $v\mapsto v^2$, and for $\theta_0\le\theta<\theta'$, $\widetilde U_{\theta'}=\widetilde U_\theta*\mathrm{Cauchy}(0,\theta'-\theta)$. In particular, if all zeros lie on $\Re s=\theta_0$ (which for the completed functions forces $\theta_0=\frac12$), then $\widetilde U_\theta$ is the Poisson smoothing at width $\theta-\theta_0$ of $\frac12\sum_\rho m_\rho\delta_{\Im\rho}$ and converges vaguely to it as $\theta\downarrow\theta_0$. For $\xi$ this is the Cauchy flow of the book's Poisson structure result, credited to Nicholas Polson (Chapter 8 of his monograph On Hilbert's 8th Problem, 2026).
results.label: lv:thm:semigroup

results.name: Laplace transform of Bessel hitting times with curvature
results.summary: The hitting time of radius a by the radial Brownian motion on the three dimensional space form of curvature kappa has an explicit Laplace transform, is a GGC with equally spaced Thorin atoms shifted by minus kappa/2, and is an exponential tilt of the flat case. The flat case is classical (Ciesielski and Taylor 1962), and for kappa < 0 the process is the Bessel process of dimension three with drift (Salminen and Vallois 2007), the norm of a three dimensional Brownian motion with drift, where the formula also follows from the Cameron Martin formula; the formula for the whole family, its Thorin measure and its reading as an exponential tilt are the book's.
results.statement: For real $\kappa$ let $s_\kappa(z)=\sin(\sqrt\kappa z)/\sqrt\kappa$ (so that $s_{-1}=\sinh$, $s_0(z)=z$ and $s_1=\sin$), and let $J^{(\kappa)}_a$ be the hitting time of the radius $a$ from the centre by the radial part of Brownian motion on the three dimensional space form of curvature $\kappa$, the diffusion with generator $\frac12\frac{d^2}{dx^2}+\sqrt\kappa\cot(\sqrt\kappa x)\frac d{dx}$, with $a<\pi/\sqrt\kappa$ when $\kappa>0$. For $\kappa=0$ this is the hitting time $J_a$ of $a$ by the three dimensional Bessel process started at $0$. For $u\ge0$, $\mathbb{E}e^{-uJ^{(\kappa)}_a}=\frac{\sqrt{2u-\kappa}\;s_\kappa(a)}{\sinh\big(a\sqrt{2u-\kappa}\big)}$ (read through $\sinh(ix)/i=\sin x$ when $\kappa>2u$), the Laplace transform of a GGC with Thorin measure $\sum_{n\ge1}\delta_{\pi^2n^2/2a^2-\kappa/2}$. Equivalently, the law of $J^{(\kappa)}_a$ is the exponential tilt $e^{\kappa t/2}\Pr(J_a\in dt)/\mathbb{E}e^{\kappa J_a/2}$ of the law of $J_a$.
results.label: prop:biane:skappa

results.name: Klein Gordon criterion for real zeros
results.summary: If an even positive kernel is the boundary value of a solution of a Klein Gordon equation with a real potential bounded below, with the stated decay and nonvanishing conditions, then every zero of its Fourier transform is real and its square is a Dirichlet eigenvalue.
results.statement: Let $g$ be even, positive and continuous on $\mathbb{R}$ with $\int g(w)e^{c|w|}\,dw<\infty$ for every $c$, and $G(t)=\int g(w)e^{itw}\,dw$. Suppose that there are $x_0\in\mathbb{R}$, a real continuous function $V$ on $[x_0,\infty)$ bounded below, and $F\in C^2([x_0,\infty)\times\mathbb{R})$ such that (a) $(\partial_x^2-\partial_w^2-V(x))F=0$ and $F(x_0,\cdot)=g$; (b) $F$ and its partial derivatives of order at most two are $O(e^{-c|w|})$ for every $c>0$, uniformly for $x$ in compact subsets of $[x_0,\infty)$, and $\Psi_\mu(x)=\int F(x,w)e^{\mu w}\,dw$ lies in $L^2((x_0,\infty))$ for every $\mu\in\mathbb{C}$; (c) $\Psi_\mu$ is not identically zero for any $\mu\in\mathbb{C}$. Then every zero of $G$ is real, and its square is an eigenvalue of $-\frac{d^2}{dx^2}+V$ on $[x_0,\infty)$ with a Dirichlet condition at $x_0$.
results.label: thm:biane:kg

results.name: De Bruijn Newman constant of Pólya's function is finite
results.summary: The Gaussian deformations of Pólya's Bessel function have only real zeros exactly from a finite time Lambda_P at most zero onward, by an argument of Newman, so its de Bruijn Newman constant is not minus infinity, contrary to a conjecture of the first author's earlier note.
results.statement: For real $t$ let $P_t(\theta)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}e^{tu^2/4}e^{-2\pi\cosh2u}\,e^{i\theta u}\,du$, so that $P_0(\theta)=K_{i\theta/2}(2\pi)$ is Pólya's Macdonald function. There is a constant $\Lambda_P$ with $-\infty<\Lambda_P\le0$ such that $P_t$ has only real zeros if and only if $t\ge\Lambda_P$.
results.label: prop:biane:lambdaP

results.name: A property that survives Gaussian damping cannot imply real zeros
results.summary: No property of even positive kernels that implies real zeros and survives a fixed Gaussian damping can hold for Riemann's kernel Phi, for Pólya's asymptote or for the Bessel kernel, which excludes a family of constructions with room to spare, using the theorems of Rodgers and Tao and of Newman.
results.statement: Let $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}\big(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2}\big)\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2u})$ be the Pólya kernel of Riemann's xi function, with $\xi(\frac12+i\theta)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)\cos(\theta u)\,du$, and $\Phi^*(u)=8\pi^2\cosh\frac{9u}2\,e^{-2\pi\cosh2u}$ Pólya's asymptotic replacement. Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property of even, positive, integrable kernels such that (i) if $\mathcal{P}(g)$ holds, then $\int g(u)e^{i\theta u}\,du$ has only real zeros, and (ii) there is $\varepsilon>0$ such that $\mathcal{P}(g)$ implies $\mathcal{P}(e^{-\varepsilon u^2/4}g)$. (a) If (ii) holds for $g=\Phi$, then $\mathcal{P}(\Phi)$ is false. (b) If (ii) holds for all $g$ with the same $\varepsilon$, then $\mathcal{P}(g)$ is false for every kernel $g$ that is $O(e^{-|u|^b})$ for some $b>2$ and satisfies $g(u)e^{Cu^4}\to0$ as $|u|\to\infty$ for every $C$; in particular $\mathcal{P}$ fails for $\Phi$, for $\Phi^*$ and for $e^{-2\pi\cosh2u}$.
results.label: prop:biane:damping

results.name: Open question on a diffusion for the clock of the Riemann xi function
results.summary: Is there, without assuming RH, a diffusion on a half line with an entrance boundary whose hitting time of a level has the Laplace transform of the clock of Riemann's xi function scaled by four?
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)\zeta(s)$ and let $T$ be the clock of $\xi$, the random time with Laplace transform $\mathbb{E}e^{-uT}=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u)$ (it exists without any hypothesis). Is there a diffusion on a half line, with an entrance boundary, whose hitting time of a level from the entrance boundary has the Laplace transform $\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+2\sqrt u)$, that of $4T$, as the clock $\tau_\infty$ of Pólya's Bessel function has the transform $K_0(2\pi)/K_{\sqrt u}(2\pi)$? By Kent's theorem such a hitting time is $\sum_ne_n/\lambda_n$ over the Dirichlet eigenvalues $\lambda_n>0$ of the generator, so a positive answer implies the Riemann hypothesis; under the Riemann hypothesis and the simplicity of the zeros, Krein's inverse spectral theory gives a generalised diffusion with the eigenvalues $\gamma^2/4$, $\frac12+i\gamma$ running over the zeros with $\gamma>0$. The question asks for one constructed without the Riemann hypothesis, for example as a perturbation of the diffusion for Pólya's function, with generator $\frac{d^2}{dx^2}+2\frac{\psi'}\psi\frac d{dx}$ and $\psi(x)=K_0(e^x)$, whose potential $e^{2x}$ has the right Weyl law.
results.label: q:biane:radial

results.name: Open question on a Klein Gordon extension of Pólya's kernel
results.summary: Does the kernel of Riemann's xi function, rescaled, admit a Klein Gordon extension with a real potential asymptotic to e^{2x}, which would imply RH?
results.statement: Let $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}\big(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2}\big)\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2u})$ be the Pólya kernel of Riemann's xi function and $g(w)=\Phi(w/2)$. Does $g$ admit a Klein Gordon extension, that is: a real continuous potential $V$ on some $[x_0,\infty)$, bounded below and asymptotic to $e^{2x}$ at $+\infty$, and a function $F\in C^2([x_0,\infty)\times\mathbb{R})$ with $(\partial_x^2-\partial_w^2-V(x))F=0$ and $F(x_0,\cdot)=g$, such that $F$ and its partial derivatives of order at most two are $O(e^{-c|w|})$ for every $c>0$, uniformly for $x$ in compact sets, and $\Psi_\mu(x)=\int F(x,w)e^{\mu w}\,dw$ lies in $L^2((x_0,\infty))$ for every complex $\mu$ and is not identically zero for any $\mu$? By the Klein Gordon criterion a positive answer implies the Riemann hypothesis. Under the Riemann hypothesis the question asks whether $\mu\mapsto2\xi(\frac12+2\mu)$ is, up to normalisation, the Jost function of such a potential whose Klein Gordon solution has the boundary value $g$.
results.label: q:biane:kg

results.name: Open question on the de Bruijn Newman constants of Pólya's functions
results.summary: What are the de Bruijn Newman constants of Pólya's Bessel function and of his function Xi star, at what height do the first nonreal zeros appear, and do they appear through collisions of real zeros?
results.statement: For real $t$ let $P_t(\theta)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}e^{tu^2/4}e^{-2\pi\cosh2u}\,e^{i\theta u}\,du$ (so that $P_0(\theta)=K_{i\theta/2}(2\pi)$ is Pólya's Macdonald function) and $\Xi^*_t(\theta)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}e^{tu^2/4}\Phi^*(u)e^{i\theta u}\,du$ with Pólya's kernel $\Phi^*(u)=8\pi^2\cosh\frac{9u}2\,e^{-2\pi\cosh2u}$. The de Bruijn Newman constant $\Lambda_P$ of $P$, the least $t$ from which all zeros of $P_t$ are real, satisfies $-\infty<\Lambda_P\le0$, and the same holds for the constant $\Lambda_{\Xi^*}$ of $\Xi^*$. What are $\Lambda_P$ and $\Lambda_{\Xi^*}$? At what height do the first nonreal zeros of $P_t$ appear as $t$ decreases through $\Lambda_P$, and do they appear, as for the de Bruijn Newman flow of Riemann's $\Xi$, through the collision of two real zeros?
results.label: q:biane:lambda

results.name: Open question on a family joining the two clocks
results.summary: Is there a one parameter family of laws joining the drifted first passage time and the sum of two Bessel hitting times, each member with a reciprocal symmetry encoding a functional equation, along which the index side Thorin measure can be followed?
results.statement: Let $H$ be the first passage time of Brownian motion with drift $\sqrt{2\pi}$ to the level $\sqrt{2\pi}$, whose Mellin transform is $\mathbb{E}H^s=2e^{2\pi}K_{s-1/2}(2\pi)$ and for which $1/H$ has the law of $H$ size biased by $H$, a reciprocal symmetry that encodes the functional equation $\mathbb{E}H^s=\mathbb{E}H^{1-s}$. Let $S_2=J_1+J'_1$ be the sum of two independent hitting times of the level $1$ by the three dimensional Bessel process started at $0$, for which $2\xi(s)=\mathbb{E}\big[(\pi S_2/2)^{s/2}\big]$ with Riemann's xi function $\xi$, the functional equation coming from Jacobi's theta transformation. Is there a one parameter family of laws joining the drifted first passage time and the sum of two Bessel hitting times, each with a reciprocal symmetry that encodes a functional equation, along which the index side Thorin measure can be followed? The curvature family of Brownian hitting times, an exponential tilt of the Bessel hitting time, breaks the symmetry. Positivity of the index side Thorin measure at the Bessel end is the Riemann hypothesis.
results.label: q:biane:curv

results.name: Pólya kernel from a sum of two maxima of exponential variables
results.summary: The square e^{2Y} of the variable e^Y built from Riemann's xi function has the law of a sum of two independent copies of the maximum M_4 of independent exponential variables, and the Pólya kernel is recovered from the density of the square root of that sum by an explicit change of variables.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)\zeta(s)$ be Riemann's xi function and $Y$ the random variable with $\mathbb{E}e^{sY}=2\xi(s)$ for every complex $s$. Let $M_4$ be the maximum of independent exponential random variables with one variable of each rate $\pi n$, $n\ge1$, and one more of each rate $\pi(2m-1)$, $m\ge1$, so that $\Pr(M_4\le t)=\prod_{n\ge1}(1-e^{-\pi nt})\prod_{m\ge1}(1-e^{-\pi(2m-1)t})=\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}(-1)^ne^{-\pi n^2t}$ for $t>0$, and let $M_4'$ be an independent copy of $M_4$. Then (i) $e^{2Y}$ has the same law as $M_4+M_4'$. (ii) The density of $e^Y=\sqrt{M_4+M_4'}$ is $f(y)=4\sum_{n\ge1}\big(2\pi^2n^4y^3-3\pi n^2y\big)e^{-\pi n^2y^2}$ for $y>0$, and the Pólya kernel $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}\big(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2}\big)\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2u})$, the even function with $\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)e^{i\theta u}\,du=\xi(\frac12+i\theta)$, satisfies $\Phi(u)=\frac12e^{3u/2}f(e^u)$.
results.label: mw:prop:sum

results.name: Khinchin factorisation of the tilted maximum of exponential variables
results.summary: For sigma above one, the maximum M_4 of independent exponential variables, tilted by the factor m^{sigma/2} and multiplied by an independent geometric factor 4^{-K} that modifies only the prime 2, has the law of a gamma variable divided by pi times the square of a zeta distributed integer.
results.statement: Fix $\sigma>1$. Let $M_4$ be the maximum of independent exponential random variables with one variable of each rate $\pi n$, $n\ge1$, and one more of each rate $\pi(2m-1)$, $m\ge1$, and let $\widetilde M_4$ have the tilted law $\Pr(\widetilde M_4\in dm)\propto m^{\sigma/2}\Pr(M_4\in dm)$. Let $K$, $N_\sigma$ and $\Gamma_{1+\sigma/2}$ be independent of each other and of $\widetilde M_4$, where $\Pr(K=k)=(1-a)a^k$ for $k\ge0$ with $a=2^{1-\sigma}$; $N_\sigma=\prod_pp^{G_p}$ is zeta distributed with parameter $\sigma$, that is $\Pr(N_\sigma=n)=n^{-\sigma}/\zeta(\sigma)$ for $n\ge1$, the product running over the primes $p$ with independent geometric variables $G_p$, $\Pr(G_p=k)=(1-p^{-\sigma})p^{-k\sigma}$; and $\Gamma_{1+\sigma/2}$ is gamma distributed with shape $1+\sigma/2$ and scale $1$. Then $\widetilde M_4\,4^{-K}$ has the same law as $\Gamma_{1+\sigma/2}/(\pi N_\sigma^2)=\frac{\Gamma_{1+\sigma/2}}\pi\prod_pp^{-2G_p}$.
results.label: mw:thm:khinchin

results.name: Wald couples of the maximum of exponential variables and the logistic law
results.summary: The maximum M_4 of independent exponential variables, paired with a uniform variable on (-1,1) scaled by the square root of pi over two, is a Wald couple, as is the pair of sums of two independent copies, and the square root of M_4 times a standard normal variable has the logistic law. The van Dantzig pair involved is classical and the logistic statement is due to Andrews and Mallows and to Stefanski; the book's addition is their reading through the maximum in the language of Wald couples.
results.statement: Call a pair $(\tau,\varsigma)$ of independent random variables with $\tau\ge0$ a Wald couple if $\mathbb{E}e^{s\varsigma}<\infty$ and $\mathbb{E}e^{s\varsigma}\,\mathbb{E}e^{-s^2\tau/2}=1$ for all real $s$; equivalently, with $Z$ standard normal and independent of $\tau$, the characteristic functions $\varphi_1$ of $\varsigma$ and $\varphi_2$ of $\sqrt\tau\,Z$ form a van Dantzig pair, $\varphi_2(t)=1/\varphi_1(it)$. Let $M_4$ be the maximum of independent exponential random variables with one variable of each rate $\pi n$, $n\ge1$, and one more of each rate $\pi(2m-1)$, $m\ge1$, so that $\mathbb{E}e^{-\lambda M_4}=\sqrt{\pi\lambda}/\sinh\sqrt{\pi\lambda}$, let $M_4'$ be an independent copy, let $\upsilon,\upsilon_1,\upsilon_2$ be uniform on $(-1,1)$, independent of each other and of $M_4,M_4'$, and let $c=\sqrt{\pi/2}$. Then $(M_4,c\upsilon)$ and $(M_4+M_4',c(\upsilon_1+\upsilon_2))$ are Wald couples. The associated van Dantzig pairs are $(\sin(ct)/(ct),\ ct/\sinh(ct))$, the characteristic functions of $c\upsilon$ and of $\sqrt{M_4}\,Z$ with $Z$ standard normal and independent of $M_4$, and their squares, and $\sqrt{M_4}\,Z$ has the logistic law, with characteristic function $ct/\sinh(ct)$.
results.label: mw:thm:wald

results.name: Stieltjes criterion for RH through the smoothed Thorin density of the clock
results.summary: The Riemann Hypothesis is equivalent to each of the following: the clock is a GGC, the function G'/G, minus the logarithmic derivative of its transform 1/G, is a Stieltjes function, its heat trace W is completely monotone, and the smoothed Thorin density r_eta(x), the imaginary part of G'/G at minus x minus i eta divided by pi, is nonnegative for all real x and all eta above zero. The form through r_eta is new, and the others are in the book.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)\zeta(s)$, let $\rho$ run over the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$ with $\operatorname{Im}\rho>0$, counted with multiplicity, put $a_\rho=-(\rho-\frac12)^2$ and $G(\lambda)=\xi(\frac12+\sqrt\lambda)/\xi(\frac12)=\prod_\rho(1+\lambda/a_\rho)$. Let $T$ be the clock, the random variable with $\mathbb{E}e^{-\lambda T}=1/G(\lambda)$, which exists with no hypothesis on the zeros. Put $W(x)=\sum_\rho e^{-a_\rho x}$ for $x>0$, so that $(G'/G)(\lambda)=\sum_\rho(\lambda+a_\rho)^{-1}=\int_0^\infty e^{-\lambda x}W(x)\,dx$, and $r_\eta(x)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Im}\frac{G'}G(-x-i\eta)$ for $x\in\mathbb{R}$ and $\eta>0$, wherever $-x-i\eta$ is not a pole of $G'/G$. The following are equivalent. (a) The Riemann Hypothesis (RH). (b) $T$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC), that is $\mathbb{E}e^{-\lambda T}=\exp\big(-a\lambda-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+\lambda/x)\,U(dx)\big)$ for some $a\ge0$ and positive measure $U$, the Thorin measure; then $T$ has the same law as $\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$, and its Thorin measure is $U_{\mathrm{RH}}=\sum_{\gamma>0}\delta_{\gamma^2}$, the ordinates $\gamma=\operatorname{Im}\rho$ counted with multiplicity. (c) $G'/G$ is a Stieltjes function, that is of the form $b+\int_{[0,\infty)}\sigma(dx)/(\lambda+x)$ with $b\ge0$ and $\sigma$ a positive measure. (d) $r_\eta(x)\ge0$ for all $x\in\mathbb{R}$ and $\eta>0$ for which $-x-i\eta$ is not a pole of $G'/G$. (e) $W$ is completely monotone. In that case $r_\eta(x)=\sum_{\gamma>0}\eta/(\pi((x-\gamma^2)^2+\eta^2))$ is the Poisson smoothing of $U_{\mathrm{RH}}$ at scale $\eta$ and $U_{\mathrm{RH}}((0,x])=N(\sqrt x)$, where $N(t)$ is the number of zeros $\rho$ with $0<\operatorname{Im}\rho\le t$, counted with multiplicity.
results.label: mw:thm:stieltjes

results.name: An off line zero makes the smoothed Thorin density of the clock negative
results.summary: If a zero has real part beta above one half and ordinate gamma, the smoothed Thorin density r_eta of the clock at the point gamma squared minus delta squared, with delta equal to beta minus one half, tends to minus infinity as eta increases to twice delta times gamma. An explicit formula gives its value for eta below that and shows when it is negative.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)\zeta(s)$, let $\rho'$ run over the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$ with $\operatorname{Im}\rho'>0$, counted with multiplicity, put $a_{\rho'}=-(\rho'-\frac12)^2$, $G(\lambda)=\xi(\frac12+\sqrt\lambda)/\xi(\frac12)=\prod_{\rho'}(1+\lambda/a_{\rho'})$, so that $1/G$ is the Laplace transform of the clock, and $r_\eta(x)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Im}\frac{G'}G(-x-i\eta)$ for $x\in\mathbb{R}$ and $\eta>0$. Let $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ be a zero of multiplicity $m$ with $\beta>\frac12$ and $\gamma>0$, and put $\delta=\beta-\frac12$, $x_\rho=\gamma^2-\delta^2$ and $b=2\delta\gamma$, so that $a_\rho=x_\rho-ib$. Then $r_\eta(x_\rho)\to-\infty$ as $\eta\uparrow b$. More precisely, for $0<\eta<b$ such that $-x_\rho-i\eta$ is not a pole of $G'/G$, $\pi r_\eta(x_\rho)=\eta\Big(A_\eta-\frac{2m}{b^2-\eta^2}\Big)$, where $A_\eta=\frac1\eta\sum_{\rho'}\operatorname{Im}\,(a_{\rho'}-x_\rho-i\eta)^{-1}$, the sum running over the zeros $\rho'$ with $\operatorname{Im}\rho'>0$, counted with multiplicity, whose $a_{\rho'}$ is neither $a_\rho$ nor $\overline{a_\rho}$. Hence $r_\eta(x_\rho)<0$ at every $\eta\in(0,b)$ with $A_\eta<2m/b^2$. If all the other zeros lie on the critical line, $A_\eta\to A_0=\sum_{\gamma'}(\gamma'^2-x_\rho)^{-2}$ as $\eta\downarrow0$, the sum running over the ordinates $\gamma'>0$ of those zeros, counted with multiplicity.
results.label: mw:lem:detect

results.name: An explicit GGC within a stated Laplace distance of the clock
results.summary: The sum of independent exponential variables divided by the squares of the ordinates of the zeros up to height 3 times 10^12 is a GGC whose Laplace transform is within 2.5 times 10^-11 of the transform of the clock, by a certified bound that uses the verification of RH up to that height and nothing about the zeros above it.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)\zeta(s)$, let $\rho_k=\beta_k+i\gamma_k$, $k\ge1$, be the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$ with $\gamma_k>0$ in nondecreasing order of $\gamma_k$, counted with multiplicity, and put $a_k=-(\rho_k-\frac12)^2$, $G(\lambda)=\xi(\frac12+\sqrt\lambda)/\xi(\frac12)=\prod_k(1+\lambda/a_k)$ and $G_K(\lambda)=\prod_{k\le K}(1+\lambda/\gamma_k^2)$. Let $T$ be the clock, with $\mathbb{E}e^{-\lambda T}=1/G(\lambda)$. For laws $P,Q$ on $[0,\infty)$ with Laplace transforms $L_P,L_Q$ let $d_L(P,Q)=\sup_{\lambda\ge0}|L_P(\lambda)-L_Q(\lambda)|$. Let $H=3\times10^{12}$ and let $N$ be the number of zeros with $0<\gamma_k\le H$, all of which lie on the critical line by the verification of RH up to height $H$ of Platt and Trudgian. Let $T^{[N]}=\sum_{k\le N}e_k/\gamma_k^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_k$, the GGC with Laplace transform $1/G_N$, and put $\varepsilon_H=\sum_{k>N}1/|a_k|$ and $S_K=\sup_{\lambda\ge0}\lambda/G_K(\lambda)$ for $K\le N$. Then $d_L\big(T,T^{[N]}\big)\le S_K\,\varepsilon_H$ for every $K\le N$, with $\varepsilon_H<1.4798\times10^{-12}$ and $S_{1700}<16.85$, so that $d_L\big(T,T^{[N]}\big)<2.5\times10^{-11}$. The proof uses only the verification of RH up to height $H$ and makes no assumption on the zeros above $H$.
results.label: mw:prop:approx

results.name: Term of one zero in the Thorin density of the basepoint family in the lambda chart
results.summary: In the Laplace variable lambda the term of a single zero in the Thorin density at basepoint alpha is a sum of two Poisson kernels divided by twice the square root of lambda. It equals a factor kappa above one times a function that is a Cauchy density when delta is positive, has total mass the sign of delta, and near its peak is a Lorentzian of full width 4 |delta| gamma up to a relative error of order delta squared over gamma squared.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function, $\alpha>\frac12$, $P_\delta(\theta)=\delta/(\pi(\delta^2+\theta^2))$ the Poisson kernel of width $\delta$ (so that $P_{-a}=-P_a$), and $u_\alpha(\lambda)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}\xi(\alpha+i\sqrt\lambda)/(2\pi\sqrt\lambda)$ for $\lambda>0$, the density in the variable $\lambda$ of the Thorin measure of the shifted clock $T_\alpha$, the law with Laplace transform $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt\lambda)$, when every zero has real part below $\alpha$. Let $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ be a nontrivial zero of $\zeta$ with $\gamma>0$ and put $\delta=\alpha-\beta\ne0$ and $c=\alpha-\rho=\delta-i\gamma$. The term of $\rho$ in $u_\alpha=\sum_{\gamma>0}u_\rho$, where the zeros $\rho$ and $\bar\rho$ are paired, is $u_\rho(\lambda)=\big(P_\delta(\sqrt\lambda-\gamma)+P_\delta(\sqrt\lambda+\gamma)\big)/(2\sqrt\lambda)$ for $\lambda>0$, and it satisfies the following. (a) $u_\rho(\lambda)=\kappa_\rho(\lambda)C_\rho(\lambda)=\delta(\lambda+|c|^2)/(\pi\sqrt\lambda\,|c^2+\lambda|^2)$, where $\kappa_\rho(\lambda)=(\lambda+\gamma^2+\delta^2)/(2\gamma\sqrt\lambda)$ and $C_\rho(\lambda)=\frac1\pi\cdot2\delta\gamma/\big((\lambda-\gamma^2+\delta^2)^2+4\delta^2\gamma^2\big)$; for $\delta>0$, $C_\rho$ is the Cauchy density centred at $\gamma^2-\delta^2$ with half width $2\delta\gamma$. (b) $\int_0^\infty u_\rho(\lambda)\,d\lambda=\operatorname{sign}\delta$. (c) $\kappa_\rho(\lambda)\ge\sqrt{1+\delta^2/\gamma^2}>1$ for every $\lambda>0$, $\kappa_\rho(\gamma^2-\delta^2)=(1-\delta^2/\gamma^2)^{-1/2}$ when $|\delta|<\gamma$, and for $K\ge1$ and $|\delta|\le\gamma/(2K)$, $|\kappa_\rho(\lambda)-1|\le(K^2/2+1)\,\delta^2/\gamma^2$ for $|\lambda-\gamma^2|\le K|\delta|\gamma$. Hence near its peak the term is a Lorentzian of full width $4|\delta|\gamma$ at half height, with the sign of $\delta$, up to a relative error $O(\delta^2/\gamma^2)$, while $u_\rho(\lambda)\sim\delta/(\pi(\gamma^2+\delta^2)\sqrt\lambda)$ as $\lambda\downarrow0$ and $u_\rho(\lambda)\sim\delta/(\pi\lambda^{3/2})$ as $\lambda\to\infty$.
results.label: mw:prop:lambda

results.name: The clock is not a maximum of independent exponential variables
results.summary: The negative logarithm of the distribution function of the clock is not completely monotone, so the clock is not the maximum of independent exponential variables with any rates, nor of a Poisson cloud of exponential clocks. The proof compares the first two exponential terms of the tail of the clock, and the coefficient of the second is negative where complete monotonicity would force it to be nonnegative.
results.statement:
Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function, $T$ the clock, the random variable with $\mathbb{E}e^{-\lambda T}=\xi( rac12)/\xi( rac12+\sqrt\lambda)$, and $F_T(t)=\Pr(T\le t)$. Then $-\log F_T$ is not completely monotone on $(0,\infty)$. Hence $T$ does not have the law of a maximum of independent exponential variables $E_i/r_i$, with $E_i$ standard exponential and deterministic rates $r_i>0$ with $\sum_ie^{-r_it}<\infty$ for $t>0$, for any choice of the rates, nor of the maximum of a Poisson cloud of exponential clocks, that is of the variables $E_i/x_i$ attached to the points $x_i$ of a Poisson process of intensity $
u$ on $(0,\infty)$; for both of these laws $-\log F(t)=\int e^{-xt}\,
u(dx)$ for a positive measure $
u$, which is completely monotone in $t$. The proof uses the verification of RH up to height $3	imes10^{12}$ and the simplicity of the zeros of height below $200$.
results.label: mw:prop:nomax

results.name: Gumbel limit for maxima of independent copies of the clock and of the maximum M_4
results.summary: The maximum of n independent copies of the clock, scaled by the square of the first zero ordinate and centred at an explicit logarithm, converges to the Gumbel law, and divided by log n it tends to the reciprocal of that square; the maximum of n copies of M_4, scaled by pi and centred at log(2n), has the same Gumbel limit. This is Gnedenko's theorem applied to the exponential tails of M_4 and of the clock; the book's addition is the reading of the norming constant of the clock as the first atom of its Thorin measure, with the constant given by the first residue.
