results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function, $\Xi(\theta)=\xi(\frac12+i\theta)$, $\gamma_1$ the least positive ordinate of a zero of $\zeta$ (the zero $\frac12+i\gamma_1$ is simple) and $R_1=-2\gamma_1\Xi(0)/\Xi'(\gamma_1)$, the residue at $\lambda=-\gamma_1^2$ of $\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt\lambda)$, the Laplace transform of the clock $T$. Let $M_4$ be the maximum of independent exponential random variables with one variable of each rate $\pi n$, $n\ge1$, and one more of each rate $\pi(2m-1)$, $m\ge1$, and let $M_4^{(j)}$ and $T^{(j)}$, $j\le n$, be independent copies of $M_4$ and of $T$. (i) $\Pr(M_4>t)\sim2e^{-\pi t}$ as $t\to\infty$, and $\Pr\big(\pi\max_{j\le n}M_4^{(j)}-\log(2n)\le x\big)\to\exp(-e^{-x})$ as $n\to\infty$, for every real $x$. (ii) $\Pr(T>t)\sim(R_1/\gamma_1^2)\,e^{-\gamma_1^2t}$ as $t\to\infty$, $\Pr\Big(\gamma_1^2\max_{j\le n}T^{(j)}-\log\frac{R_1n}{\gamma_1^2}\le x\Big)\to\exp(-e^{-x})$ for every real $x$, and $\max_{j\le n}T^{(j)}/\log n\to1/\gamma_1^2$ in probability.
results.label: mw:prop:gnedenko

results.name: Convergence of the finite maxima and of the finite stages of xi
results.summary: Truncating the maximum M_4 at N exponential variables of each kind gives a maximum that differs from M_4 only on an event of probability at most C sqrt(N) e^{-pi sqrt(N)/2}, and the finite stage xi_N of the xi function and its symmetrisation converge to xi uniformly on compact subsets of the open critical strip at the rate N^{1/4} e^{-pi sqrt(N)/4}.
results.statement: Let $(E_n)_{n\ge1}$ and $(E'_m)_{m\ge1}$ be independent standard exponential random variables, for $N\ge1$ let $M_4^{(N)}=\max\big\{E_n/(\pi n)\ (n\le N),\ E'_m/(\pi(2m-1))\ (m\le N)\big\}$, and let $M_4=\lim_NM_4^{(N)}$ be the maximum of all the variables $E_n/(\pi n)$ and $E'_m/(\pi(2m-1))$, $n,m\ge1$. Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)\zeta(s)$ be Riemann's xi function, and define the finite stage $\xi_N(s)=\frac{(s-1)\,\mathbb{E}(M_4^{(N)})^{s/2}}{2(1-2^{1-s})}$ and its symmetrisation $\xi_N^{\mathrm{sym}}(s)=\frac12\big(\xi_N(s)+\xi_N(1-s)\big)$, so that the same expression with $M_4$ in place of $M_4^{(N)}$ is $\xi(s)$ (here $\xi_N$ is the finite stage, not $\xi$ evaluated at $N$). Then (i) $M_4^{(N)}\uparrow M_4$ almost surely, and $\Pr(M_4^{(N)}\ne M_4)\le C\sqrt N\,e^{-\pi\sqrt N/2}$ for a constant $C$ independent of $N$. (ii) For every compact set $K$ in the open strip $0<\operatorname{Re}s<1$ there is a constant $C_K$ with $\sup_K|\xi_N-\xi|\le C_K\,N^{1/4}e^{-\pi\sqrt N/4}$ and $\sup_K|\xi_N^{\mathrm{sym}}-\xi|\le C_K\,N^{1/4}e^{-\pi\sqrt N/4}$ for all $N$.
results.label: mw:thm:finite

results.name: Zeros of the symmetrised finite stages and a sufficient condition for RH
results.summary: By Hurwitz's theorem the zeros of the finite stages converge to the zeros of xi in the open strip, a simple zero on the critical line is approached by exactly one zero of the symmetrised stage, which lies on the line, and if the symmetrised stages have no zeros in the right half of the strip up to heights tending to infinity along some sequence of stages then RH holds. Whether RH implies that hypothesis on the stages is open.
results.statement: Let $M_4^{(N)}$ be the maximum of the independent exponential variables $E_n/(\pi n)$ ($n\le N$) and $E'_m/(\pi(2m-1))$ ($m\le N$), with $E_n,E'_m$ independent standard exponential variables, let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)\zeta(s)$ be Riemann's xi function, $\xi_N(s)=\frac{(s-1)\,\mathbb{E}(M_4^{(N)})^{s/2}}{2(1-2^{1-s})}$ the finite stage and $\xi_N^{\mathrm{sym}}(s)=\frac12\big(\xi_N(s)+\xi_N(1-s)\big)$ its symmetrisation. (a) Every zero of $\xi$ in the open strip $0<\operatorname{Re}s<1$ is a limit of zeros of $\xi_N$, and of zeros of $\xi_N^{\mathrm{sym}}$, with multiplicity, and every limit of zeros of $\xi_N$ inside the open strip is a zero of $\xi$. (b) If $\rho=\frac12+i\gamma$ is a simple zero of $\xi$, then for all large $N$ the function $\xi_N^{\mathrm{sym}}$ has exactly one zero in a small disc about $\rho$, and that zero lies on the critical line. (c) Suppose that there are $N_j\to\infty$ and heights $h_j\to\infty$ such that $\xi^{\mathrm{sym}}_{N_j}$ has no zeros in $\{\frac12<\operatorname{Re}s<1,\ |\operatorname{Im}s|<h_j\}$ for every $j$. Then the Riemann Hypothesis holds. In particular this is so if there are $c>0$ and $N_0$ such that for every $N\ge N_0$ the function $\xi^{\mathrm{sym}}_N$ has no zeros in $\{\frac12<\operatorname{Re}s<1,\ |\operatorname{Im}s|<c\sqrt N\}$.
results.label: mw:cor:hurwitz

results.name: Finite order GGC, Bondesson and HCM classes of the clock, and RH as the infinite order case
results.summary: From the verification of RH up to height 3 times 10^12 the clock lies in the finite order GGC and Bondesson classes up to order 1.16 times 10^25 and its Laplace transform is hyperbolically completely monotone up to order 9 times 10^12, while RH is equivalent to the clock being a GGC, to its being in the Bondesson class, and to its transform being hyperbolically completely monotone.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)\zeta(s)$ and let $T$ be the clock, with Laplace transform $\varphi(\lambda)=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt\lambda)$ and Lévy density $W(x)/x$, where $W(x)=\sum_\rho e^{(\rho-1/2)^2x}$ is summed over the nontrivial zeros $\rho$ of $\zeta$ with $\operatorname{Im}\rho>0$, counted with multiplicity. A function $f$ on an interval is $k$ monotone if $(-1)^jf^{(j)}\ge0$ for $0\le j\le k$, and completely monotone if it is $k$ monotone for every $k$. For $k\ge1$ let $\mathrm{GGC}_k$ be the class of laws on $[0,\infty)$ with a Lévy density $\ell$ such that $x\ell(x)$ is $k$ monotone, and $\mathrm{BO}_k$ the class with $\ell$ itself $k$ monotone, so that $\mathrm{GGC}_k\subset\mathrm{BO}_k$, $\mathrm{GGC}_1$ is the self decomposable class, $\bigcap_k\mathrm{GGC}_k$ is the class GGC of generalised gamma convolutions and $\bigcap_k\mathrm{BO}_k=\mathrm{BO}$ is the Bondesson class. A positive function $\varphi$ on $(0,\infty)$ is HCM (hyperbolically completely monotone) of order $k$ if for every $u>0$ the function $w\mapsto\varphi(uv)\varphi(u/v)$, $w=v+1/v\ge2$, is $k$ monotone on $[2,\infty)$, and HCM if it is HCM of every order. Let $H=3\times10^{12}$. Statements (i) and (ii) are unconditional: they use the verification of RH up to height $H$ of Platt and Trudgian. (i) $T\in\mathrm{GGC}_k$, and hence $T\in\mathrm{BO}_k$, for every $k\le1.16\times10^{25}$. (ii) $\varphi$ is HCM of order $k$ for every $k\le9\times10^{12}$. (iii) With no hypothesis, the following are equivalent: RH; $T$ is a GGC; $T\in\mathrm{BO}$; $\varphi$ is HCM; $\varphi$ is HCM of every order.
results.label: mw:thm:bondesson

results.name: Finite arithmetic form of the basepoint density below basepoint one
results.status_text: conditional on Part (b) assumes the Riemann hypothesis. Part (a) holds without any hypothesis, and part (c) holds without any hypothesis when delta is at least one half and otherwise needs that every zero lies within delta of the critical line, which the Riemann hypothesis gives for every delta above zero
results.conditions: Part (b) assumes the Riemann hypothesis. Part (a) holds without any hypothesis, and part (c) holds without any hypothesis when delta is at least one half and otherwise needs that every zero lies within delta of the critical line, which the Riemann hypothesis gives for every delta above zero.
results.summary: For basepoint alpha equal to one half plus delta, a Fejér tapered sum over the primes below e^X, two explicit pole terms and one gamma integral define a quantity A_X, which is half the sum over all zeros rho of a function that is nonnegative on the real line, evaluated at (rho minus one half)/i, is nonnegative under RH, and tends to the real part of the logarithmic derivative of xi at alpha plus it as X grows when every zero lies within delta of the critical line.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function, $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function, $\psi$ the digamma function, $\alpha=\frac12+\delta$ with $\delta>0$, $t\in\mathbb{R}$ and $X>0$. Put $g_X(x)=e^{-\delta|x|}\cos(tx)\,(1-|x|/X)_+$ and $h_X(r)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}g_X(x)e^{irx}\,dx$, so that $h_X\ge0$ on $\mathbb{R}$: it is $(2\pi)^{-1}$ times the convolution of the two sided Poisson kernel $h_\infty(r)=\frac\delta{\delta^2+(t-r)^2}+\frac\delta{\delta^2+(t+r)^2}$ with the Fejér kernel $4\sin^2(Xr/2)/(Xr^2)$. Define $A_X(\delta,t)=\frac12\Big[h_X(\tfrac i2)+h_X(-\tfrac i2)-\log\pi+\frac1{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb{R}}h_X(r)\operatorname{Re}\psi\big(\tfrac14+\tfrac{ir}2\big)\,dr-2\sum_{n<e^X}\frac{\Lambda(n)}{n^{\alpha}}\cos(t\log n)\Big(1-\frac{\log n}X\Big)\Big]$, where $h_X(\tfrac i2)+h_X(-\tfrac i2)=2\operatorname{Re}\big[J(-\delta+\tfrac12+it)+J(-\delta-\tfrac12+it)\big]$ with $J(c)=-1/c+(e^{cX}-1)/(Xc^2)$. For a nontrivial zero $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ of $\zeta$ put $\gamma_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)/i$. Then (a) unconditionally, $A_X(\delta,t)=\frac12\sum_\rho h_X(\gamma_\rho)$, the sum over all nontrivial zeros. (b) Under RH, $A_X(\delta,t)\ge0$ for every $X$, $\delta$ and $t$; in particular a single triple $(\delta,t,X)$ with $A_X(\delta,t)<0$ would disprove RH. (c) If every zero has $|\beta-\frac12|<\delta$ (under RH, or unconditionally when $\delta\ge\frac12$), then $A_X(\delta,t)\to\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}\xi(\alpha+it)$ as $X\to\infty$.
results.label: mw:prop:AX

results.name: Zero freeness of the symmetric finite stages of the maximum
results.summary: Find heights tending to infinity such that, for infinitely many N, the symmetric finite stage of the maximum has no zeros in the right half of the critical strip below that height, for instance heights of order the square root of N; either statement would prove RH. Numerical counts for N up to 96 suggest that the zeros stay on the line up to a height of order N, and a mechanism for that is the first thing to find.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function. For $N\ge1$ let $M_4^{(N)}$ be the maximum of the independent exponential variables $E_n/(\pi n)$ ($n\le N$) and $E'_m/(\pi(2m-1))$ ($m\le N$), with $E_n,E'_m$ independent standard exponential variables, so that $\Pr(M_4^{(N)}\le t)=\sum_{m\ge0}p^{(N)}_me^{-\pi mt}$ where $\sum_{m\ge0}p^{(N)}_mq^m=\prod_{n\le N}(1-q^n)\prod_{m\le N}(1-q^{2m-1})$, and put $D_N(s)=\sum_{m\ge1}p^{(N)}_mm^{-s/2}$, a Dirichlet polynomial with integer coefficients. Let $F_N(s)=\frac{s-1}2\,\mathbb{E}\big(M_4^{(N)}\big)^{s/2}=-\frac{s-1}2\,\Gamma(1+\frac s2)\pi^{-s/2}D_N(s)$ and $F^{\mathrm{sym}}_N(s)=\frac12\big(F_N(s)+F_N(1-s)\big)$; as $N\to\infty$, $F^{\mathrm{sym}}_N\to\mathfrak q\,\xi$ uniformly on compact subsets of the open strip $0<\operatorname{Re}s<1$, with $\mathfrak q(s)=1-2^{-s}-2^{s-1}$. Find heights $h_N\to\infty$ such that for infinitely many $N$ the function $F^{\mathrm{sym}}_N$ has no zeros with $\frac12<\operatorname{Re}s<1$ and $|\operatorname{Im}s|<h_N$, for instance $h_N=c\sqrt N$ with some $c>0$. Either statement implies the Riemann Hypothesis, by Hurwitz's theorem, because a zero of $\xi$ in that region would be a zero of the limit $\mathfrak q\,\xi$. Numerical counts of zeros by the argument principle show, for $N=8$, $16$, $32$, $48$, $64$ and $96$, that all zeros of $F^{\mathrm{sym}}_N$ with $-1\le\operatorname{Re}s\le2$ and $0<\operatorname{Im}s\le T^*(N)$ lie on the critical line, for a height $T^*(N)$ of order $N$ (at $N=128$ a pair outside the strip $0<\operatorname{Re}s<1$ appears at height $60.7$, while the strip has no off line zero below $130$), and the sharper conjecture is $T^*(N)\ge\kappa N$ for some $\kappa>0$ and all $N$, which would also imply RH. A mechanism for $T^*(N)$, presumably through the ratio $|D_N(\sigma+it)/D_N(1-\sigma+it)|$, is the first thing to find.
results.label: mw:prob:hurwitz

results.name: A termwise positive continuation of the prime form below basepoint one
results.summary: Is there a continuation of the sine squared prime form of the Thorin density below basepoint one that is positive term by term, for instance through smoothed prime sums with a cutoff near e^{1/epsilon} whose loss can be controlled by the logarithmic derivative of xi at alpha, the gamma sum and the pole terms? A positive answer for every basepoint in (alpha_0, 1] would prove the zero free region beta at most alpha_0.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function. For $\alpha>1$ the density $v_\alpha(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}\xi(\alpha+i\theta)$ has the sine squared prime form, through a signed canonical measure (atoms $\Lambda(n)n^{-\alpha}$ at $\log n$, with $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function, an archimedean density and a pole density) whose prime and gamma terms are nonnegative and whose pole terms are negative; its positivity, which is Lagarias positivity for $\alpha>1$, comes from the absence of zeros with real part at least one, not from the terms one by one. The book continues this form below $\alpha=1$ by compensation, and shows that the compensated sine squared sum converges for every $\alpha'>\alpha$ exactly when $\zeta$ has no zero with $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha$; a smoothed finite form, built from a Fejér tapered sum over the primes with explicit pole terms and a gamma integral, continues the identity below $\alpha=1$ but is not positive term by term. Is there a continuation of the prime form below $\alpha=1$ that is positive term by term? The prime sum diverges there, but smoothed versions of it, with $n^{-\alpha}$ replaced by a weight that cuts off at $n\approx e^{1/\varepsilon}$, remain positive termwise, and the question is whether the loss from the cutoff can be controlled by $(\xi'/\xi)(\alpha)$, the gamma sum and the pole terms. A positive answer on $\alpha\in(\alpha_0,1]$ would prove the zero free region $\beta\le\alpha_0$, that is, that $\zeta$ has no zero with real part above $\alpha_0$.
results.label: mw:prob:lagarias

results.name: Existence of the half flow clock for small positive times
results.summary: For times t between 0 and 0.2, does the law with Laplace transform R_t(lambda/2), half of the clock of the de Bruijn Newman flow, exist as a probability law, and is it infinitely divisible? Unconditionally it is known to exist at t = 0, where it is half the clock, and to exist and be a GGC for t at least 0.2; under RH it exists and is a GGC for every t at least 0.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function, $\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}\big(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u}\big)\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})$ the Pólya kernel in the rescaled variable of Rodgers and Tao, so that $H_0(z)=\int_0^\infty\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cos(zu)\,du=\frac18\xi(\frac12+\frac{iz}2)$, and $H_t(z)=\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cos(zu)\,du$ its de Bruijn Newman deformation, with de Bruijn Newman constant $\Lambda$, the least $t$ from which all zeros of $H_t$ are real, known to satisfy $0\le\Lambda\le0.2$ by Rodgers and Tao, Platt and Trudgian, and the Polymath project. Let $R_t(u)=H_t(0)/H_t(2i\sqrt u)$, the Laplace transform of the clock of the flow, with $R_0(u)=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u)$. For $t\ge\Lambda$, $R_t$ is the transform of a GGC with Thorin measure $\sum_k\delta_{(z_k(t)/2)^2}$, where $z_k(t)>0$ are the positive zeros of $H_t$, each pair $\pm z$ giving one atom; so the law $T_t$ with Laplace transform $\lambda\mapsto R_t(\lambda/2)$ exists and is a GGC for $t\ge0.2$ unconditionally and, under RH, for every $t\ge0$, and $T_0$ is half the clock, which exists unconditionally. For $0<t<0.2$, does $T_t$ exist as a probability law, and is it infinitely divisible? This is the analogue along the de Bruijn Newman flow of the existence of the clock; it would need an explicit formula for the heat trace of the flow, which the Gaussian tilt destroys.
results.label: mw:prob:flow

results.name: An analogue of the Khinchin factorisation at one half
results.summary: Is there an analogue at sigma equal to one half of the Khinchin factorisation of the tilted maximum, that is, a factorisation of the tilted law of the clock or of the Pólya variable through a law built from the primes, with the explicit formula replacing the Euler product?
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(\theta)=\xi(\frac12+i\theta)$. For $\sigma>1$ the maximum $M_4$ of independent exponential variables with one variable of each rate $\pi n$ and one more of each rate $\pi(2m-1)$, tilted to the law $\propto x^{\sigma/2}\Pr(M_4\in dx)$ and multiplied by an independent factor $4^{-K}$ with $\Pr(K=k)=(1-a)a^k$ for $k\ge0$ and $a=2^{1-\sigma}$, has the law of $\Gamma_{1+\sigma/2}/(\pi N_\sigma^2)$, where $\Gamma_{1+\sigma/2}$ is a gamma variable of shape $1+\sigma/2$ and scale $1$ and $N_\sigma$ is an independent zeta distributed integer, $\Pr(N_\sigma=n)=n^{-\sigma}/\zeta(\sigma)$, built from the primes by the Euler product. Is there an analogue of this factorisation at $\sigma=\frac12$, that is, a factorisation of the tilted law of the clock $T$ (the random variable with Laplace transform $\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt\lambda)$) or of the Pólya variable (the variable with characteristic function $\Xi(\theta)/\Xi(0)$) through a law built from the primes, with the explicit formula replacing the Euler product?
results.label: mw:prob:khinchin

results.name: Each term of the theta series kernel is an explicit combination of two Gumbel kernels of fractional order
results.summary: With $x=-4u-\log(\pi n^2)$, $\phi_n(u)\,du=\pi^{-1/4}n^{-1/2}\Gamma(\frac54)[\frac58g_{9/4}(x)-\frac34g_{5/4}(x)]\,dx$ with $g_k(x)=e^{-kx}\exp(-e^{-x})/\Gamma(k)$, and its Fourier transform is $\frac14n^{-s}\xi(s)/\zeta(s)$ with $s=(1+iz)/2$.
results.statement: Let $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}\phi_n(u)$ with $\phi_n(u)=(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})e^{-\pi n^2e^{4u}}$ and let $g_k(x)=e^{-kx}\exp(-e^{-x})/\Gamma(k)$ be the density of $-\log G_k$ for a gamma variable $G_k$ of shape $k$. With $x=-4u-\log(\pi n^2)$, as densities in $x$, $\phi_n(u)\,du=\pi^{-1/4}n^{-1/2}\Gamma(\frac54)[\frac58g_{9/4}(x)-\frac34g_{5/4}(x)]\,dx$. The signed mass of the term is $-\frac18\pi^{-1/4}\Gamma(\frac54)n^{-1/2}$, and the formal sum of the masses, regularised by $\zeta$, is $-\frac18\pi^{-1/4}\Gamma(\frac54)\zeta(\frac12)=\frac14\xi(\frac12)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi$. With $s=(1+iz)/2$, $\int_{\mathbb R}\phi_n(u)e^{izu}\,du=\frac14n^{-s}\xi(s)/\zeta(s)$.
results.label: ev:thm:decomp

results.name: Zeros of the Dirichlet polynomial of the Dyck chain at n equal to 25600 below height 60 (computed)
results.summary: For the Dirichlet polynomial $F_n(s)=\mathbb{E}Y_n^s$ of the Dyck chain at $n=25600$, an argument principle count in ball arithmetic gives 13 zeros with $-4<\operatorname{Re}s<6$ and $0<\operatorname{Im}s<60$, none with real part above $\frac12$ (between $0.0907$ and $0.4553$), 13 being the number of ordinates $\gamma_k$ below 60; a computation at this $n$ only.
results.statement: Let $H_n$ be the height of a uniform Dyck path of length $2n$, $Y_n=\sqrt{2/\pi}\,H_n/\sqrt{2n}$, $F_n(s)=\mathbb{E}Y_n^s$ (a Dirichlet polynomial in $s$), and $\gamma_k$ the positive ordinates of the zeros $\frac12+i\gamma_k$ of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line. The number of Dyck paths of length $2n$ and height at most $h$ is $\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}\big[\binom{2n}{n+k(h+2)}-\binom{2n}{n-1+k(h+2)}\big]$, out of $\binom{2n}{n}/(n+1)$. At $n=25600$, with these probabilities as balls at $256$ bits, the argument principle on the boundary of $-4<\operatorname{Re}s<6$, $0<\operatorname{Im}s<60$ counts $13$ zeros of $F_n$, in the bands $0<\operatorname{Im}s<20$, $20<\operatorname{Im}s<40$ and $40<\operatorname{Im}s<60$ the numbers $1$, $5$ and $7$ that the ordinates $\gamma_k$ have (there are $13$ of them below $60$). There is no zero with $\frac12<\operatorname{Re}s<6$ and $0<\operatorname{Im}s<60$, and the real parts of the $13$ zeros run from $0.0907$ (the highest, at height $59.126$) to $0.4553$ (the lowest, at height $14.072$). Followed in $n$ from $25600$ through $12800$, $6400$ and $3200$ down to $1600$, with Newton's method started at the zero found for the next larger $n$, the $13$ zeros stay distinct and to the left of the line, and the zero of lowest height lies at distance $0.3082$, $0.1544$ and $0.0773$ from $\frac12+i\gamma_1$ for $n=1600$, $6400$ and $25600$. The count is for $n=25600$ only: at $n=1600$ the same contour holds $14$ zeros, and Newton's method started at $\frac12+i\gamma_k$ does not stay near it for $k=4,\dots,12$ (the starts $k=7$ and $8$ converge to one zero), so the zeros are identified by following them in $n$. This is a computation and no proof for other $n$. The computation follows a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book.
results.label: ev:res:dyckcensus

results.name: Lattice bias expansion of the Dirichlet polynomial of the Dyck chain (conjecture)
results.summary: Conjecture that $F_n(s)=2\xi(s)-\frac{3s}{\sqrt{\pi n}}\xi(s-1)+O(1/n)$ locally uniformly on $\operatorname{Re}s>0$ for the Dirichlet polynomial of the Dyck chain, consistent with the mean height of de Bruijn, Knuth and Rice.
results.statement: Let $H_n$ be the height of a uniform Dyck path of length $2n$, $Y_n=\sqrt{2/\pi}\,H_n/\sqrt{2n}$, $F_n(s)=\mathbb{E}Y_n^s$, and $\xi$ the Riemann xi function. Conjecture (open): uniformly on every compact subset of $\operatorname{Re}s>0$, $F_n(s)=2\xi(s)-\frac{3s}{\sqrt{\pi n}}\xi(s-1)+O(1/n)$. At $s=1$ it says $\mathbb{E}H_n=\sqrt{\pi n}-\frac32+O(n^{-1/2})$, which agrees with the expansion of de Bruijn, Knuth and Rice, and it implies that $F_n\to2\xi$ locally uniformly on $\operatorname{Re}s>0$. The zeros computed for the chain agree with its consequence (computed). The conjecture follows a heuristic about the lattice of heights in a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book.
results.label: ev:conj:lbias

results.name: First order displacement of the zeros of the Dyck chain polynomial from the zeros of xi (conditional)
results.status_text: conditional on The lattice bias conjecture, that $F_n(s)=2\xi(s)-\frac{3s}{\sqrt{\pi n}}\xi(s-1)+O(1/n)$ locally uniformly on $\operatorname{Re}s>0$
results.conditions: The lattice bias conjecture, that $F_n(s)=2\xi(s)-\frac{3s}{\sqrt{\pi n}}\xi(s-1)+O(1/n)$ locally uniformly on $\operatorname{Re}s>0$
results.summary: Assuming the lattice bias conjecture, each simple zero $\rho$ of $\xi$ has exactly one zero of $F_n$ at $\rho+\delta_nc_{\rm D}(\rho)+O(1/n)$ for large $n$, with $\delta_n=3/(2\sqrt{2n})$.
results.statement: Let $F_n(s)=\mathbb{E}Y_n^s$ be the Dirichlet polynomial of the Dyck chain ($Y_n=\sqrt{2/\pi}\,H_n/\sqrt{2n}$, $H_n$ the height of a uniform Dyck path of length $2n$), $\xi$ the Riemann xi function and $\delta_n=3/(2\sqrt{2n})$. Assume that, uniformly on compact subsets of $\operatorname{Re}s>0$, $F_n(s)=2\xi(s)-\frac{3s}{\sqrt{\pi n}}\xi(s-1)+O(1/n)$. Let $\rho$ be a simple zero of $\xi$ and put $c_{\rm D}(\rho)=\sqrt{2/\pi}\,\rho\,\xi(\rho-1)/\xi'(\rho)=\sqrt{2/\pi}\,\rho\,\xi(2-\rho)/\xi'(\rho)$. There is a constant $C$ such that for all large $n$, $F_n$ has exactly one zero $z_n(\rho)$ in the disc $|s-\rho-\delta_nc_{\rm D}(\rho)|<C/n$; thus $z_n(\rho)=\rho+\delta_nc_{\rm D}(\rho)+O(1/n)$. The conditional statement is proved by Rouch\'e's theorem from the conjecture.
results.label: ev:prop:lbias

results.name: Phase formula for the lattice bias coefficient at a zero on the critical line
results.summary: For a simple zero $\frac12+i\gamma$ of $\xi$ the displacement coefficient $c_{\rm D}$ equals $-C_{\rm D}(\gamma)e^{-i\Theta(\gamma)}/Z'(\gamma)$ with explicit positive $C_{\rm D}$ and phase $\Theta$, so the sign of its real part is that of $-\cos\Theta(\gamma)/Z'(\gamma)$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the Riemann xi function, $\rho=\frac12+i\gamma$, $\gamma>0$, a simple zero of $\zeta$ on the critical line, $Z$ the Hardy function with Riemann Siegel phase $\theta$ ($\zeta(\frac12+it)=e^{-i\theta(t)}Z(t)$), and $c_{\rm D}(\rho)=\sqrt{2/\pi}\,\rho\,\xi(\rho-1)/\xi'(\rho)$. Then $c_{\rm D}(\rho)=-C_{\rm D}(\gamma)e^{-i\Theta(\gamma)}/Z'(\gamma)$ with $C_{\rm D}(\gamma)=\frac{\sqrt2}{\pi}\,|\frac32-i\gamma|\,\big|\Gamma(\frac34+\frac{i\gamma}2)/\Gamma(\frac14+\frac{i\gamma}2)\big|\,|\zeta(\frac32+i\gamma)|>0$ and $\Theta(\gamma)=\theta(\gamma)+\arctan\tanh\frac{\pi\gamma}2+\arg\zeta(\frac32+i\gamma)-\arctan\frac3{2\gamma}$, so that $\operatorname{Re}c_{\rm D}(\rho)$ has the sign of $-\cos\Theta(\gamma)/Z'(\gamma)$.
results.label: ev:prop:lbphase

results.name: Lattice bias displacement of the Dyck chain zeros, computed for 200 zeros of xi and the zero near the 64th (computed)
results.summary: In ball arithmetic $\operatorname{Re}c_{\rm D}(\rho_k)<0$ for $k\le63$ and $>0$ first at $k=64$, and the Dyck chain zero near $\rho_{64}$ lies to the right of the critical line for $10^5\le n\le10^8$, agreeing with the first order law; a computation and no proof.
results.statement: Let $\rho_k=\frac12+i\gamma_k$ be the zeros of $\zeta$ on the critical line in order of height, $c_{\rm D}(\rho)=\sqrt{2/\pi}\,\rho\,\xi(\rho-1)/\xi'(\rho)$, $\delta_n=3/(2\sqrt{2n})$, and $F_n(s)=\mathbb{E}Y_n^s$, with $Y_n=\sqrt{2/\pi}\,H_n/\sqrt{2n}$ and $H_n$ the height of a uniform Dyck path of length $2n$, the Dirichlet polynomial of the Dyck chain with zero $z_n(\rho_k)$ near $\rho_k$. In ball arithmetic, from the first $200$ zeros of a stored list, $\xi'(\rho_k)\ne0$ for every $k\le200$, $\operatorname{Re}c_{\rm D}(\rho_k)<0$ for every $k\le63$, $c_{\rm D}(\rho_1)=-6.72018-9.54303i$, $c_{\rm D}(\rho_{64})=53.08757-266.82638i$ (radius below $10^{-55}$), and among $k\le200$, $\operatorname{Re}c_{\rm D}(\rho_k)>0$ exactly for $k=64$, $92$, $115$, $126$, $136$, $160$, $165$, $183$ and $187$. At $n=6400$ and $25600$, Newton's method started at $\rho_k+\delta_nc_{\rm D}(\rho_k)$, $k\le13$, converges to the zeros of the census of $F_n$, each alone in a square of half side $0.25$ by the argument principle, and the distance $|z_n(\rho_k)-\rho_k-\delta_nc_{\rm D}(\rho_k)|$ falls by a factor between $3.77$ and $4.64$ from $n=6400$ to $n=25600$, for $11$ of the $13$ zeros between $3.94$ and $4.14$, as a remainder $O(1/n)$ predicts; for $\rho_1$ at $n=25600$ the law gives the real part $\frac12-0.04455$ against $\frac12-0.04470$. The zero of $F_n$ near $\rho_{64}$, followed from $n=10^8$ down to $10^5$, lies to the right of the line at every computed $n$: $\operatorname{Re}z_n(\rho_{64})-\frac12$ is $0.1615$, $0.1348$, $0.0837$, $0.0456$, $0.0223$, $0.0118$ and $0.0061$ at $n=10^5$, $3\cdot10^5$, $10^6$, $3\cdot10^6$, $10^7$, $3\cdot10^7$ and $10^8$, against the first order values $\delta_n\operatorname{Re}c_{\rm D}(\rho_{64})$ from $0.1781$ down to $0.00563$, and for $10^6\le n\le10^8$ the product $n\,|z_n(\rho_{64})-\rho_{64}-\delta_nc_{\rm D}(\rho_{64})|$ lies between $6.33\cdot10^4$ and $6.61\cdot10^4$. The first order regime needs $\delta_n|c_{\rm D}(\rho_{64})|$ small: $|c_{\rm D}(\rho_{64})|=272.1$, so this is $0.91$ at $n=10^5$ and $0.029$ at $n=10^8$. The neighbours $\rho_{63}$ and $\rho_{65}$ stay to the left, with real parts $\frac12-0.0283$ and $\frac12-0.0227$ at $n=10^8$. The computation uses Newton's method on ball enclosures of the exact law with the terms below $10^{-110}$ dropped and not bounded, checked against a second law with another cut, and uniqueness by the argument principle, sampled; it is a computation. The result follows a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book.
results.label: ev:res:lbias

results.name: All zeros of Xi are real if and only if the reciprocal xi law is a GGC, and real and simple if and only if it is the hitting time of a string
results.summary: RH holds if and only if $L$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution with positive Thorin measure $\sum_k\delta_{\gamma_k^2}$; the zeros are all real and simple if and only if $L$ is the Laplace transform of the hitting time of a Krein string with positive mass; the same holds for any even real entire $\widehat H$ of order below two with $\widehat H(0)>0$.
results.statement: Let $\Xi$ be the Riemann Xi function, $\xi$ the Riemann xi function, $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}\phi_n(u)$ with $\phi_n(u)=(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})e^{-\pi n^2e^{4u}}$ the theta series kernel, and $H(z)=\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(zu)\,du=\frac18\Xi(z/2)$. Write $\pm\gamma_k$ for the zeros of $\Xi$, so that $\frac12+i\gamma_k$ are the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$, ordered by real part (under the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) they are all real and $0<\gamma_1\le\gamma_2\le\cdots$), $L(s)=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)=H(0)/H(2i\sqrt s)$, which under RH equals $\prod_k(1+s/\gamma_k^2)^{-1}$, and $T$ for the random variable with Laplace transform $L$. Then the following are equivalent: all zeros of $\Xi$ are real (RH); $L$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) whose Thorin measure $\sum_k\delta_{\gamma_k^2}$ is positive. Moreover, all zeros of $\Xi$ are real and simple if and only if there is a Krein string with positive mass whose hitting time $T$ satisfies $\mathbb Ee^{-sT}=L(s)$. The same statements hold with $\widehat H$ and $\widehat L(s)=\widehat H(0)/\widehat H(2i\sqrt s)$ in place of $H$ and $L$, for $\widehat H$ an even real entire function of order less than two with $\widehat H(0)>0$.
results.label: ev:cor:rh

results.name: Under RH with simple zeros the tail of the hitting time is a sum of exponentials and its excess is exponential with rate the first squared ordinate
results.status_text: conditional on RH, simple zeros, and $|\xi'(\rho)|\ge e^{-C|\gamma|}$ for some constant $C$ and all zeros $\rho=\frac12+i\gamma$
results.conditions: RH, simple zeros, and $|\xi'(\rho)|\ge e^{-C|\gamma|}$ for some constant $C$ and all zeros $\rho=\frac12+i\gamma$
results.summary: If RH holds, the zeros are simple and $|\xi'(\rho)|\ge e^{-C|\gamma|}$ for some constant $C$ and all zeros $\rho$, then $\mathbb P(T>x)=\sum_kc_ke^{-\gamma_k^2x}$ with $c_k=\prod_{j\ne k}(1-\gamma_k^2/\gamma_j^2)^{-1}$, so the excess of $T$ over a high threshold is asymptotically exponential with rate $\gamma_1^2$.
results.statement: Let $\Xi$ be the Riemann Xi function, $\xi$ the Riemann xi function, $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}\phi_n(u)$ with $\phi_n(u)=(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})e^{-\pi n^2e^{4u}}$ the theta series kernel, and $H(z)=\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(zu)\,du=\frac18\Xi(z/2)$. Write $\pm\gamma_k$ for the zeros of $\Xi$, so that $\frac12+i\gamma_k$ are the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$, ordered by real part (under the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) they are all real and $0<\gamma_1\le\gamma_2\le\cdots$), $L(s)=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)=H(0)/H(2i\sqrt s)$, which under RH equals $\prod_k(1+s/\gamma_k^2)^{-1}$, and $T$ for the random variable with Laplace transform $L$. If RH holds, the zeros are simple and $|\xi'(\rho)|\ge e^{-C|\gamma|}$ for some constant $C$ and all zeros $\rho$, then $\mathbb P(T>x)=\sum_kc_ke^{-\gamma_k^2x}$ with $c_k=\prod_{j\ne k}(1-\gamma_k^2/\gamma_j^2)^{-1}=2i\xi(\frac12)/(\gamma_k\xi'(\frac12+i\gamma_k))$. In particular the excess of $T$ over a high threshold is asymptotically exponential with rate $\lambda_1=\gamma_1^2$, the bottom of the spectrum of the string; this last clause needs only the two term tail, which has no hypothesis on $\xi'$.
results.label: ev:prop:tail

results.name: Hankel test: the zeros of an even entire kernel with infinitely many zeros are real if and only if two families of Hankel determinants are positive
results.summary: For an even real entire $\widehat H$ of order below two with infinitely many zeros and $\sum_k|w_k|<\infty$, all zeros are real and nonzero if and only if $D_n=\det[\mu_{i+j+1}]_{i,j=0}^{n-1}$ and $D_n'=\det[\mu_{i+j+2}]_{i,j=0}^{n-1}$ are positive for all $n\ge1$.
results.statement: Let $\widehat H$ be an even real entire function of order less than two with $\widehat H(0)>0$ and infinitely many zeros $\pm\widehat\gamma_k$ (counted in the variable $s$ with $\widehat H(2i\sqrt s)=\widehat H(0)\prod_k(1+s/\widehat\gamma_k^2)$), let $\mu_j=\sum_k\widehat\gamma_k^{-2j}$ be the power sums of the inverse atoms (the cumulants of the candidate hitting time divided by $(j-1)!$), $w_k=\widehat\gamma_k^{-2}$, and assume $\sum_k|w_k|<\infty$. The zeros of $\widehat H$ are all real (and nonzero) if and only if all the Hankel determinants $D_n=\det[\mu_{i+j+1}]_{i,j=0}^{n-1}$ and $D_n'=\det[\mu_{i+j+2}]_{i,j=0}^{n-1}$, $n\ge1$, are positive.
results.label: ev:prop:hankel

results.name: Clock and van Dantzig partner of a ferromagnetic law
results.summary: The clock of a ferromagnetic law is a generalised gamma convolution with drift equal to the Gaussian part and one unit Thorin atom at the square of each positive zero of its characteristic function, and the law has a partner of Pólya frequency type forming a van Dantzig pair with it.
results.statement: A real random variable $X$ is called ferromagnetic if it is symmetric, $\mathbb{E}e^{b_0X^2}<\infty$ for some $b_0>0$, and its moment generating function $L_X(z)=\mathbb{E}e^{zX}$, which is then entire, vanishes only on the imaginary axis; equivalently every zero of the characteristic function $\varphi_X(\theta)=L_X(i\theta)$ is real. By Newman's theorem such an $X$ has the Hadamard form $L_X(s)=e^{bs^2}\prod_k(1+s^2/c_k^2)$ with $b\ge0$, $c_k>0$ and $\sum_kc_k^{-2}<\infty$, each $c_k$ repeated according to the multiplicity of the zero $ic_k$. Let $X$ be ferromagnetic with this form, let $e_k$ be independent standard exponential variables and $Z$ a standard normal variable independent of them, and put $T_X=b+\sum_ke_k/c_k^2$ and $Y_X=Z\sqrt{2T_X}$; the series converges almost surely and in mean. Then (i) $\mathbb{E}e^{-uT_X}=1/L_X(\sqrt{u})$ for $u\ge0$, and $T_X$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC, a law on $[0,\infty)$ with Laplace transform $\exp\{-b\lambda-\int\log(1+\lambda/t)\,\mu(dt)\}$ for a drift $b\ge0$ and a positive Thorin measure $\mu$) with drift $b$ and Thorin measure $\sum_k\delta_{c_k^2}$, one unit atom for each pair of zeros $\pm ic_k$. (ii) $\mathbb{E}e^{i\theta Y_X}=1/L_X(\theta)$ for real $\theta$, so that $\varphi_{Y_X}(\theta)\,\varphi_X(i\theta)=1$ and $(\varphi_X,\varphi_{Y_X})$ is a van Dantzig pair, and $Y_X\overset{d}{=}\sqrt{2b}\,Z+\sum_kL_k/c_k$ with independent standard Laplace variables $L_k$, whose characteristic function is $1/(1+\theta^2)$. (iii) The moment generating function of $Y_X$ is $1/\varphi_X(t)$ for $|t|<c_1=\min_kc_k$ and infinite for $|t|\ge c_1$, unless $X$ is Gaussian. (iv) Unless $X$ is degenerate, $Y_X$ has a Pólya frequency density of infinite order. (v) $\kappa_m(T_X)=(-1)^{m+1}m!\,\kappa_{2m}(X)/(2m)!$ for $m\ge1$, where $\kappa_j$ denotes the $j$th cumulant; in particular $\mathbb{E}T_X=\frac12\operatorname{Var}X$ and $\operatorname{Var}T_X=-\kappa_4(X)/12$.
results.label: fm:thm:dual

results.name: Ferromagnetic laws are closed under convergence in law
results.summary: A limit in law of ferromagnetic random variables is ferromagnetic, the variances converge and the moment generating functions converge locally uniformly on the complex plane.
results.statement: A real random variable $X$ is called ferromagnetic if it is symmetric, $\mathbb{E}e^{b_0X^2}<\infty$ for some $b_0>0$, and its moment generating function $L_X(z)=\mathbb{E}e^{zX}$, which is then entire, vanishes only on the imaginary axis; Gaussian laws are allowed. Let $X_n$ be ferromagnetic and suppose that $X_n\to X$ in law. Then $X$ is ferromagnetic, $\operatorname{Var}X_n\to\operatorname{Var}X$, and $L_{X_n}\to L_X$ locally uniformly on $\mathbb{C}$.
results.label: fm:thm:closed

results.name: RH holds exactly when the Pólya law is a limit in law of ferromagnetic laws
results.summary: The Riemann Hypothesis is equivalent to the Pólya law being a limit in law of ferromagnetic laws.
results.statement: A real random variable $X$ is called ferromagnetic if it is symmetric, $\mathbb{E}e^{b_0X^2}<\infty$ for some $b_0>0$, and its moment generating function $\mathbb{E}e^{zX}$, which is then entire, vanishes only on the imaginary axis. The Pólya law is the law of the symmetric random variable $X$ with density $p=\Phi/\xi(\frac12)$, where $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ and $\Phi(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}(4\pi^2n^4e^{9t/2}-6\pi n^2e^{5t/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2t})$; its moment generating function is $\mathbb{E}e^{sX}=\xi(\frac12+s)/\xi(\frac12)$. The Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if the Pólya law is a limit in law of ferromagnetic laws.
results.label: fm:cor:limit

results.name: A uniform law mixed with an atom at the origin is not ferromagnetic
results.summary: The mixture of the uniform law on [-1,1] and a point mass at the origin is symmetric and unimodal but not ferromagnetic, so mixtures of ferromagnetic laws need not be ferromagnetic.
results.statement: A real random variable is called ferromagnetic if it is symmetric, has $\mathbb{E}e^{b_0X^2}<\infty$ for some $b_0>0$, and its moment generating function, which is then entire, vanishes only on the imaginary axis. Let $U$ be uniform on $[-1,1]$, so that $\mathbb{E}e^{sU}=\sinh s/s$. For every $0<q<1$ the mixture $(1-q)\,\mathrm{Unif}[-1,1]+q\,\delta_0$ of the uniform law on $[-1,1]$ with weight $1-q$ and the point mass at $0$ with weight $q$ is symmetric and unimodal but not ferromagnetic: its moment generating function $(1-q)\sinh s/s+q$ has no real zero, only finitely many zeros on the imaginary axis, and infinitely many zeros in all, so that all but finitely many of its zeros are off the imaginary axis. Consequently, for every $0<q<1$ and every small enough $a>0$, the mixture of the uniform laws on $[-1,1]$ and on $[-a,a]$ with weights $1-q$ and $q$ is not ferromagnetic. Both components of these mixtures are ferromagnetic, so the class of ferromagnetic laws is not closed under mixtures.
results.label: fm:thm:atom

results.name: The Pólya law is not a scale mixture of the triangular law, and its kernel has one inflection point
results.summary: A scale mixture of the triangular law by a probability law has a nonnegative characteristic function with no real zero when the mixing law has an absolutely continuous part, so the Pólya law is not such a mixture, and its kernel has exactly one positive inflection point $u^*$, certified as $0.237265287187425249$ in ball arithmetic (credited to a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book).
results.statement:
Let $f_2(x)=(1-|x|)_+$ be the triangular density on $[-1,1]$, so that its characteristic function is $4\sin^2(	heta/2)/	heta^2$, and call $X$ a scale mixture of $f_2$ for a probability law $
u$ on $(0,\infty)$ if $X=rY$ with $r\sim
u$ independent of $Y\sim f_2$. Let $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1} igl(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2} igr)\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2u})$ be the Pólya kernel, so that $\Xi(	heta)=\xi( rac12+i	heta)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)\cos(	heta u)\,du$ for Riemann's completed zeta function $\xi$. (i) If $X$ is a scale mixture of $f_2$ for $
u$, then $\mathbb{E}e^{i	heta X}\ge0$ for real $	heta$, and for $	heta
e0$ it vanishes exactly when $
u$ is carried by $\{2\pi j/|	heta|:j\ge1\}$; in particular if $
u$ has a nonzero absolutely continuous part, $\mathbb{E}e^{i	heta X}$ has no real zeros. (ii) The Pólya law, with density proportional to $\Phi$, is not a scale mixture of $f_2$ for any probability law: with $y_n=\pi n^2e^{2u}$ and $R(y)=32y^4-224y^3+330y^2-75y$, $\Phi''(u)= rac12e^{u/2}\sum_{n\ge1}R(y_n)e^{-y_n}$, $\Phi''(0)<0$, and $\Phi''(u)>0$ for $u\ge rac12\log(7/\pi)$, whereas a mixture of the convex functions $(1-x/r)_+$ is convex on $(0,\infty)$. (iii) $\Phi$ has exactly one positive inflection point $u^*$, with $\Phi''<0$ on $[0,u^*)$, $\Phi''>0$ on $(u^*,\infty)$ and $\Phi'''(u^*)>0$; certified in ball arithmetic, $u^*=0.23726528718742524911$. The proof of (ii) and (iii) uses three inequalities certified in ball arithmetic.
results.label: fm:prop:triangle

results.name: Shoulder theorem for symmetric laws on an interval
results.summary: A symmetric density on [-1,1] that vanishes at plus and minus 1 and is nonincreasing on [0,1] gives a ferromagnetic law if it is concave on [0,1], and does not if it is convex on [0,1] and not linear on its support.
results.statement: A real random variable is called ferromagnetic if it is symmetric, has $\mathbb{E}e^{b_0X^2}<\infty$ for some $b_0>0$, and its moment generating function, which is then entire, vanishes only on the imaginary axis; equivalently every zero of its characteristic function $\varphi_X$ is real. Let $p$ be a symmetric probability density on $[-1,1]$ that is absolutely continuous and nonincreasing on $[0,1]$, with $p(1)=0$, let $[-c,c]$ with $0<c\le1$ be its support, and let $X$ have density $p$. (i) If $p$ is concave on $[0,1]$, then $X$ is ferromagnetic. (ii) If $p$ is convex on $[0,1]$ and not linear on $[0,c]$, then $X$ is not ferromagnetic; moreover $\varphi_X\ge0$ on $\mathbb{R}$, and its real zeros, if any, are double and lie in a lattice $(2\pi/s_0)\mathbb{Z}$ with $0<s_0<c$.
results.label: fm:thm:shoulder

results.name: Ferromagnetic laws among the kernels 1 minus |x|^b, k monotone kernels and products of uniform laws
results.summary: The law with density proportional to 1 minus |x|^b is ferromagnetic exactly when b is at least 1, the k monotone kernel exactly when k is at most 2, the densities (1 minus x squared) to the power m with 0 < m at most 1 are ferromagnetic, and a product of two independent uniform variables is not.
results.statement: A real random variable is called ferromagnetic if it is symmetric, has $\mathbb{E}e^{b_0X^2}<\infty$ for some $b_0>0$, and its moment generating function, which is then entire, vanishes only on the imaginary axis. (i) The law with density proportional to $1-|x|^b$ on $[-1,1]$, $b>0$, is ferromagnetic if and only if $b\ge1$. In Khinchine's form, $UR$ with $U$ uniform on $[-1,1]$ and $R$ independent with the Beta$(a,1)$ law (density $ar^{a-1}$ on $[0,1]$) is ferromagnetic if and only if $a\ge2$. (ii) For an integer $k\ge1$ the symmetric $k$ monotone kernel $f_k(x)=\frac k2(1-|x|)_+^{k-1}$ (the uniform density for $k=1$ and the triangle density for $k=2$) is ferromagnetic if and only if $k\le2$. (iii) The laws with density proportional to $(1-x^2)^m$ on $[-1,1]$ with $0<m\le1$, which include the semicircle law, are ferromagnetic. (iv) The product $U_1U_2$ of two independent uniform variables on $[-1,1]$, with density $\frac12\log(1/|x|)$ on $[-1,1]$, is not ferromagnetic.
results.label: fm:cor:shoulder

results.name: Densities nondecreasing in |x| and mixtures of uniform laws on shells are ferromagnetic
results.summary: Every symmetric density on [-1,1] that is nondecreasing in |x|, equivalently every mixture of uniform laws on the shells a at most |x| at most 1, is ferromagnetic.
results.statement: A real random variable is called ferromagnetic if it is symmetric, has $\mathbb{E}e^{b_0X^2}<\infty$ for some $b_0>0$, and its moment generating function, which is then entire, vanishes only on the imaginary axis. Every symmetric probability density on $[-1,1]$ that is nondecreasing in $|x|$ is ferromagnetic. Equivalently, every mixture of the uniform laws on the shells $\{a\le|x|\le1\}$, $0\le a<1$, is ferromagnetic.
results.label: fm:thm:ushaped

results.name: Residue expansion of the Mellin transform of a ferromagnetic clock and of a pair
results.summary: Under stated summability conditions the Mellin transform of the Laplace transform of the clock of a ferromagnetic law, and of a sum of two independent copies, is $\pi/\sin\pi w$ times an explicit series over the zeros of the characteristic function.
results.statement: Let $X$ be a ferromagnetic random variable (a characteristic function $\varphi_X$ with only real zeros) with $b=0$ in its Hadamard product and infinitely many simple zeros $\pm ic_k$, $0<c_1<c_2<\cdots$, so that $L_X(s)=\mathbb{E}e^{sX}=\prod_k(1+s^2/c_k^2)$, and let $T_X=\sum_ke_k/c_k^2$ be its clock, with $e_k$ independent standard exponential variables. Put $\mathcal D_X(w)=\Gamma(w)\mathbb{E}T_X^{-w}=\int_0^\infty u^{w-1}(1/L_X(\sqrt u)-1)\,du$ for $-1<\operatorname{Re}w<0$, and $A_k=-2/(c_k\varphi_X'(c_k))$, $B_k=2(c_k\varphi_X''(c_k)-\varphi_X'(c_k))/(c_k^2\varphi_X'(c_k)^3)$. (i) Near $u=-c_k^2$, $1/L_X(\sqrt u)=A_k(1+u/c_k^2)^{-1}+O(1)$ and $1/L_X(\sqrt u)^2=A_k^2(1+u/c_k^2)^{-2}+B_k(1+u/c_k^2)^{-1}+O(1)$. (ii) If $1/L_X(\sqrt u)=1+\sum_kA_k((1+u/c_k^2)^{-1}-1)$ for $u\ge0$ and $\sum_k|A_k|c_k^{2\sigma}<\infty$ for some $\sigma\in(-1,0)$, then $\mathcal D_X(w)=\frac{\pi}{\sin\pi w}\sum_kA_kc_k^{2w}$ for $-1<\operatorname{Re}w\le\sigma$. (iii) If $1/L_X(\sqrt u)^2=1+\sum_k[A_k^2((1+u/c_k^2)^{-2}-1)+B_k((1+u/c_k^2)^{-1}-1)]$ for $u\ge0$ and $\sum_k(A_k^2+|B_k|)c_k^{2\sigma}<\infty$ for some $\sigma\in(-1,0)$, then for an independent copy $X'$ of $X$, $\mathcal D_{X+X'}(w)=\frac{\pi}{\sin\pi w}\sum_k[(1-w)A_k^2+B_k]c_k^{2w}$ for $-1<\operatorname{Re}w\le\sigma$. The result is from a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book.
results.label: fm:prop:residue

results.name: Mellin transform of the clock of a sum of k uniform spins as a combination of zeta values
results.summary: For $X_k=\pi(U_1+\dots+U_k)$ the Mellin transform of the clock is an explicit Gamma factor times a series that is a finite combination of $\zeta(2w+1+2i)$, with the cases $k=1,4,6$ written out.
results.statement: Let $U_1,\dots,U_k$ be independent random variables uniform on $[-1,1]$, $X_k=\pi(U_1+\dots+U_k)$, and $\mathcal D_{X_k}(w)=\Gamma(w)\mathbb{E}T^{-w}$ the Mellin transform of the Laplace transform of the clock $T$ of $X_k$ (the sum of $e_j/c_j^2$ over the zeros $\pm c_j$ of the characteristic function, $e_j$ independent standard exponential variables). For $\operatorname{Re}w>0$, $\mathcal D_{X_k}(w)=2(2\pi)^{-2w}\Gamma(2w+k)\sum_{m\ge0}\binom{m+k-1}{k-1}(m+\frac k2)^{-2w-k}$. For $k=2r$ the series is $\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}a_{r,i}\zeta(2w+1+2i)$, where $a_{r,i}$ is the coefficient of $j^{2r-1-2i}$ in $j\prod_{l=1}^{r-1}(j^2-l^2)/(2r-1)!$, and for $k=2r+1$ it is $\sum_{i=0}^rb_{r,i}(2^{2w+1+2i}-1)\zeta(2w+1+2i)$, where $b_{r,i}$ is the coefficient of $h^{2r-2i}$ in $\prod_{l=1}^r(h^2-(l-\frac12)^2)/(2r)!$. The first and the last of these coefficients are not $0$, so for $k\ge3$ the series has at least two terms. In particular $\mathcal D_{X_1}(w)=4\pi^{-2w}(1-2^{-2w-1})\Gamma(2w+1)\zeta(2w+1)$, $\mathcal D_{X_4}(w)=\frac13(2\pi)^{-2w}\Gamma(2w+4)[\zeta(2w+1)-\zeta(2w+3)]$ and $\mathcal D_{X_6}(w)=\frac1{60}(2\pi)^{-2w}\Gamma(2w+6)[\zeta(2w+1)-5\zeta(2w+3)+4\zeta(2w+5)]$. The result is from a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book.
results.label: fm:prop:kspins

results.name: Zeros of the Mellin transform of the clock for one, four and six uniform spins (computed)
results.summary: For sums of four and six independent copies of $\pi U$ the Mellin transform of the clock has nonreal zeros that do not lie on one vertical line, computed in ball arithmetic.
results.statement: Let $U_1,\dots,U_k$ be independent uniform on $[-1,1]$ and $X_k=\pi(U_1+\dots+U_k)$, and let $\mathcal D_{X_k}$ be the Mellin transform of the Laplace transform of the clock of $X_k$ (the clock being the sum of $e_j/c_j^2$ over the zeros $\pm c_j$ of the characteristic function). In the variable $z=2w+1$, for $k=1$ the nonreal zeros of $\mathcal D_{X_1}$ are those of $\zeta(z)$ and the points $z=2\pi im/\log2$, $m\ne0$, so they lie on the two lines $\operatorname{Re}z=\frac12$ (under the Riemann Hypothesis) and $\operatorname{Re}z=0$; for $k=2$ they are the zeros of $\xi(z)$. For $k=4$ and $k=6$ they do not lie on one vertical line: $\zeta(z)-\zeta(z+2)$ vanishes at $z=1.76891972665+23.3078297413i$ and $z=0.650238826497+31.7124838244i$, and $\zeta(z)-5\zeta(z+2)+4\zeta(z+4)$ at $z=3.18634599215+31.979112615i$ and $z=1.51363208762+41.215007487i$ (computed in ball arithmetic, each zero alone in a square of half side $7.5\cdot10^{-9}$ by the argument principle). The statement for $k=4,6$ is a computation.
results.label: fm:res:kzeros

results.name: The density (1+cos t)/2pi gives a ferromagnetic law whose Mellin transform has zeros off one line (computed)
results.summary: For the ferromagnetic law with density $(1+\cos t)/2\pi$ on $[-\pi,\pi]$ the pair has a Mellin transform that is a combination of three shifted copies of the uniform one, with zeros at six different real parts, computed.
results.statement: Let $X$ have the density $(1+\cos t)/2\pi$ on $[-\pi,\pi]$, which is $C^1$ and not $C^2$ at $\pm\pi$, let $X'$ be an independent copy, and let $\mathcal D_Y(w)$ be the Mellin transform of the Laplace transform of the clock of $Y$ (the clock being the sum of $e_k/c_k^2$ over the zeros $\pm c_k$ of the characteristic function of $Y$, $e_k$ independent standard exponential variables), $U,U'$ independent uniform on $[-1,1]$. The characteristic function of $X$ is that of $\pi U$ divided by $Q(\theta^2)$ with $Q(x)=1-x$, the zeros are $c_k=k+1$, $k\ge1$, the law is ferromagnetic, and $\mathcal D_{X+X'}(w)=\mathcal D_{\pi U+\pi U'}(w)+2\mathcal D_{\pi U+\pi U'}(w+1)+\mathcal D_{\pi U+\pi U'}(w+2)$, a combination of $\zeta(-2w)$, $\zeta(-2w-2)$ and $\zeta(-2w-4)$. Its residue weights $A_k=2(-1)^{k+1}(k^2+2k)$ grow like $k^2$. In the box $-1<\operatorname{Re}w<1$, $\frac12<\operatorname{Im}w<30$, which holds the $13$ zeros $\frac{\rho_k-1}2$, $\gamma_k<60$, of $\mathcal D_{\pi U+\pi U'}$ ($\rho_k=\frac12+i\gamma_k$ the zeros of $\zeta$ on the critical line), $\mathcal D_{X+X'}$ has no zero, and in $-3<\operatorname{Re}w<-2$, $\frac12<\operatorname{Im}w<30$ it has $6$, at $-2.443554+15.837821i$, $-2.976747+19.238797i$, $-2.479242+21.119434i$, $-2.273308+24.426843i$, $-2.862245+26.206760i$ and $-2.756588+28.553832i$, so not on one vertical line (computed in ball arithmetic).
results.label: fm:res:onecos

results.name: Deformation of the uniform pair, the first two Mellin zeros leave the line at different rates (computed)
results.summary: Along the ferromagnetic densities proportional to $1+\varepsilon t^2$ on $[-\pi,\pi]$ the first two zeros of the Mellin transform of the pair move with computed velocities having different nonzero real parts, so no theorem for all such densities can put the zeros on one line.
results.statement: For $\varepsilon\ge0$ let $X_\varepsilon$ have the density $(1+\varepsilon t^2)/(2\pi+\frac23\pi^3\varepsilon)$ on $[-\pi,\pi]$, which is nondecreasing in $|t|$, so that $X_\varepsilon$ and the sum $X_\varepsilon+X_\varepsilon'$ with an independent copy are ferromagnetic, and let $\mathcal D_{X_\varepsilon+X_\varepsilon'}$ be the Mellin transform of the Laplace transform of the clock of the pair. At $\varepsilon=0$ the zeros $w_k(0)=\frac{\rho_k-1}2$ of $\mathcal D_{\pi U+\pi U'}$ ($U,U'$ independent uniform on $[-1,1]$, $\rho_k$ the zeros of $\zeta$ on the critical line) move, where $\rho_k$ is simple, with $\frac{dw_k}{d\varepsilon}(0)=-\dot{\mathcal D}(w_k(0))/\mathcal D'_{\pi U+\pi U'}(w_k(0))$ by the implicit function theorem, $\dot{\mathcal D}$ being the derivative of $\mathcal D_{X_\varepsilon+X_\varepsilon'}$ in $\varepsilon$ at $\varepsilon=0$. The computed values are $\frac{dw_1}{d\varepsilon}(0)=5.89145-13.09321i$ and $\frac{dw_2}{d\varepsilon}(0)=1.56442-16.25014i$, with real parts different from $0$ and from each other (computed by quadrature with three rules that agree). So for small $\varepsilon>0$ the first two zeros leave the line $\operatorname{Re}w=-\frac14$ at different rates, and the nonreal zeros of $\mathcal D_{X_\varepsilon+X_\varepsilon'}$ do not lie on one vertical line although every $X_\varepsilon$ is ferromagnetic. By this computation no theorem whose hypotheses hold for all symmetric densities on an interval that are nondecreasing in $|t|$ can put the zeros of the Mellin transform of the pair on one line.
results.label: fm:res:deform

results.name: The Pólya law has no Gaussian component and no ferromagnetic summand with finitely many zeros
results.summary: With no hypothesis on the zeros, an independent summand of a symmetric law whose log moment generating function is o(s^2) has log moment generating function o(s^2) as well, so the Pólya law has no Gaussian component and is not a sum of independent ferromagnetic variables one of which is nonzero with finitely many zeros.
results.statement: Let $X$ be a symmetric random variable with $\mathbb{E}e^{sX}<\infty$ for every real $s$ and $\log\mathbb{E}e^{sX}=o(s^2)$ as $s\to\infty$, and suppose that $X\overset{d}{=}D+R$ with $D$ and $R$ independent. Then $\log\mathbb{E}e^{sD}=o(s^2)$ as $|s|\to\infty$. In particular, if $D$ is ferromagnetic (symmetric, with $\mathbb{E}e^{b_0D^2}<\infty$ for some $b_0>0$ and a moment generating function vanishing only on the imaginary axis) and not $0$, then in its Hadamard form $\mathbb{E}e^{sD}=e^{bs^2}\prod_k(1+s^2/c_k^2)$ the Gaussian factor has $b=0$, and the characteristic function of $D$ has infinitely many zeros. The Pólya variable, the symmetric random variable with density $\Phi/\xi(\frac12)$ and moment generating function $\xi(\frac12+s)/\xi(\frac12)$, where $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ and $\Phi(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}(4\pi^2n^4e^{9t/2}-6\pi n^2e^{5t/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2t})$, satisfies the hypothesis with no assumption on the zeros of $\zeta$. So it has no Gaussian component (it is not the sum of an independent normal variable of positive variance and another variable), and it is not a finite or convergent infinite sum of independent ferromagnetic variables of which one is not $0$ and has a characteristic function with finitely many zeros.
results.label: fm:thm:nosqrt

results.name: Powers of the exponential of the Pólya variable are not infinitely divisible for exponent below 2
results.summary: For every real beta with 0 less than |beta| less than 2 the variable e to the beta X is not infinitely divisible, with no hypothesis on the zeros.
results.statement: Let $X$ be the Pólya variable, the symmetric random variable with density $p=\Phi/\xi(\frac12)$, where $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ and $\Phi(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}(4\pi^2n^4e^{9t/2}-6\pi n^2e^{5t/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2t})$. For every real $\beta$ with $0<|\beta|<2$ the random variable $e^{\beta X}$ is not infinitely divisible. No hypothesis on the zeros of $\zeta$ is used.
results.label: fm:prop:notid

results.name: The exponential of the Pólya variable is not a generalised gamma convolution
results.summary: Size biasing the Biane Pitman Yor variable (pi/2) S_2 by a power q in (0,1) destroys the generalised gamma convolution property, and in particular e to the 2X is not a generalised gamma convolution.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$, and let $B_0=\sum_{m\ge1}\Gamma_m/(\pi m^2)$ with independent Gamma$(2,1)$ variables $\Gamma_m$; this is the variable $\frac\pi2S_2$ of Biane, Pitman and Yor, a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) with Laplace transform $(\sqrt{\pi\lambda}/\sinh\sqrt{\pi\lambda})^2$ and $\mathbb{E}B_0^\sigma=2\xi(2\sigma)$ for every complex $\sigma$. For $0<q<1$ let $B_q$ be $B_0$ size biased by $B_0^q$, that is $\mathbb{E}g(B_q)=\mathbb{E}[B_0^qg(B_0)]/\mathbb{E}B_0^q$, so that $\mathbb{E}B_q^\sigma=\xi(2\sigma+2q)/\xi(2q)$. A GGC is a law on $[0,\infty)$ with Laplace transform $\exp\{-b\lambda-\int\log(1+\lambda/t)\,\mu(dt)\}$ for a drift $b\ge0$ and a positive Thorin measure $\mu$. Then for every $0<q<1$ the variable $B_q$ is not a GGC. In particular $e^{2X}$ is not a GGC, where $X$ is the Pólya variable, the symmetric random variable with density $\Phi/\xi(\frac12)$, $\Phi(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}(4\pi^2n^4e^{9t/2}-6\pi n^2e^{5t/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2t})$, and moment generating function $\xi(\frac12+s)/\xi(\frac12)$, because $e^{2X}\overset{d}{=}B_{1/4}$. No hypothesis on the zeros is used.
results.label: fm:thm:notggc

results.name: Size bias principle for sums of gamma variables with integer shapes
results.summary: Size biasing a sum of independent gamma variables with integer shapes by a power q in (0,1) raises every shape by q at the cost of an independent generalised gamma convolution that puts mass q on each gap between consecutive rates.
results.statement: Let $Y=\sum_{n=1}^K\Gamma_n/\tau_n$ with $0<\tau_1<\dots<\tau_K$ and independent gamma variables $\Gamma_n$ with integer shapes $t_n\ge1$ and unit scale, let $0<q<1$, and let $Y_q$ be $Y$ size biased by $Y^q$, that is $\mathbb{E}g(Y_q)=\mathbb{E}[Y^qg(Y)]/\mathbb{E}Y^q$. Then $Y_q+G\overset{d}{=}\sum_{n=1}^K\Gamma_n'/\tau_n$, where the $\Gamma_n'$ are independent gamma variables with shapes $t_n+q$ and unit scale, and $G$, independent of $Y_q$, is a generalised gamma convolution without drift whose Thorin measure has a continuous distribution function $\theta_G$ that vanishes on $(0,\tau_1]$, increases by exactly $q$ on each interval $[\tau_k,\tau_{k+1}]$ and is constant on $[\tau_K,\infty)$.
results.label: fm:thm:sbp

results.name: Factorisation of the exponential of the Pólya variable against a Biane Pitman Yor variable
results.summary: Adding an independent generalised gamma convolution without drift to the size biased Biane Pitman Yor variable B_q gives (pi/2) S_{2+q}, and in particular e to the 2X plus an independent generalised gamma convolution has the law of (pi/2) S_{9/4}.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$, let $B_0=\sum_{m\ge1}\Gamma_m/(\pi m^2)$ with independent Gamma$(2,1)$ variables $\Gamma_m$ (the variable $\frac\pi2S_2$ of Biane, Pitman and Yor, with $\mathbb{E}B_0^\sigma=2\xi(2\sigma)$), and for $0<q<1$ let $B_q$ be $B_0$ size biased by $B_0^q$, so that $\mathbb{E}B_q^\sigma=\xi(2\sigma+2q)/\xi(2q)$. Let $\frac\pi2S_{2+q}=\sum_{m\ge1}\Gamma_m'/(\pi m^2)$ with independent gamma variables $\Gamma_m'$ of shape $2+q$ and unit scale, with Laplace transform $(\sqrt{\pi\lambda}/\sinh\sqrt{\pi\lambda})^{2+q}$. Then $B_q+G_q\overset{d}{=}\frac\pi2S_{2+q}$, where $G_q$ is independent of $B_q$ and is a generalised gamma convolution (a law on $[0,\infty)$ with Laplace transform $\exp\{-b\lambda-\int\log(1+\lambda/t)\,\mu(dt)\}$) without drift whose Thorin measure has a continuous distribution function $\theta_q$ with $\theta_q=0$ on $(0,\pi]$ and $\theta_q(\pi m^2)=(m-1)q$ for every $m\ge1$. In particular $e^{2X}+G_{1/4}\overset{d}{=}\frac\pi2S_{9/4}$, where $X$ is the Pólya variable, the symmetric random variable with density $\Phi/\xi(\frac12)$, $\Phi(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}(4\pi^2n^4e^{9t/2}-6\pi n^2e^{5t/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2t})$, and moment generating function $\xi(\frac12+s)/\xi(\frac12)$, because $e^{2X}\overset{d}{=}B_{1/4}$. No hypothesis on the zeros is used.
results.label: fm:thm:factor

results.name: The exponential of the Pólya variable is self decomposable with a Lévy density built from the theta function
results.summary: The size biased Biane Pitman Yor variable B_q is self decomposable with a Lévy density built from the theta function, between 2 omega(x)/x and (2+q) omega(x)/x, so e to the 2X is self decomposable, hence infinitely divisible and unimodal, without being a generalised gamma convolution.
results.statement: Let $\omega(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}e^{-\pi n^2x}$, let $B_q$, $0<q<1$, be the variable $B_0=\sum_{m\ge1}\Gamma_m/(\pi m^2)$ (independent Gamma$(2,1)$ variables $\Gamma_m$, the variable $\frac\pi2S_2$ of Biane, Pitman and Yor) size biased by $B_0^q$, and let $\theta_q$ be the distribution function of the Thorin measure of the generalised gamma convolution $G_q$ in the identity $B_q+G_q\overset{d}{=}\frac\pi2S_{2+q}$, where $\frac\pi2S_{2+q}$ has Laplace transform $(\sqrt{\pi\lambda}/\sinh\sqrt{\pi\lambda})^{2+q}$; $\theta_q$ is continuous, vanishes on $(0,\pi]$, and satisfies $\theta_q(\pi m^2)=(m-1)q$. Then $B_q$ is self decomposable, with no drift and Lévy density $k_q(x)/x$, where $k_q(x)=(2+q)\,\omega(x)-\int_0^\infty e^{-tx}\,d\theta_q(t)$ and $2\,\omega(x)\le k_q(x)\le(2+q)\,\omega(x)$. In particular $e^{2X}$, with $X$ the Pólya variable (the symmetric random variable with density $\Phi/\xi(\frac12)$, where $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ and $\Phi(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}(4\pi^2n^4e^{9t/2}-6\pi n^2e^{5t/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2t})$, and with moment generating function $\xi(\frac12+s)/\xi(\frac12)$), which has the law of $B_{1/4}$, is self decomposable, hence infinitely divisible and unimodal; its Lévy density lies between $2\omega(x)/x$ and $\frac94\omega(x)/x$, and it is not a generalised gamma convolution. No hypothesis on the zeros is used.
results.label: fm:thm:sd

results.name: Hyperbolically completely monotone densities of the powers of the exponential of the Pólya variable
results.summary: The power e to the beta X of the exponential of the Pólya variable has a hyperbolically completely monotone density, so it is a generalised gamma convolution, for |beta| at least 5.5791422 by a certified computation in ball arithmetic, and has none for |beta| at most 5.5791395.
results.statement: Let $X$ be the Pólya variable, the symmetric random variable with density $p=\Phi/\xi(\frac12)$, where $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ and $\Phi(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}(4\pi^2n^4e^{9t/2}-6\pi n^2e^{5t/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2t})$. A density $f$ on $(0,\infty)$ is hyperbolically completely monotone (HCM) if for every $u>0$ the function $f(uv)f(u/v)$ of $w=v+1/v$ is completely monotone; an HCM law is a generalised gamma convolution (Bondesson). The variable $e^{\beta X}$ has an HCM density, and so is a generalised gamma convolution, for $|\beta|\ge5.5791422$, and it does not have an HCM density for $|\beta|\le5.5791395$. The proof of the first statement is computer assisted, in ball arithmetic. No hypothesis on the zeros is used.
results.label: fm:prop:hcm

results.name: The Stern row counts c_N(m) as coprime pairs of the Calkin Wilf tree, and the limit of Knauf's partition function, with a new proof of Knauf's limit
results.summary: The number of times m occurs among the Stern values s(k), 2^N at most k below 2^(N+1), counts the coprime pairs with sum m of bounded depth in the Calkin Wilf tree, equals Euler's phi of m for m at most N+1, vanishes beyond the Fibonacci number F_(N+2), and the sums of the row equal 3^N; the partition function converges to zeta(beta-1) over zeta(beta) (the limit is due to Knauf).
results.statement: Let $s$ be Stern's diatomic sequence, $s(1)=1$, $s(2n)=s(n)$, $s(2n+1)=s(n)+s(n+1)$, let $Z_N(\beta)=\sum_{k=2^N}^{2^{N+1}-1}s(k)^{-\beta}=\sum_{m\ge1}c_N(m)m^{-\beta}$ for complex $\beta$, where $c_N(m)$ is the number of $k$ with $2^N\le k<2^{N+1}$ and $s(k)=m$, let $\varphi$ be Euler's function and $F_n$ the Fibonacci numbers with $F_1=F_2=1$. Then $c_N(1)=1$, and for $m\ge2$, $c_N(m)$ is the number of coprime pairs $(p,q)$ of positive integers with $p+q=m$ for which $p/q$ has depth at most $N-1$ in the Calkin Wilf tree (root $1/1$, the children of $p/q$ being $p/(p+q)$ and $(p+q)/q$). Hence $c_N(m)$ does not decrease with $N$, $c_N(m)=\varphi(m)$ for $m\le N+1$, $c_N(m)=0$ for $m>F_{N+2}$, and $c_N(m)\to\varphi(m)$ as $N\to\infty$. Moreover $Z_N(\beta)\to\zeta(\beta-1)/\zeta(\beta)$ as $N\to\infty$ for $\operatorname{Re}\beta>2$, increasingly for real $\beta>2$, and $Z_N(-1)=\sum_m m\,c_N(m)=3^N$.
results.label: fm:prop:stern

results.name: Perron identity for Knauf's partition function, with the depth profile term and the remainder R_N
results.summary: For every N, Knauf's partition function equals zeta(beta-1)/zeta(beta) plus a profile term W_N(2-beta)/zeta(2) plus an explicit Euler Maclaurin type remainder R_N, which is analytic at beta = 2.
results.statement: Let $s$ be Stern's diatomic sequence, $s(1)=1$, $s(2n)=s(n)$, $s(2n+1)=s(n)+s(n+1)$, let $c_N(m)$ be the number of $k$ with $2^N\le k<2^{N+1}$ and $s(k)=m$, which vanishes for $m>F_{N+2}$ ($F_n$ the Fibonacci numbers, $F_1=F_2=1$), let $Z_N(\beta)=\sum_{k=2^N}^{2^{N+1}-1}s(k)^{-\beta}=\sum_m c_N(m)m^{-\beta}$ be the partition function of Knauf's spin chain, let $\varphi$ and $\mu$ be Euler's and Möbius's functions, and let $w_N(x)=c_N(m)/\varphi(m)$ for $m\le x<m+1$, $m\ge1$, and $w_N(x)=1$ for $0<x<1$, and let $W_N(z)=\int_0^\infty w_N(x)x^{z-1}\,dx$ for $\operatorname{Re}z>0$, which is $1/z$ plus an entire function. For $\operatorname{Re}\beta>1$, $\beta\ne2$, $Z_N(\beta)=\zeta(\beta-1)/\zeta(\beta)+W_N(2-\beta)/\zeta(2)+R_N(\beta)$, where $R_N(\beta)=\sum_{d\ge1}\mu(d)d^{-\beta}r_d(\beta)$, $r_d(\beta)=\sum_{n\ge1}n^{1-\beta}w_N(dn)-\zeta(\beta-1)-d^{\beta-2}W_N(2-\beta)$, and the series converges absolutely. $R_N$ extends analytically to $\beta=2$, and $C_N(\beta)=Z_N(\beta)-W_N(2-\beta)/\zeta(2)$ is meromorphic on the plane with a single pole, at $\beta=2$, which is simple with residue $1/\zeta(2)$.
results.label: fm:prop:perron

results.name: Conjecture that the remainder R_N of Knauf's partition function tends to zero on a strip around the line 3/2
results.summary: The remainder R_N of the Perron identity for Knauf's chain is conjectured to tend to zero locally uniformly on an open strip around the line Re beta = 3/2, which would put the zeros of the corrected sum near the points 1 plus rho; it does not decide RH.
results.statement: Let $R_N$ be the remainder of the Perron identity for the partition function $Z_N(\beta)=\sum_{k=2^N}^{2^{N+1}-1}s(k)^{-\beta}$ of Knauf's spin chain, where $s$ is Stern's diatomic sequence, so that $Z_N-W_N(2-\beta)/\zeta(2)=\zeta(\beta-1)/\zeta(\beta)+R_N$ with $W_N(z)=\int_0^\infty w_N(x)x^{z-1}\,dx$, where $w_N(x)=c_N(m)/\varphi(m)$ for $m\le x<m+1$ and $w_N=1$ on $(0,1)$, $c_N(m)$ is the number of $k$ with $2^N\le k<2^{N+1}$ and $s(k)=m$ ($s$ Stern's diatomic sequence), and $\varphi$ is Euler's function. Conjecture: there is an open strip $\sigma_1<\operatorname{Re}\beta<\sigma_2$ with $1\le\sigma_1<\frac32<\sigma_2\le2$ on which $R_N\to0$ locally uniformly as $N\to\infty$. If it holds, then by Hurwitz's theorem every point $1+\rho$ in the strip, for $\rho$ a nontrivial zero of $\zeta$, is the limit of as many zeros of the corrected sum $Z_N-W_N(2-\beta)/\zeta(2)$ as its multiplicity, and no other limit points occur in the strip. The computations support it only at the first twenty points $1+\rho_n$ on the line $\operatorname{Re}\beta=\frac32$, and at $\beta=\frac32+2i$ the modulus of $R_N$ stays between $0.021$ and $0.051$ for $10\le N\le34$ with no decrease. The consequence does not decide the Riemann Hypothesis, since the zeros of the corrected sum would converge to the points $1+\rho$ whether or not $\operatorname{Re}\rho=\frac12$.
results.label: fm:conj:R

results.name: Computed zeros of Knauf's partition function and of the corrected sum near the points 1 plus rho
results.summary: For even N from 10 to 34 the disc of radius 0.3 about each of the first twenty points 1 plus rho contains exactly one zero of Knauf's partition function and one of the corrected sum, found by Newton's method with a sampled winding number, and removing the profile term lowers the mean distance only at N = 14 and for N at least 24 (computation, not a ball proof).
results.statement: Let $Z_N(\beta)=\sum_{k=2^N}^{2^{N+1}-1}s(k)^{-\beta}$ be the partition function of Knauf's spin chain, $s$ Stern's diatomic sequence, let $C_N=Z_N-W_N(2-\beta)/\zeta(2)$ be the corrected sum with the profile term removed, and let $\rho_n$ be the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$ with positive ordinate, in increasing order of ordinate. For every even $N$ from $10$ to $34$ and every $n\le20$, the disc of radius $0.3$ about $1+\rho_n$ contains exactly one zero of $Z_N$ and exactly one zero of $C_N$, found by Newton's method from $1+\rho_n$ (winding number on the circle, sampled; a computation, not a ball proof), and the largest distance of such a zero from $1+\rho_n$ is $0.243$. Removing the profile term does not bring the zeros consistently closer: the mean distance is smaller for $C_N$ only at $N=14$ and at every computed $N$ from $24$ on. At $N=34$ the mean distances are $0.0081$ for $Z_N$ and $0.0047$ for $C_N$.
results.label: fm:res:fisher

results.name: Circle lemma for palindromic polynomials with small middle coefficients, and the Farey chain above beta star of N
results.summary: A palindromic polynomial 1 + x^N + Q with nonnegative palindromic middle part of total weight below 2 has all its zeros simple and on the unit circle, which gives the Lee and Yang property of the Farey chain in a field for beta above beta star of N.
results.statement: Let $P(x)=1+x^N+Q(x)$ with $Q(x)=\sum_{k=1}^{N-1}a_kx^k$ and $a_k=a_{N-k}\ge0$. If $Q(1)<2$, the zeros of $P$ are simple and lie on the unit circle. Consequence: the Farey chain of Kleban and Özlük has configurations the words $\varpi_1\cdots\varpi_N$ in $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$ and $B=A^{\mathsf T}$, energy $\log\operatorname{tr}(\varpi_1\cdots\varpi_N)$, and partition function in the field $x=e^h$ equal to $Z^{\rm F}_N(\beta,x)=\sum(\operatorname{tr}\varpi_1\cdots\varpi_N)^{-\beta}x^{n_B}$, with $n_B$ the number of letters $B$. Since $A^N$ and $B^N$ have trace $2$ and every other word has trace at least $3$, $Z^{\rm F}_N(\beta,x)=2^{-\beta}(1+x^N+Q_{N,\beta}(x))$ with $Q_{N,\beta}(1)=\sum(2/\operatorname{tr}\varpi_1\cdots\varpi_N)^\beta$ over the other words, strictly decreasing in $\beta$, so for every $\beta>\beta^*(N)$, the root of $2^\beta Z^{\rm F}_N(\beta,1)=4$, all zeros of $x\mapsto Z^{\rm F}_N(\beta,x)$ are simple and on the unit circle (the Lee and Yang property at $(\beta,N)$).
results.label: fm:lem:circle

results.name: Computed Lee and Yang threshold of the Farey chain in a field for even N from 10 to 36
results.summary: For even N from 10 to 36 there is a computed threshold, rising from 1.2424 to 1.8329 and below beta star of N, above which the zeros of the Farey partition function in the field lie on the unit circle and below which, at every computed β down to 0.2, some do not (computation on a grid with bisection; the final bracket is certified by a Sturm count for N at most 32).
results.statement: For the Farey chain in a field, with partition function $Z^{\rm F}_N(\beta,x)=\sum(\operatorname{tr}\varpi_1\cdots\varpi_N)^{-\beta}x^{n_B}$, with $n_B$ the number of letters $B$, over the words $\varpi_1\cdots\varpi_N$ in $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$ and $B=A^{\mathsf T}$, the computation finds for each even $N$ from $10$ to $36$ a threshold $\beta_{\rm LY}(N)$ such that all zeros of $x\mapsto Z^{\rm F}_N(\beta,x)$ lie on the unit circle at every computed $\beta\ge\beta_{\rm LY}(N)$ and some do not at every computed $\beta$ with $0<\beta<\beta_{\rm LY}(N)$ (grid of step $0.1$ on $0.2\le\beta\le4$, one transition at every $N$, then bisection). For $N\le32$ the bracket of width $3\times10^{-11}$ is certified by a Sturm count in ball arithmetic at 400 bits, and for $N=34,36$ it is a double precision bisection. At the threshold four zeros meet on the circle as two double zeros $e^{\pm i\theta_N}$, and just below it they leave the circle as a quartet $e^{\pm u\pm i\theta}$. The threshold rises with $N$ from $1.2424$ at $N=10$ to $1.8329$ at $N=36$ and stays below $\beta^*(N)$, the root of $2^\beta Z^{\rm F}_N(\beta,1)=4$, which falls from $2.1056$ to $2.0525$. This is a computation for these $N$ and says nothing about larger $N$.
results.label: fm:res:ly

results.name: Conjecture on the Lee and Yang property of the Farey chain in a field above and below beta equal to 2
results.summary: For every beta above 2 the Farey chain in a field is conjectured to have the Lee and Yang property for all large N, and for every beta between 0 and 2 to fail it for all large N.
results.statement: For the Farey chain in a field, with partition function $Z^{\rm F}_N(\beta,x)=\sum(\operatorname{tr}\varpi_1\cdots\varpi_N)^{-\beta}x^{n_B}$, with $n_B$ the number of letters $B$, over the words $\varpi_1\cdots\varpi_N$ in $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$ and $B=A^{\mathsf T}$, say that it has the Lee and Yang property at $(\beta,N)$ when every zero of $x\mapsto Z^{\rm F}_N(\beta,x)$ lies on the unit circle. Conjecture: for every $\beta>2$ the property holds at $(\beta,N)$ for all large $N$, and for every $\beta$ with $0<\beta<2$ it fails for all large $N$. The value $2$ is the inverse temperature of the phase transition of the chain, not a fit: free fits of the computed thresholds $\beta_{\rm LY}(N)$ in powers of $1/N$ extrapolate to values between $2.017$ and $2.086$, all above $2$.
results.label: fm:conj:ly

results.name: Mixed shoulders and the sine transform of the slope (open problem)
results.summary: Decide which symmetric densities on an interval whose slope first rises and then falls give ferromagnetic laws, beyond the symmetric slopes settled in the book; on the half line the slope of the Pólya density also rises and then falls, and the Riemann Hypothesis is the statement that its sine transform has only real zeros.
results.statement: A real random variable is called ferromagnetic if it is symmetric, has $\mathbb{E}e^{b_0X^2}<\infty$ for some $b_0>0$, and its moment generating function vanishes only on the imaginary axis. Let $p$ be a symmetric probability density on $[-1,1]$, absolutely continuous and nonincreasing on $[0,1]$ with $p(1)=0$, and put $g=-p'\ge0$ on $(0,1)$. For a variable $X$ with density $p$ and characteristic function $\varphi_X$, integration by parts gives $z\,\varphi_X(z)=2\int_0^1g(y)\sin(zy)\,dy$, so $X$ is ferromagnetic if and only if the sine transform of the slope $g$ has only real zeros. The book decides the case in which $g$ is monotone: $X$ is ferromagnetic if $p$ is concave on $[0,1]$, and not ferromagnetic if $p$ is convex on $[0,1]$ and not linear on its support. Open problem: decide the slopes that first rise and then fall. One class is settled. If $g$ is symmetric about $\frac12$, then $p(0)=\int_0^1g=1$, so that $u\mapsto g(\frac12+u)$ is a probability density on $[-\frac12,\frac12]$, and $X\overset{d}{=}\frac12U+B$ with $U$ uniform on $[-1,1]$ and $B$ independent with that density; since $\sin(z/2)/(z/2)$ has only real zeros, $X$ is then ferromagnetic exactly when $B$ is. For the beta slopes $g(y)\propto y^a(1-y)^b$ with $a,b\ge0$ this decides the diagonal $a=b$, where $B$ is a symmetric beta law and $X$ is ferromagnetic, and the shoulder theorem decides the edges: $X$ is ferromagnetic for $b=0$, where $p$ is concave, and not for $a=0<b$, where $p$ is convex and not linear. The rest of the quadrant is not decided. On the half line the slope of the Pólya law, the symmetric law with density $\Phi/\xi(\frac12)$ where $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ and $\Phi(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}(4\pi^2n^4e^{9t/2}-6\pi n^2e^{5t/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2t})$, rises and then falls, and the Riemann Hypothesis is the statement that its sine transform has only real zeros.
results.label: fm:prob:shoulder

results.name: Does the Pólya law belong to the Griffiths Simon class (open problem)
results.summary: Decide whether the Pólya law is a weak limit of suitably scaled sums of ferromagnetically coupled Ising spins, a positive answer to which would imply the Riemann Hypothesis.
results.statement: The Griffiths Simon class consists of the weak limits of suitably scaled sums of ferromagnetically coupled Ising spins; its laws are ferromagnetic, that is symmetric with a moment generating function that vanishes only on the imaginary axis. The class of Ellis, Monroe and Newman consists of the laws with density $e^{-V(x)}$, $V$ even and $V'$ convex on $[0,\infty)$, and their weak limits; by a theorem of Newman the Pólya law (the symmetric law with density $\Phi/\xi(\frac12)$, where $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ and $\Phi(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}(4\pi^2n^4e^{9t/2}-6\pi n^2e^{5t/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2t})$, and with moment generating function $\xi(\frac12+s)/\xi(\frac12)$) belongs to it. Open problem: does the Pólya law belong to the Griffiths Simon class? A positive answer would imply the Riemann Hypothesis. Under Ingham's hypothesis, that the positive ordinates of the zeros of $\zeta$ are linearly independent over the rationals, the Pólya law is not a sum of independent scaled fair signs, so the spins of any approximating system would have to be coupled.
results.label: fm:prob:gs

results.name: Splitting the zeros of the Pólya characteristic function into two characteristic functions (open problem)
results.summary: Under the Riemann Hypothesis, decide whether the ordinates can be split into two nonempty sets, each giving a product that is a characteristic function.
results.statement: Assume the Riemann Hypothesis, and let $X$ be the Pólya variable (the symmetric random variable with density $\Phi/\xi(\frac12)$, where $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ and $\Phi(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}(4\pi^2n^4e^{9t/2}-6\pi n^2e^{5t/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2t})$, and with moment generating function $\xi(\frac12+s)/\xi(\frac12)$), so that its characteristic function is $\varphi_X(t)=\prod_\gamma(1-t^2/\gamma^2)$ over the positive ordinates $\gamma$ of the zeros of $\zeta$, with no Gaussian factor. Open problem: can the ordinates be split into two nonempty sets $A$ and $A'$ such that $\prod_{\gamma\in A}(1-t^2/\gamma^2)$ and $\prod_{\gamma\in A'}(1-t^2/\gamma^2)$ are both characteristic functions? This is the same as writing $X=D+R$ with $D$ and $R$ independent, ferromagnetic and not $0$, and both sets are then infinite. Under Ingham's hypothesis, that the positive ordinates are linearly independent over the rationals, no three ordinates are in arithmetic progression, so no piece is a scaled fair sign or a scaled uniform variable, whose zeros form arithmetic progressions.
results.label: fm:prob:split

results.name: Which ferromagnetic laws have all nonreal zeros of the clock Mellin transform on one vertical line? (open problem)
results.summary: Decide for which ferromagnetic laws the Mellin transform of the clock has all its nonreal zeros on one vertical line, and whether the uniform pair is, up to scale, the only pair from the U shaped class with this property.
results.statement: For a ferromagnetic law $X$ let $\mathcal D_X(w)=\Gamma(w)\mathbb{E}T_X^{-w}$ be the Mellin transform of the Laplace transform of its clock $T_X$ (the sum of $e_k/c_k^2$ over the zeros $\pm c_k$ of the characteristic function). Open problem: for which ferromagnetic laws $X$ does $\mathcal D_X$ have nonreal zeros, all of them on one vertical line? The uniform pair $\pi U+\pi U'$ ($U,U'$ independent uniform on $[-1,1]$) has this property if and only if the Riemann Hypothesis holds, since $\mathcal D_{\pi U+\pi U'}(w)=2\pi^{-w}\Gamma(w)\xi(1+2w)$. The sums of one, four and six independent copies of $\pi U$ do not have it (for four and six computed), and neither do the pairs $X_\varepsilon+X_\varepsilon'$ with density proportional to $1+\varepsilon t^2$ on $[-\pi,\pi]$ for small $\varepsilon>0$ (computed), so no theorem whose hypotheses hold for every symmetric density on an interval that is nondecreasing in $|t|$ can give it. Is the uniform pair, up to scale, the only pair $X+X'$ with $X$ a symmetric density on an interval nondecreasing in $|t|$ that has it? A first step is the first order motion of the zeros along the densities $\frac1{2\pi}+\varepsilon g$ on $[-\pi,\pi]$, which is linear in $g$: is there an even $g\ne0$ with $\int g=0$ along which every zero $\frac{\rho_k-1}2$ keeps its real part to first order?
results.label: fm:prob:mellin

results.name: Positivity of the zero completed laws and the threshold near K = 5000 (open problem)
results.summary: Compute the positivity threshold of the zero completed laws near K equal to 5000, where two fits to the ratio of the threshold to the Gaussian variance part ways, and decide whether every zero completed law is a probability density.
