results.summary: The book asks for the gap law of the one variable ferromagnetism test when clusters of zeros are as wide as the spacing of their neighbours, so that a certificate states exactly how much of the strip it excludes.
results.statement: For one pair off the line, the exact criterion of the book gives the law $\eta-w^*=\tfrac12\phi^2\eta^3(1+O(\eta))$, so the one variable test, ferromagnetism of $\cosh(wx)\,p$, measures the distance of an isolated pair from the line to third order. For clusters that are small compared with their distance from the other zeros each cluster is seen through its own field, among simple pairs the widest decide the threshold, and a double pair is missed by the fixed fraction $1-\cos\tfrac\pi4$ of its distance rather than to third order. What remains is clusters as wide as the spacing of their neighbours, so that a certificate for the tilt in a window says exactly how much of the strip it excludes; such a certificate can exclude at most the zeros with $\operatorname{Re}s>\tfrac12+w/\cos\tfrac\pi4$ unless simplicity of the zeros is also certified.
results.label: route:prob:gap

results.name: Problem: a family along the Euler product with propagating Lee and Yang property
results.summary: The book asks for an integer indexed family of laws or spins built from the Euler product of zeta whose Lee and Yang property or Toeplitz positivity propagates from one member to the next and whose limit is the Pólya spin.
results.statement: For a curve the point counts over all extensions $\mathbb F_{q^n}$ are governed by the same $2g$ eigenvalues, and positivity of the Toeplitz form propagates along $n$. Find a family of laws or spins indexed by an integer, built from the Euler product of $\zeta$, whose Lee and Yang property, or Toeplitz positivity, can be propagated from one member to the next, and whose limit is the Pólya spin. Finite truncations of the Euler product are not such a family.
results.label: route:prob:family

results.name: Problem: the two spin Lee and Yang property for every w above some w_0 below one half
results.summary: The book asks for a proof of the two spin Lee and Yang property for every w above some w_0 below one half, which is a zero free half plane Re s above one half plus w_0, the quasi Riemann hypothesis.
results.statement: Prove the two spin Lee and Yang property for every $w>w_0$, for one $w_0<\tfrac12$. By the book's pair corollary the two spin form at every $w>w_0$ is the zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\tfrac12+w_0$, the quasi Riemann hypothesis. A proof by the methods of this book would be a proof of positivity from the primes at a level below one.
results.label: route:prob:qrh

results.name: Jensen polynomials of the Pólya moments as finite free products (open problem)
results.summary: Find factorisations of the normalised coefficients of the Jensen polynomials of the Pólya moment sequence into two real rooted polynomials, which would give real zeros, or show that none exist with factors of a given kind.
results.statement: Let $X$ be the Pólya variable, the symmetric random variable with density $p=\Phi/\xi(\frac12)$, where $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ and $\Phi(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}(4\pi^2n^4e^{9t/2}-6\pi n^2e^{5t/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2t})$; its moment generating function is $\mathbb{E}e^{sX}=\xi(\frac12+s)/\xi(\frac12)$. Put $b_j=\mathbb{E}X^{2j}/(2j)!$, so that $\Xi(t)/\Xi(0)=\sum_{j\ge0}(-1)^jb_jt^{2j}$ with $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, and for $d,n\ge0$ let $J_{d,n}(x)=\sum_{i=0}^d\binom di(n+i)!\,b_{n+i}x^i$ be the Jensen polynomial of degree $d$ and shift $n$ of the sequence $j!\,b_j$. Pólya proved that the Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if every $J_{d,n}$ has only real zeros. The finite free multiplicative convolution $\boxtimes_d$ of polynomials of degree $d$ multiplies their normalised coefficients (the coefficient of $x^{d - i}$ divided by $\binom di$, up to the sign $(-1)^i$) and keeps roots real and of one sign when both factors have real roots of one sign. The normalised coefficients of the reversed Jensen polynomial $x^dJ_{d,n}(1/x)$ are, up to the signs $(-1)^i$, the numbers $(n+i)!\,b_{n+i}$ for $0\le i\le d$. A factorisation $(n+i)!\,b_{n+i}=\alpha_i\beta_i$ into the normalised coefficients of two polynomials with only real roots of one sign would therefore give real zeros of $J_{d,n}$. Open problem: find such factorisations for every shift $n$ at a fixed degree $d$, or show that none exists with factors of a given kind. The obvious split, a Gaussian multiplier sequence $q^{i^2}$ with $0<q\le1$ times a residual close to the coefficients of $(1+x)^d$, fails, because a root of multiplicity $d$ splits into nonreal roots under a generic perturbation. Dividing the normalised coefficients of a polynomial with real roots of one sign by $(a)_i=a(a+1)\cdots(a+i-1)$ keeps its roots real, but multiplying them by $(a)_i$ does not (it turns $(1+x)^2$ into $1+2ax+a(a+1)x^2$, whose discriminant is $-4a<0$). A factorisation has to put real structure into both factors.
results.label: prob:wigfree:jensen

results.name: Laguerre and Meixner Pollaczek expansions of the Pólya density (open problem)
results.summary: Find a variable in which the Pólya density or the Xi function has an expansion in Laguerre or Meixner Pollaczek polynomials with positive coefficients and truncations with only real zeros.
results.statement: Let $X$ be the Pólya variable, the symmetric random variable with density $p=\Phi/\xi(\frac12)$, where $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ and $\Phi(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}(4\pi^2n^4e^{9t/2}-6\pi n^2e^{5t/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2t})$, and let $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$. The book proves that for no $a>0$ is $|X|$ or $X^2$ a scale mixture of Gamma$(a)$ laws, and that, under the Riemann Hypothesis, removing a gamma layer keeps zeros real while adding one does not: the function $G_a(u)=\sum_kb_ku^k/(a)_k$, with $b_k=\mathbb{E}X^{2k}/(2k)!$ and $(a)_k=a(a+1)\cdots(a+k-1)$, lies in the Laguerre Pólya class (the entire functions that are locally uniform limits of real rooted polynomials) for every $a>0$, whereas multiplying the coefficients by $(a)_k$ instead does not preserve real zeros. Open problem: find a variable in which the Pólya density, or $\Xi$ itself, has an expansion in Laguerre or Meixner Pollaczek polynomials with positive coefficients and truncations with only real zeros. The symmetric Meixner Pollaczek expansions treated in the book converge slowly, and a real rooted construction from their coefficients is a separate open problem of the chapter on the reciprocal zeta function.
results.label: prob:wigfree:laguerre

results.name: Jacobi parameters of the zero measure and the local semicircle model (open problem)
results.summary: Prove under the Riemann Hypothesis that the Jacobi parameters of the measure of the inverse squared ordinates satisfy alpha_n ~ 2 beta_n ~ L_n/2, a spectral form of the Riemann von Mangoldt formula, and explain the scatter of the ratios.
results.statement: Let $\gamma_1\le\gamma_2\le\cdots$ be the positive ordinates of the zeros $\frac12\pm i\gamma_j$ of $\zeta$, put $a_j=\gamma_j^2$ and let $\nu=\sum_ja_j^{-1}\delta_{1/a_j}$, a measure whose moments are computed from the Taylor coefficients at the centre of the Xi function $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, where $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ is Riemann's xi function. Under the Riemann Hypothesis $\nu$ is a positive measure and all its Jacobi parameters exist: write $\alpha_n$ for the diagonal entries and $\beta_n>0$ for the off diagonal entries of its Jacobi matrix, the recurrence coefficients of its orthogonal polynomials. A semicircle law is a local model for them: constant parameters $\alpha_n=\alpha$, $\beta_n=\beta$ give the semicircle law on $[\alpha-2\beta,\alpha+2\beta]$, and a local model with right end $L_n$ of the interval for row $n$ has $\alpha_n=\frac12L_n$ and $\beta_n=\frac14L_n$. Let $N$ be the smooth Riemann von Mangoldt count of the ordinates, $n(L)=\int_{(0,L^{-1/2})}dN(T)/\sqrt{1-LT^2}$, and define $L_n$ by $n(L_n)=n$. Open problem: under the Riemann Hypothesis, prove that $\alpha_n\sim2\beta_n\sim\frac12L_n$ as $n\to\infty$, a spectral form of the Riemann von Mangoldt formula. A table in the book supports it to a few per cent for $n\le49$, but the local model is a heuristic, outside the scaling of Kuijlaars and Van Assche (1999). Also decide between the rules $n(L_n)=n$ and $n(L_n')=n-\frac12$, which the data do not separate, and explain the scatter of the ratios, about six per cent, through the individual gaps between the zeros.
results.label: prob:wigfree:jacobi

results.name: Order at which a zero collision is registered by the Hankel test (open problem)
results.summary: Find the rule giving the order of the Hankel matrix at which the collision of a pair of zeros along the de Bruijn Newman flow is registered, and follow the failure times of the Hankel test to orders of a few hundred.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be Riemann's xi function, $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$ the Xi function, and $H_t$ the de Bruijn Newman heat flow in the normalisation of Rodgers and Tao, which the book uses: $8H_t(2\theta)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(v)e^{tv^2/4}\cos(\theta v)\,dv$, where $\Phi(v)=\sum_{n\ge1}(4\pi^2n^4e^{9v/2}-6\pi n^2e^{5v/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2v})$, so that $8H_0(2\theta)=\Xi(\theta)$. Write $\pm\theta_j(t)$ for the zeros of $\theta\mapsto H_t(2\theta)$, so that $\theta_j(0)=\gamma_j$, where $\frac12\pm i\gamma_j$ are the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$, numbered by height. For every $t<0$ the function $H_t$ has nonreal zeros, by the theorem of Rodgers and Tao, and as $t$ decreases from $0$ pairs of consecutive real zeros $\theta_k(t),\theta_{k+1}(t)$, which start at $(\gamma_k,\gamma_{k+1})$, collide and leave the real axis. Let $\mathcal H_N(t)=[m_{i+j}(t)]_{i,j<N}$ be the Hankel matrix of order $N$ of the moments $m_n(t)=\sum_j\theta_j(t)^{-2n-2}$ (at $t=0$ these are $m_n(0)=\sum_k\gamma_k^{-2n-2}$). Under the Riemann Hypothesis $\mathcal H_N(0)$ is positive definite. Let $n_{\rm fail}(t)$ be the least $N$ for which $\mathcal H_N(t)$ is not positive definite and $t^*_N=\sup\{t<0:n_{\rm fail}(t)\le N\}$, the time, going back from $t=0$, at which the Hankel test of order $N$ first fails. Under the Riemann Hypothesis every $t^*_N$ is negative, $t^*_N\le t^*_{N+1}$ and $t^*_N\to0$. The book computes $t^*_N$ for $N\le50$ and explains the steps of the staircase by collisions. The rule suggested in an unpublished note of N. G. Polson, that the collision of $(\gamma_k,\gamma_{k+1})$ is registered from order about $2k+2$ on, holds for $N=30$ and $40$ and fails at $N=50$: it gives the collision of $(\gamma_{24},\gamma_{25})$ at $t=-1.144$, while the matrix of order $50$ registers $(\gamma_{27},\gamma_{28})$, for which $2k+2=56$, at $t=-1.0325$, before $(\gamma_{24},\gamma_{25})$ has collided. Open problem: find the rule that gives the order at which a pair is registered, as a function of the index $k$ of the pair and of its distance from the axis, and follow the staircase of $t^*_N$ to orders of a few hundred, towards the limit $0$ that it has under the Riemann Hypothesis.
results.label: prob:wigfree:window

results.name: Unconditional brackets for the collision times of zeros along the de Bruijn Newman flow (open problem)
results.summary: Find a priori control of the nonreal zeros of the heat evolved Xi function at negative times so that the book's brackets for collision times become statements computed from the Xi function at time zero alone.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be Riemann's xi function, $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$ the Xi function, and $H_t$ the de Bruijn Newman heat flow in the normalisation of Rodgers and Tao, which the book uses: $8H_t(2\theta)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(v)e^{tv^2/4}\cos(\theta v)\,dv$, where $\Phi(v)=\sum_{n\ge1}(4\pi^2n^4e^{9v/2}-6\pi n^2e^{5v/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2v})$, so that $8H_0(2\theta)=\Xi(\theta)$; as $t$ decreases below $0$, pairs of adjacent real zeros of $H_t$ collide and leave the real axis, and $H_t$ has nonreal zeros for every $t<0$ by the theorem of Rodgers and Tao. The book brackets the collision times of such pairs by quantities computed along the flow and through the nonreal zeros of $H_t$, and checks the hypotheses of the brackets on a grid of times for the $58$ collisions of a census computed in the book. Open problem: find a priori control of the nonreal zeros of $H_t$ for $t<0$, of how far they travel and how close to a gap between real zeros they come, which would make the brackets statements about $H_t$ computed from $H_0$ alone.
results.label: prob:wigfree:collide

results.name: Extending the derivative sign ladder of the heat trace without new information on the zeros (open problem)
results.summary: Find a mechanism, for instance a functional equation for the law of the clock under the Upsilon transform, that extends the proved ranges of derivative signs of the heat trace without further information on the zeros.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function, $\gamma_k$ the ordinates of its zeros $\frac12\pm i\gamma_k$ in the upper half plane, $a_k=\gamma_k^2$ and $W(t)=\sum_ke^{-ta_k}$ the heat trace of the zeros. Let $T$ be the clock, the positive random variable with Laplace transform $1/G(u)$, $G(u)=\xi(\frac12+\sqrt{u})/\xi(\frac12)$, which has Lévy measure $W(x)\,dx/x$. The Upsilon transform sends an infinitely divisible law $\mu$ with Lévy process $(X_t)$, $X_1\sim\mu$, to the law of $\int_0^1\log(1/t)\,dX_t$, and the class BO is the class of infinitely divisible laws on $[0,\infty)$ whose Lévy measure has a completely monotone density. The book proves the derivative signs $(-1)^kW^{(k)}>0$ on ranges that grow with the height to which the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) is verified, and complete monotonicity of $W$ on $(0,\infty)$ is RH. Open problem: find a mechanism that extends these ranges with no new information on the zeros, for instance a functional equation for the law of $T$ under the Upsilon transform, as suggested in an unpublished note of N. G. Polson. The book restricts the form such an equation can take: with no hypothesis $T$ is not the Upsilon image of a law in BO, and under RH $T$ is the Upsilon image of the law $\mu_0$, the self decomposable law with no drift and Lévy measure $N(x^{-1/2})\,dx/x$, where $N(T)$ is the number of ordinates $\gamma_k\le T$, which is neither a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) nor in BO.
results.label: prob:wigfree:ladder

results.name: Four off line zeros that pass the finite heat trace tests
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2017, version 24 of 2026), On Hilbert's 8th problem, arXiv:1708.02653.
results.summary: Moving a close pair of zeros of xi on the critical line to four zeros at distance one quarter off the line gives an even entire function whose heat trace still passes the finite tests (infinite divisibility, self decomposability, log convexity, and at large heights positive Hankel blocks and derivative signs up to order 10^17).
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function and $W(t)=\sum_je^{-a_jt}$ its heat trace ($a_j=-(\rho_j-\tfrac12)^2$, one zero $\rho_j$ from each pair $\{\rho,1-\rho\}$, counted with multiplicity); the clock is $\xi(\tfrac12)/\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt u)$. (a) There are ordinates $1000<A<B\le2000$ of zeros on the critical line, with $B-A\le2$, such that, with $g=(A+B)/2$ and $w=\tfrac14+ig$, $F(s)=\frac{\xi(\frac12+s)}{\xi(\frac12)}\,\frac{(1-s^2/w^2)(1-s^2/\bar w^2)}{(1+s^2/A^2)(1+s^2/B^2)}$ is an even entire function with the order, type and reflection symmetry of $\xi(\tfrac12+s)$ and with four zeros off the critical line, and the following hold. The reciprocal clock $1/F(\sqrt u)$ is the Laplace transform of an infinitely divisible, self decomposable law, and its heat trace $W_F(t)=W(t)+2\operatorname{Re}e^{-at}-e^{-A^2t}-e^{-B^2t}$, $a=-w^2=g^2-\tfrac1{16}-\tfrac{ig}2$, which is $t$ times its Lévy density, is strictly log convex. $W_F$ has the same small time expansion as $W$ through the constant term, and $1/F$ has the same nearest poles as the reciprocal Xi function. (b) Let $N\ge1$ and $R\ge T_N$, where $T_N=20000N\sqrt{1+\log N}$, and suppose that every zero of $\xi$ with ordinate in $(0,R+50]$ lies on the critical line. Then the pair can instead be chosen with $R<A\le B\le R+50$ and $B-A<2$ (if $A=B$, a multiple zero supplies both), so that $F$ keeps every property listed in (a) and the leading $N\times N$ Hankel blocks $[c_{i+j}]_{i,j<N}$ and $[c_{i+j+1}]_{i,j<N}$ of $W_F$, with $c_k=(-1)^kW_F^{(k)}$, remain positive definite at every $t>0$. If moreover $R\ge10^{12}$, the derivative signs are also preserved: $(-1)^kW_F^{(k)}(t)>0$ for every $t>0$ and every integer $0\le k\le10^{17}$. For every $N\le3\times10^7$ the verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021) establishes the hypothesis on the zeros for $R=\max(T_N,10^{12})$, so that such an $F$ with both properties exists unconditionally.
results.label: thm:ch13:perturb

results.name: A pair of zeros off the line at the height of a line zero: its contribution to the density at resolution epsilon is positive exactly when epsilon is below d over sqrt 3 or above d
results.summary: The zeros $\frac12$ and $\frac12\pm d$ at one ordinate contribute to $\pi\rho_\varepsilon$ a rational function that is positive at every $\theta$ if and only if $\varepsilon<d/\sqrt3$ or $\varepsilon>d$; so when every off line zero shares its ordinate with a line zero and the distances have a positive infimum $d_0$, the density is positive on every line with $0<\varepsilon<d_0/\sqrt3$ although zeros lie to the right of it.
results.statement: Let $d>0$, $\varepsilon>0$, $\varepsilon\ne d$ and $u=(\theta-\gamma)^2$. The zeros $\frac12+i\gamma$ and $\frac12\pm d+i\gamma$ contribute to $\pi\rho_\varepsilon(\theta)$ the quantity $\varepsilon(3u^2+6\varepsilon^2u+(3\varepsilon^2-d^2)(\varepsilon^2-d^2))/((\varepsilon^2+u)((d-\varepsilon)^2+u)((d+\varepsilon)^2+u))$, which is positive at every $\theta$ if and only if $\varepsilon<d/\sqrt3$ or $\varepsilon>d$. Hence, if every zero off the line of an entire function with the order, symmetry and reality of $\xi$ shares its ordinate with a zero on the line of at least its multiplicity, and the distances $d$ have a positive infimum $d_0$, its density is positive at every height on every line $\operatorname{Re}s=\frac12+\varepsilon$ with $0<\varepsilon<d_0/\sqrt3$, although zeros lie to the right of these lines. To first order in $\varepsilon$ the contribution is $\varepsilon(3u^2+d^4)/(u(u+d^2)^2)>0$ for every $d$, as $P(x)=x(x^2+d^2)$ satisfies $P'^2-PP''=3x^4+d^4>0$ on the real line.
results.label: tx4:prop:triple

results.name: Certified zero of a Mellin transform closes the Bernstein Pick route to RH
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2017, version 24 of 2026), On Hilbert's 8th problem, arXiv:1708.02653.
results.summary: A certified simple zero of the meromorphically continued Mellin transform M of the Pólya density near -8.494 + 2.938i gives the canonical interpolant of the moment ratios a nonreal pole, so no Bernstein interpolant is a complete Bernstein function and the Bernstein Pick route to RH is closed.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function, $\Xi(z)=\xi(\tfrac12+iz)$, $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}\bigl(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2}\bigr)\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2u})$ the Pólya kernel, so that $\Xi(\theta)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)\cos(\theta u)\,du$, and let $X$ be a random variable with the Pólya density $\Phi/\Xi(0)$. Put $M(s)=\mathbb{E}|X|^{2s}$, analytic for $\operatorname{Re}s>-\tfrac12$ and continued meromorphically to $\operatorname{Re}s<0$ by $M(s)=\frac{2\,\Gamma(2s+1)\sin(-\pi s)}{\pi\,\Xi(0)}\int_0^\infty\Xi(\theta)\,\theta^{-2s-1}\,d\theta$ for $-\tfrac12<\operatorname{Re}s<0$, and let $\varphi_I(s)=4(s-\tfrac12)M(s-1)/M(s)$, the canonical interpolant of the moment ratios. Then $M$ has exactly one zero in the disc $|s-s_1|<10^{-8}$ with centre $s_1=-8.494182256992559+2.937767068567584i$; the zero is simple, and $M(s-1)$ does not vanish in the disc. Hence $\varphi_I$ has a nonreal pole, and every Bernstein interpolant of the moment ratios (a Bernstein function that takes the values $\varphi_I(n)$ at the integers $n\ge1$) agrees with $\varphi_I$ on $(1,\infty)$ and cannot be continued through that pole, so none is a complete Bernstein function. For every $0<q<1$ the sequence $n\varphi_I(n)/(n-q)$ has no Bernstein interpolant either.
results.label: thm:ch13:mellin

results.name: Local model for the first failing derivative order of the heat trace near an off line quadruple
results.summary: To leading order, if two consecutive zeros of xi on the line are replaced by an off line quadruple at distance $\delta$ from the line and height $g$, with $\Delta$ the larger gap to the nearest line zeros and $\delta\ll\Delta\ll g$, the first derivative order at which a sign fails, for the heat trace restricted to the quadruple and its two neighbouring zeros on the line, is $k^*=\omega^*g^2/(2\delta\Delta)$, about $\frac\pi4g^2/(\delta\Delta)$, at a time depending on $\delta$ and $\Delta$ only; the comparison of this time with the seven certified failure times of the book's table, within 0.20 to 2.76 per cent, is a computation.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function. Let $F$ be obtained from $\xi$ by replacing two consecutive zeros of $\xi$ on the critical line by the quadruple of zeros $\tfrac12\pm\delta\pm ig$, where $g$ is the midpoint of the two ordinates and $\delta>0$, the other zeros being unchanged, and let $W_F(t)=\sum_je^{-a_jt}$ be the heat trace of $F$ ($a_j=-(\rho_j-\tfrac12)^2$, one zero $\rho_j$ from each pair $\{\rho,1-\rho\}$ of zeros of $F$, counted with multiplicity). For an order $k>0$, not necessarily an integer, let $c_k^F(t)=\sum_ja_j^ke^{-a_jt}$ with $a_j^k$ the principal power (for an integer $k$ this is $(-1)^kW_F^{(k)}(t)$). Let $g-\Delta_-$ and $g+\Delta_+$ be the ordinates of the nearest zeros of $F$ on the critical line below and above $g$, and put $\Delta=\max(\Delta_-,\Delta_+)$. Assume $\delta\ll\Delta\ll g$ and write $\omega=2k\delta\Delta/g^2$ and $\kappa=2k\Delta^2/g^2$. Restricted to the quadruple and these two zeros, $c_k^F(t)<0$ for some $t>0$ if and only if, to leading order, $\min_{0\le\eta\le1}\bigl[2\cos(\omega\eta)+e^{-\kappa(1-\eta)}\bigr]<0$ (the neglected terms are relative errors $O(\delta/\Delta)$ in the weight of the quadruple, $O(\delta^2/(g\Delta))$ in its phase and $O(\kappa\Delta/g)$ in the exponent of the neighbouring zero). The first failing order, the least $k$ for which this holds, is $k^*=\frac{\omega^*g^2}{2\delta\Delta}$, where $\omega^*=\frac\pi2+\frac\delta\Delta\bigl(1+\log\frac\Delta{2\delta}\bigr)+O\bigl(\frac{\delta^2}{\Delta^2}+\frac\Delta g\bigr)$, so that $k^*=\frac\pi4\,\frac{g^2}{\delta\Delta}\,(1+o(1))$ as $\delta/\Delta\to0$ and $\Delta/g\to0$. The failure is at the time $t^*=\frac{k^*}{g^2}\bigl(1+O(\Delta/g)\bigr)=\frac{\omega^*}{2\delta\Delta}\bigl(1+O(\Delta/g)\bigr)$, which involves $\delta$ and $\Delta$ only. The book compares the time $t^*_{\mathrm{loc}}=\omega^*/(2\delta\Delta)$, without the remainder, with the certified failure times $t^*$ of its table of first failing orders, seven rows with $g$ from $185.24$ to $1977.22$, $\delta=\frac14$ and $\delta=0.1$, and $\Delta$ read from the zeros: the difference $100\,(t^*_{\mathrm{loc}}/t^*-1)$ is between $0.20$ and $2.76$ per cent. This comparison is a computation, not part of the proposition.
results.label: xg:prop:local

results.name: Tilted Pólya representation of xi and its derivative
results.summary: Moving the line of integration of Pólya's integral into the strip of analyticity of the Pólya kernel gives exact integral formulas for $\xi$ and $\xi'$ on a line at distance $\delta$ from the edge of the strip, with kernel bounds of order $\delta^{-5/2}$.
results.statement: Let $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge 1}\bigl(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2} - 3\pi n^2e^{5u/2}\bigr)\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2u})$ be the Pólya kernel, an even function that is analytic in the strip $|\operatorname{Im}u|<\pi/4$, and let $\xi$ be the completed zeta function, so that $\xi(\frac12+s)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)e^{su}\,du$. Let $0<\delta<\pi/4$ and $\eta=\pi/4 - \delta$. Then for every complex $s$, $\xi(\frac12+s)=e^{i\eta s}\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(x+i\eta)\,e^{sx}\,dx$ and $\xi'(\frac12+s)=e^{i\eta s}\int_{\mathbb{R}}(x+i\eta)\,\Phi(x+i\eta)\,e^{sx}\,dx$. For real $x$, $|\Phi(x+i\eta)|\le C_\delta$ and $|(x+i\eta)\Phi(x+i\eta)|\le C_\delta$, with $C_\delta=O(\delta^{-5/2})$ as $\delta\to 0$.
results.label: prop:tilt

results.name: Mass defect of the Thorin measure on a window
results.summary: When every zero up to height $\Theta$ lies on the critical line, the Thorin mass of the window $(0,\Theta^2]$ equals the zero count $N(\Theta)$ minus $(\varepsilon/\pi)\,\Xi'(\Theta)/\Xi(\Theta)$ up to a remainder of order $\varepsilon^2$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed zeta function, $\Xi(\theta)=\xi(\frac12+i\theta)$, and for $\varepsilon>0$ let $\mu_\varepsilon$ be the signed measure on $(0,\infty)$ whose density in the variable $\theta=\sqrt{z}$ is the Thorin density $\rho_\varepsilon(\theta)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\frac12+\varepsilon+i\theta)$, so that $\mu_\varepsilon((0,\Theta^2])=\int_0^\Theta\rho_\varepsilon(\theta)\,d\theta$. Let $N(\Theta)$ be the number of zeros $\rho$ of $\xi$ with $0<\operatorname{Im}\rho\le\Theta$, counted with multiplicity. Suppose that $\Theta$ is not the ordinate of a zero and that every zero with $0<\operatorname{Im}\rho\le\Theta$ lies on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\frac12$. Then $\mu_\varepsilon((0,\Theta^2])=N(\Theta) - \frac{\varepsilon}{\pi}\,\frac{\Xi'(\Theta)}{\Xi(\Theta)}+O(\varepsilon^2)$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow 0$. The book also shows that the remainder is in fact $O(\varepsilon^3)$.
results.label: prop:mass

results.name: Signatures of an off line zero in the Thorin density
results.summary: The effect of an off line pair of zeros on the Thorin density is computed in closed form: a displacement that keeps the count has total variation $\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{4\pi}(\delta/\varepsilon)^2$ per displaced zero to leading order for $\delta<\varepsilon$, an omitted pair has total variation $\frac4\pi\arcsin(\varepsilon/\delta)$, and a displaced zero has negative mass $\frac1\pi\arcsin(\varepsilon/\delta)$, the last two for $\delta>\varepsilon$; the quadratic growth of the first is the square root law of Polson (2026).
results.statement: Let $P_a(x)=a/(\pi(a^2+x^2))$ for $a>0$ be the Poisson (Cauchy) kernel, $P_{-a}=-P_a$, and $P_0$ the unit point mass at the origin, and write $\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{TV}}$ for the total variation norm on $\mathbb{R}$. For $\varepsilon>0$ the Thorin density $\rho_\varepsilon(\theta)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\frac12+\varepsilon+i\theta)$ of the completed zeta function $\xi$ is a sum over the zeros $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ with $\gamma>0$ of kernels $P_{1/2+\varepsilon - \beta}(\theta - \gamma)$ together with their reflections at $-\gamma$: a zero on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\frac12$ with ordinate $\gamma$ contributes $P_\varepsilon$ centred at $\gamma$, and a pair of off line zeros $\frac12\pm\delta+i\gamma$ with $0<\delta<\frac12$ contributes $P_{\varepsilon+\delta}+P_{\varepsilon - \delta}$ centred at $\gamma$. Let $\varepsilon>0$ and $0<\delta<\frac12$. (i) If two line zeros at height $\gamma$ are replaced by the quadruple $\frac12\pm\delta\pm i\gamma$, the density near $\gamma$ changes by $2g$, where $g=\frac12(P_{\varepsilon+\delta}+P_{\varepsilon - \delta}) - P_\varepsilon$ is the change per displaced zero, and for $\delta<\varepsilon$, $\|g\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{4\pi}(\delta/\varepsilon)^2+O(\delta^4/\varepsilon^4)$. (ii) If the pair $\frac12\pm\delta+i\gamma$ exists but a list of line zeros omits it, the difference is $P_{\varepsilon+\delta}+P_{\varepsilon - \delta}$, and its total variation norm is $2$ for $\delta\le\varepsilon$ and $\frac8\pi\arctan\sqrt{(\delta+\varepsilon)/(\delta - \varepsilon)} - 2=\frac4\pi\arcsin(\varepsilon/\delta)$ for $\delta>\varepsilon$. (iii) For $\delta>\varepsilon$ the negative part of $\frac12(P_{\varepsilon+\delta}+P_{\varepsilon - \delta})$, the density of one displaced zero, has mass $\frac2\pi\arctan\sqrt{(\delta+\varepsilon)/(\delta - \varepsilon)} - \frac12=\frac1\pi\arcsin(\varepsilon/\delta)=\frac{\varepsilon}{\pi\delta}+O(\varepsilon^3/\delta^3)$. The expansion $g=\frac{\delta^2}{2}\,\partial_a^2P_a|_{a=\varepsilon}+O(\delta^4)$ behind (i), by which the signature grows like the square of the displacement, is Proposition 19.7 of Polson (2026).
results.label: prop:signature

results.name: Littlewood identity for the cumulative Thorin mass
results.summary: The cumulative Thorin mass at resolution $\varepsilon$ is $\pi^{-1}$ times the derivative in $\varepsilon$ of the integral of $\log|\xi|$ along the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\frac12+\varepsilon$, which links the mass to the integral of $\log|\xi|$ on the critical line.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed zeta function and, for $\varepsilon>0$ and $T>0$, let $M_\varepsilon(T)=\pi^{-1}\int_0^T\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\frac12+\varepsilon+it)\,dt$ be the cumulative Thorin mass at resolution $\varepsilon$ up to height $T$; it equals $\pi^{-1}\arg\xi(\frac12+\varepsilon+iT)$, with the argument continued along the vertical line from the real axis, where $\xi>0$. Let $T>0$. For every $\varepsilon>0$ such that $\xi$ has no zero on the segment from $\frac12+\varepsilon$ to $\frac12+\varepsilon+iT$, $\pi M_\varepsilon(T)=\frac{\partial}{\partial\varepsilon}\int_0^T\log\bigl|\xi(\frac12+\varepsilon+it)\bigr|\,dt$, and for every $\varepsilon>0$, $\int_0^T\log\bigl|\xi(\frac12+\varepsilon+it)\bigr|\,dt=\int_0^T\log\bigl|\xi(\frac12+it)\bigr|\,dt+\pi\int_0^\varepsilon M_{\varepsilon'}(T)\,d\varepsilon'$, where $M_{\varepsilon'}(T)$ is defined except for the finitely many $\varepsilon'$ at which the segment meets a zero.
results.label: prop:littlewood

results.name: Zero density identity from the Thorin mass
results.summary: The cumulative Thorin mass at resolution $\varepsilon$ plus a short horizontal correction equals the zero count $N(T)$ minus twice the number of zeros to the right of the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\frac12+\varepsilon$, and at $\varepsilon=\frac12$ it is Backlund's unconditional count of $N(T)$.
results.statement:
Let $\xi$ be the completed zeta function. For $\varepsilon>0$ and $T>0$ let $M_\varepsilon(T)=\pi^{-1}\arg\xi( rac12+\varepsilon+iT)$ be the cumulative Thorin mass, the argument being continued along the vertical line from the real axis, where $\xi>0$, and let $	au_\varepsilon(T)$ be $\pi^{-1}$ times the change of $\arg\xi$ along the horizontal segment from $ rac12+\varepsilon+iT$ to $ rac12+iT$. Let $N(T)$ be the number of zeros $ho$ with $0<\operatorname{Im}ho\le T$, and $
u(\sigma,T)$ the number of those with $\operatorname{Re}ho>\sigma$, both counted with multiplicity. Let $\varepsilon>0$ and $T>0$, with $T$ not the ordinate of a zero and no zero of $\xi$ on the segment from $ rac12+\varepsilon$ to $ rac12+\varepsilon+iT$. Then $M_\varepsilon(T)+	au_\varepsilon(T)=N(T) - 2\,
u( rac12+\varepsilon,T)$. The segment condition holds at $\varepsilon= rac12$, and $
u(1,T)=0$, which gives the unconditional count $N(T)=M_{1/2}(T)+	au_{1/2}(T)$, and $
u( rac12+\varepsilon,T)= rac12\,[N(T) - M_\varepsilon(T) - 	au_\varepsilon(T)]$ for every $\varepsilon$ satisfying the hypotheses.
results.label: prop:zerodensity

results.name: Velocity of a zero of the de Bruijn Newman function at time zero through Hardy's function
results.summary: The velocity at time zero of a simple zero of the de Bruijn Newman function under the backward heat flow is half the sum of the ratio of the second to the first derivative of Hardy's function at the corresponding zero, a rational term and a digamma term, and the last two terms contribute a drift of minus pi over four for high zeros (credited to a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book).
results.statement: Let $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}\bigl(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u}\bigr)\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})$ and $H_t(z)=\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi(u)\cos(zu)\,du$, so that $H_0(z)=\frac18\Xi(z/2)$ with $\Xi(\theta)=\xi(\frac12+i\theta)$ for Riemann's completed zeta function $\xi$, and let $Z$ be Hardy's function, $Z(\theta)=e^{i\vartheta(\theta)}\zeta(\frac12+i\theta)$, with $\vartheta$ the Riemann Siegel theta function. Let $\gamma_n$ be the $n$th positive zero of $Z$ and suppose it is simple, so that $z_n=2\gamma_n$ is a simple zero of $H_0$ and moves smoothly with $t$ near $t=0$ under the backward heat flow $\partial_tH_t=-\partial_z^2H_t$. Then $\dot z_n(0)=\frac12\Bigl[\frac{Z''(\gamma_n)}{Z'(\gamma_n)}+\frac{4\gamma_n}{\gamma_n^2+1/4}-\operatorname{Im}\psi\bigl(\tfrac14+\tfrac{i\gamma_n}2\bigr)\Bigr]$, where $\psi$ is the digamma function, and the last two terms tend to $-\frac\pi2$ as $\gamma_n\to\infty$, a drift of $-\frac\pi4$ in $\dot z_n$. The first $34$ zeros move down at $t=0$ and the $35$th, at $\gamma_{35}=111.874659177$, moves up, with $\dot z_{35}(0)=+0.0595012982$, all $35$ signs certified in ball arithmetic.
results.label: prop:ch21:velocity

results.name: Critical point lower bound for the collision time of zeros under the backward heat flow
results.summary: While all zeros stay real and simple, a gap between two zeros of a real polynomial cannot close under the backward heat flow before the time one over Laguerre's quantity at the critical point of the gap, and z squared minus a squared attains the bound.
results.statement: Let $f_s$, $s\ge0$, be real entire functions of genus at most one, smooth in $(z,s)$, with $\partial_sf_s=\partial_z^2f_s$; for a real polynomial $p$ and $D=d/dz$ one such family is $f_s=e^{sD^2}p=\sum_{k\ge0}s^kp^{(2k)}/k!$. For a real entire function $f$ of genus at most one with zeros $z_j$, Laguerre's quantity is $\mathcal{L}_f(x)=-\frac{d^2}{dx^2}\log|f(x)|=\big(f'(x)^2-f(x)f''(x)\big)/f(x)^2=\sum_j(x-z_j)^{-2}$, a real sum because nonreal zeros come in conjugate pairs. Fix a gap between two adjacent simple real zeros $z_k(s)<z_{k+1}(s)$ of $f_s$, which move continuously until they meet, if they do. When all zeros of $f_s$ are real, $f_s'/f_s$ falls from $+\infty$ to $-\infty$ across the gap and vanishes at exactly one point $c(s)$, the critical point of the gap; put $\ell(s)=\mathcal{L}_{f_s}(c(s))$. Let $S>0$. If all zeros of $f_\sigma$ are real and simple for $0\le\sigma<S$, then $\dot\ell\le\ell^2$ on $[0,S)$ and $\ell(\sigma)\le\ell(0)/(1-\sigma\ell(0))$ for $0\le\sigma<\min(S,1/\ell(0))$. In particular, if $p$ is a real polynomial with only real simple zeros, and the first collision of any two zeros of $e^{sD^2}p$ happens at $s=s_1$, between the two zeros that bound the gap $(z_k,z_{k+1})$ of $p$ at $s=0$, then $s_1\ge1/\mathcal{L}_p(c_k)$, where $c_k$ is the critical point of $p$ in that gap. The bound is attained by $p(z)=z^2-a^2$.
results.label: thm:wigbiane:riccati

results.name: Biane form lower bound for the collision time of zeros under the backward heat flow
results.summary: While all zeros of a real polynomial stay real and simple, a gap between two adjacent zeros cannot close under the backward heat flow before the time one over the minimum of Laguerre's quantity over the gap, a bound at least as strong as the one from the critical point and attained by z squared minus a squared.
results.statement: Let $f_s$, $s\ge0$, be real entire functions of genus at most one, smooth in $(z,s)$, with $\partial_sf_s=\partial_z^2f_s$; for a real polynomial $p$ and $D=d/dz$ one such family is $f_s=e^{sD^2}p=\sum_{k\ge0}s^kp^{(2k)}/k!$. For a real entire function $f$ of genus at most one with zeros $z_j$, Laguerre's quantity is $\mathcal{L}_f(x)=-\frac{d^2}{dx^2}\log|f(x)|=\big(f'(x)^2-f(x)f''(x)\big)/f(x)^2=\sum_j(x-z_j)^{-2}$, a real sum because nonreal zeros come in conjugate pairs. Fix a gap between two adjacent simple real zeros $z_k(s)<z_{k+1}(s)$ of $f_s$, which move continuously until they meet, if they do. The quantity $\mathcal{L}_{f_s}$ tends to $+\infty$ at both ends of the gap; let $m(s)$ be its minimum over the gap and $D^+m$ the upper right Dini derivative of $m$. Let $S>0$. If all zeros of $f_\sigma$ are real and simple for $0\le\sigma<S$, then $D^+m\le m^2$ on $[0,S)$ and $m(\sigma)\le m(0)/(1-\sigma m(0))$ for $0\le\sigma<\min(S,1/m(0))$. In particular, if $p$ is a real polynomial with only real simple zeros, and the first collision of any two zeros of $e^{sD^2}p$ happens at $s=s_1$, between the two zeros that bound the gap $(z_k,z_{k+1})$ of $p$ at $s=0$, then $s_1\ge1/\min_{(z_k,z_{k+1})}\mathcal{L}_p$. This bound is at least as strong as the critical point bound $1/\mathcal{L}_p(c_k)$, where $c_k$ is the critical point of $p$ in the gap, because the minimum does not exceed the value at $c_k$, and it is attained by $p(z)=z^2-a^2$.
results.label: thm:wigbiane:biane2

results.name: Local lower bound for the closing of a gap with a correction from the nonreal zeros
results.summary: For the minimum m of Laguerre's quantity over a gap between real zeros, the upper right Dini derivative is at most one plus an explicit correction, computed from the nonreal zeros, times m squared, which bounds the time at which the gap closes from below.
results.statement: Let $f_s$, $s\ge0$, be real entire functions of genus at most one, smooth in $(z,s)$, with $\partial_sf_s=\partial_z^2f_s$, for example $f_s=e^{sD^2}p$ with $D=d/dz$ and $p$ a real polynomial. Let $\mathcal{L}(x)=-\frac{d^2}{dx^2}\log|f_s(x)|=\sum_j(x-z_j)^{-2}$, over the zeros $z_j$ of $f_s$, be Laguerre's quantity (a real sum, because nonreal zeros come in conjugate pairs). Fix a gap between two adjacent simple real zeros of $f_s$, which move continuously until they meet, if they do; $\mathcal{L}\to+\infty$ at both ends of the gap. Let $m(s)$ be the minimum of $\mathcal{L}$ over the gap, $D^+m$ its upper right Dini derivative, and at a time $s$ let $u$ be a point of the gap where the minimum is attained, with $m=m(s)=\mathcal{L}(u)>0$. For the conjugate pairs $a\pm ib$, $b>0$, of nonreal zeros of $f_s$, each pair counted once, put $B_p=\sum b^2|u-a|^{-p}$, and assume that $B_4$, $B_5$ and $B_6$ are finite. Then $\mathcal{L}''(u)-3m^2\le\eta m^2$, where $\eta=\big(36\,mB_4+108\,B_4^2+72\,(m+6B_4)^{1/2}B_5+120\,B_6\big)/m^2$, and $D^+m(s)\le(1+\eta)m^2$. Hence, if the two zeros bounding the gap meet at a time $s_c$, and $m>0$ and $\eta\le\bar\eta$ on $[0,s_c)$ for a constant $\bar\eta$ (with $\eta$ evaluated at a minimiser at each time), then $s_c\ge1/\big((1+\bar\eta)\,m(0)\big)$. All of this holds with the coefficient $72$ in $\eta$ replaced by $36$, by the sharp inequality $S_4\le\tfrac12S_2^2+\tfrac12S_2^{1/2}|S_3|$ for the power sums $S_k=\sum_jx_j^k$ of a real square summable sequence $(x_j)$.
results.label: thm:wigbiane:local

results.name: Lower bound for the closing of a gap from the quantity delta, with no knowledge of the nonreal zeros
results.summary: A quantity delta computed from the function and its first four derivatives at the minimiser of Laguerre's quantity over a gap between real zeros controls the growth of that minimum under the backward heat flow, and when delta stays at most zero until the collision the gap cannot close before Biane's time, one over the initial minimum of Laguerre's quantity, even when nonreal zeros are present.
results.statement: Let $f_s$, $s\ge0$, be real entire functions of genus at most one, smooth in $(z,s)$, with $\partial_sf_s=\partial_z^2f_s$, for example $f_s=e^{sD^2}p$ with $D=d/dz$ and $p$ a real polynomial, and let $\mathcal{L}(x)=-\frac{d^2}{dx^2}\log|f_s(x)|$ be Laguerre's quantity. Fix a gap between two adjacent simple real zeros of $f_s$, let $m(s)$ be the minimum of $\mathcal{L}$ over the gap, $D^+m$ its upper right Dini derivative, and at a time $s$ let $u$ be a point of the gap where the minimum is attained, with $m=m(s)=\mathcal{L}(u)>0$. For the conjugate pairs $a\pm ib$, $b>0$, of nonreal zeros of $f_s$, each pair counted once, put $B_p=\sum b^2|u-a|^{-p}$, assume that $B_4$, $B_5$ and $B_6$ are finite, and put $\eta=\big(36\,mB_4+108\,B_4^2+72\,(m+6B_4)^{1/2}B_5+120\,B_6\big)/m^2$. Put $\delta=\mathcal{L}''(u)/m^2-3$, computed from $f_s$ and its first four derivatives at $u$. Then $D^+m(s)\le(1+\delta)m^2$ and $\delta\le\eta$, and $\delta\le0$ when all zeros of $f_s$ are real. Hence, if the two zeros bounding the gap meet at a time $s_c$, and $m>0$ and $\delta\le\bar\delta$ on $[0,s_c)$ for a constant $\bar\delta>-1$, then $s_c\ge1/\big((1+\bar\delta)\,m(0)\big)$; if $\delta\le0$ throughout, the collision cannot come before Biane's time $1/m(0)$, exactly as for functions with only real zeros.
results.label: cor:wigbiane:delta

results.name: Upper bound (deadline) for the closing time of a gap between real zeros
results.summary: If the share Q of the other zeros and the sum W over the nonreal zeros stay below constants rho and W bar for which 3 rho plus the square root of 9 rho squared plus 6 W bar is less than the initial minimum of Laguerre's quantity over a gap between two real zeros, the gap closes, by a collision of one of its bounding zeros with another zero, no later than an explicit logarithmic time.
results.statement: Let $f_s$, $s\ge0$, be real entire functions of genus at most one, smooth in $(z,s)$, with $\partial_sf_s=\partial_z^2f_s$, for example $f_s=e^{sD^2}p$ with $D=d/dz$ and $p$ a real polynomial, and let $\mathcal{L}(x)=-\frac{d^2}{dx^2}\log|f_s(x)|=\sum_j(x-z_j)^{-2}$ be Laguerre's quantity (a real sum, because nonreal zeros come in conjugate pairs). Fix a gap between two adjacent simple real zeros $z_k<z_{k+1}$ of $f_s$, let $m(s)$ be the minimum of $\mathcal{L}$ over the gap, and let $u$ be a point where it is attained, so $m=\mathcal{L}(u)$. Write $m=P+Q$, where $P=(u-z_k)^{-2}+(u-z_{k+1})^{-2}$ is the share of the two zeros bounding the gap and $Q=\sum(u-z)^{-2}$ over all the other zeros $z$ of $f_s$, and let $W=\sum|u-z|^{-4}$ over the nonreal zeros $z$ of $f_s$. While the two zeros bounding the gap are real, the right derivative $m'(s^+)$ exists and is the least value of $\mathcal{L}''(u)-2m^2$ over the minimisers $u$, and at every minimiser $\mathcal{L}''(u)-2m^2\ge m^2-6mQ+3Q^2-6W$. Suppose that, for constants $\rho$ and $\bar W$ with $9\rho^2+6\bar W>0$, $Q\le\rho$ and $W\le\bar W$ at every minimiser for as long as the two zeros bounding the gap are real, and that $m(0)>r_1$, where $r_{1,2}=3\rho\pm(9\rho^2+6\bar W)^{1/2}$. Then the gap closes, one of the two zeros bounding it meeting another zero, at a time $s_c\le s^*=\frac{1}{r_1-r_2}\log\frac{m(0)-r_2}{m(0)-r_1}$. If all zeros are real, then $W=0$, so $\bar W=0$ may be taken, and for $\rho>0$ one has $s^*=(6\rho)^{-1}\log\big(m(0)/(m(0)-6\rho)\big)=1/m(0)+3\rho/m(0)^2+12\rho^2/m(0)^3+\cdots$.
results.label: thm:wigbiane:upper

results.name: Deadline for the closing of a gap in terms of the quantity kappa
results.summary: The deadline for the closing of a gap holds with six times the bound on W replaced by the largest negative part of a quantity kappa, computed from the function at the minimiser and the two zeros bounding the gap, and this form is never weaker.
results.statement: Let $f_s$, $s\ge0$, be real entire functions of genus at most one, smooth in $(z,s)$, with $\partial_sf_s=\partial_z^2f_s$, and let $\mathcal{L}(x)=-\frac{d^2}{dx^2}\log|f_s(x)|=\sum_j(x-z_j)^{-2}$ be Laguerre's quantity. Fix a gap between two adjacent simple real zeros $z_k<z_{k+1}$ of $f_s$, let $m(s)$ be the minimum of $\mathcal{L}$ over the gap, let $u$ be a point where it is attained, and put $x_j=1/(u-z_j)$ for the zeros $z_j$ of $f_s$, $P=x_k^2+x_{k+1}^2$, $Q=\sum_{j\ne k,k+1}x_j^2$, so that $m=P+Q$, and $W=\sum|x_j|^4$ over the nonreal zeros. Put $\kappa=\mathcal{L}''(u)-3P^2$, computed from $f_s$ at $u$ and the two zeros bounding the gap. Then $\kappa=3\big(x_k^2-x_{k+1}^2\big)^2+6\sum_{j\ne k,k+1}x_j^4\ge-6W$, with $\kappa\ge0$ when all zeros are real. Put $\bar\kappa=\max\big(0,\sup(-\kappa)\big)$, the supremum over the minimisers at the times before the collision. If $Q\le\rho$ at every minimiser for as long as the two zeros bounding the gap are real, with $9\rho^2+\bar\kappa>0$, and $m(0)>r_1$, where $r_{1,2}=3\rho\pm(9\rho^2+\bar\kappa)^{1/2}$, then the gap closes, one of the two zeros bounding it meeting another zero, at a time $s_c\le\frac{1}{r_1-r_2}\log\frac{m(0)-r_2}{m(0)-r_1}$. This bound is never weaker than the same bound with $6\bar W$ in place of $\bar\kappa$, where $\bar W$ is a constant with $W\le\bar W$ at every minimiser for as long as the two zeros bounding the gap are real, since then $\bar\kappa\le6\bar W$.
results.label: cor:wigbiane:kappa

results.name: Control of the nonreal zeros of the de Bruijn Newman function at negative times
results.summary: No bound is known, computed from the de Bruijn Newman function at time zero, for how far its nonreal zeros travel at negative times or how close to a gap between real zeros they come, and such control would make the lower and upper bounds for the closing time of a gap unconditional statements about that function.
results.statement: For real $t$ let $H_t(z)=\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi(u)\cos(zu)\,du$ be the de Bruijn Newman function, with $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}\big(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u}\big)\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})$, so that $H_0(z)=\tfrac18\Xi(z/2)$ with $\Xi(\theta)=\xi(\tfrac12+i\theta)$ for Riemann's completed zeta function $\xi$. As $t$ decreases from $0$ the zeros of $H_t$ move by the backward heat flow, and the book bounds from below and from above, in terms of $H_0$ alone, the time at which a gap between two adjacent real zeros closes, under hypotheses along the flow that the computation checks on a grid of times but cannot yet guarantee in advance. Problem: find a bound for how far the nonreal zeros of $H_t$, $t<0$, travel, and for how close to a gap between real zeros they come. No such bound is known, and such control would make the lower and upper bounds for the closing time of a gap unconditional statements about $H_t$, computed from $H_0$ alone.
results.label: prob:wigbiane:control

results.name: Shielding deficit identity for a pair of adjacent real zeros of the de Bruijn Newman function (Newton 2026, Zenodo)
results.summary: A telescoping identity (Newton 2026, Zenodo) expresses the shielding deficit of a pair of adjacent real zeros as a sum over the exterior gaps of the relative deviations of those gaps from the pair's gap, when all zeros are real and the exterior zeros tend to infinity.
results.statement: Let $a<b$ be adjacent simple real zeros of an entire function with zeros $\rho$ (here the de Bruijn Newman function $H_t$), with gap $g=b-a$, and put $S_{a,b}=\sum_{\rho\ne a,b}\frac{1}{(a-\rho)(b-\rho)}$ and $\mathrm{Def}=2-g^2S_{a,b}$. On each side of the pair number the exterior gaps outward, write them $g(1+\varepsilon_m)$ with $\varepsilon_m>-1$, and put $D_0=0$, $D_m=\sum_{j\le m}\varepsilon_j$, so that the $m$th exterior zero on that side is at distance $g(m+D_m)$ from the nearer end of the pair. Then on one side, for every $N\ge1$, $1-\sum_{m=1}^N\frac{1}{(m+D_m)(m+1+D_m)}=\sum_{m=1}^N\frac{\varepsilon_m}{(m+D_{m-1})(m+D_m)}+\frac{1}{N+1+D_N}$. If all zeros are real and the exterior zeros tend to infinity on both sides, then $\mathrm{Def}=\sum_{\text{sides}}\sum_{m\ge1}\frac{\varepsilon_m}{(m+D_{m-1})(m+D_m)}$. The result is due to Newton (2026, Zenodo).
results.label: nw:thm:shield

results.name: Consequences of the shielding deficit identity: lattice, truncated lattice, single enlarged gap, one sided bound and monotonicity of the smallest gap (Newton 2026, Zenodo)
results.summary: Five consequences of the shielding deficit identity: the lattice has zero deficit, a truncated lattice with $R$ exterior zeros per side has deficit $2/(R+1)$, a single enlarged gap contributes $\delta/(j(j+\delta))$, the positive part of the deficit is at most $g^{-1}\sum_j j^{-2}$ times the excess of the exterior gaps over $g$, and a smallest gap of a configuration does not shrink forward in time.
results.statement: In the setting of the shielding deficit identity (adjacent simple real zeros $a<b$ with gap $g$, $\mathrm{Def}=2-g^2S_{a,b}$, exterior gaps $g(1+\varepsilon_m)$ on each side, $\varepsilon_m>-1$, and the flow $\frac{d(g^2)}{dt}=4\,\mathrm{Def}$ for the de Bruijn Newman function): (a) if all $\varepsilon_m=0$ then $\mathrm{Def}=0$ and $g$ is constant, as for the lattice of zeros of $e^{\kappa^2t}\sin\kappa z$; (b) keeping $R$ exterior zeros on each side of a regular lattice of gap $g$ leaves $\mathrm{Def}=2/(R+1)$; (c) a single enlarged exterior gap $g(1+\delta)$ at position $j$ contributes exactly $\delta/(j(j+\delta))$; (d) with $d_{\nu,j}$ the exterior gaps on the sides $\nu=L,R$ and $[x]_+=\max(x,0)$, $[\mathrm{Def}]_+\le g^{-1}\sum_{j\ge1}j^{-2}\big[(d_{L,j}-g)_++(d_{R,j}-g)_+\big]$, and by (c) the constant $j^{-2}$ is optimal to first order; (e) if the configuration has a smallest gap $g>0$ (a finite configuration or a lattice) and $g$ is that gap, then every $\varepsilon_m\ge0$, so $\mathrm{Def}\ge0$ and the smallest gap does not shrink forward in time, with equality only for the lattice. The book notes that (e) does not apply to $H_t$, which has no smallest gap. The result is due to Newton (2026, Zenodo).
results.label: nw:cor:shield

results.name: The de Bruijn Newman function as a Gaussian average and the reciprocal transform of the tilted clock as a Gaussian smoothing of xi
results.summary: For $t>0$ the de Bruijn Newman function $H_t$ is the Gaussian average $\mathbb{E}H_0(z+i\sqrt{2t}Z)$ of $H_0$, and $1/R_t(\sigma^2)$, the reciprocal of the Laplace transform of the tilted clock when $t$ is at least the de Bruijn Newman constant, is the Gaussian smoothing of $\xi(\frac12+\sigma)$ with variance $t/2$, normalised at $\sigma=0$.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be Riemann's completed zeta function, $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}\bigl(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u}\bigr)\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})$, $H_t(z)=\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi(u)\cos(zu)\,du$ for real $t$ (so that $H_0(z)=\frac18\xi(\frac12+\frac{iz}2)$) and $R_t(s)=H_t(0)/H_t(2i\sqrt s)$ for $s\ge0$. The function $R_0(s)=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)$ is the Laplace transform of the clock $T$, which exists with no hypothesis on the zeros, and for $t$ at least the de Bruijn Newman constant $\Lambda$, $R_t$ is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution $T_t$, the tilted clock. Let $Z$ be a standard normal variable. Then for every $t>0$, $H_t(z)=\mathbb{E}\,H_0\bigl(z+i\sqrt{2t}\,Z\bigr)$ for all $z\in\mathbb{C}$, and $\dfrac1{R_t(\sigma^2)}=\dfrac{\mathbb{E}\,\xi\bigl(\frac12+\sigma+\sqrt{t/2}\,Z\bigr)}{\mathbb{E}\,\xi\bigl(\frac12+\sqrt{t/2}\,Z\bigr)}$ for $\sigma\ge0$. So for $t>0$ the tilt is Gaussian convolution, along the real axis of $\sigma$, of the even function $\sigma\mapsto\xi(\frac12+\sigma)$, with variance $t/2$, normalised at $\sigma=0$.
results.label: xg:prop:gauss

results.name: The mean of the tilted clock increases with the tilt
results.summary: The mean of the tilted clock increases strictly with the tilt parameter at every tilt at which the clock exists, by the Cauchy Schwarz inequality for the moments of the reweighted kernel (credited to a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book).
results.statement: Let $\Phi(v)=2\sum_{n\ge1}\bigl(2\pi^2n^4e^{9v/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5v/2}\bigr)\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2v})$ be the Pólya kernel, $\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)=\frac12\Phi(2u)$, and $H_t(z)=\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cos(zu)\,du$ the de Bruijn Newman function, so that $8H_t(2\theta)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(v)e^{tv^2/4}\cos(\theta v)\,dv$. Let $M_k(t)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}v^{2k}e^{tv^2/4}\Phi(v)\,dv$, and for those $t$ at which $R_t(u)=H_t(0)/H_t(2i\sqrt u)$ is the Laplace transform of a law $T_t$ (the tilted clock, which exists at $t=0$ and for every $t\ge\Lambda$, so for every $t\ge0.2$, with $\Lambda$ the de Bruijn Newman constant), with mean $\mathbb{E}T_t=M_1(t)/(2M_0(t))$. Since $M_k'(t)=\frac14M_{k+1}(t)$, $\frac{d}{dt}\mathbb{E}T_t=\frac{M_0(t)M_2(t)-M_1(t)^2}{8M_0(t)^2}>0$ by the Cauchy Schwarz inequality, at every $t$ at which $T_t$ exists.
results.label: res:ch21:meanup

results.name: Large tilt of the clock: the limit is twice the Brownian exit time
results.summary: As the tilt $t\to\infty$, the tilted clock divided by the square of the mode $u_t$ of the tilted kernel converges in law to twice the exit time of Brownian motion from $(-1,1)$, its Laplace transform tends to $1/\cosh(2\sqrt s)$, and $u_t$ times the $j$th positive zero of $H_t$ tends to $\pi(j-\frac12)$.
results.statement: Let $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}\bigl(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u}\bigr)\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})$, $H_t(z)=\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi(u)\cos(zu)\,du$ (so that $H_0(z)=\frac18\xi(\frac12+\frac{iz}2)$ for Riemann's completed zeta function $\xi$) and $R_t(s)=H_t(0)/H_t(2i\sqrt s)$. Let $\Lambda$ be the de Bruijn Newman constant, so that $H_t$ has only real zeros exactly when $t\ge\Lambda$. For $t\ge\Lambda$, in particular for $t\ge0.2$ (the bound $\Lambda\le0.2$ of Platt and Trudgian 2021), let $0<z_1(t)\le z_2(t)\le\cdots$ be the positive zeros of $H_t$; then $R_t$ is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution $T_t$, the tilted clock, with Thorin atoms $z_j(t)^2/4$. For large $t$ let $u_t$ be the mode of $u\mapsto e^{tu^2}\Phi(u)$ on $(0,\infty)$, so that $e^{4u_t}\sim tu_t/(2\pi)$ as $t\to\infty$. Let $C$ be the exit time of standard Brownian motion from $(-1,1)$, with $\mathbb{E}e^{-\theta C}=1/\cosh\sqrt{2\theta}$. Then as $t\to\infty$, $R_t(s/u_t^2)\to1/\cosh(2\sqrt s)$ for every $s\ge0$, $T_t/u_t^2$ converges in law to $2C$ (whose Laplace transform is $1/\cosh(2\sqrt s)$), and $u_tz_j(t)\to\pi(j-\frac12)$ for every $j\ge1$.
results.label: xg:prop:large

results.name: The tilted clock is not monotone under the common exponential coupling
results.summary: Coupling the tilted clock at different tilts through the same independent exponential variables does not make it almost surely monotone in the tilt on any right neighbourhood of $t=0.2$, because the atoms of the zeros numbered 64 and 92 rise there, a computation in double precision that is not certified, and at $t=0$ the same holds conditionally on RH (credited to a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book).
results.statement: For $t\ge0.2$ every zero of the de Bruijn Newman function $H_t(z)=\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi(u)\cos(zu)\,du$ with $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}\bigl(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u}\bigr)\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})$ is real (Platt and Trudgian 2021), so the tilted clock is $T_t=\sum_jE_j/a_j(t)$ with $a_j(t)$ the squares of the half zeros $z_j(t)/2$ (the Thorin atoms) and $E_j$ independent standard exponential variables, the same for every $t$ (the common coupling). By the equation of motion of the zeros, computed with Gauss Hermite quadrature in double precision (not certified; the two velocities are unchanged to $3\times10^{-17}$ between $60$ and $90$ nodes), $\dot z_{64}(0.2)=+0.26897$ and $\dot z_{92}(0.2)=+0.13385$, the only two rising zeros among the first $100$, so $a_{64}$ and $a_{92}$ increase. Hence for $h>0$ small enough, $T_{0.2+h}<T_{0.2}$ with positive probability, since $T_{0.2+h}-T_{0.2}=cE_{64}+Y$ with $c<0$ and $Y$ independent of $E_{64}$ and the exponential variable $E_{64}$ is unbounded; so the coupling is not almost surely monotone on any right neighbourhood of $t=0.2$. At $t=0$ the same argument with $\dot z_{35}(0)>0$ of the velocity formula (certified in ball arithmetic) gives the statement on every right neighbourhood of $0$, conditional on RH, which the coupling at $t=0$ needs. It does not decide whether the tilted clock is stochastically increasing in $t$.
results.label: res:ch21:coupling

results.name: Problem: is the tilted clock stochastically increasing in the tilt
results.summary: The book asks whether the tilted clock is stochastically increasing in the tilt $t$ for $t$ at least the de Bruijn Newman constant, which unconditionally means for $t\ge0.2$, the increasing mean being necessary but not sufficient.
results.statement: Let $H_t(z)=\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi(u)\cos(zu)\,du$ be the de Bruijn Newman function, with $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}\bigl(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u}\bigr)\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})$, $\Lambda$ the de Bruijn Newman constant, and for $t\ge\Lambda$ (so unconditionally for $t\ge0.2$) let $T_t$ be the tilted clock, the nonnegative variable with Laplace transform $R_t(u)=H_t(0)/H_t(2i\sqrt u)$. Problem: is $T_t$ stochastically increasing in $t$ on $t\ge\Lambda$, that is, is $P(T_t\le x)$, whose Laplace transform in $x$ is $R_t(u)/u$, nonincreasing in $t$ for every $x>0$? The failure of the common exponential coupling does not decide it, since another coupling may be monotone, and an increasing mean is necessary but not sufficient.
results.label: prob:ch21:order

results.name: Gaussian smoothing of a reciprocal GGC transform is again one
results.summary: Gaussian smoothing in the variable $\sqrt s$ of the reciprocal of the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution (GGC) with discrete Thorin measure and no drift is again the reciprocal of such a transform, the Thorin atoms obey, while they are simple, the motion equation of the de Bruijn Newman flow, and the mean of the GGC satisfies $\frac{d}{d\lambda}\mathbb{E}S_\lambda=(\mathbb{E}S_\lambda)^2-\frac32\operatorname{Var}S_\lambda$.
results.statement: A generalized gamma convolution (GGC) with Thorin measure $U\ge0$ and no drift is a law on $[0,\infty)$ with Laplace transform $\exp\bigl(-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+s/z)\,U(dz)\bigr)$. Let $a_j>0$ with $\sum_ja_j^{-1}<\infty$, and let $M(\sigma)=\prod_j(1+\sigma^2/a_j)$, an even entire function of genus zero in $\sigma^2$, so that $1/M(\sqrt s)$ is the Laplace transform of the GGC with the discrete Thorin measure $\sum_j\delta_{a_j}$. Let $Z$ be a standard normal variable and, for $c>0$, $M_c(\sigma)=\mathbb{E}\,M(\sigma+cZ)\big/\mathbb{E}\,M(cZ)$. Then $M_c(\sigma)=\prod_j(1+\sigma^2/a_j(c))$ with real $a_j(c)>0$, so that $1/M_c(\sqrt s)$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC $S_\lambda$ with the Thorin measure $\sum_j\delta_{a_j(c)}$, where $\lambda=2c^2$. While the atoms are simple they obey, as functions of $\lambda$, the motion equation $\dfrac{da_j}{d\lambda}=\dfrac12+2\sum_{k\ne j}\dfrac{a_j}{a_j-a_k}$, and $\dfrac{d}{d\lambda}\mathbb{E}S_\lambda=(\mathbb{E}S_\lambda)^2-\dfrac32\operatorname{Var}S_\lambda$.
results.label: xg:thm:smooth

results.name: Concentration of the Laguerre expressions at the origin along the whole de Bruijn Newman flow, with positivity of $L_{n,t}$ on every window for large $n$ (Newton 2026, Zenodo)
results.summary: For the probability measures $\mathbb{E}_{n,t}$ defining the Laguerre expressions $L_{n,t}$ of the de Bruijn Newman function, the second moment of the centred variable tends to zero uniformly in $0\le t\le\frac12$, so for every $X$ the expression $L_{n,t}(x)$ is positive on $|x|\le X$ for all large $n$, uniformly in $t$ (Newton 2026, Zenodo); the index is not effective.
results.label: nw:thm:conc

results.name: Compact uniform asymptotic of the Laguerre ratio $k_nL_{n+1,t}(x)/L_{n,t}(x)$ along the whole de Bruijn Newman flow (Newton 2026, Zenodo)
results.summary: For every $X$, uniformly in $0\le t\le\frac12$ and $|x|\le X$, the ratio $k_nL_{n+1,t}(x)/L_{n,t}(x)$ equals $c_n(t)(1+o(1))=\frac18(\log n)^2(1+o(1))$ (Newton 2026, Zenodo), the second equality using the Lambert centring proposition, whose proof in the book is a sketch.
results.statement: Let $L_{n,t}$ be the Laguerre expressions of the de Bruijn Newman function $H_t$, $k_n$ their normalising constants and $c_n(t)=k_nL_{n+1,t}(0)/L_{n,t}(0)$ (as in the book). For every $X<\infty$, uniformly in $0\le t\le\frac12$ and $|x|\le X$, $\frac{k_nL_{n+1,t}(x)}{L_{n,t}(x)}=c_n(t)(1+o(1))=\frac18(\log n)^2(1+o(1))$ as $n\to\infty$. The first equality follows from the concentration theorem for $\mathbb{E}_{n,t}[w^2]$ and the second from the Lambert centring $c_n(t)=\frac18\mathcal{W}(n/\pi)^2+o(\log n)$, which the book proves only by a sketch. The result is due to Newton (2026, Zenodo).
results.label: nw:thm:compact

results.name: If the de Bruijn Newman constant is positive, the zeros at that time include a multiple real zero
results.summary: If the de Bruijn Newman constant Lambda is positive then the function H at time Lambda has a multiple real zero, so RH holds if and only if H_t has only simple zeros for every t in (0,0.2]; the proof uses Polymath Theorem 1.5 and the bound 0.2 of Platt and Trudgian, and is from a note of Nicholas Polson.
results.statement: Let $\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}\big(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u}\big)\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})$ and $H_t(z)=\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cos(zu)\,du$, entire in $z$ and $t$, so that $H_0(z)=\frac18\Xi(z/2)$ with $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$ and $\xi$ Riemann's xi function. Let $\Lambda$ be the de Bruijn Newman constant, so that $H_t$ has only real zeros exactly for $t\ge\Lambda$ (Newman; $\Lambda\le\frac12$ by de Bruijn). If $\Lambda>0$, then $H_\Lambda$ has a multiple real zero. Hence the Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if $H_t$ has only simple zeros for every $t\in(0,0.2]$. The proof uses Theorem 1.5 of the Polymath project (for an absolute constant $C$ and every $0<t\le\frac12$ every zero $x+iy$ of $H_t$ with $|x|\ge e^{C/t}$ is real and simple) and the bound $\Lambda\le0.2$ of Platt and Trudgian when the Riemann Hypothesis fails.
results.label: ft:cor:collide

results.name: Local Rouché criterion for backward persistence of an adjacent pair of real simple zeros of the de Bruijn Newman function (Newton 2026, Zenodo)
results.summary: If an explicit integral $\psi_Y(\sigma)$ is smaller than the minimum of $|H_{t_*}|$ on a contour around an adjacent pair of real simple zeros, then the pair stays real and simple for the backward time $\sigma$ and the gap shrinks by at most $2r$ (Newton 2026, Zenodo).
results.statement: Let $H_t(z)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\nu_t(u)e^{izu}\,du$ be the de Bruijn Newman function with $\nu_t(u)=\frac12\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)e^{tu^2}$ and $\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}$ the even de Bruijn Newman kernel, let $t_*\ge0$, and let $a<b$ be adjacent real simple zeros of $H_{t_*}$ with $g_*=b-a$. Let $0<r<g_*/2$ and let $\Omega$ be a conjugation invariant Jordan domain containing the closed discs $D_a$, $D_b$ of radius $r$ about $a$, $b$ and the segment between them, with no other zero of $H_{t_*}$ in $\overline\Omega$. Put $\Gamma=\partial D_a\cup\partial D_b\cup\partial\Omega$, $Y=\max_\Gamma|\operatorname{Im}z|$, $m=\min_\Gamma|H_{t_*}|$ and $\psi_Y(\sigma)=\int_0^\infty\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)e^{t_*u^2+Yu}(1-e^{-\sigma u^2})\,du$. If $\psi_Y(\sigma)<m$, then for $0\le\tau\le\sigma$ the function $H_{t_*-\tau}$ has exactly one zero in each of $D_a$, $D_b$, both real and simple, and no other zero in $\Omega$; so the gap $g$ of the pair satisfies $g\ge g_*-2r$ and, with $\mathrm{Def}$ the shielding deficit and $\frac{d(g^2)}{dt}=4\,\mathrm{Def}$, $4\int\mathrm{Def}\,dt\le g_*^2-(g_*-2r)^2$ over the interval. The result is due to Newton (2026, Zenodo).
results.label: nw:prop:local

results.name: Obstruction at height: the absolute value Rouché criterion certifies only backward steps of size $O(e^{-\delta a})$ at a real zero $a$ of the de Bruijn Newman function (Newton 2026, Zenodo, mechanism corrected)
results.summary: No criterion of the form $\psi_Y(\sigma)<m$ certifies a fixed backward step $\sigma>0$ at every height, since $\min_\Gamma|H_{t_*}|$ decays like $e^{-\delta a}$ while $\psi_Y(\sigma)\ge\psi_0(\sigma)>0$ does not decay; the step such a criterion can certify at height $a$ is $O(e^{-\delta a})$ (Newton 2026, Zenodo, with the mechanism corrected in the book).
results.statement: With the notation of the local Rouché criterion ($H_t$ the de Bruijn Newman function, $\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}$ its even kernel, $\psi_Y(\sigma)=\int_0^\infty\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)e^{t_*u^2+Yu}(1-e^{-\sigma u^2})\,du$, $m=\min_\Gamma|H_{t_*}|$ on a contour $\Gamma$), fix $t_*\ge0$, $\sigma>0$ and $0<\delta<\pi/8$, and let $C(\delta,t)=\frac12\int_{\mathbb{R}}|\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u+i\delta)|e^{t(u^2-\delta^2)+|u|}\,du<\infty$. For every real zero $a\ge1$ of $H_{t_*}$ and every contour $\Gamma$ containing a point $a+i\eta$ with $0<\eta\le1$, $\min_\Gamma|H_{t_*}|\le C(\delta,t_*)e^{-\delta a}<\psi_0(\sigma)\le\psi_Y(\sigma)$ as soon as $a>\delta^{-1}\log\big(C(\delta,t_*)/\psi_0(\sigma)\big)$. So no criterion of the form $\psi_Y(\sigma)<m$ certifies a fixed step $\sigma>0$ at every height, and the step it can certify at height $a$ is $O(e^{-\delta a})$. The book notes that this concerns bounds through the absolute value of the integrand only. The result is due to Newton (2026, Zenodo), with the mechanism corrected in the book.
results.label: nw:prop:height

results.name: Threshold theorem along the flow for the shifted clocks of the heat flow function
results.summary: For every time $t\ge0$ and basepoint $\alpha\ge\frac12$, the shifted clock of the heat flow function $\xi_t$ is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution exactly when no zero of $\xi_t$ has real part above $\alpha$, and its Thorin measure is then an explicit sum of Cauchy kernels and atoms over the zeros.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be Riemann's xi function, $\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})$, $H_t(z)=\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cos(zu)\,du$ (so $H_0(z)=\frac18\xi(\frac12+\frac{iz}2)$) and $\xi_t(s)=8H_t(-2i(s-\frac12))=8\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cosh((2s-1)u)\,du$, so that $\xi_0=\xi$. For $t\ge0$ and $\alpha\ge\frac12$ let $\varphi_{t,\alpha}(u)=\xi_t(\alpha)/\xi_t(\alpha+\sqrt u)$ for $u\ge0$, the shifted time $t$ clock (for $\alpha=\frac12$ it is $R_t(u)=H_t(0)/H_t(2i\sqrt u)$, the transform of the centre clock of the flow). A generalized gamma convolution (GGC) is a random variable $Y\ge0$ with $\mathbb{E}e^{-uY}=\exp\{-au-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+u/z)\,U(dz)\}$ for $u>0$, a drift $a\ge0$ and a Thorin measure $U$. Then $\varphi_{t,\alpha}$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC if and only if $\alpha\ge\sup_\rho\operatorname{Re}\rho$ over the zeros $\rho$ of $\xi_t$. In that case there is no drift, and the Thorin measure, written in the variable $\theta=\sqrt z$ on $\theta>0$, is $\sum_{\rho=\beta+i\gamma,\ \gamma>0,\ \beta<\alpha}\bigl[P_{\alpha-\beta}(\theta-\gamma)+P_{\alpha-\beta}(\theta+\gamma)\bigr]\,d\theta+\sum_{\rho=\alpha+i\gamma,\ \gamma>0}m_\rho\,\delta_\gamma$, where the sums run over the zeros $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ of $\xi_t$ with $\gamma>0$ (in the first sum each zero is repeated according to its multiplicity $m_\rho$), $P_a(x)=a/(\pi(a^2+x^2))$ is the Cauchy density of scale $a>0$ and $\delta_\gamma$ is the point mass at $\gamma$. For $t=0$ this is the threshold theorem for the shifted clock of $\xi$.
results.label: cp:thm:transfer

results.name: Minimum at the origin of the Thorin density of the shifted clocks along the heat flow
results.summary: For $t\ge\Lambda$ and basepoint $\alpha>\frac12$ the real part of $\xi_t'/\xi_t$ on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha$ is at most $(\alpha-\frac12)V_t$ at the real point, and, under explicit bounds on $\alpha-\frac12$, is at least its value there on explicit ranges (below the first zero ordinate, near zeros, in windows with many zeros, and for all smaller basepoints once at one basepoint $\alpha'$ it is at least $(\alpha'-\frac12)V_t$ at every height above the first zero ordinate), which gives the GGC property of the shifted clock with the constant part of its Thorin density removed; the parts other than (iv) follow a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function, $\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})$ and $\xi_t(s)=8\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cosh((2s-1)u)\,du$ the heat flow deformation of $\xi$ (so $\xi_0=\xi$). Let $\Lambda\le0.2$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021) be the de Bruijn Newman constant, and let $t\ge\Lambda$, so that the zeros of $\xi_t$ are $\frac12\pm i\theta_k$ with $0<\theta_1\le\theta_2\le\cdots$ (all $\theta_k=\theta_k(t)$ real, counted with multiplicity). Put $T_t$ for the positive random variable with $\mathbb{E}e^{-uT_t}=\prod_k(1+u/\theta_k^2)^{-1}=\xi_t(\frac12)/\xi_t(\frac12+\sqrt u)$, so that $\mathbb{E}T_t=\sum_k\theta_k^{-2}$ and $\operatorname{Var}T_t=\sum_k\theta_k^{-4}$, and $V_t=(\log\xi_t)''(\frac12)=2\sum_k\theta_k^{-2}=2\mathbb{E}T_t$. For $\alpha>\frac12$ let $a=\alpha-\frac12$, $v_t(\alpha,\theta)=\operatorname{Re}(\xi_t'/\xi_t)(\alpha+i\theta)$, $b_t(\alpha)=v_t(\alpha,0)$, $v(\theta)=v_t(\alpha,\theta)$ and $b=b_t(\alpha)$. The shifted clock is $\varphi_{t,\alpha}(u)=\xi_t(\alpha)/\xi_t(\alpha+\sqrt u)$, and $\tilde\varphi_{t,\alpha}(u)=\varphi_{t,\alpha}(u)e^{b\sqrt u}$ is the shifted clock with the constant part of its Thorin density (which is $v(\theta)/\pi$ in the variable $\theta=\sqrt z$) removed; $\tilde\varphi_{t,\alpha}$ is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution (GGC) exactly when $v(\theta)\ge b$ for every $\theta$. Then (i) $b\le aV_t$. (ii) If $a^2\le\frac35\theta_1^2$, then $v(\theta)\ge b$ for $|\theta|\le\theta_1$; if $a\le\frac12$ and $V_t<4$, then $v(\theta)>b$ at every $\theta$ within $D_t=(1/V_t-\frac14)^{1/2}$ of some $\theta_k$. (iii) Let $a\le\frac12$ and $V_t<4$. If, for some $T_*\ge\theta_1$, every $\theta\in[\theta_1,T_*]$ is within $D_t$ of some $\theta_k$, and for every $\theta>T_*$ some $w>0$ has $\#\{k:|\theta_k-\theta|\le w\}>V_t(w^2+\frac14)$, then $v\ge b$ (and then $\tilde\varphi_{t,\alpha}$ is a GGC transform for every $\alpha\in[\frac12,1]$). (iv) Let $\alpha'>\frac12$ and $a'=\alpha'-\frac12$ with $a'^2\le\frac35\theta_1^2$. If $v_t(\alpha',\theta)\ge a'V_t$ for every $\theta\ge\theta_1$, then $v_t(\alpha,\cdot)\ge b_t(\alpha)$ for every $\alpha\in(\frac12,\alpha']$ (and then $\tilde\varphi_{t,\alpha}$ is a GGC transform for every $\alpha\in[\frac12,\alpha']$). (v) As $\theta\to0$, $(v(\theta)-b)/\theta^2\to\sum_k2a(3\theta_k^2-a^2)/(a^2+\theta_k^2)^3=6a\operatorname{Var}T_t+O(a^3)$. For $\alpha=\frac12$, $b_t(\frac12)=0$ and $\tilde\varphi_{t,1/2}=\varphi_{t,1/2}$.
results.label: cp:prop:minflow

results.name: Heat flow function as a shifted Gaussian average of Riemann's xi function
results.summary: In the upper half plane the heat flow function $\xi_t$ equals the Gamma factor times $e^{t\ell^2/4}$ times a Gaussian average $\zeta_t$ of $\xi(s+h)$ divided by $g(s)e^{h\ell(s)}$ over a complex shifted mean, with an explicit bound on the deviation of that quotient from $\zeta(s+h)$.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=g(s)\zeta(s)$ be Riemann's xi function with $g(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)$, put $\ell=g'/g$, let $\xi_t(s)=8\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cosh((2s-1)u)\,du$ with $\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})$ be the heat flow function ($\xi_0=\xi$), and let $Z$ be standard normal. For $t\ge0$ and $\operatorname{Im}s>0$, $\xi_t(s)=g(s)\,e^{t\ell(s)^2/4}\,\zeta_t(s)$ with $\zeta_t(s)=\mathbb{E}\,\Psi\bigl(s,\frac t2\ell(s)+\sqrt{t/2}\,Z\bigr)$ and $\Psi(s,h)=\xi(s+h)/(g(s)e^{h\ell(s)})$. Moreover $\Psi(s,h)=\zeta(s+h)e^{r(s,h)}$ with $r(s,h)=h^2\int_0^1(1-u)\,\ell'(s+uh)\,du$, and if $Y=\min\bigl(\operatorname{Im}s,\operatorname{Im}s+\frac t2\operatorname{Im}\ell(s)\bigr)>0$, then $|r(s,h)|\le|h|^2\bigl(\frac1{4Y}+\frac7{4Y^2}\bigr)$ for every $h\in\frac t2\ell(s)+\mathbb{R}$.
results.label: cp:lem:shift

results.name: Zero count of the heat flow function and a Backlund type bound on its argument term
results.summary: For every $t\ge0$ the number of zeros of $\xi_t$ with ordinate in $(0,T]$ equals an explicit main term plus an argument term $S_t(T)$, with the main term $\frac T{2\pi}\log\frac T{2\pi e}+\frac78+\frac t{16}\log\frac T{2\pi}$ up to $O((1+t\log T)/T)$, and $S_t$ is bounded by a Jensen formula estimate under two checkable hypotheses; the proof follows a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=g(s)\zeta(s)$ be Riemann's xi function with $g(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)$, $\ell=g'/g$, and $\xi_t(s)=8\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cosh((2s-1)u)\,du$ with $\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})$ the heat flow function ($\xi_0=\xi$), and $\zeta_t=\xi_t/(g\,e^{t\ell^2/4})$. Let $t\ge0$ and let $N_t(T)$ be the number of zeros $\rho$ of $\xi_t$ with $0<\operatorname{Im}\rho\le T$, counted with multiplicity whether or not they lie on the critical line. For $T>0$ not an ordinate let $\pi S_t(T)$ be the change of a continuous argument of $\zeta_t$ along the segments from $2$ to $2+iT$ and from $2+iT$ to $\frac12+iT$, starting from $\arg\zeta_t(2)=0$ (at ordinates take right limits); $S_0=S$ is the usual argument term of the Riemann zeta function. (i) $N_t(T)=1+\vartheta(T)/\pi+\frac t{4\pi}\operatorname{Im}\bigl(\ell(\frac12+iT)^2\bigr)+S_t(T)$, where $\vartheta$ is the Riemann Siegel theta function. (ii) The main term is $\frac T{2\pi}\log\frac T{2\pi e}+\frac78+\frac t{16}\log\frac T{2\pi}+O\bigl((1+t\log T)/T\bigr)$. (iii) Let $T>\frac52$. If $\operatorname{Re}\zeta_t(2+iy)>0$ for $0\le y\le T$, and $M(\omega)\ge\max\bigl(|\zeta_t(2+iT+\frac52e^{i\omega})|,|\zeta_t(2+iT+\frac52e^{-i\omega})|\bigr)$ for $0\le\omega\le2\pi$, then $|S_t(T)|\le\frac12+\frac1{\log(5/3)}\Bigl(\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}\log M(\omega)\,d\omega-\log\operatorname{Re}\zeta_t(2+iT)\Bigr)$.
results.label: cp:prop:count

results.name: GGC property at time 0.2 of the shifted clock with the constant part of its Thorin density removed, for basepoints up to 10, conditional on a computed bound
results.status_text: conditional on The inequality $v_{0.2}(10,\theta)\ge\frac{19}2V_{0.2}$ for every $\theta\ge\theta_1(0.2)$, where $v_{0.2}(10,\theta)=\operatorname{Re}(\xi_{0.2}'/\xi_{0.2})(10+i\theta)$. The book computes it only for $\theta_1(0.2)\le\theta\le10^4$ on a grid of step $0.05$ with a Gauss Hermite quadrature whose error is not bounded, so it is not certified there and not proved for larger $\theta$ (Problem on the bound for $\zeta_{0.2}'/\zeta_{0.2}$ on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=10$). The proof also uses $\frac35\theta_1(0.2)^2\ge(\frac{19}2)^2$, which the book takes from the tabulated value $\operatorname{Var}T_{0.2}=3.77203\times10^{-5}$ (computed, not certified) through $\theta_1(0.2)\ge(\operatorname{Var}T_{0.2})^{-1/4}=12.76$
results.conditions: The inequality $v_{0.2}(10,\theta)\ge\frac{19}2V_{0.2}$ for every $\theta\ge\theta_1(0.2)$, where $v_{0.2}(10,\theta)=\operatorname{Re}(\xi_{0.2}'/\xi_{0.2})(10+i\theta)$. The book computes it only for $\theta_1(0.2)\le\theta\le10^4$ on a grid of step $0.05$ with a Gauss Hermite quadrature whose error is not bounded, so it is not certified there and not proved for larger $\theta$ (Problem on the bound for $\zeta_{0.2}'/\zeta_{0.2}$ on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=10$). The proof also uses $\frac35\theta_1(0.2)^2\ge(\frac{19}2)^2$, which the book takes from the tabulated value $\operatorname{Var}T_{0.2}=3.77203\times10^{-5}$ (computed, not certified) through $\theta_1(0.2)\ge(\operatorname{Var}T_{0.2})^{-1/4}=12.76$.
results.summary: If the real part of $\xi_{0.2}'/\xi_{0.2}$ at $10+i\theta$ is at least $\frac{19}2V_{0.2}$ for all $\theta\ge\theta_1(0.2)$ (computed, not certified, on $\theta_1(0.2)\le\theta\le10^4$), then the shifted clock of $\xi_{0.2}$ with the constant part of its Thorin density removed is a GGC transform for every basepoint in $[\frac12,10]$.
results.statement: Let $\xi_t$ be the heat flow function ($\xi_t(s)=8\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cosh((2s-1)u)\,du$ with $\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})$, $\xi_0=\xi$ Riemann's xi function). Its zeros at time $0.2$ are $\frac12\pm i\theta_k(0.2)$, $0<\theta_1(0.2)\le\theta_2(0.2)\le\cdots$ (since the de Bruijn Newman constant satisfies $\Lambda\le0.2$, Platt and Trudgian 2021), and $V_{0.2}=(\log\xi_{0.2})''(\frac12)=2\sum_k\theta_k(0.2)^{-2}$. For $\alpha\ge\frac12$ let $v_{0.2}(\alpha,\theta)=\operatorname{Re}(\xi_{0.2}'/\xi_{0.2})(\alpha+i\theta)$, $b_{0.2}(\alpha)=v_{0.2}(\alpha,0)$ and $\tilde\varphi_{0.2,\alpha}(u)=\frac{\xi_{0.2}(\alpha)}{\xi_{0.2}(\alpha+\sqrt u)}e^{b_{0.2}(\alpha)\sqrt u}$. Suppose that $v_{0.2}(10,\theta)\ge\frac{19}2V_{0.2}$ for every $\theta\ge\theta_1(0.2)$. Then $\tilde\varphi_{0.2,\alpha}$ is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution for every $\alpha\in[\frac12,10]$. The proof needs only $\theta_1(0.2)\ge12.76$, which follows from $\operatorname{Var}T_{0.2}=\sum_k\theta_k(0.2)^{-4}\ge\theta_1(0.2)^{-4}$, $T_{0.2}$ being the positive variable with $\mathbb{E}e^{-uT_{0.2}}=\xi_{0.2}(\frac12)/\xi_{0.2}(\frac12+\sqrt u)$, and the tabulated value $\operatorname{Var}T_{0.2}=3.77203\times10^{-5}$ (computed, not certified). The hypothesis is computed, not certified, for $\theta_1(0.2)\le\theta\le10^4$: on a grid of step $0.05$, with a Gauss Hermite quadrature whose error is not bounded, the least margin is $v_{0.2}(10,\theta)-\frac{19}2V_{0.2}=0.1163$, at $\theta=14.0768$.
results.label: cp:cor:minflow

results.name: Phase diagram theorem, de Bruijn's strip theorem in Thorin form
results.summary: The set of points $(t,\alpha)$ where the shifted clock of the heat flow function is a generalized gamma convolution is carried along parabolas by the flow (de Bruijn's strip theorem in Thorin form), the de Bruijn Newman constant is the minimum of $t+2(\alpha-\frac12)^2$ over it, and RH holds exactly when the corner $(0,\frac12)$ belongs to it.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be Riemann's xi function, $\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})$, $H_t(z)=\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cos(zu)\,du$ (so $H_0(z)=\frac18\xi(\frac12+\frac{iz}2)$) and $\xi_t(s)=8H_t(-2i(s-\frac12))$, so that $\xi_0=\xi$ and a zero $x+iy$ of $H_t$ is the zero $\frac12-\frac y2+\frac{ix}2$ of $\xi_t$. For $t\ge0$ and $\alpha\ge\frac12$ let $\varphi_{t,\alpha}(u)=\xi_t(\alpha)/\xi_t(\alpha+\sqrt u)$ for $u\ge0$ (the shifted time $t$ clock), and let the GGC region $\mathcal{G}$ be the set of points $(t,\alpha)$ with $t\ge0$ and $\alpha\ge\frac12$ at which $\varphi_{t,\alpha}$ is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution; by the threshold theorem for the clocks of $\xi_t$ this holds exactly when $\xi_t$ has no zero with real part above $\alpha$, that is, when every zero $x+iy$ of $H_t$ has $|y|\le2(\alpha-\frac12)$. Let $\Lambda$ be the de Bruijn Newman constant, so that $H_t$ has only real zeros exactly when $t\ge\Lambda$. (i) If $(t_0,\alpha_0)\in\mathcal{G}$, then $(t,\alpha)\in\mathcal{G}$ for every $t\ge t_0$ and every $\alpha\ge\frac12$ with $(\alpha-\frac12)^2+\frac t2\ge(\alpha_0-\frac12)^2+\frac{t_0}2$. (ii) $\Lambda=\min\{t+2(\alpha-\frac12)^2:(t,\alpha)\in\mathcal{G}\}$. (iii) The Riemann Hypothesis (every zero of $\xi$ has real part $\frac12$) holds if and only if $(0,\frac12)\in\mathcal{G}$, and if and only if for every $\delta>0$ there is $t\in[0,\delta]$ with $(t,\frac12+\sqrt{(\delta-t)/2})\in\mathcal{G}$.
