Part (i) is de Bruijn's strip theorem (if the zeros of $H_{t_0}$ lie in $|\operatorname{Im}z|\le\Delta$, then the zeros of $H_t$ lie in $(\operatorname{Im}z)^2\le\max(\Delta^2-2(t-t_0),0)$ for $t\ge t_0$) read through the threshold theorem, and parts (ii) and (iii) also use the theorem of Rodgers and Tao that $\Lambda\ge0$.
results.label: cp:thm:phase

results.name: Winding number certificate for the point (0.2, 0.6) of the phase diagram
results.summary: Given a barrier above which zeros are excluded (Polymath15 provide one; no script of the book checks it), if a ball arithmetic evaluation of $\xi_{0.2}$ on a grid along the left, top and right edges of a rectangle (on the bottom edge, which is real, $\xi_{0.2}$ is positive) satisfies explicit inequalities with an argument sum in $(-\pi,\pi)$, then $\xi_{0.2}$ has no zero with real part above $0.6$, so the point $(0.2,0.6)$ lies in the GGC region and $\Lambda\le0.22$.
results.statement: Let $\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})$ and $\xi_t(s)=8\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cosh((2s-1)u)\,du$, the de Bruijn Newman deformation of Riemann's xi function $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ (so $\xi_0=\xi$), and $H_t(z)=\frac18\xi_t(\frac12+\frac{iz}2)=\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cos(zu)\,du$. The kernel $\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}$ continues analytically to $|\operatorname{Im}u|<\pi/8$. For $0<\eta<\pi/8$ and real $x$ put $K_\eta(0.2,x)=4\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\bigl|e^{0.2(u+i\eta)^2}\bigr|\,|\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u+i\eta)|\,e^{2xu}\,du$ and $\bar K_\eta(0.2,R)=\max_{|x|\le R}K_\eta(0.2,x)$; they give the bound $|\xi_{0.2}(\frac12+x+i\theta)|\le K_\eta(0.2,x)e^{-2\eta\theta}$ for $\theta\ge0$. Let $X>0$ be a barrier for the point $(0.2,0.6)$ in the variable of $H_{0.2}$, as Polymath15 provide one (no script of the book checks it), that is, a number such that $H_{0.2}$ has no zero $z$ with $\operatorname{Re}z\ge X$ and $\operatorname{Im}z>0.2$, so that $\xi_{0.2}$ has no zero with $\operatorname{Re}s>0.6$ and $\operatorname{Im}s\ge X/2$, and let $Q=\{s:0.6\le\operatorname{Re}s\le0.9,\ 0\le\operatorname{Im}s\le X/2\}$. Let $s_0,\dots,s_M$ be points of the left, top and right edges of $Q$, in order along the boundary of $Q$ from one bottom corner, $s_0$, to the other, $s_M$, and including the two top corners, and let $B_j$ be ball enclosures of $\xi_{0.2}(s_j)$ with radii $\varepsilon_j$. Suppose that for every $j$ there are $r>0$ and a tilt $\eta\in(0,\pi/8)$ (both may depend on $j$) such that $|s_{j+1}-s_j|\,\frac{\bar K_\eta(0.2,\,0.4+r)}{r}\,e^{-2\eta(\theta_j-r)}+\varepsilon_j+\varepsilon_{j+1}<\min|B_j|$, where $\theta_j=\min(\operatorname{Im}s_j,\operatorname{Im}s_{j+1})$, $\min|B_j|$ is the smallest modulus of a point of the ball $B_j$ and the factor $e^{-2\eta(\theta_j-r)}$ may be replaced by $1$ when $\theta_j\le r$, and that $\sum_j\operatorname{Arg}(B_{j+1}/B_j)$ (principal values), evaluated in ball arithmetic, lies within $(-\pi,\pi)$. (The bottom edge needs no points: $\xi_t(\sigma)>0$ for every real $\sigma$ and every $t\ge0$, so the argument of $\xi_{0.2}$ does not change along it.) Then $\xi_{0.2}$ has no zero in $Q$, hence no zero with real part above $0.6$: the point $(0.2,0.6)$ lies in the GGC region (the shifted clock $\xi_{0.2}(0.6)/\xi_{0.2}(0.6+\sqrt u)$ is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution), and the de Bruijn Newman constant satisfies $\Lambda\le0.22$.
results.label: cp:thm:cert

results.name: Certificate in Thorin form, positive logarithmic derivative on a rectangle excludes zeros
results.summary: If, for some $\frac12<\alpha<\sigma_1$ and $T>0$, the real part of the logarithmic derivative of $\xi_t$ is positive at every point $\sigma+i\theta$ of the rectangle $[\alpha,\sigma_1]\times[0,T]$ where $\xi_t$ does not vanish, then $\xi_t$ has no zero with real part in $(\alpha,\sigma_1]$ and ordinate in $(0,T)$.
results.statement: Let $\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})$ and $\xi_t(s)=8\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cosh((2s-1)u)\,du$, the de Bruijn Newman deformation of Riemann's xi function, and for real $\sigma,\theta$ with $\xi_t(\sigma+i\theta)\ne0$ put $v_t(\sigma,\theta)=\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\xi_t'(\sigma+i\theta)/\xi_t(\sigma+i\theta)\bigr)$ (when the shifted clock $\xi_t(\alpha)/\xi_t(\alpha+\sqrt u)$ is a generalized gamma convolution, $v_t(\alpha,\theta)/\pi$ is its Thorin density in the variable $\theta=\sqrt z$, away from atoms). Let $t\ge0$, $\frac12<\alpha<\sigma_1$ and $T>0$, and suppose $v_t(\sigma,\theta)>0$ for every $(\sigma,\theta)\in[\alpha,\sigma_1]\times[0,T]$ at which $\xi_t(\sigma+i\theta)\ne0$. Then $\xi_t$ has no zero $\beta+i\gamma$ with $\alpha<\beta\le\sigma_1$ and $0<\gamma<T$.
results.label: cp:prop:thorincert

results.name: No zero of the time 0.2 function in the rectangle up to height 160, certified
results.summary: A computation in ball arithmetic certifies that $\xi_{0.2}$ has no zero with real part between $0.6$ and $0.9$ and ordinate between $0$ and $160$, which checks the finite part of the certificate for the point $(0.2,0.6)$ of the phase diagram below height $160$ (the certificate needs it up to the barrier of Polymath15, near height $3\times10^{10}$).
results.statement: Let $\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})$ and $\xi_t(s)=8\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cosh((2s-1)u)\,du$, the de Bruijn Newman deformation of Riemann's xi function $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ (so $\xi_0=\xi$). Then $\xi_{0.2}$ has no zero $s$ with $0.6\le\operatorname{Re}s\le0.9$ and $0\le\operatorname{Im}s\le160$. This is certified by a computation in ball arithmetic (Arb, called from Python): $\xi_{0.2}$ is evaluated by the trapezoid rule for its integral with an enclosure of the error of the rule, and the boundary of the rectangle $[0.6,0.9]\times[0,160]$ is walked counterclockwise, up the right edge, along the top and down the left edge, in $23{,}219$ steps, with the step condition of the winding number certificate for the point $(0.2,0.6)$ (the step length times an explicit bound for $|\xi_{0.2}'|$ along the step, plus the radii of the enclosures at its two ends, is below the smallest modulus of the enclosure at its start) verified at every step. The bottom edge is not walked, since $\xi_{0.2}$ is real and positive on the real axis. The winding number of $\xi_{0.2}$ around the rectangle is enclosed in $[0\pm3.47\times10^{-7}]$, so it is $0$.
results.label: cp:thm:rig

results.name: Pair of zeros near height 185 still real at time minus 0.287979, certified
results.summary: A certified computation in ball arithmetic shows that the pair of zeros of the heat flow function near height $185$ is still real at time $-0.287979$, the upper end of the book's bracket for the time of their collision, and certified signs next to the double zero located by Newton's method lower that end to $-0.287979837008$.
results.statement: Let $\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})$ and, for real $t$ of either sign, $\xi_t(s)=8\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cosh((2s-1)u)\,du$, the de Bruijn Newman deformation of Riemann's xi function (so $\xi_0$ is the xi function), and $H_t(z)=\frac18\xi_t(\frac12+\frac{iz}2)$. A zero $\frac12+i\gamma$ of $\xi_t$ on the critical line is the real zero $z=2\gamma$ of $H_t$, and while the real zeros are simple they move by $dz_k/dt=2\sum_{j\ne k}(z_k-z_j)^{-1}$. Let $\gamma_{71}<\gamma_{72}$ be the ordinates of the 71st and 72nd zeros of $\xi$ in the upper half plane, the pair near height $185$. At $t=-0.287979$ the signs of $\xi_t(\frac12+i\theta)$ at the $131$ points $\theta=184.6+0.01k$, $k=0,\dots,130$, certified in ball arithmetic (Arb) at $640$ bits from the trapezoid sum for the integral with an enclosure of its discretisation error, show two sign changes; hence the real function $\theta\mapsto\xi_t(\frac12+i\theta)$ has at least two zeros in $[184.6,185.9]$, and the pair $(\gamma_{71},\gamma_{72})$ is still real at $t=-0.287979$. This is the certified upper end of the book's bracket $[-0.28803,-0.287979]$ for the time at which the pair collides when $t$ decreases from $0$; the lower end $-0.28803$ rests on the asymptotic pair law $D^2\approx8(t-t_*)$ for the distance $D$ of the pair in the variable $z$ near its collision time $t_*$, and is not certified. Newton's method on the same trapezoid sum puts the double zero of the pair at $z_*=370.78087$, $t_*=-0.287979837009$; a Krawczyk test certifies a real double zero of the trapezoid sum itself (a statement about the sum, not about $H_t$) in a box of half width $2^{-400}$ about this point, and at $t=t_*+1.2\times10^{-12}$ certified signs $+,-,+$ of $H_t$ at $z_*-4\times10^{-6}$, $z_*$ and $z_*+4\times10^{-6}$ show that the pair is still real there, so the collision lies below $-0.287979837008$. The floating point integration of the motion of the first $600$ zeros that the book reports with this result (with the monotonicity of two gap functionals at the sampled times) is computed, not certified, and is not claimed here.
results.label: cp:prop:gas

results.name: Open problem on the candidate Thorin densities at times 0 and 0.2 near the Polymath15 barrier
results.summary: Compute the functions $v_t/\pi$ of the heat flow function (the Thorin densities of its shifted clocks where these are generalized gamma convolutions) at $t=0$ and $t=0.2$ at heights near $3\times10^{10}$ and measure how their difference grows with the height.
results.statement: Let $\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})$ and $\xi_t(s)=8\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cosh((2s-1)u)\,du$, the de Bruijn Newman deformation of Riemann's xi function (so $\xi_0$ is the xi function), with $H_t(z)=\frac18\xi_t(\frac12+\frac{iz}2)$, and put $v_t(\alpha,\theta)=\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\xi_t'(\alpha+i\theta)/\xi_t(\alpha+i\theta)\bigr)$; when the shifted clock $\xi_t(\alpha)/\xi_t(\alpha+\sqrt u)$ is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution, $v_t(\alpha,\theta)/\pi$ is its Thorin density in the variable $\theta=\sqrt z$, away from atoms. Problem: compute $v_t(\alpha,\theta)$ at $t=0$ and at $t=0.2$ near the barrier of Polymath15, at heights $\theta$ near $3\times10^{10}$, with a Riemann Siegel type evaluator of $H_{0.2}$ such as the effective approximation of Polymath15, and measure how the difference between the functions $v_{0.2}/\pi$ and $v_0/\pi$ grows with the height. The book computes this difference only for $\theta\le100$, from the Pólya integral.
results.label: cp:prob:high

results.name: Open problem on the boundary of the GGC region for 0 at most t at most 0.2
results.summary: Describe the boundary $\alpha^*(t)$ of the GGC region for $0\le t\le0.2$, decide whether it is continuous, and whether $(\alpha^*(t)-\frac12)^2+\frac t2$ is strictly decreasing where $\alpha^*(t)>\frac12$.
results.statement: Let $\xi_t(s)=8\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cosh((2s-1)u)\,du$ be the de Bruijn Newman deformation of Riemann's xi function, with $\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})$. The GGC region $\mathcal{G}$ is the set of points $(t,\alpha)$, $t\ge0$, $\alpha\ge\frac12$, at which the shifted clock $\xi_t(\alpha)/\xi_t(\alpha+\sqrt u)$ is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution; this holds exactly when $\alpha\ge\alpha^*(t)$, where $\alpha^*(t)=\max(\frac12,\sup\operatorname{Re}\rho)$ over the zeros $\rho$ of $\xi_t$. Problem: describe the boundary $\alpha^*(t)$ of $\mathcal{G}$ for $0\le t\le0.2$ as far as computation and the known zero free regions allow; is $\alpha^*$ continuous, and is $(\alpha^*(t)-\frac12)^2+\frac t2$ strictly decreasing in $t$ where $\alpha^*(t)>\frac12$? (By the phase diagram theorem it is nonincreasing there.)
results.label: cp:prob:boundary

results.name: Open problem on a coordinate on the phase diagram for the symmetrised truncations
results.summary: Find explicit truncations of the heat flow function, built from finitely many terms without the zeros and converging to it on compact sets, and a point $(t,\alpha)$ outside the known part of the phase diagram such that infinitely many truncations have no zero to the right of $\alpha$ below heights that grow to infinity; Hurwitz's theorem would then add the point to the GGC region.
results.statement: Let $\xi_t(s)=8\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cosh((2s-1)u)\,du$ be the de Bruijn Newman deformation of Riemann's xi function, with $\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})$, and let the GGC region $\mathcal{G}$ be the set of points $(t,\alpha)$, $t\ge0$, $\alpha\ge\frac12$, at which $\xi_t$ has no zero with real part above $\alpha$, equivalently at which the shifted clock $\xi_t(\alpha)/\xi_t(\alpha+\sqrt u)$ is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution. The symmetrised truncations are $K_n(w)=\pi^{-w}F_n(w)+\pi^{w-1/2}F_n(\frac12-w)$ with $F_n(w)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[\bigl(\sum_{k\le n}k^{-2}(e_k+e_k')\bigr)^w\bigr]$, where $e_k,e_k'$ are independent standard exponential variables; Conjecture S says that, for every $n$, all zeros of $K_n$ in the strip $0<\operatorname{Re}w<\frac12$ lie on the line $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$, and at $t=0$, $\alpha=\frac12$ the Hurwitz argument shows that this for infinitely many $n$ would imply the Riemann Hypothesis. The known part of $\mathcal{G}$ consists of the points $(0,1)$ (the critical strip), $(0.2,0.6)$ (Polymath15) and a point on the level set $t+2(\alpha-\frac12)^2=0.2$ (Polymath15 with the verification of Platt and Trudgian), conditionally on an announced zero free half plane also $(0,\frac78)$, and every point $(t,\alpha)$ with $\alpha\ge\frac12$, $t\ge t_0$ and $(\alpha-\frac12)^2+\frac t2\ge(\alpha_0-\frac12)^2+\frac{t_0}2$ for one of these points $(t_0,\alpha_0)$ (de Bruijn's strip theorem in Thorin form). Problem: give the symmetrised truncations a coordinate on the phase diagram: for some $(t,\alpha)$ outside the known part, is there a family of explicit truncations of $\xi_t$, built from finitely many terms of the Pólya integral or of a Dirichlet series and making no use of the zeros, as the $K_n$ are, that converges to $\xi_t$ uniformly on compact sets, together with heights $h_n\to\infty$ such that for infinitely many $n$ the $n$th truncation has no zero with $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha$ and $|\operatorname{Im}s|<h_n$? Hurwitz's theorem would then make $(t,\alpha)$ a new point of $\mathcal{G}$; at $t=0$ and $\alpha=\frac12$ the question for the $K_n$ is Conjecture S, and for the finite stages of the Pólya density as a maximum of exponential variables it is the open problem posed with those stages.
results.label: cp:prob:trunc

results.name: Open problem on the Cholesky factor of the Weil Gram matrix
results.summary: Compute the Cholesky factor of the Weil Gram matrix on hat functions for decreasing width and increasing support, and decide whether its entries converge to an object built from the arithmetic.
results.statement: For $h$ smooth enough, with $\hat h(r)=\int h(x)e^{irx}\,dx$, let $W(h)=\hat h(\frac i2)+\hat h(-\frac i2)-\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\Lambda(n)}{\sqrt n}\bigl(h(\log n)+h(-\log n)\bigr)+\frac1{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb{R}}\hat h(r)\operatorname{Re}\psi\bigl(\frac14+\frac{ir}2\bigr)\,dr-h(0)\log\pi$, where $\Lambda$ is von Mangoldt's function and $\psi=\Gamma'/\Gamma$; by Weil's explicit formula $W(h)=\sum_\rho\hat h(\gamma_\rho)$ over the zeros $\rho=\frac12+i\gamma_\rho$ of Riemann's xi function. For $g$ supported in $[-L/2,L/2]$ and $h=g*\tilde g$ with $\tilde g(x)=\overline{g(-x)}$, under the Riemann Hypothesis (every $\gamma_\rho$ real) $W(h)=\sum_\rho|\hat g(\gamma_\rho)|^2\ge0$ (Weil's criterion). Take the hat functions $g_j(x)=\max(0,1-|x-c_j|/w)$ at nodes $c_j$ spaced $w$ apart inside $[-L/2,L/2]$, $N=L/w-1$ functions in all, and the Weil Gram matrix $G_{jk}=W(g_j*\tilde g_k)$, which is Hermitian. Problem: compute the Cholesky factor of $G$ for decreasing $w$ and increasing $L$, and decide whether its entries converge to an object built from the arithmetic, as the first test of a factorisation $W(g*\tilde g)=\|Ag\|^2$ with $A$ built from the arithmetic.
results.label: cp:prob:chol

results.name: Open problem on a global functional of the zeros that is monotone along the flow
results.summary: Find a global functional of the zeros of $H_t$, monotone along the flow and insensitive to individual close pairs, whose positivity at $t=0$ excludes collisions at positive time.
results.statement: Let $\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})$ and $H_t(z)=\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cos(zu)\,du$, the de Bruijn Newman deformation of Riemann's xi function (so $H_0(z)=\frac18\xi(\frac12+\frac{iz}2)$); while simple, its zeros $z_k(t)$ move by $dz_k/dt=2\sum_{j\ne k}(z_k-z_j)^{-1}$, like a log gas. Problem: find a global functional of the zeros of $H_t$, insensitive to individual close pairs, that is monotone along the flow and whose positivity at $t=0$ excludes collisions at positive time. Biane's gap functional, the minimum over one gap of Laguerre's quantity, is local; the functional asked for should instead be one quantity for all the zeros.
results.label: cp:prob:gas

results.name: Open problem on explicit bounds for the heat flow zeta factor and the argument term up to time 0.2
results.summary: Prove that the real part of $\xi_{0.2}'/\xi_{0.2}$ on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=10$ is at least $\frac{19}2V_{0.2}$ at every height above the first zero ordinate, and prove an explicit logarithmic bound for the argument term $S_t(T)$ for $0<t\le0.2$.
results.statement: Let $\xi_t$ be the heat flow function ($\xi_t(s)=8\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cosh((2s-1)u)\,du$, $\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})$, $\xi_0=\xi$), $V_{0.2}=(\log\xi_{0.2})''(\frac12)$, $\theta_1(0.2)$ the least positive ordinate of a zero of $\xi_{0.2}$, $v_{0.2}(10,\theta)=\operatorname{Re}(\xi_{0.2}'/\xi_{0.2})(10+i\theta)$, $\zeta_t=\xi_t/(g\,e^{t\ell^2/4})$ with $g(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)$ and $\ell=g'/g$, and $S_t(T)$ the argument term of the zero count of $\xi_t$ (the change of $\arg\zeta_t$ along the segments from $2$ to $2+iT$ and $2+iT$ to $\frac12+iT$, divided by $\pi$). Problem (a): prove that $v_{0.2}(10,\theta)\ge\frac{19}2V_{0.2}$ for every $\theta\ge\theta_1(0.2)$, which would make the shifted clock of $\xi_{0.2}$, with the constant part of its Thorin density removed, a GGC transform for every basepoint in $[\frac12,10]$; it suffices to bound $|\zeta_{0.2}-1|$ on the discs of radius $5$ about $10+i\theta$ by a small constant uniform in $\theta$ (computed: at the four sampled heights the largest of $256$ sampled values of $|\zeta_{0.2}-1|$ on each boundary circle is at most $0.0326$, which is not a bound on the discs). Problem (b): for $0<t\le0.2$ prove an explicit bound $|S_t(T)|\le c_1\log T+c_2$ for $T\ge T_1$, for instance by proving, with an explicit majorant $M$, the two hypotheses of the Backlund type bound for $S_t$ ($\operatorname{Re}\zeta_t(2+iy)>0$ for $0\le y\le T$, and $M(\omega)\ge|\zeta_t(2+iT+\frac52e^{\pm i\omega})|$ for $0\le\omega\le2\pi$) (computed: the minimum of $\operatorname{Re}\zeta_{0.2}(2+iy)$ over $0\le y\le200$ is $0.69006$, near $y=14.015$). At $t=0$ much sharper explicit bounds are known (Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong 2022).
results.label: cp:prob:rvm

results.name: Uniqueness of Cauchy deconvolution for admissible measures
results.summary: Two admissible measures with the same convolution with a Cauchy density of width $a$ are equal, by the semigroup property and Fubini's theorem.
results.statement: Let $P_a(x)=(a/\pi)/(a^2+x^2)$ be the Cauchy density of width $a>0$. Call a signed measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ admissible when $\int(1+x^2)^{-1}d|\mu|(x)<\infty$. If $\mu_1,\mu_2$ are admissible and $P_a*\mu_1=P_a*\mu_2$ then $\mu_1=\mu_2$. The proof applies the semigroup property $P_a*P_b=P_{a+b}$ to the difference, shows its Poisson extension vanishes for heights above $a$ and hence on the whole upper half plane, and uses that an admissible measure is the vague boundary value of its Poisson integral.
results.label: cd:prop:unique

results.name: The range of convolution with a Cauchy density on L2, unboundedness of the inverse, and a positive bounded datum outside the range
results.summary: On $L^2$ the range of $P_a*$ is the set of $u$ with $\int e^{2a|\omega|}|\widehat u|^2<\infty$, the inverse is unbounded between all Sobolev norms, and $2+\cos(x^2)$ is not $P_a*\mu$ for any admissible $\mu$ although its Poisson extension continues to an entire harmonic function.
results.statement: Let $P_a(x)=(a/\pi)/(a^2+x^2)$, $a>0$, with Fourier transform $\widehat f(\omega)=\int f(x)e^{-i\omega x}dx$, so $\widehat{P_a}=e^{-a|\omega|}$, and let $H^s$ be the Sobolev space of order $s$. (a) For $f\in L^2(\mathbb{R})$, $\int e^{2a|\omega|}|\widehat{P_a*f}|^2d\omega=\int|\widehat f|^2d\omega$, and every $u$ with $\int e^{2a|\omega|}|\widehat u|^2d\omega<\infty$ equals $P_a*f$ for some $f\in L^2$. (b) For all real $s,t$, $\sup_f\|f\|_{H^t}/\|P_a*f\|_{H^s}=\infty$. (c) The function $u(x)=2+\cos(x^2)$ is positive and bounded, its Poisson extension continues to an entire harmonic function, and yet $u\ne P_a*\mu$ for every $a>0$ and every measure $\mu$ with $\int(1+t^2)^{-1}d|\mu|(t)<\infty$.
results.label: cd:prop:range

results.name: A positive datum with a signed source: the two atom example and its critical width
results.summary: For $\mu=\delta_0-q\delta_d$ the datum $P_a*\mu$ is nonnegative if and only if $q\le(r-d)/(r+d)$ with $r=\sqrt{d^2+4a^2}$, so a positive datum can have a signed source and no positive one at width $a$; the partial deconvolutions are positive exactly up to an explicit critical width, with $c^*=\frac14$ for $q=9-4\sqrt5$, $a=\frac12$, $d=1$.
results.statement: Let $P_a(x)=(a/\pi)/(a^2+x^2)$, $d>0$, $0<q<1$, $a>0$ and $\mu=\delta_0-q\delta_d$. Then $P_a*\mu=P_a-qP_a(\cdot-d)\ge0$ on $\mathbb{R}$ if and only if $q\le(r-d)/(r+d)$ with $r=\sqrt{d^2+4a^2}$. By uniqueness of the deconvolution, the signed measure $\mu$ is then the only source of this datum at width $a$. The partial deconvolution $P_{a-c}*\mu$, $0\le c<a$, is nonnegative if and only if $q\le(r_c-d)/(r_c+d)$ with $r_c=\sqrt{d^2+4(a-c)^2}$, that is, if and only if $c\le c^*=a-\frac12\sqrt{m^2-d^2}$ with $m=\frac{1+q}{1-q}d$. For $q=9-4\sqrt5$, $a=\frac12$ and $d=1$ this gives $c^*=\frac14$ exactly.
results.label: cd:ex:signed

results.name: The critical width of a positive datum for Cauchy deconvolution is attained when finite
results.summary: For a nonnegative $u$ with $\int u/(1+x^2)<\infty$, a positive source at width $c$ exists for every finite $c\le c^*(u)$ and for no larger $c$, where $c^*(u)$ is the supremum of the widths with a positive source, which is attained when finite.
results.statement:
Let $P_c(x)=(c/\pi)/(c^2+x^2)$ with $P_0*
u=
u$, and let $u\ge0$ satisfy $\int u(x)(1+x^2)^{-1}dx<\infty$. Put $c^*(u)=\sup\{c\ge0:\ u=P_c*
u	ext{ for some measure }
u\ge0\}\in[0,\infty]$, so that $c=0$ always qualifies. Then a positive source at width $c$ exists for every finite $c\le c^*(u)$ and for no $c>c^*(u)$; in particular the supremum is attained when it is finite. The proof uses that the admissible widths form an interval and the Herglotz and Riesz characterisation of nonnegative harmonic functions on a half plane.
results.label: cd:prop:critical

results.name: A positive source exists at width c if and only if the harmonic extension continues as a nonnegative harmonic function to the half plane y > -c
results.summary: For a continuous $u\ge0$ with $\int u/(1+x^2)<\infty$, $u=P_c*\nu$ with $\nu\ge0$ if and only if the Poisson extension of $u$ extends to a nonnegative harmonic function on $y>-c$, with the linear term of the Herglotz and Riesz representation shown to vanish.
results.statement: Let $u\ge0$ be continuous with $\int u(x)(1+x^2)^{-1}dx<\infty$ and let $h(x,y)=(P_y*u)(x)$, $y>0$, be its Poisson (harmonic) extension to the upper half plane, with $P_y$ the Cauchy density of width $y$. For $c>0$ the following are equivalent: (i) $u=P_c*\nu$ for a measure $\nu\ge0$; (ii) $h$ extends to a nonnegative harmonic function on the half plane $y>-c$. The proof of (ii) implies (i) uses the Herglotz and Riesz representation of nonnegative harmonic functions on a half plane and shows that its linear coefficient vanishes.
results.label: cd:thm:herglotz

results.name: Hölder stability of Cauchy deconvolution between levels by the three lines theorem, with sharp exponent
results.summary: $\|P_b*\mu\|_2\le\|P_a*\mu\|_2^{(b-b_0)/(a-b_0)}\|P_{b_0}*\mu\|_2^{(a-b)/(a-b_0)}$ for $b_0<b<a$, so data errors $\varepsilon$ at width $a$ and a bound $M$ at width $b_0$ give an error $\varepsilon^\kappa(2M)^{1-\kappa}$ at width $b$, and the exponent is attained.
results.statement: Let $P_y$ be the Cauchy density of width $y>0$, with $P_0*\mu=\mu$, let $b_0<b<a$ and let $\mu$ be a signed measure with $P_{b_0}*\mu\in L^2(\mathbb{R})$, where for $b_0<0$ this means $\mu=P_{|b_0|}*\lambda$ with $\lambda\in L^2$ and $P_{b_0}*\mu$ stands for $\lambda$; for $y>b_0$, $P_y*\mu$ means $P_{y-b_0}*(P_{b_0}*\mu)$. Then $\|P_b*\mu\|_2\le\|P_a*\mu\|_2^{\kappa}\,\|P_{b_0}*\mu\|_2^{1-\kappa}$ with $\kappa=(b-b_0)/(a-b_0)$. In particular, if two sources have data at width $a$ within $\varepsilon$ in $L^2$ and both are bounded by $M$ at width $b_0$, they agree at width $b$ to within $\varepsilon^\kappa(2M)^{1-\kappa}$. The exponent $\kappa$ is attained in rate. The proof is Hölder's inequality on the Fourier side, equivalently convexity of $y\mapsto\log\|P_y*\mu\|_2$.
results.label: cd:thm:holder

results.name: Sharp Hölder exponent (b+w)/(a+w) for Cauchy deconvolution of finite signed sources
results.summary: For a finite signed measure $\nu$ of total variation at most $B$ and $h=P_w*\nu$, $\|P_b*h\|_2\le\sqrt2D^{1-\kappa}\|P_a*h\|_2^\kappa$ for $w\ge0$ and $-w<b<a$, with $\kappa=(b+w)/(a+w)$ and $D=B/\sqrt{2\pi(b+w)}$, and no larger exponent holds uniformly over this class.
results.statement:
Let $P_y$ be the Cauchy density of width $y>0$ with $P_0*
u=
u$. Let $
u$ be a finite signed measure of total variation at most $B$, let $w\ge0$, $h=P_w*
u$ (with $P_b*h$ meaning $P_{b+w}*
u$ when $b<0$) and let $-w<b<a$. Then $\|P_b*h\|_2\le\sqrt2\,D^{1-\kappa}\|P_a*h\|_2^{\kappa}$ with $\kappa=(b+w)/(a+w)$ and $D=B/\sqrt{2\pi(b+w)}$, and no larger exponent holds uniformly over this class. The upper bound is a split of the frequencies at a cutoff chosen as a function of the data error, and the sharpness is shown by the sources $B\phi(x)\cos(\Omega x)dx$ with $\Omega	o\infty$ for a fixed nonnegative kernel $\phi$ with transform $(1-|\omega|)_+$.
results.label: cd:prop:finite

results.name: Two level Hölder bound for positive sources of Cauchy deconvolution with data in L2 on the line
results.summary: For nonnegative sources with data $u_j=P_a*\mu_j\in L^2$ within $\varepsilon$, $\|P_b*(\mu_1-\mu_2)\|_2\le\varepsilon^\kappa((a/d)(\|u_1\|_2+\|u_2\|_2))^{1-\kappa}$ for $0<d<b<a$, with no a priori bound needed.
results.statement: Let $P_y$ be the Cauchy density of width $y>0$. If $\mu_1,\mu_2\ge0$ are measures, $u_j=P_a*\mu_j\in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ and $\|u_1-u_2\|_2\le\varepsilon$, then for $0<d<b<a$, $\|P_b*(\mu_1-\mu_2)\|_2\le\varepsilon^\kappa\bigl((a/d)(\|u_1\|_2+\|u_2\|_2)\bigr)^{1-\kappa}$ with $\kappa=(b-d)/(a-d)$. The proof uses the pointwise bound $P_d\le(a/d)P_a$ and the three lines bound. The statement is for data in $L^2$ on the whole line; the case of data on a window is a problem of the chapter.
results.label: cd:cor:positive

results.name: Logarithmic stability of Cauchy deconvolution for sources in a Sobolev ball, sharp in order and in the constant
results.summary: If $\|\mu\|_{H^s}\le M$ and $\|P_a*\mu\|_2\le\varepsilon$ then $\|\mu\|_2\le C_sM(2a/\log(M/\varepsilon))^s$ for $\varepsilon/M$ small, and no bound of smaller order holds uniformly over the Sobolev ball.
results.statement: Let $P_a$ be the Cauchy density of width $a>0$, $s>0$, and $H^s$ the Sobolev space of order $s$; $C_s$ denotes a constant depending only on $s$. Suppose $\|\mu\|_{H^s}\le M$ and $\|P_a*\mu\|_2\le\varepsilon$, with $\varepsilon/M$ small enough depending on $a$ and $s$. Then $\|\mu\|_2\le C_sM\bigl(2a/\log(M/\varepsilon)\bigr)^s$, and no bound of smaller order holds uniformly over the class: the modulus of continuity of the inverse is of this order. The sharp modulus $\sup\{\|\mu\|_2:\|\mu\|_{H^s}\le M,\|P_a*\mu\|_2\le\varepsilon\}$ is $(1+o(1))M(a/\log(M/\varepsilon))^s$ as $\varepsilon/M\to0$.
results.label: cd:thm:log

results.name: Polynomial upper rate for density deconvolution with Cauchy noise and a target analytic in a strip
results.summary: For Cauchy noise of width $a$ and a density with $\int e^{2w|\omega|}|\widehat f|^2\le2\pi M^2$, the spectral cutoff estimator with $\Omega=\log n/(2(a+w))$ has root mean integrated squared error $O(n^{-w/(2(a+w))})$, an upper bound.
results.statement: Let $Y_1,\dots,Y_n$ be i.i.d. observations $Y_j=X_j+E_j$, with $X_j$ of density $f$ independent of $E_j$, Cauchy noise of width $a>0$, with $\int e^{2w|\omega|}|\widehat f(\omega)|^2d\omega\le2\pi M^2$ for some $w>0$, where $\widehat f(\omega)=\int f(x)e^{-i\omega x}dx$. The spectral cutoff estimator $\widehat f_n(x)=(2\pi)^{-1}\int_{|\omega|\le\Omega}e^{a|\omega|}\widehat\phi_n(\omega)e^{i\omega x}d\omega$, with $\widehat\phi_n(\omega)=n^{-1}\sum_{j\le n}e^{-i\omega Y_j}$ and $\Omega=\log n/(2(a+w))$, has root mean integrated squared error $O(n^{-w/(2(a+w))})$. This is an upper bound only; no lower bound is claimed.
results.label: cd:prop:strip

results.name: Problem: estimating the critical width of noisy positive data
results.summary: Estimate the critical width $c^*(u)$ from noisy data $u+$noise; for atomic sources it is the smallest pole width, but there is no uniform rate without weights bounded below because $c^*$ is discontinuous.
results.statement: Let $u\ge0$ with $\int u(x)(1+x^2)^{-1}dx<\infty$ and $c^*(u)=\sup\{c\ge0:u=P_c*\nu\text{ for some measure }\nu\ge0\}$, with $P_c$ the Cauchy density of width $c$. Given noisy data $u+\text{noise}$, estimate $c^*(u)$. For atomic sources with positive weights $c^*$ is the smallest width among the poles, estimable by a matrix pencil on a class with bounded order, weights bounded below, separation and no aliasing; without weights bounded below there is no uniform rate, since $c^*$ is discontinuous ($(1-\delta)P_A+\delta P_r$ has $c^*=r<A$ for every $\delta>0$). For general sources $c^*$ is a boundary of a convex cone in an infinite dimensional space. Status: open.
results.label: cd:prob:width

results.name: Problem: positivity and rates for the Thorin family
results.summary: Positive sources $P_w*\nu$ with mass at most $B$ have polynomial exponent $w/(a+w)$ from smoothing and the mass bound, not from positivity; is the Thorin family in a class on which positivity alone gives a polynomial rate?
results.statement: Let $P_a$ be the Cauchy density of width $a>0$. Positive sources of the form $P_w*\nu$ with $\nu\ge0$ of mass at most $B$ have the polynomial exponent $w/(a+w)$ for deconvolution at $b=0$, but this comes from the smoothing and the mass bound, not from positivity, and the zero counting measure of the Riemann zeta function has infinite mass. Positivity does not improve the logarithmic minimax rate over smoothness classes of densities in the worst case, and prescribing a number of sign changes of the Fourier transform does not help. Open: is the Thorin family, the family of the solutions $\mu\ge0$ of $P_{1-\theta}*\mu=u_1$, $\frac12\le\theta<1$, with $u_1(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(1+iv)$ and $\xi$ the completed zeta function, in a class on which positivity alone gives a polynomial rate?
results.label: cd:prob:rates

results.name: Problem: Hölder bound between levels from data on a window for positive sources
results.summary: For positive sources and data known only on a window, does positivity give a Hölder bound between levels without an a priori bound below the target, with an exponent determined by the data?
results.statement: Let $P_y$ be the Cauchy density of width $y>0$. The three lines bound needs an a priori bound at a level below the target, and for nonnegative sources with data in $L^2$ on the whole line this bound is removed. For data known only on a window, the mass in a window of a positive source is controlled by the data alone. Open: does positivity give a Hölder bound between levels from data on a window, without any a priori bound below the target, with an exponent determined by the data?
results.label: cd:prob:three

results.name: Tilt family of the clock: the Thorin property at one tilt is equivalent to RH
results.summary: The Esscher tilt of the clock of xi maps generalized gamma convolutions to generalized gamma convolutions in both directions and leaves the imaginary part of the point attached to each zero unchanged, so the Thorin property at one tilt is equivalent to the property at every tilt and to RH (the case of the rational field of the tilt theorem for Dedekind zeta functions).
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $G(u)=\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt u)/\xi(\tfrac12)$, an entire function of $u$. Each pair $\{\rho,1-\rho\}$ of zeros $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ of $\xi$ gives the number $a_\rho=-(\rho-\tfrac12)^2=\gamma^2-(\beta-\tfrac12)^2-2i\gamma(\beta-\tfrac12)$, and Hadamard's product gives the absolutely convergent product $G(u)=\prod(1+u/a_\rho)$. For $u_0\ge0$ put $\widetilde\varphi_{u_0}(u)=G(u_0)/G(u_0+u)$ for $u\ge0$, the Laplace transform of the clock $T$ of $\xi$ (the variable with $\mathbb{E}e^{-uT}=\xi(\tfrac12)/\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt u)$) tilted by $e^{-u_0T}$; for $u_0=0$ it is the Laplace transform of $T$ itself. A generalized gamma convolution (GGC) Laplace transform is a function $\exp\bigl(-du-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+u/z)\,U(dz)\bigr)$ with drift $d\ge0$ and a positive Thorin measure $U$. Then: (a) for $u_1\ge0$, $\widetilde\varphi_{u_0+u_1}(u)=\widetilde\varphi_{u_0}(u_1+u)/\widetilde\varphi_{u_0}(u_1)$, so the tilt by $u_1$ is the Esscher transform by $e^{-u_1\widetilde T_{u_0}}$, where $\widetilde T_{u_0}$ has transform $\widetilde\varphi_{u_0}$; it maps GGC transforms to GGC transforms and moves the Thorin measure up by $u_1$; backward, if $\widetilde\varphi_{u_0+u_1}$ is a GGC transform with Thorin measure carried by $(u_1,\infty)$, then $\widetilde\varphi_{u_0}(u)=\widetilde\varphi_{u_0+u_1}(u-u_1)/\widetilde\varphi_{u_0+u_1}(-u_1)$ is a GGC transform with the Thorin measure moved down by $u_1$, the denominator being $G(u_0+u_1)/G(u_0)$, finite and positive. (b) $\widetilde\varphi_{u_0}$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC if and only if every $u_0+a_\rho$ is real and positive; the imaginary part of $u_0+a_\rho$ is $-2\gamma(\beta-\tfrac12)$, which does not depend on $u_0$. (c) The following are equivalent: $\widetilde\varphi_{u_0}$ is a GGC transform for one $u_0\ge0$; it is a GGC transform for every $u_0\ge0$; the Riemann Hypothesis holds.
results.label: tf:thm:tilt

results.name: Poisson semigroup of the basepoint family and its converse
results.summary: The Thorin densities of the shifted clocks satisfy the Poisson semigroup identity from any level to the right of all zeros, with no hypothesis from level one half on, and the identity fails from every level $\varepsilon_0\ge0$ that has a zero to its right and lies at positive distance from the offsets of the zeros.
results.statement:
Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function with zeros $ho= eta+i\gamma$ counted with multiplicity. For real $\varepsilon$ and $	heta$ such that $	frac12+\varepsilon+i	heta$ is not a zero put $ho_\varepsilon(	heta)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(	frac12+\varepsilon+i	heta)$, the Thorin density at level $\varepsilon$ (in the chart $	heta=\sqrt z$ it is the Thorin density of the shifted clock $\xi(	frac12+\varepsilon)/\xi(	frac12+\varepsilon+\sqrt u)$ for $\varepsilon>0$, whenever that is a generalized gamma convolution and no zero lies on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=	frac12+\varepsilon$). Let $P_a(x)=a/(\pi(a^2+x^2))$ for real $a
e0$, so that $P_a$ is the Cauchy density of scale $a$ for $a>0$, $P_{-a}=-P_a$ and $P_a*P_b=P_{a+b}$ for $a,b>0$. Hadamard's product gives the absolutely convergent expansion $ho_\varepsilon(	heta)=\sum_ho P_{\varepsilon-( eta- rac12)}(	heta-\gamma)$ over all zeros with multiplicity, for $\varepsilon
e eta-	frac12$. (a) If $\varepsilon_0> eta-	frac12$ for every zero, then $ho_{\varepsilon_0+a}=P_a*ho_{\varepsilon_0}$ for every $a>0$ (convolution in $	heta$) and $ho_\varepsilon>0$ for every $\varepsilon\ge\varepsilon_0$; this hypothesis holds, with no assumption on the zeros, for every $\varepsilon_0\ge	frac12$. (b) If $\varepsilon_0\ge0$ lies at positive distance from the set $\{ eta-	frac12\}$ of the offsets of the zeros and some zero has $ eta-	frac12>\varepsilon_0$, then $ho_{\varepsilon_0+a}
e P_a*ho_{\varepsilon_0}$ for some $a>0$.
results.label: tf:thm:poisson

results.name: Deconvolution form of RH
results.summary: RH holds if and only if the Thorin density at a basepoint to the right of all zeros is the Cauchy smoothing of a positive measure on the line, which is then the sum of unit point masses at the ordinates of the zeros, repeated according to multiplicity, and more generally the density deconvolves to a positive measure at level $\varepsilon_1$ exactly when no zero has offset $\beta-\tfrac12$ above $\varepsilon_1$.
results.statement:
Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function with zeros $ho= eta+i\gamma$ of multiplicity $m_ho$, let $ho_\varepsilon(	heta)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(	frac12+\varepsilon+i	heta)$ be the Thorin density at level $\varepsilon$, and let $P_a(x)=a/(\pi(a^2+x^2))$ be the Cauchy density of scale $a>0$; $*$ denotes convolution in $	heta$. Let $\varepsilon_0> eta-	frac12$ for every zero (for instance $\varepsilon_0\ge	frac12$, which needs no assumption) and let $0\le\varepsilon_1<\varepsilon_0$. (a) There is a positive measure $
u$ on $\mathbb{R}$ with $\int(1+x^2)^{-1}
u(dx)<\infty$ and $ho_{\varepsilon_0}=P_{\varepsilon_0-\varepsilon_1}*
u$ if and only if $ eta-	frac12\le\varepsilon_1$ for every zero. When it exists, $
u$ is unique: it is $ho_{\varepsilon_1}\,d	heta$ if $ eta-	frac12<\varepsilon_1$ for every zero, and otherwise the vague limit of $ho_\varepsilon\,d	heta$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow\varepsilon_1$, which carries the point masses $m_ho\delta_\gamma$ at the zeros with $ eta-	frac12=\varepsilon_1$. (b) In particular RH holds if and only if $ho_{\varepsilon_0}=P_{\varepsilon_0}*\mu$ for a positive measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ (the condition $\int(1+x^2)^{-1}\mu(dx)<\infty$ is then automatic, because $P_{\varepsilon_0}*\mu=ho_{\varepsilon_0}$ is finite), and then $\mu=\sum_\gamma\delta_\gamma$, the sum over the ordinates of all zeros, of both signs, with multiplicity.
results.label: tf:thm:deconv

results.name: Thorin density near the critical line and Laguerre's quantity
results.summary: For small epsilon the Thorin density at level epsilon equals epsilon over pi times Laguerre's quantity, the negative second derivative of the logarithm of the absolute value of Xi, up to $O(\varepsilon^3)$, and a hypothetical off line quadruple at distance delta contributes minus two over delta squared to that quantity at its own ordinate, up to $O(\gamma^{*-2})$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function, $\Xi(\theta)=\xi(\tfrac12+i\theta)$, and for real $\varepsilon$ and $\theta$ such that $\tfrac12+\varepsilon+i\theta$ is not a zero put $\rho_\varepsilon(\theta)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\tfrac12+\varepsilon+i\theta)$. Let $\theta$ be real and not the ordinate of a zero on the critical line. Then $\rho_\varepsilon(\theta)=\frac{\varepsilon}{\pi}\mathcal L_\Xi(\theta)+O(\varepsilon^3)$ as $\varepsilon\to0$, where $\mathcal L_\Xi(\theta)=-\frac{d^2}{d\theta^2}\log|\Xi(\theta)|=\sum_\rho(\theta-\gamma_\rho)^{-2}$ is Laguerre's quantity, $\gamma_\rho=-i(\rho-\tfrac12)=\gamma-i(\beta-\tfrac12)$ runs over the zeros of $\Xi$, and the sum is real because the zeros of $\Xi$ come in conjugate pairs. Under RH, $\mathcal L_\Xi(\theta)=\sum_\gamma(\theta-\gamma)^{-2}>0$. A quadruple of zeros $\tfrac12\pm\delta\pm i\gamma^*$ with $\delta>0$ and $\gamma^*>0$ contributes $2\operatorname{Re}(\theta-\gamma^*+i\delta)^{-2}+2\operatorname{Re}(\theta+\gamma^*+i\delta)^{-2}$ to $\mathcal L_\Xi(\theta)$, which equals $-2/\delta^2+O(\gamma^{*-2})$ at $\theta=\gamma^*$.
results.label: tf:prop:nearline

results.name: Visibility curve of a hypothetical off line quadruple and its closed forms in three lattice models
results.summary: At the ordinate of a hypothetical off line quadruple at distance delta, the Thorin density at level epsilon, when the other zeros contribute positively there, is negative exactly when epsilon is below delta and delta is below the visibility distance $\delta_{\mathrm{det}}(\varepsilon)$, which is given in closed form in three lattice models, increases with epsilon and exceeds epsilon by about Delta over pi at large epsilon; this is a theorem about a model with a hypothetical quadruple, not about the zeros of xi.
results.statement: No off line zero of $\xi$ is known; consider a hypothetical zero set (zeros $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ counted with multiplicity, for instance the zeros of $\xi$ with a quadruple added by hand) that contains a quadruple $\tfrac12\pm\delta\pm i\gamma^*$ with $\delta>0$ and $\gamma^*>0$. Let $P_a(x)=a/(\pi(a^2+x^2))$ for real $a\ne0$ and let $\rho_\varepsilon(\theta)=\sum_\rho P_{\varepsilon-(\beta-\frac12)}(\theta-\gamma)$ be the Thorin density at level $\varepsilon$ of the zero set (for the zeros of $\xi$ it equals $\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\tfrac12+\varepsilon+i\theta)$). Let $\rho^0_\varepsilon$ be the same sum over all zeros other than the two zeros $\tfrac12\pm\delta+i\gamma^*$, so that the images $\tfrac12\pm\delta-i\gamma^*$ of the quadruple at $-\gamma^*$ are included in it, and suppose $\rho^0_\varepsilon(\gamma^*)>0$. Then for $0<\varepsilon<\delta$, $\rho_\varepsilon(\gamma^*)<0$ if and only if $\delta<\delta_{\mathrm{det}}(\varepsilon)$, where $\delta_{\mathrm{det}}(\varepsilon)^2=\varepsilon^2+\frac{2\varepsilon}{\pi\rho^0_\varepsilon(\gamma^*)}$, which depends on $\delta$ through the images; so the level $\varepsilon$ sees the quadruple at its ordinate exactly for the distances $\varepsilon<\delta<\delta_{\mathrm{det}}(\varepsilon)$. In the lattice models the other zeros are the following points of the critical line and nothing else (the images at $-\gamma^*$ and the distant zeros are neglected), with spacing $\Delta>0$: in model (ii) the points $\gamma^*\pm(k+\tfrac12)\Delta$, $k\ge0$ (the quadruple sits at the midpoint of a gap); in model (i) the points $\gamma^*\pm k\Delta$, $k\ge1$ (the quadruple replaces the zero at $\gamma^*$); in model (iii) the points $\gamma^*\pm(k+\tfrac12)\Delta$, $k\ge1$ (the quadruple replaces the two zeros that bound a gap and sits at its midpoint). Then \[\delta_{\mathrm{det}}(\varepsilon)^2=\varepsilon^2+\begin{cases}\dfrac{2\varepsilon\Delta}{\pi\tanh(\pi\varepsilon/\Delta)} & \text{in (ii)},\\[2.5ex] \dfrac{2\varepsilon}{\frac\pi\Delta\coth\frac{\pi\varepsilon}\Delta-\frac1\varepsilon} & \text{in (i)},\\[2.5ex] \dfrac{2\varepsilon}{\frac\pi\Delta\tanh\frac{\pi\varepsilon}\Delta-\frac{2\varepsilon}{\varepsilon^2+\Delta^2/4}} & \text{in (iii)}.\end{cases}\] As $\varepsilon\to0$ these tend to $\delta_c^2=2\Delta^2/\pi^2$, $6\Delta^2/\pi^2$ and $2\Delta^2/(\pi^2-8)$ respectively; for $\varepsilon\ge\Delta$ all three satisfy $\delta_{\mathrm{det}}(\varepsilon)^2-\varepsilon^2=2\varepsilon\Delta/\pi+O(\Delta^2)$, that is $\delta_{\mathrm{det}}(\varepsilon)-\varepsilon=(\Delta/\pi)\bigl(1+O(\Delta/\varepsilon)\bigr)$; and in all three $\delta_{\mathrm{det}}$ is increasing in $\varepsilon$.
results.label: tf:prop:curve

results.name: Number of levels needed in the lattice models, one quarter of log h
results.summary: In the lattice models a single hypothetical off line quadruple at any distance up to one half is detected at its ordinate by the sign of Laguerre's quantity together with K levels, no test of this kind uses fewer than K levels, and K equals one quarter of log(h over 2 pi) plus O(log log h) at height h; this is a statement about a model, not about the zeros of xi.
results.statement: Consider the three lattice models of a single hypothetical off line quadruple $\tfrac12\pm\delta\pm i\gamma^*$ among zeros of the critical line with spacing $\Delta=2\pi/\log(h/2\pi)$ at height $h$: the other zeros are the points $\gamma^*\pm(k+\tfrac12)\Delta$, $k\ge0$, in model (ii), the points $\gamma^*\pm k\Delta$, $k\ge1$, in model (i), and the points $\gamma^*\pm(k+\tfrac12)\Delta$, $k\ge1$, in model (iii), and the images of the quadruple at $-\gamma^*$ and the distant zeros are neglected. Let $S(\varepsilon)=\sum(\varepsilon^2+(\gamma-\gamma^*)^2)^{-1}$ over the other zeros $\tfrac12+i\gamma$, $\delta_{\mathrm{det}}(\varepsilon)=\sqrt{\varepsilon^2+2/S(\varepsilon)}$ the visibility distance (the level $\varepsilon$ detects, at the ordinate $\gamma^*$, the quadruple at distance $\delta$, that is $\rho_\varepsilon(\gamma^*)<0$ for the Thorin density $\rho_\varepsilon(\theta)=\sum_\rho P_{\varepsilon-(\beta-\frac12)}(\theta-\gamma)$ of the zero set, with $P_a(x)=a/(\pi(a^2+x^2))$, exactly when $\varepsilon<\delta<\delta_{\mathrm{det}}(\varepsilon)$), and $\delta_c=\delta_{\mathrm{det}}(0)=\sqrt{2/S(0)}$, which equals $(\sqrt2/\pi)\Delta$, $(\sqrt6/\pi)\Delta$ and $\sqrt{2/(\pi^2-8)}\,\Delta$ in models (ii), (i), (iii) (the first order test is the sign of Laguerre's quantity $\mathcal L_\Xi(\gamma^*)=-(\log|\Xi|)''(\gamma^*)$ with $\Xi(\theta)=\xi(\tfrac12+i\theta)$, which in the model is the sign of $S(0)-2/\delta^2$, so that it detects the quadruple exactly for $\delta<\delta_c$). Put $\varepsilon_1=\delta_c$ and $\varepsilon_{k+1}=\delta_{\mathrm{det}}(\varepsilon_k)$, and let $K$ be the least $k\ge0$ with $\varepsilon_{k+1}>\tfrac12$, so that $K=0$ if $\delta_c>\tfrac12$. (a) The sign of $\mathcal L_\Xi(\gamma^*)$, together with positivity of $\rho_\varepsilon(\gamma^*)$ at the levels $\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_K$, each moved down slightly so that consecutive bands overlap, detects a single off line quadruple at every distance in $(0,\tfrac12]$. (b) No test made at the ordinate, that is the sign of $\mathcal L_\Xi(\gamma^*)$ together with the sign of $\rho_\varepsilon(\gamma^*)$ at finitely many levels, that detects a single off line quadruple at every distance in $(0,\tfrac12]$ uses fewer than $K$ levels. (c) $K=\tfrac14\log(h/2\pi)+O(\log\log h)$ as $h\to\infty$.
results.label: tf:cor:levels

results.name: No averaging stable property carries real zeros
results.summary: A property of entire functions that is preserved by Gaussian averaging and implies that all zeros are real holds for no function $H_t$ of the de Bruijn Newman family, at no real time and in particular not at time zero.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function, $\Xi(\theta)=\xi(\tfrac12+i\theta)$, $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}\bigl(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2}\bigr)\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2u})$ the Pólya kernel, and for real $t$ let $H_t(z)=\tfrac12\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi(2u)\cos(zu)\,du$ be the de Bruijn Newman function, defined for every real $t$ because $\Phi(2u)$ decays like $e^{9u}\exp(-\pi e^{4u})$, with $H_0(z)=\tfrac18\Xi(z/2)$. For $s>0$ and $Z$ a standard normal variable, $H_{t-s}(z)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[H_t(z+\sqrt{2s}\,Z)\bigr]$ for complex $z$. Let $\mathcal P$ be a property of entire functions that is preserved by the Gaussian average $f\mapsto\mathbb{E}f(\cdot+\sqrt{2s}\,Z)$ for some $s>0$. If $\mathcal P$ implies that all zeros are real, then $H_t$ has the property $\mathcal P$ for no real $t$.
results.label: tf:cor:average

results.name: Question: a certificate with a few levels for the actual zeros
results.summary: The book asks for levels whose positivity, together with positivity of Laguerre's quantity, excludes all off line zeros of xi up to a given height, and whether the number of levels is still of order log of the height when several off line zeros, irregular spacing and minima off the ordinates are allowed.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function, $\Xi(\theta)=\xi(\tfrac12+i\theta)$, $\rho_\varepsilon(\theta)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\tfrac12+\varepsilon+i\theta)$ the Thorin density at level $\varepsilon$ and $\mathcal L_\Xi=-(\log|\Xi|)''$ Laguerre's quantity. In a lattice model with one hypothetical off line quadruple among regularly spaced zeros of the critical line, tested only at its ordinate, about $\tfrac14\log(h/2\pi)$ levels are needed at height $h$. The problem is to turn this into a certificate for the actual zeros: find levels $\varepsilon_1<\dots<\varepsilon_K$ such that positivity of every $\rho_{\varepsilon_k}$ on $[0,h]$, together with positivity of $\mathcal L_\Xi$, excludes all off line zeros of $\xi$ up to height $h$, allowing several off line zeros, irregular spacing and minima of $\rho_\varepsilon$ off the ordinates of the zeros. Is $K$ still of order $\log h$? The book notes that such a certificate would be finite information and a different verification of RH up to height $h$, from $\xi$ on lines to the right of the critical line rather than from sign changes on it.
results.label: tf:prob:levels

results.name: Question: stability with an a priori bound that comes from the Thorin structure
results.summary: The book asks whether the a priori bound that the three lines theorem needs on a zero free strip can come from the Thorin structure itself, for instance from positivity of the Thorin density at the levels already certified.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and suppose that the strip $\tfrac12+\varepsilon_1\le\operatorname{Re}s\le\tfrac12+\varepsilon_0$ is free of zeros. Hadamard's three lines theorem bounds the error of an approximation $g$ to $\xi'/\xi$ at level $\varepsilon$ (on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\tfrac12+\varepsilon$) by $\eta^{\lambda}M^{1-\lambda}$ with $\lambda=(\varepsilon-\varepsilon_1)/(\varepsilon_0-\varepsilon_1)$, where $\eta$ is the error at level $\varepsilon_0$ and $M$ is a bound at level $\varepsilon_1$. The bound $M$ presupposes the zero free strip. Is there a formulation in which the a priori bound comes from the Thorin structure itself, for instance from positivity of the Thorin density $\rho_\varepsilon=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\tfrac12+\varepsilon+i\,\cdot)$ at the levels already certified?
results.label: tf:prob:three

results.name: Question: which positivity statements fail for negative heat time by a mechanism visible at finite height
results.summary: The book asks which positivity statements, for instance the GGC property of the clock or the Pólya frequency property of the density of $Z\sqrt{2T}$, can be shown to fail for negative heat time by a mechanism visible at finite height, as Lehmer pairs make the de Bruijn Newman constant visible.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $H_t$ the de Bruijn Newman function, with $H_0(z)=\tfrac18\Xi(z/2)$ for $\Xi(\theta)=\xi(\tfrac12+i\theta)$ and $R_t(s)=H_t(0)/H_t(2i\sqrt s)$, so that $R_0(s)=\xi(\tfrac12)/\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt s)$ is the Laplace transform of the clock $T$ of $\xi$. Since $H_t$ has nonreal zeros for every $t<0$ (Rodgers and Tao), a property of $H_0$ that implies real zeros fails for $H_t$ at every $t<0$. Which of the positivity statements of the book, for instance the generalized gamma convolution (GGC) property of the clock, whose Laplace transform is $R_0$, or the Pólya frequency property of the density of $Z\sqrt{2T}$ (with $Z$ a standard normal variable independent of $T$), can be shown to fail for $t<0$ by a mechanism visible at finite height, as Lehmer pairs make the de Bruijn Newman constant $\Lambda$ close to $0$ visible (Csordas, Smith and Varga 1994)?
results.label: tf:prob:heat

results.name: Question: the window of levels below delta, its distribution over heights and the sine kernel
results.summary: The book asks for the distribution over heights of the visibility distance and of the onset level at which a hypothetical off line quadruple at distance delta becomes visible, in terms of local zero statistics, compared with the prediction of the sine kernel.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and add by hand a hypothetical quadruple $\tfrac12\pm\delta\pm i\gamma^*$ to its zeros, at an ordinate $\gamma^*$. Let $\rho^0_\varepsilon(\gamma^*)$ be the Thorin density at level $\varepsilon$ and at the ordinate $\gamma^*$ of the other zeros, $\delta_{\mathrm{det}}(\varepsilon)^2=\varepsilon^2+2\varepsilon/(\pi\rho^0_\varepsilon(\gamma^*))$ the visibility curve (the level $\varepsilon$ sees the quadruple at its ordinate exactly when $\varepsilon<\delta<\delta_{\mathrm{det}}(\varepsilon)$) and $\delta_c=\lim_{\varepsilon\to0}\delta_{\mathrm{det}}(\varepsilon)$ the first order visibility distance. For a quadruple at distance $\delta>\delta_c$ the levels at which the test detects it form a set contained in $(0,\delta)$, an interval $(\varepsilon_c,\delta)$ in the examples of the book; at the ordinate $\varepsilon_c$ is the inverse of the visibility curve. Describe the distribution of $\delta_{\mathrm{det}}$, and of the onset $\varepsilon_c(\delta,\gamma^*)$, over heights in terms of the local zero statistics, and compare it with the prediction of the sine kernel.
results.label: tf:prob:window

results.name: The deconvolved Thorin functional is Weil's distribution
results.summary: With no hypothesis on the zeros, deconvolving the Thorin density of the shifted clock by the Cauchy kernel gives a functional that does not depend on the basepoint and equals the sum of a test function over the zeros, which Weil's explicit formula computes from the gamma factor, the pole and the primes.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function, with nontrivial zeros $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ counted with multiplicity, and put $\gamma_\rho=-i(\rho-\frac12)=\gamma-i(\beta-\frac12)$, so that the $\gamma_\rho$ are the zeros of $\Xi(\theta)=\xi(\frac12+i\theta)$. For real $\alpha$ and $\theta$ let $v_\alpha(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\alpha+i\theta)$. Call $\varepsilon_0>0$ to the right of the zeros if $\beta<\frac12+\varepsilon_0$ for every zero; every $\varepsilon_0\ge\frac12$ is, because $\zeta$ has no zero with $\beta\ge1$, so no hypothesis on the zeros is needed. For such $\varepsilon_0$ let $\varrho_{\varepsilon_0}(\theta)=\pi^{-1}v_{1/2+\varepsilon_0}(\theta)$, the Thorin density of the shifted clock at the basepoint $\frac12+\varepsilon_0$ in the chart $\theta=\sqrt z$ (the Poisson smoothing of the zeros). Write $P_a(x)=a/(\pi(a^2+x^2))$ for the Cauchy density of scale $a>0$ and $\hat f(t)=\int f(x)e^{itx}\,dx$, so that $\hat P_a(x)=e^{-a|x|}$. Let $\mathcal{B}$ be the space of even functions $\varphi(\theta)=\frac1{2\pi}\int\hat\varphi(x)e^{-i\theta x}\,dx$ with $\hat\varphi$ of compact support, Lipschitz, and with $\hat\varphi'$ of bounded variation; each such $\varphi$ is entire of exponential type, with $\varphi(\theta+is)=O(\theta^{-2})$ uniformly for $|s|\le1$. For $a\ge0$ let $P_a^{-1}\varphi\in\mathcal{B}$ be the function with Fourier transform $\hat\varphi(x)e^{a|x|}$. Let $\varepsilon_0$ be to the right of the zeros and, for $\varphi\in\mathcal{B}$, put $D(\varphi)=\int\varrho_{\varepsilon_0}(\theta)\,(P_{\varepsilon_0}^{-1}\varphi)(\theta)\,d\theta$. Then $D(\varphi)$ does not depend on $\varepsilon_0$, and with $g(x)=\hat\varphi(x)/2\pi$, so that $\varphi(\theta)=\int g(x)e^{i\theta x}dx=\hat g(\theta)$, \[ D(\varphi)=\sum_\rho\varphi(\gamma_\rho)=\hat g(\tfrac i2)+\hat g(-\tfrac i2)-(\gamma_E+\log\pi)\,g(0)+\int_0^\infty\frac{2\big(e^{-2x}g(0)-e^{-x/2}g(x)\big)}{1-e^{-2x}}\,dx-2\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\Lambda(n)}{\sqrt n}\,g(\log n), \] where the sum over $\rho$ runs over all zeros with multiplicity, in conjugate pairs, and converges absolutely, $\gamma_E$ is Euler's constant and $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function. The second expression is Weil's explicit formula on $\mathcal{B}$, so $D$ is computed from the gamma factor, the pole and the primes $n$ with $\log n$ in the support of $g$; it is the action on $g$ of Weil's distribution $\sum_\rho e^{(\rho-1/2)x}$, that is, $\langle D,g\rangle=\sum_\rho\hat g(\gamma_\rho)$. Moreover, through the $x$ form of its archimedean term, the Thorin functional $U$ of the clock (the linear functional with $\langle U,\psi\rangle=\sum_k\psi(a_k)$ over the exponents $a_k=-(\rho_k-\frac12)^2$, one for each pair of zeros $\{\rho,1-\rho\}$, defined by the explicit formula, in which no zero appears) extends to $\mathcal{B}$, and then $D(\varphi)=2\langle U,\varphi(\sqrt{\cdot})\rangle$.
results.label: dc:thm:weil

results.name: Damped Weil criterion
results.summary: For $0\le\varepsilon\le\frac12$, Weil's quadratic form damped by $e^{-\varepsilon|x|}$ is nonnegative on every test function exactly when no zero of $\zeta$ has real part above $\frac12+\varepsilon$, which is Weil's criterion for RH at $\varepsilon=0$, holds with no hypothesis at $\varepsilon=\frac12$, and at $\varepsilon=\frac38$ is equivalent to the half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ announced in October 2026 and not refereed.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function with nontrivial zeros $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ counted with multiplicity, $\gamma_\rho=-i(\rho-\frac12)$, and for $\varepsilon>0$ let $\varrho_\varepsilon(\theta)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\frac12+\varepsilon+i\theta)$, the Poisson smoothing of the zeros. Weil's distribution $D$ acts on an even Lipschitz function $g$ of compact support with $g'$ of bounded variation by $\langle D,g\rangle=\sum_\rho\hat g(\gamma_\rho)$, where $\hat g(t)=\int g(x)e^{itx}\,dx$ (Weil's explicit formula computes this from the gamma factor, the pole of $\zeta$ and the primes), and on a function that is not even through its even part. For a bounded function $h$ of bounded variation and compact support let $\tilde h(x)=\overline{h(-x)}$, so that $h*\tilde h$ is Lipschitz with $\widehat{h*\tilde h}=|\hat h|^2$, and for $\varepsilon\ge0$ put $Q_\varepsilon(h)=\langle D,e^{-\varepsilon|x|}(h*\tilde h)\rangle$, Weil's form damped by $e^{-\varepsilon|x|}$. Call $\varepsilon>0$ to the right of the zeros if $\beta<\frac12+\varepsilon$ for every zero. Let $0\le\varepsilon\le\frac12$. Then $Q_\varepsilon(h)\ge0$ for every $h\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R})$ (real $h$ suffice) if and only if no nontrivial zero of $\zeta$ has $\beta>\frac12+\varepsilon$. When $\varepsilon>0$ is to the right of the zeros, $Q_\varepsilon(h)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}|\hat h(\theta)|^2\varrho_\varepsilon(\theta)\,d\theta$ for every bounded $h$ of bounded variation and compact support. In particular: at $\varepsilon=0$ this is Weil's criterion for the Riemann Hypothesis; at $\varepsilon=\frac12$ it holds with no hypothesis on the zeros; and the zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ announced in October 2026, which has not been refereed, is equivalent to $Q_{3/8}\ge0$.
results.label: dc:thm:damped

results.name: Ladder theorem: least eigenvalue of the damped Weil form on a window
results.status_text: conditional on Parts (a) and (b), for a level $0<\varepsilon<\frac12$: that the closed half plane $\operatorname{Re}s\ge\frac12+\varepsilon$ contains no zero of $\zeta$ (that $\varepsilon$ is to the right of the zeros). This zero free half plane is not proved for any $\varepsilon<\frac12$; the half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ announced in October 2026 and not refereed would give it for $\varepsilon>\frac38$ only.; Parts (a) and (b), for a level $0<\varepsilon<\frac12$: that $v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(\theta)>v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(0)$ for every real $\theta\ne0$ and $v_{1/2+\varepsilon}''(0)>0$, that is, that the Thorin density has a strict, nondegenerate global minimum at the origin. The book certifies this only up to a finite height, and the strict minimum at the origin on every line $\frac12<\alpha<1$ at once is equivalent to RH.; Parts (a) and (b), for a level $0<\varepsilon<\frac12$: that $\liminf_{|\theta|\to\infty}v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(\theta)>v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(0)$, that is, that the minimum is not approached at infinity. This is not known for $0<\varepsilon<\frac12$ without RH, under which it holds.; Part (c), first half (the nonnegativity and the decay of $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12,a)$): the Riemann Hypothesis. All hypotheses of (a) and (b) hold at $\varepsilon=\frac12$ with no assumption on the zeros, and the second half of (c), the negativity for large $a$ if RH fails, needs no hypothesis. For $\varepsilon>\frac12$ the chapter does not discuss whether the hypotheses on $v_{1/2+\varepsilon}$ hold
results.conditions: Parts (a) and (b), for a level $0<\varepsilon<\frac12$: that the closed half plane $\operatorname{Re}s\ge\frac12+\varepsilon$ contains no zero of $\zeta$ (that $\varepsilon$ is to the right of the zeros). This zero free half plane is not proved for any $\varepsilon<\frac12$; the half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ announced in October 2026 and not refereed would give it for $\varepsilon>\frac38$ only.; Parts (a) and (b), for a level $0<\varepsilon<\frac12$: that $v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(\theta)>v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(0)$ for every real $\theta\ne0$ and $v_{1/2+\varepsilon}''(0)>0$, that is, that the Thorin density has a strict, nondegenerate global minimum at the origin. The book certifies this only up to a finite height, and the strict minimum at the origin on every line $\frac12<\alpha<1$ at once is equivalent to RH.; Parts (a) and (b), for a level $0<\varepsilon<\frac12$: that $\liminf_{|\theta|\to\infty}v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(\theta)>v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(0)$, that is, that the minimum is not approached at infinity. This is not known for $0<\varepsilon<\frac12$ without RH, under which it holds.; Part (c), first half (the nonnegativity and the decay of $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12,a)$): the Riemann Hypothesis. All hypotheses of (a) and (b) hold at $\varepsilon=\frac12$ with no assumption on the zeros, and the second half of (c), the negativity for large $a$ if RH fails, needs no hypothesis. For $\varepsilon>\frac12$ the chapter does not discuss whether the hypotheses on $v_{1/2+\varepsilon}$ hold.
results.summary: At a level $\frac12+\varepsilon$ to the right of the zeros where the Thorin density has a strict, nondegenerate global minimum at the origin not approached at infinity (true at $\varepsilon=\frac12$, an assumption below it), the least eigenvalue of Weil's form damped by $e^{-\varepsilon|x|}$ on test functions supported in $[-a,a]$ decreases to $2\xi'/\xi(\frac12+\varepsilon)$ at a rate between $c/a^2$ and $(\pi^2v''(0)/4+o(1))/a^2$, with $v(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\frac12+\varepsilon+i\theta)$, while at $\varepsilon=0$, under RH, it is nonnegative and $O(a^{-N})$ for every $N$, and if RH fails it is negative for all large $a$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function with nontrivial zeros $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ counted with multiplicity and $\gamma_\rho=-i(\rho-\frac12)$. For real $\alpha$ and $\theta$ put $v_\alpha(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\alpha+i\theta)$ and $b_\alpha=v_\alpha(0)=\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\alpha)$. Weil's distribution $D$ acts on an even Lipschitz function $g$ of compact support with $g'$ of bounded variation by $\langle D,g\rangle=\sum_\rho\hat g(\gamma_\rho)$, where $\hat g(t)=\int g(x)e^{itx}\,dx$ (Weil's explicit formula computes this from the gamma factor, the pole of $\zeta$ and the primes). For a bounded real function $h$ of bounded variation and compact support let $\tilde h(x)=h(-x)$ and, for $\varepsilon\ge0$, $Q_\varepsilon(h)=\langle D,e^{-\varepsilon|x|}(h*\tilde h)\rangle$; for $a>0$ let $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12+\varepsilon,a)$ be the infimum of $Q_\varepsilon(h)/\|h\|_2^2$ over all such $h\ne0$ supported in $[-a,a]$ (only the prime powers $n\le e^{2a}$ enter $Q_\varepsilon(h)$ for these $h$). Let $\varepsilon>0$ be to the right of the zeros, that is, $\beta<\frac12+\varepsilon$ for every zero, and suppose that $v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(\theta)>v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(0)$ for every $\theta\ne0$ (a strict global minimum at the origin), that $v_{1/2+\varepsilon}''(0)>0$ (nondegenerate), and that $\liminf_{|\theta|\to\infty}v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(\theta)>v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(0)$ (not approached at infinity). Then: (a) $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12+\varepsilon,a)$ is nonincreasing in $a$, and $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12+\varepsilon,a)\ge2b_{1/2+\varepsilon}>0$ for every $a>0$; (b) $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12+\varepsilon,a)\to2b_{1/2+\varepsilon}$ as $a\to\infty$, and there are constants $c,a_0>0$ such that for all $a\ge a_0$, $\frac c{a^2}\le\lambda_{\min}(\frac12+\varepsilon,a)-2b_{1/2+\varepsilon}\le\frac{\pi^2v_{1/2+\varepsilon}''(0)/4+o(1)}{a^2}$, where $o(1)\to0$ as $a\to\infty$; (c) at $\varepsilon=0$, with none of the hypotheses above: if the Riemann Hypothesis holds, then $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12,a)\ge0$ for every $a$ and, for every $N$, $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12,a)=O(a^{-N})$ as $a\to\infty$, so that $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12,a)\to0$; if the Riemann Hypothesis fails, then $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12,a)<0$ for all large $a$.
results.label: dc:thm:ladder

results.name: Certified rungs of the ladder
results.summary: Certify in interval arithmetic that the least eigenvalue of Weil's damped form on test functions supported in $[-4,4]$ is positive at $\varepsilon=0.05$, $0.1$, $0.2$ and $0.375$, and find how far in the window a certificate can be pushed.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function with zeros $\rho$ and $\gamma_\rho=-i(\rho-\frac12)$. Weil's distribution $D$ acts on an even Lipschitz function $g$ of compact support with $g'$ of bounded variation by $\langle D,g\rangle=\sum_\rho\hat g(\gamma_\rho)$, $\hat g(t)=\int g(x)e^{itx}\,dx$ (Weil's explicit formula computes this from the gamma factor, the pole and the primes). For bounded real $h$ of bounded variation and compact support let $\tilde h(x)=h(-x)$ and $Q_\varepsilon(h)=\langle D,e^{-\varepsilon|x|}(h*\tilde h)\rangle$, and for $a>0$ let $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12+\varepsilon,a)$ be the infimum of $Q_\varepsilon(h)/\|h\|_2^2$ over all such $h\ne0$ supported in $[-a,a]$. Certify, in interval arithmetic, that $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12+\varepsilon,a)>0$ for $\varepsilon\in\{0.05,0.1,0.2,0.375\}$ and $a=4$, which by monotonicity in $a$ covers every $a\le4$, and determine how far in $a$ a certificate can be pushed at fixed $\varepsilon$. Each certificate would be unconditional, and at $\varepsilon=\frac38$ it would agree with what the announced zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ gives, namely $\lambda_{\min}\ge0$, and could be checked independently of it. Certifying one rung needs a lower bound for the bottom of the spectrum, not the variational upper bounds and extrapolated values the book computes; the book has not done this.
results.label: dc:prob:cert

results.name: The exact rate of the ladder
results.summary: Prove that the scaled excess of the least eigenvalue of the damped Weil form over its limit tends to the upper constant $\pi^2v''(0)/4$ of the ladder theorem, and find the next term; numerical fits are consistent with the limit and with a positive correction of order $1/a$, and neither is proved.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function with zeros $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ and $\gamma_\rho=-i(\rho-\frac12)$, and put $v_\alpha(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\alpha+i\theta)$ and $b_\alpha=v_\alpha(0)=\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\alpha)$. Weil's distribution $D$ acts on an even Lipschitz function $g$ of compact support with $g'$ of bounded variation by $\langle D,g\rangle=\sum_\rho\hat g(\gamma_\rho)$, $\hat g(t)=\int g(x)e^{itx}\,dx$. For bounded real $h$ of bounded variation and compact support let $\tilde h(x)=h(-x)$ and $Q_\varepsilon(h)=\langle D,e^{-\varepsilon|x|}(h*\tilde h)\rangle$, and for $a>0$ let $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12+\varepsilon,a)$ be the infimum of $Q_\varepsilon(h)/\|h\|_2^2$ over all such $h\ne0$ supported in $[-a,a]$. Let $\varepsilon>0$ be to the right of the zeros ($\beta<\frac12+\varepsilon$ for every zero), and suppose that $v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(\theta)>v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(0)$ for every $\theta\ne0$, that $v_{1/2+\varepsilon}''(0)>0$, and that $\liminf_{|\theta|\to\infty}v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(\theta)>v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(0)$. Prove that $a^2\big(\lambda_{\min}(\frac12+\varepsilon,a)-2b_{1/2+\varepsilon}\big)\to\pi^2v_{1/2+\varepsilon}''(0)/4$ as $a\to\infty$, and find the next term. Under these hypotheses the book proves only that this scaled excess is at most $\pi^2v_{1/2+\varepsilon}''(0)/4+o(1)$ and at least a positive constant $c$. The book's numerical fits of converged, extrapolated values are consistent with the limit and with a positive correction of order $1/a$, so that $\pi^2v_{1/2+\varepsilon}''(0)/4$ would not be an upper bound at finite $a$; neither the limit nor the order of the correction is proved.
results.label: dc:prob:rate

results.name: The transition of the ladder at the line
results.summary: Describe the least eigenvalue of the damped Weil form jointly as the window half length $a$ tends to infinity and the depth $\varepsilon$ tends to zero, where the rate is algebraic for fixed $\varepsilon>0$ under the hypotheses of the ladder theorem and faster than any power of $a$ at $\varepsilon=0$ under RH.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function with zeros $\rho$ and $\gamma_\rho=-i(\rho-\frac12)$, and put $b_\alpha=\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\alpha)$ for real $\alpha$ and $V_\xi=(\log\xi)''(\frac12)$. Weil's distribution $D$ acts on an even Lipschitz function $g$ of compact support with $g'$ of bounded variation by $\langle D,g\rangle=\sum_\rho\hat g(\gamma_\rho)$, $\hat g(t)=\int g(x)e^{itx}\,dx$. For bounded real $h$ of bounded variation and compact support let $\tilde h(x)=h(-x)$ and $Q_\varepsilon(h)=\langle D,e^{-\varepsilon|x|}(h*\tilde h)\rangle$, and for $a>0$ let $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12+\varepsilon,a)$ be the infimum of $Q_\varepsilon(h)/\|h\|_2^2$ over all such $h\ne0$ supported in $[-a,a]$. Describe $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12+\varepsilon,a)$ jointly as $a\to\infty$ and $\varepsilon\to0$. For fixed $\varepsilon>0$, under the hypotheses of the ladder theorem (the level $\varepsilon$ to the right of the zeros, and the Thorin density $\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\frac12+\varepsilon+i\theta)$ having a strict, nondegenerate global minimum at $\theta=0$ that is not approached at infinity), the limit is $2b_{1/2+\varepsilon}$, which is at most $2V_\xi\,\varepsilon$ and asymptotic to it as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, and the rate is algebraic; at $\varepsilon=0$, under RH, the decay is faster than any power of $a$. The questions are: on which curves $\varepsilon=\varepsilon(a)\to0$ does $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12+\varepsilon,a)$ stay comparable to $2b_{1/2+\varepsilon}$, and does the crossover occur at $\varepsilon$ of the order of the mean spacing of the zeros at height $e^{2a}$?
results.label: dc:prob:transition

results.name: Uniformity of the damped Weil form from structure
results.summary: Find a structural reason, valid for all windows, why Weil's form damped by $e^{-\varepsilon|x|}$ is nonnegative on test functions supported in $[-a,a]$ for some fixed $\varepsilon<\frac12$, which by the damped Weil criterion would prove the zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac12+\varepsilon$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function with zeros $\rho$ and $\gamma_\rho=-i(\rho-\frac12)$. Weil's distribution $D$ acts on an even Lipschitz function $g$ of compact support with $g'$ of bounded variation by $\langle D,g\rangle=\sum_\rho\hat g(\gamma_\rho)$, $\hat g(t)=\int g(x)e^{itx}\,dx$ (Weil's explicit formula computes this from the gamma factor, the pole and the primes). For bounded real $h$ of bounded variation and compact support let $\tilde h(x)=h(-x)$ and $Q_\varepsilon(h)=\langle D,e^{-\varepsilon|x|}(h*\tilde h)\rangle$. Find a structural reason, valid for all $a$, why $Q_\varepsilon(h)\ge0$ for every such $h$ supported in $[-a,a]$ (that is, $Q_\varepsilon\ge0$ on $L^2[-a,a]$) for some fixed $\varepsilon<\frac12$, using properties of the archimedean and pole terms that dominate the primes up to $e^{2a}$ uniformly in $a$. By the damped Weil criterion, any such argument proves the zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac12+\varepsilon$.
results.label: dc:prob:uniform

results.name: The Thorin measure of reciprocal xi is absolutely continuous with the explicit density (1/pi) Re xi'/xi at every level from one
results.summary: For every level $\theta\ge1$ the measure $\sum_\rho\mathrm{Cauchy}(\gamma_\rho,\theta-\sigma_\rho)$ has real analytic density $\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\theta+iv)$, at $\theta=1$ a gamma part minus a compensated prime sum, valid also at $v=0$.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$, let $\rho=\sigma_\rho+i\gamma_\rho$ run over its zeros with multiplicity, $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function, and for $\theta>\sigma_\rho$ for every $\rho$ (in particular for every $\theta>1$, and also for $\theta=1$ because $\zeta(1+it)\ne0$) let $\mathfrak U_\theta=\sum_\rho\mathrm{Cauchy}(\gamma_\rho,\theta-\sigma_\rho)$ be the positive measure on $\mathbb{R}$ with $\int\mathfrak U_\theta(dv)/(1+v^2)<\infty$, where $\mathrm{Cauchy}(\gamma,c)$ has density $(c/\pi)/(c^2+(v-\gamma)^2)$. Then $\mathfrak U_\theta$ is absolutely continuous with real analytic density $u_\theta(v)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\theta+iv)=\frac1\pi\partial_\sigma\log|\xi(\sigma+iv)|$ at $\sigma=\theta$, and $\mathfrak U_\theta((0,V])=\frac1\pi\arg\xi(\theta+iV)$ for the branch with $\arg\xi(\theta)=0$. At $\theta=1$, for every real $v$, $u_1(v)=\frac1\pi\bigl[\frac1{1+v^2}-\frac{\log\pi}2+\frac12\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Gamma'}{\Gamma}(\frac{1+iv}2)-\lim_{X\to\infty}\bigl(\sum_{n\le X}\frac{\Lambda(n)}n\cos(v\log n)-\frac{\sin(v\log X)}{v}\bigr)\bigr]$, where $\sin(v\log X)/v$ means $\log X$ at $v=0$; the limit exists locally uniformly, equals $\operatorname{Re}C(1+iv)$ with $C(s)=-\zeta'(s)/\zeta(s)-1/(s-1)$, and $u_1(0)=(2+\gamma_E-\log4\pi)/(2\pi)$ with $\gamma_E$ Euler's constant, while the cosine series itself has no limit. For $\theta>1$, $u_\theta(v)=\frac1\pi\bigl[\frac\theta{\theta^2+v^2}+\frac{\theta-1}{(\theta-1)^2+v^2}-\frac{\log\pi}2+\frac12\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Gamma'}{\Gamma}(\frac{\theta+iv}2)-\sum_{n\ge2}\Lambda(n)n^{-\theta}\cos(v\log n)\bigr]$ with the prime sum absolutely convergent.
results.label: lo:thm:density

results.name: The Fourier transform of the level one Thorin measure carries the prime powers as atoms, an explicit formula for one test function
results.summary: As tempered distributions $\widehat{\mathfrak U_1}$ is the transform of the smooth part plus $1$ minus point masses $\Lambda(n)/n$ at $\pm\log n$, equal on the zero side to $\sum_\rho e^{-(1-\sigma_\rho)|\omega|}e^{-i\omega\gamma_\rho}$, which is a Weil type explicit formula.
results.statement: With $\mathfrak U_1=\sum_\rho\mathrm{Cauchy}(\gamma_\rho,1-\sigma_\rho)$ the level one Thorin measure of $\xi$ (zeros $\rho=\sigma_\rho+i\gamma_\rho$), $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function, $P_c(v)=(c/\pi)/(c^2+v^2)$, $\widehat f(\omega)=\int e^{-i\omega v}f(v)\,dv$, and for $\theta\ge1$ $g_\theta(v)=\frac1\pi[\theta/(\theta^2+v^2)-\frac12\log\pi+\frac12\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Gamma'}\Gamma(\frac{\theta+iv}2)]$: as tempered distributions $\widehat{\mathfrak U_1}(\omega)=\widehat{g_1}(\omega)+1-\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\Lambda(n)}n(\delta_{\log n}+\delta_{-\log n})(\omega)$, the constant $1$ being the transform of the atom at $0$ that the pole of $\zeta$ contributes in the limit $\theta\downarrow1$, and on the zero side $\widehat{\mathfrak U_1}(\omega)=\sum_\rho e^{-(1-\sigma_\rho)|\omega|}e^{-i\omega\gamma_\rho}$ as the limit of the sums over $|\gamma_\rho|<T$. Equivalently, for every Schwartz function $\varphi$, $\sum_\rho(P_{1-\sigma_\rho}*\varphi)(\gamma_\rho)=\int g_1\varphi\,dv+\varphi(0)-\frac1{2\pi}\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\Lambda(n)}n(\widehat\varphi(\log n)+\widehat\varphi(-\log n))$. For $\theta\ge1$, $\mathfrak U_\theta=P_{\theta-1}*\mathfrak U_1$ and $\widehat{\mathfrak U_\theta}(\omega)=e^{-(\theta-1)|\omega|}\widehat{\mathfrak U_1}(\omega)$, which replaces $\Lambda(n)/n$ by $\Lambda(n)n^{-\theta}$ on the prime side.
results.label: lo:prop:spectrum

results.name: Dichotomy for the band limited backward Cauchy flow from level one: convergence at level theta' if and only if zeta has no zeros to the right of theta'
results.summary: The Fejér band limited backward flow from the level one measure converges to the level $\theta'$ Thorin measure if $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta'$, and has no measure limit if it has a zero there, so the Riemann hypothesis is convergence at every $\theta'>\frac12$.
results.statement: Let $\frac12\le\theta'<1$, $a=1-\theta'$, $\mathfrak U_\theta=\sum_\rho\mathrm{Cauchy}(\gamma_\rho,\theta-\sigma_\rho)$ the Thorin measure at level $\theta$ of $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$, over its zeros $\rho=\sigma_\rho+i\gamma_\rho$ with multiplicity ($\mathrm{Cauchy}(\gamma,c)$ the Cauchy law of centre $\gamma$ and width $c$, $\mathrm{Cauchy}(\gamma,0)=\delta_\gamma$), $\Phi_\Omega(v)=(1-\cos\Omega v)/(\pi\Omega v^2)$ the Fejér kernel, and $K_{\theta',\Omega}$ the inverse Fourier transform of $(1-|\omega|/\Omega)_+e^{a|\omega|}$. The band limited backward flow is $B_{\theta',\Omega}\mathfrak U_1=\mathfrak U_1*K_{\theta',\Omega}$. (i) If $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta'$, then $B_{\theta',\Omega}\mathfrak U_1=\mathfrak U_{\theta'}*\Phi_\Omega$, which converges vaguely to $\mathfrak U_{\theta'}$ as $\Omega\to\infty$, with $\int B_{\theta',\Omega}\mathfrak U_1(v)\,dv/(v^2+s)\to\int\mathfrak U_{\theta'}(dv)/(v^2+s)$ for every $s>0$; if moreover $\theta'>\sigma_\rho$ for every zero the convergence is locally uniform as densities. (ii) If $\zeta$ has a zero $\rho$ with $\sigma_\rho>\theta'$, there is no signed measure $\mu$ with $\int|\mu|(dv)/(1+v^2)<\infty$ such that $\int B_{\theta',\Omega}\mathfrak U_1(v)\,dv/(v^2+s)\to\int\mu(dv)/(v^2+s)$ as $\Omega\to\infty$ for all large $s$. Hence the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to convergence of the flow at every $\theta'>\frac12$.
results.label: lo:thm:dichotomy

results.name: Computation: the Fourier backward flow from samples of the level one density on Re s = 1 places a peak within 0.035 of each of 109 zeros
results.summary: A the Arb library (python flint) computation, not a theorem, samples $u_1$ on $[0,400]$ from $\zeta$ and $\zeta'$ on $\operatorname{Re}s=1$ only and shows peaks within $0.035$ of the $109$ zeros in $100<v<300$ at $\theta'=\frac34$ and within $0.027$ at $\theta'=\frac12$; the sharp cutoff rings and the Fejér window does not.
