results.statement: The computation samples the level one Thorin density $u_1(v)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(1+iv)$, $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$, on $[0,400]$ at spacing $0.05$ from $\zeta$ and $\zeta'$ on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=1$ only (the Arb library (python flint) balls at $128$ bits, with the analytic value of $u_1(0)$), applies a Hann window and the backward multiplier $e^{(1-\theta')|\omega|}$ with a cutoff at $\Omega$, and inverts. A peak is a local maximum of the output in $100<v<300$ of height at least a quarter of the maximum, and the $109$ zeros of $\zeta$ in that range are those counted by $N(300)-N(100)=138-29$. With a sharp cutoff the output at $\theta'=0.75$, $\Omega=40$ has $109$ peaks, each within $0.035$ of a zero, and is positive; at $\theta'=0.5$, $\Omega=40$ it has $109$ peaks within $0.027$ of the zeros and minimum $-3.2$; at $\theta'=0.5$, $\Omega=60$ it has $213$ peaks, $109$ at the zeros, error $0.042$ and minimum $-16.5$, which is ringing of the cutoff. With the Fejér window at $\theta'=0.5$, $\Omega=60$ it has $109$ peaks, error $0.025$ and minimum $-0.020$. The statement covers only these runs, and the sharp cutoff is not covered by the convergence theorem for the backward flow.
results.label: lo:res:flow

results.name: A positive solution of the Cauchy deconvolution of the level one density exists exactly when zeta has the zero free half plane, and the total Kullback Leibler residual detects it
results.summary: A positive measure $x$ with $P_{1-\theta'}*x=u_1$ exists iff $\zeta\ne0$ on $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta'$ (then $x=\mathfrak U_{\theta'}$), and the total discretised residual tends to $0$ in that case and stays bounded away from $0$ otherwise.
results.statement: Let $\theta'\in[\frac12,1)$, $a=1-\theta'$, $P_a(v)=(a/\pi)/(a^2+v^2)$, $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ with zeros $\rho=\sigma_\rho+i\gamma_\rho$, $\mathfrak U_\theta=\sum_\rho\mathrm{Cauchy}(\gamma_\rho,\theta-\sigma_\rho)$ its Thorin measure at level $\theta$ (defined when no zero has $\sigma_\rho>\theta$; $\mathrm{Cauchy}(\gamma,0)=\delta_\gamma$), and $u_1(v)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(1+iv)$ the density of $\mathfrak U_1$. (a) There is a positive measure $x$ on $\mathbb{R}$ with $\int x(dv)/(1+v^2)<\infty$ and $P_a*x=u_1$ if and only if $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta'$; it is then unique and equals $\mathfrak U_{\theta'}$. (b) Let $h_k\to0$ and $L_k\to\infty$ with $h_k^2L_k\log L_k\to0$, let $v_i\in h_k\mathbb{Z}\cap[-L_k,L_k]$, $y_i=u_1(v_i)$, and $D_k=\inf_xh_k\sum_i\bigl(y_i\log\frac{y_i}{m_i(x)}-y_i+m_i(x)\bigr)$, with the infimum over positive measures $x$ on the grid $h_k\mathbb{Z}$ with $\sum_jx_j/(1+j^2h_k^2)<\infty$ and $m_i(x)=(P_a*x)(v_i)$. Then $D_k\to0$ if $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta'$, and $\liminf_kD_k>0$ if it has one.
results.label: lo:prop:emres

results.name: Computation: the EM inversion of the level one density separates an injected off line quartet of zeros from a control
results.summary: EM runs of $10^4$ steps on windows of $u_1$ with two consecutive zeros replaced by a quartet at real part $\sigma$ show a residual floor near $7\times10^{-3}$ for $\theta'=0.75$, $\sigma=0.85$ against below $10^{-7}$ for a control, and slower decay than the control, without a floor in $10^4$ steps, for $\sigma=\theta'=0.75$ and for $\theta'=0.5$, $\sigma=0.75$; a finite run certifies neither alternative.
results.statement: The computation runs the EM iteration for the Cauchy deconvolution of the level one Thorin density $u_1(v)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(1+iv)$ of $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ on the data window $[100,300]$ (unknown on $[80,320]$, spacing $0.05$) and on $[150,250]$, with the total Kullback Leibler residual as the plain sum over the data points. The two zeros nearest the centre of the window ($\gamma=198.0153$ and $201.2648$) are replaced by a quartet $\rho,1-\bar\rho,\bar\rho,1-\rho$ with real part $\sigma$ at their midpoint, total mass kept to $10^{-4}$, and compared with a control of two line zeros at the midpoint. At $\theta'=0.75$, $\sigma=0.85$ the quartet residual after $10^4$ steps is $7.03\times10^{-3}$ on both windows to $0.3$ per cent, a floor, while the control and the real data fall below $10^{-7}$. At $\theta'=0.5$, $\sigma=0.75$ the quartet residual is $1.85\times10^{-2}$ against $1.08\times10^{-3}$ for the control and has not reached a floor. At $\theta'=0.75=\sigma$ the residual keeps decaying, more slowly than the control. The statement covers only these runs: a finite run certifies neither the existence nor the nonexistence of a positive solution.
results.label: lo:res:inject

results.name: Computation: generative Bayesian computation under a GUE prior counts the zeros of zeta in unit bins from the level one Thorin density
results.summary: A computation, not a theorem: a quantile network trained on GUE simulations of the level one density gives rounded posterior median counts equal to the true number of zeros in 196 and 197 of 200 unit bins for two seeds, within one in all, with quantiles calibrated to about 0.05.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ and $u_1(v)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(1+iv)$ its level one Thorin density. The computation trains, for two seeds, a quantile network (two hidden layers of $256$ rectified units, pinball loss, quantile levels $0.1$, $0.5$, $0.9$) on $24000$ simulated windows in which the ordinates of the zeros are eigenvalues of a GUE matrix of size $400$ unfolded to a density drawn uniformly from $[0.45,0.8]$, all zeros on the critical line; the input is the sum of Cauchy densities of width $\frac12$ at the simulated ordinates on a grid of spacing $0.1$, plus the Cauchy smoothing of the mean density for the zeros beyond, and the targets are the counts of zeros in eight unit bins at the centre of a window of length $16$. On the $25$ windows of the real $u_1$ centred at $v=150,158,\dots,342$ ($200$ bins) the rounded posterior median equals the true count in $196$ and $197$ bins and is within one of it in all $200$; on held out simulations the interval $[q_{0.1},q_{0.9}]$ covers $0.806$ and $0.796$ of the counts (nominal $0.8$), and $0.805$ and $0.775$ on the real windows. The formulation is heuristic and the statement covers only these runs: the prior puts every zero on the critical line, and the network counts zeros in bins and does not locate them.
results.label: lo:res:gbc

results.name: Open problem: the data augmentation sampler and a generative Bayesian inversion with the EM reconstruction as a feature
results.summary: Run the data augmentation sampler for the real level one density, compare its posterior spread at $\theta'=0.75$ and $0.5$ with the EM estimate, and build a calibrated GBC inversion with zero positions as continuous outputs.
results.statement: Let $u_1(v)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(1+iv)$ be the level one Thorin density of $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$. Implement a data augmentation Gibbs sampler for the Cauchy deconvolution of $u_1$ and compare its posterior spread at $\theta'=0.75$ and $\theta'=0.5$ with the EM point estimate; then build a generative Bayesian computation inversion with the EM reconstruction as an input feature and the positions of the zeros as continuous outputs, and calibrate its quantiles on held out simulations.
results.label: lo:prob:sampler

results.name: Open problem: characterise the level one Thorin densities of functions of the Selberg class without reference to zeros
results.summary: Which densities of the form of the level one prime formula with coefficients $a_n\ge0$ on prime powers are level one Thorin densities of $\Xi(1)/\Xi(1+\sqrt s)$ with $\Xi$ in the Selberg class?
results.statement: Characterise, without reference to zeros, the functions $\frac1\pi[g(v)-\lim_{X\to\infty}(\sum_{n\le X}a_n\cos(v\log n)-\sin(v\log X)/v)]$ with $a_n\ge0$ supported on prime powers and $g$ a smooth gamma part that are the Thorin densities at level one of a function $\Xi(1)/\Xi(1+\sqrt s)$ with $\Xi$ in the Selberg class. The Thorin conditions constrain the growth and the integrability near $0$ but say nothing about the arithmetic of the $a_n$. The Selberg class needs the completed function, the gamma factors, the conductor, the poles and the sign of the coefficients of $-L'/L$ to be specified.
results.label: lo:prob:selberg

results.name: Open problem: the rate of convergence of the backward flow and the exponential growth lower bound when a zero lies to the right
results.summary: Give the rate of locally uniform convergence of the band limited backward flow in $\Omega$ and $\theta'-\theta_0$, and show growth like $e^{(\sigma_{\max}-\theta')\Omega}$ up to polynomial factors when a zero lies to the right of $\theta'$.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ have zeros $\rho=\sigma_\rho+i\gamma_\rho$, $\theta_0=\sup_\rho\sigma_\rho$, $\mathfrak U_\theta=\sum_\rho\mathrm{Cauchy}(\gamma_\rho,\theta-\sigma_\rho)$ its Thorin measure at level $\theta$, and $B_{\theta',\Omega}\mathfrak U_1=\mathfrak U_1*K_{\theta',\Omega}$ the band limited backward flow, $K_{\theta',\Omega}$ the inverse Fourier transform of $(1-|\omega|/\Omega)_+e^{(1-\theta')|\omega|}$. For $\theta'\in(\theta_0,1)$ give the rate of locally uniform convergence of $B_{\theta',\Omega}\mathfrak U_1$ to $\mathfrak U_{\theta'}$ in terms of $\Omega$ and $\theta'-\theta_0$, and, when $\sigma_{\max}=\sup\sigma_\rho>\theta'$ is attained by a zero, show that $\sup_{|v|\le V}|B_{\theta',\Omega}\mathfrak U_1(v)|$ grows like $e^{(\sigma_{\max}-\theta')\Omega}$ up to polynomial factors. For one zero with $d=\sigma-\theta'>0$ the Fejér inverse at distance $t$ from its ordinate is $(\pi\Omega)^{-1}\operatorname{Re}[(e^{z\Omega}-1-z\Omega)/z^2]$ with $z=d+it$, asymptotic to $e^{d\Omega}/(\pi d^2\Omega)$ at $t=0$; with infinitely many zeros the supremum need not be attained and the cancellations are part of the problem.
results.label: lo:prob:rate

results.name: Open problem: a prior allowing off line zeros and the posterior of the offset delta at the real level one density
results.summary: Replace the GUE prior of the generative Bayesian inversion by one allowing zero pairs at $\frac12\pm\delta+i\gamma$ and train the quantile network to report the posterior of $\delta$ for each detected zero.
results.statement: Replace the GUE prior for the zeros in the generative Bayesian computation inversion of the level one Thorin density $u_1(v)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(1+iv)$ of $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ by a prior that allows a fraction of the zeros off the critical line, for instance pairs at $\frac12\pm\delta+i\gamma$ with $\delta$ drawn from a prior on $[0,\frac12)$, and train the quantile network to report the posterior of $\delta$ for each detected zero. The posterior of $\delta$ at the real $u_1$ is then a window by window numerical diagnostic at the resolution the data allow, conditional on the prior, and not a certificate.
results.label: lo:prob:delta

results.name: One sided approach in the Dyck chain: the criterion implies RH, and conditionally on the lattice bias conjecture it fails for T above gamma 64
results.status_text: conditional on The lattice bias conjecture, that $F_n(s)=2\xi(s)-\frac{3s}{\sqrt{\pi n}}\xi(s-1)+O(1/n)$ locally uniformly on $\operatorname{Re}s>0$ (for the failure of the hypothesis)
results.conditions: The lattice bias conjecture, that $F_n(s)=2\xi(s)-\frac{3s}{\sqrt{\pi n}}\xi(s-1)+O(1/n)$ locally uniformly on $\operatorname{Re}s>0$ (for the failure of the hypothesis)
results.summary: If the Dirichlet polynomial of the Dyck chain converges to $2\xi$ locally uniformly on $\operatorname{Re}s>0$ and has no zero in $\frac12<\operatorname{Re}s<1$, $0<\operatorname{Im}s<T$ for large $n$ for every $T$, then RH holds (proved); under the lattice bias conjecture the zero free hypothesis holds for $T<\gamma_{64}$ and fails for every $T>\gamma_{64}$, so this criterion cannot prove RH along this chain.
results.statement: Let $H_n$ be the height of a uniform Dyck path of length $2n$, $Y_n=\sqrt{2/\pi}\,H_n/\sqrt{2n}$, $F_n(s)=\mathbb{E}Y_n^s$ (a Dirichlet polynomial), $\xi$ the Riemann xi function, and $\rho_k=\frac12+i\gamma_k$ the zeros of $\xi$ on the critical line in order of height, with $\gamma_{64}=169.9119\ldots$. (1) Proved: if $F_n\to2\xi$ locally uniformly on $\operatorname{Re}s>0$ and, for every $T>0$, $F_n$ has no zero in $\frac12<\operatorname{Re}s<1$, $0<\operatorname{Im}s<T$ for all large $n$, then the Riemann Hypothesis holds: if it fails, the functional equation and the symmetry $\xi(\bar s)=\overline{\xi(s)}$ give a zero $\rho$ of $\xi$ with $\frac12<\operatorname{Re}\rho<1$ and $\operatorname{Im}\rho>0$, and by Hurwitz's theorem, for $T>\operatorname{Im}\rho$, $F_n$ has zeros in that rectangle for all large $n$. (2) Conditional on the conjecture that, uniformly on compact subsets of $\operatorname{Re}s>0$, $F_n(s)=2\xi(s)-\frac{3s}{\sqrt{\pi n}}\xi(s-1)+O(1/n)$: the zero free hypothesis holds for $T<\gamma_{64}$ and fails for every $T>\gamma_{64}$. The zeros of $\xi$ below height $170$ are $\rho_1,\dots,\rho_{64}$, simple and on the line. For $T>\gamma_{64}$ the zero $z_n(\rho_{64})$ of $F_n$ near $\rho_{64}$ tends to $\rho_{64}$ and has real part $\frac12+\delta_n\operatorname{Re}c_{\rm D}(\rho_{64})+O(1/n)>\frac12$ for large $n$, with $\delta_n=3/(2\sqrt{2n})$ and $c_{\rm D}(\rho)=\sqrt{2/\pi}\,\rho\,\xi(\rho-1)/\xi'(\rho)$, since $\operatorname{Re}c_{\rm D}(\rho_{64})>53.08$ (computed in ball arithmetic). For $T<\gamma_{64}$, $F_n\to2\xi$ uniformly on the closed rectangle, and the only zeros of $F_n$ near $\rho_1,\dots,\rho_{63}$ are to the left of the line for large $n$ because $\operatorname{Re}c_{\rm D}(\rho_k)<0$ (computed in ball arithmetic). So conditionally on the conjecture the hypothesis fails, and this criterion of one sided approach cannot prove RH along this chain. For $10^5\le n\le10^8$ the zero near $\rho_{64}$ lies to the right of the line (computed). Open: prove the conjecture, which would also give the locally uniform convergence of the first hypothesis. The implication and the argument are from notes of Nicholas Polson merged into the book.
results.label: ev:res:dyckside

results.name: Log concavity of the Poisson likelihood and of the gamma prior posterior in the discretised Cauchy deconvolution
results.summary: The Poisson log likelihood of $y=Ax$ is concave on the orthant, and with independent gamma priors of shapes at least one the posterior is log concave.
results.statement: Let $A$ be a matrix with positive entries, $y$ a vector of nonnegative data, and $\ell(x)=\sum_i\bigl(y_i\log(Ax)_i-(Ax)_i\bigr)$ the Poisson log likelihood on the open orthant $x>0$. Then $\ell$ is concave. With independent gamma priors $x_j\sim\mathrm{Gamma}(\alpha_j,\beta_j)$, $\alpha_j\ge1$, the posterior density $\pi(x)\propto e^{\ell(x)}\prod_jx_j^{\alpha_j-1}e^{-\beta_jx_j}$ is log concave on the orthant. In the discretised deconvolution of the book, $A_{ij}=hP_{1-\theta'}(v_i-w_j)$ with $P_a$ the Cauchy density of scale $a$. The sampling clause of the chapter (sampling to total variation accuracy $\varepsilon$ in polynomial time for a log concave density, by a theorem of Applegate, Kannan and Polson) is cited and needs a bound on a ratio of radii that is not proved.
results.label: cx:thm:logconcave

results.name: The level one data must be supplied to absolute precision e to the minus (1 minus theta') Omega for the linear inverse
results.summary: Resolving the Thorin measure at level $\theta'$ up to frequency $\Omega$ by the linear inverse needs the density $u_1$ to absolute precision $e^{-(1-\theta')\Omega}$, which is sharp.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the Riemann xi function, $u_1(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(1+iv)$ the level one density, $\theta'\in[\frac12,1)$ and let the Thorin measure at level $\theta'$ be recovered from $u_1$ by inverting the convolution with the Cauchy density of scale $1-\theta'$, whose Fourier transform is $e^{-(1-\theta')|\omega|}$. Let $\Omega$ be the largest frequency to be resolved. Then for the linear inverse the level one data must be supplied to absolute precision $e^{-(1-\theta')\Omega}$ on the scale of $u_1$, that is, to $(1-\theta')\Omega/\log 2$ binary digits, and this is sharp: an error of size $\delta$ at frequency $\omega$ in the Fourier transform of $u_1$ produces an error of size $\delta e^{(1-\theta')|\omega|}$ in the inverted measure.
results.label: cx:prop:precision

results.name: What EM computes for the backward Cauchy flow: the Thorin measure at level theta' when zeta has no zeros to the right of theta'
results.summary: Under three growth conditions on the grids, the EM limits converge vaguely to the Thorin measure at level $\theta'$ with residual tending to zero if $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta'$, and the residual stays bounded away from zero if it has one.
results.statement: Let $\frac12\le\theta'<1$, $a=1-\theta'$, $\xi$ the Riemann xi function and $u_1(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(1+iv)$. For a grid of spacing $h$ with data points $v_i=ih$, $|i|\le M$, in the window $[-V,V]$ and unknown points $w_j=jh$, $|j|\le N$, in the window $[-W,W]$, $W>V$, let $A_{ij}=hP_a(v_i-w_j)$ with $P_a(x)=(a/\pi)/(a^2+x^2)$, $y_i=u_1(v_i)$, $R_h(x)=h\sum_{|i|\le M}\bigl(y_i\log\frac{y_i}{(Ax)_i}-y_i+(Ax)_i\bigr)$, $R_h^*=\min_{x\ge0}R_h(x)$, let $x_h$ be any minimiser (for instance the limit of EM from a positive start) and $\mu_h=\sum_jx_{h,j}h\,\delta_{w_j}$. Consider grids with $h\to0$ and $V\to\infty$. (a) If $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta'$ and $(\log W)^2/(W-V)\to0$, $(W-V)^2\log V/V^2\to0$ and $h^2V\log^2V\to0$, then $R_h^*\to0$ and $\mu_h$ converges vaguely to the Thorin measure $\mathfrak U_{\theta'}$, whose density is $\sum_\rho P_{\theta'-\operatorname{Re}\rho}(v-\operatorname{Im}\rho)$ over the zeros $\rho$ of $\xi$ with multiplicity, with $P_0$ read as the unit point mass. (b) If $\zeta$ has a zero of real part greater than $\theta'$, then $\liminf R_h^*>0$, whatever the choice of $W>V$.
results.label: cx:prop:what

results.name: The von Neumann and Ulam Monte Carlo estimator for the backward Cauchy flow has infinite variance for small grid spacing
results.summary: For $t=h/(\pi(1-\theta'))<t_0=0.52219\ldots$ the operator $|I-A|$ has spectral radius above one and the estimator of the Neumann series $\sum_k(I-A)^ky$ has infinite second moment from every starting state; for $t>t_0$ the radius is below one.
results.statement: Let $\theta'\in[\frac12,1)$, let $A$ be the square section of order $2N+1$ of the Toeplitz matrix $A_{ij}=hP_{1-\theta'}((i-j)h)$ with $P_a(x)=(a/\pi)/(a^2+x^2)$, and let $t=h/(\pi(1-\theta'))$. Let $t_0=0.52219\ldots$ be the root in $(0,1)$ of $\coth(1/t)=2t$. If $t<t_0$, in particular if $h<\pi(1-\theta')/2$, the bi infinite operator $|I-A|$ has spectral radius $1-2t+\coth(1/t)>1$, and so do its sections for all $N\ge N_0(h,\theta')$. For such a section consider the von Neumann and Ulam estimator of $\sum_{k\ge0}(I-A)^ky$: at state $j$ it stops with probability $q_j\in(0,1)$ and otherwise moves to $k$ with probability $(1-q_j)p_{jk}$, $p_{jk}>0$ wherever $(I-A)_{jk}\ne0$, and it returns the product of the weights $(I-A)_{jk}/((1-q_j)p_{jk})$ along the path times $y_j/q_j$ at the stopping state $j$. Its second moment is infinite from every starting state. If $t_0<t\le1$ the spectral radius of $|I-A|$ is below one for the bi infinite operator and all its sections, and the conclusion fails for the choice $q_j=1-r_j$, $p_{jk}=|(I-A)_{jk}|/r_j$ with $r_j$ the row sums of $|I-A|$.
results.label: cx:prop:vnvar

results.name: Subordinated heat trace: the Thorin measure at level theta is the heat flow of the zeros run to first passage times of Brownian motion
results.summary: The Cauchy law is a Gaussian scale mixture over the first passage time of Brownian motion, so if $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta_0$ the Thorin measure at level $\theta>\theta_0$ is the sum over the nontrivial zeros of the heat flow of $\delta_{\gamma_\rho}$ run to the random time $T_{\theta-\sigma_\rho}$.
results.statement: Let $T_a$ be the first passage time to level $a>0$ of a Brownian motion, with density $\ell_a(t)=a(2\pi)^{-1/2}t^{-3/2}e^{-a^2/(2t)}$. Then $\frac{a/\pi}{a^2+(v-\gamma)^2}=\int_0^\infty\frac{e^{-(v-\gamma)^2/(2t)}}{\sqrt{2\pi t}}\ell_a(t)\,dt$, so $\gamma+B(T_a)$ has the Cauchy law of centre $\gamma$ and scale $a$ for an independent Brownian motion $B$, and $e^{-a|\omega|}=\int_0^\infty e^{-t\omega^2/2}\ell_a(t)\,dt$. Consequently, if $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta_0$ and $\theta>\theta_0$, the Thorin measure $\mathfrak U_\theta$, with density $\sum_\rho P_{\theta-\sigma_\rho}(v-\gamma_\rho)$ over the nontrivial zeros $\rho=\sigma_\rho+i\gamma_\rho$ of $\zeta$ with multiplicity and $P_a(x)=(a/\pi)/(a^2+x^2)$, equals $\sum_\rho\int_0^\infty(e^{t\Delta/2}\delta_{\gamma_\rho})\,\ell_{\theta-\sigma_\rho}(t)\,dt$, the sum over the nontrivial zeros of the heat flow of $\delta_{\gamma_\rho}$ run to the random time $T_{\theta-\sigma_\rho}$. Under the Riemann hypothesis it is the heat flow of $\sum_\rho\delta_{\gamma_\rho}$ to the single random time $T_{\theta-1/2}$.
results.label: cx:prop:subord

results.name: The reciprocal xi transform at level theta is a GGC if and only if zeta has no zeros right of theta, if and only if the real part of xi'/xi is positive there
results.summary: For $\frac12\le\theta<1$: $F_\theta(s)=\xi(\theta)/\xi(\theta+\sqrt s)$ is a GGC Laplace transform if and only if $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta$, if and only if $\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)>0$ on $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta$; for $\theta=\frac12$ the last equivalence is Lagarias's theorem.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the Riemann xi function and, for $\frac12\le\theta<1$, $F_\theta(s)=\xi(\theta)/\xi(\theta+\sqrt s)$ on the plane cut along $(-\infty,0]$ with the principal square root. A generalised gamma convolution (GGC) has Laplace transform $\exp(-as-\int_0^\infty\log(1+s/u)U(du))$ with $a\ge0$ and a positive Thorin measure $U$. For $\frac12\le\theta<1$ the following are equivalent: (i) $F_\theta$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC, that is, the measure $U_\theta$ of the zeros is a positive Thorin measure; (ii) $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta$; (iii) $\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(s)>0$ for $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta$, that is, $u_\sigma(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\sigma+iv)>0$ for every $\sigma>\theta$ and every real $v$. For $\theta=\frac12$ the equivalence of (ii) and (iii) is the theorem of Lagarias.
results.label: cx:thm:positivity

results.name: Mass deficit identity: twice the number of zeros right of the level equals the drop of the integrated density plus a boundary term
results.summary: For $\frac12<\theta<1$ and $T$ with no zero on the two segments, $2N(\theta,T)=M_1(T)-M_\theta(T)+\pi^{-1}\Delta_{\mathrm{top}}(\theta,T)$, an identity between an integer and computable integrals that decides the existence of zeros right of $\theta$ up to height $T$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the Riemann xi function, $u_\sigma(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\sigma+iv)$ and $M_\sigma(T)=\int_0^Tu_\sigma(v)\,dv$. Let $\frac12<\theta<1$ and $T>0$, and suppose no zero of $\xi$ lies on the segment $\operatorname{Re}s=\theta$, $0\le\operatorname{Im}s\le T$, nor on the segment $\operatorname{Im}s=T$, $\theta\le\operatorname{Re}s\le1$. Let $N(\theta,T)$ be the number of zeros with $\operatorname{Re}\rho>\theta$ and $0<\operatorname{Im}\rho<T$. Then $2N(\theta,T)=M_1(T)-M_\theta(T)+\pi^{-1}\Delta_{\mathrm{top}}(\theta,T)$, where $\Delta_{\mathrm{top}}(\theta,T)=-\int_\theta^1\operatorname{Im}(\xi'/\xi)(\sigma+iT)\,d\sigma$ is the change of $\arg\xi$ along the top side.
results.label: cx:prop:deficit

results.name: The level mass function theta to M_theta(T) is continuous if and only if every zero below height T is on the critical line
results.summary: $M_\theta(T)=M_1(T)+\pi^{-1}\Delta_{\mathrm{top}}(\theta,T)-2N(\theta,T)$ is a real analytic function plus a step function whose jumps sit exactly at the real parts of the off line zeros below height $T$, of size twice their multiplicity.
results.statement: With $\xi$, $u_\sigma$, $M_\sigma(T)=\int_0^Tu_\sigma(v)\,dv$, $N(\theta,T)$ and $\Delta_{\mathrm{top}}(\theta,T)=-\int_\theta^1\operatorname{Im}(\xi'/\xi)(\sigma+iT)\,d\sigma$ as in the mass deficit identity, let $T>0$ not be the ordinate of a zero. For $\theta\in(\frac12,1]$ not the real part of a zero below height $T$, $M_\theta(T)=M_1(T)+\pi^{-1}\Delta_{\mathrm{top}}(\theta,T)-2N(\theta,T)$. The first two terms form a real analytic function of $\theta$ with derivative $\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Im}(\xi'/\xi)(\theta+iT)$, and $2N(\theta,T)$ is a step function that drops by $2m$ as $\theta$ decreases through $\operatorname{Re}\rho$, for each zero $\rho$ of multiplicity $m$ with $\operatorname{Re}\rho>\frac12$ and $0<\operatorname{Im}\rho<T$. Hence $\theta\mapsto M_\theta(T)$ extends continuously to $(\frac12,1]$ if and only if every zero below height $T$ lies on the critical line, and its jumps occur exactly at the real parts of the off line zeros, of size twice the total multiplicity of the zeros with that real part and ordinate below $T$.
results.label: cx:cor:levelmass

results.name: Certified positivity of u_{3/4} and u_{7/8} on [0,1420] and 1000 zeros on the critical line below 1419.9, in ball arithmetic
results.summary: A computation in ball arithmetic at two precisions (96 and 160 bits) certifies that $u_{3/4}$ and $u_{7/8}$ are positive on $[0,1420]$ and that $\xi$ has exactly $1000$ zeros below height $1419.9$, all on the critical line and simple; this is a computer assisted result covering only this range, and the count of zeros is known (Platt and Trudgian).
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the Riemann xi function, $u_\theta(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\theta+iv)$, $\Xi(v)=\xi(\frac12+iv)$, $T^*=1419.9$, $N(T)$ the number of zeros $\rho$ of $\zeta$ with $0<\operatorname{Im}\rho<T$ and $N(\theta,T)$ the number of those with $\operatorname{Re}\rho>\theta$. A computation in ball arithmetic (run at $96$ and at $160$ bits, with Taylor bounds for $u_\theta$ on cells and the argument change of $\xi$ along a path and a rectangle) establishes: (i) $u_{3/4}(v)>0$ and $u_{7/8}(v)>0$ for $0\le v\le1420$; (ii) $N(T^*)=1000$; (iii) $N(\frac34,T^*)=0$, with $\int_0^{T^*}u_{3/4}(v)\,dv=1000.01952570266\ldots$ to within $10^{-20}$; (iv) $\Xi$ has $1000$ certified sign changes in $(0,T^*)$. Consequently every zero of $\zeta$ with $0<\operatorname{Im}\rho<T^*$ lies on the critical line and is simple. The statement covers only this range of heights.
results.label: cx:thm:certified

results.name: Global minimum of the Thorin density u_{7/8} at the origin, given the announced zero free half plane
results.status_text: conditional on The zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ for the Riemann zeta function, announced in the quasi Riemann hypothesis preprints (OpenAI 2026, Liu 2026), unrefereed and not checked for this book
results.conditions: The zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ for the Riemann zeta function, announced in the quasi Riemann hypothesis preprints (OpenAI 2026, Liu 2026), unrefereed and not checked for this book.
results.summary: Given that $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>7/8$, $\mathfrak U_{7/8}\ge u_{7/8}(0)\,dv$ with $u_{7/8}(0)=0.0055146635278\ldots$ and $u_{7/8}(v)>u_{7/8}(0)$ for $v\ne0$ off the ordinates of zeros on $\operatorname{Re}s=7/8$; the verification on $[13.5,1420]$ is a computation.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the Riemann xi function and $u_\theta(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\theta+iv)$. If $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$, then, as measures, $\mathfrak U_{7/8}\ge u_{7/8}(0)\,dv$, where $\mathfrak U_{7/8}$ is the Thorin measure with density $u_{7/8}$ (with atoms at the ordinates of zeros on $\operatorname{Re}s=\frac78$ if there are any) and $u_{7/8}(0)=\pi^{-1}(\xi'/\xi)(\frac78)=0.0055146635278\ldots$, and $u_{7/8}(v)>u_{7/8}(0)$ wherever $v\ne0$ is not the ordinate of a zero on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\frac78$. The proof is a computation, with least certified bound on $[13.5,1420]$ equal to $0.0272$ at $v=17.49$ for $\theta=\frac78$.
results.label: cx:thm:globalmin

results.name: Global minimum of u_theta at the origin for every level between 7/8 and 1, given the announced zero free half plane
results.status_text: conditional on The zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ for the Riemann zeta function, announced in the quasi Riemann hypothesis preprints (OpenAI 2026, Liu 2026), unrefereed and not checked for this book. The monotonicity of $\theta\mapsto u_\theta(0)$ is unconditional
results.conditions: The zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ for the Riemann zeta function, announced in the quasi Riemann hypothesis preprints (OpenAI 2026, Liu 2026), unrefereed and not checked for this book. The monotonicity of $\theta\mapsto u_\theta(0)$ is unconditional.
results.summary: Given that $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>7/8$, for every $\theta\in[7/8,1]$ and every real $v\ne0$ off the ordinates of zeros on $\operatorname{Re}s=\theta$, $u_\theta(v)>u_\theta(0)$, so $\mathfrak U_\theta-u_\theta(0)\,dv\ge0$; unconditionally $\theta\mapsto u_\theta(0)$ is increasing on $[\frac12,\infty)$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the Riemann xi function, $u_\theta(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\theta+iv)$ and $\mathfrak U_\theta$ the Thorin measure at level $\theta$, with density $u_\theta$ for $\theta>\frac78$. Suppose $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$. Then for every $\theta\in[\frac78,1]$ and every real $v\ne0$ that is not the height of a zero on $\operatorname{Re}s=\theta$, $u_\theta(v)>u_\theta(0)=\pi^{-1}(\xi'/\xi)(\theta)$, and the singular part of $\mathfrak U_\theta$ consists of positive atoms, which occur only if $\theta=\frac78$ and a zero lies on $\operatorname{Re}s=\frac78$; so $\mathfrak U_\theta-u_\theta(0)\,dv$ is a positive measure. Unconditionally, $\theta\mapsto u_\theta(0)$ is increasing on $[\frac12,\infty)$. The values of $u_\theta(0)$ run from $0.0055147$ at $\theta=\frac78$ to $0.0073516$ at $\theta=1$.
results.label: cx:thm:uniform

results.name: Level by level theorem: a zero free half plane right of theta is equivalent to the global minimum of u_theta' at the origin for all theta' in [theta,1], with an explicit excess bound
results.summary: For $\frac12<\theta\le1$, no zeros of $\zeta$ in $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta$ is equivalent to $u_{\theta'}(v)\ge u_{\theta'}(0)$ for all $\theta'\in[\theta,1]$; when they hold, the excess $u_{\theta'}(v)-u_{\theta'}(0)$ has an explicit lower bound whose numerical constants ($w^*=0.0294450$, brackets above $0.1014$ and $0.0151$) are computed; the direction from (i) to (ii) is computer assisted.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the Riemann xi function, $u_\theta(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\theta+iv)$ and $\frac12<\theta\le1$. The following are equivalent: (i) $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta$; (ii) for every $\theta'\in[\theta,1]$, $u_{\theta'}(v)\ge u_{\theta'}(0)$ for all real $v$ that are not heights of zeros on $\operatorname{Re}s=\theta'$. When they hold, $\mathfrak U_{\theta'}\ge u_{\theta'}(0)\,dv$ as measures for $\theta'\in[\theta,1]$, and for every $\theta'\in[\theta,1]$, with $c=2\theta'-1$ and the sum over all nontrivial zeros $\rho=\sigma_\rho+i\gamma_\rho$ of $\zeta$ with multiplicity, $u_{\theta'}(v)-u_{\theta'}(0)\ge\frac c{2\pi}\bigl(\sum_\rho\frac1{c^2+(v-\gamma_\rho)^2}-\pi w^*\bigr)$ with $w^*=0.0294450$, where the bracket $\sum_\rho\frac1{c^2+(v-\gamma_\rho)^2}-\pi w^*$ is at least $\pi(0.06174-w^*)>0.1014$ for $13.5\le|v|\le1418.9$ and at least $7/65-\pi w^*>0.0151$ for $|v|\ge1418.9$. The numerical constants and brackets are computed, not proved by hand.
results.label: cx:thm:lbl

results.name: The slope of the excess of the Thorin density: certified infima near 0.1758 to 0.1793, and under RH the minimum 0.183899 in the first gap at v equal to 17.4979
results.status_text: conditional on The Riemann hypothesis, for the clause on the limiting bracket $X$ (its minimiser and value in the first gap). The lower bounds for $\inf B_c$ are a computation in ball arithmetic that needs only the hypothesis stated, no zeros of $\zeta$ in $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta$, which holds for $\theta=1$
results.conditions: The Riemann hypothesis, for the clause on the limiting bracket $X$ (its minimiser and value in the first gap). The lower bounds for $\inf B_c$ are a computation in ball arithmetic that needs only the hypothesis stated, no zeros of $\zeta$ in $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta$, which holds for $\theta=1$.
results.summary: Under the hypothesis of the level by level theorem the bracket of the excess has infima at least $0.17575$ ($c=1$) to $0.17927$ ($c\downarrow0$) on $13.5\le|v|\le1418.9$, approached near $v=17.49$; under the Riemann hypothesis the limiting bracket $X$ has a unique minimiser $v^*\in[17.4978,17.4980]$ in the first gap with $0.1838985448\le X(v^*)\le0.1838987563$; the bounds are computed and the clause on $X$ is conditional on the Riemann hypothesis.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the Riemann xi function, $\theta\in(\frac12,1]$ be such that $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta$, $\theta'\in[\theta,1]$, $c=2\theta'-1$, $\gamma$ run over the ordinates of the zeros with multiplicity (both signs), $V_c(v)=\sum_{|\gamma|<1419.9}\bigl(\frac{c^2}4+(v-\gamma)^2\bigr)^{-1}$ and $B_c(v)=V_c(v)-V_c(0)-2\sum_{|\gamma|\ge1419.9}\gamma^{-2}$, the lower bound for $\frac{2\pi}c(u_{\theta'}(v)-u_{\theta'}(0))$ in which the zeros below height $1419.9$ are on the critical line by the certified computation of the book. A computation shows $\inf_{13.5\le|v|\le1418.9}B_c(v)\ge0.17575$ for $c=1$, $0.17838$ for $c=\frac12$, $0.17904$ for $c=\frac14$ and $0.17927$ as $c\downarrow0$, each infimum approached at $v=17.49$ to $17.50$, between the first two zeros. Under the Riemann hypothesis the limiting bracket $X(v)=\lim_{c\downarrow0}\frac{2\pi}c(u_{\theta'}(v)-u_{\theta'}(0))=\sum_\rho\bigl(\frac1{(v-\gamma_\rho)^2}-\frac1{\gamma_\rho^2}\bigr)$ has in the first gap between the zeros $14.1347$ and $21.0220$ a unique minimiser $v^*\in[17.4978,17.4980]$, and $0.1838985448\le X(v^*)\le0.1838987563$. The statement that $17.4979$ minimises $X$ over all of $13.5\le|v|\le1418.9$ is the author's computation, not rerun, and is not claimed here.
results.label: cx:prop:slope

results.name: A posteriori bound: the error of a window mass of a positive measure against the Thorin measure is bounded by the residual against a weight
results.summary: If $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta'$ and $\mu$ is a finite positive measure with residual $r=P_a*\mu-u_1$, then $|\int\varphi\,d\mu-\int\varphi\,d\mathfrak U_{\theta'}|\le\int|r||\psi|\,dv$ with $\psi=\mathcal F^{-1}[e^{a|\omega|}\widehat\varphi]$.
results.statement: Let $\theta'\in[\frac12,1)$, $a=1-\theta'$, $P_a(x)=(a/\pi)/(a^2+x^2)$, and suppose $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta'$, so that the Thorin measure $\mathfrak U_{\theta'}$ exists and $P_a*\mathfrak U_{\theta'}=u_1\,dv$ with $u_1(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(1+iv)$. Let $\mu$ be a finite positive measure and $r=P_a*\mu-u_1$ on $\mathbb{R}$. For a test function $\varphi$ with $\int e^{a|\omega|}|\widehat\varphi(\omega)|\,d\omega<\infty$ put $\psi=\mathcal F^{-1}[e^{a|\omega|}\widehat\varphi]$, and assume that $\psi\cdot(P_a*\mu+u_1)$ is integrable. Then $\bigl|\int\varphi\,d\mu-\int\varphi\,d\mathfrak U_{\theta'}\bigr|\le\int_{\mathbb{R}}|r(v)||\psi(v)|\,dv$.
results.label: cx:prop:apost

results.name: From certified Gaussian window mass and centroid to the location of a zero, under the Riemann hypothesis
results.status_text: conditional on The Riemann hypothesis, so that $\mathfrak U_{1/2}=\sum_\rho\delta_{\gamma_\rho}$
results.conditions: The Riemann hypothesis, so that $\mathfrak U_{1/2}=\sum_\rho\delta_{\gamma_\rho}$.
results.summary: Under the Riemann hypothesis, certified bounds on the mass and first moment of a Gaussian window around a zero give $|\gamma_*-c|\le(|\widehat m|+B_1+\Theta)/(\widehat M-B_0)$.
results.statement: Assume the Riemann hypothesis, so that the Thorin measure at level $\frac12$ is $\mathfrak U_{1/2}=\sum_\rho\delta_{\gamma_\rho}$ over the ordinates with multiplicity. Let $\varphi(v)=e^{-(v-c)^2/(2\sigma^2)}$, let $\int\varphi\,d\mathfrak U_{1/2}\in[\widehat M-B_0,\widehat M+B_0]$ with $\widehat M>B_0$ and $\int(v-c)\varphi\,d\mathfrak U_{1/2}\in[\widehat m-B_1,\widehat m+B_1]$ be given bounds, let $\gamma_*$ be an ordinate with $|\gamma_*-c|\le R$, and let $\Theta\ge\sum_{\gamma\ne\gamma_*}(|\gamma-c|+R)\varphi(\gamma)$, the sum over the other ordinates with multiplicity. Then $|\gamma_*-c|\le\frac{|\widehat m|+B_1+\Theta}{\widehat M-B_0}$.
results.label: cx:cor:zeroloc

results.name: Smoothed prime sum for u_1: exact identity and error bound under a local hypothesis on the zeros
results.summary: For $v\ge2$ and $X\ge2$ the smoothed prime sum $u_1^X(v)$ differs from $u_1(v)$ by an exact expression in the zeros, and if every zero within $Y$ of height $v$ lies on the critical line the error is at most $\pi^{-1}[c_\Gamma n(v)X^{-1/2}+27\log v/X]$ with $c_\Gamma\le8.34$ and $n(t)=0.39\log t+7$, plus a term of order $n(v+Y+1)e^{-\pi Y/2}$, a term $2.5X^{-3/2}\log(v+2)$ and a pole term $\sqrt{\pi/(v\sinh\pi v)}$ that does not decay in $X$; the timing of the nonuniform FFT is the author's and is not claimed.
results.statement: Let $v\ge2$, $X\ge2$, $s=1+iv$, $L=\zeta'/\zeta$, $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function and $u_1(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(1+iv)$, and let $u_1^X(v)=\frac1\pi\bigl[\frac1{1+v^2}-\frac{\log\pi}2+\frac12\operatorname{Re}\psi(\frac{1+iv}2)-\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\Lambda(n)}n e^{-n/X}\cos(v\log n)\bigr]$ with $\psi$ the digamma function. Then $\pi(u_1(v)-u_1^X(v))=-\operatorname{Re}\sum_\rho\Gamma(\rho-s)X^{\rho-s}+\operatorname{Re}\Gamma(1-s)X^{1-s}+\operatorname{Re}[X^{-1}L(s-1)]+\operatorname{Re}R_X(s)$, with $R_X(s)=(2\pi i)^{-1}\int_{\operatorname{Re}w=-3/2}(-L(s+w))\Gamma(w)X^w\,dw$ and $|R_X(s)|\le2.5X^{-3/2}\log(v+2)$. If every zero with $|\gamma-v|\le Y$, $Y\ge1$, lies on the critical line, then $|u_1(v)-u_1^X(v)|\le\frac1\pi\bigl[c_\Gamma n(v)X^{-1/2}+2.6c_\Gamma'n(v+Y+1)e^{-\pi Y/2}+\sqrt{\pi/(v\sinh\pi v)}+\frac{27\log v}X+\frac{2.5\log(v+2)}{X^{3/2}}\bigr]$, where $n(t)=0.39\log t+7$ bounds the number of ordinates in any interval of length one below height $t$, $c_\Gamma\le8.34$ and $c_\Gamma'\le2.51$ are the explicit gamma function constants of the chapter.
results.label: cx:thm:fastu1

results.name: Open problem: the two phase rate of EM for the continuous Cauchy deconvolution at an atomic target
results.summary: Prove a sublinear phase with $k(R_k-R^*)$ near a constant of order $50$ lasting of the order of $10^4$ steps, then faster convergence on the atoms, and explain the observed exponents of the accelerated scheme.
results.statement: For EM applied to the continuous Cauchy deconvolution $P_a*\mu=u_1$ at an atomic target, with $R_k$ the residual after $k$ steps and $R^*$ its limit, prove the two phase picture of the chapter: a sublinear phase with $k(R_k-R^*)$ near a constant of order $50$ (observed $54.7$, $51.9$, $49.5$, $48.1$ at $k=500$, $1000$, $2000$, $3000$), lasting of the order of $10^4$ steps on the data of the chapter, followed by faster convergence on the support of the atoms with a grid independent rate, and compute that rate from the curvature of the divergence at the atoms. For the accelerated scheme with restart, explain the observed three point exponents, which oscillate between $0.6$ and $2.8$ with a running value near $1.3$. The problem is open, and the numbers are observations.
results.label: cx:prob:twophase

results.name: Open problem: a closed form for the limiting slope 0.183899 of the excess of the Thorin density under RH
results.summary: Does $\mathcal C(v^*)$, with $\mathcal C=\partial_v^2\log|\xi(\frac12+iv)|$ and $v^*=17.4979$ the zero of $\mathcal C'$ between the first two zeros, have an expression in known constants?
results.statement: Under the Riemann hypothesis, with $\gamma$ running over the positive ordinates of the zeros, $\log|\xi(\frac12+iv)|=\log\xi(\frac12)+\sum_{\gamma>0}\log|1-v^2/\gamma^2|$. Put $\mathcal C(v)=\partial_v^2\log|\xi(\frac12+iv)|$, so that the limiting bracket of the excess of the Thorin density is $X(v)=\mathcal C(0)-\mathcal C(v)$, and let $v^*=17.4979$ be the zero of $\mathcal C'$ between the first two zeros, where $X(v^*)=0.183899$ to six digits. Does $\mathcal C(v^*)$, equivalently $X(v^*)$, have an expression in known constants? This is not known.
results.label: cx:prob:closedform

results.name: Open problem: evaluate the level one Thorin density to accuracy epsilon in time polynomial in log v and log(1/epsilon)
results.summary: The smoothed prime sum gives accuracy $\varepsilon$ in time polynomial in $\log v$ and $1/\varepsilon$; is there an algorithm polynomial in $\log v$ and $\log(1/\varepsilon)$?
results.statement: Let $u_1(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(1+iv)$. The smoothed prime sum evaluates $u_1(v)$ to accuracy $\varepsilon$ in time polynomial in $\log v$ and in $1/\varepsilon$. Is there an algorithm polynomial in $\log v$ and $\log(1/\varepsilon)$? Such an algorithm for $\zeta$ and $\zeta'$ on $\operatorname{Re}s=1$ would give one; the converse is not known, and the question is open.
results.label: cx:prob:polylog

results.name: Open problem: the best residual after k steps of a first order method for a single Cauchy blurred atom
results.summary: For one atom at $\gamma$ blurred by $P_a$ and observed exactly, what is the best achievable $h\sum_i|\psi_\gamma(v_i)||r_i|$ after $k$ steps of any first order method on the cone, as a function of $k$, $h$ and $a$?
results.statement: For a single atom at $\gamma$ blurred by the Cauchy density $P_a$ and observed exactly on a grid of spacing $h$, with $r_i$ the residuals at the grid points $v_i$ and $\psi_\gamma$ the weight of the a posteriori window bound for a window centred at $\gamma$, what is the best achievable value of $h\sum_i|\psi_\gamma(v_i)||r_i|$ after $k$ steps of any first order method on the cone of nonnegative measures, as a function of $k$, $h$ and $a$? The question is open.
results.label: cx:prob:bestresidual

results.name: The explicit formula for every smooth compactly supported test function, read as the deconvolution at level one half
results.summary: The Guinand and Weil explicit formula is proved for every test function in C_c^infty, even or not, in the form of the Cauchy deconvolution from level one to level one half, with the multiplier e^{|omega|/2} turning the weights Lambda(n)/n into Lambda(n)/sqrt(n).
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function, let $\rho=\sigma_\rho+i\gamma_\rho$ run over its zeros (the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$, with multiplicity), let $\Lambda$ be the von Mangoldt function and $\gamma_E$ Euler's constant. For every $g\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R})$, with the sum over $\rho$ absolutely convergent, $$\sum_\rho\int_{\mathbb{R}}g(\omega)\,e^{(\sigma_\rho-\frac12)|\omega|}\,e^{-i\omega\gamma_\rho}\,d\omega=\int_{\mathbb{R}}g(\omega)\,e^{|\omega|/2}\,d\omega-\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\Lambda(n)}{\sqrt n}\bigl(g(\log n)+g(-\log n)\bigr)+(1-\log\pi-\gamma_E)\,g(0)+\sum_{k\ge1}\Bigl[\frac{g(0)}{k+1}-\int_{\mathbb{R}}g(\omega)\,e^{-(2k+\frac12)|\omega|}\,d\omega\Bigr].$$ For even $g$ this is the explicit formula of Guinand and Weil; for odd $g$ both sides vanish. Under the Riemann hypothesis the left side is $\sum_\rho\widehat g(\gamma_\rho)$, $\widehat g(x)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}g(\omega)e^{-i\omega x}\,d\omega$. Under the Riemann hypothesis the theorem is the Fourier form of the deconvolution $P_{1/2}*\mu=u_1$, $\mu=\sum_\rho\delta_{\gamma_\rho}$, of the level one density $u_1(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(1+iv)$, with $P_a$ the Cauchy density of width $a$: the multiplier $e^{|\omega|/2}$ that undoes the Cauchy kernel is the factor $\sqrt n$ that turns the weights $\Lambda(n)/n$ of the level one spectrum into the weights $\Lambda(n)/\sqrt n$ of the formula.
results.label: es:thm:explicit

results.name: An unresolvable perturbation of the Cauchy deconvolution at width one half
results.summary: Two positive measures at total variation distance one have data P_{1/2} convolved with them within epsilon of one function once 0.72 e^{-Omega/2} is at most 2 epsilon, so the deconvolution is exponentially ill posed for a general measure.
results.statement:
Let $\Omega>0$, $L\ge1$, $\chi_L(v)=(2\pi L^2)^{-1/2}e^{-v^2/2L^2}$, $N=\int_{\mathbb{R}}|\cos(\Omega v)|\,\chi_L(v)\,dv$ and $
u=N^{-1}\cos(\Omega v)\,\chi_L(v)\,dv$, and let $P_{1/2}(x)=(1/2\pi)/(1/4+x^2)$ be the Cauchy density of width $ rac12$. Then the total variation norm of $
u$ is $1$, the Fourier transform $\widehat
u$ is concentrated within $O(1/L)$ of $\pm\Omega$, and $\|P_{1/2}*
u\|_\infty\le\sqrt{\pi/8}\,L^{-1}e^{1/8L^2}e^{-\Omega/2}\le0.72\,e^{-\Omega/2}$. Consequently, if $0.72\,e^{-\Omega/2}\le2\varepsilon$ and $\mu$ is a positive measure with $\mu\ge N^{-1}\chi_L\,dv$, then $\mu$ and $\mu+
u$ are positive measures at total variation distance $1$ whose data $P_{1/2}*\mu$ and $P_{1/2}*(\mu+
u)$ lie within $\varepsilon$ in the supremum norm of one function, so data of accuracy $\varepsilon$ do not distinguish them. The heuristic reading of this at scale $\delta=\pi/\Omega$ (primes to $e^{\pi/\delta}$) is not a theorem.
results.label: es:prop:resolution

results.name: The Gaussian tapered Fourier transform of the level one density is a sum of damped exponentials, one per zero
results.summary: The tapered transform of the level one density equals a sum over the zeros of damped complex exponentials whose poles carry both the ordinate and the real part of each zero, plus an explicit remainder of order e^{-l^2 omega^2/2}; no hypothesis on the real parts is made.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function with zeros $\rho=\sigma_\rho+i\gamma_\rho$, $a_\rho=1-\sigma_\rho\in(0,1)$, $P_a(x)=(a/\pi)/(a^2+x^2)$, and $u_1(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(1+iv)=\sum_\rho P_{a_\rho}(v-\gamma_\rho)$. Let $w(v)=e^{-(v-c)^2/2\ell^2}$ with $\ell>0$ and $F(\omega)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}u_1(v)\,w(v)\,e^{i\omega(v-c)}\,dv$. Then for $\omega\ell^2>1$, $$F(\omega)=\sum_\rho w(\gamma_\rho+ia_\rho)\,e^{-a_\rho\omega}e^{i\omega(\gamma_\rho-c)}+R(\omega),$$ where $w(x+iy)=w(x)e^{y^2/2\ell^2}e^{-iy(x-c)/\ell^2}$ is the entire extension of the taper, the series converges absolutely, and with $Y=\omega\ell^2$ $$|R(\omega)|\le\frac1\pi\,e^{-\ell^2\omega^2/2}\sum_\rho a_\rho\int_{\mathbb{R}}\frac{e^{-(x-c)^2/2\ell^2}\,dx}{(x-\gamma_\rho)^2+(Y-a_\rho)^2},\qquad\int_{\mathbb{R}}\frac{e^{-(x-c)^2/2\ell^2}\,dx}{(x-\gamma)^2+B^2}\le\min\Bigl(\frac\pi B,\frac{\sqrt{2\pi}\,\ell}{B^2}\Bigr).$$ In particular for $\omega_j=\omega_0+j\Delta$ with $\omega_0\ell^2>1$, $F(\omega_j)=\sum_\rho A_\rho z_\rho^{\,j}+R(\omega_j)$ with $|R(\omega_j)|\le C_0e^{-\ell^2\omega_j^2/2}$, $C_0$ the above bound on $|R(\omega_0)|$ divided by $e^{-\ell^2\omega_0^2/2}$, $A_\rho=w(\gamma_\rho+ia_\rho)e^{-a_\rho\omega_0}e^{i\omega_0(\gamma_\rho-c)}$ and $z_\rho=e^{\Delta(-a_\rho+i(\gamma_\rho-c))}$: the pole $z_\rho$ has modulus giving $a_\rho$ and argument giving $\gamma_\rho-c$ modulo $2\pi/\Delta$. Nothing is assumed about the real parts $\sigma_\rho$.
results.label: es:thm:taper

results.name: Posterior concentration for the atoms of the tapered transform model on a window
results.summary: In the window model of the tapered transform with a spike free prior on the atoms, the posterior concentrates at the true zeros, including their real parts, at the rate of the noise, under hypotheses on bias and aliasing that do not hold at the settings of the chapter's computations, and it decides nothing about the Riemann hypothesis.
results.statement: Fix a window centre $c$, a taper width $\ell$, a step $\Delta$, samples $\omega_j=\omega_0+j\Delta$, $0\le j<J$, with $\omega_0\ell^2>1$, and a radius $R$ with $2R\Delta<2\pi$. The data are $F=\Phi(\vartheta^0)+b$ with $\Phi(\vartheta)_j=\sum_{m=1}^MA_mz_m^{\,j}$, $z_m=e^{\Delta(-a_m+i(\gamma_m-c))}$, where $\vartheta^0$ collects the zeros $(\gamma_m,a_m,A_m)$ with $|\gamma_m-c|\le R$ (ordinate, width $a_m=1-\sigma_m$, amplitude) and $b$ is the deterministic bias from the zeros beyond $R$ and the remainder of the tapered transform; the observation is $Y=F+\tau\xi$ with $\xi\in\mathbb{C}^J$ having independent standard normal real and imaginary parts. Fix $s>0$, $0<a_-<a_+<1$, $0<\alpha_-<A_+$ and an integer $M_{\max}$ with $J\ge2M_{\max}$. For $0\le M\le M_{\max}$ let $K_M$ be the compact set of $\vartheta=(\gamma_m,a_m,A_m)_{m\le M}$ with $c-R\le\gamma_1<\dots<\gamma_M\le c+R$, $\gamma_{m+1}-\gamma_m\ge s$, $a_m\in[a_-,a_+]$, $\alpha_-\le|A_m|\le A_+$. Let the prior be $\Pi=\sum_Mp_M\Pi_M$ with $\Pi_M$ having a density on $K_M$ between $\pi_->0$ and $\pi_+$. Let $\vartheta^0$ be an interior point of $K_{M^0}$ with $p_{M^0}>0$, $\|b\|_2\le B\tau$, and $d(\vartheta,\vartheta^0)=\max_m(|\gamma_m-\gamma^0_m|+|a_m-a^0_m|+|A_m-A^0_m|)$ if $M=M^0$, $d=\infty$ otherwise. Then there are $\tau_0,r_0,K,\kappa_0>0$, depending on $\vartheta^0$, the sets $K_M$, the prior, $J$, $\Delta$ and $B$, such that for $\tau\le\tau_0$ and $K\tau\le\varepsilon\le r_0$, with probability at least $1-e^{-\kappa_0\varepsilon^2/\tau^2}$, $\Pi(d(\vartheta,\vartheta^0)\le\varepsilon\mid Y)\ge1-e^{-\kappa_0\varepsilon^2/\tau^2}$. In particular, for fixed $\varepsilon_1>0$ and $\|b\|_2\le B\tau$, as $\tau\to0$ the posterior probability that every component has $|\sigma_m-\frac12|\le\varepsilon_1$ tends to $1$ in probability if every zero of $\vartheta^0$ has $|\sigma^0_m-\frac12|<\varepsilon_1$, and to $0$ if one has $|\sigma^0_m-\frac12|>\varepsilon_1$. The hypotheses (bias below the noise, no aliasing) are incompatible at the settings of the chapter's computations, and the theorem is indifferent between the Riemann hypothesis and its negation.
results.label: es:thm:concentration

results.name: The real part of an off line pair of zeros is resolved only at the rate tau to the one half
results.summary: Because the functional equation forces off line zeros to come in pairs at one half plus and minus delta and the data depend on delta only through delta squared, the real part is resolved at the rate (tau/norm of t_perp)^{1/2} for data accurate to tau, and no test, whatever the method, does better.
results.statement: Work in the window model of the tapered transform at a level $\theta>\frac12$ with $a_0=\theta-\frac12$, samples $\omega_j=\omega_0+j\Delta$, $0\le j<J$, and $f(a)_j=\exp(-q^2/2\ell^2+i\omega_jq)$, $q=(\gamma-c)+ia$. One ordinate $\gamma$ carries either a zero on the line or a pair at real parts $\frac12\pm\delta$, $0\le\delta\le\delta_+<a_0$, entering the samples as $A\,g(\eta;\gamma)$ with $g(\eta;\gamma)=f(a_0-\sqrt\eta)+f(a_0+\sqrt\eta)$, $\eta=\delta^2$, and one complex amplitude $A$ common to the two members (the functional equation puts zeros off the line in such pairs); the other $M$ zeros enter as $\sum_{m\le M}A_mz_m^{\,j}$ with $z_m=e^{\Delta(-a_m+i(\gamma_m-c))}$. Write $\vartheta'=(\gamma,A,(\gamma_m,a_m,A_m)_{m\le M})$, of real dimension $D'=3+4M$, and $\Phi(\eta,\vartheta')\in\mathbb{C}^J=\mathbb{R}^{2J}$ for the noiseless samples. Assume (H1) $Y=\Phi(\eta^0,\vartheta'^0)+b+\tau\xi$ with $\xi$ having independent standard normal real and imaginary parts and $\|b\|_2\le B\tau$; (H2) the parameter set is $[0,\eta_+]\times K'$ with $\eta_+=\delta_+^2$, $K'$ compact, $\eta^0\in[0,\eta_+)$, $\vartheta'^0$ interior to $K'$ and $\Phi$ injective on it; (H3) the Jacobian $T'$ of $\vartheta'\mapsto\Phi(\eta^0,\vartheta')$ at $\vartheta'^0$ has rank $D'$ and, with $t=\partial_\eta\Phi(\eta^0,\vartheta'^0)$ and $t_\perp=(I-P')t$ for the orthogonal projection $P'$ onto the range of $T'$, $\|t_\perp\|>0$; (H4) the prior puts mass $1-p<1$ at $\eta=0$ and density $p\,\pi(\sqrt\eta)/2\sqrt\eta$ on $(0,\eta_+]$ with $\pi$ continuous and positive on $[0,\delta_+]$, and independently $\vartheta'$ has a density bounded on $K'$, continuous and positive at $\vartheta'^0$. Let $r_\tau=\tau/\|t_\perp\|$ and $\tau\to0$ with $B$ and $\vartheta'^0$ fixed, and with $\eta^0$ fixed in (i) and (ii). Then (i) for every $M_\tau\to\infty$, $\Pi(|\eta-\eta^0|>M_\tau r_\tau\mid Y)\to0$ in probability, so $\delta$ is located within $(M_\tau r_\tau)^{1/2}$ if $\delta^0=0$; (ii) for $\eta^0=0$ and $\delta_1=c\,r_\tau^{1/2}$ the two error probabilities of any test of $\delta=0$ against $\delta=\delta_1$, whatever the method, sum to at least $1-c^2/2-O(\tau)$; (iii) for $\eta^0=v\,r_\tau$, $v\ge0$ fixed, with $\|b\|_2=o(\tau)$, the matched filter statistic $Z=\langle t_\perp,r\rangle/(\tau\|t_\perp\|)$, with $t_\perp$ taken at $\eta=0$ and $r$ the residual of the least squares fit of $\Phi(0,\cdot)$ over $K'$, satisfies $Z=v+\zeta_\perp+o_P(1)$ with $\zeta_\perp$ standard Gaussian, the one sided test $Z>z_\alpha$ has asymptotic level $\alpha$ and power $1-N(z_\alpha-v)$, $N$ the standard normal distribution function and $z_\alpha=N^{-1}(1-\alpha)$, which is $\frac12$ at $\delta^*=(z_\alpha r_\tau)^{1/2}$, and twice the log generalised likelihood ratio of $\eta\ge0$ against $\eta=0$ is $\max(Z,0)^2+o_P(1)$. The theorem needs the bias below the noise and no aliasing, so it does not cover the chapter's runs on the zeros of $\zeta$.
results.label: es:thm:singular

results.name: Bayes factors for a zero on the line against a pair at one half plus and minus delta
results.summary: With the spike and slab prior on the pair the Bayes factor for the line against the pair grows like tau to the minus one half, against tau to the minus one for the single zero alternative the functional equation forbids, so the functional equation takes the square root of the evidence.
results.statement: In the setting of the rate theorem for the real part of a pair (hypotheses H1 to H4, noise level $\tau$, scale $s=\|t_\perp\|/\tau$), put the spike and slab prior on the pair: $\delta=0$ with probability $1-p$, and otherwise $\delta$ with a density $\pi$ continuous and positive on $[0,\delta_+]$. Let $G(Z)=\int_0^\infty u^{-1/2}e^{Zu-u^2/2}\,du$ and $Z$ the matched filter statistic of that theorem. (a) If $\eta^0=0$, or $\eta^0=v\,r_\tau$ with $v$ fixed, $\|b\|_2=o(\tau)$, and $\vartheta'$ has the same prior under the line and the pair, the Bayes factor for the line against the pair is $\mathrm{BF}_{01}=\dfrac{2\,s^{1/2}}{\pi(0)\,G(Z)}(1+o_P(1))$; under the null $Z$ is asymptotically standard Gaussian and $\mathrm{BF}_{01}\asymp\tau^{-1/2}$ in probability. (b) Under a pair with fixed $\delta\in(0,\delta_+)$, if the prior density of $\vartheta'$ is bounded below on $K'$ and every point of $K'$ has prior mass at least $c\tau^{D'}$ within distance $\tau$, then $\log\mathrm{BF}_{01}=-D(\delta)^2(1+o_P(1))/2\tau^2$ with $D(\delta)=\delta^2\|t_\perp\|+O(\delta^4)$. (c) Against the alternative of a single zero of width $a_0+\varepsilon$, with $\varepsilon$ having a density positive and continuous at $0$ and $\|(I-P')\partial_\varepsilon\Phi\|>0$, the same data give $\mathrm{BF}_{01}\asymp\tau^{-1}$ in probability under the null. All of this is in the free amplitude model with a common amplitude for the pair.
results.label: es:thm:bf

results.name: The density at a level between one half and one is a signed sum of Lorentzians, and the Riemann hypothesis fixes every damping rate
results.summary: At a level theta in (1/2,1] that is not the real part of a zero, the density and its tapered transform are signed sums over the zeros with widths abs(theta minus sigma), and the Riemann hypothesis holds if and only if every damping rate equals theta minus one half.
results.statement: Let $\frac12<\theta\le1$ with $\theta\ne\sigma_\rho$ for every zero $\rho=\sigma_\rho+i\gamma_\rho$ of the completed zeta function $\xi$, let $P_b(x)=(b/\pi)/(b^2+x^2)$ and $u_\theta(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\theta+iv)$. Then $u_\theta(v)=\sum_\rho\operatorname{sgn}(\theta-\sigma_\rho)P_{|\theta-\sigma_\rho|}(v-\gamma_\rho)$ and $\widehat{u_\theta}(\omega)=\sum_\rho\operatorname{sgn}(\theta-\sigma_\rho)e^{-|\theta-\sigma_\rho||\omega|}e^{-i\omega\gamma_\rho}$. For $\omega\ell^2>1$ the tapered transform $F_\theta(\omega)=\int u_\theta(v)w(v)e^{i\omega(v-c)}dv$ with the Gaussian taper $w(v)=e^{-(v-c)^2/2\ell^2}$ equals $\sum_\rho\operatorname{sgn}(\theta-\sigma_\rho)\,w(\gamma_\rho+i|\theta-\sigma_\rho|)\,e^{-|\theta-\sigma_\rho|\omega}e^{i\omega(\gamma_\rho-c)}+R_\theta(\omega)$, with $R_\theta$ bounded as in the tapered transform theorem with $a_\rho$ replaced by $|\theta-\sigma_\rho|$. For samples $\omega_j=\omega_0+j\Delta$, a zero with $\sigma_\rho>\theta$ gives the pole $e^{\Delta(-(\sigma_\rho-\theta)+i(\gamma_\rho-c))}$, of modulus $e^{-\Delta(\sigma_\rho-\theta)}$, with an amplitude of sign opposite to the taper profile, while its partner $1-\sigma_\rho<\theta$ gives a pole at the same ordinate with the profile's sign. The Riemann hypothesis holds if and only if every damping rate $|\theta-\sigma_\rho|$ equals $\theta-\frac12$.
results.label: es:prop:level

results.name: Matrix pencil on a window at height 3e12, a demonstration inside the verified range
results.summary: A computation by the authors, not rerun for the book, in which the matrix pencil on data at level 0.6 returned 52 components near height 3e12 with real parts within 1.4e-8 of one half, and a sign change certificate puts a zero on the line within 1e-7 of each ordinate; the count and the real parts are not certified, and the window lies inside the range verified by Platt and Trudgian.
results.statement: A demonstration, computed and not a finding about the zeros: the window centred at $c=3\times10^{12}+100$ lies inside the range $0<\gamma\le3\,000\,175\,332\,800$ in which Platt and Trudgian verified the Riemann hypothesis. From $1001$ values of $u_{0.6}(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(0.6+iv)$ at spacing $0.02$ (level $0.6$, taper $\ell=2$, ball arithmetic at $160$ bits), the matrix pencil returned $52$ components with amplitudes on the taper profile within $6$ of the centre, the smooth count being $51.36$, each with real part $0.5000000\pm1.4\times10^{-8}$ read from the modulus of its pole; this is a floating point estimate, not a certificate, and the selection of components presumes the real part $\frac12$. The authors' certificate (not rerun) is a sign change of Hardy's function $Z$ in ball arithmetic on $[\gamma-10^{-7},\gamma+10^{-7}]$ for all $52$ of the $52$ ordinates, which places a zero on the line within $10^{-7}$ of each; an independent scan in ball arithmetic at $160$ bits finds exactly $52$ certified sign changes in $[c-6,c+6]$, but the comparison with the pencil's ordinates one by one was not made. Not certified: that these are all the zeros of the window (a sign scan cannot see two zeros inside one step, and no winding number or Turing method was completed) and the real parts.
results.label: es:res:window3e12

results.name: Matrix pencil on a window at height 1e13 plus 100, above the verified range, computed
results.summary: At height 1e13 plus 100, above the range verified by Platt and Trudgian, the matrix pencil on data at level 0.6 returns 53 components whose real parts lie within 4.7e-9 of one half, a floating point estimate and not a certificate.
results.statement: A computation with scripts written for the book: the window centred at $c=10^{13}+100$, above the verified range of Platt and Trudgian ($\gamma\le3\,000\,175\,332\,800$), level $0.6$, taper $\ell=2$, $1001$ values $u_{0.6}(v_k)$, $v_k=c-10+0.02k$, each a ball at $160$ bits, $\omega\in[5,85]$ at spacing $0.2$, a Hankel matrix of order $200$ in double precision and model order $132$. The pencil returns $53$ components with amplitude on the taper profile within $6$ of the centre, at ordinates from $c-5.7$ to $c+5.8$ (the smooth count is $53.66$), the ratio of amplitude to profile being $1$ to within $1.6\times10^{-7}$; the selection compares the amplitude with the profile at the pole's own width, so no real part is assumed. The largest $|\sigma_\rho-\frac12|$ over the $53$ poles is $4.7\times10^{-9}$ (median $7.1\times10^{-11}$), an estimate from a double precision pencil and not a certificate, and it is not a proof of the Riemann hypothesis in the window.
results.label: es:res:pencil1e13

results.name: Fifty three certified zeros on the critical line in a window at height 1e13 plus 100, above the verified range
results.summary: A ball arithmetic scan certifies 53 sign changes of Hardy's function, hence 53 zeros of zeta on the critical line, in a window centred at 1e13 plus 100, above the range verified by Platt and Trudgian; the count of zeros in the window and the real parts are not certified, and nothing is certified off the line.
results.statement: In ball arithmetic at $160$ bits, with each step of $0.02$ having opposite signs of Hardy's function $Z(t)=e^{i\vartheta(t)}\zeta(\frac12+it)$ at its ends, the interval $[c-6,c+6]$ with $c=10^{13}+100$, above the height $3\,000\,175\,332\,800$ verified by Platt and Trudgian, contains $53$ certified sign changes, with bisection brackets of width $10^{-10}$ certified at both ends again at $192$ bits; hence $\zeta$ has at least $53$ zeros on the critical line in that interval, each located to $10^{-10}$. The pencil of the same chapter returns the same $53$ ordinates (the largest difference is $3.9\times10^{-9}$). Not certified: the number of zeros in the window (a sign scan cannot see two zeros inside one step of $0.02$, the smallest gap found is $0.0326$, and no Turing method or winding number was run) and the real parts; nothing is certified off the line. The certified statement is only that these $53$ zeros lie on the line, and it is not a proof of the Riemann hypothesis in the window.
results.label: es:res:zeros1e13

results.name: Open problem, a rigorous matrix pencil with a perturbation bound under the model error
results.summary: State and prove a perturbation bound for the matrix pencil under the model error of the tapered transform, so that verified linear algebra on ball data encloses the zeros, and compare the enclosures with the winding number route.
results.statement: The matrix pencil applied to the tapered transform $F(\omega_j)=\sum_\rho A_\rho z_\rho^{\,j}+R(\omega_j)$ of the level one density $u_1$ of the completed zeta function makes the Hankel matrix of exact finite rank only in the limit, because of the far zeros and the remainder $R$. The problem: state and prove a perturbation bound for the pencil under this model error, which together with verified linear algebra on ball data (in the sense of Rump) would give rigorous enclosures of the zeros from level one data, and compare the width of the resulting enclosures with the winding number route of the argument principle. Status: open.
results.label: es:prob:rigorous_pencil

results.name: Open problem, characterise and remove the spurious pencil components at the edges of windows
results.summary: Characterise the few components that pass the amplitude filter at the edges of overlapping windows without being zeros, and prove under explicit hypotheses that agreement of two windows or the phase of the amplitude removes them.
results.statement: In the many window use of the matrix pencil on the tapered transform of $u_1$, a few components at the edges of overlapping windows pass the amplitude filter without being zeros. The problem: characterise them (the expectation is that they are the pencil's representation of the taper's tail of the next zeros outside the window, with poles close to the genuine ones and amplitudes off the profile), and prove under explicit hypotheses on the separation and the amplitudes that a rule based on the agreement of two windows, or on the phase $e^{i(\omega_0-a/\ell^2)(\gamma-c)}$ of the amplitude predicted by the tapered transform theorem, removes all of them. Status: open.
results.label: es:prob:spurious

results.name: Open problem, windows at greater height with a rigorous argument principle and the cost of a full certificate
results.summary: Make the argument principle rigorous at large height with an explicit bound for the derivative of zeta on a small disc, estimate the height at which a certified window is feasible within a day, and compare the many window scheme above 3000175332800 with Turing's method.
results.statement: The matrix pencil runs on one window of fifty two or fifty three zeros at heights $3\times10^{12}$ and $10^{13}$ at the cost of the Riemann and Siegel sum, $t^{1/2}$ terms per value, which Hiary's method would bring to $t^{1/3+o(1)}$. The problem: make the argument principle rigorous at large height, with an explicit bound for $|\zeta'|$ on a small disc from the explicit convexity bounds, so that the count of zeros in the window is certified and not only their existence on the line; estimate the height at which a window of the pencil with its full certificate is feasible within a day, and run it; and determine whether the many window scheme at a fixed height, for example $10^3$ zeros above $3\,000\,175\,332\,800$, is competitive with Turing's method for that range when the real parts are wanted as output and not only tested. Status: open.
results.label: es:prob:higher_wider

results.name: Open problem, the adaptive prior in full: sine kernel process with marked ordinates and a spike and slab on the pairs
results.summary: Place the sine kernel determinantal process on marked distinct ordinates, a pair counting as one point marked by its displacement, implement the posterior on the number, positions and marks of the zeros in a window, and report it separately from the argument principle certificate.
results.statement: The problem: place the sine kernel determinantal process on marked distinct ordinates, a pair of zeros at real parts $\frac12\pm\delta$ counting as one point marked by its displacement, and implement the posterior on the number, the positions and the marks of the zeros in a window, with the spike and slab prior on the marks, by reversible jump or by a determinantal birth and death sampler started at the pencil; measure on the many window run whether it removes the spurious components; state the count with its multiplicity (a double zero counts twice), and report the posterior probability of each count, conditional on the model, separately from the argument principle certificate, which it does not replace. Status: open.
results.label: es:prob:adaptive_prior

results.name: Open problem, the constant in the tau to the one half rate and the design that maximises the information
results.summary: Find the design of taper, bandwidth and level that maximises the information norm of t_perp over tau for a given cost, and determine how it scales with the height through the gaps to the neighbouring zeros.
results.statement: The detectable displacement of an off line pair of zeros is $\delta^*=(z_\alpha\tau/\|t_\perp\|)^{1/2}$, with $\tau$ the standard deviation per real coordinate and $t_\perp$ the part of the tangent of the pair orthogonal to the tangent space of the other zeros, depending on the taper, the bandwidth and the level. The problem: find the design that maximises the information $\|t_\perp\|/\tau$, and not $\|t_\perp\|$ alone, for a given cost, and determine how it scales with the height, through the gaps to the neighbouring zeros, which enter $t_\perp$ through the projection, and not through the mean density alone. Status: open.
results.label: es:prob:constant_rate

results.name: Cauchy transport: the density at level theta is the Cauchy smoothing of the critical zeros plus a signed defect from zeros off the line
results.summary: For every $\theta>\frac12$, $u_\theta=P_{\theta-1/2}*\mathfrak U_{1/2}+R_\theta$ where $R_\theta$ is the sum of the Cauchy pairs of the zeros off the critical line, which is the identity of densities at every level, with $R_\theta=0$ under the Riemann hypothesis.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function with zeros $\rho=\sigma_\rho+i\gamma_\rho$ counted with multiplicity, $P_a(x)=\frac{a}{\pi(a^2+x^2)}$ for $a>0$, $Q_a(x)=\frac{a}{\pi(a^2+x^2)}$ for real $a\ne0$, $u_\theta(v)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\theta+iv)$ and $\mathfrak U_{1/2}=\sum_{\sigma_\rho=1/2}\delta_{\gamma_\rho}$. For $\theta>\frac12$ and $\theta+iv$ not a zero, $u_\theta=P_{\theta-1/2}*\mathfrak U_{1/2}+R_\theta$ with $R_\theta(v)=\sum_{\sigma_\rho>1/2}\bigl[Q_{\theta-\sigma_\rho}+Q_{\theta-1+\sigma_\rho}\bigr](v-\gamma_\rho)$, the sum over the zeros off the critical line each taken together with its reflection $1-\bar\rho$. In particular $u_1=P_{1/2}*\mathfrak U_{1/2}+R_1$, the pair of a zero off the line being positive at $\theta=1$ and signed only for $\theta<\sigma_\rho$. Under the Riemann hypothesis $R_\theta=0$.
results.label: cf:prop:transport

results.name: Local positivity of the Thorin density from any zero free region that narrows with the height
results.summary: If every zero has $\sigma_\rho\le1-\eta(\lvert\gamma_\rho\rvert)$ for a nonincreasing $\eta$ with values in $(0,\frac12]$, then $u_\theta(v)>0$ whenever $\theta>\frac12$, $\theta\ge1-\eta(\lvert v\rvert+\frac12)$ and $\xi(\theta+iv)\ne0$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function with zeros $\rho=\sigma_\rho+i\gamma_\rho$ and $u_\theta(v)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\theta+iv)$. Let $\eta:[0,\infty)\to(0,\frac12]$ be nonincreasing and suppose every zero satisfies $\sigma_\rho\le1-\eta(\lvert\gamma_\rho\rvert)$. Then $u_\theta(v)>0$ whenever $\theta>\frac12$, $\theta\ge1-\eta(\lvert v\rvert+\frac12)$ and $\xi(\theta+iv)\ne0$. The proof groups the zeros of the Hadamard sum into orbits of $\rho\mapsto1-\bar\rho$; an orbit with $\sigma_\rho>\theta$ is negative only within distance $\frac12$ of its ordinate.
results.label: cf:cor:localpos

results.name: The density tends to the critical zero counting measure as the level tends to one half, zeros off the line being invisible
results.summary: As $\theta\downarrow\frac12$ the densities $u_\theta$ converge in the sense of distributions to $\mathfrak U_{1/2}=\sum_{\sigma_\rho=1/2}\delta_{\gamma_\rho}$, because the pair of a zero off the line tends to $-P+P=0$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function with zeros $\rho=\sigma_\rho+i\gamma_\rho$ and $u_\theta(v)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\theta+iv)=\sum_\rho Q_{\theta-\sigma_\rho}(v-\gamma_\rho)$ with $Q_a(x)=\frac{a}{\pi(a^2+x^2)}$. As $\theta\downarrow\frac12$, in the sense of distributions, $u_\theta\to\mathfrak U_{1/2}=\sum_{\sigma_\rho=1/2}\delta_{\gamma_\rho}$. A zero $\rho$ off the line and its reflection $1-\bar\rho$ contribute $Q_{\theta-\sigma_\rho}+Q_{\theta-1+\sigma_\rho}\to Q_{1/2-\sigma_\rho}+Q_{\sigma_\rho-1/2}=0$, because $a\mapsto Q_a$ is continuous from $\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}$ to $L^1(\mathbb{R})$ and the far terms are bounded by $\lvert\gamma_\rho\rvert^{-2}$ uniformly in $\theta\in[\frac12,1]$.
results.label: cf:prop:ends

results.name: The four zeros of the Davenport and Heilbronn function off the critical line below height 200 and their enclosures
results.summary: Computation in ball arithmetic, certifying the zeros found by Spira (1994): the zeros of the Davenport and Heilbronn function $f$ with $0<\gamma<200$ off the line are exactly $0.8085171825+85.6993484854i$, $0.6508300806+114.1633427308i$, $0.5743560505+166.4793059132i$, $0.7242576946+176.7024612429i$ and their reflections, each certified as the only zero in a square of half width $10^{-16}$.
results.statement: Let $\kappa=(\sqrt{10-2\sqrt5}-2)/(\sqrt5-1)$ and $f(s)=5^{-s}\bigl[\zeta(s,\frac15)+\kappa\zeta(s,\frac25)-\kappa\zeta(s,\frac35)-\zeta(s,\frac45)\bigr]$ the Davenport and Heilbronn function, with $\zeta(s,a)$ the Hurwitz zeta function, and $\Lambda(s)=(5/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)f(s)$, which is entire with $\Lambda(s)=\Lambda(1-s)$. Computed in ball arithmetic: the zeros of $f$ off the critical line with $0<\gamma<200$ are $0.8085171825+85.6993484854i$, $0.6508300806+114.1633427308i$, $0.5743560505+166.4793059132i$, $0.7242576946+176.7024612429i$ together with their reflections in the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\frac12$, each the only zero in a square of half width $10^{-16}$ about its centre, so the printed decimals are correct. The count rests on $130$ zeros of $\Lambda$ with $0<\gamma<200$ by the argument principle against $122$ sign changes of $\Lambda(\frac12+it)$ on a grid of step $\frac1{50}$, the difference $8=2\cdot4$ being the off line zeros and their reflections. This is a computation and not a statement for all heights. The zeros were found by Spira (1994); the ball arithmetic enclosures and the count are the book's.
results.label: cf:res:dhzeros

results.name: A symmetric pair of zeros off the line exceeds a double zero on the line by a second order term in the deviation, growing like the fifth inverse power of the level
results.summary: At the common ordinate a pair at real parts $\frac12\pm\delta$ exceeds a double critical zero by $\frac{2\delta^2}{\pi a(a^2-\delta^2)}$ at level $a=\theta-\frac12$, and $\int(\partial_a^2P_a)^2=\frac3{4\pi a^5}$, so the information about $\delta$ is second order and grows like $a^{-5}$.
results.statement: Let $P_a(x)=\frac{a}{\pi(a^2+x^2)}$, $a=\theta-\frac12>\delta>0$. At the centre $v=\gamma$ the density at level $\theta$ of a pair of zeros at $\frac12\pm\delta+i\gamma$ exceeds that of a double zero at $\frac12+i\gamma$ by $\Delta(a,\delta)=\frac1\pi\bigl(\frac1{a-\delta}+\frac1{a+\delta}\bigr)-\frac2{\pi a}=\frac{2\delta^2}{\pi a(a^2-\delta^2)}$. In the parameter $\eta=\delta^2$ the pair differs from the double zero by $\eta\,\partial_a^2P_a+O(\eta^2)$, and $\int_{\mathbb{R}}(\partial_a^2P_a(x))^2dx=\frac3{4\pi a^5}$.
results.label: cf:prop:detect

results.name: Open: the best resolution of the symmetric pair parameter from data at levels above a threshold
results.summary: Posed as open: what resolution of $\eta=\delta^2$ is possible from levels $\theta\ge\theta_{\min}$, and does the pair parametrised particle filter reach it.
results.statement: Consider a symmetric pair of zeros of the completed Riemann zeta function at $\frac12\pm\delta+i\gamma$, with parameter $\eta=\delta^2$, and data given by the density $u_\theta(v)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\theta+iv)$ at levels $\theta\ge\theta_{\min}$ with observation error. What is the best possible resolution of $\eta$, and does the particle filter with the pair parametrisation reach it? This is posed as an open problem.
results.label: cf:op:pairres

results.name: Non asymptotic concentration inequality for a Feynman Kac particle system with multinomial resampling and fixed potentials under a ratio minorisation of the mutation kernels
results.summary: For the idealised system with multinomial resampling, fixed potentials and fixed kernels, $\mathbb P(\lvert\eta_n^N(f)-\eta_n(f)\rvert\ge x)\le2(n+1)\exp(-Nx^2/(2S_n^2))$ and the root mean square error is at most $S_n/\sqrt N$, for every $f$ of oscillation at most one; it does not cover the samplers run in the chapter.
results.statement: Let $\eta_0$ be a probability measure on a space $E$, $G_0,\dots,G_{n-1}$ positive bounded potentials with $\sup G_k/\inf G_k<\infty$, $M_1,\dots,M_n$ Markov kernels, $\eta_{k+1}=\Psi_{G_k}(\eta_k)M_{k+1}$ with $\Psi_G(\mu)(dx)=G(x)\mu(dx)/\mu(G)$, and let $\eta_k^N$ be the empirical measure of the particle system that draws $N$ independent particles from $\eta_0$ and then, given generation $k$, $N$ independent particles from $\Psi_{G_k}(\eta_k^N)M_{k+1}$ (multinomial resampling followed by mutation). With $\mathcal Q_{k+1}(x,dy)=G_k(x)M_{k+1}(x,dy)$, $G_{k,n}=\mathcal Q_{k+1}\cdots\mathcal Q_n(1)$, $\mathcal P_{k,n}f=\mathcal Q_{k+1}\cdots\mathcal Q_n(f)/G_{k,n}$, $g_{k,n}=\sup_{x,y}G_{k,n}(x)/G_{k,n}(y)$, $\varkappa_{k,n}$ the Dobrushin coefficient of $\mathcal P_{k,n}$ and $S_n=\sum_{k=0}^ng_{k,n}\varkappa_{k,n}$, for every measurable $f$ with oscillation at most $1$, every $N$ and every $x>0$, $\mathbb P(\lvert\eta_n^N(f)-\eta_n(f)\rvert\ge x)\le2(n+1)\exp(-Nx^2/(2S_n^2))$ and $\mathbb E[(\eta_n^N(f)-\eta_n(f))^2]^{1/2}\le S_n/\sqrt N$. The theorem covers a fixed schedule and fixed kernels, not samplers with adaptive tempering or random walk Metropolis moves. The proof is given (in the style of Del Moral 2004).
results.label: cf:thm:conc

results.name: Concentration bound uniform in the number of tempering steps for the Cauchy flow when the parameters stay away from the levels
results.summary: On the parameter space with zeros at distance at least $\varsigma$ from every level, the total log likelihood has finite oscillation $\Omega_\varsigma$, and with equal tempering increments and ratio minorised kernels the error probability is at most $2\exp(-\frac12Nx^2\epsilon^6e^{-2c})$ for every number of steps.
results.statement: Consider the Gaussian tolerance posterior of the chapter, in which zeros $\sigma_j+i\gamma_j$, $j\le K$, in a window of heights are fitted to the values $y_l(v_i)$ of the density at levels $\theta_l$ and heights $v_i$ with tolerance $\varepsilon$, and the parameter space is restricted to $\Theta_\varsigma=\{z:\lvert\theta_l-\sigma_j\rvert\ge\varsigma\text{ for all levels }\theta_l\text{ and zeros }j\}$. Then the total log likelihood $\ell$ has $\operatorname{osc}(\ell)\le\Omega_\varsigma=\frac1{2\varepsilon^2}\sum_{l,i}\bigl(\lvert y_l(v_i)\rvert+\frac K{\pi\varsigma}\bigr)^2$, and a tempering schedule with $n=\max(1,\lceil\Omega_\varsigma/c\rceil)$ equal increments has potentials with $\sup G/\inf G\le e^c$. If the mutation kernels satisfy the ratio minorisation $M(x,\cdot)\ge\epsilon M(y,\cdot)$ for all $x,y$, then for every posterior functional $f$ of oscillation at most one, for the idealised particle system of the concentration theorem of the chapter, $\mathbb P(\lvert\eta_n^N(f)-\eta_n(f)\rvert\ge x)\le2\exp(-\frac12Nx^2\epsilon^6e^{-2c})$ for every $N$ and every $x>0$. Without the minorisation the concentration theorem holds with its finite constant $S_n$, which is not uniform in $n$. Random walk Metropolis kernels do not satisfy the minorisation.
results.label: cf:cor:cauchyconc

results.name: What the density at level one determines: unique continuation for entire functions of order one, a counterexample without the order condition, and the Poisson inversion
results.summary: For real entire functions of order at most one with zeros in the strip, equal densities at level one on an interval give equal logarithmic derivatives and equal densities at every level; the order hypothesis cannot be dropped, and under no zero at or beyond $\frac34$ recovering $u_{3/4}$ from $u_1$ multiplies the error at frequency $\omega$ by $e^{\lvert\omega\rvert/4}$.
results.statement: Let $F_1,F_2$ be real entire functions of order at most one with all zeros in $0<\operatorname{Re}s<1$ and $u^{(j)}_\theta(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(F_j'/F_j)(\theta+iv)$. (a) If $u^{(1)}_1=u^{(2)}_1$ on an interval then $F_1'/F_1=F_2'/F_2$, so $u^{(1)}_\theta=u^{(2)}_\theta$ for every $\theta$.
