results.statement: Let $e_k,e_k'$ be independent standard exponential variables and $F_n(w)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[\bigl(\sum_{k\le n}k^{-2}(e_k+e_k')\bigr)^w\bigr]$ for $\operatorname{Re}w>-2$. Conjecture T says that for every $n\ge1$, $F_n$ has no zeros with $\operatorname{Re}w>\frac14$ (which, if it held for infinitely many $n$, would imply the Riemann Hypothesis by Hurwitz's theorem, since $F_n\to2\pi^w\xi(2w)$). Conjecture T is false: for all sufficiently large $n$, $F_n$ has a zero with $\operatorname{Re}w>\frac14$ near $\rho_{213}/2$, where $\rho_{213}=\frac12+i\gamma_{213}$ and $\gamma_{213}=415.4552\ldots$ is the ordinate of the 213th zero of the zeta function in the upper half plane. The proof uses that the first $1.5\times10^9$ zeros lie on the critical line and are simple (van de Lune, te Riele and Winter), the first order displacement $\kappa(\rho)=\rho\,\xi(\rho-2)/(2\pi\,\xi'(\rho))$ of the zero of $F_n$ near $\rho/2$, and a ball arithmetic enclosure $233.95<\operatorname{Re}\kappa(\rho_{213})<233.96$. The statement is for all sufficiently large $n$ and gives no explicit $n$; the book notes that the first order regime requires $n$ large compared with $|\kappa(\rho_{213})|\approx2311$.
results.label: rz:cor:Tfalse

results.name: Symmetrised truncations: symmetry, limit and persistence of simple zeros on the line
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: The symmetrised truncations $K_n$ are symmetric about the line $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$, converge to $4\xi(2w)$, and keep every simple zero of $\xi(2w)$ on the line as a zero exactly on the line for all large $n$.
results.statement: Let $e_k,e_k'$ be independent standard exponential variables, $F_n(w)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[\bigl(\sum_{k\le n}k^{-2}(e_k+e_k')\bigr)^w\bigr]$ for $\operatorname{Re}w>-2$, and define the symmetrised truncation and its restriction to the line by \[ K_n(w)=\pi^{-w}F_n(w)+\pi^{w-\frac12}F_n(\tfrac12-w),\qquad Z_n(y)=K_n(\tfrac14+iy). \] Then $K_n(\frac12-w)=K_n(w)$ and $K_n(\bar w)=\overline{K_n(w)}$, so $Z_n$ is real for real $y$ and the zeros of $K_n$ off the line $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$ come in quadruples. As $n\to\infty$, $K_n\to4\,\xi(2w)$ locally uniformly on $-\frac74<\operatorname{Re}w<\frac94$, where $\xi$ is the completed zeta function. Every simple zero $\frac14+i\frac\gamma2$ of $\xi(2w)$ on the line $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$ is, for all large $n$, the limit of a zero of $K_n$ lying exactly on that line.
results.label: rz:prop:symtrunc

results.name: Real rooted symmetrised truncations for infinitely many n imply the Riemann Hypothesis
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: If for infinitely many $n$ all zeros of the symmetrised truncation $K_n$ in the strip $0<\operatorname{Re}w<\frac12$ lie on the line $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$, then the Riemann Hypothesis holds.
results.statement: Let $e_k,e_k'$ be independent standard exponential variables, $F_n(w)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[\bigl(\sum_{k\le n}k^{-2}(e_k+e_k')\bigr)^w\bigr]$ for $\operatorname{Re}w>-2$, and $K_n(w)=\pi^{-w}F_n(w)+\pi^{w-\frac12}F_n(\tfrac12-w)$. If for infinitely many $n$ all zeros of $K_n$ in the strip $0<\operatorname{Re}w<\frac12$ lie on the line $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$, then the Riemann Hypothesis holds.
results.label: rz:thm:symhurwitz

results.name: Zeros of the approximate functional equation truncations of zeta, N equal to 2 and 3
results.summary: All but finitely many zeros of the approximate functional equation truncation of zeta with N equal to 2 lie on the critical line and are counted by theta over pi plus a bounded error, whereas the truncation with N equal to 3 has zeros off the line at arbitrarily large heights with real parts approaching every number in an interval; this is from a note of Nicholas Polson (compare Spira and Gonek and Montgomery).
results.statement: Let $\chi$ be the factor in $\zeta(s)=\chi(s)\zeta(1-s)$, $\zeta_N(s)=\sum_{m\le N}m^{-s}+\chi(s)\sum_{m\le N}m^{s-1}$ and $\vartheta$ the Riemann Siegel theta function. Write $s=\sigma+i\tau$. (i) All but finitely many zeros of $\zeta_2$ in $0<\sigma<1$ lie on the critical line $\sigma=\frac12$, and the number of zeros with $0<\tau\le T$ is $\vartheta(T)/\pi+O(1)$. (ii) Let $\sigma^*$ be the root of $2^{-\sigma}+3^{-\sigma}=1$. For every $\sigma_0\in(\frac12,\sigma^*)$ there are zeros $\sigma_k+i\tau_k$ of $\zeta_3$ with $\tau_k\to\infty$ and $\sigma_k\to\sigma_0$. In particular $\zeta_3$ has zeros off the critical line at arbitrarily large heights.
results.label: rz:prop:zetaN

results.name: Single term bound: no off line zeros of the symmetrised truncation above explicit heights
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: A single term bound shows that for $n=1$ to $6$, $8$ and $10$ the symmetrised truncation $K_n$ has no zero off the line in the strip above explicit heights $Y_n$ between $4.81$ and $21232$, which are obtained by evaluating the explicit bounds numerically.
results.statement: For $n\ge1$ let $\alpha_k,\beta_k$ ($k\le n$) be defined by the partial fraction expansion $\prod_{j\le n}(1+\lambda/j^2)^{-2}=\sum_{k\le n}k^{-2}\bigl\{\alpha_k(1+\lambda/k^2)^{-1}+\beta_k(1+\lambda/k^2)^{-2}\bigr\}$ (so $\beta_k=k^2\prod_{j\le n,\,j\ne k}(1-k^2/j^2)^{-2}$ and $\alpha_k=-2\beta_k\sum_{j\le n,\,j\ne k}k^2/(j^2-k^2)$), and put $Q_n(u)=\sum_{k\le n}k^{-2u}(\alpha_k+\beta_ku)$. Then $F_n(u-1)=\Gamma(u)Q_n(u)$ for $F_n(w)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[\bigl(\sum_{k\le n}k^{-2}(e_k+e_k')\bigr)^w\bigr]$ with $e_k,e_k'$ independent standard exponentials, and the symmetrised truncation is $K_n(w)=\pi^{-w}F_n(w)+\pi^{w-\frac12}F_n(\frac12-w)$. For $y>|\alpha_1|/|\beta_1|$ let \[ \delta_n(y)=\sum_{k=2}^nk^{-2}\frac{|\beta_k|y+|\alpha_k|}{|\beta_1|y-|\alpha_1|},\qquad \delta_n'(y)=\sum_{k=2}^nk^{-2}\frac{2\log k\,(|\beta_k|y+|\alpha_k|)+|\beta_k|}{|\beta_1|y-|\alpha_1|}+\delta_n(y)\,\frac{|\beta_1|}{|\beta_1|y-|\alpha_1|}, \] where $\delta_n'$ is a bound for a derivative used in the proof and is not the derivative of $\delta_n$. If $\delta_n(y)<1$ and \[ \log\frac y\pi-\frac1y-\frac{|\beta_1|}{|\beta_1|y-|\alpha_1|}-\frac{\delta_n'(y)}{1-\delta_n(y)}>0, \] then $K_n$ has no zeros off the line $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$ in $0<\operatorname{Re}w<\frac12$ at any height (imaginary part) at least $y$. The condition holds for all $y\ge Y_n$, with $Y_1=4.81$, $Y_2=5.85$, $Y_3=7.11$, $Y_4=9.08$, $Y_5=12.8$, $Y_6=20.8$, $Y_8=104.1$ and $Y_{10}=21232$ (values obtained by evaluating the bounds with the exact coefficients).
results.label: rz:thm:Yn

results.name: Conjecture S for n up to 6 and n = 8 above explicit heights
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: Conjecture S is proved for $n=1$ to $6$ and $n=8$ above the explicit heights of the single term bound, which are evaluated numerically, and below those heights it is only checked numerically by floating point argument principle counts.
results.statement: Let $K_n(w)=\pi^{-w}F_n(w)+\pi^{w-\frac12}F_n(\frac12-w)$ be the symmetrised truncation, with $F_n(w)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[\bigl(\sum_{k\le n}k^{-2}(e_k+e_k')\bigr)^w\bigr]$ and $e_k,e_k'$ independent standard exponential variables. Conjecture S says that all zeros of $K_n$ in the strip $0<\operatorname{Re}w<\frac12$ lie on the line $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$. Proved: for $n=1,2,3,4,5,6,8$ the zeros of $K_n$ in the strip at height at least $Y_n$ lie on the line, with $Y_1=4.81$, $Y_2=5.85$, $Y_3=7.11$, $Y_4=9.08$, $Y_5=12.8$, $Y_6=20.8$, $Y_8=104.1$ (the heights of the single term bound). Below these heights the book verifies the same statement for these $n$ only numerically, by floating point argument principle counts and not by an enclosure (up to heights $6,7,8$ for $n=1,2,3$, up to $70$ for $4\le n\le6$ and up to $140$ for $n=8$); that part is not a certified result.
results.label: rz:cor:Ssmall

results.name: Torus bound for the symmetrised truncations
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: Explicit inequalities on the extremes of the Dirichlet polynomial $P_n$ and its logarithmic derivative over the torus of prime phases imply that the symmetrised truncation $K_n$ has no zero off the line $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$ in the strip $0<\operatorname{Re}w<\frac12$ at a given height or above.
results.statement: Let $\alpha_k,\beta_k$ ($k\le n$) be defined by $\prod_{j\le n}(1+\lambda/j^2)^{-2}=\sum_{k\le n}k^{-2}\bigl\{\alpha_k(1+\lambda/k^2)^{-1}+\beta_k(1+\lambda/k^2)^{-2}\bigr\}$, so that $F_n(u-1)=\Gamma(u)Q_n(u)$ with $Q_n(u)=\sum_{k\le n}k^{-2u}(\alpha_k+\beta_ku)=uP_n(u)+R_n(u)$, $P_n(u)=\sum_{k\le n}\beta_kk^{-2u}$, $R_n(u)=\sum_{k\le n}\alpha_kk^{-2u}$, for $F_n(w)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[\bigl(\sum_{k\le n}k^{-2}(e_k+e_k')\bigr)^w\bigr]$ with $e_k,e_k'$ independent standard exponentials, and let $K_n(w)=\pi^{-w}F_n(w)+\pi^{w-\frac12}F_n(\frac12-w)$. For real $x$ and $\omega=(\omega_p)_{p\le n}$ in the torus $\mathbb{T}^{\pi(n)}$ of phases indexed by the primes $p\le n$, put $P_n(x,\omega)=\sum_{k\le n}\beta_kk^{-2x}\exp\bigl(-i\sum_{p\le n}v_p(k)\,\omega_p\bigr)$, where $v_p(k)$ is the exponent of $p$ in $k$, let $P_n'(x,\omega)=-\sum_{k\le n}2\log k\,\beta_kk^{-2x}\exp\bigl(-i\sum_{p\le n}v_p(k)\,\omega_p\bigr)$, $r(x)=\sum_{k\le n}|\alpha_k|k^{-2x}$ and $r'(x)=\sum_{k\le n}2\log k\,|\alpha_k|k^{-2x}$. Let $m_n=\min|P_n(x,\omega)|$, $M_n=\max\{-\operatorname{Re}(P_n'/P_n)(x,\omega)\}$ and $\ell_n=\max|P_n'/P_n|(x,\omega)$ over $\omega\in\mathbb{T}^{\pi(n)}$ and the band $1.2\le x\le1.3$, and \[ B_n(y)=\max_{0.3\le\sigma\le\frac12,\ \omega}\ \frac{\log\bigl(|P_n(\tfrac32-\sigma,\omega)|+r(\tfrac32-\sigma)/y\bigr)-\log\bigl(|P_n(1+\sigma,\omega)|-r(1+\sigma)/y\bigr)}{2\sigma-\frac12}. \] If $m_n>r(1.2)/y$, \[ \log\frac y\pi-\frac2y-M_n-\frac{\ell_n\,r(1.2)+r'(1.2)+r(1.2)/y}{y\,\bigl(m_n-r(1.2)/y\bigr)}>0\quad\text{and}\quad\log\frac y\pi-\frac1y>B_n(y), \] then $K_n$ has no zeros off the line $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$ in $0<\operatorname{Re}w<\frac12$ at height $y$, and the same holds at every larger height.
results.label: rz:thm:torus

results.name: Conjecture S for n up to 24, 32 and 36 above explicit thresholds
results.origin_text: Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: Conjecture S is proved for $n=7$, $9$ to $24$, $32$ and $36$ above explicit height thresholds by torus bounds certified in ball arithmetic, and below the thresholds it is only checked numerically; with the small $n$ results it covers every $n\le24$ and $n=32,36$.
results.statement: Let $K_n(w)=\pi^{-w}F_n(w)+\pi^{w-\frac12}F_n(\frac12-w)$ be the symmetrised truncation, with $F_n(w)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[\bigl(\sum_{k\le n}k^{-2}(e_k+e_k')\bigr)^w\bigr]$ and $e_k,e_k'$ independent standard exponential variables. Conjecture S says that all zeros of $K_n$ in the strip $0<\operatorname{Re}w<\frac12$ lie on the line $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$. Proved, by torus bounds whose final boxes are enclosed in ball arithmetic: for $n=16,17,\dots,24,32,36$ the zeros of $K_n$ in the strip at height at least the threshold lie on the line, with thresholds $30,34,37,41,46,50,56,62,69$ for $n=16,\dots,24$ and $213$, $558$ for $n=32$, $36$; and the same holds for $n=7$ and $9\le n\le15$ above the thresholds $14,24,31,41,57,84,131,229$ for $n=7,9,10,11,12,13,14,15$. For all these $n$ the statement is also verified numerically below the thresholds, by floating point argument principle counts, which are not certified. Together with the case $n=1,\dots,6,8$ above explicit heights, this covers every $n\le24$ and $n=32,36$. The torus bounds behind the thresholds are proved in the book; in Polson's 2026 book On Hilbert's 8th Problem the corresponding corollary supposes that the extremes of the torus function, estimated by global optimisation and not enclosed, are bounds.
results.supersedes: Corollary 30.11 of Polson (2026) is conditional: it supposes that the torus extremes, estimated by global optimisation and not enclosed, are bounds.
results.label: rz:cor:Storus

results.name: Thorin positivity of R is Weil's criterion
results.origin_text: Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: The reciprocal Xi function $R$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution exactly when Weil's distribution is positive definite, by combining Polson's rigidity theorem with Weil's criterion, so Thorin positivity of $R$ is Weil's criterion in other coordinates and gives no new criterion.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ and $R(s)=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)$. Let $D(x)=\sum_\rho e^{(\rho-\frac12)x}$ be Weil's distribution, summed over the nontrivial zeros $\rho$ of $\zeta$, whose action on a test function $h$ is $\sum_\rho\hat h(\gamma_\rho)$ with $\gamma_\rho=-i(\rho-\frac12)$ and $\hat h$ the Fourier transform of $h$. Then $R$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution (whose Thorin measure is then $\sum_{\gamma>0}\delta_{\gamma^2}$ over the ordinates of the zeros) if and only if $D$ is positive definite, that is, $\sum_\rho\hat h(\gamma_\rho)\ge0$ for every $h=g*\tilde g$ with $g$ smooth and compactly supported and $\tilde g(x)=\overline{g(-x)}$. Both conditions are equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis: the first by Proposition 3.4 of Polson's 2026 book On Hilbert's 8th Problem, the second by Weil's criterion (Weil 1952; Bombieri 2000). The proposition combines the two; the correspondence between Thorin measures and Weil's distribution behind it is formal.
results.supersedes: Theorem 30.13 of Polson (2026) states the correspondence between Thorin positivity of $R$ and positive definiteness of Weil's distribution as a theorem.
results.label: rz:thm:weil

results.name: Weil positivity on the Bernstein cone
results.origin_text: Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: Unconditionally, Weil's functional $\sum_\rho\hat h(\gamma_\rho)$ is positive for every test function $\hat h$ that is a Laplace transform in $r^2$ of a nonnegative weight under an integrability condition, including Thorin type products, $\operatorname{sech}(cr)$ and $(1+r^2/a)^{-m}$; it integrates the positivity of the heat trace of the zeros (Polson 2026, Theorem A), for which the book gives a second proof certified with the verification of RH to height 50 and interval enclosures.
results.statement: For $y>0$ let $W(y)=\frac12\sum_\rho e^{y(\rho-\frac12)^2}$, the sum over all nontrivial zeros $\rho$ of the Riemann zeta function (the heat trace of the zeros), and put $\gamma_\rho=-i(\rho-\frac12)$. Let $\hat h(r)=\int_0^\infty e^{-yr^2}g(y)\,dy$ with $g\ge0$, $g\not\equiv0$ and $\int_0^1g(y)\,y^{-1/2}\bigl(1+\log(1/y)\bigr)\,dy+\int_1^\infty g(y)\,dy<\infty$, so that $\hat h$ is a completely monotone function of $r^2$. Then \[ \sum_\rho\hat h(\gamma_\rho)=2\int_0^\infty W(y)\,g(y)\,dy>0, \] the sum being over all nontrivial zeros. In particular Weil's functional $\sum_\rho\hat h(\gamma_\rho)$ is positive for every test function of Thorin type $\hat h(r)=\prod_k(1+r^2/t_k)^{-1}$ (a nonempty product with $t_k>0$ and $\sum_k1/t_k<\infty$), for $\hat h(r)=\operatorname{sech}(cr)$ with $c>0$, and for $\hat h(r)=(1+r^2/a)^{-m}$ with $a>0$ and $m>\frac12$. No hypothesis on the zeros is made. The positivity of $W(y)$ for every $y>0$, which with the identity gives the result, is Theorem A of Polson's 2026 book On Hilbert's 8th Problem; the book gives a second proof of it, which uses the verification of the Riemann Hypothesis up to height $50$ and interval enclosures, and corrects the integrability condition and the examples of Theorem 30.14 of that book.
results.supersedes: Theorem 30.14 of Polson (2026) has the integrability condition with $\log(1/y)$ in place of $1+\log(1/y)$, Thorin products without nonemptiness or $\sum_k1/t_k<\infty$, and $(1+r^2/a)^{-m}$ without $m>\frac12$, and its proof uses the verification of the Riemann Hypothesis to height $3\times10^{12}$.
results.label: rz:thm:bernsteincone

results.name: The de Bruijn Newman flow as a path of GGCs
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: For every $t$ at least the de Bruijn Newman constant, $R_t=H_t(0)/H_t(2i\sqrt s)$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution with atoms at the squared half zeros of $H_t$, so it is a GGC for every $t\ge0.2$ unconditionally, and the Riemann Hypothesis holds exactly when $R_t$ is a GGC for arbitrarily small $t>0$.
results.statement: Let $\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}\bigl(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u}\bigr)\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})$, $H_t(z)=\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cos(zu)\,du$ (so that $H_0(z)=\frac18\xi(\frac12+\frac{iz}2)$ for the completed zeta function $\xi$) and $R_t(s)=H_t(0)/H_t(2i\sqrt s)$, so that $R_0(s)=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)=R(s)$. Let $\Lambda$ be the de Bruijn Newman constant, so that $H_t$ has only real zeros exactly when $t\ge\Lambda$. Then for every $t\ge\Lambda$, $R_t$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution with Thorin measure $\sum_k\delta_{(z_k(t)/2)^2}$, where $z_k(t)>0$ are the positive zeros of $H_t$ listed with multiplicity. In particular $R_t$ is a GGC for every $t\ge0.2$, unconditionally (using the bound $\Lambda\le0.2$ of Platt and Trudgian, which improves the bound $0.22$ of the Polymath project). The Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if $R_t$ is a GGC for arbitrarily small $t>0$ (and, since $\Lambda\ge0$ by Rodgers and Tao, if and only if $\Lambda=0$).
results.label: rz:thm:dbn

results.name: No GGC multiplier can create the positivity of R
results.origin_text: Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: Multiplying $R$ by the Laplace transform of any generalised gamma convolution gives a generalised gamma convolution exactly when the Riemann Hypothesis holds, so no such multiplier can manufacture the positivity; for the normalised reciprocal zeta function only one direction holds for every multiplier.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$, $R(s)=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)$, $G(s)=\Gamma(\frac14+\frac{\sqrt s}2)\,\pi^{-\sqrt s/2}/\Gamma(\frac14)$ and $\varphi(s)=R(s)G(s)=\zeta(\frac12)/\bigl((1-4s)\zeta(\frac12+\sqrt s)\bigr)$, and let $c=\frac12(\log\pi-\psi(\frac14))\approx2.68609$ with $\psi$ the digamma function. Let $V$ be the Laplace transform of any generalised gamma convolution (GGC). Then $V\cdot R$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC if and only if the Riemann Hypothesis holds. For $\varphi$ only one direction holds for every $V$: if $V\cdot\varphi$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC, then the Riemann Hypothesis holds. The converse depends on $V$: it fails for $V\equiv1$ (since $\varphi$ is not a GGC, unconditionally), and holds for $V(s)=e^{-c\sqrt s}/G(s)$, which is the Laplace transform of a GGC and for which $V\varphi=e^{-c\sqrt s}R$ is the floor of the reciprocal Xi function. In Polson's 2026 book On Hilbert's 8th Problem the same is claimed with $\varphi$ in place of $R$, that is, both directions for every multiplier, which fails for $V\equiv1$; the book keeps one direction.
results.supersedes: Proposition 30.16 of Polson (2026) states that the same is true with $\varphi$ in place of $R$, that is, both directions for every generalised gamma convolution multiplier, which fails for the multiplier $1$ by Theorem 28.9 of that book.
results.label: rz:prop:nomult

results.name: Conjecture S for infinitely many n
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: The book asks for a proof that the symmetrised truncations $K_n$ have all their zeros in the strip $0<\operatorname{Re}w<\frac12$ on the line $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$ for infinitely many $n$, which would imply the Riemann Hypothesis.
results.statement: Let $e_k,e_k'$ be independent standard exponential variables, $F_n(w)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[\bigl(\sum_{k\le n}k^{-2}(e_k+e_k')\bigr)^w\bigr]$ for $\operatorname{Re}w>-2$, and $K_n(w)=\pi^{-w}F_n(w)+\pi^{w-\frac12}F_n(\frac12-w)$ the symmetrised truncation. Conjecture S: for every $n\ge1$ all zeros of $K_n$ in the strip $0<\operatorname{Re}w<\frac12$ lie on the line $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$. Problem: prove that this holds for infinitely many $n$; by a Hurwitz argument this would imply the Riemann Hypothesis. The book proves it above explicit heights for $n\le24$ and $n=32,36$ and checks it numerically below those heights. Since the one sided Conjecture T (no zero of $F_n$ with $\operatorname{Re}w>\frac14$) and the Hermite Biehler inequality for $\pi^{-w}F_n(w)$ fail for large $n$, a proof must establish real rootedness without a one sided inequality, for instance by an interlacing argument in $n$, or by following the zeros of $K_n(\frac14+iy)$ continuously in a parameter interpolating between $n$ and $n+1$ and excluding collisions of zeros on the line.
results.label: rz:prob:S

results.name: Torus method beyond n = 36
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: The book asks for an extension of the torus bound for the symmetrised truncations with narrower bands around $x=\frac54$, and for the first $n$ at which the torus function $P_n$ has zeros with $x\ge\frac54$.
results.statement: Let $\alpha_k,\beta_k$ ($k\le n$) be the partial fraction coefficients of the Laplace transform $\prod_{j\le n}(1+\lambda/j^2)^{-2}$ of $\sum_{k\le n}k^{-2}(e_k+e_k')$, with $\beta_k=k^2\prod_{j\le n,\,j\ne k}(1-k^2/j^2)^{-2}$, and let $P_n(x,\omega)=\sum_{k\le n}\beta_kk^{-2x}\exp\bigl(-i\sum_{p\le n}v_p(k)\,\omega_p\bigr)$ be the torus function of the Dirichlet polynomial $P_n(u)=\sum_{k\le n}\beta_kk^{-2u}$ (phases $\omega_p$ indexed by the primes $p\le n$, $v_p(k)$ the exponent of $p$ in $k$). The torus method proves Conjecture S, that all zeros of the symmetrised truncation $K_n$ in $0<\operatorname{Re}w<\frac12$ lie on $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$, above explicit heights for $n=7$, $9\le n\le24$ and $n=32,36$ (the cases $n\le6$ and $n=8$ come from a single term bound); at $n=40$ the threshold, estimated by optimisation and not certified, is already near $4900$, and with the band $1.2\le x\le1.3$ the method ends between $n=40$ and $n=44$, where the torus minimum of $|P_n|$ in the band reaches zero. Problem: extend the torus bound with narrower bands around $x=\frac54$, and find the first $n$ at which $P_n$ has torus zeros with $x\ge\frac54$.
results.label: rz:prob:torus

results.name: From finite order to all orders for the floor
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: The book asks whether the argument that proves $(-1)^nk^{(n)}(y)>0$ for the canonical function $k$ of the floor of the reciprocal Xi function up to order $10^{10}$ extends to every order, which would imply the Riemann Hypothesis; the signs are already known to order $10^{17}$ (Polson 2017, version 24 of 2026) and, by the book's heat trace estimates, to order $1.16\times10^{25}$.
results.statement: Let $W(y)=\frac12\sum_\rho e^{y(\rho-\frac12)^2}$, the sum over the nontrivial zeros $\rho$ of the Riemann zeta function, let $c=\frac12(\log\pi-\psi(\frac14))\approx2.68609$, and let $k(y)=W(y)+c/(2\sqrt{\pi y})$ be the canonical function of the floor $e^{-c\sqrt s}\,\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)$ of the reciprocal Xi function. The book proves, by a two range argument, that $(-1)^nk^{(n)}(y)>0$ for every $y>0$ and every $n\le10^{10}$, the bound on $n$ in that argument coming only from the height $3\times10^{12}$ to which the Riemann Hypothesis is verified, and the small $y$ branch of the proof holds for every $n$ on $(0,0.05/n]$. This is a separate proof of a smaller range: the same signs hold for every $n\le10^{17}$ by Theorem 7.10 of Polson's arXiv paper 1708.02653 (version 24, 2026), which proves them for $W$, and the book proves them for every $n\le1.16\times10^{25}$ by sharper estimates of the heat trace; the signs for every $n$ would make $k$ completely monotone, which is equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis. Problem: can the two regimes be made to overlap for all $n$? This asks for a prime side estimate for $(-1)^nk^{(n)}(y)$ on a range $y\le y_n$ with $y_n$ growing at least linearly in $n$. In the proof the obstruction is the factor $2^n$ in the Cauchy estimate on the circle of radius $y/2$; a circle of radius close to $y$ loses only a factor of order $n$, but that argument also stops at a finite order.
results.label: rz:prob:allorders

results.name: Beyond the Bernstein cone
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: The book asks for the largest cone of test functions, closed under the operations that preserve the Thorin structure, on which Weil positivity can be proved unconditionally, and for how far such a cone can localise in height.
results.statement: Weil's functional $\sum_\rho\hat h(\gamma_\rho)$, with $\gamma_\rho=-i(\rho-\frac12)$ for the nontrivial zeros $\rho$ of the Riemann zeta function, is unconditionally positive for every test function $\hat h$ completely monotone in $r^2$ under an integrability condition (the Bernstein cone). Problem: find the largest cone of test functions, closed under the operations that preserve the Thorin structure, on which positivity of Weil's functional can be proved unconditionally, and determine how far it can localise in height.
results.label: rz:prob:cone

results.name: Deforming the binary product
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: The book asks where and how the positivity of the interference pattern of arithmetic progressions in the pseudo spectral trace formula can fail along the path from the binary product at $\sigma=0$ to the critical line.
results.statement: With the necklace weights $b_n(q)$ of the Vere-Jones factorisation, each Euler factor $(1-p^{-\sigma-u})^{-1}$ of $\zeta(\sigma+u)$ equals $\prod_{n\ge1}(1+p^{-nu})^{b_n(p^{-\sigma})}$, with integer multiplicities $0$ and $1$ at $\sigma=0$ (Euler's binary product) and necklace multiplicities $b_n(p^{-1/2})$ at $\sigma=\frac12$. The pseudo spectral trace formula writes the heat trace of the zeros of $\zeta$ (under the Riemann Hypothesis $\sum_{\gamma>0}e^{-x\gamma^2}$, and in general $\frac12\sum_\rho e^{x(\rho-\frac12)^2}$), net of its smooth part, as $e^{x/4}$ plus the sum over primes $p$ and $n\ge1$ of $b_n(p^{-1/2})$ times the heat trace $\sum_{k\ge0}e^{-x((2k+1)\pi/(n\log p))^2}$ of the arithmetic progression $(2k+1)\pi/(n\log p)$, net of its mean $n\log p/(4\sqrt{\pi x})$. Problem: follow this formula along the path $q=p^{-\sigma}$, $0\le\sigma\le\frac12$, and determine where and how the positivity of the interference pattern of the progressions can fail.
results.label: rz:prob:binary

results.name: Regularising the autocorrelation of the Pólya kernel
results.origin_text: Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: The book asks for the regularised form of the Meixner characteristic function convolved with the positive lattice measure $\mathcal A$, and whether it has a Thorin or Lee and Yang structure in $v$.
results.statement: Let $p(\tau)=|\Gamma(\frac14+\frac{i\tau}2)|^2/(2^{3/2}\pi^{3/2})$ be the Meixner density, $\Phi$ the Pólya kernel (an even function with Fourier transform $\Xi(\tau)=\xi(\frac12+i\tau)$) and $\mathcal C(v)=\int p(\tau)\,|\zeta(\frac12+i\tau)|^2e^{iv\tau}\,d\tau$. Then $(\Phi*\Phi)(v)=2^{-3/2}\bigl(\frac{d^2}{dv^2}-\frac14\bigr)^2\mathcal C(v)$. Formally $\mathcal C=\operatorname{sech}(\cdot)^{1/2}*\mathcal A$, where $\operatorname{sech}(v)^{1/2}$ is the characteristic function of the Meixner law and $\mathcal A=\sum_{m,n\ge1}(mn)^{-1/2}\delta_{\log(m/n)}$ is a positive, positive definite measure. The lattice series diverges: truncated at $m,n\le X$ it grows linearly in $X$, through the square of the pole term of the partial sums of $\zeta$, and the factor $(\frac{d^2}{dv^2}-\frac14)^2$ does not remove this growth. Problem: find the regularised form of $\operatorname{sech}(\cdot)^{1/2}*\mathcal A$ and decide whether it has a Thorin or Lee and Yang structure in $v$. In Polson's 2026 book On Hilbert's 8th Problem the problem is posed up to a logarithmic divergence removed by the pole; the book finds linear growth that the factor does not remove.
results.supersedes: Open Problem 30.22 of Polson (2026) poses the problem up to a logarithmic divergence removed by the pole.
results.label: rz:prob:meixner

results.name: Unimodality of w and of the density f
results.origin_text: Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: The book asks for proofs that the canonical function $w$ of the normalised reciprocal zeta function and the density $f$ of its law are unimodal, which is supported only by numerical evidence.
results.statement: Let $w(x)=e^{x/4}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{4\pi x}}\sum_{n\ge2}\Lambda(n)\,n^{-1/2}e^{-(\log n)^2/4x}$ be the canonical function of the normalised reciprocal zeta function $\varphi(s)=\zeta(\frac12)/\bigl((1-4s)\zeta(\frac12+\sqrt s)\bigr)$ and $f$ the density of the law with Laplace transform $\varphi$, which satisfies Steutel's equation $xf(x)=\int_0^xf(x-y)\,w(y)\,dy$. The book proves that $w'>0$ on $(0,0.004]$ and $w'<0$ on $[4.52,\infty)$; a grid evaluation (computed, not proved) finds exactly one sign change of $w'$ on $[0.004,4.6]$, at $x_m=0.015851\ldots$, and numerically $f$ rises from $0.365089$ to its maximum $0.366883$ at $x=0.024046$ and then decreases. Problem: prove that $w$ is unimodal, and prove that $f$ is unimodal with mode near $0.0240$, for instance from Steutel's equation and the unimodality of $w$. Yamazato's theorem, that every self decomposable law is unimodal, does not apply to the law of $\varphi$, which is infinitely divisible and not self decomposable. In Polson's 2026 book On Hilbert's 8th Problem the unimodality of $w$ is stated as a theorem, whose proof uses a bound on $w''$ that is not derived, and the problem asks only for the unimodality of $f$; the book proves only the two end ranges of $w'$ and asks for both.
results.supersedes: Theorem 28.12 of Polson (2026) states that $w$ is unimodal, with a proof that uses a bound on $w''$ not derived there, and Open Problem 30.23 asks only for the unimodality of $f$.
results.label: rz:prob:unimodal

results.name: Infinite divisibility across the strip
results.summary: The book asks whether $w_\sigma(x)>0$ for every $\sigma$ in $(0,1)$ and every $x>0$, that is whether the shifted reciprocal zeta function is infinitely divisible on every vertical line of the critical strip.
results.statement: For $\sigma\in(0,1)$ let $\varphi_\sigma(s)=\zeta(\sigma)/\bigl((1-s/(1-\sigma)^2)\zeta(\sigma+\sqrt s)\bigr)$ and $w_\sigma(x)=e^{(1-\sigma)^2x}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{4\pi x}}\sum_{n\ge2}\Lambda(n)\,n^{-\sigma}e^{-(\log n)^2/4x}$, its canonical function, with $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function. Problem: is $w_\sigma(x)>0$ for every $\sigma\in(0,1)$ and every $x>0$? Positivity gives infinite divisibility of $\varphi_\sigma$ with Lévy density $w_\sigma(x)/x$. The book proves $w_{1/2}>0$ and checks $w_\sigma>0$ numerically only for $x\le10^3$ and at nine values of $\sigma$. For $\frac12<\sigma<1$ the method of the case $\sigma=\frac12$ may apply, since the terms of the zeros below the verified height are Poisson kernels of positive width, so the question reduces to the sign of the explicit pole and archimedean terms at large $x$, whose limit is governed by $\zeta'(\sigma)/\zeta(\sigma)>0$. For the completed functions $R_\sigma(s)=\xi(\sigma)/\xi(\sigma+\sqrt s)$ the answer is known: $R_\sigma$ is infinitely divisible for every $\sigma>\frac12$ with no hypothesis; since $\varphi_\sigma$ differs from $R_\sigma$ by the gamma factor and elementary factors in $\sqrt s$, this does not settle the question for $w_\sigma$.
results.label: rz:prob:strip

results.name: Meixner Pollaczek truncations with real zeros
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: The book asks for a weighting of the coefficients of the symmetric Meixner Pollaczek expansion of $(\tau^2+\frac14)Z(\tau)$, or a Jensen type construction from them, whose polynomials are real rooted with zeros converging to the ordinates of the zeta zeros.
results.statement: Let $Z$ be Hardy's function and $p(\tau)=|\Gamma(\frac14+\frac{i\tau}2)|^2/(2^{3/2}\pi^{3/2})$ the Meixner density. The truncations of the expansion of the real even function $(\tau^2+\frac14)Z(\tau)$ in the even Meixner Pollaczek polynomials $P^{(1/4)}_{2m}(\tau/2;\frac\pi2)$, which are orthogonal for $p$, are real even polynomials. The symmetric expansion captures the first ordinate at degree $40$ but converges slowly, and the real zeros of its truncations do not track the ordinates of the zeros of the zeta function. Problem: is there a weighting of its coefficients, or a Jensen type construction from them, whose polynomials are real rooted and whose zeros converge to the ordinates?
results.label: rz:prob:mptrunc

results.name: Nyman Beurling criterion and the sech expansion
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: The book asks how the completeness question of Lai and Vere-Jones for dilates of $\operatorname{sech}$ relates to the Nyman Beurling criterion, and whether the sech expansion of $1/\zeta(\frac12+\sqrt s)$ has an $L^2$ version on the boundary.
results.statement: For $\operatorname{Re}\sqrt s>\frac12$ the book writes $1/\zeta(\frac12+\sqrt s)=1+\sum_{N\ge2}A_N\operatorname{sech}(\sqrt s\log N)$ with explicit Möbius type weights $A_N$ supported on the powers $N=n^m$ with $n$ squarefree and $m$ odd, and $A_N=\mu(N)/(2\sqrt N)$ for squarefree $N$ ($\mu$ the Möbius function). Problem: relate the completeness question of Lai and Vere-Jones for the dilates $\{\operatorname{sech}(\lambda x)\}$ to the Nyman Beurling criterion for the Riemann Hypothesis, and decide whether the sech expansion admits an $L^2$ version on the boundary $\operatorname{Re}\sqrt s=\frac12$.
results.label: rz:prob:nymanbeurling

results.name: Product representations of the law of R
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: The book asks whether the compensation in the formal deconvolution of the reciprocal zeta law into the reciprocal Xi law can be absorbed into a product of independent generalised gamma convolution variables, since an unconditional representation of that kind would prove the Riemann Hypothesis.
results.statement: Let $X_R$ be a random variable with Laplace transform $R(s)=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)$ and $X_\varphi$ one with Laplace transform $\varphi(s)=\zeta(\frac12)/\bigl((1-4s)\zeta(\frac12+\sqrt s)\bigr)$. The class of generalised gamma convolutions (GGC) is closed under independent sums, independent products and weak limits, so an unconditional representation of $X_R$ built from independent GGC variables by sums, products and weak limits would make $R$ a GGC and prove the Riemann Hypothesis; for $X_\varphi$ the book proves that no such representation exists, and the harmonic mean is not a closure operation of the class. The factorisation of $\varphi$ into $R$ and the gamma factor $\Gamma(\frac14+\frac{\sqrt s}2)\pi^{-\sqrt s/2}/\Gamma(\frac14)$ gives, formally, $X_R$ as $X_\varphi$ minus a positive stable law of index $\frac12$ and a compensated series of independent variables $Y_{c_n}$, where $\mathbb{E}e^{-sY_\kappa}=\kappa/(\kappa+\sqrt s)$ and $c_n=2n+\frac12$ for $n\ge0$. Question: can the compensation be absorbed into a product?
results.label: rz:prob:xrproduct

results.name: Truncations converge locally uniformly, and GRH for chi 4 is equivalent to zero free compact subsets of the left half strip for large n
results.summary: If $R_n\to0$ in probability then $M_n\to M$ locally uniformly on $0<\Re z<\frac12$, and GRH for $\chi_4$ holds if and only if every compact subset of $0<\Re z<\frac14$ is free of zeros of $M_n$ for all large $n$.
results.statement: Let $\chi_4$ be the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $L(s,\chi_4)$ the Dirichlet beta function, $\xi_4(s)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)L(s,\chi_4)$ its completion (entire and symmetric about $s=\frac12$), $\lambda_*=2\pi^2$, $\lambda_k=\lambda_*(k-\frac12)^2$, $\omega=\sum_{k\ge1}e_k/\lambda_k$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_k$ (so $\mathbb Ee^{-\lambda\omega}=\operatorname{sech}\sqrt{\lambda/2}$), $\omega_n=\sum_{k\le n}e_k/\lambda_k$ and $T_n=\omega-\omega_n$ the tail with cumulants $\kappa_j(T_n)=(j-1)!\,q_j(n)$, $q_j(n)=\sum_{k>n}\lambda_k^{-j}$. The Mellin transform is $M(z)=\mathbb E\,\omega^{-z}=(2\pi)^z\xi_4(2z)$, and the nontrivial zeros of $L(s,\chi_4)$ are the points $z=\rho/2$ of the strip $0<\Re z<\frac12$ where $M$ vanishes. A truncation is a random variable $R_n\ge0$ independent of $\omega_n$, with $M_n(z)=\mathbb E(\omega_n+R_n)^{-z}$. Suppose $R_n\to0$ in probability, as for the hard cutoff $R_n=0$ and for every nonnegative remainder with $\mathbb ER_n=\mathbb ET_n$. Then $M_n\to M$ locally uniformly on $0<\Re z<\frac12$, and the Generalised Riemann Hypothesis (GRH) for $\chi_4$ holds if and only if every compact subset of $0<\Re z<\frac14$ is free of zeros of $M_n$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
results.label: tr:thm:local

results.name: The tail cumulants of the beta lattice have an explicit expansion in the truncation index
results.summary: For fixed $j\ge1$, $q_j(n)=\lambda_*^{-j}\{n^{1-2j}/(2j-1)-\frac j{12}n^{-2j-1}+O(n^{-2j-3})\}$, so $c_n=\mathbb ET_n=1/(\lambda_*n)+O(n^{-3})$, $v_n=\operatorname{Var}T_n=1/(3\lambda_*^2n^3)+O(n^{-5})$ and $\kappa_3(T_n)=2/(5\lambda_*^3n^5)+O(n^{-7})$.
results.statement: Let $\chi_4$ be the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $L(s,\chi_4)$ the Dirichlet beta function, $\xi_4(s)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)L(s,\chi_4)$ its completion (entire and symmetric about $s=\frac12$), $\lambda_*=2\pi^2$, $\lambda_k=\lambda_*(k-\frac12)^2$, $\omega=\sum_{k\ge1}e_k/\lambda_k$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_k$ (so $\mathbb Ee^{-\lambda\omega}=\operatorname{sech}\sqrt{\lambda/2}$), $\omega_n=\sum_{k\le n}e_k/\lambda_k$ and $T_n=\omega-\omega_n$ the tail with cumulants $\kappa_j(T_n)=(j-1)!\,q_j(n)$, $q_j(n)=\sum_{k>n}\lambda_k^{-j}$. The Mellin transform is $M(z)=\mathbb E\,\omega^{-z}=(2\pi)^z\xi_4(2z)$, and the nontrivial zeros of $L(s,\chi_4)$ are the points $z=\rho/2$ of the strip $0<\Re z<\frac12$ where $M$ vanishes. A truncation is a random variable $R_n\ge0$ independent of $\omega_n$, with $M_n(z)=\mathbb E(\omega_n+R_n)^{-z}$. Then for fixed $j\ge1$, $q_j(n)=\lambda_*^{-j}\{n^{1-2j}/(2j-1)-\frac j{12}n^{-2j-1}+O(n^{-2j-3})\}$. In particular $c_n=\mathbb ET_n=\frac1{\lambda_*n}-\frac1{12\lambda_*n^3}+O(n^{-5})$, $v_n=\operatorname{Var}T_n=q_2(n)=\frac1{3\lambda_*^2n^3}-\frac1{6\lambda_*^2n^5}+O(n^{-7})$ and $\kappa_3(T_n)=\frac2{5\lambda_*^3n^5}+O(n^{-7})$.
results.label: tr:lem:tail

results.name: The truncated Mellin transform differs from M by a multiple of M(z+r), and each simple zero is displaced by a multiple of the first unmatched cumulant difference
results.summary: With $r=m+1$ and $p=2r-1$, $M_n(z)-M(z)=-\frac{(-1)^r\Delta_{r,n}}{r!}(z)_rM(z+r)+O_K(n^{-p-2}+n^{-2p})$, and a simple zero $z_0=\rho/2$ of $M$ is displaced by $z_n-z_0=\frac{(-1)^r\Delta_{r,n}}{r!}(z_0)_r\frac{M(z_0+r)}{M'(z_0)}+O(n^{-p-2}+n^{-2p})$, with $M(z_0+r)/M'(z_0)=(2\pi)^r\xi_4(\rho+2r)/(2\xi_4'(\rho))$.
results.statement: Let $\chi_4$ be the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $L(s,\chi_4)$ the Dirichlet beta function, $\xi_4(s)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)L(s,\chi_4)$ its completion (entire and symmetric about $s=\frac12$), $\lambda_*=2\pi^2$, $\lambda_k=\lambda_*(k-\frac12)^2$, $\omega=\sum_{k\ge1}e_k/\lambda_k$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_k$ (so $\mathbb Ee^{-\lambda\omega}=\operatorname{sech}\sqrt{\lambda/2}$), $\omega_n=\sum_{k\le n}e_k/\lambda_k$ and $T_n=\omega-\omega_n$ the tail with cumulants $\kappa_j(T_n)=(j-1)!\,q_j(n)$, $q_j(n)=\sum_{k>n}\lambda_k^{-j}$. The Mellin transform is $M(z)=\mathbb E\,\omega^{-z}=(2\pi)^z\xi_4(2z)$, and the nontrivial zeros of $L(s,\chi_4)$ are the points $z=\rho/2$ of the strip $0<\Re z<\frac12$ where $M$ vanishes. A truncation is a random variable $R_n\ge0$ independent of $\omega_n$, with $M_n(z)=\mathbb E(\omega_n+R_n)^{-z}$. Fix $m\ge0$, $r=m+1$, $p=2r-1$, and let $R_n\ge0$ be independent of $\omega_n$ with $\kappa_j(R_n)=\kappa_j(T_n)$ for $1\le j<r$, such that for a constant $C$ independent of $n$ and $j$, $\log\mathbb Ee^{-tR_n}=\sum_{j\ge1}(-1)^j\kappa_j(R_n)t^j/j!$ for $0\le t<n^2/C$ and $|\kappa_j(R_n)|/j!\le C^jn^{1-2j}$. Put $\Delta_{r,n}=\kappa_r(T_n)-\kappa_r(R_n)$ and $(z)_r=z(z+1)\cdots(z+r-1)$. Then uniformly for $z$ in a compact subset $K$ of $\Re z>0$, $M_n(z)-M(z)=-\frac{(-1)^r\Delta_{r,n}}{r!}(z)_rM(z+r)+O_K(n^{-p-2}+n^{-2p})$. Let $\rho=\frac12+i\gamma$ be a simple zero of $\xi_4$ and $z_0=\rho/2$. For all large $n$ a fixed small disc about $z_0$ contains exactly one zero $z_n$ of $M_n$, it is simple, and $z_n-z_0=\frac{(-1)^r\Delta_{r,n}}{r!}(z_0)_r\frac{M(z_0+r)}{M'(z_0)}+O(n^{-p-2}+n^{-2p})$ with $\frac{M(z_0+r)}{M'(z_0)}=\frac{(2\pi)^r\xi_4(\rho+2r)}{2\xi_4'(\rho)}$. If $\Delta_{r,n}=d\,n^{-p}+o(n^{-p})$ with $d\ne0$, then $z_n-z_0=D_rn^{-p}+o(n^{-p})$ with $D_r=\frac{(-1)^rd\,(2\pi)^r(z_0)_r\,\xi_4(\rho+2r)}{2\,r!\,\xi_4'(\rho)}\ne0$.
results.label: tr:thm:drift

results.name: The hard cutoff zeros drift at the rate 1 over n and the mean corrected zeros at 1 over n cubed, with the coefficient delta m
results.summary: For a simple zero $\rho=\frac12+i\gamma$ of $\xi_4$, $z_0=\rho/2$, $(z)_r=z(z+1)\cdots(z+r-1)$, $z_n$ the zero of $M_n$ in a fixed small disc about $z_0$ (unique and simple for large $n$) and $\delta_m=\frac{(-1)^{m+1}(z_0)_{m+1}\xi_4(\rho+2m+2)}{2(m+1)(2m+1)\pi^{m+1}\xi_4'(\rho)}$, the hard cutoff has $z_n=z_0+\delta_0/n+O(n^{-2})$ and the mean correction $R_n=\mathbb ET_n$ has $z_n=z_0+\delta_1/n^3+O(n^{-5})$; a remainder that matches the first $m$ cumulants of $T_n$, satisfies the analyticity and growth bounds of the drift law and has $\kappa_{m+1}(R_n)=o(n^{-(2m+1)})$ is displaced by $\delta_mn^{-(2m+1)}(1+o(1))$.
results.statement: Let $\chi_4$ be the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $L(s,\chi_4)$ the Dirichlet beta function, $\xi_4(s)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)L(s,\chi_4)$ its completion (entire and symmetric about $s=\frac12$), $\lambda_*=2\pi^2$, $\lambda_k=\lambda_*(k-\frac12)^2$, $\omega=\sum_{k\ge1}e_k/\lambda_k$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_k$ (so $\mathbb Ee^{-\lambda\omega}=\operatorname{sech}\sqrt{\lambda/2}$), $\omega_n=\sum_{k\le n}e_k/\lambda_k$ and $T_n=\omega-\omega_n$ the tail with cumulants $\kappa_j(T_n)=(j-1)!\,q_j(n)$, $q_j(n)=\sum_{k>n}\lambda_k^{-j}$. The Mellin transform is $M(z)=\mathbb E\,\omega^{-z}=(2\pi)^z\xi_4(2z)$, and the nontrivial zeros of $L(s,\chi_4)$ are the points $z=\rho/2$ of the strip $0<\Re z<\frac12$ where $M$ vanishes. A truncation is a random variable $R_n\ge0$ independent of $\omega_n$, with $M_n(z)=\mathbb E(\omega_n+R_n)^{-z}$. Fix $m\ge0$, $r=m+1$, $p=2r-1$, and let $R_n\ge0$ be independent of $\omega_n$ with $\kappa_j(R_n)=\kappa_j(T_n)$ for $1\le j<r$, such that for a constant $C$ independent of $n$ and $j$, $\log\mathbb Ee^{-tR_n}=\sum_{j\ge1}(-1)^j\kappa_j(R_n)t^j/j!$ for $0\le t<n^2/C$ and $|\kappa_j(R_n)|/j!\le C^jn^{1-2j}$. Put $\Delta_{r,n}=\kappa_r(T_n)-\kappa_r(R_n)$ and $(z)_r=z(z+1)\cdots(z+r-1)$. Let $\rho=\frac12+i\gamma$ be a simple zero of $\xi_4$, $z_0=\rho/2$, and $\delta_m=\frac{(-1)^{m+1}(z_0)_{m+1}\,\xi_4(\rho+2m+2)}{2(m+1)(2m+1)\,\pi^{m+1}\,\xi_4'(\rho)}$. Let $z_n$ be the zero of $M_n$ in a fixed small disc about $z_0$ (unique and simple for large $n$). For the hard cutoff $R_n=0$, $z_n=z_0+\delta_0/n+O(n^{-2})$. For the mean correction $R_n=\mathbb ET_n$ (a constant), $z_n=z_0+\delta_1/n^3+O(n^{-5})$. For a remainder that satisfies the hypotheses above at order $m$ and has $\kappa_{m+1}(R_n)=o(n^{-(2m+1)})$ the displacement is $\delta_mn^{-(2m+1)}(1+o(1))$.
results.label: tr:cor:named

results.name: Remainders matching mean and variance but not the third cumulant give different drifts, so the formula of delta 2 needs the matching hypothesis
results.summary: With $r=3$, a simple zero $\rho$ of $\xi_4$, $z_0=\rho/2$, $z_n$ the zero of $M_n$ near $z_0$ and $\delta_2=-\frac{(z_0)_3\xi_4(\rho+6)}{30\pi^3\xi_4'(\rho)}$ with $(z_0)_3=z_0(z_0+1)(z_0+2)$, the gamma remainder matching the mean and variance of $T_n$ gives $z_n=z_0+\frac49\delta_2n^{-5}+O(n^{-7})$, a sum of two such gamma variables gives $z_0-\frac19\delta_2n^{-5}+O(n^{-7})$, and a bounded two point remainder gives a displacement of exact order $n^{-3}$.
results.statement: Let $\chi_4$ be the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $L(s,\chi_4)$ the Dirichlet beta function, $\xi_4(s)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)L(s,\chi_4)$ its completion (entire and symmetric about $s=\frac12$), $\lambda_*=2\pi^2$, $\lambda_k=\lambda_*(k-\frac12)^2$, $\omega=\sum_{k\ge1}e_k/\lambda_k$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_k$ (so $\mathbb Ee^{-\lambda\omega}=\operatorname{sech}\sqrt{\lambda/2}$), $\omega_n=\sum_{k\le n}e_k/\lambda_k$ and $T_n=\omega-\omega_n$ the tail with cumulants $\kappa_j(T_n)=(j-1)!\,q_j(n)$, $q_j(n)=\sum_{k>n}\lambda_k^{-j}$. The Mellin transform is $M(z)=\mathbb E\,\omega^{-z}=(2\pi)^z\xi_4(2z)$, and the nontrivial zeros of $L(s,\chi_4)$ are the points $z=\rho/2$ of the strip $0<\Re z<\frac12$ where $M$ vanishes. A truncation is a random variable $R_n\ge0$ independent of $\omega_n$, with $M_n(z)=\mathbb E(\omega_n+R_n)^{-z}$. Let $c_n=\mathbb ET_n$, $v_n=\operatorname{Var}T_n$, $\rho=\frac12+i\gamma$ a simple zero of $\xi_4$, $z_0=\rho/2$, $z_n$ the zero of $M_n$ in a fixed small disc about $z_0$ (unique and simple for large $n$), and $\delta_2=-\frac{(z_0)_3\,\xi_4(\rho+6)}{30\,\pi^3\,\xi_4'(\rho)}$ with $(z_0)_3=z_0(z_0+1)(z_0+2)$. Let $R_n$ have the gamma law with shape $c_n^2/v_n$ and scale $v_n/c_n$. Then $R_n$ satisfies, for a constant $C$ independent of $n$ and $j$, $\log\mathbb Ee^{-tR_n}=\sum_{j\ge1}(-1)^j\kappa_j(R_n)t^j/j!$ for $0\le t<n^2/C$ and $|\kappa_j(R_n)|/j!\le C^jn^{1-2j}$, and $z_n=z_0+\frac49\delta_2\,n^{-5}+O(n^{-7})$. A remainder $R_n=G_{1,n}+G_{2,n}$, a sum of two independent gamma variables with the same mean and variance and the same natural scale, gives $z_n=z_0-\frac19\delta_2\,n^{-5}+O(n^{-7})$. A bounded remainder $R_n=b_n+hB_n$ with $B_n$ a Bernoulli variable, $h>0$ small and fixed, matched to the mean and variance, has $z_n-z_0=c\,n^{-3}+O(n^{-5})$ with $c\ne0$.
results.label: tr:prop:gamma

results.name: The sign of the real part of the drift is the sign of minus sin Theta m times the derivative of the Hardy function of chi 4
results.summary: For a simple zero $\rho=\frac12+i\gamma$, $\gamma>0$, of $\xi_4$ with $z_0=\rho/2$ and $\delta_m$ the drift coefficient of the zeros of the truncated Mellin transforms of the beta lattice, $\delta_m=iC_m(\gamma)e^{i\Theta_m(\gamma)}/Z_\beta'(\gamma)$ with $C_m>0$ and $\Theta_m=\vartheta_\beta(\gamma)+\arg L(\rho+2m+2,\chi_4)-\sum_{j=0}^m[\arctan\frac{1/2+2j}\gamma+\arctan\frac{3/2+2j}\gamma]$, so $\operatorname{sgn}\Re\delta_m=\operatorname{sgn}[-\sin\Theta_m\,Z_\beta'(\gamma)]$.
results.statement: Let $\chi_4$ be the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $L(s,\chi_4)$ the Dirichlet beta function, $\xi_4(s)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)L(s,\chi_4)$ its completion (entire and symmetric about $s=\frac12$), $\lambda_*=2\pi^2$, $\lambda_k=\lambda_*(k-\frac12)^2$, $\omega=\sum_{k\ge1}e_k/\lambda_k$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_k$ (so $\mathbb Ee^{-\lambda\omega}=\operatorname{sech}\sqrt{\lambda/2}$), $\omega_n=\sum_{k\le n}e_k/\lambda_k$ and $T_n=\omega-\omega_n$ the tail with cumulants $\kappa_j(T_n)=(j-1)!\,q_j(n)$, $q_j(n)=\sum_{k>n}\lambda_k^{-j}$. The Mellin transform is $M(z)=\mathbb E\,\omega^{-z}=(2\pi)^z\xi_4(2z)$, and the nontrivial zeros of $L(s,\chi_4)$ are the points $z=\rho/2$ of the strip $0<\Re z<\frac12$ where $M$ vanishes. A truncation is a random variable $R_n\ge0$ independent of $\omega_n$, with $M_n(z)=\mathbb E(\omega_n+R_n)^{-z}$. Put $G(s)=(4/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)$, so that $\xi_4=\frac2{\sqrt\pi}GL$, let $\vartheta_\beta(x)=\arg G(\frac12+ix)$ and $Z_\beta(x)=e^{i\vartheta_\beta(x)}L(\frac12+ix,\chi_4)$ (real), the Riemann Siegel function and the Hardy function of $\chi_4$. Let $\rho=\frac12+i\gamma$, $\gamma>0$, be a simple zero of $\xi_4$, $z_0=\rho/2$, $(z)_r=z(z+1)\cdots(z+r-1)$, and for $m\ge0$ let $\delta_m=\frac{(-1)^{m+1}(z_0)_{m+1}\,\xi_4(\rho+2m+2)}{2(m+1)(2m+1)\,\pi^{m+1}\,\xi_4'(\rho)}$. Then $\delta_m=\frac{i\,C_m(\gamma)e^{i\Theta_m(\gamma)}}{Z_\beta'(\gamma)}$ with $C_m(\gamma)>0$ and $\Theta_m(\gamma)=\vartheta_\beta(\gamma)+\arg L(\rho+2m+2,\chi_4)-\sum_{j=0}^m[\arctan\frac{1/2+2j}\gamma+\arctan\frac{3/2+2j}\gamma]$, so that $\operatorname{sgn}\Re\delta_m=\operatorname{sgn}[-\sin\Theta_m(\gamma)Z_\beta'(\gamma)]$, zero included. For a remainder $R_n\ge0$ independent of $\omega_n$ with $\kappa_j(R_n)=\kappa_j(T_n)$ for $1\le j\le m$ such that, for a constant $C$ independent of $n$ and $j$, $\log\mathbb Ee^{-tR_n}=\sum_{j\ge1}(-1)^j\kappa_j(R_n)t^j/j!$ for $0\le t<n^2/C$ and $|\kappa_j(R_n)|/j!\le C^jn^{1-2j}$, and with $\eta_m=\lim_n[\kappa_{m+1}(T_n)-\kappa_{m+1}(R_n)]/\kappa_{m+1}(T_n)$ the displacement $z_n-z_0$ of the zero $z_n$ of $M_n$ near $z_0$ is $\eta_m\delta_mn^{-(2m+1)}(1+o(1))$ when the limit exists and $\eta_m\ne0$, and the sign of the real part is $\operatorname{sgn}[-\eta_m\sin\Theta_m(\gamma)Z_\beta'(\gamma)]$ when $\eta_m\sin\Theta_m\ne0$.
results.label: tr:thm:phase

results.name: L(s,chi 4) has 379 zeros below height 500 by sign changes, all simple and on the line as far as the computation sees, with five anomalous Gram parities
results.summary: Sign changes of $Z_\beta$ on two grids give $379$ zeros of $L(s,\chi_4)$ with $0<\gamma<500$, all simple and on the critical line as far as the computation sees (minimal gap $0.1336$); the count is not certified. Exactly five have anomalous Gram parity, at $\gamma=138.7502,290.2521,364.4197,400.8264,422.5104$, and $\Re\delta_1<0$ exactly there, where $\delta_m$ is the drift coefficient of the zeros of the truncated Mellin transforms of the beta lattice ($m=1$ for the mean correction) and $Z_\beta$ the Hardy function of $\chi_4$.
results.statement: Let $\chi_4$ be the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $L(s,\chi_4)$ the Dirichlet beta function, $\vartheta_\beta$ and $Z_\beta$ the Riemann Siegel and Hardy functions of $\chi_4$ with $\vartheta_\beta(x)=\arg[(4/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)]_{s=1/2+ix}$. Put $Z_\beta(x)=e^{i\vartheta_\beta(x)}L(\frac12+ix,\chi_4)$ (real), $\xi_4(s)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)L(s,\chi_4)$, and for a zero $\rho$ with $z_0=\rho/2$ and $(z)_r=z(z+1)\cdots(z+r-1)$ let $\delta_m=\frac{(-1)^{m+1}(z_0)_{m+1}\,\xi_4(\rho+2m+2)}{2(m+1)(2m+1)\,\pi^{m+1}\,\xi_4'(\rho)}$, the drift coefficient of the zeros of the truncated Mellin transforms of the beta lattice ($m=0$ for the hard cutoff, $m=1$ for the mean correction). Locating the sign changes of $Z_\beta$ on $0<x<500$ on two independent grids (steps $0.02$ and $0.0137$) and refining at two precisions gives $379$ zeros, all simple and on the critical line as far as the computation sees (the minimal gap is $0.1336$), in agreement with $\vartheta_\beta(500)/\pi=379.15$. The count is not certified, since there is no Turing bound. Measuring the Gram parity by $\lfloor\vartheta_\beta(\gamma)/\pi\rfloor$ minus the zero number, $374$ zeros have offset $-1$ and five do not, at $\gamma=138.7502$, $290.2521$, $364.4197$, $400.8264$ and $422.5104$ (zero numbers $78$, $195$, $258$, $291$, $309$). The mean correction has $\Re\delta_1<0$ exactly at these five zeros and at no other, and the hard cutoff has $\Re\delta_0<0$ at the last four.
results.label: tr:res:gram

results.name: One sided criterion fails at order m if some critical zero is approached from the left
results.summary: For a remainder matching the first $m$ cumulants of $T_n$ under the drift law bounds, with $\eta_m$ the limiting relative deficit of $\kappa_{m+1}$ and $\delta_m$ the drift coefficient of the zeros of the truncated Mellin transforms of the beta lattice: if some simple critical zero $\rho$ of $\xi_4$ has $\Re(\eta_m\delta_m)<0$, then for all large $n$ the function $M_n$ has a zero in $0<\Re z<\frac14$, so no criterion that $M_n$ is free of zeros there for infinitely many $n$ can hold at order $m$ for this remainder.
results.statement: Let $\chi_4$ be the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $L(s,\chi_4)$ the Dirichlet beta function, $\xi_4(s)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)L(s,\chi_4)$ its completion (entire and symmetric about $s=\frac12$), $\lambda_*=2\pi^2$, $\lambda_k=\lambda_*(k-\frac12)^2$, $\omega=\sum_{k\ge1}e_k/\lambda_k$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_k$ (so $\mathbb Ee^{-\lambda\omega}=\operatorname{sech}\sqrt{\lambda/2}$), $\omega_n=\sum_{k\le n}e_k/\lambda_k$ and $T_n=\omega-\omega_n$ the tail with cumulants $\kappa_j(T_n)=(j-1)!\,q_j(n)$, $q_j(n)=\sum_{k>n}\lambda_k^{-j}$. The Mellin transform is $M(z)=\mathbb E\,\omega^{-z}=(2\pi)^z\xi_4(2z)$, and the nontrivial zeros of $L(s,\chi_4)$ are the points $z=\rho/2$ of the strip $0<\Re z<\frac12$ where $M$ vanishes. A truncation is a random variable $R_n\ge0$ independent of $\omega_n$, with $M_n(z)=\mathbb E(\omega_n+R_n)^{-z}$. Fix $m\ge0$ and a remainder $R_n\ge0$ independent of $\omega_n$ with $\kappa_j(R_n)=\kappa_j(T_n)$ for $1\le j\le m$ such that, for a constant $C$ independent of $n$ and $j$, $\log\mathbb Ee^{-tR_n}=\sum_{j\ge1}(-1)^j\kappa_j(R_n)t^j/j!$ for $0\le t<n^2/C$ and $|\kappa_j(R_n)|/j!\le C^jn^{1-2j}$, for which $\eta_m=\lim_n[\kappa_{m+1}(T_n)-\kappa_{m+1}(R_n)]/\kappa_{m+1}(T_n)$ exists, and for a simple zero $\rho$ of $\xi_4$ let $z_0=\rho/2$, $(z)_r=z(z+1)\cdots(z+r-1)$ and $\delta_m=\frac{(-1)^{m+1}(z_0)_{m+1}\,\xi_4(\rho+2m+2)}{2(m+1)(2m+1)\,\pi^{m+1}\,\xi_4'(\rho)}$. If some simple zero $\rho=\frac12+i\gamma$ of $\xi_4$ on the critical line has $\Re(\eta_m\delta_m)<0$, then for all large $n$ the function $M_n$ has a zero in $0<\Re z<\frac14$, so no criterion of the form that $M_n$ has no zero in $0<\Re z<\frac14$ for infinitely many $n$ can hold at order $m$ for this remainder.
results.label: tr:cor:nogo

results.name: Infinitely many Gram anomalies with a margin force infinitely many zeros with negative real drift
results.summary: With $\sigma=2m+\frac52$, $\epsilon_\sigma=\sum_{k\ge1}(2k+1)^{-\sigma}<1$ and $B_m(\gamma)=\arcsin\epsilon_\sigma+\sum_{j=0}^m[\arctan\frac{1/2+2j}\gamma+\arctan\frac{3/2+2j}\gamma]$, $|\Theta_m-\vartheta_\beta|\le B_m$, and infinitely many simple critical zeros with $-\sin\vartheta_\beta(\gamma)Z_\beta'(\gamma)<0$ and $\operatorname{dist}(\vartheta_\beta(\gamma),\pi\mathbb Z)>B_m(\gamma)$ give infinitely many zeros with $\Re\delta_m<0$.
results.statement: Let $\chi_4$ be the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $L(s,\chi_4)$ the Dirichlet beta function, $\xi_4(s)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)L(s,\chi_4)$ its completion (entire and symmetric about $s=\frac12$), $\lambda_*=2\pi^2$, $\lambda_k=\lambda_*(k-\frac12)^2$, $\omega=\sum_{k\ge1}e_k/\lambda_k$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_k$ (so $\mathbb Ee^{-\lambda\omega}=\operatorname{sech}\sqrt{\lambda/2}$), $\omega_n=\sum_{k\le n}e_k/\lambda_k$ and $T_n=\omega-\omega_n$ the tail with cumulants $\kappa_j(T_n)=(j-1)!\,q_j(n)$, $q_j(n)=\sum_{k>n}\lambda_k^{-j}$. The Mellin transform is $M(z)=\mathbb E\,\omega^{-z}=(2\pi)^z\xi_4(2z)$, and the nontrivial zeros of $L(s,\chi_4)$ are the points $z=\rho/2$ of the strip $0<\Re z<\frac12$ where $M$ vanishes. A truncation is a random variable $R_n\ge0$ independent of $\omega_n$, with $M_n(z)=\mathbb E(\omega_n+R_n)^{-z}$. Put $G(s)=(4/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)$, so that $\xi_4=\frac2{\sqrt\pi}GL$, let $\vartheta_\beta(x)=\arg G(\frac12+ix)$ and $Z_\beta(x)=e^{i\vartheta_\beta(x)}L(\frac12+ix,\chi_4)$ (real), the Riemann Siegel function and the Hardy function of $\chi_4$. For a simple zero $\rho=\frac12+i\gamma$, $\gamma>0$, of $\xi_4$ let $z_0=\rho/2$, $(z)_r=z(z+1)\cdots(z+r-1)$, $\delta_m=\frac{(-1)^{m+1}(z_0)_{m+1}\,\xi_4(\rho+2m+2)}{2(m+1)(2m+1)\,\pi^{m+1}\,\xi_4'(\rho)}$ and $\Theta_m(\gamma)=\vartheta_\beta(\gamma)+\arg L(\rho+2m+2,\chi_4)-\sum_{j=0}^m[\arctan\frac{1/2+2j}\gamma+\arctan\frac{3/2+2j}\gamma]$. Let $\sigma=2m+\frac52$, $\epsilon_\sigma=\sum_{k\ge1}(2k+1)^{-\sigma}<1$ and $B_m(\gamma)=\arcsin\epsilon_\sigma+\sum_{j=0}^m[\arctan\frac{1/2+2j}\gamma+\arctan\frac{3/2+2j}\gamma]$. Then $|\Theta_m(\gamma)-\vartheta_\beta(\gamma)|\le B_m(\gamma)$. If infinitely many simple critical zeros satisfy $-\sin\vartheta_\beta(\gamma)Z_\beta'(\gamma)<0$ and $\operatorname{dist}(\vartheta_\beta(\gamma),\pi\mathbb Z)>B_m(\gamma)$, then infinitely many zeros have $\Re\delta_m<0$.
results.label: tr:prop:gram

results.name: If the symmetrised truncations have only critical zeros for infinitely many n then GRH holds for chi 4
results.summary: If for infinitely many $n$ all zeros of $F_n(z)=g_n(z)+g_n(\frac12-z)$ in $0<\Re z<\frac12$ lie on $\Re z=\frac14$, then GRH holds for $\chi_4$.
results.statement: Let $\chi_4$ be the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $L(s,\chi_4)$ the Dirichlet beta function, $\xi_4(s)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)L(s,\chi_4)$ its completion (entire and symmetric about $s=\frac12$), $\lambda_*=2\pi^2$, $\lambda_k=\lambda_*(k-\frac12)^2$, $\omega=\sum_{k\ge1}e_k/\lambda_k$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_k$ (so $\mathbb Ee^{-\lambda\omega}=\operatorname{sech}\sqrt{\lambda/2}$), $\omega_n=\sum_{k\le n}e_k/\lambda_k$ and $T_n=\omega-\omega_n$ the tail with cumulants $\kappa_j(T_n)=(j-1)!\,q_j(n)$, $q_j(n)=\sum_{k>n}\lambda_k^{-j}$. The Mellin transform is $M(z)=\mathbb E\,\omega^{-z}=(2\pi)^z\xi_4(2z)$, and the nontrivial zeros of $L(s,\chi_4)$ are the points $z=\rho/2$ of the strip $0<\Re z<\frac12$ where $M$ vanishes. A truncation is a random variable $R_n\ge0$ independent of $\omega_n$, with $M_n(z)=\mathbb E(\omega_n+R_n)^{-z}$. Put $g_n(z)=(2\pi)^{-z}M_n(z)$ and $F_n(z)=g_n(z)+g_n(\frac12-z)$, for remainders with $R_n\to0$ in probability. If for infinitely many $n$ all zeros of $F_n$ in $0<\Re z<\frac12$ lie on $\Re z=\frac14$, then the Generalised Riemann Hypothesis holds for $\chi_4$.
results.label: tr:thm:symhurwitz

results.name: Each simple critical zero is the limit of exactly one zero of the symmetrised truncation, and that zero is critical
results.summary: Every simple zero of $\xi_4(2z)$ on $\Re z=\frac14$ is, for all large $n$, the limit of exactly one zero of $F_n$ in a small disc about it, and that zero lies on $\Re z=\frac14$.
results.statement: Let $\chi_4$ be the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $L(s,\chi_4)$ the Dirichlet beta function, $\xi_4(s)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)L(s,\chi_4)$ its completion (entire and symmetric about $s=\frac12$), $\lambda_*=2\pi^2$, $\lambda_k=\lambda_*(k-\frac12)^2$, $\omega=\sum_{k\ge1}e_k/\lambda_k$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_k$ (so $\mathbb Ee^{-\lambda\omega}=\operatorname{sech}\sqrt{\lambda/2}$), $\omega_n=\sum_{k\le n}e_k/\lambda_k$ and $T_n=\omega-\omega_n$ the tail with cumulants $\kappa_j(T_n)=(j-1)!\,q_j(n)$, $q_j(n)=\sum_{k>n}\lambda_k^{-j}$. The Mellin transform is $M(z)=\mathbb E\,\omega^{-z}=(2\pi)^z\xi_4(2z)$, and the nontrivial zeros of $L(s,\chi_4)$ are the points $z=\rho/2$ of the strip $0<\Re z<\frac12$ where $M$ vanishes. A truncation is a random variable $R_n\ge0$ independent of $\omega_n$, with $M_n(z)=\mathbb E(\omega_n+R_n)^{-z}$. Put $g_n(z)=(2\pi)^{-z}M_n(z)$ and $F_n(z)=g_n(z)+g_n(\frac12-z)$, for remainders with $R_n\to0$ in probability. Every simple zero of $\xi_4(2z)$ on $\Re z=\frac14$ is, for all large $n$, the limit of exactly one zero of $F_n$ in a small disc about it, and that zero lies on $\Re z=\frac14$.
results.label: tr:prop:symlocal

results.name: The Hermite coefficients of Xi are generated by the Gaussian smoothing G a, with an explicit moment formula
results.summary: For every $a>0$, $\sum_{m\ge0}b_m(a)z^{2m}/\sqrt{(2m)!}=\sqrt{2\pi}\,\pi^{-1/4}\sqrt a\,e^{z^2/2}G_a(\sqrt2az)$ with $G_a(\tau)=\int\Phi(u)e^{-a^2u^2/2}\cos(\tau u)\,du$, and $b_m(a)=\sqrt{2\pi}\,\pi^{-1/4}\sqrt a\sqrt{(2m)!}\sum_{k=0}^m\frac{(-1)^k2^ka^{2k}\nu_k(a)}{(2k)!\,2^{m-k}(m-k)!}$ with $\nu_k=\int\Phi(u)e^{-a^2u^2/2}u^{2k}du>0$.
results.statement: Let $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2u})$ be the P\'olya kernel, positive and even, and $\Xi(t)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ the Riemann Xi function. Let $h_n(x)=\pi^{-1/4}(2^nn!)^{-1/2}H_n(x)e^{-x^2/2}$ be the orthonormal Hermite functions, with $H_n$ the physicists' Hermite polynomials. For a scale $a>0$ put $c_n(a)=\sqrt a\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)h_n(au)\,du$, $t_m=a\sqrt{4m+1}$ and $b_m(a)=\sqrt{2\pi}\,(-1)^mc_{2m}(a)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Xi(t)h_{2m}(t/a)a^{-1/2}\,dt$. Let $G_a(\tau)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)e^{-a^2u^2/2}\cos(\tau u)\,du$ (the Gaussian smoothing of $\Xi$ of variance $a^2$) and $\nu_k(a)=\int\Phi(u)e^{-a^2u^2/2}u^{2k}du>0$. Then for every $a>0$, $\sum_{m\ge0}b_m(a)\frac{z^{2m}}{\sqrt{(2m)!}}=\sqrt{2\pi}\,\pi^{-1/4}\sqrt a\;e^{z^2/2}\,G_a(\sqrt2\,az)$, and $b_m(a)=\sqrt{2\pi}\,\pi^{-1/4}\sqrt a\,\sqrt{(2m)!}\sum_{k=0}^m\frac{(-1)^k2^ka^{2k}\nu_k(a)}{(2k)!\,2^{m-k}(m-k)!}$.
results.label: tr:thm:heat

results.name: The normalised Hermite coefficient equals Xi at the turning point up to an explicit error of order a to the fourth
results.summary: For $0<a\le a_0$ and $m\ge0$, $|b_m(a)/A_m(a)-\Xi(t_m)|\le M_4(a_0)a^4/12$ and $b_m/A_m=\Xi(t_m)+a^4Q(t_m)+R_m(a)$ with $|R_m|\le M_8(a_0)a^8/672$, where $Q(t)=\frac{\Xi'''(t)}{6t}-\frac{\Xi''(t)}{4t^2}+\frac{\Xi'(t)}{4t^3}$ and $Q(0)=\frac1{12}\int\Phi u^4du$.
results.statement: Let $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2u})$ be the P\'olya kernel, positive and even, and $\Xi(t)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ the Riemann Xi function. Let $h_n(x)=\pi^{-1/4}(2^nn!)^{-1/2}H_n(x)e^{-x^2/2}$ be the orthonormal Hermite functions, with $H_n$ the physicists' Hermite polynomials. For a scale $a>0$ put $c_n(a)=\sqrt a\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)h_n(au)\,du$, $t_m=a\sqrt{4m+1}$ and $b_m(a)=\sqrt{2\pi}\,(-1)^mc_{2m}(a)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Xi(t)h_{2m}(t/a)a^{-1/2}\,dt$. Let $A_m(a)=\sqrt2\,\pi^{1/4}\sqrt a\sqrt{(2m)!}/(2^mm!)$ and $M_k(a_0)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)|u|^ke^{a_0^2u^2/2}du$. Then for every $a_0>0$, $0<a\le a_0$ and integer $m\ge0$, $|b_m(a)/A_m(a)-\Xi(t_m)|\le\frac{M_4(a_0)}{12}a^4$ and $b_m(a)/A_m(a)=\Xi(t_m)+a^4Q(t_m)+R_m(a)$ with $|R_m(a)|\le\frac{M_8(a_0)}{672}a^8$, where $Q(t)=\frac{\Xi'''(t)}{6t}-\frac{\Xi''(t)}{4t^2}+\frac{\Xi'(t)}{4t^3}$ for $t\ne0$ and $Q(0)=\frac{\Xi^{(4)}(0)}{12}=\frac1{12}\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)u^4du$ is an even entire function.
results.label: tr:thm:herm

results.name: The index of the first negative Hermite coefficient satisfies 4 a squared m star tends to gamma 1 squared
results.summary: With $m^*(a)=\min\{m:b_m(a)<0\}$ and $\gamma_1=14.134725\ldots$, for small $a$ the index $m^*(a)$ exists and $\lim_{a\to0}4a^2m^*(a)=\gamma_1^2$; more precisely $m^*(a)=\lfloor(\gamma_a^2/a^2-1)/4\rfloor+1$ with $\gamma_a=\gamma_1-a^4Q(\gamma_1)/\Xi'(\gamma_1)+O(a^8)$ and $Q(t)=\frac{\Xi'''(t)}{6t}-\frac{\Xi''(t)}{4t^2}+\frac{\Xi'(t)}{4t^3}$, the zero near $\gamma_1$ of $t\mapsto\int\Phi(u)y_{a^4,t}(u)du$.
results.statement: Let $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2u})$ be the P\'olya kernel, positive and even, and $\Xi(t)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ the Riemann Xi function. Let $h_n(x)=\pi^{-1/4}(2^nn!)^{-1/2}H_n(x)e^{-x^2/2}$ be the orthonormal Hermite functions, with $H_n$ the physicists' Hermite polynomials. For a scale $a>0$ put $c_n(a)=\sqrt a\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)h_n(au)\,du$, $t_m=a\sqrt{4m+1}$ and $b_m(a)=\sqrt{2\pi}\,(-1)^mc_{2m}(a)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Xi(t)h_{2m}(t/a)a^{-1/2}\,dt$. Let $Q(t)=\frac{\Xi'''(t)}{6t}-\frac{\Xi''(t)}{4t^2}+\frac{\Xi'(t)}{4t^3}$ ($t\ne0$), $\gamma_1=14.134725\ldots$ the first positive zero of $\Xi$ (simple), $m^*(a)=\min\{m\ge0:b_m(a)<0\}$, and $y_{z,t}$ the even solution of $y''+(t^2-zu^2)y=0$ with $y(0)=1$, $y'(0)=0$. Then for every $0<\delta<\gamma_1$ and $a$ small, $b_m(a)>0$ for all $m$ with $t_m\le\gamma_1-\delta$, the index $m^*(a)$ exists, and $\lim_{a\to0}4a^2m^*(a)=\gamma_1^2$. If $\gamma_a$ is the unique zero near $\gamma_1$ of $t\mapsto\int\Phi(u)y_{a^4,t}(u)du$, then $\gamma_a=\gamma_1-a^4Q(\gamma_1)/\Xi'(\gamma_1)+O(a^8)$ and $m^*(a)=\lfloor(\gamma_a^2/a^2-1)/4\rfloor+1$ for small $a$.
results.label: tr:cor:first

results.name: A verified sign change count of the Hermite coefficients together with an upper bound on the zero count proves real and simple zeros
results.summary: If computed normalised coefficients with rigorous errors $e_m$ exceed $e_m+E_m$ in absolute value, where $E_m$ bounds $|b_m/A_m-\Xi(t_m)|$, the signs of $b_m$ and $\Xi(t_m)$ agree, and $S$ such sign changes together with $N(T)\le S$, with $N(T)$ the number of zeros $t$ of $\Xi$ with $0<\Re t<T$, show that all those zeros are real and simple.
results.statement: Let $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2u})$ be the P\'olya kernel, positive and even, and $\Xi(t)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ the Riemann Xi function. Let $h_n(x)=\pi^{-1/4}(2^nn!)^{-1/2}H_n(x)e^{-x^2/2}$ be the orthonormal Hermite functions, with $H_n$ the physicists' Hermite polynomials. For a scale $a>0$ put $c_n(a)=\sqrt a\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)h_n(au)\,du$, $t_m=a\sqrt{4m+1}$ and $b_m(a)=\sqrt{2\pi}\,(-1)^mc_{2m}(a)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Xi(t)h_{2m}(t/a)a^{-1/2}\,dt$. Let $A_m(a)=\sqrt2\,\pi^{1/4}\sqrt a\sqrt{(2m)!}/(2^mm!)$ and $M_k(a_0)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)|u|^ke^{a_0^2u^2/2}du$. Let $\widetilde b_m/A_m$ be computed values of $b_m/A_m$ with rigorous errors $e_m$, and $E_m$ a rigorous bound for $|b_m/A_m-\Xi(t_m)|$ (for example $M_4(a_0)a^4/12$). If $|\widetilde b_m/A_m|>e_m+E_m$ then $\operatorname{sgn}\widetilde b_m=\operatorname{sgn}\Xi(t_m)$. Suppose there are $S$ sign changes at pairs of adjacent sampling points $t_m$ below $T$, all with this property. Then $\Xi$ has $S$ zeros in disjoint intervals, and if an independent rigorous method gives that the number $N(T)$ of zeros $t$ of $\Xi$ with $0<\Re t<T$ (the zeros $\frac12+it$ of $\zeta$ with ordinate in $(0,T)$), counted with multiplicity, is at most $S$ (Turing's method), then all zeros $t$ of $\Xi$ with $0<\Re t<T$ are real and simple.
results.label: tr:prop:verified

results.name: If each simple zero gives one sign change the mean run of the Hermite coefficient signs is asymptotic to pi T over a squared log of T over 2 pi
results.status_text: conditional on the zeros $t$ of $\Xi$ with $T\le\Re t\le T+H$ are real and simple and the sign changes of $(b_m(a))$ with $t_m\in[T,T+H]$ correspond one to one to them
results.conditions: the zeros $t$ of $\Xi$ with $T\le\Re t\le T+H$ are real and simple and the sign changes of $(b_m(a))$ with $t_m\in[T,T+H]$ correspond one to one to them
results.summary: If the zeros $t$ of $\Xi$ with $T\le\Re t\le T+H$ are real and simple and the sign changes of $(b_m(a))$ with $t_m\in[T,T+H]$ correspond one to one to them, the mean number of coefficient steps per sign change is the number $TH/(2a^2)+O(H^2/a^2+1)$ of grid points in the window over $N(T+H)-N(T)$, the number of zeros $t$ of $\Xi$ with $T\le\Re t<T+H$, $=\frac H{2\pi}\log\frac T{2\pi}+O(H^2/T+\log T)$, asymptotic to $\pi T/(a^2\log(T/2\pi))$ for fixed $a$, $H\to\infty$, $H=o(T)$.
results.statement: Let $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2u})$ be the P\'olya kernel, positive and even, and $\Xi(t)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ the Riemann Xi function. Let $h_n(x)=\pi^{-1/4}(2^nn!)^{-1/2}H_n(x)e^{-x^2/2}$ be the orthonormal Hermite functions, with $H_n$ the physicists' Hermite polynomials. For a scale $a>0$ put $c_n(a)=\sqrt a\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)h_n(au)\,du$, $t_m=a\sqrt{4m+1}$ and $b_m(a)=\sqrt{2\pi}\,(-1)^mc_{2m}(a)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Xi(t)h_{2m}(t/a)a^{-1/2}\,dt$. Let $N(T)$ be the number of zeros $t$ of $\Xi$ with $0<\Re t<T$ (the zeros $\frac12+it$ of $\zeta$ with ordinate in $(0,T)$), counted with multiplicity. Assume the zeros $t$ of $\Xi$ with $T\le\Re t\le T+H$ are real and simple and the sign changes of $(b_m(a))$ with $t_m\in[T,T+H]$ correspond one to one to them. Then the mean number of coefficient steps per sign change is the number $TH/(2a^2)+O(H^2/a^2+1)$ of grid points in the window divided by $N(T+H)-N(T)=\frac H{2\pi}\log\frac T{2\pi}+O(H^2/T+\log T)$, and for fixed $a$, $H\to\infty$ and $H=o(T)$ the ratio is asymptotic to $\pi T/(a^2\log(T/2\pi))$.
results.label: tr:prop:run

results.name: The friable approximant of Xi is exponentially close to Xi in a strip, with the accuracy set by the first omitted prime
results.summary: For $|\operatorname{Im}t|\le\frac32$ the friable approximant satisfies $|\Xi_P(t)-\Xi(t)|\le|t^2+\frac14|\,\delta_P$ with $\delta_P\le e^{-\pi q^2}/(\pi q^2(1-e^{-2\pi q}))$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. Let $\mathcal F(P)$ be the set of positive integers all of whose prime factors are at most $P$ (the $P$ friable integers), $\psi_P(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathcal F(P)}e^{-\pi n^2x}$, and let the friable approximant be $\Xi_P(t)=\frac12-2(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty\psi_P(e^{2u})e^{u/2}\cos(tu)\,du$ (the same formula with all integers $n$ gives $\Xi$). Let $q$ be the least prime above $P$ and $D_P=\Xi_P-\Xi$ the deficit. Let $\delta_P=\sum_{m\notin\mathcal F(P)}e^{-\pi m^2}/(\pi m^2)$. For $|\operatorname{Im}t|\le\frac32$, $|\Xi_P(t)-\Xi(t)|\le|t^2+\frac14|\,\delta_P$, and $\delta_P\le e^{-\pi q^2}/(\pi q^2(1-e^{-2\pi q}))$.
results.label: mi:thm:approx

results.name: Certified tracking: a Rouche criterion for a real zero of the friable approximant near a simple zero of Xi
results.summary: If a simple zero $\gamma$ of $\Xi$ has $|\Xi|>|t^2+\frac14|\delta_P$ on a circle of radius $r\le\frac32$ about it, then $\Xi_P$ has exactly one zero in the disc, it is real, and its shift from $\gamma$ is given to first order by $-(\Xi_P-\Xi)(\gamma)/\Xi'(\gamma)$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. Let $\mathcal F(P)$ be the set of positive integers all of whose prime factors are at most $P$ (the $P$ friable integers), $\psi_P(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathcal F(P)}e^{-\pi n^2x}$, and let the friable approximant be $\Xi_P(t)=\frac12-2(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty\psi_P(e^{2u})e^{u/2}\cos(tu)\,du$ (the same formula with all integers $n$ gives $\Xi$). Let $q$ be the least prime above $P$ and $D_P=\Xi_P-\Xi$ the deficit. Let $\delta_P=\sum_{m\notin\mathcal F(P)}e^{-\pi m^2}/(\pi m^2)$. If $\gamma$ is a simple zero of $\Xi$ and $|\Xi(t)|>|t^2+\frac14|\delta_P$ on the circle $|t-\gamma|=r\le\frac32$, then $\Xi_P$ has exactly one zero $\gamma_P$ in the disc $|t-\gamma|<r$, it is real, and $\gamma_P-\gamma=-(\Xi_P-\Xi)(\gamma)/\Xi'(\gamma)\,(1+O(\eta))$, where $\eta$ is the ratio of $\max|\Xi_P-\Xi|$ on the disc to $\min|\Xi|$ on the circle.
results.label: mi:cor:rouche

results.name: The symmetrised finite Euler product of Xi has zeros near the lines of its poles with real part tending to one
results.summary: The unregularised symmetrisation F_P of the finite Euler product has zeros within order k to the power minus one half of the poles 1 plus 2 pi i k over log p for infinitely many k, so their real parts tend to one and those of the mirror zeros to zero; this is from a note of Nicholas Polson.
results.statement: Let $P\ge2$, let $\zeta_P(s)=\prod_{p\le P}(1-p^{-s})^{-1}$ be the Euler product over the primes $p\le P$, $\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)$, $E_P(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)\zeta_P(s)$ and $F_P(s)=E_P(s)+E_P(1-s)$, a function with poles on $\operatorname{Re}s=0$ and $\operatorname{Re}s=1$. Let $p\le P$ be prime. For infinitely many integers $k$, $F_P$ has a zero $s_k$ with $\big|s_k-1-\frac{2\pi ik}{\log p}\big|=O(|k|^{-1/2})$, and for $P=2$ every $k$ with $|k|$ large enough qualifies. So $\operatorname{Re}s_k\to1$, and the zeros $1-\bar s_k$ have real parts tending to $0$.
results.label: mi:prop:polezeros

results.name: The folded kernel of the friable approximant has a kink of exact size c_P, so Xi_P tends to c_P on the real line and has finitely many real zeros
results.summary: The folded kernel of $\Xi_P$ has a corner at the origin of size $c_P=\sum_{m\notin\mathcal F(P)}(4\pi m^2-1)e^{-\pi m^2}\sim4\pi q^2e^{-\pi q^2}>0$, so $\Xi_P(t)\to c_P$ along the real axis and $\Xi_P$ has finitely many real zeros.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. Let $\mathcal F(P)$ be the set of positive integers all of whose prime factors are at most $P$ (the $P$ friable integers), $\psi_P(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathcal F(P)}e^{-\pi n^2x}$, and let the friable approximant be $\Xi_P(t)=\frac12-2(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty\psi_P(e^{2u})e^{u/2}\cos(tu)\,du$ (the same formula with all integers $n$ gives $\Xi$). Let $q$ be the least prime above $P$ and $D_P=\Xi_P-\Xi$ the deficit. Fold $\Xi_P$ as $\Xi_P(t)=(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty k_P(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ with kernel $k_P(u)=e^{-u/2}-2e^{u/2}\psi_P(e^{2u})$ and put $c_P=-k_P'(0)$. Then $c_P=\sum_{m\notin\mathcal F(P)}(4\pi m^2-1)e^{-\pi m^2}=4\pi q^2e^{-\pi q^2}(1+O(q^{-2}))>0$, and $\Xi_P(t)=c_P+O_P(t^{-2})$ as $t\to\infty$ along $\mathbb{R}$. Hence $\Xi_P$ has finitely many real zeros.
results.label: mi:thm:kink

results.name: No reweighting of Riemann's theta series by summable weights has infinitely many real zeros
results.summary: For nonzero real weights $w_n$ with $\sum|w_n|n^{-\sigma}<\infty$ for every $\sigma>0$ (this includes the friable truncations), the reweighted function has finitely many real zeros and infinitely many nonreal zeros.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. For real weights $w=(w_n)\ne0$ with $\sum_n|w_n|n^{-\sigma}<\infty$ for every $\sigma>0$ (this includes the weights $1_{\mathcal F(P)}$, for which the sum is $\prod_{p\le P}(1-p^{-\sigma})^{-1}$, and so $\Xi_P$), put $\psi_w(x)=\sum_nw_ne^{-\pi n^2x}$ and $\Xi_w(t)=\frac12-2(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty\psi_w(e^{2u})e^{u/2}\cos(tu)\,du$. Then $\Xi_w$ is even, entire of order at most one, and has finitely many real zeros and infinitely many nonreal zeros.
results.label: mi:thm:noproxy

results.name: Theta series truncated to N terms of Xi: constants, real zeros and nonreal zeros for N equal to 1 and 2 (computed)
results.summary: For the theta series cut after one or two terms the transform tends to a positive constant $c_E$ on the real line ($1.71806\cdot10^{-4}$ and $5.89126\cdot10^{-11}$), has 2 and 6 real zeros in $0<t\le60$ against 13 for Xi, and has the listed nonreal zeros; the zero counts and positions are a computation, a note of Nicholas Polson.
