results.statement: Let $\psi_N(x)=\sum_{n\le N}e^{-\pi n^2x}$ and $\Xi_w(t)=\frac12-2(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty\psi_N(e^{2u})e^{u/2}\cos(tu)\,du$, the weights being $w_n=1$ for $n\le N$ and $0$ otherwise; this is even and entire of order at most one, with finitely many real zeros and infinitely many nonreal zeros, and it tends to $c_E=\sum_{m>N}(4\pi m^2-1)e^{-\pi m^2}>0$ on $\mathbb{R}$. Computed: $c_E=1.71806\cdot10^{-4}$ for $N=1$ and $c_E=5.89126\cdot10^{-11}$ for $N=2$. In $0<t\le60$ the function $\Xi_w$ has $2$ real zeros for $N=1$, at $14.1659$ and $19.5639$, and $6$ for $N=2$, at $14.1347$, $21.0220$, $25.0109$, $30.4243$, $32.9388$ and $37.4954$, against the $13$ zeros of the Riemann Xi function $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$ there. Its nonreal zeros with $0<\operatorname{Re}t\le60$ and $0<\operatorname{Im}t\le12$ are $22.915+4.666i$ and $27.930+9.028i$ for $N=1$, and $41.190+1.462i$, $45.418+4.421i$, $49.549+7.364i$ and $53.720+10.074i$ for $N=2$. These values come from the argument principle and are a computation at these two values of $N$ and this range only. The computation follows a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book.
results.label: mi:res:trunc

results.name: The deficit Xi_P minus Xi is positive on the real line and decreases as the prime bound grows
results.summary: For every prime $P$ and real $t$, $\Xi_P(t)-\Xi(t)>0$, and the deficit decreases strictly as $P$ increases, so $\Xi_P>\Xi_{P'}>\Xi$ on $\mathbb{R}$ for $P<P'$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. Let $\mathcal F(P)$ be the set of positive integers all of whose prime factors are at most $P$ (the $P$ friable integers), $\psi_P(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathcal F(P)}e^{-\pi n^2x}$, and let the friable approximant be $\Xi_P(t)=\frac12-2(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty\psi_P(e^{2u})e^{u/2}\cos(tu)\,du$ (the same formula with all integers $n$ gives $\Xi$). Let $q$ be the least prime above $P$ and $D_P=\Xi_P-\Xi$ the deficit. For all real $t$, $D_P(t)>0$, and $D_P>D_{P'}$ when $P<P'$ are primes. Hence $\Xi_P>\Xi_{P'}>\Xi$ on $\mathbb{R}$.
results.label: mi:thm:positive

results.name: The transform of no theta term vanishes on the real line, and the Laplace law is a mixture of the Polya law and a pole law
results.summary: The cosine transform of every term of the theta series is positive on the real line, so the zeros of Xi are exactly the solutions of $(t^2+\frac14)W(t)=1$ with $W>0$ on the real line, and the Laplace density is the mixture, with weights $1-\upsilon$ and $\upsilon$ where $\upsilon=0.00575844$ (computed), of the Polya law convolved with a Laplace law and an explicit law $p_V$; a note of Nicholas Polson.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)\zeta(s)$, $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, $\psi(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}e^{-\pi n^2x}$ for $x>0$, and for $n\ge1$ and complex $t$ let $C_{\pi n^2}(t)=2\int_0^\infty e^{u/2}e^{-\pi n^2e^{2u}}\cos(tu)\,du$ and $W(t)=4\int_0^\infty\psi(e^{2u})e^{u/2}\cos(tu)\,du=2\sum_{n\ge1}C_{\pi n^2}(t)$. Then $2\Xi(t)=1-(t^2+\frac14)W(t)$ for every complex $t$, and $C_{\pi n^2}(t)>0$ for every $n\ge1$ and every real $t$, so $W>0$ on $\mathbb{R}$. Hence the zeros of $\Xi$ in $\mathbb{C}$ are exactly the solutions of $(t^2+\frac14)W(t)=1$, and the Riemann Hypothesis says that every solution is real: the transform of no term of the theta series vanishes on the real line, and the zeros of $\Xi$ come from the cancellation between the pole term and the whole series. Further, $C_{\pi n^2}(t)/C_{\pi n^2}(0)$ is the characteristic function of the symmetric density proportional to $e^{|u|/2}\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2|u|})$, the law of $\pm\frac12\log X$ with an independent fair sign, where $X$ has density proportional to $x^{-3/4}e^{-\pi n^2x}$ on $[1,\infty)$. So $W(t)/W(0)$ is the characteristic function of the mixture of these laws with weights $2C_{\pi n^2}(0)/W(0)$, with density $p_V(u)=2e^{|u|/2}\psi(e^{2|u|})/W(0)$, where $W(0)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(\pi n^2)^{-1/4}\Gamma(\frac14,\pi n^2)=0.0230338$ (computed). Let $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})e^{-\pi n^2e^{4u}}$, an even function with $\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi=\xi(\frac12)$, so that $\Phi/\xi(\frac12)$ is the Polya density with characteristic function $\Xi(t)/\Xi(0)$, and $\varkappa(u)=\frac14e^{-|u|/2}$ the Laplace density. Then $\varkappa=(1-\upsilon)\,\varkappa\ast\frac{\Phi}{\xi(1/2)}+\upsilon\,p_V$ with $\upsilon=W(0)/4=1-2\xi(\frac12)=0.00575844$ (computed): the Laplace law is the mixture, with weights $1-\upsilon$ and $\upsilon$, of the Polya law plus an independent Laplace variable and of the law $p_V$. The result is from notes of Nicholas Polson merged into the book.
results.label: mi:res:laws

results.name: Uniform Lorentzian bound: the deficit of the friable approximant is a sum of Lorentzians with an explicit uniform relative error
results.summary: For $a\ge9\pi$ the cosine transform $C_a$ of $e^{-ae^w}e^{w/4}$ equals the Lorentzian $\mathcal L_a(t)=e^{-a}b/(b^2+t^2/4)$ with relative error at most $\delta(a)\le5.61/a$, uniformly in real $t$, and the deficit $D_P$ is the corresponding sum over the omitted integers.
results.statement: For $a\ge9\pi$ put $b=a-\frac14$, $f_a(w)=e^{-ae^w}e^{w/4}$, $C_a(t)=\int_0^\infty f_a(w)\cos(tw/2)\,dw$ and $\mathcal L_a(t)=e^{-a}b/(b^2+t^2/4)$. For all real $t$, $|C_a(t)-\mathcal L_a(t)|\le\delta(a)\mathcal L_a(t)$ with $\delta(a)=\frac1b\big[\frac{2ab^2}{(b-1)^3}+\frac{2ab}{(b-1)^2}+\frac{2a^2}{(b-2)^3}+\frac a{b-1}\big]\le5.61/a$. The deficit of the friable approximant $\Xi_P$ (the difference of $\Xi_P$ and Riemann's $\Xi$, for $\mathcal F(P)$ the integers with all prime factors at most $P$) is $D_P(t)=(t^2+\frac14)\sum_{m\notin\mathcal F(P)}C_{\pi m^2}(t)$, so it is a sum of Lorentzians of half widths about $2\pi m^2$ over the omitted integers $m$, with relative error $\delta(\pi q^2)$ for $q$ the least prime above $P$.
results.label: mi:thm:lorentz

results.name: Curvature: the logarithm of the deficit of the friable approximant is uniformly almost convex for t at least 14
results.summary: For every prime $P$ and $t\ge14$, $(\log D_P)''(t)\ge-0.0239$ for the deficit $D_P=\Xi_P-\Xi$, with an explicit bound in terms of the least omitted prime.
results.statement: Let $\mathcal F(P)$ be the set of positive integers all of whose prime factors are at most $P$ (the $P$ friable integers), $\psi_P(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathcal F(P)}e^{-\pi n^2x}$, and let the friable approximant be $\Xi_P(t)=\frac12-2(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty\psi_P(e^{2u})e^{u/2}\cos(tu)\,du$ (the same formula with all integers $n$ gives $\Xi$). Let $q$ be the least prime above $P$ and $D_P=\Xi_P-\Xi$ the deficit. For $a\ge9\pi$ and $b=a-\frac14$ let $\delta=\delta(a)$ be the constant of the uniform Lorentzian bound, $r_1(a)=\frac1{2(1-\delta)b}\big(1+\frac{a^2}{(b-2)^2}+\frac a{(b-1)^2}+\frac{2a}{b-1}\big)$ and $r_2(a)=\frac1{4(1-\delta)b}\big(\frac4b+\frac{2a^2}{(b-2)^3}+\frac{2a}{(b-1)^3}+\frac{4a}{(b-1)^2}\big)$; these bound $|C_a'|/C_a$ and $|C_a''|/C_a$ uniformly in $t$, where $C_a$ is the cosine transform of $e^{-ae^w}e^{w/4}$ at $t/2$. For every prime $P$ and $t\ge14$, with $a_q=\pi q^2$, $(\log D_P)''(t)\ge-2/t^2-r_2(a_q)-r_1(a_q)^2\ge-0.0239$.
results.label: mi:thm:curv

results.name: Real zeros of the friable approximant live in the negative humps of Xi, in pairs, and surviving humps are nested in P
results.summary: Every real zero of $\Xi_P$ lies in a negative hump of $\Xi$ and each hump holds an even number of zeros; for humps below the verified height of RH and shorter than $18.29$, a hump holds none, one double or two simple zeros, according to the sign of $\max(|\Xi|-D_P)$ on it, and surviving humps are nested in $P$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. Let $\mathcal F(P)$ be the set of positive integers all of whose prime factors are at most $P$ (the $P$ friable integers), $\psi_P(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathcal F(P)}e^{-\pi n^2x}$, and let the friable approximant be $\Xi_P(t)=\frac12-2(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty\psi_P(e^{2u})e^{u/2}\cos(tu)\,du$ (the same formula with all integers $n$ gives $\Xi$). Let $q$ be the least prime above $P$ and $D_P=\Xi_P-\Xi$ the deficit. A negative hump is a maximal interval $I_j\subset(0,\infty)$ on which $\Xi<0$, of length $\ell_j$. (1) Every real zero of $\Xi_P$ lies in a negative hump, and $\Xi_P(\gamma)=D_P(\gamma)>0$ at every zero $\gamma$ of $\Xi$. (2) Each hump holds an even number of zeros of $\Xi_P$ counted with multiplicity, and the number $R_P$ of positive real zeros is even. (3) Suppose every zero of $\Xi$ whose real part lies within $\frac12$ of $I_j$ is real (by the verification of the Riemann Hypothesis of Platt and Trudgian (2021) this holds for every hump below $3\cdot10^{12}$) and $\ell_j<18.29$. Then $I_j$ holds no zero, one double zero or two simple zeros of $\Xi_P$, and two simple zeros exactly when $\max_{I_j}(|\Xi|-D_P)>0$. (4) If $I_j$ carries zeros of $\Xi_P$ then it carries zeros of $\Xi_{P'}$ for every prime $P'>P$.
results.label: mi:thm:humps

results.name: Count: the number of positive real zeros of the friable approximant is twice the number of negative humps of Xi deeper than the deficit
results.summary: Under the hypotheses of the hump theorem the number $R_P$ of positive real zeros of $\Xi_P$ is twice the number of humps with $\max(|\Xi|-D_P)>0$, there is a unique height $\tau_P^+$ beyond which $\Xi_P>0$, and $R_P\le2\lceil N(\tau_P^+)/2\rceil$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. Let $\mathcal F(P)$ be the set of positive integers all of whose prime factors are at most $P$ (the $P$ friable integers), $\psi_P(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathcal F(P)}e^{-\pi n^2x}$, and let the friable approximant be $\Xi_P(t)=\frac12-2(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty\psi_P(e^{2u})e^{u/2}\cos(tu)\,du$ (the same formula with all integers $n$ gives $\Xi$). Let $q$ be the least prime above $P$ and $D_P=\Xi_P-\Xi$ the deficit. Let $N(T)$ count the zeros of $\Xi$ in $(0,T]$ with multiplicity, $A(t)=\frac12(t^2+\frac14)\pi^{-1/4}|\Gamma(\frac14+\frac{it}2)|$, so that $\Xi=-AZ$ with $Z$ Hardy's function, and $I_j$ the negative humps of $\Xi$. Assume that for every hump meeting $(0,\tau_P^+)$ the local hypotheses hold (all zeros of $\Xi$ within $\frac12$ of the hump are real, by the verification of the Riemann Hypothesis of Platt and Trudgian (2021) below height $3\cdot10^{12}$, and its length is below $18.29$). Then $R_P=2\#\{j:\max_{I_j}(|\Xi|-D_P)>0\}$. Let $\tau_P^+$ solve $D_P(\tau)=0.63A(\tau)\tau^{1/6}\log\tau$; the solution is unique for $\tau\ge14$ and $\Xi_P>0$ on $(\tau_P^+,\infty)$ (this uses Hiary's bound $|\zeta(\frac12+it)|\le0.63t^{1/6}\log t$). Then $R_P\le2\lceil N(\tau_P^+)/2\rceil$.
results.label: mi:thm:count

results.name: Conjecture: the number of real zeros of the friable approximant is the zero count at the breakdown height plus a correction from the peaks of Hardy's function
results.summary: The number $R_P$ of positive real zeros of $\Xi_P$ is conjectured to equal $N(\tau_P^*)$ plus $\frac2{\pi^2}\log\frac{\tau_P^*}{2\pi}$ times the mean log peak of Hardy's function on negative humps near $\tau_P^*$, up to an error of order $\sqrt{\log q\,\log\log q}$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. Let $\mathcal F(P)$ be the set of positive integers all of whose prime factors are at most $P$ (the $P$ friable integers), $\psi_P(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathcal F(P)}e^{-\pi n^2x}$, and let the friable approximant be $\Xi_P(t)=\frac12-2(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty\psi_P(e^{2u})e^{u/2}\cos(tu)\,du$ (the same formula with all integers $n$ gives $\Xi$). Let $q$ be the least prime above $P$ and $D_P=\Xi_P-\Xi$ the deficit. Let $N(T)$ count the zeros of $\Xi$ in $(0,T]$, $R_P$ the number of positive real zeros of $\Xi_P$, $\tau_P^*$ the breakdown height, the solution of $A(\tau)=D_P(\tau)$ (about $4q^2$, a heuristic formula checked by computation) and $m_Z(T)$ the mean of $\log\max|Z|$ over the negative humps near $T$, for $Z$ Hardy's function. Conjecture: $R_P=N(\tau_P^*)+\frac2{\pi^2}\log\frac{\tau_P^*}{2\pi}\,m_Z(\tau_P^*)+O\big((\log q)^{1/2}(\log\log q)^{1/2}\big)$.
results.label: mi:conj:survey

results.name: Kink budget: the limit of the friable approximant with a smooth even kernel replacing the pole term
results.summary: If the pole kernel $e^{-u/2}$ in the folded kernel of $\Xi_P$ is replaced by an even smooth kernel $\kappa$ with derivatives $O(e^{-u/2})$, the limit of the modified function along the real axis is $c_P-\frac12-\kappa'(0+)$.
results.statement: Let $\mathcal F(P)$ be the set of positive integers all of whose prime factors are at most $P$ (the $P$ friable integers), $\psi_P(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathcal F(P)}e^{-\pi n^2x}$, and let the friable approximant be $\Xi_P(t)=\frac12-2(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty\psi_P(e^{2u})e^{u/2}\cos(tu)\,du$ (the same formula with all integers $n$ gives $\Xi$). Let $q$ be the least prime above $P$ and $D_P=\Xi_P-\Xi$ the deficit. Let $c_P=\sum_{m\notin\mathcal F(P)}(4\pi m^2-1)e^{-\pi m^2}$ be the kink constant. Replace the pole kernel $e^{-u/2}$ in the folded kernel $k_P(u)=e^{-u/2}-2e^{u/2}\psi_P(e^{2u})$ by an even kernel $\kappa$, smooth on $[0,\infty)$ with all derivatives $O(e^{-u/2})$, and let $\Xi_P^\kappa(t)=(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty(k_P+\kappa-e^{-u/2})(u)\cos(tu)\,du$. Then $\lim_{t\to\infty}\Xi_P^\kappa(t)=c_P-\frac12-\kappa'(0+)$ along $\mathbb{R}$.
results.label: mi:prop:kinkbudget

results.name: Reweighting: among weights in [0,1] vanishing on a given set, the indicator of the complement has the smallest deficit
results.summary: For weights $0\le w_n\le w_n'\le1$ the deficits satisfy $D_w\ge D_{w'}\ge0$ with $D_{w'}>0$ unless all $w_n'=1$, so the friable truncation has the smallest deficit among weights in $[0,1]$ that vanish on the omitted set.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. For weights $w=(w_n)$ let $\Xi_w(t)=\frac12-2(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty\psi_w(e^{2u})e^{u/2}\cos(tu)\,du$ with $\psi_w(x)=\sum_nw_ne^{-\pi n^2x}$, and $D_w=\Xi_w-\Xi=(t^2+\frac14)\sum_n(1-w_n)C_{\pi n^2}$, where $C_a$ is the cosine transform of $e^{-ae^w}e^{w/4}$ at $t/2$. If $0\le w_n\le w_n'\le1$ for every $n$ then $D_w\ge D_{w'}\ge0$ on $\mathbb{R}$, with $D_{w'}>0$ unless every $w_n'=1$. So among weights in $[0,1]$ that vanish on a given set of integers, the indicator of its complement has the smallest deficit.
results.label: mi:prop:reweight

results.name: The friable approximants for P = 2 and 3 are uniformly close to Xi on the imaginary axis and have no zero there
results.summary: The relative error $\sup_y|\Xi_P(iy)/\Xi(iy)-1|$ is at most $6.8\times10^{-13}$ for $P=2$ and $3.4\times10^{-35}$ for $P=3$, so neither has a zero on the imaginary axis; the suprema of a proved bound were computed on a grid.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. Let $\mathcal F(P)$ be the set of positive integers all of whose prime factors are at most $P$ (the $P$ friable integers), $\psi_P(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathcal F(P)}e^{-\pi n^2x}$, and let the friable approximant be $\Xi_P(t)=\frac12-2(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty\psi_P(e^{2u})e^{u/2}\cos(tu)\,du$ (the same formula with all integers $n$ gives $\Xi$). Let $q$ be the least prime above $P$ and $D_P=\Xi_P-\Xi$ the deficit. For $P=2$ and $P=3$, $\sup_{y\in\mathbb{R}}|\Xi_P(iy)/\Xi(iy)-1|$ is at most $6.8\times10^{-13}$ for $P=2$ and at most $3.4\times10^{-35}$ for $P=3$. In particular $\Xi_P$ has no zero on $i\mathbb{R}$. The bound rests on the proved estimate $|\Xi_P(iy)-\Xi(iy)|\le|y^2-\frac14|\sum_{m\notin\mathcal F(P)}(\pi m^2)^{-s}\Gamma(s,\pi m^2)$ with $s=\frac12(|y|+\frac12)$, whose supremum after division by $\Xi(iy)=\xi(\frac12+y)>0$ was computed at $30$ digits on a grid of step $0.1$ on $[0,40]$ and shown to decrease beyond it; it is a computation, not a certified enclosure.
results.label: mi:prop:axis

results.name: Shift identity: Xi is the average of two shifts of the transform of Phi divided by cosh, which contains Miyatake's identity
results.summary: For every $b>0$ and complex $z$, $\Xi(z)=\frac12\{g_b(z+ib)+g_b(z-ib)\}$, that is $\Xi=\cos(b\,d/dz)g_b$; Miyatake's identity is the case $b=\frac92$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. Let $\Phi$ be Riemann's kernel, $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})e^{-\pi n^2e^{2u}}$, so that $\Xi(t)=2\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ and $\Phi$ is positive and even. For $b>0$ put $g_b(z)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)\operatorname{sech}(bu)\,e^{izu}\,du$ (the transform of $\Phi/\cosh(bu)$), an entire even function of order at most one, real on $\mathbb{R}$. For every $b>0$ and $z\in\mathbb{C}$, $\Xi(z)=\frac12\{g_b(z+ib)+g_b(z-ib)\}$, that is $\Xi=\cos(b\partial)g_b$ with $\partial=d/dz$. Miyatake's identity is the case $b=\frac92$ (with his transform $g(x)=g_{9/2}(2x)/(4\pi^2)$).
results.label: mi:prop:shiftb

results.name: Levy area, Polya Gamma clock and Thorin atoms: the transform of Phi over cosh is Xi smoothed by Levy's stochastic area
results.summary: The transform $g_b$ equals the expectation of $\Xi(x+2b\mathcal A)$ for Lévy's stochastic area $\mathcal A$, and the expectation of the de Bruijn Newman function at a Pólya Gamma random negative time, so $\Xi\mapsto g_b$ is convolution with an extended generalised gamma convolution with Thorin atoms at the odd multiples of $\pi/(2b)$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. Let $\Phi$ be Riemann's kernel, $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})e^{-\pi n^2e^{2u}}$, so that $\Xi(t)=2\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ and $\Phi$ is positive and even. For $b>0$ put $g_b(z)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)\operatorname{sech}(bu)\,e^{izu}\,du$ (the transform of $\Phi/\cosh(bu)$), an entire even function of order at most one, real on $\mathbb{R}$. Let $\mathcal A=\frac12\int_0^1(W^1dW^2-W^2dW^1)$ be Lévy's stochastic area of a planar Brownian motion $(W^1,W^2)$, with $\mathbb{E}e^{i\lambda\mathcal A}=\operatorname{sech}(\lambda/2)$, let $\varpi$ be a Pólya Gamma variable $\mathrm{PG}(1,0)$ with $\mathbb{E}e^{-s\varpi}=\operatorname{sech}\sqrt{s/2}$, and $\mathcal H_\lambda(z)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)e^{\lambda u^2}e^{izu}\,du$ the de Bruijn Newman family. For real $x$, $g_b(x)=\mathbb{E}\,\Xi(x+2b\mathcal A)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Xi(x-y)\frac1{2b}\operatorname{sech}\frac{\pi y}{2b}\,dy=\mathbb{E}_\varpi[\mathcal H_{-2b^2\varpi}(x)]$, and $2b\mathcal A\overset d=2b\sqrt\varpi\,\mathcal N\overset d=\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{2b}{(2k-1)\pi}L_k$ with $\mathcal N$ standard normal and $L_k$ independent standard Laplace variables. Hence $\Xi\mapsto g_b$ is convolution with an extended generalised gamma convolution whose Thorin measure has atoms at $\pm(2k-1)\pi/(2b)$.
results.label: mi:thm:levyarea

results.name: Logistic partition: 2 xi is the sum of two logistic weighted expectations of a power of a random variable
results.summary: For $c>0$, $2\xi(s)$ is the sum of the expectations of $\Upsilon^s/(1+\Upsilon^c)$ and $\Upsilon^{s+c}/(1+\Upsilon^c)$, for the random variable $\Upsilon$ of the Biane Pitman Yor identity, and the logistic weight is a Pólya Gamma mixture.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Upsilon=V^{1/2}$ with $V$ the random variable of the Biane Pitman Yor identity for $\xi$ (as defined in the book), and $\varpi\sim\mathrm{PG}(1,0)$ a Pólya Gamma variable. For $c>0$, $2\xi(s)=\mathbb{E}[\Upsilon^s/(1+\Upsilon^c)]+\mathbb{E}[\Upsilon^{s+c}/(1+\Upsilon^c)]$; with $c=2b$ and $s=\frac12+iz$ the two terms are $g_b(z+ib)$ and $g_b(z-ib)$, for $g_b$ the transform of $\Phi/\cosh(bu)$. The logistic weight is the Pólya Gamma mixture $\Upsilon^c/(1+\Upsilon^c)=\frac12\Upsilon^{c/2}\mathbb{E}_\varpi\exp(-\frac12\varpi c^2(\log\Upsilon)^2)$ (Polson, Scott and Windle 2013).
results.label: mi:prop:logistic

results.name: Exponential tail: the transform of Phi over cosh has a residue term C_b e^{-pi z/(2b)} exactly when b exceeds 2
results.summary: For $b>2$ the transform $g_b$ equals $C_be^{-\pi z/(2b)}$ plus a faster decaying error, with $C_b=\frac{2\pi}b\Phi(\frac{i\pi}{2b})$, uniformly in horizontal strips; for $b<2$ there is no residue and $g_b(x)=O(e^{-\tau x})$ for every $\tau<\pi/4$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. Let $\Phi$ be Riemann's kernel, $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})e^{-\pi n^2e^{2u}}$, so that $\Xi(t)=2\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ and $\Phi$ is positive and even. For $b>0$ put $g_b(z)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)\operatorname{sech}(bu)\,e^{izu}\,du$ (the transform of $\Phi/\cosh(bu)$), an entire even function of order at most one, real on $\mathbb{R}$. Let $b>2$, $\pi/(2b)<\tau<\min(\pi/4,3\pi/(2b))$ and $Y>0$. Then, uniformly for $\operatorname{Re}z\ge0$ and $|\operatorname{Im}z|\le Y$, $g_b(z)=C_be^{-\pi z/(2b)}+O(e^{-\tau\operatorname{Re}z})$ with $C_b=\frac{2\pi}b\,\Phi(\frac{i\pi}{2b})$. For $b<2$ there is no residue and $g_b(x)=O(e^{-\tau x})$ for every $\tau<\pi/4$.
results.label: mi:thm:tail

results.name: Cusp asymptotics: the residue constant C_b of the transform of Phi over cosh as b decreases to 2
results.summary: With $\delta=\pi(b-2)/(4b)$, as $b\downarrow2$ the constant $C_b$ is asymptotic to $-\frac{\pi^3}{32b}(2\delta)^{-1/2}\delta^{-4}e^{-\frac\pi8\cot\delta}$ and is negative and super exponentially small.
results.statement: Let $\Phi$ be Riemann's kernel, $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})e^{-\pi n^2e^{2u}}$, so that $\Xi(t)=2\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ and $\Phi$ is positive and even. For $b>2$ put $C_b=\frac{2\pi}b\Phi(\frac{i\pi}{2b})$ (the residue constant of the transform of $\Phi/\cosh(bu)$) and $\delta=\pi(b-2)/(4b)$. As $b\downarrow2$, $C_b=-\frac{\pi^3}{32b}(2\delta)^{-1/2}\delta^{-4}e^{-\frac\pi8\cot\delta}(1+O(b-2))$.
results.label: mi:thm:cusp

results.name: For b above 2 with C_b nonzero the transform of Phi over cosh has finitely many real zeros and is not in the Laguerre Polya class
results.summary: For $b>2$ with $C_b\ne0$ the transform $g_b$ has finitely many real zeros and infinitely many nonreal zeros, so it is not in the Laguerre Pólya class; in particular Miyatake's transform ($b=\frac92$, $C_{9/2}>0$) is not.
results.statement: Let $\Phi$ be Riemann's kernel, $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})e^{-\pi n^2e^{2u}}$, so that $\Xi(t)=2\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ and $\Phi$ is positive and even. For $b>0$ put $g_b(z)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)\operatorname{sech}(bu)\,e^{izu}\,du$ (the transform of $\Phi/\cosh(bu)$), an entire even function of order at most one, real on $\mathbb{R}$. For $b>2$ with $C_b=\frac{2\pi}b\Phi(\frac{i\pi}{2b})\ne0$, $g_b$ has finitely many real zeros, infinitely many nonreal zeros, and is not in the Laguerre Pólya class. In particular Miyatake's transform, for which $b=\frac92$ and $C_{9/2}>0$, is not.
results.label: mi:cor:notLP

results.name: Polar part of the Miyatake kernel in the variable cosh t: a simple pole at cos(2 pi/9) with positive residue r_0
results.summary: As a function of $c=\cosh t$ the kernel $\psi_{\mathrm M}$ is analytic on $\operatorname{Re}c>0$ except for one simple pole at $c_0=\cos\frac{2\pi}9$ with residue $r_0=0.009206406367>0$ (digits certified), so $\psi_{\mathrm M}$ is the sum of the theta terms $n^4e^{-2\pi n^2c}$, an exponential mixture $\psi_{\mathrm E}$ carrying the pole and a part analytic on the half plane; a note of Nicholas Polson.
results.statement: Let $\Phi$ be Riemann's kernel, $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})e^{-\pi n^2e^{2u}}$, analytic for $|\operatorname{Im}u|<\frac\pi4$, and let $\psi_{\mathrm M}(t)=\Phi(t/2)/(8\pi^2\cosh(9t/4))$, an even function of $t$ on the strip $|\operatorname{Im}t|<\frac\pi2$. The map $t\mapsto c=\cosh t$ sends this strip, modulo $t\mapsto-t$, one to one onto the half plane $\operatorname{Re}c>0$, so $\psi_{\mathrm M}$ is a function of $c$ there. As a function of $c$, $\psi_{\mathrm M}$ is analytic on $\operatorname{Re}c>0$ except for a simple pole at $c_0=\cos\frac{2\pi}9$ with residue $r_0=\frac{\sin(2\pi/9)}{18\pi^2}\Phi(\frac{i\pi}9)=\frac{\sin(2\pi/9)}{8\pi^3}C_{9/2}>0$, where $C_{9/2}=\frac{4\pi}9\Phi(\frac{i\pi}9)>0$ is the residue constant of the transform of $\Phi$ divided by $\cosh(9u/2)$. Consequently $\psi_{\mathrm M}(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}n^4e^{-2\pi n^2\cosh t}+\psi_{\mathrm E}(t)+\psi_{\mathrm A}(t)$, where $\psi_{\mathrm E}(t)=r_0e^{-2\pi(\cosh t-c_0)}/(\cosh t-c_0)=r_0\int_{2\pi}^\infty e^{c_0a}e^{-a\cosh t}\,da$ (the integral for $\operatorname{Re}\cosh t>c_0$) and $\psi_{\mathrm A}$ is analytic in $c$ on all of $\operatorname{Re}c>0$. Moreover $r_0=0.009206406367$, computed in interval arithmetic with all digits shown certified. The result is from a note of Nicholas Polson.
results.label: mi:prop:polar

results.name: The exponent is forced: an exponential mixture of Pólya Bessel functions has finitely many real zeros unless its exponent is cos(2 pi/9)
results.summary: For $0<\theta<\frac\pi2$, $\theta\ne\frac{2\pi}9$, the exponential mixture $\mathcal E_\theta$ with exponent $\cos\theta$ of the Pólya functions $\frac12\{K_{9/4+iz/2}(a)+K_{9/4-iz/2}(a)\}$ has the asymptotic $\frac{\pi\cos(9\theta/4)}{\sin\theta}e^{-\theta z/2}+O(e^{-\tau\operatorname{Re}z})$, finitely many real zeros, infinitely many nonreal zeros, and is not in the Laguerre Pólya class; only $\cos\frac{2\pi}9$, the exponent of the polar part, is left open.
results.statement: Let $0<\theta<\frac\pi2$ and $a_0>0$, let $K_\nu$ be the modified Bessel function of the second kind, and put $\mathcal E_\theta(z)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\frac{\cosh(9u/2)\,e^{-a_0(\cosh2u-\cos\theta)}}{\cosh2u-\cos\theta}e^{izu}\,du=\int_{a_0}^\infty e^{a\cos\theta}\,\frac12\{K_{\frac94+\frac{iz}2}(a)+K_{\frac94-\frac{iz}2}(a)\}\,da$, the exponential mixture with exponent $\cos\theta$ of the Pólya functions $\frac12\{K_{\frac94+\frac{iz}2}(a)+K_{\frac94-\frac{iz}2}(a)\}$ (the transforms of $\cosh(9u/2)e^{-a\cosh2u}$). For $\theta/2<\tau<\frac\pi4$ and $Y>0$, uniformly for $\operatorname{Re}z\ge0$ and $|\operatorname{Im}z|\le Y$, $\mathcal E_\theta(z)=\frac{\pi\cos(9\theta/4)}{\sin\theta}e^{-\theta z/2}+O(e^{-\tau\operatorname{Re}z})$. If $\theta\ne\frac{2\pi}9$, then $\mathcal E_\theta$ has finitely many real zeros and infinitely many nonreal zeros, and it is not in the Laguerre Pólya class. The conclusion leaves only $\theta=\frac{2\pi}9$, where $\cos(9\theta/4)=0$; whether $\mathcal E_{2\pi/9}$ is in the Laguerre Pólya class is open. The result is from a note of Nicholas Polson.
results.label: mi:prop:rigid

results.name: A Meixner convolution: the polar transform is a Pólya frequency density convolved with a Laguerre Pólya function
results.summary: With $c_1=\cos\frac\pi9$ and $\mathcal U(u)=\cosh(9u/2)/(2(\cosh u-c_1))$ a universal factor, the transform $\Xi^{\mathcal U}$ of $\mathcal U(u)e^{-2\pi\cosh2u}$ is in the Laguerre Pólya class, the Meixner density $q_\varphi$ with characteristic function $(1+\cos\varphi)/(\cosh u+\cos\varphi)$ is a Pólya frequency function and a Gaussian mixture, and the polar transform $\Xi^{\mathrm E}$ equals a constant times $q_{\pi/9}*\Xi^{\mathcal U}$; a note of Nicholas Polson, using theorems of Pólya and Schoenberg.
results.statement: Let $c_1=\cos\frac\pi9$ and $c_0=\cos\frac{2\pi}9=2c_1^2-1$, and let $\mathcal U(u)=\frac{\cosh(9u/2)}{2(\cosh u-c_1)}=\cosh\frac{7u}2+2c_1\cosh\frac{5u}2+(1+2c_0)\cosh\frac{3u}2+(1+2c_1)\cosh\frac u2$, so that $\cosh(9u/2)/(\cosh2u-c_0)=\mathcal U(u)/(\cosh u+c_1)$. Let $P(z)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}e^{-2\pi\cosh2u}e^{izu}\,du$ and $\Xi^{\mathcal U}(z)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\mathcal U(u)e^{-2\pi\cosh2u}e^{izu}\,du=\sum_jm_j\cos(\frac{b_j}2\partial)P$ with $(b_j,m_j)=(7,1),(5,2c_1),(3,1+2c_0),(1,1+2c_1)$, where $\cos(\beta\partial)f(z)=\frac12\{f(z+i\beta)+f(z-i\beta)\}$. (i) $\mathcal U$ is a universal factor in the sense of Pólya, and $\Xi^{\mathcal U}$ is in the Laguerre Pólya class. (ii) For $0\le\varphi<\pi$ let $q_\varphi(x)=\frac{(1+\cos\varphi)\sinh(\varphi x)}{\sin\varphi\,\sinh(\pi x)}$, with $q_0(x)=2x/\sinh(\pi x)$. Then $q_\varphi$ is a probability density with $\int_{\mathbb{R}}q_\varphi(x)e^{iux}\,dx=\frac{1+\cos\varphi}{\cosh u+\cos\varphi}$ and variance $1/(1+\cos\varphi)$, and it is a Pólya frequency function (by Schoenberg's characterisation). Moreover $\frac{1+\cos\varphi}{\cosh u+\cos\varphi}=\mathbb{E}\,e^{-\varsigma_\varphi u^2}$ with $\varsigma_\varphi=\sum_{k\ge0}\big(\frac{e_k}{((2k+1)\pi-\varphi)^2}+\frac{e_k'}{((2k+1)\pi+\varphi)^2}\big)$, $\mathbb{E}\varsigma_\varphi=\frac1{2(1+\cos\varphi)}$, for independent standard exponential variables $e_k,e_k'$. Hence for every kernel $k$ for which the integrals converge, the transform of $k(u)(1+\cos\varphi)/(\cosh u+\cos\varphi)$ is $q_\varphi*\hat k$ ($\hat k$ the transform of $k$); for $k=\Phi$, Riemann's kernel $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})e^{-\pi n^2e^{2u}}$ (so that $\Xi(z)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)e^{izu}\,du$), it is $\mathbb{E}\,\mathcal H_{-\varsigma_\varphi}$ with $\mathcal H_\lambda(z)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)e^{\lambda u^2}e^{izu}\,du$ the de Bruijn Newman family, a flow at a random negative time. (iii) Let $r_0=\frac{\sin(2\pi/9)}{18\pi^2}\Phi(\frac{i\pi}9)=0.009206406367$, the residue at $\cosh t=c_0$ of the Miyatake kernel $\Phi(t/2)/(8\pi^2\cosh(9t/4))$ as a function of $\cosh t$, and let $\Xi^{\mathrm E}(z)=8\pi^2r_0\int_{\mathbb{R}}\frac{\cosh(9u/2)\,e^{-2\pi(\cosh2u-c_0)}}{\cosh2u-c_0}e^{izu}\,du$, the transform of the polar part. Then $\Xi^{\mathrm E}=\frac{8\pi^2r_0e^{2\pi c_0}}{1+c_1}\,q_{\pi/9}*\Xi^{\mathcal U}$. The result is from a note of Nicholas Polson, using Pólya's theorems on universal factors and on the zeros of $K_{iz}$ and Schoenberg's theorem.
results.label: mi:prop:meixner

results.name: The bottom of the cosh ladder is at most the largest real part of a zero of zeta minus one half
results.summary: The bottom rung $B_{\cosh}$ of the cosh ladder satisfies $B_{\cosh}\le\sigma_{\max}-\frac12$, where $\sigma_{\max}$ is the supremum of the real parts of the nontrivial zeros of zeta.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. For real $b$ let $F_b(z)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)\cosh(bu)e^{izu}\,du=\frac12\{\Xi(z+ib)+\Xi(z-ib)\}$, so that $F_b(x)=\operatorname{Re}\xi(\frac12+b+ix)$ on $\mathbb{R}$. Let $B_{\cosh}=\inf\{b\ge0: F_b\text{ has only real zeros}\}$ (the bottom of the cosh ladder; $B_{\cosh}\le\frac12$ by de Bruijn's strip theorem) and $\sigma_{\max}=\sup\operatorname{Re}\rho$ over the nontrivial zeros $\rho$ of zeta. Then $B_{\cosh}\le\sigma_{\max}-\frac12$.
results.label: mi:prop:BTheta

results.name: Conjecture: the bottom of the cosh ladder lies between the asymptotic and the global quasi Riemann abscissa
results.summary: The bottom rung of the cosh ladder is conjectured to satisfy $\sigma_{\max}^\infty-\frac12\le B_{\cosh}\le\sigma_{\max}-\frac12$ with $\sigma_{\max}^\infty=\limsup_{\gamma\to\infty}\beta$; the upper bound is proved.
results.statement: With $F_b(z)=\int\Phi(u)\cosh(bu)e^{izu}\,du$, so that $F_b(x)=\operatorname{Re}\xi(\frac12+b+ix)$ on $\mathbb R$, the cosh ladder of Riemann's xi function, $B_{\cosh}=\inf\{b\ge0: F_b\text{ has only real zeros}\}$ its bottom rung, $\sigma_{\max}=\sup\operatorname{Re}\rho$ and $\sigma_{\max}^\infty=\limsup_{\gamma\to\infty}\beta$ over the nontrivial zeros $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ of zeta: conjecturally $\sigma_{\max}^\infty-\frac12\le B_{\cosh}\le\sigma_{\max}-\frac12$. The upper bound is proved; the lower bound is conjectured. Under the conjecture, lowering the unconditional bound $B_{\cosh}\le\frac12$ is equivalent to a quasi Riemann hypothesis whenever $\sigma_{\max}$ is approached at large height.
results.label: mi:conj:quasi

results.name: Paired form: zeta has no zero to the right of alpha exactly when the real and imaginary parts of xi on the line alpha interlace
results.summary: For $\alpha>\frac12$, zeta has no zero with real part at least $\alpha$ exactly when $E_\alpha(z)=\xi(\alpha-iz)$ is Hermite Biehler, exactly when the real and imaginary parts of $\xi(\alpha+it)$ have only real simple strictly interlacing zeros; hence RH holds if and only if this holds for every $\alpha>\frac12$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function, $\alpha>\frac12$, $E_\alpha(z)=\xi(\alpha-iz)$ and $E^\#(z)=\overline{E(\bar z)}$. The following are equivalent: (i) $\zeta(s)\ne0$ for $\operatorname{Re}s\ge\alpha$; (ii) $E_\alpha$ is Hermite Biehler, that is $|E_\alpha(z)|>|E_\alpha^\#(z)|$ for $\operatorname{Im}z>0$; (iii) $\operatorname{Re}\xi(\alpha+it)$ and $\operatorname{Im}\xi(\alpha+it)$, as entire functions of $t$, have only real simple zeros, and these strictly interlace. Hence the paired bottom rung, the infimum of the $\alpha-\frac12$ for which these hold, is exactly $\sigma_{\max}-\frac12$ (with $\sigma_{\max}$ the supremum of the real parts of the nontrivial zeros), and the Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if (iii) holds for every $\alpha>\frac12$.
results.label: mi:thm:paired

results.name: Real zeros of the real and imaginary parts of xi on a vertical line right of one half have asymptotically full density
results.summary: For $\alpha>\frac12$ with no zero of zeta on the line, $\theta_\alpha(T)-\theta_\alpha(-T)=\pi(N^\pm(T)-2N^\pm_{>\alpha}(T))+O(\log T)$, so $\operatorname{Re}\xi(\alpha+it)$ and $\operatorname{Im}\xi(\alpha+it)$ each have at least $N^\pm(T)-2N^\pm_{>\alpha}(T)-O(\log T)$ real zeros in $[-T,T]$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function, $N^\pm(T)$ the number of nontrivial zeros $\beta+i\gamma$ of zeta with $|\gamma|\le T$, $N^\pm_{>\alpha}(T)$ the number of them with $\beta>\alpha$, and $\theta_\alpha(t)=\arg\xi(\alpha+it)$. For $\alpha>\frac12$ with $\beta\ne\alpha$ for every zero, $\theta_\alpha(T)-\theta_\alpha(-T)=\pi(N^\pm(T)-2N^\pm_{>\alpha}(T))+O(\log T)$. Hence $\operatorname{Re}\xi(\alpha+it)$ and $\operatorname{Im}\xi(\alpha+it)$ each have at least $N^\pm(T)-2N^\pm_{>\alpha}(T)-O(\log T)$ real zeros in $[-T,T]$. If moreover $F_b$, for $b=\alpha-\frac12$ and $F_b(z)=\operatorname{Re}\xi(\alpha+iz)$, satisfies the Riemann von Mangoldt formula with error $O(\log T)$, its nonreal zeros with $|\operatorname{Re}z|\le T$ number at most $2N^\pm_{>\alpha}(T)+O(\log T)$.
results.label: mi:thm:density

results.name: Interlacing across rungs: criteria for the zeros of the real and imaginary parts of xi on two lines to alternate or to fail to alternate
results.summary: For $1<\alpha<\alpha'$ the phase difference of $\xi$ on the two lines is $\frac{h\pi}4$ up to $\mathcal I=\log(\zeta(\alpha)/\zeta(\alpha'))$, so the zeros of the real parts (or of the imaginary parts) alternate for large height when $[\frac{h\pi}4-\mathcal I,\frac{h\pi}4+\mathcal I]$ lies between consecutive multiples of $\pi$, and the real and imaginary parts alternate when it lies between consecutive odd multiples of $\frac\pi2$, while they fail to alternate at arbitrarily large height when a multiple of $\pi$, or an odd multiple of $\frac\pi2$, lies inside $(\frac{h\pi}4-J,\frac{h\pi}4+J)$; a note of Nicholas Polson.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)\zeta(s)$ be Riemann's xi function. For $\alpha>1$ let $A_\alpha(t)=\operatorname{Re}\xi(\alpha+it)$ and $B_\alpha(t)=\operatorname{Im}\xi(\alpha+it)$ for real $t$, and write $\xi(\alpha+it)=|\xi(\alpha+it)|e^{i\theta_\alpha(t)}$ with $\theta_\alpha$ continuous and $\theta_\alpha(0)=0$. Let $1<\alpha<\alpha'$, $h=\alpha'-\alpha$, $D=\theta_{\alpha'}-\theta_\alpha$, $\mathcal I=\int_\alpha^{\alpha'}M(\sigma)\,d\sigma=\log\frac{\zeta(\alpha)}{\zeta(\alpha')}$ where $M(\sigma)=-\zeta'(\sigma)/\zeta(\sigma)=\sum_n\Lambda(n)n^{-\sigma}$ ($\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function), $\arg\zeta(\sigma+it)=\operatorname{Im}\log\zeta(\sigma+it)$ with $\log\zeta(s)=\sum_n\Lambda(n)n^{-s}/\log n$, and $J=\sum_p(\arctan p^{-\alpha}-\arctan p^{-\alpha'})\le\mathcal I$ with the sum over primes $p$. Then $D(t)=\frac{h\pi}4+\arg\zeta(\alpha'+it)-\arg\zeta(\alpha+it)+O(1/t)$, so $|D(t)-\frac{h\pi}4|\le\mathcal I+O(1/t)$. Two sequences of zeros alternate if between any two consecutive zeros of either there is exactly one zero of the other. (i) If $[\frac{h\pi}4-\mathcal I,\frac{h\pi}4+\mathcal I]\subset(k\pi,(k+1)\pi)$ for an integer $k$, the zeros of $A_\alpha$ and $A_{\alpha'}$ alternate for large $t$, and so do those of $B_\alpha$ and $B_{\alpha'}$. (ii) If $[\frac{h\pi}4-\mathcal I,\frac{h\pi}4+\mathcal I]\subset(k\pi-\frac\pi2,k\pi+\frac\pi2)$ for an integer $k$, the zeros of $A_\alpha$ and $B_{\alpha'}$ alternate for large $t$, and so do those of $B_\alpha$ and $A_{\alpha'}$. (iii) If a multiple of $\pi$ lies in $(\frac{h\pi}4-J,\frac{h\pi}4+J)$, the zeros of $A_\alpha$ and $A_{\alpha'}$ fail to alternate at arbitrarily large $t$ (two consecutive zeros of one function with no zero of the other between them); if an odd multiple of $\frac\pi2$ does, so do those of $A_\alpha$ and $B_{\alpha'}$. The result is from a note of Nicholas Polson.
results.label: mi:prop:pairs

results.name: Non interlacing: the zeros of A_alpha and of the Bessel functions K do not alternate with the real zeros of Xi
results.summary: For $\alpha>1$ the real part of $\xi(\alpha+it)$ has $N(T)-S(T)+O_\alpha(1)$ zeros up to $T$, and $\operatorname{Re}K_{9/4+it/2}(a)$ has $\frac T{2\pi}(\log\frac Ta-1)+O_a(1)$, so neither alternates with the real zeros of $\Xi$ for large $t$ (for the Bessel functions with $a>2\pi$ under the Riemann Hypothesis), and two Bessel functions with different $a$ do not alternate; a note of Nicholas Polson.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function, $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, $\vartheta$ the Riemann Siegel theta function, $N(T)=\frac{\vartheta(T)}\pi+1+S(T)$ the number of zeros $\gamma$ of $\Xi$ with $0<\gamma\le T$ and $S(T)=\frac1\pi\arg\zeta(\frac12+iT)$. (i) For $\alpha>1$, $A_\alpha(t)=\operatorname{Re}\xi(\alpha+it)$ has $N(T)-S(T)+O_\alpha(1)$ zeros in $(0,T]$; hence the zeros of $A_\alpha$ do not alternate with the real zeros of $\Xi$ for large $t$. (ii) For $a>0$ and $K_\nu$ the modified Bessel function of the second kind, $\operatorname{Re}K_{\frac94+\frac{it}2}(a)$ has $\frac T{2\pi}(\log\frac Ta-1)+O_a(1)$ zeros in $(0,T]$; hence two of these functions with different $a$ do not alternate for large $t$, and none alternates with the real zeros of $\Xi$ for large $t$ if $a\le2\pi$, or, under the Riemann Hypothesis, if $a>2\pi$. Alternation means that between any two consecutive zeros of either sequence there is exactly one zero of the other. The result is from a note of Nicholas Polson.
results.label: mi:prop:noninter

results.name: Collision of one pair of zeros under a random vertical average: the critical spread depends on the variance and the fourth moment
results.summary: For a real entire function $G$ of order less than two and $F_\eta(z)=((z-a)^2+\eta^2)G(z)$, the average $\mathbb{E}F_\eta(z+is\ell)$ over a symmetric unit variance bounded or normal $\ell$ has near $a$ a nonreal pair of zeros for $s<s_c$, a double real zero at $s_c$ and two real zeros for $s>s_c$, with $s_c^2=\eta^2-d_c\eta^4+O(\eta^6)$ and $d_c=\tau_1^2-\frac{m_4-1}2\tau_2$; a note of Nicholas Polson.
results.statement: Let $G$ be a real entire function of order less than two, $a\in\mathbb{R}$ with $G(a)\ne0$, $\tau_j=G^{(j)}(a)/G(a)$ and $F_\eta(z)=((z-a)^2+\eta^2)G(z)$ for $\eta>0$. Let $\ell$ be a symmetric random variable, bounded or standard normal, with $\mathbb{E}\ell^2=1$ and fourth moment $m_4=\mathbb{E}\ell^4$, and put $d_c=\tau_1^2-\frac{m_4-1}2\tau_2$. For every $K>|d_c|$ there are $r>0$ and $\eta_0>0$ such that for $0<\eta<\eta_0$ and $s>0$ with $|s^2-\eta^2|\le K\eta^4$ the function $z\mapsto\mathbb{E}F_\eta(z+is\ell)$ has exactly two zeros in $|z-a|<r$, and there is $s_c$ with $s_c^2=\eta^2-d_c\,\eta^4+O(\eta^6)$ such that the two zeros are a nonreal conjugate pair for $s<s_c$, a double real zero at $a+\tau_1\eta^2+O(\eta^4)$ for $s=s_c$, and real and distinct for $s>s_c$. The result is from a note of Nicholas Polson.
results.label: mi:prop:collision

results.name: Cosine and Gaussian tilts of the Pólya law with variance at least 9/64 if there is no zero beyond 7/8
results.status_text: conditional on The Riemann zeta function has no zero with real part greater than 7/8 (announced by OpenAI in October 2026, not refereed, and not proved in the book)
results.conditions: The Riemann zeta function has no zero with real part greater than 7/8 (announced by OpenAI in October 2026, not refereed, and not proved in the book).
results.summary: If the Riemann zeta function has no zero with real part above 7/8, then tilting the Pólya density by cosh(at) with a at least 3/8, or by other multipliers of variance at least 9/64, gives a ferromagnetic law, against 1/2 and 1/4 with no hypothesis.
results.statement: Let $X$ be the Pólya variable, the symmetric random variable with density $p=\Phi/\xi(\frac12)$, where $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ and $\Phi(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}(4\pi^2n^4e^{9t/2}-6\pi n^2e^{5t/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2t})$. For $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_N>0$ and $\mu\ge0$ put $m(t)=e^{\mu t^2}\prod_{k\le N}\cosh(\lambda_kt)$ and $c(m)=2\mu+\sum_{k\le N}\lambda_k^2$, so that $m(t)=\mathbb{E}e^{tY}$ for $Y=\sqrt{2\mu}\,Z+\sum_k\lambda_k\varepsilon_k$ with $Z$ standard normal and $\varepsilon_k$ independent fair random signs, and $c(m)=\operatorname{Var}Y$; the same applies with $N=\infty$ when $\sum_k\lambda_k^2<\infty$. A law is ferromagnetic if it is symmetric, has $\mathbb{E}e^{b_0X^2}<\infty$ for some $b_0>0$, and its moment generating function vanishes only on the imaginary axis. Assume that $\zeta$ has no zero with real part greater than $\frac78$. Then the zeros of $z\mapsto\int\Phi(t)m(t)e^{izt}\,dt$ lie in the strip $|\operatorname{Im}z|\le(\max(\frac9{64}-c(m),0))^{1/2}$. In particular the law with density proportional to $m\,p$ is ferromagnetic whenever $\operatorname{Var}Y\ge\frac9{64}$; for example $\cosh(at)\,p(t)$ is ferromagnetic for $a\ge\frac38$ and $\frac{\sinh(ct)}{ct}\,p(t)$ for $c\ge\frac{3\sqrt3}8$. With no hypothesis on the zeros the same statements hold with $\frac14$ in place of $\frac9{64}$, by theorems of de Bruijn (1950), so that $\cosh(at)\,p(t)$ is ferromagnetic for $a\ge\frac12$.
results.label: fm:prop:bruijn

results.name: Ferromagnetic laws with density proportional to a multiplier times exp(-a cosh(l t)), Bessel transform and clock
results.summary: Multiplying the kernel exp(-a cosh(l t)) by a product of cosh factors and a Gaussian factor always gives a ferromagnetic law with no Gaussian component, whose moment generating function and clock are explicit averages of Macdonald functions K of real order, with the clock for no multiplier a sum of exponential variables divided by the squared zeros of K of imaginary order; this is from a note of Nicholas Polson.
results.statement:
A symmetric real random variable $X$ is called ferromagnetic if $\mathbb{E}e^{b_0X^2}<\infty$ for some $b_0>0$ and its moment generating function $L_X(z)=\mathbb{E}e^{zX}$, which is then entire, vanishes only on the imaginary axis; by Newman's theorem $L_X(s)=e^{bs^2}\prod_k(1+s^2/c_k^2)$ with $b\ge0$ and $c_k>0$. Let $K_
u(a)=\int_0^\infty e^{-a\cosh u}\cosh(
u u)\,du$ be the Macdonald function, for $a>0$ and complex order $
u$. Let $a,\ell>0$, $\mu\ge0$ and $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_N\ge0$, let $Z$ be standard normal and $\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_N$ independent signs $\pm1$ with probability $ rac12$ each, independent of $Z$, let $Y=\sqrt{2\mu}\,Z+\sum_{k\le N}\lambda_k\varepsilon_k$, so that $m(t)=\mathbb{E}e^{tY}=e^{\mu t^2}\prod_{k\le N}\cosh(\lambda_kt)$, and let $q$ be the probability density on $\mathbb{R}$ proportional to $m(t)e^{-a\cosh\ell t}$. Then: (i) $q$ is ferromagnetic, it has Gaussian moments of all orders, and its Gaussian component is zero ($b=0$). (ii) $\int_{\mathbb{R}}m(t)e^{-a\cosh\ell t}\,dt= rac2\ell\,\mathbb{E}K_{Y/\ell}(a)$ and the moment generating function of $q$ is $L_q(s)=\mathbb{E}K_{(s+Y)/\ell}(a)/\mathbb{E}K_{Y/\ell}(a)$ for complex $s$; for $\mu=0$ the expectations are averages over the $2^N$ values of $Y$. (iii) The clock $T_q$ of $q$ is the generalised gamma convolution, with drift $b=0$ and a unit Thorin atom at the square of each positive zero of the characteristic function of $q$, whose Laplace transform is $\mathbb{E}e^{-uT_q}=1/L_q(\sqrt u)$; here $\mathbb{E}e^{-uT_q}=\mathbb{E}K_{Y/\ell}(a)/\mathbb{E}K_{(\sqrt u+Y)/\ell}(a)$ for $u\ge0$. For $m\equiv1$, $T_q=\ell^{-2}\sum_je_j/
u_j(a)^2$ with $e_j$ independent standard exponential variables and $0<
u_1(a)\le
u_2(a)\le\cdots$ the zeros of $
u\mapsto K_{i
u}(a)$ on $(0,\infty)$ listed with multiplicity.
results.label: fm:thm:bessel

results.name: Laws on a Bessel kernel as logarithms of mixtures of generalised inverse Gaussian laws
results.summary: Each law with density proportional to m(t) exp(-a cosh(l t)) is the law of the logarithm of a generalised inverse Gaussian variable with a random index weighted by the Macdonald function, so that for no Gaussian factor it can be sampled exactly; this is from a note of Nicholas Polson.
results.statement: Let $a,\ell>0$, $\mu\ge0$, $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_N\ge0$, $Z$ standard normal, $\varepsilon_k$ independent signs, $Y=\sqrt{2\mu}\,Z+\sum_{k\le N}\lambda_k\varepsilon_k$, $m(t)=\mathbb{E}e^{tY}$ and $q$ the probability density proportional to $m(t)e^{-a\cosh\ell t}$. Let $K_v(a)=\int_0^\infty e^{-a\cosh u}\cosh(vu)\,du$, and for real $v$ let $G_v$ have the generalised inverse Gaussian density $g^{v-1}e^{-\frac a2(g+1/g)}/(2K_v(a))$ on $(0,\infty)$. Let $V$ be a random index with $\mathbb{E}h(V)=\mathbb{E}[h(Y/\ell)K_{Y/\ell}(a)]/\mathbb{E}K_{Y/\ell}(a)$ and, given $V$, let $G_V$ have the density of index $V$. Then $q$ is the law of $\ell^{-1}\log G_V$, and also the law of $\varepsilon\,\ell^{-1}\log G_{|V|}$, with $\varepsilon$ a sign independent of $V$ and $G_{|V|}$. For $\mu=0$, $V$ takes the values $\ell^{-1}\sum_k\eta_k\lambda_k$, $\eta\in\{\pm1\}^N$, with probabilities proportional to $K_{\ell^{-1}\sum_k\eta_k\lambda_k}(a)$.
results.label: fm:prop:besselgig

results.name: No sequence of laws on a convergent Bessel kernel with Laguerre Pólya multipliers converges in law to the Pólya law
results.summary: A sequence of laws with density proportional to a Laguerre Pólya multiplier times exp(-a_n cosh(l_n t)), with kernel parameters converging to positive limits, cannot converge in law to the Pólya law, with or without RH, because the Pólya density has a natural boundary; this answers a question of a note of Nicholas Polson.
results.statement: Let $p=\Phi/\xi(\frac12)$ be the Pólya density, where $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ and $\Phi(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}(4\pi^2n^4e^{9t/2}-6\pi n^2e^{5t/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2t})$, a function with a natural boundary on the lines $\operatorname{Im}t=\pm\pi/4$. Let $a_n\to a$ and $\ell_n\to\ell$ with $a,\ell>0$, and let $q_n$ be the probability density proportional to $m_n(t)e^{-a_n\cosh\ell_nt}$, where $m_n(t)=\psi_n(it)$ for an even entire function $\psi_n$ of the Laguerre Pólya class with $\psi_n(0)>0$, that is $\psi_n(z)=\psi_n(0)e^{-\alpha_nz^2}\prod_j(1-z^2/z_{n,j}^2)$ with $\alpha_n\ge0$, $z_{n,j}>0$ and $\sum_jz_{n,j}^{-2}<\infty$. Then $q_n$ does not converge in law to $p$. The multipliers $e^{\mu t^2}\prod_{k\le N}\cosh(\lambda_kt)$ with $\mu,\lambda_k\ge0$ are of this form, and so are $e^{\mu t^2}\prod_{k\ge1}\cosh(\lambda_kt)$ with $\sum_k\lambda_k^2<\infty$. Consequently a sequence of laws of Theorem fm:thm:bessel (multipliers $e^{\mu t^2}\prod_{k\le N}\cosh(\lambda_kt)$), which are ferromagnetic, converging in law to $p$ would prove RH, by the closure of ferromagnetic laws under convergence in law, and its kernel parameters $(a_n,\ell_n)$ would have no limit point in $(0,\infty)^2$; whether such a sequence exists is not known.
results.label: fm:prop:fixedkernel

results.name: Coupled spins with Bessel kernel laws and a ferromagnetic interaction have ferromagnetic nonnegative combinations
results.summary: For spins whose single laws are the Bessel kernel laws of the ferromagnetic theorem, coupled by a nonnegative symmetric interaction J, every combination of the spins with nonnegative coefficients is ferromagnetic; this is from notes of Nicholas Polson.
results.statement: A symmetric real random variable $X$ is called ferromagnetic if $\mathbb{E}e^{b_0X^2}<\infty$ for some $b_0>0$ and its moment generating function $L_X(z)=\mathbb{E}e^{zX}$, which is then entire, vanishes only on the imaginary axis. Let $q_1,\dots,q_N$ be probability densities on $\mathbb{R}$, each proportional to $m_i(t)e^{-a_i\cosh\ell_it}$ with $a_i,\ell_i>0$ and $m_i(t)=e^{\mu_it^2}\prod_{k\le N_i}\cosh(\lambda_{ik}t)$ with $\mu_i,\lambda_{ik}\ge0$ (the laws of the Bessel kernel theorem, which are ferromagnetic with Gaussian moments of all orders). Let $J=(J_{ij})$ be a symmetric matrix with $J_{ij}\ge0$ and $J_{ii}=0$, and let $(X_1,\dots,X_N)$ have density on $\mathbb{R}^N$ proportional to $\exp\big(\sum_{i<j}J_{ij}t_it_j\big)\prod_iq_i(t_i)$. Then $M=\sum_ic_iX_i$ is ferromagnetic for all $c_1,\dots,c_N\ge0$, not all $0$.
results.label: fm:cor:coupled

results.name: Zeros of the transform of two weakly coupled Bessel spins move by order J at a simple zero and by plus or minus the square root of J at a common zero
results.summary: For the sum of two coupled spins with Bessel kernel laws, a simple zero of one characteristic function that is not a zero of the other moves by J times the logarithmic derivative of the other, and a common simple zero splits into a real pair at distance twice the square root of J, as J decreases to zero; this is from notes of Nicholas Polson.
results.statement: Let $q_1,q_2$ be laws of the Bessel kernel theorem (densities proportional to $m_i(t)e^{-a_i\cosh\ell_it}$ with $a_i,\ell_i>0$ and $m_i(t)=e^{\mu_it^2}\prod_{k\le N_i}\cosh(\lambda_{ik}t)$, $\mu_i,\lambda_{ik}\ge0$), with characteristic functions $\varphi_1,\varphi_2$. For $J>0$ let $(X_1,X_2)$ have density proportional to $e^{Jt_1t_2}q_1(t_1)q_2(t_2)$, so that the characteristic function of $X_1+X_2$ is proportional to $Z_J(\theta)=\sum_{n\ge0}\frac{(-J)^n}{n!}\varphi_1^{(n)}(\theta)\varphi_2^{(n)}(\theta)$. As $J\downarrow0$: (i) if $\alpha$ is a simple zero of $\varphi_1$ and $\varphi_2(\alpha)\ne0$, then $Z_J$ has a zero $\alpha+J\varphi_2'(\alpha)/\varphi_2(\alpha)+O(J^2)$. (ii) If $\alpha$ is a simple zero of both $\varphi_1$ and $\varphi_2$, then $Z_J$ has the two real zeros $\alpha\pm\sqrt J+\frac J4\big(\frac{\varphi_1''}{\varphi_1'}+\frac{\varphi_2''}{\varphi_2'}\big)(\alpha)+O(J^{3/2})$, at distance $2\sqrt J+O(J^{3/2})$.
results.label: fm:prop:levelrep

results.name: Mellin transform of the clock of the Bessel K pair has no zero in a box where the uniform pair has two (computed)
results.summary: For two copies of the Bessel K law with characteristic function $K_{i\theta/4}(\pi)/K_0(\pi)$ the Mellin transform of the clock has no zero in a box holding two zeros of the uniform pair, by a sampled argument principle count that is not a ball proof.
results.statement: Let $q$ be the law with characteristic function $\varphi_q(\theta)=K_{i\theta/4}(\pi)/K_0(\pi)$ ($K_\nu$ the modified Bessel function of the second kind), the ferromagnetic law with density proportional to $e^{-\pi\cosh4t}$ on $\mathbb{R}$; for the sum of two independent copies the number of zeros of the characteristic function in $(0,\theta]$ has the main terms of the Riemann von Mangoldt formula. Let $\mathcal D$ be the Mellin transform of the Laplace transform of the clock (the sum of $e_k/c_k^2$ over the zeros $\pm c_k$ of the characteristic function, $e_k$ independent standard exponential variables). The transform of the pair of two copies, and that of a single copy, have no zero in the box $-0.95<\operatorname{Re}w<-0.05$, $\frac12<\operatorname{Im}w<11$, in which the transform of the uniform pair $\pi U+\pi U'$ has the two zeros $\frac{\rho_1-1}2$ and $\frac{\rho_2-1}2$, where $\rho_k=\frac12+i\gamma_k$ are the first two zeros of $\zeta$ on the critical line (computed: the argument principle on the boundaries of the boxes $\frac12<\operatorname{Im}w<\frac{17}2$ and $\frac{17}2<\operatorname{Im}w<11$, sampled, not a ball proof, with the uniform pair computed by the same quadrature as a control, which gives winding $1$ in each box). The result follows a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book.
results.label: fm:res:besselmellin

results.name: The components of the theta series in Riemann's formula and their mixture are not ferromagnetic
results.summary: The laws with densities proportional to $e^{|t|/2}\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2|t|})$ and to their sum over $n\ge1$ have a characteristic function that is positive on the real line, entire and with infinitely many zeros, none real, so none is ferromagnetic.
results.statement: For $n\ge1$ let $r_n(t)=e^{|t|/2}\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2|t|})$, and consider the laws on $\mathbb{R}$ with densities proportional to $r_n$ and to $\sum_{m\ge1}r_m$ (the components of the theta series in Riemann's formula for the xi function and their mixture). Each of these laws is symmetric, has finite moments of all orders (indeed $\mathbb{E}e^{b|X|}<\infty$ for every $b\ge0$, so the characteristic function is entire of order at most one), and has a characteristic function positive on $\mathbb{R}$, and none of them is ferromagnetic, that is, none has a characteristic function with only real zeros: each characteristic function has infinitely many zeros and none of them is real. For $n=1$ the characteristic function has $5$ zeros in the box $0\le\operatorname{Re}\theta\le40$, $0\le\operatorname{Im}\theta\le30$, the two of least modulus being $13.0885+10.8707i$ and $20.1987+15.0786i$ (computed by the argument principle). The result is from a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book.
results.label: fm:prop:nocomponent

results.name: Zero completed laws of the Pólya variable, the Maxwell construction and a criterion for RH
results.summary: Keeping the first K zero factors of the Pólya characteristic function and a Gaussian factor gives laws that are exactly ferromagnetic for K up to 16 by a Maxwell construction with a certified inequality, ferromagnetic whenever nonnegative, and whose characteristic functions converge to that of the Pólya law exactly when the Riemann Hypothesis holds.
results.statement: Let $X$ be the Pólya variable, the symmetric random variable with density $p=\Phi/\xi(\frac12)$, where $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ and $\Phi(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}(4\pi^2n^4e^{9t/2}-6\pi n^2e^{5t/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2t})$, with characteristic function $\varphi_X$. Let $\gamma_1\le\gamma_2\le\cdots$ be the positive ordinates of the zeros $\frac12\pm i\gamma_k$ of $\zeta$ on the critical line, with multiplicity, and put $s_K=\sum_{k\le K}\gamma_k^{-2}$, $\beta_K=\frac12\operatorname{Var}X - s_K$ and $\varphi_K(\theta)=e^{-\beta_K\theta^2}\prod_{k\le K}(1-\theta^2/\gamma_k^2)$. Let $M_1,M_2,\dots$ be independent symmetric Maxwell variables (density $x^2e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}$, characteristic function $(1-\theta^2)e^{-\theta^2/2}$, variance $3$), each ferromagnetic, and let $Z$ be a standard normal variable independent of them. A law is ferromagnetic if it is symmetric, has $\mathbb{E}e^{b_0X^2}<\infty$ for some $b_0>0$, and its moment generating function vanishes only on the imaginary axis. (i) With no hypothesis, $\beta_K>0$ for every $K$. If $3s_K\le\operatorname{Var}X$, then $\varphi_K$ is the characteristic function of $X_K=(\operatorname{Var}X-3s_K)^{1/2}Z+\sum_{k\le K}M_k/\gamma_k$, whose law $f_K$ is ferromagnetic, with $\operatorname{Var}X_K=\operatorname{Var}X$ and $\kappa_4(X_K)=-12\sum_{k\le K}\gamma_k^{-4}$. The condition $3s_K\le\operatorname{Var}X$ holds for $K\le16$ and fails for $K=17$, a certified computation in ball arithmetic ($3s_{16}=0.0456803$, $\operatorname{Var}X=0.0462100$, $3s_{17}=0.0463006$). (ii) For every $K$, if the inverse Fourier transform $f_K$ of $\varphi_K$ is nonnegative, then $f_K$ is a ferromagnetic probability density. (iii) The Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if $\varphi_K\to\varphi_X$ pointwise as $K\to\infty$. Under the Riemann Hypothesis, $f_K$ converges in law to the Pólya law along every sequence of $K$ for which $f_K\ge0$.
results.label: fm:thm:zc

results.name: RH is equivalent to an identity in law between the smoothed Pólya variable and a series of Maxwell variables
results.summary: The Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if the Pólya variable plus an independent Gaussian of half its variance has the law of the series of independent Maxwell variables divided by the ordinates of the zeros.
results.statement: Let $X$ be the Pólya variable, the symmetric random variable with density $p=\Phi/\xi(\frac12)$, where $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ and $\Phi(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}(4\pi^2n^4e^{9t/2}-6\pi n^2e^{5t/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2t})$, and let $Z$ be a standard normal variable independent of $X$. Let $\gamma_1\le\gamma_2\le\cdots$ be the positive ordinates of the zeros $\frac12\pm i\gamma_k$ of $\zeta$ on the critical line, with multiplicity, let $M_1,M_2,\dots$ be independent symmetric Maxwell variables with density $x^2e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}$, and put $\mathcal M=\sum_kM_k/\gamma_k$, a series that converges almost surely because its terms are independent and centred with summable variances $3\gamma_k^{-2}$. Then the Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if $X+\big(\tfrac12\operatorname{Var}X\big)^{1/2}Z\overset{d}{=}\mathcal M$.
results.label: fm:thm:maxwell

results.name: Total variation distance from the Pólya law to ferromagnetic laws is below two millionths, with no hypothesis
results.summary: With no hypothesis the total variation distance from the Pólya law to the ferromagnetic laws is below 1.932 × 10^-6 by a certified computation in ball arithmetic and below 1.266 × 10^-4 by an explicit construction, below 6.024 × 10^-6 by a fitted law on a Bessel kernel (a note of Nicholas Polson), and it is zero exactly when the Riemann Hypothesis holds.
results.statement: Let $X$ be the Pólya variable, the symmetric random variable with density $p=\Phi/\xi(\frac12)$, where $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ and $\Phi(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}(4\pi^2n^4e^{9t/2}-6\pi n^2e^{5t/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2t})$. A law is ferromagnetic if it is symmetric, has $\mathbb{E}e^{b_0Y^2}<\infty$ for some $b_0>0$, and its moment generating function vanishes only on the imaginary axis. Let $\delta$ be the infimum of the total variation distances $\sup_A|P(X\in A)-P(Y\in A)|$ from $X$ to ferromagnetic variables $Y$; when $Y$ has a density $f$ the distance is $\operatorname{TV}(f,p)=\frac12\int|f - p|$. Let $\gamma_1\le\gamma_2\le\cdots$ be the positive ordinates of the zeros $\frac12\pm i\gamma_k$ of $\zeta$ on the critical line, with multiplicity, put $s_K=\sum_{k\le K}\gamma_k^{-2}$ and $\beta_K=\frac12\operatorname{Var}X - s_K$, and let $f_K$ be the function with Fourier transform $\varphi_K(\theta)=e^{-\beta_K\theta^2}\prod_{k\le K}(1-\theta^2/\gamma_k^2)$. With no hypothesis on the zeros: $f_{16}$ is a ferromagnetic probability density, an explicit sum of a normal variable and Maxwell variables, and $\operatorname{TV}(f_{16},p)<1.266\times10^{-4}$, so that $\delta<1.266\times10^{-4}$; and $f_{150}$ is a ferromagnetic probability density by a computer assisted proof in ball arithmetic (the polynomial in the Hermite basis that multiplies the Gaussian is positive on the real line) with $\operatorname{TV}(f_{150},p)<1.932\times10^{-6}$, so that $\delta<1.932\times10^{-6}$; and the law $q$ with density proportional to $\cosh(\lambda t)\,e^{-a\cosh\ell t}$, $\lambda=2.146184$, $a=5.483952$, $\ell=2.062866$, is ferromagnetic (by Theorem fm:thm:bessel: the law proportional to $e^{-a\cosh\ell t}$ is ferromagnetic since $z\mapsto K_{iz}(a)$ has only real zeros (P\'olya), and the tilt by $\cosh(\lambda t)$ keeps it ferromagnetic; $L_q(s)=\frac{K_{(s+\lambda)/\ell}(a)+K_{(s-\lambda)/\ell}(a)}{2K_{\lambda/\ell}(a)}$) and $\operatorname{TV}(q,p)<6.024\times10^{-6}$, so that $\delta<6.024\times10^{-6}$. The distances are enclosed in ball arithmetic, with explicit bounds for the discretisation and the tails. The Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if $\delta=0$.
results.label: fm:prop:tvcert

results.name: A cusped weight never gives a ferromagnetic tilt nor a GGC tilted clock
results.summary: For every $\mu>0$ the Pólya law tilted by the cusped weight $e^{-\mu|t|/2}$ is not ferromagnetic and the correspondingly tilted clock is not a generalized gamma convolution, because the transform $H^{(\mu)}$ of the tilted kernel is a Cauchy average of the xi function with a tail of order $1/z^2$, so it is positive beyond some height and has finitely many real zeros.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be the completed Riemann zeta function, $\Phi(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}(4\pi^2n^4e^{9t/2}-6\pi n^2e^{5t/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2t})$ and $p=\Phi/\xi(\frac12)$ the Pólya density, and $\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)=\frac12\Phi(2u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})$, the kernel of the de Bruijn Newman flow, with $H_0(z)=\int_0^\infty\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cos(zu)\,du=\frac18\xi(\frac12+\frac{iz}2)$. A law is ferromagnetic if it is symmetric, has $\mathbb{E}e^{b_0X^2}<\infty$ for some $b_0>0$, and its moment generating function vanishes only on the imaginary axis. Let $\mu>0$ and $H^{(\mu)}(z)=\int_0^\infty e^{-\mu u}\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cos(zu)\,du$. With $C$ a standard Cauchy variable, $H^{(\mu)}(z)=\mathbb{E}\,H_0(z+\mu C)$ and $z^2H^{(\mu)}(z)\to\mu\,\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(0)=0.4467\,\mu$ as $z\to\infty$ along the reals. Hence $H^{(\mu)}$ is positive beyond some height, has finitely many real zeros and infinitely many nonreal ones, the law with density proportional to $e^{-\mu|t|/2}p(t)$ is not ferromagnetic, and the tilted clock $R^{(\mu)}(s)=H^{(\mu)}(0)/H^{(\mu)}(2i\sqrt s)$ is not the Laplace transform of a GGC (a generalized gamma convolution, a law on $[0,\infty)$ with Laplace transform $\exp(-bs-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+s/z)\,U(dz))$ with drift $b\ge0$ and Thorin measure $U\ge0$), for any $\mu>0$.
results.label: xg:thm:cauchy

results.name: Laplace weighted de Bruijn Newman function H^[a] and a sufficient condition for RH
results.summary: The weight 1 over 1 plus a squared u squared gives a function H^[a] that is an average of the de Bruijn Newman function at Laplace shifted points and an exponential mixture of backward heat flows, and if it has only real zeros for one a then RH holds; whether it has real zeros is open.
results.statement: Let $\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}$ be the de Bruijn Newman kernel, $H_t(z)=\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cos(zu)du$ and, for $a>0$, $H^{[a]}(z)=\int_0^\infty\frac{\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)}{1+a^2u^2}\cos(zu)du$. Let $L$ be a standard Laplace variable with density $\frac12e^{-|y|}$. Then $H^{[a]}(z)=\mathbb{E}H_0(z+aL)$, $H^{[a]}=\int_0^\infty e^{-v}H_{-va^2}dv$, an exponential mixture of backward heat flows, and $H_0=(1-a^2\frac{d^2}{dz^2})H^{[a]}$. Consequently, if $H^{[a]}$ has only real zeros for one $a>0$, then the Riemann hypothesis holds: $H^{[a]}$ is even, real on $\mathbb{R}$ and entire of order one, so it is in the Laguerre Pólya class, and so is $H_0=(1-a\frac d{dz})(1+a\frac d{dz})H^{[a]}$ by Laguerre's theorem. The weight has poles at $u=\pm i/a$, so it is not an entire multiplier; RH is not known to imply that $H^{[a]}$ has real zeros, and whether it has them for some $a>0$ is open. Credited to a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book.
results.label: xg:prop:laplace

results.name: If the folded kernels have only real zeros in the disc of radius 2c(N+1)^2 for every N then RH holds
results.summary: If there is $c>0$ such that for every $N\ge1$ all zeros of $H^F_N$ in the disc $|z|<2c(N+1)^2$ are real, then RH holds. The height rule itself is not proved: it is checked in the range described in the chapter (Rouch\'e certificate for $N=1,\dots,4$, computed for $N=5$).
results.statement: Let $\Phi^F_N=\sum_{n\le N}\phi_n$ be the folded kernel and $H^F_N$ its cosine transform, $R_N=\Phi-\Phi^F_N=\sum_{n>N}\phi_n$ on $u\ge0$ and $E_N=H-H^F_N$, so that $E_N(z)=\int_0^\infty R_N(u)\cos(zu)\,du$, where $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}\phi_n(u)$ with $\phi_n(u)=(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})e^{-\pi n^2e^{4u}}$, and $H(z)=\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(zu)\,du=\frac18\Xi(z/2)$ with $\Xi$ the Riemann Xi function. Suppose there is $c>0$ such that for every $N\ge1$ all zeros of $H^F_N$ in the disc $|z|<2c(N+1)^2$ are real. Then RH holds. (The hypothesis, the height rule, is a heuristic balance of the kink against the size of $H$ and is verified in the book only for $N=1,\dots,4$ with $c=3.6$, by a Rouch\'e certificate, and for $N=5$ in floating point.)
results.label: ev:prop:reduction

results.name: Kink bound: the error of the folded kernel decays like 1/x^2 with an explicit constant
results.summary: For real $x\ne0$, $|E_N(x)|\le B_N/x^2$ with $B_N=|R_N'(0)|+\|R_N''\|_{L^1(0,\infty)}$, from $E_N(x)=-R_N'(0)/x^2-x^{-2}\int_0^\infty R_N''(u)\cos(xu)\,du$.
results.statement: Let $\Phi^F_N=\sum_{n\le N}\phi_n$ be the folded kernel and $H^F_N$ its cosine transform, $R_N=\Phi-\Phi^F_N=\sum_{n>N}\phi_n$ on $u\ge0$ and $E_N=H-H^F_N$, so that $E_N(z)=\int_0^\infty R_N(u)\cos(zu)\,du$, where $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}\phi_n(u)$ with $\phi_n(u)=(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})e^{-\pi n^2e^{4u}}$, and $H(z)=\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(zu)\,du=\frac18\Xi(z/2)$ with $\Xi$ the Riemann Xi function. For real $x\ne0$, $E_N(x)=-R_N'(0)/x^2-x^{-2}\int_0^\infty R_N''(u)\cos(xu)\,du$ and $|E_N(x)|\le B_N/x^2$ with $B_N=|R_N'(0)|+\|R_N''\|_{L^1(0,\infty)}$.
results.label: ev:lem:kink

results.name: Rouche certificate: a circle inequality and a sign change count show that all zeros of the folded kernel below a height are real
results.summary: Let $T$ lie strictly between two consecutive ordinates and suppose $\Xi$ has exactly $2\mathcal N(T)$ zeros in $|w|<T$, all real and simple. If $|E_N|<|H|$ on $z=2Te^{i\vartheta}$, $\vartheta\in[0,\pi/2]$, and $H^F_N(2x)$ has $\mathcal N(T)$ sign changes on $(0,T)$, then every zero of $H^F_N(2x)$ with $|x|<T$ is real. The inequality was certified in ball arithmetic only for $N=1,\dots,4$ at the tabulated heights, and checked in floating point for $N=5$.
results.statement: Let $\Phi^F_N=\sum_{n\le N}\phi_n$ be the folded kernel and $H^F_N$ its cosine transform, $R_N=\Phi-\Phi^F_N=\sum_{n>N}\phi_n$ on $u\ge0$ and $E_N=H-H^F_N$, so that $E_N(z)=\int_0^\infty R_N(u)\cos(zu)\,du$, where $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}\phi_n(u)$ with $\phi_n(u)=(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})e^{-\pi n^2e^{4u}}$, and $H(z)=\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(zu)\,du=\frac18\Xi(z/2)$ with $\Xi$ the Riemann Xi function. Let $\mathcal N(T)$ be the number of ordinates $\gamma\in(0,T)$ of nontrivial zeros $\frac12+i\gamma$ of $\zeta$ and let $T$ lie strictly between two consecutive ordinates, and suppose $\Xi$ has exactly $2\mathcal N(T)$ zeros in $|w|<T$, all real and simple. If $|E_N(2Te^{i\vartheta})|<|H(2Te^{i\vartheta})|$ for $\vartheta\in[0,\pi/2]$, and $H^F_N(2x)$ has $\mathcal N(T)$ sign changes on $(0,T)$, then every zero of $H^F_N(2x)$ with $|x|<T$ is real. (In the book the inequality is certified in ball arithmetic for $N=1,2,3,4$ at $T=14.4,17.5$ ($N=1$), $31.7,35.3$ ($N=2$), $51.4,57.9$ ($N=3$), $86.1,97.3$ ($N=4$), given the count of zeros of $\Xi$ in the disc, and tested in floating point only for $N=5$.)
results.label: ev:prop:rouche

results.summary:
For integer $\mu\ge0$ and $a>0$, $\operatorname{Re}K_{\mu+i

results.name: The boundary problem with a boundary law with a point mass and poles is self adjoint with real eigenvalues, positive under a sign condition
results.summary: If $\beta_\mu(\lambda)=\alpha-m\lambda-\sum_{j=1}^J\sigma_j/(q_j-\lambda)$ with $m\ge0$, $\sigma_j>0$, $q_j$ real, the eigenvalue problem is that of a self adjoint operator (Liouville operator with a point mass $m$ at $0$ and $J$ coupled coordinates), with real eigenvalues, positive if the energy form is nonnegative, for example if every $q_j>0$ and $\alpha\ge\sum_j\sigma_j/q_j$. No string or hitting time is constructed for the extended system.
results.statement: Consider the Liouville problem $-g''+a^2e^{2\tau}g=\lambda g$ on $(0,\infty)$ with boundary condition $g'(0)=\beta_\mu(\lambda)g(0)$. Suppose $\beta_\mu(\lambda)=\alpha-m\lambda-\sum_{j=1}^J\sigma_j/(q_j-\lambda)$ with $m\ge0$, $\sigma_j>0$ and $q_j$ real. Then the eigenvalue problem, away from the poles, is the eigenvalue problem of a self adjoint operator built from the Liouville operator on $(0,\infty)$ with a point mass $m$ at $0$ and $J$ extra coordinates $w_j$ coupled to $g(0)$, with stiffness $q_j$, unit mass and coupling $-\sqrt{\sigma_j}$. Its eigenvalues are real. If in addition the energy form is nonnegative, for example if every $q_j>0$ and $\alpha\ge\sum_j\sigma_j/q_j$, they are positive, so that the corresponding $\nu$ are real. This does not make the extended system a string: no hitting time is constructed for it.
results.label: ev:prop:ext

results.name: The mean of the candidate hitting time of the de Bruijn and Newman family increases in the flow time
results.summary: For $H_t(z)=\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi(u)\cos(zu)\,du$ the mean $\mu_1(t)=\sum_k\gamma_k(t)^{-2}=2\mathbb E_t[U^2]$ satisfies $d\mu_1/dt=2\operatorname{Var}_t(U^2)>0$, with $U$ of density proportional to $e^{tu^2}\Phi(u)$ on $(0,\infty)$.
results.statement: Let $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})e^{-\pi n^2e^{4u}}$, so that $\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(zu)\,du=\frac18\Xi(z/2)$, $H_t(z)=\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi(u)\cos(zu)\,du$ and let $U$ have density proportional to $e^{tu^2}\Phi(u)$ on $(0,\infty)$. Let $T_t$ be the candidate hitting time, with Laplace transform $H_t(0)/H_t(2i\sqrt s)$. The mean of the candidate hitting time is $\mu_1(t)=\mathbb ET_t=2\mathbb E_t[U^2]$, and $d\mu_1/dt=2\operatorname{Var}_t(U^2)>0$. Equivalently $\mu_1(t)=\sum_k\gamma_k(t)^{-2}$, with $\pm2\gamma_k(t)$ the zeros of $H_t$ counted with multiplicity.
results.label: ev:prop:dbn

results.name: Cotangent law: the boundary values of the shifted Bessel kernels grow like cot(pi mu/2) times sqrt(lambda_k)
results.status_text:
conditional on the asymptotic $K_{\mu+i
u}(a)= rac12\Gamma(\mu+i
u)(a/2)^{-\mu-i
u}(1+O((a/2
u)^{2\mu}))$ for large $
u$, used in a sketch with heuristic error terms (only the leading term, from the phase computation, is derived)
