the asymptotic $K_{\mu+i
u}(a)= rac12\Gamma(\mu+i
u)(a/2)^{-\mu-i
u}(1+O((a/2
u)^{2\mu}))$ for large $
u$, used in a sketch with heuristic error terms (only the leading term, from the phase computation, is derived)
results.summary: For fixed $a>0$ and non integer $\mu>0$, $\beta_k=\cot(\pi\mu/2)\sqrt{\lambda_k}(1+O((a/2\nu_k)^{2\mu}))+O(1)$ as $k\to\infty$. The phase computation giving the leading term was rederived; the error terms are a sketch and heuristic.
results.statement:
Let $a>0$, $\mu>0$ not an integer, $K$ the modified Bessel function of the second kind, $
u_k$ the positive zeros of $
u\mapsto\operatorname{Re}K_{\mu+i
u}(a)$, $\lambda_k=
u_k^2$ and $ eta_k=g'(0)/g(0)$ for $g(	au)=K_{i
u_k}(ae^	au)$, that is $ eta_k=aK_{i
u_k}'(a)/K_{i
u_k}(a)$. As $k	o\infty$, $ eta_k=\cot(\pi\mu/2)\sqrt{\lambda_k}\,(1+O((a/2
u_k)^{2\mu}))+O(1)$. The statement is proved by a sketch only for the leading term (the phase computation $\arg\Gamma(\mu+i
u)-
u\log(a/2)= rac\pi2+k\pi$ with Stirling's formula); the error terms are heuristic. It matches every integer case of the shift theorem.
results.label: ev:prop:cot

results.name: The coefficients of the tail expansion alternate in sign when the atoms are real and simple
results.summary: If the atoms $\gamma_1^2<\gamma_2^2<\cdots$ are real and simple, then $\operatorname{sign}c_k=(-1)^{k-1}$ for $c_k=\prod_{j\ne k}(1-\gamma_k^2/\gamma_j^2)^{-1}$.
results.statement: Let $\gamma_1^2<\gamma_2^2<\cdots$ be real and simple atoms and $c_k=\prod_{j\ne k}(1-\gamma_k^2/\gamma_j^2)^{-1}$. Then $\operatorname{sign}c_k=(-1)^{k-1}$.
results.label: ev:prop:sign

results.name: RH holds if and only if the reciprocal xi law is a Polya frequency density
results.summary: RH holds if and only if $L(s)=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)$ is the Laplace transform of a P\'olya frequency density; under RH that density is log concave, the hazard rate of $X$ is increasing and the mean excess function decreases from $e(0)=\sum_k\gamma_k^{-2}=0.0231050$ to $\gamma_1^{-2}=0.00500524$.
results.statement: Let $\Xi$ be the Riemann Xi function, $\xi$ the Riemann xi function, $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}\phi_n(u)$ with $\phi_n(u)=(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})e^{-\pi n^2e^{4u}}$ the theta series kernel, and $H(z)=\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(zu)\,du=\frac18\Xi(z/2)$. Write $\pm\gamma_k$ for the zeros of $\Xi$, so that $\frac12+i\gamma_k$ are the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$, ordered by real part (under the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) they are all real and $0<\gamma_1\le\gamma_2\le\cdots$), $L(s)=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)=H(0)/H(2i\sqrt s)$, which under RH equals $\prod_k(1+s/\gamma_k^2)^{-1}$, and $T$ for the random variable with Laplace transform $L$. Let $X$ have the law with Laplace transform $L$ (so $X=T$). Then RH holds if and only if $L(s)=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)$ is the Laplace transform of a P\'olya frequency density. Under RH that density is log concave, the hazard rate of $X$ is increasing, and the mean excess function decreases monotonically, $e(0)=\sum_k\gamma_k^{-2}=0.0231050$ (computed) down to $e(\infty)=\gamma_1^{-2}=0.00500524$.
results.label: ev:cor:pf

results.name: Mean excess function: two term expansion with an exponential rate under RH, simple zeros and a lower bound for xi prime
results.status_text: conditional on RH (all zeros of $\Xi$ are real), all zeros simple, and $|\xi'(\rho)|\ge e^{-C|\gamma|}$ for some constant $C$ and all zeros $\rho=\frac12+i\gamma$
results.conditions: RH (all zeros of $\Xi$ are real), all zeros simple, and $|\xi'(\rho)|\ge e^{-C|\gamma|}$ for some constant $C$ and all zeros $\rho=\frac12+i\gamma$
results.summary: Under RH with simple zeros and $|\xi'(\rho)|\ge e^{-C|\gamma|}$, with $\lambda_k=\gamma_k^2$, $e(u)=1/\lambda_1+Ae^{-(\lambda_2-\lambda_1)u}+O(e^{-\min(\lambda_3-\lambda_1,2(\lambda_2-\lambda_1))u})$ with $A=(c_2/c_1)(1/\lambda_2-1/\lambda_1)>0$, and the excess law converges to the exponential law of rate $\lambda_1$ in total variation at rate $e^{-(\lambda_2-\lambda_1)u}$.
results.statement: Let $\Xi$ be the Riemann Xi function, $\xi$ the Riemann xi function, $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}\phi_n(u)$ with $\phi_n(u)=(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})e^{-\pi n^2e^{4u}}$ the theta series kernel, and $H(z)=\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(zu)\,du=\frac18\Xi(z/2)$. Write $\pm\gamma_k$ for the zeros of $\Xi$, so that $\frac12+i\gamma_k$ are the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$, ordered by real part (under the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) they are all real and $0<\gamma_1\le\gamma_2\le\cdots$), $L(s)=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)=H(0)/H(2i\sqrt s)$, which under RH equals $\prod_k(1+s/\gamma_k^2)^{-1}$, and $T$ for the random variable with Laplace transform $L$. Assume RH, that the zeros are simple and that $|\xi'(\rho)|\ge e^{-C|\gamma|}$ for some constant $C$ and all zeros $\rho$ (a hypothesis not known to hold), put $\lambda_k=\gamma_k^2$ and let $e(u)$ be the mean excess function of $X$ with $\mathbb P(X>x)=\sum_kc_ke^{-\lambda_kx}$. Then $e(u)=\sum_kc_ke^{-\lambda_ku}/\lambda_k\big/\sum_kc_ke^{-\lambda_ku}=\frac1{\lambda_1}+Ae^{-(\lambda_2-\lambda_1)u}+O(e^{-\min(\lambda_3-\lambda_1,\,2(\lambda_2-\lambda_1))u})$ with $A=\frac{c_2}{c_1}(\frac1{\lambda_2}-\frac1{\lambda_1})>0$. The excess law of $X$ over $u$ converges to the exponential law with rate $\lambda_1$ in total variation at rate $e^{-(\lambda_2-\lambda_1)u}$. Without simple zeros the two term form follows from the two term tail with $w_k/\lambda_k$ in place of $c_k$ for $k=1,2$.
results.label: ev:prop:meexp

results.name: A proof by Spitzer's identity and Euler Maclaurin summation that the expected maximum of a symmetric stable walk has the constant of Comtet and Majumdar, zeta of s over a sine factor
results.summary: For a random walk with symmetric stable steps of index $\mu\in(1,2]$ and $s=1/\mu$, $\mathbb EM_n=\frac{\Gamma(1-s)}{\pi s}n^s+\frac{\Gamma(1-s)\zeta(1-s)}{\pi}+O(n^{s-1})$, so the constant is $\zeta(s)/((2\pi)^s\sin(\pi s/2))$, by Spitzer's identity and Euler Maclaurin summation.
results.statement: Let $S_n$ be a random walk whose steps $X$ are symmetric stable with $\mathbb Ee^{ikX}=e^{-|k|^\mu}$, $1<\mu\le2$, let $M_n=\max_{0\le j\le n}S_j$ and $s=1/\mu$. Then $\mathbb EM_n=\frac{\Gamma(1-s)}{\pi s}n^s+\frac{\Gamma(1-s)\zeta(1-s)}{\pi}+O(n^{s-1})$, where $\zeta$ is the Riemann zeta function. Hence the constant term, found by Comtet and Majumdar, is $C_\mu=I(s)=\zeta(s)/\{(2\pi)^s\sin(\pi s/2)\}$, with $I(s)=\frac1\pi\int_0^\infty x^{-s}(\frac1{e^x-1}-\frac1x)\,dx$.
results.label: cg:prop:spitzer

results.name: The logarithm of the Laplace transform of the uniform law is a regularised integral against Lebesgue minus counting measure
results.summary: For $x>0$, $\ln\frac{1-e^{-x}}{x}=-\lim_{R\to\infty}\{\int_0^R(1-e^{-xt})\frac{dt}t-\sum_{1\le n\le R}\frac{1-e^{-xn}}n\}$, and for $0<\operatorname{Re}z<1$, $\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_0^Rt^{-z}(d\lfloor t\rfloor-dt)=\zeta(z)$.
results.statement: For $x>0$, $\ln\frac{1-e^{-x}}{x}=-\lim_{R\to\infty}\{\int_0^R(1-e^{-xt})\frac{dt}{t}-\sum_{1\le n\le R}\frac{1-e^{-xn}}{n}\}$, a regularised integral against the signed measure $dt-d\lfloor t\rfloor$ with a common upper cutoff $R$, where $\lfloor t\rfloor$ is the integer part. For $0<\operatorname{Re}z<1$, $\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_0^Rt^{-z}(d\lfloor t\rfloor-dt)=-z\int_0^\infty\{t\}t^{-z-1}\,dt=\zeta(z)$, with $\{t\}$ the fractional part and $\zeta$ the Riemann zeta function. The two parts of the signed measure are mutually singular and $\int_1^\infty|dt-d\lfloor t\rfloor|/t=\infty$, so the representation is regularised and not a signed L\'evy measure.
results.label: cg:prop:signed

results.name: If locally uniform limits of GGC reciprocals approximate Xi then RH holds
results.summary: If even real entire functions $\Xi_\delta$ of order below two with $\Xi_\delta(0)>0$, each with $\Xi_\delta(0)/\Xi_\delta(i\sqrt w)$ a GGC transform, converge to $\Xi$ locally uniformly, then RH holds; under RH the constant family qualifies.
results.statement: Let $\Xi$ be the Riemann Xi function and let $\Xi_\delta$ be even, real on $\mathbb R$, entire of order less than two with $\Xi_\delta(0)>0$, such that $\Xi_\delta\to\Xi$ locally uniformly as $\delta\to0$ and each $w\mapsto\Xi_\delta(0)/\Xi_\delta(i\sqrt w)$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution (GGC). Then all zeros of $\Xi$ are real, that is the Riemann Hypothesis holds. Conversely, under the Riemann Hypothesis the constant family $\Xi_\delta=\Xi$ qualifies.
results.label: cg:cor:closure

results.name: The shifted zeta is an explicit series of zeta at s plus k with a tangent factor
results.summary: For $0<\delta<2\pi$, $\pi I_\delta(s)=\Gamma(1-s)F_\delta(s)$ with $F_\delta(s)=\operatorname{Li}_{1-s}(e^{-\delta})-\Gamma(s)\delta^{-s}=\sum_{k\ge0}\zeta(1-s-k)(-\delta)^k/k!$, and $\zeta_\delta(s)=\sum_{k\ge0}(\delta/2\pi)^k\frac{(s)_k}{k!}\frac{\sin(\pi s/2)}{\sin(\pi(s+k)/2)}\zeta(s+k)=\zeta(s)+\frac\delta{2\pi}s\tan\frac{\pi s}2\zeta(s+1)-\cdots$.
results.statement: Let $g(x)=\frac1{e^x-1}-\frac1x$, $\delta>0$, $I_\delta(s)=\frac1\pi\int_0^\infty x^{-s}g(x+\delta)\,dx$ for $0<\operatorname{Re}s<1$, $\zeta_\delta(s)=(2\pi)^s\sin(\pi s/2)I_\delta(s)$ (so $\zeta_0=\zeta$), $\operatorname{Li}_\sigma$ the polylogarithm and $(s)_k$ the rising factorial. For $0<\delta<2\pi$, $\pi I_\delta(s)=\Gamma(1-s)F_\delta(s)$ with $F_\delta(s)=\operatorname{Li}_{1-s}(e^{-\delta})-\Gamma(s)\delta^{-s}=\sum_{k\ge0}\zeta(1-s-k)(-\delta)^k/k!$, and $\zeta_\delta(s)=\sum_{k\ge0}(\delta/2\pi)^k\frac{(s)_k}{k!}\frac{\sin(\pi s/2)}{\sin(\pi(s+k)/2)}\zeta(s+k)=\zeta(s)+\frac{\delta}{2\pi}s\tan\frac{\pi s}2\,\zeta(s+1)-\frac{\delta^2}{8\pi^2}s(s+1)\zeta(s+2)-\cdots$. The ratio of sines is $(-1)^j$ for $k=2j$ and $(-1)^j\tan(\pi s/2)$ for $k=2j+1$.
results.label: cg:thm:expansion

results.name: Obstructions: the shifted xi function has a pole at s equal 3, its zeros drift, and its reciprocal is not a GGC transform
results.summary: For $0<\delta<2\pi$, $\xi_\delta$ is meromorphic and not entire, with a pole at $s=3$ for every such $\delta$ and poles at $s=-1,-2,\dots$; a pole at $s=2m+1$ ($m\ge2$) occurs exactly when $F_\delta(2m+1)\ne0$ and fails for some $\delta$ (computed values $4.7215$ at $s=5$, $3.0416$ at $s=7$). The zeros move by a first order drift and, when $\xi_\delta(\frac12)\ne0$, $\xi_\delta(\frac12)/\xi_\delta(\frac12+\sqrt w)$ is not a GGC transform nor the Laplace transform of any positive measure.
results.statement:
Let $0<\delta<2\pi$, $g(x)= rac1{e^x-1}- rac1x$, $F_\delta(s)=\operatorname{Li}_{1-s}(e^{-\delta})-\Gamma(s)\delta^{-s}$ with $\operatorname{Li}$ the polylogarithm, $\zeta_\delta(s)=(2\pi)^s\sin(\pi s/2) rac1\pi\int_0^\infty x^{-s}g(x+\delta)\,dx$ for $0<\operatorname{Re}s<1$, continued meromorphically, and $\xi_\delta(s)= rac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta_\delta(s)= rac12s(s-1)\pi^{(s-1)/2}\Gamma( rac{1-s}2)F_\delta(s)$. (a) $\xi_\delta$ is meromorphic and not entire. It has a pole at $s=3$ for every $\delta\in(0,2\pi)$, because $F_\delta(3)=4\sum_{k\ge1}\operatorname{Re}(\delta-2\pi ik)^{-3}<0$, and poles at $s=-1,-2,-3,\dots$ For $m\ge2$ it has a pole at $s=2m+1$ exactly when $F_\delta(2m+1)
e0$. The values $F_\delta(5)=0$ at $\delta=4.7215$ and $F_\delta(7)=0$ at $\delta=3.0416$ are computed (not proved), so for those $\delta$ there is no pole at $s=5$, respectively $s=7$. (b) Each simple zero $ho= rac12+i\gamma$ of the Riemann zeta function $\zeta$ moves to $ho_\delta=ho- rac\delta{2\pi} rac{ho	an(\piho/2)\zeta(ho+1)}{\zeta'(ho)}+O(\delta^2)$, and $\xi_\delta(s)
e\xi_\delta(1-s)$. (c) If $\xi_\delta( rac12)
e0$, the function $w\mapsto\xi_\delta( rac12)/\xi_\delta( rac12+\sqrt w)$ is not the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution, nor of any positive measure.
results.label: cg:prop:obstructions

results.name: A signed L\'evy measure gives a Thorin density, which is nonnegative if and only if a logarithmic derivative inequality holds
results.summary: If $f'/f(s)-f'/f(\alpha)=\int(e^{-\alpha x}-e^{-sx})M(dx)$ for a signed measure $M$, then $\log\frac{f(\alpha+w)}{f(\alpha)}-w\frac{f'}f(\alpha)=\int_0^\infty\log(1+w^2/y^2)\kappa_\alpha(y)\,dy$ with $\kappa_\alpha(y)=\frac1\pi[\operatorname{Re}\frac{f'}f(\alpha+iy)-\frac{f'}f(\alpha)]$, and if $\kappa_\alpha\ge0$ the compensated reciprocal is a GGC transform.
results.statement: Let $f$ be analytic and without zeros on $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha_0$ and positive on $(\alpha_0,\infty)$, and let $M$ be a signed measure on $(0,\infty)$ with $\int(1\wedge x)e^{-\alpha x}|M|(dx)<\infty$ for every $\alpha>\alpha_0$ such that $\frac{f'}f(s)-\frac{f'}f(\alpha)=\int_0^\infty(e^{-\alpha x}-e^{-sx})M(dx)$ for $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha_0$ and $\alpha>\alpha_0$. Then for every $\alpha>\alpha_0$ and $w\ge0$, $\log\frac{f(\alpha+w)}{f(\alpha)}-w\frac{f'}f(\alpha)=\int_0^\infty\log(1+w^2/y^2)\kappa_\alpha(y)\,dy$ with $\kappa_\alpha(y)=\frac1\pi\int_0^\infty(1-\cos xy)e^{-\alpha x}M(dx)=\frac1\pi[\operatorname{Re}\frac{f'}f(\alpha+iy)-\frac{f'}f(\alpha)]$. If $\kappa_\alpha\ge0$, then $u\mapsto\frac{f(\alpha)}{f(\alpha+\sqrt{2u})}\exp\{\sqrt{2u}\,\frac{f'}f(\alpha)\}$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) with Thorin density $\tau_\alpha(z)=\kappa_\alpha(\sqrt{2z})/\sqrt{2z}$.
results.label: cg:thm:thorinfromlevy

results.name: Zeros on a vertical line give a Thorin density that is a sum of Lorentzians tending to point masses at the ordinates
results.summary: If $f'/f(s)=a+\sum_k(s-\rho_k)^{-1}$ with all $\rho_k=\beta_0+it_k$ on one line, $\{t_k\}$ symmetric, $0\notin\{t_k\}$, then at $\alpha=\beta_0+\varepsilon$, $\kappa_\alpha(y)=\frac1\pi\sum_k[\ell_\varepsilon(y-t_k)-\ell_\varepsilon(t_k)]$, and if $\sum t_k^{-2}<\infty$, $\kappa_\alpha(y)\,dy\to\sum_{t_k>0}\delta_{t_k}$ vaguely as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$.
results.statement: Let $f$ be analytic and without zeros on $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha_0$ and positive on $(\alpha_0,\infty)$, let $M$ be a signed measure on $(0,\infty)$ with $\int(1\wedge x)e^{-\alpha x}|M|(dx)<\infty$ and $\frac{f'}f(s)-\frac{f'}f(\alpha)=\int_0^\infty(e^{-\alpha x}-e^{-sx})M(dx)$ for $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha_0$ and $\alpha>\alpha_0$, let $\kappa_\alpha(y)=\frac1\pi[\operatorname{Re}\frac{f'}f(\alpha+iy)-\frac{f'}f(\alpha)]$, so that $\log\frac{f(\alpha+w)}{f(\alpha)}-w\frac{f'}f(\alpha)=\int_0^\infty\log(1+w^2/y^2)\kappa_\alpha(y)\,dy$ for $w\ge0$, and let $a$ be real, suppose $f'/f(s)=a+\sum_k(s-\rho_k)^{-1}$ (symmetric summation) with all $\rho_k=\beta_0+it_k$ on one vertical line, the set $\{t_k\}$ symmetric and $0\notin\{t_k\}$, and write $\ell_\varepsilon(x)=\varepsilon/(\varepsilon^2+x^2)$ for the Cauchy kernel. Then for $\alpha=\beta_0+\varepsilon$, $\varepsilon>0$, $\kappa_\alpha(y)=\frac1\pi\sum_k[\ell_\varepsilon(y-t_k)-\ell_\varepsilon(t_k)]$. If $\sum_kt_k^{-2}<\infty$ then $\kappa_\alpha(y)\,dy\to\sum_{t_k>0}\delta_{t_k}(dy)$ vaguely on $(0,\infty)$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, and $\int_0^\infty\log(1+w^2/y^2)\kappa_\alpha(y)\,dy$ tends to $\sum_{t_k>0}\log(1+w^2/t_k^2)$.
results.label: cg:cor:lorentz

results.name: The tilted uniform law has a strictly positive Thorin density for every positive tilt, a Lorentzian smoothing of the lattice 2 pi m
results.summary: For every $\delta>0$, $\pi\kappa_\delta(y)=\frac{y^2}{\delta(\delta^2+y^2)}-\frac12\coth\frac\delta2\frac{1-\cos y}{\cosh\delta-\cos y}=\sum_{m\ge1}[\ell_\delta(y-2\pi m)+\ell_\delta(y+2\pi m)-2\ell_\delta(2\pi m)]>0$ for $y>0$, so the compensated tilted reciprocal of $\varphi_U(s)=(1-e^{-s})/s$ is a GGC transform, and as $\delta\downarrow0$ the Thorin measure tends to $\sum_{m\ge1}\delta_{2\pi m}$ vaguely.
results.statement: Let $\varphi_U(s)=(1-e^{-s})/s$ be the Laplace transform of the uniform law on $(0,1)$, $g=\varphi_U'/\varphi_U$ (so $g(x)=\frac1{e^x-1}-\frac1x$), $\ell_\delta(x)=\delta/(\delta^2+x^2)$ and $\kappa_\delta(y)=\frac1\pi\int_0^\infty(1-\cos xy)e^{-\delta x}(dx-d\lfloor x\rfloor)=\frac1\pi[\operatorname{Re}g(\delta+iy)-g(\delta)]$ for $y>0$, with $g(s)=\frac1{e^s-1}-\frac1s$ and $\lfloor x\rfloor$ the integer part. For every $\delta>0$, $\pi\kappa_\delta(y)=\frac{y^2}{\delta(\delta^2+y^2)}-\frac12\coth\frac\delta2\frac{1-\cos y}{\cosh\delta-\cos y}=\sum_{m\ge1}[\ell_\delta(y-2\pi m)+\ell_\delta(y+2\pi m)-2\ell_\delta(2\pi m)]$, and $\kappa_\delta(y)>0$ for all $y>0$. Hence $u\mapsto\frac{\varphi_U(\delta)}{\varphi_U(\delta+\sqrt{2u})}e^{\sqrt{2u}\,g(\delta)}$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) with Thorin density $\tau_\delta(z)=\kappa_\delta(\sqrt{2z})/\sqrt{2z}$. As $\delta\downarrow0$, $\kappa_\delta(y)\,dy\to\sum_{m\ge1}\delta_{2\pi m}$ vaguely, and $\log\frac{\sinh(w/2)}{w/2}=\sum_{m\ge1}\log(1+\frac{w^2}{4\pi^2m^2})$, so $(w/2)/\sinh(w/2)$ is the Laplace transform in $u=w^2/2$ of $\sum_me_m/(2\pi^2m^2)$ with independent standard exponential $e_m$, a GGC with Thorin measure $\sum_m\delta_{2\pi^2m^2}$ (a law of Biane, Pitman and Yor type).
results.label: cg:thm:uniform

results.name: The shifted zeta equals (2 pi) to the s times the Mellin transform of the positive Thorin density of the tilted uniform law
results.summary: For $1<\operatorname{Re}s<3$ and every $\delta>0$, $\zeta_\delta(s)=(2\pi)^s\int_0^\infty y^{-s}\kappa_\delta(y)\,dy$, and at $\delta=0$ the right side is formally $\zeta(s)$; formally the identity of Comtet and Majumdar is the Mellin transform of the lattice Thorin measure $\sum_m\delta_{2\pi m}$ of the uniform law, divergent for $0<s<1$, and the shift smooths it into a positive density.
results.statement: Let $g(s)=\frac1{e^s-1}-\frac1s$, let $\kappa_\delta(y)=\frac1\pi[\operatorname{Re}g(\delta+iy)-g(\delta)]$ for $y>0$, the positive Thorin density of the uniform law on $(0,1)$ tilted by $\delta$, and $\zeta_\delta(s)=(2\pi)^s\sin(\pi s/2)\frac1\pi\int_0^\infty x^{-s}g(x+\delta)\,dx$ (continued analytically in $s$; for $\delta<2\pi$ it equals $\sum_{k\ge0}(\delta/2\pi)^k\frac{(s)_k}{k!}\frac{\sin(\pi s/2)}{\sin(\pi(s+k)/2)}\zeta(s+k)$, with $(s)_k$ the rising factorial). For $1<\operatorname{Re}s<3$ and every $\delta>0$, $\zeta_\delta(s)=(2\pi)^s\int_0^\infty y^{-s}\kappa_\delta(y)\,dy$. At $\delta=0$ the right side is formally $(2\pi)^s\sum_{m\ge1}(2\pi m)^{-s}=\zeta(s)$.
results.label: cg:thm:mellinthorin

results.name: Kink theorem: the Gauss damped Riemann kernel has finitely many real zeros and infinitely many nonreal zeros
results.summary: For every $\delta>0$, $\Xi_\delta(t)=2\int_0^\infty\Phi_\delta(u)\cos(ut)\,du$ with $\Phi_\delta=2\sum_ne^{-\pi n^2\delta}\Phi_n$ has finitely many real zeros and infinitely many nonreal zeros, because $\Phi_\delta'(0)>0$ gives $t^2\Xi_\delta(t)\to-2\Phi_\delta'(0)<0$; so $\Xi_\delta(0)/\Xi_\delta(i\sqrt w)$ is not a GGC transform.
results.statement: Let $\Phi_n(u)=(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2u})$, $\Phi=2\sum_{n\ge1}\Phi_n$, so that $\Xi(t)=2\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(ut)\,du$ for the Riemann Xi function. For $\delta>0$ let $\Phi_\delta=2\sum_{n\ge1}e^{-\pi n^2\delta}\Phi_n$ on $[0,\infty)$ and $\Xi_\delta(t)=2\int_0^\infty\Phi_\delta(u)\cos(ut)\,du$, an even real entire function of order one with $\Xi_\delta(0)>0$. Then $\Xi_\delta$ has only finitely many real zeros and infinitely many nonreal zeros, because $\Phi_\delta'(0)>0$ (using $\sum_n\Phi_n'(0)=0$, from the evenness of $\Phi$, and $\Phi_n'(0)<0$ for $n\ge2$) and $t^2\Xi_\delta(t)\to-2\Phi_\delta'(0)<0$ as $t\to\infty$ along $\mathbb R$. Consequently $\Xi_\delta(0)/\Xi_\delta(i\sqrt w)$ is not the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution.
results.label: cg:thm:kink

results.name: Modular constraints: a Laguerre P\'olya damped kernel must have vanishing odd derivatives of the damped kernel at the origin
results.summary: For real weights $w_n$ with $\sum_n|w_n|n^Ae^{-\pi n^2}<\infty$ for every $A\ge0$, if $\Xi_w\in\mathcal{LP}$ and $\Xi_w$ is not $e^{-at^2}$ times a polynomial, then $\sum_nw_n\Phi_n^{(2j+1)}(0)=0$ for every $j\ge0$.
results.statement: Let $\Phi_n(u)=(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2u})$ for $n\ge1$, the terms of the Riemann kernel $\Phi=2\sum_n\Phi_n$ for which $\Xi(t)=2\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(ut)\,du$ is the Riemann Xi function, let $\Phi_w=2\sum_{n\ge1}w_n\Phi_n$ with real weights $w_n$ such that $\sum_n|w_n|n^Ae^{-\pi n^2}<\infty$ for every $A\ge0$, and $\Xi_w(t)=2\int_0^\infty\Phi_w(u)\cos(ut)\,du$. If $\Xi_w$ lies in the Laguerre P\'olya class $\mathcal{LP}$ (locally uniform limits of real polynomials with only real zeros) and is not of the form $e^{-at^2}$ times a polynomial, then $\sum_nw_n\Phi_n^{(2j+1)}(0)=0$ for every $j\ge0$.
results.label: cg:cor:modular

results.name: Jensen polynomial laws mu_d of the reciprocal xi function: convergence, existence if and only if RH, and existence up to degree 2e17
results.summary: $J_d\to G$ locally uniformly; if $J_d$ has only real zeros then $1/J_d$ is the transform of a GGC law $\mu_d$ (a pure birth chain passage time); RH iff $\mu_d$ exists for all $d$, and then $\mu_d\Rightarrow\mu$; $\mu_d$ exists for $d\le2\cdot10^{17}$ unconditionally (quoted); $\mu_d$ has mean $c_1$ and variance exceeding that of $\mu$ by $2c_2/d$.
results.statement: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. Write $G(u)=\sum_{k\ge0}c_ku^k$, so that $G(u)=\mathbb E\cosh(\sqrt u\,V)$ with $V$ symmetric with density $\Phi/\Xi(0)$ ($\Phi$ Riemann's kernel, $\Xi(z)=\xi(\frac12+iz)$) and $c_k=\mathbb E V^{2k}/(2k)!>0$. For $d\ge1$ let $J_d(u)=\sum_{k=0}^d\binom dk\frac{k!}{d^k}c_ku^k=\sum_{k=0}^dc_k\prod_{j<k}(1-\frac jd)u^k$ (up to scaling the Jensen polynomial of degree $d$ and shift $0$ of Griffin, Ono, Rolen and Zagier). (1) $J_d\to G$ uniformly on compact sets, without any hypothesis. (2) If $J_d$ has only real zeros, they are negative, $J_d(u)=\prod_{j\le d}(1+u/\ell_{d,j})$, and $1/J_d$ is the Laplace transform of the GGC law $\mu_d$ of $\sum_{j\le d}e_j/\ell_{d,j}$, the time a pure birth chain with rates $\ell_{d,1},\dots,\ell_{d,d}$ takes to pass through $d$ states. (3) RH holds if and only if $\mu_d$ exists for every $d$, and then $\mu_d\Rightarrow\mu$. (4) $\mu_d$ exists for every $d\le2\cdot10^{17}$, unconditionally (quoted from Griffin, Ono, Rolen and Zagier, who quote Chass\'e). (5) Every $\mu_d$ has the same mean $c_1$ as $\mu$, and its variance exceeds that of $\mu$ by $2c_2/d$.
results.label: ht:prop:jensen

results.name: Density of a sum of independent exponentials as a Laplace transform of a B spline, the Dirichlet mean form
results.summary: For $0<\lambda_1<\dots<\lambda_N$ the density of $\sum e_k/\lambda_k$ is $(\prod\lambda_k)\frac{y^{N-1}}{(N-1)!}\int M(x;\lambda)e^{-xy}\,dx$ with $M$ the Curry and Schoenberg B spline, the density of the Dirichlet mean $\sum W_k\lambda_k$.
results.statement: Let $0<\lambda_1<\dots<\lambda_N$, let $e_k$ be independent standard exponential variables and $f_N$ the density of $\sum_{k\le N}e_k/\lambda_k$. Then $f_N(y)=(\prod_{k\le N}\lambda_k)\frac{y^{N-1}}{(N-1)!}\int M(x;\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_N)e^{-xy}\,\mathrm dx$, where $M(\cdot;\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_N)$ is the Curry and Schoenberg B spline with knots $\lambda_k$, normalised to integral one. Equivalently $M$ is the density of the Dirichlet mean $D_N=\sum_kW_k\lambda_k$ with $(W_k)$ uniform on the simplex, and the formula is the case of Dirichlet parameter $N$ of the density formula of James, Roynette and Yor.
results.label: ht:prop:bspline

results.name: A sum of exponentials is a linear functional of the Gumbel extremal process
results.summary: For $0<\lambda_1\le\lambda_2\le\cdots$ with $\sum1/\lambda_k<\infty$ and $b_k=k/\lambda_k$, $\sum e_k/\lambda_k\overset d=\sum_kb_k(G_k-G_{k+1})$, rearranged to $b_1G_1+\sum_{k\ge2}(b_k-b_{k-1})G_k$ if $k\log k/\lambda_k\to0$; under RH $\mu$ is $\sum k\gamma_k^{-2}(G_k-G_{k+1})$.
results.statement: Let $e_k$ be independent standard exponential variables and $G_1>G_2>\cdots$ the points of the Gumbel extremal process of the book. For any $0<\lambda_1\le\lambda_2\le\cdots$ with $\sum1/\lambda_k<\infty$, and $b_k=k/\lambda_k$, $\sum_ke_k/\lambda_k\overset d=\sum_{k\ge1}b_k(G_k-G_{k+1})$, and if moreover $k\log k/\lambda_k\to0$ the series may be rearranged: $\sum_{k\ge1}b_k(G_k-G_{k+1})=b_1G_1+\sum_{k\ge2}(b_k-b_{k-1})G_k$. In particular, under RH, the reciprocal xi law $\mu$ is the law of $\sum_kk\gamma_k^{-2}(G_k-G_{k+1})$. For finite $N$ the truncation $\mu_N$ is the L statistic $\sum_{k\le N}b_k(e_{(N-k+1)}-e_{(N-k)})$ of $N$ exponentials, with $e_{(0)}=0$.
results.label: ht:thm:extremal

results.name: Truncated Euler products give GGC laws Y_P, and first passage to the mean level decomposes as Y_P plus the first passage to the log of N_P
results.summary: For every $\alpha>0$ and $P$, $e^{-B\sqrt{2u}}\zeta_P(\alpha)/\zeta_P(\alpha+\sqrt{2u})$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC law $Y_P$ with zero drift and an explicit nonnegative Thorin density, in particular unconditionally at $\alpha=\frac12$; and $T_{\mathbb E\log N_P}\overset d=Y_P+T_{\log N_P}$.
results.statement: For $P\ge2$ let $\zeta_P(z)=\prod_{p\le P}(1-p^{-z})^{-1}$, fix $\alpha>0$, and let $N_P$ be the random integer with $\Pr(N_P=n)=n^{-\alpha}/\zeta_P(\alpha)$ for $n$ composed of primes up to $P$. Let $L=\log N_P$, $B_{\alpha,P}=\mathbb EL=\sum_{p\le P}\log p\,p^{-\alpha}/(1-p^{-\alpha})$, and $T_a$ the first passage time of standard Brownian motion to the level $a$. For every $\alpha>0$ and every $P$ the function $\Phi_{\alpha,P}(u)=e^{-B_{\alpha,P}\sqrt{2u}}/\mathbb Ee^{-\sqrt{2u}L}=\frac{\zeta_P(\alpha)}{\zeta_P(\alpha+\sqrt{2u})}e^{-B_{\alpha,P}\sqrt{2u}}$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC law $Y_P$ with zero drift, whose Thorin measure has density in the ordinate $\tau$ (atom positions $\tau^2/2$) equal to $\frac1\pi\sum_{p\le P}\sum_{k\ge1}\log p\,p^{-k\alpha}(1-\cos(k\tau\log p))\ge0$. In particular this holds on the critical line $\alpha=\frac12$, unconditionally. If $Y_P$ is independent of $N_P$ and of the Brownian motion, then $T_{\mathbb E\log N_P}\overset d=Y_P+T_{\log N_P}$.
results.label: ht:thm:trunc

results.name: One prime blocks, Möbius and Liouville factors and the Pólya Gamma law
results.summary: For a single prime the Thorin density of the Euler factor sums in closed form, the Liouville factor gives a GGC with density nonnegative although its terms are not, and its limit as alpha decreases to zero is the Laplace transform of a Pólya Gamma law, while for alpha above one the full products give GGC laws and for alpha below one the continued functions are not Laplace transforms.
results.statement: Fix a prime $p$, write $\ell=\log p$, $q=p^{-\alpha}$ with $\alpha>0$, $w=\sqrt{2u}$ and $\vartheta=\tau\ell$. For the Möbius (Euler factor) case the Thorin density of the one prime GGC is $\frac1\pi\sum_{k\ge1}\ell q^k(1-\cos k\vartheta)=\frac1\pi\frac{\ell q(1+q)(1-\cos\vartheta)}{(1-q)(1-2q\cos\vartheta+q^2)}$, which vanishes at $\tau=2\pi k/\ell$. For the Liouville factor, $\Phi^{+}_{p,\alpha}(u)=\frac{1+q}{1+qp^{-w}}\exp\big(-\frac{w\ell q}{1+q}\big)$ is, for every $\alpha>0$, the Laplace transform of a GGC with zero drift and Thorin density in the ordinate $\tau$ equal to $\frac1\pi\frac{\ell q(1-q)(1-\cos\vartheta)}{(1+q)(1+2q\cos\vartheta+q^2)}\ge0$, with bumps at $\tau=\pi(2k-1)/\ell$; the proof applies the sine squared lemma to the signed measure $\sum_k(-1)^{k+1}\ell q^k\delta_{k\ell}$, whose total variation is that of the Möbius case. As $\alpha\downarrow0$, $\Phi^{+}_{p,\alpha}(u)\to1/\cosh(\ell\sqrt{u/2})$, the Laplace transform of $\ell^2\omega$ with $\omega$ a Pólya Gamma variable $\mathrm{PG}(1,0)$, and the Thorin densities converge vaguely to $\sum_{k\ge1}\delta_{\pi(2k-1)/\ell}$. For $\alpha>1$ the products over all primes converge and give the GGC Laplace transforms $\frac{\zeta(\alpha)}{\zeta(\alpha+w)}e^{w\frac{\zeta'}{\zeta}(\alpha)}$ and $\frac{\zeta(2\alpha+2w)\zeta(\alpha)}{\zeta(\alpha+w)\zeta(2\alpha)}e^{wG_\lambda(\alpha)}$, with $G_\lambda(s)=\frac{\zeta'}{\zeta}(s)-2\frac{\zeta'}{\zeta}(2s)$, whose Thorin densities are $\pi^{-1}[\operatorname{Re}\frac{\zeta'}{\zeta}(\alpha+i\tau)-\frac{\zeta'}{\zeta}(\alpha)]$ and $\pi^{-1}[\operatorname{Re}G_\lambda(\alpha+i\tau)-G_\lambda(\alpha)]$. For $0<\alpha<1$ neither continued function is the Laplace transform of a probability law, whatever the zeros of $\zeta$ do: the first vanishes at $u=(1-\alpha)^2/2$, and the second, defined for $\alpha\ne\frac12$, vanishes there when $\frac12<\alpha<1$ and has a pole at $u=(\frac12-\alpha)^2/2$ when $0<\alpha<\frac12$. Credited to a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book.
results.label: ht:rem:blocks

results.name: Brownian truncated Euler product identity for xi centred at one half
results.summary: With no hypothesis on the zeros, the ratio of xi at one half and at one half plus s is for every truncation time U an exact product of a smoothed Euler product over the primes, an archimedean factor and a smoothed product over the zeros whose remainder has an explicit bound, with first passage densities as smoothing kernels.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function, $\gamma$ the zeros of $\xi(\frac12+iz)$ counted with multiplicity (so that $\frac12+i\gamma$ runs over the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$), $\gamma_1=14.1347\ldots$ the least ordinate of a zero, with $\operatorname{Re}\gamma^2\ge\gamma_1^2$ for every zero because zeros off the critical line have ordinate above $3\times10^{12}$, $T_x$ the first passage time of standard Brownian motion to the level $x>0$, $U>0$, and $s\in\mathbb{C}$ with $\operatorname{Re}(s^2)>-\gamma_1^2$. Put $B_U(x,s)=\mathbb{E}[1-e^{-s^2T_x/2};T_x\le U]=\operatorname{erfc}\frac{x}{\sqrt{2U}}-\frac12\big[e^{-xs}\operatorname{erfc}\frac{x-sU}{\sqrt{2U}}+e^{xs}\operatorname{erfc}\frac{x+sU}{\sqrt{2U}}\big]$, $k_\infty(u)=e^{u/8}-\frac{\log\pi}{2\sqrt{2\pi u}}+\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^\infty e^{-ur^2/2}\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Gamma'}{\Gamma}(\frac14+\frac{ir}2)dr$, $A_U(s)=\int_0^U(1-e^{-s^2u/2})k_\infty(u)\frac{du}u$, $R_U(s)=\sum_{\operatorname{Re}\gamma>0}[E_1(\frac{\gamma^2U}2)-E_1(\frac{(\gamma^2+s^2)U}2)]$ with $E_1(z)=\int_1^\infty e^{-zv}\frac{dv}v$, and $E_{p,U}(s)=\exp\big(\sum_{m\ge1}\frac{p^{-m/2}}mB_U(m\log p,s)\big)$. Then, with no hypothesis on the zeros, $\frac{\xi(1/2)}{\xi(1/2+s)}=e^{-A_U(s)}\prod_pE_{p,U}(s)e^{-R_U(s)}$, the product converging absolutely, and $|R_U(s)|\le\frac2Ue^{-m_sU/2}\sum_{\operatorname{Re}\gamma>0}\big(\frac1{\operatorname{Re}\gamma^2}+\frac1{\operatorname{Re}(\gamma^2+s^2)}\big)$ with $m_s=\gamma_1^2+\min(0,\operatorname{Re}(s^2))>0$. If moreover $\operatorname{Re}s>0$ and $\operatorname{Re}(s^2)\ge0$, then $E_{p,U}(s)\to(1-p^{-1/2-s})/(1-p^{-1/2})$ as $U\to\infty$. The proof uses the ordinate bound $3\times10^{12}$ for zeros off the critical line (Platt and Trudgian 2021). Credited to a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book.
results.label: ht:thm:euler

results.name: Numerical check of the Brownian truncated Euler product identity
results.summary: A floating point computation with primes up to $10^3$ or $10^6$ and the first 1700 zeros agrees with the Brownian truncated Euler product identity to better than $10^{-30}$ at six values of s and U, and the zero remainder stays below its bound; it checks the identity at these points only.
results.statement: For the Brownian truncated Euler product identity for $\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+s)$ with truncation time $U$, the two sides $\log\frac{\xi(1/2+s)}{\xi(1/2)}$ and $A_U-\sum_p\log E_{p,U}$ were computed at $(s,U)=(0.1,0.05)$, $(0.1,1)$, $(0.49,0.05)$, $(0.49,1)$, $(2,1)$ and $(0.3+3i,0.25)$, with primes up to $10^3$ for $U\le0.25$ and $10^6$ for $U=1$ and the first $1700$ zeros for the zero remainder $R_U$ (the rest being bounded by the identity's own bound). The residual of the identity is below $10^{-30}$ in every row; at $U=0.05$ the zero remainder is visible (for example $3.39\times10^{-7}$ at $s=0.1$ against a bound of $1.25\times10^{-2}$) and at $U=1$ it is below the working precision of $30$ digits. This is a computation at these six points and says nothing about other $(s,U)$.
results.label: ht:tab:euler

results.name: The Euler hitting times converge after scaling to a spectrally positive stable law of index 3/2
results.summary: As $P\to\infty$, $Z_P=(Y_P-\kappa_2(P))/\kappa_3(P)^{2/3}\Rightarrow Z$ with $\log\mathbb Ee^{-sZ}=(2s)^{3/2}/6$, with the bound $|\log\mathbb Ee^{-sZ_P}-(2s)^{3/2}/6|\le\frac{|s|^2}6\rho_4(P)$ for $\operatorname{Re}s\ge0$ and $\rho_4(P)\to0$.
results.statement: Take $\alpha=\frac12$ in the truncated Euler product laws: $Y_P$ is the GGC law with transform $\zeta_P(\frac12)e^{-B\sqrt{2u}}/\zeta_P(\frac12+\sqrt{2u})$, $L_P=\log N_P$, $\kappa_j(P)$ the $j$th cumulant of $L_P$ (so $K_P(w)=\log\mathbb Ee^{-w(L_P-\mathbb EL_P)}=\sum_{p\le P}\sum_{m\ge1}\frac{p^{-m/2}}m(e^{-wm\log p}-1+wm\log p)$), and $\rho_j(P)=\kappa_j(P)/\kappa_3(P)^{j/3}$; $Y_P$ has mean $\kappa_2(P)=\operatorname{Var}L_P$. As $P\to\infty$, $Z_P=(Y_P-\kappa_2(P))/\kappa_3(P)^{2/3}\Rightarrow Z$, $\log\mathbb Ee^{-sZ}=(2s)^{3/2}/6$ for $\operatorname{Re}s\ge0$, a spectrally positive stable law of index $\frac32$. More precisely, for $\operatorname{Re}s\ge0$, $|\log\mathbb Ee^{-sZ_P}-(2s)^{3/2}/6|\le\frac{|s|^2}6\rho_4(P)$, and $\rho_4(P)\to0$.
results.label: ht:thm:32

results.name: Thorin rigidity: any factorisation of the reciprocal xi law into two GGC laws forces RH and splits the zeros
results.summary: If $\mu=\mu_1*\mu_2$ with both factors GGC, then RH holds and the Thorin measures are $\sum a_\gamma\delta_{\gamma^2}$ and $\sum(m_\gamma-a_\gamma)\delta_{\gamma^2}$ with $0\le a_\gamma\le m_\gamma$; no GGC law with drift or a nonzero absolutely continuous Thorin part is a GGC factor with a GGC cofactor.
results.statement: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. If $\mu=\mu_1*\mu_2$ with $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$ GGC laws, then RH holds and the Thorin measures are $U_1=\sum_{\gamma>0}a_\gamma\delta_{\gamma^2}$ and $U_2=\sum_{\gamma>0}(m_\gamma-a_\gamma)\delta_{\gamma^2}$ with $0\le a_\gamma\le m_\gamma$, where $m_\gamma$ is the multiplicity of the zero ($m_\gamma=1$ for simple zeros), and $\mu_1$ is the law of $\sum_\gamma g_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent gamma variables $g_\gamma$ of shapes $a_\gamma$. No GGC law with drift or with a nonzero absolutely continuous Thorin part is a GGC factor of $\mu$ with a GGC cofactor.
results.label: ht:thm:rigid

results.name: Small time enclosure of the inverse first passage boundary of the reciprocal xi law, independent of RH
results.summary: With $F(t)=\mu(0,t]$ and $m(t)=\inf_{s\le t}b(s)$, $\sqrt t\bar\Phi_N^{-1}(F(t))\le b(t)$ and $m(t)\le\sqrt t\bar\Phi_N^{-1}(\frac12F(t))$; $-\log F(t)\sim\log^2(1/t)/(16t)$, so $\liminf b/\log(1/t)\ge1/(2\sqrt2)\ge\limsup m/\log(1/t)$, and $b\sim\log(1/t)/(2\sqrt2)$ if $b$ is nonincreasing near $0$; no use of RH.
results.statement: Let $\mu$ be the reciprocal xi law of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$, $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ over the zeros of the Riemann zeta function, and let $b$ be the boundary of the inverse first passage problem for $\mu$: $b$ is such that $\tau_b=\inf\{t>0:W_t\ge b(t)\}$ for a standard Brownian motion $W$ has law $\mu$. Write $F(t)=\mu(0,t]$ and $m(t)=\inf_{0<s\le t}b(s)$, and let $\Phi_{\mathrm N}$ be the standard normal distribution function, $\bar\Phi_{\mathrm N}=1-\Phi_{\mathrm N}$. For every $t>0$, $\sqrt t\,\bar\Phi_{\mathrm N}^{-1}(F(t))\le b(t)$ and $m(t)\le\sqrt t\,\bar\Phi_{\mathrm N}^{-1}(\frac12F(t))$. Moreover $-\log F(t)\sim(\log(1/t))^2/(16t)$ as $t\downarrow0$, so $\liminf_{t\downarrow0}b(t)/\log(1/t)\ge\frac1{2\sqrt2}$ and $\limsup_{t\downarrow0}m(t)/\log(1/t)\le\frac1{2\sqrt2}$, and if $b$ is nonincreasing near $0$ then $b(t)\sim\log(1/t)/(2\sqrt2)$. None of this depends on RH.
results.label: ht:prop:smallb

results.name: Moving a pair of zeros off the line by delta multiplies the Laplace transform by 1+6 delta^2 s/gamma^4 to first order
results.summary: Moving the pair at height $\gamma$ off the line by $\delta$ multiplies the Laplace transform, relative to the control, by $1+6\delta^2s/\gamma^4+O(\delta^2s^2/\gamma^6)$ for $|s|\ll\gamma^2$, which to first order shifts the mean by $-6\delta^2/\gamma^4$.
results.statement: Let $\mu$ be the reciprocal xi law, with Laplace transform $1/G$, $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ over the zeros of the Riemann zeta function (the control being the case of all zeros on the line). Moving the pair of zeros at height $\gamma$ off the line by $\delta$ multiplies the Laplace transform, relative to the control, by $1+6\delta^2s/\gamma^4+O(\delta^2s^2/\gamma^6)$ for $|s|\ll\gamma^2$. To first order this is the shift $\tau\mapsto\tau-6\delta^2/\gamma^4$ of the mean $\tau$.
results.label: ht:prop:resp

results.name: The reciprocal xi law as the reciprocal of an expected cosh under the size biased Biane Pitman Yor measure
results.summary: Under the size biased measure with density $Y^{1/2}/\mathbb EY^{1/2}$, $U=\log Y$ is symmetric with density $\Phi/\Xi(0)$, and $\mathbb Ee^{-s\tau}=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)=1/\mathbb E^*\cosh(\sqrt sU)$, which is $1/\mathbb E^*[\mathbb E[e^{-sT}|U]^{-1}]$ for $T$ the exit time of Brownian motion from $(-|U|/\sqrt2,|U|/\sqrt2)$.
results.statement: Let $Y=\sqrt{2/\pi}(\max_ub_u-\min_ub_u)$ for a standard Brownian bridge $b$, so that $\mathbb EY^s=2\xi(s)$, and let $\tau$ be the clock with $\mathbb Ee^{-s\tau}=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)$. Let $\mathbb P^*$ have density $Y^{1/2}/\mathbb EY^{1/2}$ with respect to $\mathbb P$ and let $U=\log Y$. Under $\mathbb P^*$ the variable $U$ is symmetric with density $\Phi/\Xi(0)$, where $\Xi(z)=\xi(\frac12+iz)$ and $\Phi$ is the kernel of Riemann and P\'olya; equivalently $U/2$ has density $2\Phi(2u)/\Xi(0)$. Moreover $\mathbb Ee^{-s\tau}=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)=1/\mathbb E^*\cosh(\sqrt sU)=1/\mathbb E^*[\mathbb E[e^{-sT}|U]^{-1}]$, where, given $U$, $T$ is the exit time of a standard Brownian motion from $(-|U|/\sqrt2,|U|/\sqrt2)$.
results.label: ht:prop:bpy

results.name: The law of the maximum of a Brownian excursion gives the Biane, Pitman and Yor identity for xi term by term
results.summary: From the explicit law of the maximum $M$ of a Brownian excursion, $Y=\sqrt{2/\pi}\,M$ has tail, mean excess and density given by the theta series, so $\mathbb{E}Y^s=2\xi(s)$ for every complex $s$ (the identity of Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001, derived term by term), and $\mathbb{P}(Y>1)=\frac12-\psi(1)=0.456783$ (computed); a note of Nicholas Polson.
results.statement: Let $M$ be the maximum of a standard Brownian excursion, whose law is (Chung 1976; Kennedy 1976) $\mathbb{P}(M\le m)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}(1-4n^2m^2)e^{-2n^2m^2}$ for $m>0$, and $Y=\sqrt{2/\pi}\,M$, which has the law of $\sqrt{2/\pi}$ times the range of a Brownian bridge, by the path transformation of Vervaat. Let $\psi(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}e^{-\pi n^2x}$, $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)\zeta(s)$ and $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})e^{-\pi n^2e^{4u}}$. Then for $y>0$, $\mathbb{P}(Y>y)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi n^2y^2-1)e^{-\pi n^2y^2}$, $\mathbb{E}(Y-y)^+=2y\,\psi(y^2)$ and the density of $Y$ is $f_Y(y)=2\Phi(\log y)\,y^{-3/2}$. Hence $\mathbb{E}Y^s=2\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)e^{(s-\frac12)u}\,du=2\xi(s)$ for every complex $s$, the identity of Biane, Pitman and Yor derived term by term from the law of $M$. With $y=e^u$, the function $k(u)=e^{-u/2}-2e^{u/2}\psi(e^{2u})$ equals $e^{-u/2}\,\mathbb{E}\min(Y,e^u)$ for $u\in\mathbb{R}$; its evenness is the case $g(y)=\min(1,e^u/y)$ of the size bias identity $\mathbb{E}g(1/Y)=\mathbb{E}\,Yg(Y)$ of Biane, Pitman and Yor, and its derivative at $0$ vanishes, which reads $\mathbb{P}(M>\sqrt{\pi/2})=\mathbb{P}(Y>1)=\frac12-\psi(1)=0.456783$ (computed). The derivation is from a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book.
results.label: ht:res:chung

results.name: The Davenport Heilbronn theta function is positive, giving a symmetric variable and a positive Polya kernel for a function violating RH
results.summary: With $a_n$ periodic mod $5$, $(a_0,\dots,a_4)=(0,1,\kappa,-\kappa,-1)$, $\kappa=0.2840790438$, $\theta_{DH}(x)=\sum a_nn\,e^{-\pi n^2x/5}>0$ for all $x>0$, so there are a probability law with Mellin transform proportional to $\xi_{DH}$, a symmetric $U_{DH}$ with $\mathbb E^*e^{wU_{DH}}=\xi_{DH}(\frac12+w)/\xi_{DH}(\frac12)$, and a positive Polya kernel $\Phi_{DH}$.
results.statement: Let $a_n$ be the Davenport and Heilbronn coefficients, periodic modulo $5$ with $(a_0,\dots,a_4)=(0,1,\kappa,-\kappa,-1)$ and $\kappa=0.2840790438$, let $\xi_{DH}$ be the completed Davenport and Heilbronn function (a function with a functional equation and an off line zero, as in the book), and $\theta_{DH}(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}a_nn\,e^{-\pi n^2x/5}$. Then $\theta_{DH}(x)>0$ for every $x>0$. Consequently there is a probability law on $(0,\infty)$ whose Mellin transform is a constant multiple of $\xi_{DH}$, a symmetric $U_{DH}$ with $\mathbb E^*e^{wU_{DH}}=\xi_{DH}(\frac12+w)/\xi_{DH}(\frac12)$, and a positive P\'olya kernel $\Phi_{DH}$.
results.label: ht:prop:dhtheta

results.name: Wiener and Gamma representation of the base point laws, and RH as monotonicity of the smoothed zero counting functions N_alpha
results.summary: For $\mu^{(\alpha)}$ with transform $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt s)$ and $h_\alpha(u)=N_\alpha^{-1}(u)^{-2}$, $X_\alpha=\int h_\alpha\,d\gamma_u$ has law $\mu^{(\alpha)}$ for every $\alpha\ge\sup_\rho\operatorname{Re}\rho$ (so every $\alpha\ge1$); RH holds iff $N_\alpha$ is nondecreasing for every $\alpha>\frac12$. (The convergence as $\alpha\downarrow\frac12$ under RH is only sketched in the book and is not entered.)
results.statement: For $\alpha>\frac12$ let $\mu^{(\alpha)}$ be the base point law with Laplace transform $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt s)$ and $N_\alpha'(t)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\alpha+it)=\frac1\pi\sum_\rho\frac{\alpha-\beta}{(\alpha-\beta)^2+(t-\gamma)^2}$ ($\beta=\operatorname{Re}\rho$), $N_\alpha(0)=0$, and $h_\alpha(u)=N_\alpha^{-1}(u)^{-2}$. On one gamma process $\gamma$, set $X_\alpha=\int_0^\infty h_\alpha(u)\,\mathrm d\gamma_u$. Then $X_\alpha$ has law $\mu^{(\alpha)}$ for every $\alpha\ge\sup_\rho\operatorname{Re}\rho$, in particular for every $\alpha\ge1$. RH holds if and only if $N_\alpha$ is nondecreasing for every $\alpha>\frac12$.
results.label: ht:prop:wg

results.name: The Taylor coefficients of xi(1/2+sqrt s) are a Polya frequency sequence if and only if RH, and unconditionally PF2
results.summary: RH holds iff $(c_n)$ is a P\'olya frequency sequence (all minors of the Toeplitz matrix $(c_{i-j})$ nonnegative), and unconditionally $(c_n)$ is PF$_2$: $c_n^2\ge c_{n-1}c_{n+1}$ for $n\ge1$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function, $F(s)=\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)/\xi(\frac12)=\sum_{n\ge0}c_ns^n$, so that $c_n=\mathbb EV^{2n}/(2n)!>0$ for the symmetric variable $V$ with density $\Phi/\Xi(0)$ ($\Phi$ Riemann's kernel), $c_0=1$, and let $s_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ for the zeros $\rho$ of $\zeta$ in the upper half plane, with $\theta_\rho\in[0,\pi)$ the angle between $s_\rho$ and the negative real axis ($\theta_\rho=0$ for a zero on the line). A sequence is PF$_k$ if all minors of its Toeplitz matrix of order at most $k$ are nonnegative, and a P\'olya frequency (PF) sequence if it is PF$_k$ for every $k$. (i) RH holds if and only if $(c_n)$ is a P\'olya frequency sequence, that is, every minor of the Toeplitz matrix $(c_{i-j})$ is nonnegative. (ii) Unconditionally, $(c_n)$ is PF$_2$: $c_n^2\ge c_{n-1}c_{n+1}$ for all $n\ge1$.
results.label: ht:thm:coef

results.name: A three term quadratic coefficient sequence is PF_k if and only if its angle is at most pi/(k+1)
results.summary: For $r>0$ and $0\le\theta<\pi$ the sequence $(1,2r^{-1}\cos\theta,r^{-2})$, the coefficients of $(1+s/re^{i\theta})(1+s/re^{-i\theta})$, is PF$_k$ if and only if $\theta\le\pi/(k+1)$.
results.statement: A sequence is PF$_k$ if all minors of order at most $k$ of its Toeplitz matrix are nonnegative. For $r>0$ and $0\le\theta<\pi$, the sequence $(1,\,2r^{-1}\cos\theta,\,r^{-2})$, the coefficient sequence of $(1+s/re^{i\theta})(1+s/re^{-i\theta})$, is PF$_k$ if and only if $\theta\le\pi/(k+1)$.
results.label: ht:lem:three

results.name: Angle theorem: if every zero has angle at most pi/(k+1) then the coefficient sequence of xi is PF_k
results.summary: If every zero of $\zeta$ satisfies $\theta_\rho\le\pi/(k+1)$, then the Taylor coefficients $(c_n)$ of $F(s)=\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)/\xi(\frac12)$ form a PF$_k$ sequence.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function, $F(s)=\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)/\xi(\frac12)=\sum_{n\ge0}c_ns^n$, so that $c_n=\mathbb EV^{2n}/(2n)!>0$ for the symmetric variable $V$ with density $\Phi/\Xi(0)$ ($\Phi$ Riemann's kernel), $c_0=1$, and let $s_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ for the zeros $\rho$ of $\zeta$ in the upper half plane, with $\theta_\rho\in[0,\pi)$ the angle between $s_\rho$ and the negative real axis ($\theta_\rho=0$ for a zero on the line). A sequence is PF$_k$ if all minors of its Toeplitz matrix of order at most $k$ are nonnegative, and a P\'olya frequency (PF) sequence if it is PF$_k$ for every $k$. If every zero of $\zeta$ satisfies $\theta_\rho\le\pi/(k+1)$, then the Taylor coefficients $(c_n)$ of $F$ form a PF$_k$ sequence.
results.label: ht:thm:angle

results.name: Unconditional rung count: the coefficient sequence of xi is PF_k for every k up to about 9.4e12
results.summary: Unconditionally $(c_n)$ is PF$_k$ for every $k\le\lfloor\pi H\rfloor-1=9424777960768$, $H=3\cdot10^{12}$; more generally PF$_K$ as soon as every zero with $\gamma\le(K+1)/\pi$ is on the line.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function, $F(s)=\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)/\xi(\frac12)=\sum_{n\ge0}c_ns^n$, so that $c_n=\mathbb EV^{2n}/(2n)!>0$ for the symmetric variable $V$ with density $\Phi/\Xi(0)$ ($\Phi$ Riemann's kernel), $c_0=1$, and let $s_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ for the zeros $\rho$ of $\zeta$ in the upper half plane, with $\theta_\rho\in[0,\pi)$ the angle between $s_\rho$ and the negative real axis ($\theta_\rho=0$ for a zero on the line). A sequence is PF$_k$ if all minors of its Toeplitz matrix of order at most $k$ are nonnegative, and a P\'olya frequency (PF) sequence if it is PF$_k$ for every $k$. Unconditionally, $(c_n)$ is PF$_k$ for every $k\le\lfloor\pi H\rfloor-1=9424777960768$, where $H=3\cdot10^{12}$ is the height to which all zeros are known to lie on the line (Platt and Trudgian). More generally, $(c_n)$ is PF$_K$ as soon as every zero with $\gamma\le(K+1)/\pi$ lies on the line.
results.label: ht:cor:rungs

results.name: Consequences of a zero free half plane beyond 7/8: GGC basepoint and even part laws, imaginary zeros of the even and odd parts of xi, and a bound on the de Bruijn Newman constant
results.status_text: conditional on $\zeta(s)\ne0$ for $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ (announced in October 2026, not refereed)
results.conditions: $\zeta(s)\ne0$ for $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ (announced in October 2026, not refereed)
results.summary: If $\zeta(s)\ne0$ for $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$, the basepoint laws $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt s)$ are GGCs for every $\alpha\ge\frac78$, with stable tails, the even and odd parts of $w\mapsto\xi(\alpha+w)$ have only imaginary zeros for $\alpha\ge\frac78$, the even part laws are GGCs for $\alpha>\frac78$, and de Bruijn's theorem gives $\Lambda\le\frac9{32}$.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)\zeta(s)$ be Riemann's xi function, $\sigma_{\max}=\sup\operatorname{Re}\rho$ over its zeros $\rho$, $\Delta=\sigma_{\max}-\frac12$, $b_\alpha=\frac{\xi'}\xi(\alpha)$, $U_\alpha(\tau)$ the clock, $\pi^{-1}$ times the continuous variation of $\arg\xi(\alpha+it)$ over $0\le t\le\tau$, and $A_\alpha(w)=\frac12(\xi(\alpha+w)+\xi(\alpha-w))$, $B_\alpha(w)=\frac1{2i}(\xi(\alpha+w)-\xi(\alpha-w))$ the even and odd parts of $w\mapsto\xi(\alpha+w)$. Assume that $\zeta(s)\ne0$ for $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$, so that $\Delta\le\frac38$ and every zero has real part in $[\frac18,\frac78]$. (i) For every $\alpha\ge\frac78$ the law $\mu^{(\alpha)}$ with Laplace transform $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt s)$ is a generalized gamma convolution (GGC). For $\alpha>\frac78$ its Thorin measure is absolutely continuous, with density $\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}\xi(\alpha+i\tau)$ in the ordinate variable $\tau$, a sum of Lorentzians of widths at least $\alpha-\frac78$, and $\mu^{(\alpha)}((y,\infty))\sim b_\alpha/\sqrt{\pi y}$ as $y\to\infty$. (ii) For $\alpha>\frac78$ the clock $U_\alpha$ is strictly increasing, and $\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}\xi>0$ on $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$; in terms of $\zeta$, $-\operatorname{Re}\frac{\zeta'}\zeta(\alpha+i\tau)<\operatorname{Re}\mathcal{A}(\alpha+i\tau)=\frac12\log\frac\tau{2\pi}+O(\tau^{-2})$ at every height $\tau$ and for every $\alpha>\frac78$, where $\mathcal{A}(s)=\frac1s+\frac1{s-1}-\frac12\log\pi+\frac12\frac{\Gamma'}\Gamma(\frac s2)$. (iii) For $\alpha\ge\frac78$ the functions $A_\alpha$ and $B_\alpha$ have only purely imaginary zeros, simple for $\alpha>\frac78$; for every $\alpha>\frac78$ the positive zeros of $t\mapsto\operatorname{Re}\xi(\alpha+it)$ are the points where $U_\alpha$ crosses the levels $k-\frac12$, $k=1,2,\dots$, and the even part law with Laplace transform $\xi(\alpha)/A_\alpha(\sqrt s)$ is a GGC. (iv) The de Bruijn Newman constant $\Lambda$, the infimum of the $t$ for which $H_t(z)=\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi(u)\cos(zu)\,du$ has only real zeros, where $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})$ and $H_0(z)=\frac18\xi(\frac{1+iz}2)$, satisfies $\Lambda\le2\Delta^2\le\frac9{32}=0.28125$, by de Bruijn's theorem.
results.label: pol:thm:qrh

results.name: Under (Q_{7/8}) the poles of 1/xi(1/2+sqrt w) lie in a parabola with vertex at most 9/64, and the sliver of the local theorem becomes thinner
results.status_text: conditional on The quasi Riemann hypothesis $(\mathrm Q_{7/8})$ of the book, which rests on the unrefereed half plane of OpenAI (2026)
results.conditions: The quasi Riemann hypothesis $(\mathrm Q_{7/8})$ of the book, which rests on the unrefereed half plane of OpenAI (2026).
results.summary: Under $(\mathrm Q_{7/8})$ every pole $(\rho-\frac12)^2$ of $1/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt w)$ has $(\operatorname{Im}w)^2\le\frac9{16}(\frac9{64}-\operatorname{Re}w)$, a parabola with vertex at most $\frac9{64}$ against $\frac14$ with no hypothesis, and the sliver in Theorem bs:thm:local can be replaced by a set of half width about $\frac34X$ instead of $X$ at abscissa $-X^2$.
results.statement: Assume $(\mathrm Q_{7/8})$, which rests on the unrefereed half plane of OpenAI (2026). Every pole $(\rho-\frac12)^2$ of $1/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt w)$ lies in the closed region $(\operatorname{Im}w)^2\le4\Delta^2(\Delta^2-\operatorname{Re}w)\le\frac9{16}(\frac9{64}-\operatorname{Re}w)$, bounded by a parabola with focus $0$ and vertex $\Delta^2\le\frac9{64}$, against the vertex $\frac14$ with no hypothesis. Theorem bs:thm:local holds with the sliver $\mathcal E_{T_0}$ replaced by the thinner set $\mathcal E'_{T_0}=\{x+iy:\ x<-T_0^2+\frac34T_0+\frac9{64},\ y^2\le\frac9{16}(\frac9{32}-x)\}$, whose half width at the abscissa $-X^2$ is about $\frac34X$, against about $X$ for $\mathcal E_{T_0}$.
results.label: tx5:prop:sliver

results.name: Gaussian smoothed Möbius sum: explicit formula over the zeros, with RH and the quasi Riemann hypothesis as growth exponents, and the trivial zero term as a finite range leading term only
results.summary: For the Gaussian smoothed Möbius sum $M_{\rm g}(x)$ the explicit formula over zeros and trivial zeros holds with a divergent trivial zero series, $\sup\operatorname{Re}\rho\le\sigma$ if and only if $M_{\rm g}(x)=O(x^{\sigma-2/3+\varepsilon})$, and the leading trivial zero term $c_1x^{-8/3}$ dominates $M_{\rm g}$ on a finite range of $x$ only; nothing in it depends on the quasi Riemann hypothesis.
results.statement: For $x>0$ let $M_{\rm g}(x)=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{(2)}x^{v-2/3}\frac{e^{(v-5/6)^2}}{\zeta(v)}dv=\frac{x^{-2/3}}{2\sqrt\pi}\sum_{n\ge1}\mu(n)(\frac xn)^{5/6}\exp(-\frac14\log^2\frac xn)$, and $\sigma_{\max}=\sup\operatorname{Re}\rho$. (i) For every $K\ge1$ there are heights $T_m\in[m,m+1]$ such that $M_{\rm g}(x)=\lim_m\sum_{|\gamma|<T_m}\operatorname{Res}_{v=\rho}\frac{x^{v-2/3}e^{(v-5/6)^2}}{\zeta(v)}+\sum_{k=1}^K\frac{e^{(2k+5/6)^2}}{\zeta'(-2k)}x^{-2k-2/3}+I_K(x)$, with $I_K(x)=O(x^{-2K-5/3})$; at a simple zero the residue is $e^{(\rho-5/6)^2}x^{\rho-2/3}/\zeta'(\rho)$, and as $K\to\infty$ the trivial zero series diverges. (ii) $\sigma_{\max}\le\sigma$ if and only if $M_{\rm g}(x)=O(x^{\sigma-2/3+\varepsilon})$ as $x\to\infty$ for every $\varepsilon>0$; RH is the exponent $-\frac16$ and $(\mathrm Q_{7/8})$ the exponent $\frac5{24}$. (iii) $M_{\rm g}(x)=c_1x^{-8/3}+E(x)+O(x^{-11/3})$ with $c_1=e^{(17/6)^2}/\zeta'(-2)=-1.00659\times10^5$ and $E$ the sum over the zeros, and $E(x)$ is not $O(x^{\sigma-2/3})$ for any $\sigma<\sigma_{\max}$; so $c_1x^{-8/3}$ is the leading term on a finite range of $x$ only. Computed three ways, $M_{\rm g}(10^3)=-5.53094\times10^{-4}$, and $M_{\rm g}(x)/(c_1x^{-8/3})=0.5495,0.9470,0.99856,0.999983$ at $x=10^3,\dots,10^6$.
results.label: tx3:prop:signal

results.name: Under (Q_{7/8}), M(x) is O(x^{7/8+epsilon}), the Möbius series converges to 1/zeta on Re s above 7/8, and the Möbius series of 1/zeta(1/2+sqrt s) converges on the parabola region H_{3/8}
results.status_text: conditional on The quasi Riemann hypothesis $(\mathrm Q_{7/8})$ of the book, which rests on the unrefereed half plane of OpenAI (2026)
results.conditions: The quasi Riemann hypothesis $(\mathrm Q_{7/8})$ of the book, which rests on the unrefereed half plane of OpenAI (2026).
results.summary: Under $(\mathrm Q_{7/8})$, $M(x)=\sum_{n\le x}\mu(n)=O(x^{7/8+\varepsilon})$ and $\sum\mu(n)n^{-s}=1/\zeta(s)$ on $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$, so the Möbius series of $1/\zeta(\frac12+\sqrt s)$ converges on $H_{3/8}$, which contains the region $H_{1/2}$ of absolute convergence; the proof is Titchmarsh's argument for RH with $\frac78$ in place of $\frac12$.
results.statement: Assume $(\mathrm Q_{7/8})$, which rests on the unrefereed half plane of OpenAI (2026). Then $M(x)=\sum_{n\le x}\mu(n)=O(x^{7/8+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, and $\sum_n\mu(n)n^{-s}$ converges to $1/\zeta(s)$ on $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$. So the Möbius series of $1/\zeta(\frac12+\sqrt s)$ converges on $H_{3/8}=\{\operatorname{Re}\sqrt s>\frac38\}=\{u+iy:\ u>\frac9{64}-\frac{16}9y^2\}$, which contains the region $H_{1/2}$ of absolute convergence of Section ch:rz1. The proof follows Titchmarsh's argument for the Riemann hypothesis, with $\frac78$ in place of $\frac12$: $1/\zeta(s)=O(|t|^\varepsilon)$ on $\operatorname{Re}s\ge\frac78+\varepsilon$, then Perron's formula and partial summation.
results.label: tx5:prop:mertens

results.name: Least prime in a progression under the half plane 7/8 for every Dirichlet L function: psi(x;q,a) = x/phi(q) + O(x^{7/8} log^2(qx)) and the least prime is O(q^{8+epsilon})
results.status_text: conditional on That no Dirichlet $L$ function vanishes in $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$, which is claimed by OpenAI (2026) and not refereed
results.conditions: That no Dirichlet $L$ function vanishes in $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$, which is claimed by OpenAI (2026) and not refereed.
results.summary: If no Dirichlet $L$ function vanishes in $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$, the explicit formula gives $\psi(x;q,a)=x/\varphi(q)+O(x^{7/8}\log^2(qx))$ uniformly in $(a,q)=1$ and the least prime $p\equiv a\pmod q$ is $O(q^{8+\varepsilon})$, weaker than Xylouris's unconditional exponent $5.2$.
results.statement: Assume, as OpenAI (2026) claims and without a refereed proof, that no Dirichlet $L$ function vanishes in $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$, so that every nontrivial zero has $\frac18\le\beta\le\frac78$ and $|\rho|\ge\frac18$. The explicit formula for $\psi(x,\chi)$ with $T=x$ (Davenport, Chapters 19 and 20) and $\sum_{|\gamma|\le x}|\rho|^{-1}=O(\log^2(qx))$ give $\psi(x;q,a)=x/\varphi(q)+O(x^{7/8}\log^2(qx))$ uniformly in $(a,q)=1$, so the least prime $p\equiv a\pmod q$ is $O(q^{8+\varepsilon})$. This is weaker than the unconditional exponent $5$ of Xylouris (2011), and it is not the Linnik constant $K$ of Chapter gl.
results.label: tx5:rem:leastprime

results.name: Compensated clock positivity on every line to the right of alpha zero under a zero free half plane, by pairing each zero with its mirror image
results.status_text: conditional on $\zeta(s)\ne0$ for $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha_0$, a fixed $\alpha_0$ with $\frac12\le\alpha_0<1$ (RH when $\alpha_0=\frac12$)
results.conditions: $\zeta(s)\ne0$ for $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha_0$, a fixed $\alpha_0$ with $\frac12\le\alpha_0<1$ (RH when $\alpha_0=\frac12$)
results.summary: If $\zeta$ has no zero with real part greater than $\alpha_0$, then $D_\alpha(r)=\operatorname{Re}\xi'/\xi(\alpha+ir)-\xi'/\xi(\alpha)$ is positive for every $\alpha>\alpha_0$ and every real $r\ne0$, proved by pairing each zero with its mirror image under $\rho\mapsto1-\bar\rho$, so that the position of a zero near the boundary does not matter.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $D_\alpha(r)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}\xi(\alpha+ir)-\frac{\xi'}\xi(\alpha)$. Let $\frac12\le\alpha_0<1$ and assume that $\zeta$ has no zero with $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha_0$. Then $D_\alpha(r)>0$ for every $\alpha>\alpha_0$ and every real $r\ne0$ (for $\alpha_0<\alpha\le1$ by the pairing argument, and for $\alpha\ge1$ with no hypothesis).
results.label: pol:thm:qrhpair

results.name: One block for each zero, the Hadamard blocks of the compensated reciprocal of xi
results.summary: Under the quasi Riemann hypothesis every zero pair contributes an explicit factor whose Thorin density is a recentred pair of Cauchy bumps, no single factor is a GGC, and the blocks sum to the Thorin density of the compensated reciprocal.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and let $\frac12\le\alpha_0<1$, suppose that $\zeta$ has no zero with $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha_0$ and let $\alpha>\alpha_0$, so that every width $c=\alpha-\beta_\rho$ of a zero $\rho=\beta_\rho+i\gamma_\rho$ from the basepoint $\alpha$ is positive. The Hadamard product splits the compensated reciprocal of $\xi$ into one factor for each pair $\rho,\bar\rho$ with $\gamma=\gamma_\rho>0$, $\Phi_{\alpha,\rho}(\frac{w^2}2)=\frac{c^2+\gamma^2}{(c+w)^2+\gamma^2}e^{2cw/(c^2+\gamma^2)}$. By Frullani's integral $-\log\Phi_{\alpha,\rho}(w^2/2)=\int_0^\infty(e^{-wy}+wy-1)\varrho_\rho(dy)$ with the signed measure $\varrho_\rho(dy)=-2y^{-1}e^{-cy}\cos(\gamma y)dy$, and the sine squared lemma gives the density $\pi^{-1}[f(c,r-\gamma)+f(c,r+\gamma)-2f(c,\gamma)]$ in the ordinate $r$, with $f(c,x)=c/(c^2+x^2)$ (Cauchy kernels of width $c$ recentred at $\pm\gamma$), which sums over the zeros to $\pi^{-1}D_\alpha(r)$, $D_\alpha(r)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}\xi(\alpha+ir)-\frac{\xi'}\xi(\alpha)$. No single block is a GGC, nor a Laplace transform, since $\Phi_{\alpha,\rho}(w^2/2)\to\infty$ as $w\to\infty$. As $c\downarrow0$ the block tends to $(1+w^2/\gamma^2)^{-1}$, an exponential law in $u=w^2/2$ whose Thorin measure is the unit atom at $r=\gamma$. Credited to a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book.
results.label: pol:rem:blocks

results.name: A quasi Riemann hypothesis at alpha zero is equivalent to the compensated clock condition on every line to its right
results.summary: For $\frac12\le\alpha_0<1$, the zeta function has no zero with real part greater than $\alpha_0$ if and only if $\operatorname{Re}\xi'/\xi(\alpha+ir)-\xi'/\xi(\alpha)\ge0$ for every $\alpha$ in $(\alpha_0,1)$ and every real $r$ at which it is defined.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and, for $\alpha>\frac12$ and real $r$, $D_\alpha(r)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}\xi(\alpha+ir)-\frac{\xi'}\xi(\alpha)$. For $\frac12\le\alpha_0<1$ the following are equivalent. (a) The zeta function has no zero with $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha_0$. (b) $D_\alpha(r)\ge0$ for every $\alpha\in(\alpha_0,1)$ and every real $r$ at which $D_\alpha$ is defined. When they hold, $D_\alpha(r)>0$ for every $\alpha\in(\alpha_0,1)$ and every real $r\ne0$.
results.label: pol:cor:equiv

results.name: The compensated reciprocal of xi is a GGC with positive Thorin density at every basepoint above 7/8 under a zero free half plane
results.status_text: conditional on $\zeta(s)\ne0$ for $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ (announced in October 2026, not refereed)
results.conditions: $\zeta(s)\ne0$ for $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ (announced in October 2026, not refereed)
results.summary: If $\zeta(s)\ne0$ for $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$, the compensated reciprocal of xi at every basepoint $\alpha>\frac78$ is a GGC whose Thorin density is positive at every height, inside the critical strip for $\frac78<\alpha<1$, although the primal measure cannot even be stated there; for $\alpha\ge1$ this holds with no hypothesis.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $b_\alpha=\frac{\xi'}\xi(\alpha)$. Assume that $\zeta(s)\ne0$ for $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$, and let $\alpha>\frac78$. Then the compensated reciprocal $e^{wb_\alpha}\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+w)$ is the Laplace transform in $u=w^2/2$ of a generalized gamma convolution, whose Thorin density $\omega_\alpha(z)=\frac1{\pi\sqrt{2z}}\big[\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}\xi(\alpha+i\sqrt{2z})-\frac{\xi'}\xi(\alpha)\big]$ is positive at every height $z>0$. For $\alpha\ge1$ this holds with no hypothesis.
results.label: pol:cor:qrhggc

results.name: GGC basepoints of the compensated reciprocal of xi form the closed half line from the largest real part of a zero
results.summary: The set of basepoints at which the compensated reciprocal of xi is a GGC is exactly the closed half line from the supremum of the real parts of the zeros, which for the supremum one half is the Riemann hypothesis.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Theta=\sup\operatorname{Re}\rho$ over the nontrivial zeros $\rho$. The set of $\alpha>0$ at which $e^{\sqrt{2u}\,b_\alpha}\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt{2u})$, with $b_\alpha=\frac{\xi'}\xi(\alpha)$, is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution is exactly $[\Theta,\infty)$. For $\alpha<\Theta$ a zero with $\operatorname{Re}\rho>\alpha$ gives the transform a pole at $u=(\rho-\alpha)^2/2$ off the negative axis, so it is not a GGC. For $\alpha>\Theta$ it is one, and at $\alpha=\Theta$ it is the weak limit of GGC laws as $\alpha\downarrow\Theta$, hence a GGC. For $\Theta=\frac12$ this is the Riemann hypothesis. A zero on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\Theta$ gives the Thorin measure at $\Theta$ an atom at its ordinate, of mass its multiplicity; if $\Theta$ is not attained there is no atom. Credited to a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book.
results.label: pol:res:halfline
